334 [p4RA] [Title page printed in black and vermilion within an elaborate woodcut architectural frame featuring an arch supported by decorated pilasters, with evangelists and floral arabesques:][^9]

**OCTOECHOS,**

**THAT IS,**

**THE BOOK OF THE EIGHT TONES**

The work of our venerable father

**JOHN DAMASCENE:**

And other God-inspired

Holy Fathers.

[p4RB] By the help of Divine grace from on high: and with the blessing of the most holy Lord and Father, the Archbishop of Constantinople, Ecumenical Patriarch.

And through the zealous diligence and expenditure of the Church Brotherhood, at the temple of the all-honorable Dormition of the Most Holy Ever-Virgin Mary, depicted in their Printing-House.

[Woodcut typographic ornament]

**IN LVIV**

In the year from the creation of the world, 7138 [1630].

And from the Nativity of Christ, 1630,

in the month of December, the 15th day.

[Woodcut printer's device of the Lviv Dormition Brotherhood: the architectural gate of the City of Lviv with three towers and a passant lion, flanked by the letters G-A-V-L]

[p5LA] [Woodcut heraldic achievement of the Mohyla family, Voivodes of Moldavia, surrounded by the initials P-B-M-M-K-P:][^10]

**UPON THE MOST RENOWNED CREST OF THEIR ILLUSTRIOUS MERCY,**

**THE MOHYLAS, VOIVODES OF MOLDAVIA.**

[p5LB] [Six-line heraldic epigram in Ruthenian verse:]

These snowy emblems they possess as their crest,

Which from of old have valiantly humbled their adversaries.

Forgetting not to vanquish wicked foes,

And to bestow upon their renowned posterity eternity:

Therefore here also they possess great renown,

And in the eternal Crown and in heaven do receive it.

[Woodcut typographic headband]

[Psalm 120 and Psalm 133]

*Behold, the Bridegroom comes at midnight, and blessed is the servant whom He shall find watching, but unworthy again is he whom He shall find heedless. Beware therefore, O my soul, lest thou be weighed down with sleep, lest thou be given over unto death, and be shut out from the kingdom. But arise, crying aloud: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, O our God; through the prayers of the Mother of God, have mercy on us. Glory:*

*Reflecting upon that fearful day, O my soul, keep watch, making bright thy lamps, enlightening them with the oil [of good works]; for thou knowest not when the voice shall come unto thee, saying: Behold, thy Bridegroom comes!*

...translate...

...eternal life...

...of the Immortal One...

*Kyrie eleison.*

*My hope is the Father, my refuge is the Son, my protection is the Holy Spirit: O Holy Trinity, glory to Thee!*

*Prayer of Saint Eustratius:*

I magnify Thee with great praises, O Lord, for Thou hast looked upon my lowliness, and hast not shut me up into the hands of the enemies, but hast saved my soul from afflictions. And now, O Master, let Thy hand cover me [f. 1vB] *Prayer of Saint Mardarios:*

O Master God, Father Almighty, O Lord, Only-Begotten Son, Jesus Christ, and Holy Spirit, one Godhead, one Power: have mercy on me, a sinner, and by the judgments which Thou knowest, save me, Thine unworthy servant; for Thou art blessed unto ages of ages. Amen.

*Mutual Forgiveness Rubric:*

Bless, holy fathers, and forgive me, a sinner...

May the Lord forgive you...

[p6RA] [Woodcut headpiece depicting Christ teaching the Apostles][^13]

**UNTO THE MOST VENERABLE IN CHRIST**

**LORD AND FATHER, HIS ILLUSTRIOUS MERCY, THE LORD**

**PETER MOHYLA, VOIVODE’S SON**

**OF THE MOLDAVIAN LANDS.**

Great Archimandrite of the Holy, Great, and Wonder-Working

**LAVRA OF THE CAVES OF KYIV.**

Unto our gracious Lord and Benefactor.

[p6RB] A true proverb it is, most illustrious and gracious Lord, our Father and Pastor, that beneficence is a golden chain and fetter whereby the human soul is secretly bound and drawn: this we ourselves have manifestly experienced. For it is evident unto the whole world what generous and illustrious benefits our Lviv Brotherhood Church hath received from Their Mercies, the illustrious rulers of Moldo-Wallachia, the renowned Mohylas, ancestors of Your Mercy—in particular, of pious memory, His Mercy Symeon, your father, and His Mercy Jeremiah, uncle of Your Illustriousness. For by their renowned and lavish expenditure our church was exalted on high, remaining unto their eternal glory.

Likewise thee also, O renowned Mohyla, our Father and Pastor, by thine outstanding noble virtues, our Brotherhood hath ever possessed as a particular benefactor, experiencing special proofs of confirmed benevolence: which have so bound, strengthened, and drawn us unto thee, that in renewing the memory of those of holy remembrance, we strive that we, well-wishers in God, might in some small part repay Their Mercies, the ancestors of Your Grace, and you their renowned descendants. Especially since virtue itself and gratitude, ready to spring forth from our hearts into open sight, demand this of us. With the memory therefore of light and grateful confession of the ancestors of Your Illustriousness, while offering yearly prayer for their souls and for the long-lasting life and health of Your Grace in this world, with fitting declarations:

[p7LA] our desire is ardently to honor and exalt the renowned family of Your Illustriousness with immortal renown. Striving therefore with all our strength, behold, following the renewal of our Brotherhood Printing-House, we issue under the illustrious name of Your Grace this very first book, filled with God-inspired consolations, and offer it unto thee, as a pious man unto a pious patron. For who is such a witness thereof, as that thou, being born of a most renowned family, having deservedly gained the royal favor of the Crown of Poland and the goodwill of His Royal Majesty our gracious King, and of the whole Commonwealth, and having formed bonds of friendship with the noble assembly of Senators of the Crown of Poland, didst renounce all these things out of piety, making an offering unto God the Creator, voluntarily embracing poverty and virginal chastity, lovingly receiving the angelic monastic habit? And immediately, by the providence of God and the favor of His Royal Majesty, by the common consent of both spiritual and lay fathers, thou wast crowned with high ecclesiastical dignity. [^14]

[p7LB] Witness thereto is thy fervent prayer unto God the Creator, unto His most pure and most blessed Mother, and unto the beloved Eastern Church. Witness also is thy zealous and pious care for the multiplication of the praise of God, for the elevation of schools, for good order in the Monastery, and for the internal and external adornment of churches. By the rule of thy piety, not only Kyiv, but the whole Rus’ land rejoices and gives thanks unto God, that unto that holy place, for the profit and consolation of all Christendom, after holy and pious men, He hath granted so holy, pious, and watchful a Pastor.

Unto thee therefore, a pious father, we offer, present, and dedicate this pious Book, and place it beneath the broad wings of our Father and Pastor. Let it fly forth under thy patronage; let it pay thee this tribute; under thy name let it go forth securely into the world. Receive therefore, most illustrious, most venerable, and gracious Father and our Pastor, this work kindly, graciously, and favorably; and deign ever to keep us, thy servants and perpetual petitioners, grateful well-wishers of Your Illustriousness, in thy gracious, fatherly love and holy prayers.

Written in Lviv. In the year from the Incarnation of the Son of God, 1631, in the month of December, the 25th day.

Unto Your Venerable Illustriousness,

our Gracious Lord,

Perpetual intercessors in God

and humble servants,

[The Stauropegion Brotherhood of the Dormition of the Most Holy Mother of God in Lviv]

---

# TONE 1: SATURDAY VESPERS, SUNDAY MATINS, AND WEEKDAY OFFICES

[f. 1rA] **Tone One**

**ON SATURDAY EVENING AT GREAT VESPERS**[^15]

*Resurrectional Stichera. Tone 1:*

Accept our evening prayers, O holy Lord, and grant us remission of sins, for Thou alone art He Who hast revealed the Resurrection unto the world.

Surround Sion, O ye peoples, and encompass her, and give glory within her unto Him Who is risen from the dead; for He is our God, Who hath delivered us from our iniquities.

Come, O ye peoples, let us sing and worship Christ, glorifying His Resurrection from the dead; for He is our God, Who hath delivered the world from the deceit of the enemy.

*Other Eastern Stichera, Tone 1:*

Rejoice, O heavens; sound the trumpet, ye foundations of the earth; cry aloud with joy, ye mountains! For behold, Emmanuel hath nailed our sins [f. 1rB] to the Cross, and, putting death to death, hath granted life, raising fallen Adam, the father of all, for He loves mankind.

Him Who was willingly crucified in the flesh for our sake, Who suffered, and was buried, and rose from the dead, let us praise, saying: Confirm Thy Church in Orthodoxy, O Christ, and make peace in our life, for Thou art good and lovest mankind.

Standing unworthy before Thy life-receiving tomb, we offer a hymn of praise unto Thine ineffable loving-kindness, O Christ our God; for Thou, being sinless, didst accept the Cross and death, that Thou mightest grant the Resurrection unto the world, as Thou lovest mankind.

Let us praise the Word, co-eternal with the Father [^16] [f. 1vA] Who ineffably came forth from a virginal womb, and willingly accepted the Cross and death for our sake, and rose in glory, saying: O Giver of life, O Lord, glory to Thee, the Savior of our souls!

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*

Let us sing of Mary the Virgin, the glory of the whole world, who blossomed forth from mankind and gave birth unto the Master, the heavenly gate, the hymn of the bodiless hosts and the adornment of the faithful. For she was revealed as heaven and the temple of the Godhead. She, having broken down the middle wall of enmity, brought in peace and opened the kingdom. Having her, therefore, as the anchor of faith, we have as our Defender the Lord Who was born of her. Be of good courage therefore, be of good courage, O people of God; for He shall conquer the enemies, for He is almighty.

*Rubrics:*

*Then: The Entrance. O Gladsome Light. The Prokeimenon of the day: The Lord is King, He is robed in majesty. But outside of a vigil, if there is an augmented litany: Vouchsafe, O Lord, and the rest.*

*At the Aposticha, Resurrectional Sticheron, Tone 1:*

[f. 1vB] By Thy Passion, O Christ, we have been set free from passions, and by Thy Resurrection we have been delivered from corruption: O Lord, glory to Thee!

*Other Stichera according to the Alphabet. Tone 1:*

*Verse: The Lord is King, He is robed in majesty.*

Let creation rejoice, let the heavens be glad; let the nations clap their hands with gladness! For Christ our Savior hath nailed our sins to the Cross, and, putting death to death, hath granted us life, raising the fallen Adam, the father of all, for He loves mankind.

*Verse: For He hath established the world, so that it cannot be moved.*

Being King of heaven and earth, O Incomprehensible One, Thou wast willingly crucified for the love of mankind! Hades, meeting Thee below, was embittered, and the souls of the righteous, receiving Thee, rejoiced; and Adam, seeing Thee, the Creator, in the nethermost regions, arose! O wonder! How did He Who is the Life of all taste of death? But as He willed to enlighten the world, crying out and saying: O Lord Who art risen from the dead, glory to Thee!

[f. 2rA] *Verse: Holiness becomes Thine house, O Lord, unto length of days.* [^17]

The Myrrh-bearing women, carrying myrrh, reached Thy tomb with haste and lamentation; and not finding Thy most pure Body, but learning from the Angel of the new and glorious miracle, they said unto the Apostles: The Lord is risen, granting great mercy unto the world!

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*

Lo, the prophecy of Isaiah is fulfilled, for a Virgin hast thou given birth, and after giving birth, as before giving birth, thou didst remain. For God was He Who was born; therefore nature was miraculously made new. But, O Mother of God, despise not the supplications of thy servants offered unto thee in thy temple; but as thou bearest the Merciful One in thine arms, have compassion upon thy servants, and pray that our souls may be saved.

*Then: Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart... Trisagion. After Our Father... Resurrectional Troparion, Tone 1:*

When the stone had been sealed by the Jews, and the soldiers were guarding [f. 2rB] Thine immaculate Body, Thou didst arise on the third day, O Savior, granting life unto the world. Therefore the Heavenly Powers cried out unto Thee, O Giver of life: Glory to Thy Resurrection, O Christ! Glory to Thy kingdom! Glory to Thy dispensation, O only Lover of mankind!

*Theotokion:*

As Gabriel proclaimed unto thee, O Virgin, *Rejoice!*, with that voice the Master of all became incarnate in thee, the holy Ark, as the righteous David said. Thou wast shown to be more spacious than the heavens, having borne thy Creator. Glory to Him Who dwelt in thee! Glory to Him Who came forth from thee! Glory to Him Who hath set us free through thy giving birth!

Nailed to the Cross, O Life of all, and accounted among the dead, O immortal Lord: Thou didst arise on the third day, O Savior, and didst raise Adam from corruption. # ON SUNDAY EVENING, AT "LORD, I HAVE CRIED"
*Penitential Stichera, Tone 1.*

*Podoben: "O all-lauded martyrs" (Прехвальніи мч̃нци):*

*The work of Joseph.*

[f. 13rA] O most good Father: Thou didst send Thine all-good Son, the Lord, to take upon His shoulder the prodigal son, to bring back the straying sheep, and to restore him unto the place whence he fell: into the fold of Thine Angels, the unerring Powers.

O most good Father: moved by the abounding goodness of Thy tender mercy, as God of majesty Thou didst bring forth all things out of non-existence; and thereafter, having fashioned man with Thine own hand in Thine image, when he was corrupted through the transgression of Thy commandments, Thou didst rebuild him as the Lover of mankind.

O Lord and Word: being the all-true Son of the heavenly Father, Thou didst appear for our sake, being the Son of man, that having taken upon Thy shoulders me, a man deceived by the guile of the serpent, like a stray sheep, Thou mightest bring me up into the heavenly fold.

[f. 13rB] *Other Stichera to the Bodiless Powers.*

*Podoben: "The same Tone and Podoben" (Гла́съ и҆ подо́бенъ то́йже):*

Bodiless Angels, standing before the throne of God and illuminated by the splendors from thence, shining with eternal outpourings of light and becoming secondary lights: pray ye that there may be granted unto our souls peace and great mercy.

Immortal Angels, as having received true life from the [ever]-gracious One Who is slow to anger, [unceasingly offer up supplication], that we may be delivered [from corrupt passions and] the captivity [of the evil one, O holy Archangels...][^23] [f. 13vA] [Thrones] of the Lord, six-winged Seraphim, and many-eyed divine Cherubim, vessels of wisdom; divine Powers and Dominions: pray unto Christ, that He may grant unto our souls peace and great mercy.

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*

Having become the pure dwelling-place of God, O pure one: pray together with the Bodiless Powers, that I may finish the journey of this life in purity, lest the evening of death overtake me unprepared and cast me into the fiery flame to be tormented; but snatch me away from this!

*Then: O Gladsome Light. After this, Prokeimenon, Tone 4:*

*Behold now, bless ye the Lord, all ye servants of the Lord [Psalm 133:1 LXX].*

*Verse: Ye that stand in the house of the Lord, in the courts of the house of our God [Psalm 133:2 LXX].*

*Then: Vouchsafe, O Lord, to keep us this evening without sin.*

*At the Aposticha, Penitential Stichera, Tone 1:*

As a great abyss are my transgressions, O Savior, and grievously am I sunken in mine iniquities; stretch forth Thy hand unto me and save me, as the God Who loves mankind, and have mercy on me.

*Verse: Unto Thee have I lifted up mine eyes, unto Thee that dwellest in heaven.*

[Ensnared] by evil thoughts and base deeds, O Savior, grant me turning unto Thee: save me and have mercy on me.

*Verse: Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us, for we are utterly filled with contempt.*

[f. 13vB] Joy of the heavenly ranks, and mighty helper of men on earth: O all-pure Virgin, save us who flee unto thee, for after God we have placed our hope in thee, O Mother of God.

*Then: Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart... and the Dismissal.*

## ON MONDAY AT MATINS

*After the 1st Kathisma, Penitential Sessional Hymns, Tone 1:*

In iniquities was I conceived, prodigal that I am; I dare not look up unto the height of heaven, but taking courage in Thy love for mankind, I cry: O God, cleanse me, a sinner, and save me!

If the righteous man scarcely be saved, where shall I, a sinner, appear, who have not borne the burden and heat of the day? But with the laborers of the eleventh hour, number me, O God, and have mercy on me.

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*

Beholding the wonder of wonders in thee, O thou full of grace, creation rejoices; for thou didst conceive without seed and ineffably give birth unto Him Whom the ranks of Angels cannot behold: Him do thou implore, O Mother of God, that our souls may be saved.

*After the 2nd Kathisma, Penitential Sessional Hymns, Tone 1:*

Haste Thou to open Thy Fatherly embrace unto me: prodigally have I squandered my life, looking upon the inexhaustible wealth of Thy bounties, O Savior; despise not now my impoverished heart. For unto Thee, O Lord, in compunction do I cry: Father, I have sinned against heaven and before Thee!

Having distanced myself without measure from Thee, prodigally have I squandered my life, [f. 14rA] ever in bondage to irrational passions; but receive me through the prayers of Thine Angels, O compassionate Father, as the prodigal son, and save me, I pray Thee!

*For the Martyrs:*

With the praise of suffering and the honor of crowns were the glorious passion-bearers clothed by Thee, O Lord; for by the endurance of wounds they conquered the lawless, and by divine power they received victory from heaven. By their supplications, deliver us also from the invisible enemy, O Savior, and save us!

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*

Protecting advocate and helper of all, unshakable hope and mediatress for the world: remember us, as thou art good, and grant remission of transgressions and salvation unto our souls, and guide us onto the paths of repentance. For unto thee do we flee in faith, and thee do we fervently entreat and lovingly implore: withhold not thy mercy from us![^24]

*Other Sessional Hymns, when the 3rd Kathisma is read, Tone 1:*

Thy judgment-seat is dreadful, and Thy judgment is righteous, but my deeds are vile; yet do Thou Thyself anticipate me, O merciful Savior, and deliver me from torment; rescue me, O Master, from the lot of the goats, and vouchsafe that I may stand at Thy right hand, O righteous Judge!

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*

Unwedded and pure Virgin Mother of God, sole protectress and shelter of the faithful: deliver from perils and tribulations and all grievous distresses those who place their hope in thee, O Maiden, and save our souls by thy divine prayers!

### CANONS FOR MONDAY MATINS

## Penitential Canon, whose Acrostic is:
### "Wash away the defilement of my transgressions, O Word." The work of Joseph.[^25]
[f. 14rB] *Ode 1, Tone 1. Heirmos:*

*Thy victorious right hand hath been glorified in strength in a manner befitting God; for, O Immortal One, as almighty it shattered the adversaries, forging a new path for Israel through the deep.*

Blot out the multitude of my sins according to the multitude of Thy mercies, I beseech Thee, O Christ, and grant me thoughts of repentance, that I may glorify the Mother of God, full of divine grace, who is beyond understanding.

Because of the tender mercy of Thy compassions, Thou didst appear on earth incarnate as man; therefore, O Word of God, receive me now who have sinned more than any man, as in repentance I fall down before Thy compassions.

*For the Martyrs:*

Imitating the death of Christ Who suffered willingly, O all-lauded and ever-memorable martyrs, ye endured manifold sufferings and death.

Bearing within you the fire of divine love, O sufferers, ye quenched it not; but ye burned up the fire of the flame of deception and extinguished all the fire of Gehenna.

*Theotokion:*

The ranks of the Bodiless Powers sing praise unto thee with us, O all-immaculate Virgin; for in awe thou didst give birth unto Him Who was truly incarnate without fiction, remaining a Virgin even as before childbirth, O Bride of God!

## Another Canon, to the Bodiless Powers. The work of Theophanes.[^26]
[f. 14vA] *Ode 1, Tone 1. Heirmos: The same.*

Standing brightly before the throne of the Master, O all-pure Angels: pray ye unto the Word Who is co-unoriginate with the Father, the Angel of Great Counsel, that He may breathe into me a word of assistance.

Ye mirrors of the God-originating light and radiance of the thrice-radiant dawn, singing in all-bright glory: pray ye for aid unto Him Who first conceived the angelic ranks and established the divine intelligible world.

*Theotokion:*

Having adorned the orders of the supreme Powers as God, He Who is higher than the Cherubim dwelt in thy virginal womb, O Mother of God, and unchangeably became flesh.

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*

*Thou Who alone knowest the weakness of human nature, and didst compassionately take form therein: gird me with power from on high, that I may cry unto Thee: Holy is the living temple of Thine ineffable glory, O Lover of mankind!*

Bow down, lament, O my soul, and cry aloud: I have sinned against the only One Who knows thy hidden secrets! And bring forth fruits of repentance, that the compassionate Lord may cleanse thee, His servant, and deliver thee from eternal [torment].

O good and compassionate Lord, save me: like the Publican I cry unto Thee with fear, dragged down deep by a multitude of sins, burdened with the weight of transgressions, and filled with boundless shame.

*For the Martyrs:*

Enlightened with the wisdom and understanding of the truth, the martyrs turned Hellenic wisdom into foolishness, manfully [f. 14vB] destroyed wickedness, and having suffered valiantly, worthily received the crowns of victory, rejoicing.

*For the Martyrs:*

Confessing the Trinity as a Monad in essence and three in Persons, O sufferers, ye destroyed the delusion of polytheism through divine faith; and ye were revealed as beacons, illuminating the hearts of all with the rays of grace.

*Theotokion:*

O pure Bride of God: thou didst give birth unto the Savior Who rests among the saints, the Son and Word co-unoriginate with the Father, Who through the Holy Spirit cleanses those who piously honor Him.

*Another Canon [to the Bodiless Powers]. Heirmos: The same.*

The Seraphim, drawing closely nigh unto the divine and deifying Light and abundantly filled with His primary outpourings, are illuminated in a primal manner; and they become secondary lights, being deified by grace.

Zealously desiring to praise the brightness of the Angels, let us fittingly entreat with purity of mind and pure lips the aid granted by God through them, that we may be renewed by their radiance.

*Theotokion:*

Vouchsafed to behold the supersubstantial light as far as is possible, Gabriel brought the joyous greeting unto thee, O all-praised Maiden, proclaiming thereby the conception of the Word and foretelling His ineffable birth.

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*

*Habakkuk, having perceived with prophetic eyes thee as the mountain overshadowed by divine grace, foreproclaimed that the Holy One of Israel would come forth from thee...*

[f. 15rA] *...for our salvation and renewal.*

Unto whom shall I liken thee, O my wretched soul, that committest evil and fearest not the Good One? Turn back, cry aloud unto Him Who willingly became poor for thy sake: O Knower of hearts, have compassion and save me!

Thou didst ordain repentance, O Christ, for those who turn unto Thee; grant it unto me, O Jesus, before the end of my life, giving me compunction and sighing, that like the harlot of old I may kiss Thy feet, O Master!

*For the Martyrs:*

Filled with spiritual waters, O martyrs, by divine nod ye were revealed as rivers of living water; and ye dried up the turbid streams of delusion, O glorious ones, and watered the hearts of the faithful.

Having valiantly contended, O divine martyrs, ye endured fire and sword and great and grievous torment; by their supplications, O Word of God, deliver from great torments those who praise them with all their soul.

*Theotokion:*

The Son Who was begotten of the Father before time, accepted birth in time, becoming incarnate of thee, O incorrupt Virgin; for the compassionate One, Who is above all days and years, desired to take away the ancient warfare of earthly men.

*Another Canon [to the Bodiless Powers]. Heirmos: The same.*

The Angels, Cherubim, and Seraphim, filled with primary beauty, shine brightly with divine rays, receiving the deifying hierarchy, and they sing: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

With ceaseless voices the sacred Seraphim sing of the thrice-radiant Unity of the Godhead, revealing the mystery of theology before the throne and teaching the Orthodox faith.

[f. 15rB] Receiving unerringly the outpouring of wisdom and multitude of knowledge from the single and simple Supreme Wisdom, the Cherubim impart it godlike unto the other ranks, sending down enlightenment unto them.

*Theotokion:*

He Who is understood to be above every nature, beyond comprehension in His divine creative power, accomplished a mystery on earth: illuminated with virginal splendors, He dwelt in thy womb, O all-pure one!

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*

*O Thou Who didst enlighten the ends of the world with the radiance of Thy coming, O Christ, and didst make them bright by Thy Cross: enlighten with the light of Thy divine knowledge the hearts of those who praise Thee in Orthodox faith.*

I have fallen into corrupt passions, and I fear the end of Thy righteous judgment-seat, O righteous Lord; therefore I pray Thee: have compassion on me, that I may perform good works that justify me.

The hidden and secret things of my heart Thou knowest, O my God, Creator, and Lord; condemn me not on that Day of Judgment when Thou shalt judge all things.

*For the Martyrs:*

Partaking of burning, the holy ones were refreshed by their divine love, being God-bearers; strengthened amid torments, the martyrs quenched the fire of temptation by endurance and withered the crafty enemy by their sufferings.

[f. 15vA] *Theotokion:*

God-inspired mouths can never declare the ineffable mystery of thy childbearing, O Maiden; for thou didst give birth unto Him Who is without change, and on thine arms dost bear Him Who holds all things in His hand.

*Another Canon [to the Bodiless Powers]. Heirmos: The same.*

Kindled with the fire of divine love, the Dominions, Authorities, and Powers, the secondary orders, sing praise with ceaseless mouths unto the God-originating one essence and power.

The spiritual ranks together with the Archangels, Angels, and Principalities in the spirit, as co-unoriginate hosts, honor the one thrice-hypostatic, illuminating Essence.

*Theotokion:*

Adorned beyond all angelic beauty, having conceived the Creator of Angels and Lord, O all-pure one higher than the Cherubim: thou becamest the animate receptacle of the incarnate God, O all-immaculate one.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*

*The lowest abyss hath compassed us about, and there is none to deliver; we were accounted as sheep for the slaughter: save Thy people, O our Christ!*

Heal the passions of my soul, O Word of God; wash me from all defilements, that I may sing praise unto Thee, O compassionate One.

Upon paths of ruin have I strayed through sinful pleasures, O Christ; but turn me back and guide me onto the path of salvation.

[f. 15vB] *For the Martyrs:*

Truly precious stones, pelted with stones, ye did not deny the living Stone, nor did ye sacrifice unto stones cut by hands, O glorious martyrs of the Lord who are crowned!

Having quickened your souls with the plow of faith, O martyrs, by the divine Spirit ye brought forth a hundredfold ear of corn through suffering, and were vouchsafed divine delight.

*Theotokion:*

Having given birth unto the Fire that created the fiery servants, thou wast revealed, O all-immaculate one, truly surpassing all creation, O all-pure Virgin, blessed and full of divine joy!

*Another Canon [to the Bodiless Powers]. Heirmos: The same.*

The ranks of the Bodiless Powers, O Lord, standing before the throne of Thy glory, O Lover of mankind, honor Thee with unceasing voices; for Thou art their strength and song.

Beholding the unfathomable beauty of the divine countenance and supersubstantial divine splendor, the Angels are illuminated by Thy divine rays; for Thou art their light and joy.

*Theotokion:*

He Who existed before, the Bodiless Word, became incarnate of thee, O all-pure one, Who by His will creates all things, and Who brought the bodiless hosts out of non-existence, as almighty.

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*

*Thee, O Mother of God, we faithful perceive as the spiritual furnace: for as the highly exalted One saved the three children, so hath God wholly renewed me, man, in thy womb: the praised and all-glorious God of our fathers.*

As of old Daniel tamed the lions by excelling in virtue, emulate him, O my soul, and by ever gazing unto God render powerless the one who [f. 16rA] ever roars like a lion, seeking to devour thee.

Through an excess of prodigality, O Lord, I have grievously defiled my soul; but possessing exceeding goodness, O Christ, receive me as the prodigal and have compassion on me as I sing: Blessed and all-glorious is the God of our fathers!

*For the Martyrs:*

Firmly strengthened by the law of Christ, the invincible martyrs cast down the wily snares of the lawless; and having finished their course lawfully, they sang: Blessed and all-glorious is the God of our fathers!

Radiant martyrs of the Lord, manifestly kindled by the light of the Trinity, ye dispelled the darkness of torture and the gloom of delusion, singing: Blessed and all-glorious is the God of our fathers!

*Theotokion:*

The laws of nature are renewed in thee: for beyond the laws of the flesh thou didst give birth unto Christ the Lawgiver, O all-immaculate one, Who ordains deliverance for all that sing: Blessed and all-glorious is the God of our fathers![^27]

*Another Canon [to the Bodiless Powers]. Heirmos: The same.*

Being unoriginate Light, O Master, shining forth from the Father Who is Light: Thou didst establish the angelic hosts as lights, mirrors receiving the flash of the unsetting brightness: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

As Lord of all, Thou manifestly savest the human race through the guardianship of the Angels; for Thou didst appoint them over all who believe and sing praise unto Thee in Orthodox faith: the praised and all-glorious God of our fathers!

Tongue and mind cannot declare Thy wonders, O Master, and the beauty of Thy works; for Thou didst illuminate [f. 16rB] every order of the heavenly Powers: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Theotokion:*

O incorrupt one, thou didst incarnate the Son Who was timelessly begotten of the Father and is God, having become man for our sake, Whom the ranks of the Bodiless Powers now serve as the praised and all-glorious God of our fathers.

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*

*In the furnace the children of Israel, as in a crucible, shining with the beauty of piety purer than gold, said: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing praise and exalt Him supremely unto all ages!*

My compassionate Redeemer, O Christ: deliver me now from the sinful gloom that holds me and from all passions, as I cry: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing praise and exalt Him supremely unto all ages!

When Thou shalt come, O Christ, in glory to judge the world: preserve those who stand marked with Thy name, crying aloud and saying: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing praise and exalt Him supremely unto all ages!

*For the Martyrs:*

Leaving earthly things, O holy martyrs of Christ, having contended valiantly on earth, ye received heavenly life, singing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing praise and exalt Him supremely unto all ages!

Wounded in mortal bodies and giving yourselves over to suffering, O glorious martyrs, ye met Christ as victors, crying: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing praise and exalt Him supremely unto all ages!

*Theotokion:*

The voices of holy mouths foreproclaimed from afar that thou, O all-pure one, wouldst become the honorable Mother of Christ Who created all things, unto Whom [f. 16vA] we sing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing praise and exalt Him supremely unto all ages!

*Another Canon [to the Bodiless Powers]. Heirmos: The same.*

Illuminated by the splendors of the angelic hosts and the rays of thrice-radiant beauty, let us faithful emulate them, singing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing praise and exalt Him supremely unto all ages!

As the divine Source of every good, He brought forth secondary lights of divine light, who receive the primal light and cry: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing praise and exalt Him supremely unto all ages!

The primal creative Mind, having established the transcendent angelic minds before all ages, draws them nigh unto Himself as they cry: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing praise and exalt Him supremely unto all ages!

*Theotokion:*

Him Who was begotten of the Father before the ages beyond all word, thou didst ineffably bear for us incarnate, O all-immaculate Virgin, unto Whom we cry: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing praise and exalt Him supremely unto all ages!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*

*The burning bush showed forth an unburnt image of thy pure childbearing; and now we pray thee to quench the furnace of temptations that rages against us, that we may unceasingly magnify thee, O Mother of God.*

Like the Canaanite woman I cry unto Thee: Have mercy on me, O Word! For my soul is sorely vexed by harmful assaults, foolishly committing unseemly deeds and feeling no divine fear of Thee, O longsuffering Lord!

Establish the steps of my soul upon the rock of Thy commandments, O Lord, and [f. 16vB] trip up the serpent who craftily seeks to overthrow me; and deliver me from his malice, as Thou art good and abundant in mercy.

*For the Martyrs:*

The martyrs passed through the unstable water of temptations and the surging waves of grievous wounds unto the joyful haven of the Kingdom on high, enjoying divine tranquility.

Having become luminous, O martyrs, ye were counted worthy of the unwaning Light; and ye dwell in the Kingdom of the firstborn, rejoicing with the choirs of Angels, with whom implore ye the Life-giving Son!

*Theotokion:*

Bearing Him Who upholds all things, and nursing Him Who gives food unto all: great and beyond understanding is thy mystery, O ark of honorable radiance, Virgin Mother of God; therefore in faith we bless thee!

*Another Canon [to the Bodiless Powers]. Heirmos: The same.*

Thou didst establish the bodiless minds as partakers of Thine ineffable glory, O Savior; and now for their sake preserve Thy people who flee unto Thee in faith and love, that we may unceasingly magnify Thee, the Master!

Thou sendest an Angel of all humility, O Almighty One, guarding Thy holy flock; for Thou art the cause of humility and love, preserving faith in divine wisdom and destroying every harmful thing by Thy power.

Praising Thy celestial delight and sweet radiance, O Master: make us inheritors of Thy Kingdom, and grant well-ordered stability, that we may unceasingly magnify Thee, the Savior!

*Theotokion:*

The intelligible angelic thrones unceasingly [f. 17rA] glorify thy childbearing; for together they stand gazing, filled with His joy, and unceasingly magnifying thee, O Mother of God!

*At the Aposticha, Penitential Stichera, Tone 1:*

Eternity awaits thee, O my soul, and the Judge is about to expose thy hidden and vile deeds; neglect not therefore to sigh, but anticipate Him, crying alone: O God, cleanse me and save me!

Condemn me not, O my Savior, who am held fast by sinful slothfulness; but awaken in me thoughts of repentance, and show me to be an earnest laborer in Thy vineyard, granting me the reward of the eleventh hour and great mercy!

*For the Martyrs:*

Come, all ye people, let us honor the passion-bearers of Christ with spiritual hymns and songs, as the enlighteners of the world and preachers of the faith, ever-flowing fountains that pour forth healings unto the faithful. By their prayers, O Christ our God, grant peace unto Thy world, and unto our souls great mercy!

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*

Receiving the prayers of sinners and despising not the sighs of the afflicted: implore Him Who was born of thy pure side, that we may be saved, O all-holy Virgin!

## ON MONDAY EVENING, AT "LORD, I HAVE CRIED"

*Penitential Stichera, Tone 1.*

*Podoben: "O all-lauded martyrs" (Прехвальніи мч̃нци):*

I have squandered all my life shamefully with harlots, O Lord; wretched that I am, like the prodigal I cry in repentance: Heavenly Father, I have sinned...

# ON MONDAY AT THE BEATITUDES
[f. 17rB] *Tone 1:*

Because of food the enemy led Adam out of Paradise; but through the Cross Christ led the thief into it, crying: Remember me when Thou comest into Thy Kingdom!

Grant me fountains of compunction by Thy mercy, O Christ God; cleanse all the defilements of my boundless evils, and make me a partaker of Thy Kingdom, O Benefactor!

We bring the ranks of Thine Angels unto Thee in supplication, O Christ; save us and have compassion on us for their sake, as Thou art all-good, overlooking all our transgressions committed knowingly and in ignorance.

*For the Martyrs:*

By the stream of your blood, O holy ones, ye drowned the spiritual Pharaoh; and now ye cease not to pour forth marvelous streams, driving away the abyss of diseases: therefore we call you blessed!

*Glory: To the Trinity:*

With the Angels let us faithful cry aloud with one voice the thrice-holy song: Holy art Thou, O Father, with the Son and the Spirit! Save us who cry unto Thee, O consubstantial Trinity, Monad God!

*Both now... Theotokion:*

Having given birth unto the unsetting Light, enlighten my darkened soul that is assailed by demonic suggestions; and deliver me from the fire to come by thy divine prayers, O all-immaculate one![^28] [f. 17vA] cleanse me and save me, and cast me not away who have distanced myself from Thee and am now impoverished through barren deeds!

Though rich, Thou didst become poor, O Christ, and didst enrich men with immortality and brightness; therefore enrich me with virtues who am impoverished through a life of pleasures, and number me with poor Lazarus, delivering me from the torment of the rich man and the Gehenna that awaits me.

Grievously have I grown rich in wickedness, loving pleasure; in this life I received good things, O Lord, and was condemned unto Gehenna; having neglected my starving mind like Lazarus, cast down before the gates of divine deeds: have compassion on me, O Lord!

*Other Stichera to the Forerunner.*

*Podoben: "The same" (то́йже):* [^29]

Marvelous Prophet, Baptist of Christ and Forerunner: my heart is dried up by wickedness; cause it to pour forth ever-flowing rivers of tears through thy prayers, I beseech thee, that being saved through thee in my many afflictions, I may magnify Him Who hath magnified thee!

Blessed Prophet, in thee do I place all my hope and the life of my human soul, who didst baptize Jesus Christ, the Abyss Who bears away the sins of the world; implore Him, O merciful John, to cleanse my heart and save me!

Wise preacher of grace, who didst foreannounce repentance unto all nations: grant that my all-wretched and desolate soul may ever bring forth fruits of repentance, O divine Forerunner, unto the salvation of our souls!

[f. 17vB] *Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*

With the great Forerunner who preached unto all the Lamb Who bears away the sins of the whole world, pray thou, O Virgin, that I, a prodigal, may escape the portion of the goats, and that He may number me, unworthy though I am, among the sheep at His right hand.

*Prokeimenon:*

*The Lord will hear me when I cry unto Him [Psalm 4:4 LXX].*

*Verse: When I called upon Thee, Thou didst hear me [Psalm 4:2 LXX].*

*At the Aposticha, Penitential Stichera, Tone 1:*

As a great abyss are my transgressions, O Savior, and grievously am I sunken in mine iniquities; stretch forth Thy hand unto me, as unto Peter, O Lord, and save me, and have mercy on me!

Because I am impoverished through evil thoughts and deeds, O Savior, grant me thoughts of repentance, O God, that I may cry unto Thee: Save me, O good Benefactor, and have mercy on me!

*For the Martyrs:*

Your confession at the tribunal, O holy ones, struck fear into the tyrant’s power and set men free from delusion; therefore even when beheaded ye cried: Let the sacrifice of our souls be acceptable before Thee, O Lord; for having loved Thee, we took no heed of temporal life, O Lover of mankind!

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*

O all-praised Virgin, with prophetic eyes Moses beheld the mystery that was in thee, the bush burning yet unconsumed; for the fire of the Godhead did not burn thy pure womb: therefore we pray thee, as the Mother of our God, to entreat peace for the world and great mercy.

## ON TUESDAY AT MATINS

[f. 18rA] *After the 1st Kathisma, Penitential Sessional Hymns, Tone 1:*

In iniquities was I conceived, prodigal that I am; I dare not look up unto the height of heaven, but trusting in Thy love for mankind, I cry: O God, cleanse me and save me!

If the righteous man scarcely be saved, where shall I, a sinner, appear, who have not borne the burden and heat of the day? But with the laborers of the eleventh hour, number me, O God, and save me!

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*

Beyond understanding and hearing, thou didst give birth on earth without a father unto Him Who is without a mother in heaven: implore Him, O Mother of God, that our souls may be saved!

*After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns, Tone 1:*

Haste Thou to open Thy Fatherly embrace unto me: prodigally have I squandered my life, looking upon the inexhaustible wealth of Thy bounties, O Savior; despise not now my impoverished heart. For unto Thee, O Lord, in compunction do I cry: Father, I have sinned against heaven and before Thee!

Beholding the wealth of Job's virtues, the enemy of the righteous plotted against him and shattered the bodily pillar; yet he stole not the spiritual treasure, for he found the blameless soul to be contrite. But having stripped me bare, he hath taken me captive: anticipate him therefore before the end, and deliver me from his corruption, O Savior, and save me!

*For the Martyrs:*

As good soldiers believing with one mind, ye feared not the threats of the tyrants, O holy ones; ye came eagerly unto Christ, taking up the precious Cross; and having finished your course [f. 18rB] ye received victory from heaven: glory to Him Who strengthened you, glory to Him Who crowned you, glory to Him Who through you works healings for all!

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*

Thou didst anticipate the despair of the Ninevites, averting the proclaimed destruction, and Thy mercy overcame Thy wrath, O Lord; have compassion now upon Thy people and Thy holy inheritance, and with Thy mighty hand cast down our enemies: through the prayers of the Mother of God, grant us Thy mercy!

*After the 3rd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns, Tone 1.*

*Podoben: "While the soldiers were guarding Thy tomb" (Гробъ твои Сп̃се):*

I have fallen among thieves through thoughts, and have been despoiled in mind; my soul hath been wounded by sins, and I lie unhealed, O most merciful Jesus; but pour forth Thy mercy through the prayers of the All-Pure One, and heal the grievous wounds of my soul!

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*

Unwedded and pure Virgin Mother of God, sole protectress and shelter of the faithful: deliver from perils and tribulations and all grievous distresses those who place their hope in thee, O Maiden, and save our souls by thy divine prayers!

### CANONS FOR TUESDAY MATINS

## Penitential Canon. The work of Joseph.[^30]
*Ode 1, Tone 1. Heirmos:*

*Let us all sing a song of victory unto God Who wrought marvelous wonders with a lofty arm, and saved Israel; for He is glorified!*

Enslaved by the passions of sin, I fall down before Thee, O Lord, that Thou mayest show me free from them, as I earnestly praise [f. 18vA] Thy goodness.

With a wretched tongue I cry out in sin, and am dead; and the enemy rejoices seeing me lying low: O Thou Who raisest the dead, quicken and save me!

*For the Martyrs:*

The ranks of the sufferers were glorified, having glorified Christ in their honorable members; they subjected the flesh, and by their suffering destroyed corruption.

As pillars and ramparts of piety, the glorious martyrs remained unshaken by the assaults of the enemy: by their prayers, O God, have compassion on us all!

*Theotokion:*

Bearing the Creator as a fiery throne, O Virgin, as a living bridal chamber and beautiful palace thou didst contain the King, Who became what we are without change or confusion.

## Another Canon, to the Holy and Great Prophet John, the Forerunner.
*Tone 1. Heirmos: The same.*

Thou wast the great voice of the Word; receive therefore our voices which we lift up unto thee, O Forerunner, delivering us from evils through thine intercession.

Shining forth like the dawn, like the sun, thou dost enlighten the ends of the earth and dispel the evil spirits; therefore drive away the gloom of our souls.

Thou didst proclaim our Life coming unto mortals, O Forerunner; therefore put to death the passions that mortify me, and show me, O blessed one, to be a partaker of divine radiance.

*Theotokion:*

Having given birth in time unto the timeless Son incarnate, O all-pure [f. 18vB] Lady: heal the ancient, wretched passions of my soul!

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*

*The stone which the builders rejected, the same is become the head of the corner; this is the rock whereupon Christ hath established His Church, which He redeemed from among the nations.*

Behold the weakness wherewith I am clothed, behold the grievous disfigurement of my soul, and give ear unto my voice, O Christ, abundant in mercy; and transform its unseemliness into fair beauty, O Savior!

Save me, the prodigal, O Jesus, who have transgressed Thy saving laws, committing all iniquity foolishly and seduced by thoughts that alienate me from Thee, O Good One!

*For the Martyrs:*

The ranks of the Bodiless Powers truly marveled at your courage, O holy ones; for suffering gloriously upon the tribunal and falling in body, ye cast down all bodiless enemies by divine power.

Still crimsoned with wounds, still bedewed with drops of blood, O passion-bearers, ye stand rejoicing before the Lord, the immortal King, crowned as victors!

*Theotokion:*

Thou didst give birth unto Him Whom the Father begat before all ages, thou didst nurse the Nourisher, knowing not man: O most glorious wonder, O new mystery, full of divine joy; therefore the great soul of the faithful doth glorify thee!

*Another Canon [to the Forerunner]. Heirmos: The same.*

From a barren womb that bore not, O Forerunner, thou didst sacredly spring forth and [f. 19rA] wast revealed fruitful in divine deeds; therefore make my heart, wholly barren of good, fruitful in virtues, that in faith I may glorify thee!

With the heavenly Bread strengthen my heart, O blessed one, weakened as it is by evil thoughts, and grant me zealously to do the will of the all-bountiful God, that in faith I, a sinner, may ever glorify thee, O Prophet.

Thou didst proclaim the Lamb Who bears away the sin of the world, O blessed Prophet; lighten, I pray thee, the heavy burden of my sins, granting me compunction that cleanses the defilements of the passions.

*Theotokion:*

The Word Who came forth taking flesh entirely, clothed Himself with the image of Adam, O incorrupt Mother of God; implore Him therefore to deliver us from passions, and from all tribulations, and from eternal fire.

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*

*Foreseeing in spirit the incarnation of the Word, the Prophet Habakkuk proclaimed, crying: When the years draw nigh, Thou shalt be known; when the time is come, Thou shalt be shown forth. Glory to Thy power, O Lord!*

The wealth which Thou gavest me, O Christ, I wickedly squandered, committing unseemly deeds; and I am become naked, clothed in deeds of dishonor; therefore I cry unto Thee: Have compassion on me, and clothe me with Thy first divine grace!

I was brought down by folly and fell grievously, and I lie upon the earth unhealed; raise me up, O Resurrection of the fallen, and establish my heart, O Christ, upon the rock of saving repentance!

[f. 19rB] *For the Martyrs:*

Imitating Christ lifted up upon the Cross, the all-glorious passion-bearers received wounds; and with streams of blood they extinguished the delusion of polytheism, pouring forth streams of healings.

Having traversed the surge and bitter tossing of torments dryshod, O divine sufferers, steered by saving hope, ye hastened unto the haven on high, filled with all joy.

*Theotokion:*

The angelic hosts marveled, beholding how He Who is invisible in appearance was seen for our sake through thee, O Virgin Mother of God; implore Him to grant salvation unto all who glorify thee in faith.

*Another Canon [to the Forerunner]. Heirmos: The same.*

Having obtained the robe of salvation for thyself in bodily nakedness, O Baptist of the Lord: clothe me, I pray thee, who am stripped bare of noble struggle, with the garment of righteousness and gladness.

Rain down upon me a drop of salvation, O Forerunner, who am wasting away through the offspring of lusts, who didst immerse in the streams of the Jordan the Torrent of delight, Jesus the Giver of life, that worthily I may glorify thee.

Neither an angel nor an intercessor saved us, but the Lord Himself Who came upon earth, for Whom thou didst make straight the paths, O blessed one; implore Him to smooth my path that leads unto salvation.[^31]

*Theotokion:*

A sacred temple of God wast thou revealed, having contained God beyond understanding, O Virgin [f. 19vA] implore Him to cleanse us from the defilements of sin, that we may be shown forth as temples and the dwelling of the divine Spirit.

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*

*Grant us Thy peace, O Son of God; for other than Thee we know no God: we call upon Thy name, for Thou art the God of the living and of the dead.*

I am filled with many and grievous falls into sin; O greatly compassionate and longsuffering Lord, have mercy on me who am condemned, and cast me not away from Thy presence!

Thou didst justify the Publican when he sighed, O Christ; imitating him, I also beat my breast and cry unto Thee: Cleanse me, O only compassionate and merciful One!

*For the Martyrs:*

Thy holy ones, O Lord, were revealed as unerring beacons, driving away the deep night of delusion and enlightening the whole universe with marvelous splendors.

As precious stones having loved Thee, the living Stone, O Master: the martyrs, rolled about by torments, cast down the great edifice of delusion.

*Theotokion:*

In two wills thou didst give birth unto the One of the honorable Trinity, O all-immaculate one, Who hath a single hypostasis: diligently implore Him that we all may be saved.

*Another Canon [to the Forerunner]. Heirmos: The same.*

Thou didst dwell in the wilderness, O Forerunner of Christ, even as Elijah of old; therefore through diligence restore my heart that is made desolate by transgressions, O all-blessed one!

Having become an unshakable pillar and [f. 19vB] bulwark for the faithful, O great Forerunner of Christ: make steadfast my mind that is shaken by the deceits of the wily one.

The Light from Light appearing upon earth was proclaimed unto the dead by thy voice, O blessed one; and we who were grievously darkened in gloom were enlightened.

*Theotokion:*

David proclaims thee as the Fleece, O Virgin, in all-pure purity; therefore I pray thee: make me an inheritor of the heavenly Kingdom, that I may call thee blessed!

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*

*Imitating the Prophet Jonah, I cry: Deliver my life from corruption, O God, and save me, O Savior of the world, who cry: Glory to Thee!*

The bones of my wretched soul are afflicted and weighed down by the burden of many pleasures; but help me, O Christ, the only help of all!

Falling into the abyss of evils and tempest of passions, I cry unto Thee, O almighty Christ: raise me up by Thy strong hand and save me!

*For the Martyrs:*

The chosen regiment of myriads of holy passion-bearers trampled upon the myriads of spiritual enemies, and was joined unto the myriads of heavenly minds.

Having dried up the deep of godlessness, O sufferers, ye inherited the torrent of delight; therefore dry up the overflow of my sin!

*Theotokion:*

Revealed as the tabernacle of sanctification, O Mary: cleanse my wretched soul defiled with pleasures, and make me a partaker of divine glory!

[f. 20rA] *Another Canon [to the Forerunner]. Heirmos: The same.*

Thou who didst preach repentance upon earth, O Baptist: show me the paths of repentance that lead me unto the light, and deliver me from the snares of deception.

Having immersed the Abyss in the river streams: dry up the abyss of my passions, granting me a fountain of tears, O Forerunner, preacher of Christ!

From diseases of soul and passions of flesh, from temptations of life and great trials and afflictions, save me, O Forerunner of the Lord!

*Theotokion:*

Mother of God and fair among women, I diligently pray thee: despise me not, O pure one, but have compassion and preserve me unharmed from great hurt!

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*

*The fire touched not nor troubled Thy children in the furnace, O Savior; then the three as with one mouth sang and blessed, saying: Blessed is the God of our fathers!*

Joseph learned endurance, and remained unmoved by all the wiles of the evil one, like a strong pillar: emulate him ever, O my soul, and despond not in evil circumstances!

Vanquished by bodily pleasures, I am become irrational though endowed with reason, O Word of God, Who by Thy word savest the well-pleasing: save me, a wretch, that blessing I may praise Thy goodness!

*For the Martyrs:*

Redeemed by the blood of Christ Who suffered in the flesh for our sake, O martyrs, for Whose sake ye chose eagerly to pour out your blood: [f. 20rB] by the building of your sacred sufferings ye were revealed as an all-bright palace, wherein rests Christ, the only King and Lord, Who translated you unto the heavenly mansions!

*Theotokion:*

Out of all generations, O all-praised Virgin, Christ chose thee alone as His dwelling, as fair and pure; and shining forth from thee like the sun, He enlightened all the earth.

*Another Canon [to the Forerunner]. Heirmos: The same.*

Having become an excellent mediator between the Old and the New, O glorious Baptist: through thine intercession implore Jesus, the Renewer of all, graciously to renew me who am grown old in sins!

As one who laid down the foundation of repentance on earth, thou wast revealed, O Forerunner of Christ and Baptist; strengthen all to attain it through thy prayers, that we may be delivered from the boundless evils that we ever commit.

Thou didst traverse the path of the wilderness, passing through all self-control, O wise one; and by the breadth of divine vision thou wast wholly illuminated with brightness: grant that we also may enjoy this, imploring Christ!

*Theotokion:*

Offer supplication unto God, O all-holy one, that He may look down upon our transgressions and boundless sins, and deliver us from the tormenting eternal fire!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*

*Him of Whom the Angels and all the hosts stand in awe as Creator and Lord: sing praise, ye priests; glorify, ye children; bless, ye people, and exalt Him supremely unto all ages!*

The crafty serpent stripped me bare of all virtues by his evil counsel; having despoiled me [f. 20vA] O my Savior Who didst expose the serpent's malice, adorn me with virtues!

When Thou comest to judge the human race, O righteous Judge: in that dread hour send me not, condemned as I am, into the fire of Gehenna, but have compassion and save me!

*For the Martyrs:*

O all-lauded martyrs of the Lord: neither tribulation, nor distress, nor sword, nor fire could separate you from the love of Christ, Who loved us out of His tender mercy!

Grappling with the deceit of the bodiless enemy, ye cast him down, O valiant sufferers; and now ye join in chorus with the Bodiless Powers, healing the passions of souls and bodies!

*Theotokion:*

Having found thee like a lily in the valleys of this life, O Mother of God, the Creator of all dwelt in thee, who art fragrant with the scents of piety and purity!

*Another Canon [to the Forerunner]. Heirmos:*

*Sing praise unto Christ God, Who preserved the children praising Him in the furnace, and turned the flaming furnace into dew; and exalt Him supremely unto all ages!*

I alone have sinned more than all men born on earth, I alone have become a transgressor of Thy laws, O Lord; therefore for the Forerunner's sake have compassion on me and save me!

Angelic in character wast thou shown forth, O Baptist John, preaching the Angel of Great Counsel unto the ends of the earth; therefore with hymns we glorify thee unto all ages!

As thou wast beheaded unjustly, O blessed one, who didst immerse the Head of Christ in the waters: [f. 20vB] strengthen us all by thy prayers to trample upon the head of the truly destructive deceiver!

*Theotokion:*

Deliver me from unseemly sin, and the flaming torment, and the tormenting gloom, O all-pure star and hall of God, O Virgin, sole advocate of the human race!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*

*The light-bearing cloud, whereinto the Master of all descended like rain from heaven upon the fleece, and became incarnate for our sake, the unoriginate One becoming man: let us all magnify as the pure Mother of our God!*

Behold the season of repentance and pure work, behold the day: perform bright deeds, drive away all the gloom of the passions and the sleep of evil despondency, O my soul, that thou mayest be a partaker of the divine Light!

Like the Publican I sigh; like the Harlot I shed tears; like the Thief I cry unto Thee: Remember me, O Compassionate One! And like the Prodigal Son I cry: I have sinned! And I fall down before Thee like the Canaanite woman: O Merciful One, despise me not, O Christ!

*For the Martyrs:*

Ye were revealed as true physicians for bodily passions and afflictions of soul, having patiently surrendered your bodies unto wounds and violent death, O all-lauded sufferers of the Lord: therefore ye are ever blessed!

The endurance of the wise passion-bearers of Christ shone more brightly than the radiance of the sun; therefore by grace it destroyed the ruler of darkness and enlightened the hearts of the faithful, shining forth with illuminating rays.

[f. 21rA] *Theotokion:*

...Of the Word Who shone forth from thy holy womb, O Virgin Mother of God, and enlightened the ends of the earth: illuminate my soul darkened by the blackness of pleasures, that in faith I may sing praise unto thee!

*Another Canon [to the Forerunner]. Heirmos: The same.*

Behold the lamp shining unto souls that are in darkness, behold the fair-working swallow that heralds the spring unto all, the great Forerunner of Christ, the mediator between the Old and the New: through whose prayers may we who sing praise be preserved!

As the friend of the Bridegroom I now offer thee as intercessor, having a multitude of sins, and I cry unto thee, O Baptist: grant me remission of debts, O all-blessed one, and rekindle the lamp of my soul, which through slothfulness is utterly extinguished!

Together with the Bodiless Angels, the honorable Apostles, the sacred passion-bearers, and the Prophets, O Forerunner: ever implore the all-good God that we may obtain eternal blessings, having thee enriched as our advocate of good things before Him!

Fair swallow, honorable nightingale, most good dove, wilderness-loving turtledove, Baptist of the Lord, shoot of the wilderness: show my soul, desolate through fruitlessness, to be fruitful in good things!

*Theotokion:*

Thou bearest Him Who upholds all things, as a Cherubic throne, and thou dost nurse Him Who nourishes us; implore Him unceasingly, O pure one full of divine joy, that Thy flock may ever be delivered from delusion and falling, captivity and every distress!

*At the Aposticha, Penitential Stichera, Tone 1:*

[f. 21rB] Eternity awaits thee, O my soul, and the Judge is about to expose thy hidden and vile deeds; neglect not therefore in these things, but anticipate Him, crying alone: O God, cleanse me and save me!

Condemn me not, O my Savior, who am held fast by sinful slothfulness; but awaken in me thoughts of repentance, and show me to be an earnest laborer in Thy vineyard, granting me the reward of the eleventh hour and great mercy!

*For the Martyrs:*

Holy soldiers of the Great King, ye resisted the commands of the tyrants, manfully disregarding torments; and having trampled upon all delusion, being worthily crowned, ye ask peace from the Savior and for our souls great mercy.

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*

I have surpassed the Harlot, the Prodigal, and the Thief in unrepentance, and the Publican in transgressions, and other secret sinners: woe is me, what shall become of me? How shall I, a wretch, escape torment? O pure one, I fall down before thee: have compassion on me by thy mercy, even as Thy Son saved those of old!

# ON TUESDAY AT THE BEATITUDES
*Tone 1:*

Because of food the enemy led Adam out of Paradise; but through the Cross Christ led the thief into it, crying: Remember me, O Lord, when Thou comest into Thy Kingdom!

Turn me back, O God, who daily sin and transgress Thy commandments, and deliver me through compunction, that I may glorify Thine ineffable tender mercy, O Lover of mankind!

Thou wast revealed as a lamp of God [^32] [f. 21vA] O Prophet, forerunner of the unwaning Light, Who was proclaimed unto us ineffably from the cloud by the voice of God: unceasingly pray Him to have mercy and save our souls!

*For the Martyrs:*

Having endured intricately woven torments, O all-lauded martyrs: ye were accounted worthy of the sublime heavenly blessings, and now ye are ever blessed by all mankind!

*Glory...*

The one Godhead in three Persons...

## ON TUESDAY EVENING, AT "LORD, I HAVE CRIED"

*Stichera of the Cross, Tone 1.*

*Podoben: "O all-lauded martyrs" (Прехвальніи мчнци):*

Being nailed to the Cross, O Christ God, as man, Thou didst deify human nature, and didst slay the serpent, the beginner of malice; Thou didst deliver us from the curse of the tree, as Thou art compassionate; Thou art come unto the world to grant blessing unto all, and great mercy!

Thou art above every created nature, O Master, and by Thine unsearchable good pleasure Thou didst deign to endure death upon the Wood, O Compassionate One; therefore the human race is clothed in immortality, and hath received its first life!

O precious Cross, cleansing-place for all the faithful, dominion of kings, consolation of all who worship thee and glorify Christ, Who stretched forth His all-pure hands upon thee out of ineffable tender mercy, and gathered all the ends of the earth into one!

*Other Stichera to the Mother of God, Tone 1.*

*Podoben: "Joy of the heavenly ranks" (Небнымъ чиномъ):*

[f. 21vB] ...we all confess, existing undivided, the Son with the Father and the living Spirit: unoriginate, unconfused, ever abiding unto ages of ages!

*Both now...*

Ever-Virgin after giving birth, even as thou wast preserved pure before birthgiving, having given birth unto God in the flesh: pray Him, O all-pure one, we beseech thee, to deliver us from fleshly and spiritual passions![^33]

Standing by the Cross of her Son and God, and beholding His long-suffering, the pure Mother wept and cried: "Woe is me, my sweetest Child! What is this that Thou sufferest unjustly, O Word of God, that Thou mayest save mankind?"

Standing by the Cross, the unwedded Bride, receiving wounds from maternal pain, cried aloud: "Leave me not childless, O my Child, who bore Thee, O Word of God! Abandon me not alone, O Only-begotten, co-eternal with the Father!"

"When I gave birth to Thee, I had no sorrow; how then do I now endure grief, beholding Thee, O Word, crucified unjustly?" cried the Virgin, weeping bitterly: "Woe is me, I cannot bear to see Thee lifted up upon the Cross, O Lover of mankind!"

*Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion:*

When thou didst see thy Son and God upon the Wood, hanging sorrowful, having stretched forth His hands upon the Cross, [f. 22rA] and His ribs pierced with a spear, the pure Mother, lamenting, cried out: "Woe is me, how dost Thou suffer, O Lover of mankind, taking away the passions of men?"

### AT THE APOSTICHA

*Stichera of the Cross, Tone 1:*

The Cross was planted upon Golgotha, and immortality blossomed forth for us from the ever-flowing fountain of the Savior's side!

An indestructible wall is the precious Cross of the Savior unto us: for hoping in it, we all are saved!

*For the Martyrs:*

O the good merchandise of yours, O holy ones! For ye gave your blood, and inherited the heavens; and having been tried for a time, ye rejoice eternally! Truly good was your merchandise: for leaving behind corruptible things, ye received incorruptible things; and rejoicing in chorus with the Angels, ye unceasingly sing unto the consubstantial Trinity!

*Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion:*

When the undefiled Virgin beheld the Lamb lifted up upon the Cross, she wept and cried: "My sweet Child, what is this new and glorious sight? How dost Thou, Who holdest all things in the hollow of Thy hand, endure to be nailed in the flesh upon the Wood?"

## ON WEDNESDAY AT MATINS

*After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymns of the Cross, Tone 1:*

When Thou wast crucified, O Christ, tyranny perished, and the power of the enemy was trampled down; for neither an Angel nor a man, but Thou Thyself, O Lord, hast saved us: glory to Thee!

We venerate the Wood of Thy Cross, O Lover of mankind, for upon it [f. 22rB] Thou wast nailed, O Life of all; Thou didst open Paradise, O Savior, unto the Thief who came to Thee in faith, and didst account him worthy of delight who confessed Thee: "Remember me, O Lord!" Accept also us who cry as that thief did: "We all have sinned; despise us not in Thy tender mercy!"

*Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion:*

Beholding the Lamb upon the Cross, the Ewe-lamb, seeing Thee crucified between two thieves, O long-suffering Word, and pierced with a spear in the ribs, exclaimed and cried with maternal voice: "What is this strange and fearful mystery, O my Jesus, ineffably accomplished? How art Thou covered by a tomb, O uncontainable God? Abandon not me who gave Thee birth, O my sweetest Son!"

*After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 1:*

Save, O Lord, Thy people, and bless Thine inheritance, granting victories unto our rulers over adversaries, and preserving Thy people by Thy Cross!

The weapon of the Cross was revealed in battles of old unto the pious Emperor Constantine, an invincible victory over enemies for the sake of faith: the contrary powers tremble before it; this is the salvation of the faithful and the boast of Paul!

*For the Martyrs:*

By the wounds of the holy ones which they suffered for Thy sake, be Thou entreated, O Lord, and heal all our sicknesses and passions, O Lover of mankind, we pray!

*Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion:*

Having acquired thee as our protection, O all-pure one, by thy prayers we are delivered from misfortunes; for being ever preserved by the Cross of the Son of God, as is [f. 22vA] due, we all piously magnify thee!

*After the 3rd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns, Tone 1.*

*Podoben: "While the soldiers were guarding Thy tomb" (Гробъ твои Сп҃се):*

When the Sun saw Thee, O Word, hung upon the Wood of the Cross, out of tender mercy, of Thine own will in the flesh: unable to bear the audacity, the glory of the sun was darkened; therefore enlighten my darkened soul with Thine unapproachable light, and save me, I pray!

Thou didst stretch forth Thy palms upon the Cross, O Compassionate One, and didst gather the nations that were far off from Thee, to glorify Thy great loving-kindness; but look down upon Thine inheritance, and cast down those who war against us, by Thy precious Cross!

*Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion:*

Beholding the Lamb and Shepherd hung dead upon the Wood, the undefiled Ewe-lamb wept and cried, exclaiming with a mother's voice: "How shall I hymn Thy condescension beyond word, O my Son, and Thy voluntary passions, O God most good?"

## ON WEDNESDAY: CANON TO THE PRECIOUS AND LIFE-CREATING CROSS
*Composition of Saint Joseph.*[^34]

*Ode 1, Tone 1. Heirmos:*

*Having delivered Israel from bitter servitude, and having passed through the impassable as on dry land: seeing the enemy drowned, they sing a song of joy unto God, Who works wonders with a high arm, for He is glorified!*

Being lifted up upon the Cross, O Christ, Thou didst raise up fallen man with Thyself, and didst cast down all the power of the enemy, O Word; therefore we praise Thy passions, Who [f. 22vB] didst deliver me from passions!

Thou art the Lord of glory, Who crownest man with glory, and wast crowned with endurance, that Thou mightest make our bold nature fruitful in divine works, O Planter!

*For the Martyrs:*

The most sacred assembly of the holy ones, having lawfully contested, washed their body in the streams of all their holy blood, and utterly destroyed the defiled sacrifices offered unto demons, O fathers!

The clouds of tortures did not defile your patient burning, O martyrs; therefore ye shone forth more brightly than the rays of the sun, illuminating for me the dawn of salvation!

*Theotokion:*

The all-pure womb of her Son was consumed as with a sword, as she beheld Him pierced with a spear: which weapon forbids entry into Paradise, denying the faithful divine entrance!

### Another Canon to the Most Holy Theotokos
*Ode 1, Tone 1. Heirmos:*

*Thy victorious right hand...*

Grant me a stream of spiritual tears, O all-immaculate one, who didst bear the Wellspring of cleansing, washing away the defilement of sins and leading my life forth in humility!

Thou becamest higher than the Cherubim, O pure Virgin, having given flesh unto God; therefore I pray thee: raise me up from the mire of passions, and lead me unto the divine beauty of dispassion!

Appear unto me, O pure and much-hymned one, in the day of judgment, delivering me from the fearful standing [f. 23rA] and fierce torment, who flee beneath thy protection, O all-pure Sovereign Lady!

*Theotokion:*

Darkness of sins holds me fast, and I am fallen, O all-pure one; raise me up, giving me a shower of tears, whereby I may wash away my defiled deeds: for thee alone do we have as intercessor, O Mother of God!

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*

*Let not the mortal boast in his wisdom or riches, but in the faith of the Lord, orthodoxly crying out unto Christ God, and singing ever: Upon the rock of Thy commandments establish me, O Master!*

The lawless dug through Thy hands and feet, O my Jesus, Who by Thy palm ineffably fashionedst man out of dust, O Christ God, and by Thy suffering didst free all from corruption!

"Let the moon and the sun stand still," cried Joshua; which was the darkening of the luminaries when God suffered in the flesh, being crucified on the Cross, whereby the principalities of dark malice were put to shame!

*For the Martyrs:*

The glorious martyrs eagerly endured wounds, and being wounded, they mightily wounded the serpent Beliar; therefore by divine assent they ever heal the wounds of our souls!

Ye cast down the pagan shrines and temples of demons, O martyrs; and by sufferings and courage ye marvelously raised up yourselves as temples by grace, capacious of the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit!

*Theotokion:*

At the hour of the passion, beholding the One fair in beauty having neither form nor comeliness, the pure Virgin cried out, weeping bitterly and exclaiming: [f. 23rB] "Woe is me, how dost Thou suffer, O Son, wishing to deliver all from passions?"

*Another Canon [to the Theotokos]. Heirmos:*

*Thou alone knowest...*

Thou wast the temple of the King of all, O all-pure one; show me who have become a den of soul-corrupting robbers through their malice to be a pure dwelling of the Holy Spirit!

Grant me an abundant shower of tears, I pray, for the stream of my sinful deeds: do thou who didst bear the calm ocean of tender mercy, Christ our God, O all-hymned Virgin Mother of God!

*Theotokion:*

Be Thou our strength and an unshakable tower, O thou who art full of divine grace, and a shield and invincible weapon: turning away the regiments of mental enemies from us, O all-pure Mother of God, who honor thee with faith and love!

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*

*Habakkuk of old heard Thy marvelous report, O Christ, and with fear cried aloud: God shall come from Teman, and the Holy One from the mountain overshadowed and dense, to save His anointed ones: glory to Thy power, O Lord!*

Wounds and stripes Thou didst endure, O Christ, healing the wounds of my heart, tasting bitter gall, taking away the corrupting sweet taste of the tree; and being nailed unto the Wood, Thou didst abolish the ancient curse!

Lifting up nations that were cast far off from Thee, being raised upon the Cross, Thou drewest them all; and Thou didst reconcile them unto the Father, O Long-suffering One, bringing them into heaven as a mediator; and in the midst of the earth Thou didst endure a reproachful passion [f. 23vA] In the sea of your blood, O divinely-blessed ones, having drowned the fish of your warfare, the noetic Pharaoh was drowned in the deep; therefore with joy ye came unto the promised land, and became heavenly citizens!

*For the Martyrs:*

Strengthened by the passion of Christ, O blessed ones, the martyrs were able to receive various passions unto the affliction of the flesh; therefore they cease not to relieve passions of both souls and bodies for those who praise and ever bless them!

*Theotokion:*

Beholding Thy unjust slaying, she who bore Thee, O Christ, wept and cried unto Thee: "O righteous Judge, my Son, how art Thou condemned unjustly, wishing to justify those who were condemned through transgression of old and slipped into corruption?"

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*

*Seeing thee, the Mountain shadowed with grace...*

Having fiercely clothed me with deep delusions away from the commandments of God, despise me not, O good one; but have compassion, I pray, and show me to be higher than his deception, who flee unto thy mercy, O all-pure one!

O only Merciful Christ God, by the prayers of her who bore Thee, have mercy and compassion on those who trust in Thee, guide us unto the light of Thy commandments, and account us worthy of eternal life!

*Theotokion:*

I am fallen into death and lie in the grave of despondency, O all-pure one, bound with the irons of my transgressions; but raise me up by thy vigilant prayer, and direct me unto repentance, I pray!

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*

*Thy never-waning Light...*

[f. 23vB] ...shine forth, O Christ, in the hearts of those who faithfully sing unto Thee, granting us Thy peace which surpasses all understanding: that in the night of ignorance, running unto the day of Thy commandments, we may glorify Thee, O Lover of mankind!

The sun, O Savior, stripped itself of light, seeing Thee hanging naked on the Tree, Who didst suspend the earth upon the waters; and the rocks were split asunder with fear, perceiving Thee lifted up, and the foundations of the earth were shaken!

Raised upon the Tree and nailed with nails, Thou didst stain Thy fingers with blood, O Long-suffering One, and being pierced in the ribs with a spear, Thou didst heal the wound of Adam, which he suffered through listening to the rib and disobeying Thee Who fashionedst him!

*For the Martyrs:*

The multitude of martyrs was wounded, having the living Tree, Christ, in their midst: for Whose sake having endured a reproachful death with courageous thought, by divine power they slew the serpent who slew our first parents!

By the drops of the blood of Christ, O pillars of the Church, ye dried up the depth of godlessness; and by divine streams of sacred miracles ye check the flow of passions for both souls and bodies; therefore ye are worthily blessed!

The undefiled and immaculate one, seeing Christ willingly raised upon the Tree, cried out weeping: "O my Son and God, having escaped birth-pangs in birthgiving, I now suffer with sorrows, beholding Thee crucified unjustly by the lawless!"

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*

*Thou Who didst enlighten...*

[f. 24rA] ...Torrents of my many transgressions have fallen upon me, O all-pure one, and have cast down the temple of my soul; but do thou who art the Guide of righteousness, O Mother of God, raise me up, thy servant!

I am stuck fast in the darkness of passions, a wretch, and drowned by the tempest of many sins; stretch forth thy hand, O Sovereign Lady, raise me up, and guide me unto the harbor of repentance!

*Theotokion:*

Grant cleansing of the defilements of my soul, and heal the diseases of my flesh, I pray; and deliver me by thy prayers from the fierce despondency that holds me fast!

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*

*I am wholly held fast by boundless passions, and have been swallowed up by the fierce whale; but raise me up from corruption, O Christ, as Thou didst Jonah of old, and by Thy passion grant me dispassion, that with the voice of praise and the spirit of truth I may sing unto Thee!*

When Moses raised up his hands on the hill, he prefigured Thy passion, Who didst stretch forth Thy palms upon the Tree and destroy the destructive dominion of the crafty one; therefore knowing Thee as Redeemer and Savior, we sing unto Thee, O Lover of mankind!

Thou didst endure death, being raised upon the Tree, and didst put to death our slayer; and quickening the creation of Thy race, O Christ, being pierced in the ribs with a spear, Thou didst pour forth two rivers of remission unto those who sing unto Thee with willing spirit![^35]

*For the Martyrs:*

Honorable in the eyes of the Lord is now your death, O holy ones, having honored all men by your precious sufferings, [f. 24rB] and put to shame the dishonorable Beliar with all his applications of tortures, who sought to cast you down by his wiles!

With all your soul attaining unto all things, O all-wise ones, through manifold tortures ye found all assistance helping you, Who clothed Himself in all humanity; therefore being torn on the judgments and receiving the fire, ye rejoice!

*Theotokion:*

Beholding Thy crucifixion, O all-pure one, she cried: "O Son, what is this strange vision that is seen? He Who heals those sick in passions, how dost Thou, O Christ, endure a novel suffering? What have Thine enemies rendered unto Thee, the Benefactor, in return for the grace they received?"

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*

*The deepest abyss hath surrounded us...*

Tear up the handwriting of my transgressions with the spear, O all-pure one, of Him Who was born of thy seedless womb; account him who flees unto thy divine protection worthy to be written in the book of the chosen!
