Heal Thy servants, O Christ, by the prayers of her who bore Thee, and send down forgiveness of sins, as Thou alone art good: for Thou art the Savior and Redeemer of all who hope in Thee!

*Theotokion:*

Slain by passions am I, O pure Virgin: do thou who didst bear the Giver of life now quicken me by thy prayers, and show me to be victorious over the evil enemy: for thee alone do we have as our helper before God!

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*

*The holy youths showed themselves of old in the furnace of fire, passing through the flame as into a bridal chamber, and singing in harmony the hymn: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!...*

[f. 24vA] ...for piety's sake, O holy youths, clearly revealed, and with one voice singing the hymn: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

Being Master, Thou didst receive blows from a servant, wishing to free me who was enslaved to the enemy; and being nailed upon the Cross, that Thou mightest save me who sing: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

All creation was shaken, O Compassionate Lord, when Thou wast crucified; when Thou wast pierced with a spear, the enemy received an all-destroying wound, and wounded Adam was healed, crying: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*For the Martyrs:*

Encircled by the Cross, the glorious company of martyrs, enduring glorious warfare, destroyed the enemy's battle arrays by grace, and received crowns of victory, crying: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

Having acquired the power of fire by the will of their endurance, the sufferers were not burned when touching the fire; but they burned up the wicked substance of impiety, crying aloud: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Stavrotheotokion:*

Thy birthgiving, O Virgin, was glorious unto all; and raised upon the Cross, He raised up fallen man with Himself, and revealed him as a citizen of heaven, who cry: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*

*Thee, the spiritual furnace...*

As having given birth to the Fountain of life, raise up my deadened soul by thy life-bearing right hand, O all-pure one, and account me worthy to cry in compunction of heart: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers, and exceeding praised!

Of thy pure blood, O Virgin, the pre-eternal God willed to become a new Adam, Whom [f. 24vB] now pray to renew me who am grown old, crying: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers, and exceeding praised!

*Theotokion:*

The enemy comes by the way of wrath, wishing unsparingly to snatch away my humble soul: dissolve his counsels, O all-pure one, and have mercy on me who sing: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers, and exceeding praised!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*

*The furnace moist with dew prefigured of old a wonder beyond nature; for the fire burned not the young children, revealing the seedless, divine birthgiving of Christ from the Virgin: therefore singing we praise: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and exalt Him supremely unto all ages!*

He Who by His nod stretched out the heaven was crucified upon the Cross of His own will, and was nailed with nails, wishing to abolish the strange fall of the first-fashioned Adam; therefore singing we praise: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and exalt Him supremely unto all ages!

When the hard-hearted assembly of the Jews raised Thee, the Stone upon the stone, the mountains were shaken, the earth trembled, O Word of God, and wavering souls were established unto divine life; therefore singing we praise: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and exalt Him supremely unto all ages!

*For the Martyrs:*

All the holy passion-bearers wove for themselves a sacred garment, patiently suffering in the filth of the flesh, and receiving the sprinkling of wounds, and now they sing rejoicing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and exalt [f. 25rA] Him supremely unto all ages!

*For the Martyrs:*

Mercilessly scraped with claws, the sufferers endured, and being torn apart without mercy on the racks, and partaking greatly of wounds, they put on incorruption and showed themselves as pillars of courage unto the faithful, crying: Bless Christ, all ye works, and exalt Him supremely unto all ages!

*Stavrotheotokion:*

The foolish assembly provoked the Child, thinking to remove Him from the earth; I became childless and sorrowful in maternal heart, cried the unwedded one of old, seeing Thee lifted up upon the Cross; but the creation glorifies Thee, the Redeemer of all, Jesus, unto all ages!

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*

*In the furnace, the youths...*

Enlighten the eyes of my heart, O pure gate of Light, driving away the clouds of passions and the deep darkness, that I may sing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and exalt Him supremely unto all ages!

Cease not to pray for all, O pure Sovereign Lady, who call upon thee as the Mother of God, O Virgin all-immaculate, and who cry: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and exalt Him supremely unto all ages!

Having ineffably given birth to Christ, the Cause of salvation, pray earnestly for all who cry, O Virgin all-hymned: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and exalt Him supremely unto all ages!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*

*The ineffable mystery of the Virgin: for heaven's majesty above contained Him not, yet He was contained within her womb; therefore coming together, we bless her, and in faith...*

[f. 25rB] ...and joy we magnify her!

When the prudent Thief of old saw Thee hung upon the Tree, O Savior, Who didst suspend the earth upon the boundless waters, he faithfully cried unto Thee: "Remember me!" With him we piously glorify Thy voluntary sufferings!

Crucified, Thou didst shake the foundations of the earth; pierced with a spear, Thou didst pour forth drops of immortality, blood and water, wherewith Thou didst cleanse humanity from passions, O Jesus; therefore singing we magnify Thee!

*For the Martyrs:*

The holy ones rejoiced in tortures, thinking within themselves as if at a noble feast, crying with voices: "Behold, Christ hath opened the contest, and now bestows crowns upon those whom He loved!"

The unique festival of the faithful is illuminated in every way, honoring the sufferings of all the invincible martyrs and their countless sicknesses: for whose sake they were accounted worthy of painless life, and delight, and everlasting enjoyment!

*Stavrotheotokion:*

Thou didst ineffably give birth to the Word, the Lover of mankind; and seeing Him suffering willingly, the Maiden cried: "What is this? The impassible God accepts suffering, that He may deliver from passions those who worship Him in faith!"

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*

*The image of thy pure birthgiving...*

Take away the heavy burden of my sins, O all-hymned Mother of God, and grant me to bear the light yoke of thy Son and God; and renewed, may I attain unto the heavenly [f. 25vA] perfection that leads upward!

I tremble as I reflect, O all-immaculate one, upon the dread day of the coming of Christ; for all my life hath ended in sins, and my soul is filled with passions: but have compassion on me, and deliver me then from all condemnation!

*Theotokion:*

Receive, O all-pure Sovereign Lady, the supplication of thine unprofitable servant, and turn the confusion of my soul and body into deep tranquility, that being saved, I may magnify thee!

### AT THE APOSTICHA, STICHERA OF THE CROSS

*Tone 1:*

Thee Who wast nailed in the flesh to the Tree and gavest us life, as Savior and Benefactor we sing unceasingly!

By Thy Cross, O Christ, there became one flock of Angels and men, and in one assembly heaven and earth rejoice: O Lord, glory to Thee!

*For the Martyrs:*

Neither tribulation, nor anguish, nor famine, nor persecution, nor wounds, nor fury of wild beasts, nor sword, nor threatening fire could separate you from Christ, O all-lauded martyrs: but through love for Him, as if striving in foreign bodies, ye forgot nature, despising death; therefore also according to the worth of your sufferings ye received your reward, and became heirs of the heavenly Kingdom: pray ye for our souls!

*Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion:*

Standing by Thy Cross, O Word of God, the Ewe-lamb and undefiled Mother wept and cried: [f. 25vB] "Woe is me, O Son, how dost Thou die upon the Cross? Woe is me, my sweet Light: whither hath the sight of Thy beauty set, which was fairer than all the children of men?"

# ON WEDNESDAY AT THE BEATITUDES
*Tone 1:*

Because of food the enemy led Adam out of Paradise; but through the Cross Christ led the Thief into it, crying: Remember me, O Lord, when Thou comest into Thy Kingdom!

Thou didst endure a reproachful passion, O Christ, and didst take away our great reproach, O Good One, and didst make us partakers of the heavenly Kingdom unto ages, who worship Thy condescension!

Thou didst cover the nakedness of Adam, O Christ, when Thou wast stripped in the flesh; and being raised upon the Cross, Thou didst raise us up from the depth of evils; therefore we glorify Thy holy descent, O Word!

By your holy sufferings, O all-lauded martyrs, having wounded the multitude of demons, ye heal all infirmities, wounds, and passions by grace truly evermore!

*Glory... Triadikon:*

The Trinity enlightens all who purely honor It and know Its undivided dominion; therefore we cry aloud: Save those who sing unto Thee in love, O Trinity!

*Both now... Theotokion:*

Standing by the Cross and beholding Christ nailed in the flesh, the all-immaculate one exclaimed and cried: "Whither hath Thy merciful beauty set, O truly ineffable One?"[^36]

## ON WEDNESDAY EVENING, AT "LORD, I HAVE CRIED"

[f. 26rA] *Stichera of the Holy Apostles, Tone 1.*

*Podoben: "O all-lauded martyrs" (Прехвальніи мꙋнци):*

Glorious Apostles, closest friends of Christ: leaving me who show mercy to the friend of the enemy through wicked deeds and am estranged from love, bring me near unto Him Whom I have embittered, through good works, showing kindness through loving-kindness!

All-wise Apostles, divinely-called disciples of Christ, teachers of the universe: by your prayers strengthen me to accept the divine teachings, and help me ever to walk the narrow path, that I may attain unto the most spacious dwelling of Paradise!

I hymn Peter the foremost, Paul, James, Andrew, and Philip, Simon, Bartholomew, and Thomas, Matthew and John, Mark and Luke, who wrote the Gospel: the divinely-chosen choir with the other Seventy, as eyewitnesses and preachers of the Word!

*Other Stichera to Saint Nicholas, Tone 1.*

*Podoben: "Joy of the heavenly ranks" (Небе́сныхъ чинѡ́въ):*

Flying across the flowers of the Church, like a fledgling of the high angelic nest, O most blessed Nicholas: thou ever criest unto God for us all who are in urgent tribulations and perils, and deliverest us by thy prayers!

Passing through the beauties of heaven, strangely [f. 26rB] thou didst understand that glory, O holy of holies; therefore also in heavenly words thou ever utterest the call of those living things, O most sacred father!

Thou didst make the adornment of the sacred vestment a beacon through active virtues, O God-bearing father; therefore also in the sacred ministry thou performest marvelous things of glorious visions, praising Him Who is fierce against us!

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*

Tossed by the abyss of transgressions, having fled unto the calm harbor of thine all-pure prayer, O Mother of God, I cry unto thee: Save me, stretching forth thy strong right hand unto thy servant, O all-immaculate one!

### AT THE APOSTICHA, STICHERA OF THE APOSTLES

*Tone 1:*

The all-powerful discipleship of the Apostles, moved by the Holy Spirit, abolished the abominable sacrifices to demons; and having preached the one Lord, delivered the nations from idol delusion and taught them to worship the consubstantial Trinity!

Let us with one voice praise Peter and Paul, Luke, Matthew, Mark, John, Andrew, Thomas, Bartholomew, Simon the Canaanite, James, and Philip; and let all the apostolic company be worthily praised!

*For the Martyrs:*

O all-lauded martyrs, the earth [f. 26vA] hath received you, and the gates of Paradise have been opened unto you; and being within, ye enjoy the Tree of life: pray Christ to grant peace and great mercy unto our souls!

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*

Rejoice, harbinger of joy, delight of the Apostles and martyrs, and protection unto us, thy servants, O Virgin!

## ON THURSDAY AT MATINS

*After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymns of the Apostles, Tone 1:*

All-wise fishers of the universe, having received from God the power of prayer, intercede now for us who cry aloud: O Lord, save Thy Emperor and Thy city, and deliver our souls from surrounding evils, for the sake of the Apostles!

*Glory...*

Let the faithful honor in hymns the divinely-sounding trumpets of Christ, the all-wise Apostles, who stirred up the Egyptian sea like horses, and drew men who were without head unto the divine harbor of salvation by the grace of the Spirit!

*Both now... Theotokion:*

Having acquired an insurmountable wall, the Theotokos Mary, come, let us the faithful bow down and fall before her: for she hath boldness to pray unto Him Who was born of her, and she saves our souls from wrath and death!

*After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 1:*

With the spiritual net of rhetorical windings, the simple fishermen having cast the net of the Cross: enlightened the nations piously to glorify Thee, the true God; therefore we cry unto Thee Who didst strengthen them: Glory to the Father, and to the Son, [f. 26vB] glory to the consubstantial Spirit; glory to Him Who through them enlightened the world!

*For the Martyrs:*

We all pray the martyrs of Christ, coming unto them with faith: for they ask for our salvation, they pour forth the grace of healing, they drive away demonic regiments, as guardians of the faith!

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*

O hope of Christians, all-pure Virgin: Whom thou didst bear as God beyond mind and word, unceasingly pray for those who hymn thee, to grant remission of all our sins and correction of life, that in faith and love we may ever glorify thee!

*After the 3rd Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 1:*

Mental luminaries, disciples of the Savior: as fiery luminaries ye illuminated the fullness of all the earth with divine teachings. Therefore I pray: enlighten my soul which is in darkness with your light-bearing rays, O all-blessed ones!

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*

The Forefathers clearly proclaimed thee beforehand as the Maiden, Mother of God; and the divine Apostles preached thee in the world; and we the cruciform flock, piously and wisely honoring thee, hymn thee and truly call thee the Mother of God!

## ON THURSDAY: CANONS TO THE HOLY APOSTLES
*Composition of Saint Theophanes.*[^37]

*Ode 1, Tone 1. Heirmos:*

*Thy victorious right hand...*

Illuminated with the divine rays [f. 27rA] of the Thrice-radiant brightness, O glorious ones, ye were truly called gods by adoption, O light-formed Apostles; therefore as is due we faithfully honor you!

Having heard the Word on earth, Who out of loving-kindness clothed Himself in flesh, O chosen servants, and having become fulfillers of all His commandments in faith, ye are ever honored, O Apostles!

With the illuminating rays of the All-Holy Spirit, O most blessed ones, enlighten me entirely, who am covered with the darkness of sins, and guide me unto the paths of repentance!

Joy of the Apostles, all-immaculate Sovereign Lady, Mother of God: as thou wast the Mother of Him Who was divinely glorified by them, with them pray that I may be delivered from the fire of Gehenna!

### Another Canon to Saint Nicholas
*Composition of Saint Joseph.*

*Ode 1, Tone 1. Heirmos:*

*Let us sing a victorious song...*

Adorned with righteous crowns and standing before the throne of grace, O Nicholas: ever save by thy prayers those who now crown thee with hymns!

Having received the grace of healings, O all-blessed Nicholas: heal the sores of my soul by thy prayers, and deliver me, I pray, from the assaults that come upon me!

By the strength of the prayer of God, O Nicholas, heal my soul utterly paralyzed by transgressions, and deliver me, I pray, from the wicked evils of life!

Drive away the darkening of my mind with thy light, O all-immaculate one, [f. 27rB] and deliver me from eternal darkness, that I may ever sing magnifying thee!

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*

*Thou alone knowest...*

The only invisible God became visible by being incarnate, and chose you as His disciples in all the world, proclaiming His name and transcendent glory, O most glorious divine Apostles!

Unto Thee alone have I sinned, O Christ, unto Thee alone have I done iniquity, and defiled my soul; in Thy mercy pity and save me, having Thine all-wise Apostles praying for me, O only Benefactor Jesus!

From the bitterness of passions and thoughts, and from every sin, as merciful Apostles deliver me, sweetening my mind through repentance, as with divine delight in heart, O all-lauded ones!

*Theotokion:*

With the bodiless ministers, O unwedded Virgin, with all the higher Powers, with the martyrs and Apostles: implore Christ, Whom thou didst incarnate of thy pure blood, that Thy servants may be saved!

*Another Canon [to Saint Nicholas]. Heirmos:*

*Let my heart be established...*

Adornment of high priests, breathing of the divine Spirit: by thy myrrh-scented prayers drive away the foul-smelling passions of my heart, O wise Nicholas, I pray!

In slothfulness do I spend my life, a wretch, and I fear the dread tribunal of Christ; whereat put me not to shame, being entreated by the sacred intercessions of Nicholas!

Filled with divine grace, [f. 27vA] O hierarch, father Nicholas: save from diverse temptations and troubles those who ever flee beneath thy protection, O all-blessed one!

*Theotokion:*

Deliver me from great affliction and from many serpentine temptations, O all-immaculate one, who didst bear for us the unwaning Light!

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*

*The Mountain shadowed by the grace of God...*

Having stirred up the godless and tempestuous sea by your coming, O divinely-chosen horses, Apostles of Christ: ye drowned the noetic enemy and drew men who were drowned unto salvation!

Receptacles of the divine radiance of the Spirit: enlighten with the light of repentance my soul darkened and receptive of great passions, O divinely-blessed Apostles!

Clouds that rained down the water of life: water divinely my soul dried up by the heat of passions, and cause it to bring forth an ear of the virtues of salvation, O all-lauded Apostles!

*Theotokion:*

Prophets, Apostles, all-lauded martyrs, with the Mother of the Redeemer: pray earnestly that we may be delivered from sins, and eternal torment, and temptations, and troubles, and afflictions!

*Another Canon [to Saint Nicholas]. Heirmos:*

*Foreseeing in the Spirit...*

As the fulfiller of all the commandments of God: help us who are upon earth to keep the ordinances that lead unto salvation, and deliver us from all approaching misfortunes, O father, hierarch Nicholas!

[f. 27vB] Having finished thy course ever with Christ: direct our paths toward Him, so that fleeing from lawless wandering, we may attain unto salvific perfection, O God-bearing father Nicholas!

Lulling all the wiles of the enemy to sleep by divine vigilance, O all-wise Nicholas: graciously shed grace upon all who keep vigil and hymn God and put thee forward as intercessor unto Him!

*Theotokion:*

The Prophet, understanding by the Spirit of God, praised thee beforehand, O pure one, as the overshadowing mountain: cool me who am melted by the heat of many transgressions by thine intercession, O Virgin, sole correction of men!

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*

*Thou Who didst enlighten with the radiance of Thy coming...*

Dropping sweetness and fair joy, ye appeared as mountains, O all-blessed Apostles: crushing all the enemy's grief and delighting the faithful!

Coming strangely unto Thine own, O Christ, they recognized Thee and cleaved sincerely unto Thee: therefore deliver me from that strange appearance, O divine Apostles of the Word!

Heal the hidden wounds of my soul by the prayers of those who clearly preached in the world Thy divine coming and passions, O Compassionate One, and Thy resurrection from the tomb!

*Theotokion:*

With all the Bodiless Ones, implore God the Word, Whom thou didst incarnate beyond word, O Virgin: that Thy servants may be freed from irrational deeds and fleshly passions!

*Another Canon [to Saint Nicholas]. Heirmos:*

*Brightly for us...*

Planted in the courts of the Lord, [f. 28rA] O father Nicholas, like a fruitful olive tree through grace: thou dost now anoint the faces of all with the oil of thy labors!

Make supplication now, O father, for thy servants: that we may receive remission of transgressions, and be delivered from surrounding afflictions and from every distress!

We pray thee, our fervent intercessor before God: leave us not, O holy one, without protection, but save us by thine accustomed prayer!

*Theotokion:*

Light-formed temple of Christ, O Maiden: by thy prayers, O Virgin Mother, make us also temples unto the Father, and the Son, and the Spirit, performing things well-pleasing!

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*

*The deepest abyss hath surrounded us...*

With verbal nets ye caught the nations unto the knowledge of the creation revealed unto men, O divinely-blessed Apostles: whom pray ye earnestly for peace!

My humble soul, my wretched soul, my unrepentant soul: repent and cry out unto Christ: "I have sinned; pity me, O Master, by the prayers of Thine Apostles, for Thou art exceeding good!"

Thou Who of old didst bring forth for Israel the fountain of waters from the rock of joy, O Christ: tear asunder my darkness and grant me to bring streams of tears, that I may hymn and magnify Thy tender mercy!

*Theotokion:*

O Virgin, who didst bring forth the wellspring through the good pleasure of the Father: pray Him as Creator and God to save from temptations and tribulations those who have placed their hope in thee!

*Another Canon [to Saint Nicholas]. Heirmos:*

*The Prophet Jonah...*

[f. 28rB] Having a multitude of tender mercies, O Christ: drive away the multitude of my evils by the prayers of Nicholas, steering my life which is ever tempest-tossed by the waves of sin![^38]

Mightily didst thou trample the enemy, O wise one: strengthen us also to crush him by thy prayers, O Nicholas, who have been enriched with thee as a divine intercessor!

Having been the true chief hierarch of Myra: breathe fragrance into our spiritual senses and ever drive away harmful, foul-smelling passions, O father Nicholas!

*Theotokion:*

Great things hath Christ done unto thee, O pure Virgin: implore Him ever to magnify His rich mercies upon us, O woman full of the grace of God!

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*

*Thee, the spiritual furnace...*

Christ the Lord, being the Wellspring of life, sent you forth, O disciples, like rivers watering with the knowledge of God all the universe, who sing: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers, and exceeding praised!

Bearing mental fire in your hearts, the divine grace of Christ: ye burnt up the substance of godlessness, O disciples; therefore burn up my material passions, who cry: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers, and exceeding praised!

Deliver me from fiery torment, O Christ, by the prayers of Thy glorious disciples, and cast me not away from Thy presence, O Lord, who cry out in repentance: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers, and exceeding praised!

*Theotokion:*

Deliver me, O Lord, from corrupting sins and passions, Who wast incorruptibly born of the Virgin, His Mother: granting incorruption unto those who sing [f. 28vA] Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers, and exceeding praised!

*Another Canon [to Saint Nicholas]. Heirmos:*

*In the furnace...*

By thy strong prayer, O wise one, firmly establish the steps of my heart upon the rock of the most bright commandments of God, saving me without fail from the malicious wiles of the evil enemy!

Ask for us remission of our many transgressions, deliver us from all the wicked things of life and from great temptations that come upon us, O sacred Nicholas, protector of all the faithful and firm foundation!

I am the wretched servant who hid the talent which I received to work good; and I fear the judgment there, wherein, O Judge of all, put me not to shame!

*Theotokion:*

Thee, the all-holy and all-immaculate shelter, we thy servants ever pray day and night with contrite thought, asking: grant deliverance from our sins, attending unto our prayers, O good one!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*

*In the furnace, the children of Israel...*

As a ray of the great Sun, He stretched you forth into all the universe, illuminating those who cry with faith, O Apostles: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing praise and exalt Him supremely unto all ages!

As verbal shepherds, as lambs of the Shepherd, as sheep of the Lamb and our Savior Christ, O God-seeing Apostles: pray unceasingly to deliver me from the mental wolf and to make me partaker of the lot of the saved!

O most wretched soul, sigh and cry unto the Lord: "I have sinned more than [f. 28vB] all, and done iniquity grievously; pity and save me, as the Good One of old, like the Publican, like the Thief, O Compassionate One, by the acceptable prayers of the Apostles!"

*Theotokion:*

With the Angels, O Mother of God, with the Apostles and martyrs and with the Prophets, implore Christ to save those who cry aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing praise and exalt Him supremely unto all ages!

*Another Canon [to Saint Nicholas]. Heirmos:*

*Him of Whom the Angels stand in awe...*

Standing upon the mountain of divine virtues, known unto the ends of the earth by high miracles, O Nicholas, revealed by signs: therefore every nation honors thee unto all ages!

In the visions of divine sweetness, O venerable one, thou didst hate the bitterness of passions and pleasures; deliver me from them, I pray Christ, to quell afflictions!

As an unshakable pillar and confirmation of the faithful: ever strengthen me who am shaken by worldly evils and demonic blastings, O all-blessed Nicholas, by thy prayers!

*Theotokion:*

Heal the passions of my heart, O all-pure one, who didst bear the Physician of all; and show me to be a partaker of the righteous lot, O Virgin, having implored Christ!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*

*The image of thy pure birthgiving...*

Ye were shown forth as divine luminaries of the Holy Spirit and light-radiant beacons; and with the light-beholding vision of your honorable and all-wise preaching, O blessed ones, ye enlightened all the universe, having driven away the darkness of idolatry!

Having become vines of the divine spiritual vineyard, ye brought forth the divine [f. 29rA] cluster, gushing forth the wine of salvation, O glorious Apostles; therefore deliver me from the drunkenness of pleasures!

I tremble, a wretch, as I contemplate that dread judgment of Thine, O my Christ; with foul deeds am I now surrounded, and condemned before judgment; therefore pity me by the prayers of Thine Apostles!

*Theotokion:*

Thou alone didst deify human nature, having given birth to the incarnate Word; Whom implore with the Apostles and martyrs, O pure and all-immaculate Virgin, for us who in faith bless and honor thee!

*Another Canon [to Saint Nicholas]. Heirmos:*

*The light-bearing cloud...*

As a light of Christ, as a light-radiant star, as a worker of miracles, as a wellspring of healings, as a speedy helper in sacred trials, as a most fervent deliverer unto those who call upon thee in afflictions, O father: we praise thee with sacred hymns!

Thee, the great shepherd and imitator of the Chief Shepherd Christ, we earnestly pray: protect thy servants from sacred misfortunes, O Nicholas, ever delivering them from all worldly assaults!

Already the end draws near; why art thou slothful, O my soul? Why art thou not zealous to live in a manner pleasing unto God? Strive, arise at last, and cry: "O Lover of mankind, have compassion on me by the prayers of Nicholas, steering my life, for Thou art good!"

*Theotokion:*

Thou who didst bear the divine Light, [f. 29rB] enlighten me who am darkened by all the assaults of the evil one and living in despondency and having angered God, O all-immaculate one; and guide me unto good works, as thou art the cause of all good things!

### AT THE APOSTICHA, STICHERA OF THE APOSTLES

*Tone 1:*

Glorious Apostles, who enlightened the universe: unceasingly pray that our souls may be saved!

Let us with one voice praise Peter and Paul, Luke, Matthew, Mark, John, Andrew, Thomas, Bartholomew, Simon the Canaanite, James, and Philip; and let all the apostolic company be worthily praised!

*For the Martyrs:*

Rejoice in the Lord, O martyrs: for ye contested with a good contest, ye resisted emperors and conquered the tyrant; ye feared not fire nor sword, nor wild beasts eating your bodies; sending up hymnody unto Christ with the Angels, ye received crowns from heaven. Ask that peace and humility and great mercy be granted unto our souls!

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*

Rejoice, O Virgin Mother of God! Rejoice, praise of all the universe! Rejoice, all-pure Mother of God, blessed one!

# ON THURSDAY AT THE BEATITUDES
*Tone 1:*

Because of food the enemy led Adam out of Paradise; but through the Cross Christ led the Thief into it, crying: Remember me, O Lord, when Thou comest into Thy Kingdom!

Having enlightened the ends of the earth with the divine rays of your teachings, ye dispelled the darkness [f. 29vA] of fierce godlessness; and having passed unto the unwaning Light, ye are faithfully blessed!

Possessing essential and hypostatic wisdom, O disciples of Christ, making all things wise: by your divine preaching ye made the world wise, and brought it unto divine understanding!

*For the Martyrs:*

Having endured tortures like the bodiless ones, O sufferers of Christ, ye mightily conquered all the bodiless enemies; therefore ye are worthily blessed unto the ages, O all-lauded ones!

*Glory... Triadikon:*

Let us worship the Trinity, with the Father, the Son and the right Spirit: in an undivided, inseparable, and co-enthroned unity, O faithful, crying: Holy art Thou, O Thrice-Holy God!

*Both now... Theotokion:*

We bless thee, O all-pure one, as thou didst prophesy; for thou didst bear God in the flesh, Whom the apostolic choir proclaimed: through whom ask for us remission of transgressions, O all-hymned one!

## ON THURSDAY EVENING, AT "LORD, I HAVE CRIED"

*Stichera of the Cross, Tone 1.*

*Podoben: "O all-lauded martyrs" (Прехвальніи, мꙋнци):*

Thou didst stretch forth Thine all-pure hands on the Cross, O Christ, calling those who were far off from Thee and bringing them near unto Thee. Therefore I pray Thee: gather me who am captive unto passions, and grant me repentance that cleanses every defilement of passion!

Thou didst lift up Thine all-pure palms upon the Tree, O Christ, and didst stain Thy fingers with blood, wishing to deliver the work of Thy divine hands, O Lover of mankind, Adam who was held by transgression in the kingdom of death; whom Thou didst raise up by Thine all-powerful authority!

Thou didst deign to suffer for our sake, O Savior, Who art unchangeable in nature and impassible [f. 29vB] in Godhead; being crucified without beginning with evildoers, Thou Who art sinless; and the sun, unable to endure the audacity, was darkened, and all the earth was shaken, knowing Thee as its Creator!

*Other Stichera, Stavrotheotokia, Tone 1.*

*Podoben: "The same" (то́йже):*

The undefiled Virgin, seeing on the Tree of old Him Whom she bore of her seedless womb, unable to endure the piercing of her bowels, tearing her hair, cried: "O Thou Who upholdest creation by Thy nod, how art Thou raised upon the Cross as one condemned, wishing in every way to save mankind?"

"Offspring ineffable of the Father pre-eternal," cried the all-pure one, looking upon my Birthgiving on [f. 30rA] the Cross: "How do I not understand for what things the ungrateful people have rewarded Thee with these? But in that Thou art come to save Thy creation, Thou endurest all things, O long-suffering and compassionate One!"[^39]

*Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion:*

Heal my soul grievously ailing with wicked passions, O all-hymned one, who didst bear Christ, the Physician and Savior of all, Who heals every infirmity, and delivers from the malice of the devil and from death him who is wounded!

### AT THE APOSTICHA, STICHERA OF THE CROSS

*Tone 1:*

The Cross was planted upon Golgotha, and immortality blossomed forth for us from the ever-flowing fountain of the Savior's side!

An indestructible wall is the precious Cross of the Savior unto us: for hoping in it, we all are saved!

*For the Martyrs:*

By the prayers, O Lord, of all the holy ones and of the Theotokos, grant us Thy peace, and have mercy on us, for Thou alone art compassionate!

*Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion:*

Beholding Thy unjust slaying, O Christ, the Virgin cried weeping unto Thee: "Sweet child, how dost Thou die unjustly? And how dost Thou hang upon the Tree, Who didst suspend all the earth upon the waters? Leave me not alone, O Benefactor rich in mercy, Thy Mother and servant, I pray!"

## ON FRIDAY AT MATINS

*After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymns of the Cross, Tone 1:*

When Thou wast crucified, O Christ, tyranny perished, [f. 30rB] and the power of the enemy was trampled down; for neither an Angel nor a man, but Thou Thyself, O Lord, hast saved us: glory to Thee!

We venerate the Wood of Thy Cross, O Lover of mankind, for upon it Thou wast nailed, O Life of all; and Thou didst open Paradise, O Savior, unto the Thief who came to Thee in faith, and didst account him worthy of delight who confessed Thee: "Remember me, O Lord!" Accept also us who cry as that thief did: "We all have sinned; despise us not in Thy tender mercy!"

*Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion:*

The undefiled Ewe-lamb, beholding the Lamb and Shepherd hung dead upon the Wood, cried weeping, exclaiming with a mother's voice: "How shall I endure Thy condescension beyond word, O my Son, and Thy voluntary passions, O God most good?"

*After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns of the Cross, Tone 1:*

The weapon of the Cross was revealed in battles of old unto the pious Emperor Constantine, an invincible victory over enemies for the sake of faith: the contrary powers tremble before it; this was salvation unto the faithful and the boast of Paul!

Thou Who of old didst fashion Adam out of dust, wast struck on the cheek by a clay hand, O Compassionate One, and didst endure crucifixion, mockery, and wounds: O the wonder! O Thy great long-suffering! Glory to Thy life-giving passions, O Lord, whereby Thou hast saved us!

*For the Martyrs:*

With the praise of suffering and eternal honor, O glorious passion-bearers, [f. 30vA] having bound yourselves unto the Lord, O holy ones; for by endurance of wounds ye conquered the lawless, and by divine power received victory from heaven. By their prayers deliver us also from the invisible enemy, O Savior, and save us!

*Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion:*

Beholding Thee dead, stretched out upon the Cross, O Christ, Thine all-immaculate Mother cried aloud: "O my Son, co-unoriginate with the Father and the Spirit, what is this ineffable dispensation of Thine, whereby Thou hast saved with Thine all-pure hand the creation of Thy compassion?"

*After the 3rd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns, Tone 1:*

When the Sun saw Thee, O Word, hung upon the Wood of the Cross, out of tender mercy, of Thine own will in the flesh: unable to bear the audacity, it was darkened, O Christ, Sun of glory! Therefore enlighten my darkened soul with Thine unapproachable light, and save me, I pray!

*Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion:*

Having acquired thee as our protection, O all-pure one, by thy prayers we are delivered from misfortunes; for being ever preserved by the Cross of thy Son, as is due, we all piously magnify thee!

## ON FRIDAY: CANON TO THE PRECIOUS AND LIFE-CREATING CROSS
*Composition of Saint Joseph.*[^40]

*Ode 1, Tone 1. Heirmos:*

*Let us sing a song of victory unto God Who helped Moses in Egypt and thereby drowned Pharaoh with all his army, for He is glorified!*

Having endured passions for our sake, Who art impassible by nature, [f. 30vB] and being crucified with evildoers, Thou didst put to death the serpent, the beginner of malice, O Word; and Thou hast saved those who worship Thee!

Being the Dayspring of daysprings, O Jesus, Thou didst come unto our nature that was bound toward the setting of life; and the sun, seeing Thee crucified, hid its light!

Having exchanged temporary death for eternal life, O noble, glorious sufferers, ye were accounted worthy of the heavenly Kingdom: therefore ye are blessed!

*For the Martyrs:*

Bravely assimilating yourselves unto the passions of Christ, ye shrink not from earthly passions, O work of corruption; and by the Word ye drive away spirits, O holy martyrs!

*Stavrotheotokion:*

As an Ewe-lamb beholding the Lamb raised upon the Cross, the Ewe-lamb exclaimed and cried: "Whither hath Thy beauty set, O Long-suffering One, O Son co-unoriginate?"

### Another Canon to the Most Holy Theotokos
*Tone 1. Heirmos:*

*A song of victory...*

Thou who alone didst give birth in time to the timeless God incarnate, O all-holy, all-pure one: heal the perennial passions of my most wretched soul!

The wounds of my soul, the perplexity of my heart, the darkening of thoughts, and the corruption of mind, do thou abolish, O all-pure one, as thou art merciful, by thy prayers!

Thou who didst bear the Light, the Redeemer of my darkness and eternal torments: deliver me, O all-pure one, that being saved, I may hymn thy loving-kindness!

*Theotokion:*

In the deep of evils and the tempest of passions am I drowned; [f. 31rA] I call upon thy calm harbor, O all-pure one: save me, for thou art a harbor unto the faithful!

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*

*Let my heart be established in Thy will, O Christ God: Who didst establish the second heaven upon the waters, and didst found the earth upon the waters, O All-powerful One!*

Thou didst stretch forth Thy palms upon the Cross, and didst stain Thy divine fingers with blood: delivering the work of Thy hands, wounded Adam, by Thy good hand, O only Good and Lover of mankind!

Thy side was pierced with a spear, correcting the slipping of the rib; He was raised upon the Wood Who received the fruit of the tree of old, and opened Paradise unto the prudent Thief!

*For the Martyrs:*

Confirmations of the Church, foremost pillars of piety, destroyers of the enemy, martyrs of the Lord: with pure thought let us bless you in hymnody!

As divine branches of the spiritual vineyard, O martyrs: the clusters brought forth by your endurance pour out wine that cheers the hearts of the faithful!

*Stavrotheotokion:*

Blessed is the fruit of thy womb, O all-hymned Virgin: Who by the Wood of His Cross made those who were corrupted through the fruit to become partakers of incorruption through divine grace!

*Another Canon [to the Theotokos]. Heirmos: The same.*

Abolish all the fruitlessness of my barren mind, and show my soul to be fruitful in virtues, O most holy Mother of God, helper of the faithful!

Deliver me, O all-immaculate one, from every assault of many serpentine temptations, [f. 31rB] and from eternal fire and darkness, who didst bear the pre-eternal Light!

By the dread tribunal, O pure one, and by that unquenchable fire, and by the fierce account, I am wholly condemned: hasten to save me, O all-pure Sovereign Lady, thy servant!

That God might deify human nature, He became man; incorruptibly, O pure Virgin, thou didst contain Him beyond word: therefore with one voice we all the faithful bless thee!

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*

*I heard, O Lord, Thy report, and was afraid; I understood Thy works, cried the Prophet, and glorified Thy power, O Lover of mankind!*

Being the righteous Lawgiver, Thou wast numbered with the lawless; Thou wast raised upon the Wood, O Benefactor Lord, wishing to justify all!

All the angelic hosts were astonished, seeing Thee on the Cross with soldiers, O Sun, conquering the prince of darkness!

*For the Martyrs:*

Having drawn grace through healings, the martyrs, receiving spiritual gifts, wash away from all soul-corrupting passions by the grace of God!

Having received the slumber of negligence, O passion-bearers, by the vigilance of divine faith ye lulled its assaults to sleep in a corner, and rejoicing ye suffered!

*Stavrotheotokion:*

"Woe is me, Child! How do I see Thee raised upon the Wood and put to death unjustly, Who grantest life?" cried the Virgin weeping!

*Another Canon [to the Theotokos]. Heirmos:*

*Foreseeing in the Spirit...*

[f. 27vA] O Virgin Theotokos, undefiled tabernacle: cleanse me who am defiled by transgressions with thy compassions, by the most honorable sprinkling, and give me a helping hand, that I may cry: Glory to thee, O pure Bride of God!

O Virgin, thou wast revealed as a sanctified temple unto God, Who dwelt within thee beyond understanding; pray Him to cleanse me from the defilements of sins, that I may be known as a temple and a spiritual dwelling-place!

Have mercy on me, O Theotokos, who alone didst give birth unto the Wellspring of mercies; and heal the fierce sickness and heartache of my soul, grant me a stream of tears and compunction before the end, and deliverance from evils!

*Theotokion:*

O holy Theotokos, who didst bear in the flesh the All-Holy One Who willed to become like unto men: cleanse us, and by thy most pure prayers show all to be partakers of the heavenly Kingdom!

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*

*Make the bright and ever-existing Light to shine forth upon us who rise early at dawn unto the judgments of Thy commandments: for Thou art the Lover of mankind, O Christ our God!*[^41]

Being lifted up in the flesh upon the Cross, Thou didst call the nations that knew Thee not unto the knowledge of Thyself: the only One of all, O only greatly merciful Christ our God!

When the passion came upon Thee unjustly, O righteous Lord, Adam who was formerly condemned was justified, and cries aloud: "Glory to Thy crucifixion, O long-suffering Lord!"

*For the Martyrs:*

Like a paradise planted by God were ye revealed, O martyrs; the passions [f. 27vB] of the honorable ones, having acquired them as sweet-smelling flowers, whereby every soul of the faithful is filled with fragrance!

*For the Martyrs:*

As fair-flowering and fruitful trees that blossomed forth the fruit of the immortality of faith and uprooted the evil roots: let us hymn the martyrs of the Lord!

*Stavrotheotokion:*

The honorable rod who sprouted forth the unfading Flower, when she beheld Him lifted up upon the Tree, cried aloud: "Leave me not childless!"

*Another Canon [to the Theotokos]. Heirmos: Grant me Thy [peace]...*

The tasting of the tree of old in Eden made me dead; but thou who didst bear the Life, O pure Mother, make me alive who was dead of old through the tree, and grant me humility!

Fierce gloom hath encompassed me, O most pure one; raise me up from the fire of passions, and deliver me from captivity and from the malice of evil demons, as I am an unprofitable servant!

Enlighten the pupils of my soul, O pure one, that I may ever behold the divine brightness and thy glory, O all-immaculate one, that I may obtain mercy and eternal glory!

*Theotokion:*

Cloud, and Paradise, and Door of light, Table and radiant Fleece, Urn carrying within the Manna: I proclaim peace unto thee, O pure Virgin Mother!

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*

*As Thou didst save the type from the whale, O Lover of mankind: lead me up also from the deep of transgressions, I pray!*

Thou Who art higher than every honor didst endure dishonor, O Christ, being lifted up upon the Cross, wishing to honor mankind!

[f. 28rA] Grant Thy forgiveness unto me, as unto all the holy ones, who am enslaved unto evil things, O most good Christ!

*For the Martyrs:*

By the pains of sufferings ye passed over unto a painless end, O holy ones, being accounted worthy of ineffable joy!

*For the Martyrs:*

Being kindled with the coals of the love of Christ, O all-wise ones: therefore cast into the fire, ye were not consumed, but prospered!

*Stavrotheotokion:*

After giving birth, O all-immaculate one, thou didst remain even as thou wast before birthgiving: for thou didst bear God, Who saved man by the Tree!

*Another Canon [to the Theotokos]. Heirmos: As the Prophet Jonah...*

Defiled by many sins, I pray thee who alone art the good and undefiled tabernacle: wash me clean from every defilement by thy mediation!

Be thou a pilot unto me, O pure one, tossed about in the abyss of evils by worldly distresses; and direct me unto the eternal haven, and save me!

The billows of thoughts, and assaults of passions, and depths of sin tempest-toss my wretched soul: help me, O holy Sovereign Lady!

*Theotokion:*

O Mary, who wast revealed as a sanctified tabernacle: cleanse my wretched soul that is defiled by pleasures!

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*

*The furnace was bedewed, O Savior, and the children, dancing in chorus, sang: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!*

When crucified, Thou didst shake creation; when slain, Thou didst put the serpent to death: blessed art Thou, O Christ, God of our fathers!

The Long-suffering One was given gall to drink [f. 28rB] pouring forth saving sweetness for me, who was deprived of the food of Paradise through pleasurable eating!

*For the Martyrs:*

The martyrs, scraped while naked, put off the operation of mortality, and received divine beauty from God!

*For the Martyrs:*

In their sufferings assimilating themselves unto the passions of Christ, the gloriously victorious martyrs readily endured the wounds inflicted by the enemy!

*Stavrotheotokion:*

Beholding the Lord crucified, the undefiled Ewe-lamb cried: "Woe is me, O my Son! How dost Thou die, O Life and Hope of the faithful?"

*Another Canon [to the Theotokos]. Heirmos: He Who in the furnace...*

Cleanse my soul that is defiled with passions, O most pure Bride of God; and swiftly destroy the cruel captivity of my mind, the perplexity of my heart, and the demonic assaults, O pure one!

As I am slain by fleshly passions, O all-immaculate one, make my mind alive and strengthen me to accomplish things pleasing unto God, that I may magnify thee, O Virgin, and ever glorify thy loving-kindness!

O Mother of God, who alone didst bear God: put to death my fleshly pleasures, swiftly wash away the defilement of my soul, deliver me from the torment of evil demons, and save me!

*Stavrotheotokion:*

Adorned with divine virtues, thou didst bear the Word co-unoriginate with the Father, O pure Virgin, Who truly covered the heavens with virtues; pray Him unceasingly to have compassion on us!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*

*Him Who wondrously saved the blessed children in the furnace...*

[f. 28vA] *...and turned the roaring, flaming furnace into dew: hymn Christ God, and highly exalt Him unto all ages!*

When Thou wast nailed to the Cross, O Savior, creation quaked; the sun quenched its rays, and the rocks were split, and Hades was swiftly despoiled, unable to endure Thy dominion!

For the condemnation of the guilty one Thou didst suffer condemnation; for him who took on nakedness, Thou didst hang naked upon the Tree, O Compassionate One: great is Thy forbearance and long-suffering!

*For the Martyrs:*

Companions of the bodiless hosts, soldiers of Christ: clad with the Cross as with an armor, ye drew up in battle array against the adversary, and trampled him under your fair feet!

*For the Martyrs:*

The noble victims stood in the midst of the tribunal, torn limb from limb, tearing down the edifice of deceit, and casting down the demonic altars!

Beholding the only Most High, Who is higher than the heavens, lifted up upon the Tree and casting down the arrogance of the enemy, she sang unto Him with a loud voice!

*Another Canon [to the Theotokos]. Heirmos: Him before Whom tremble...*

The Bodiless One is incarnate of thee in a manner fitting God; pray Him, O pure one, to put to death my fleshly passions and to make alive my soul that is deadened by sins!

Thou didst bear the Savior and God, Who healed the crushing of the first-fashioned Adam, O most pure one; pray Him to heal the wounds of my soul, which drag me down incurably!

Raise me up who am bowed down unto the depth of evil things, and conquer him who wars against me, O pure one, and [f. 28vB] despise not my soul that is wounded by shameful pleasures, O most pure one, but have compassion and save me!

*Stavrotheotokion:*

We are delivered from all manner of temptations, O most pure one, by thy vigilant prayers unto God, who judge thee to be the blessed and full-of-grace Theotokos!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*

*Thee, whom Moses beheld as the unburnt bush, and the animate ladder which Jacob saw, and the heavenly gate through which Christ our God passed: in hymns, O pure Mother, do we magnify!*

How did the disobedient people surrender unto the Cross the only Long-suffering One, Who voluntarily became poor and accepted passions, and became the Mediator of dispassion unto all who fell through Adam?

Christ accepted dishonorable crucifixion in the flesh, wishing to rest man who was dishonored by the enemy through brute beasts and who lost his ancient beauty: glory to Thy compassion that is beyond understanding!

*For the Martyrs:*

O Christ, unwaning Sun: by Thy nodding Thou didst guide unto the light of ineffable glory and brightness the soldiers who rose early unto Thee and passed through the darkness of sufferings; therefore enlighten us by their prayers!

*For the Martyrs:*

The company of sacred martyrs conquered myriads of spiritual enemies, and was joined unto myriads of holy powers, ever dispelling the dark passions of our souls by the sign of divine grace!

*Stavrotheotokion:*

[f. 29rA] Illuminate my mind and enlighten my heart with the Light that shone forth from thee, driving away the darkness of sin and banishing all the gloom of my slothfulness!

*Another Canon [to the Theotokos]. Heirmos: Radiant cloud...*

Being a lover of sin, I abide in slothfulness, and I tremble before the inexorable tribunal, O pure one; preserve me uncondemned therein by thy holy prayers, that as my protectress I may call thee blessed, O most pure one!

Lamenting, O only Virgin, before the unslumbering eye of thy Son, having committed many sins upon earth, therefore I cry unto thee: All-merciful Sovereign Lady, help me, deliver me from the misfortunes of that time, and save me, O pure one!

How fearful is the day of examination, O Maiden! How terrible is the account! How bitter is the misfortune! Who shall endure it, O most pure Sovereign Lady? Have mercy on my passion-plagued soul, and grant me forgiveness before the end, O most pure one!

*Stavrotheotokion:*

O thou who didst bear the divine Light Who shone forth from the Father: have compassion, O all-immaculate one, upon my soul that is darkened by worldly deceits and become a mockery unto enemies, and account it worthy of the light of saving repentance, O pure one!

### AT THE APOSTICHA

*Stichera of the Cross, Tone 1:*

Thee Who wast nailed in the flesh upon the Tree and didst grant life unto us, as Savior and Master we unceasingly hymn!

By Thy Cross, O Christ, one flock was made of Angels and men; and [f. 29rB] in one assembly heaven and earth rejoice: O Lord, glory to Thee!

*For the Martyrs:*

Passion-bearers of Christ, come, all ye people, let us honor them with spiritual songs and hymns: the luminaries of the world and preachers of the faith, the ever-flowing fountains from which healings pour forth unto the faithful! By their prayers, O Christ our God, grant peace unto Thy world, and great mercy unto our souls!

*Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion.*

*Podoben: "O all-lauded martyrs" (Прехвальніи мꙋнцы):*

When the Ewe-lamb and all-immaculate Sovereign Lady beheld the Lamb upon the Cross having neither form nor beauty, she wept and cried: "Woe is me! Whither hath Thy beauty set, O sweetest One? Where is Thy majesty? Where is the grace of the countenance of Thine appearance, O my dearly-beloved Son?"

# ON FRIDAY AT THE BEATITUDES
*Tone 1:*

For the sake of food the enemy led Adam out of Paradise; but through the Cross, Christ led the Thief into it, who cried: "Remember me, O Lord, in Thy Kingdom!"

Being crucified, O Sinless One, Thou didst take away the sin of the world, O Christ; and pierced in the ribs, Thou didst pour forth streams of salvation, both water and blood, restoring the crushed, O Lover of mankind!

Being voluntarily nailed upon the Tree, O Jesus God, Thou didst completely undo, O Compassionate One, the passionate exchange of Adam; and by Thy precious wounds Thou didst wound the multitude of demons!

*For the Martyrs:*

Having assimilated yourselves unto the passions of Him Who voluntarily suffered in the flesh, O glorious martyrs: ye ever lull to sleep incurable passions [f. 29vA] and drive away illnesses from men by spiritual power!

*Glory...*

We glorify Thee, the Trinity of equal power and equal honor: God the unoriginate Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit; the one Godhead in three Persons do we magnify in faith!

*Both now... Stavrotheotokion:*

When she who bore Thee in the flesh beheld Thee nailed to the Cross, O Christ God, she wept and said: "What is this that the lawless assembly of the Hebrews returns unto Thee?"

## ON FRIDAY EVENING, AT "LORD, I HAVE CRIED"

*Stichera to the Holy Martyrs, Hierarchs, and Venerable Fathers, Tone 1.*

*Podoben: "O all-lauded martyrs" (Прехвальніи мꙋнци):*

The united feast of the martyrs drowned the demonic multitude in the streams of their blood; they renounced every vain sacrifice and destroyed the idolatrous delusion, having suffered with endurance; and now they pray that there may be granted unto our souls peace and great mercy!

All-venerable pastors: by wise words and teachings ye taught all to glorify the Trinity in the unity of the Godhead, divinely avoiding both the confusion and division of Persons; and now ye pray that there may be granted unto our souls peace and great mercy!

The choir of venerable fathers lulled to sleep the fleshly desires and bridled their impulses, showing forth an angelic life; therefore they now dance in chorus in the heavenly mansions, praying unto Christ to grant unto our souls peace and great mercy!

[f. 29vB] *Other Stichera to the Martyrs, Tone 1:*

By the prayers, O Lord, of all the saints and of the Theotokos, grant us Thy peace, and have mercy on us, for Thou alone art compassionate!

They who inherited your confession, O holy ones, terrified the power of the ages and set men free from deceit; therefore, even when beheaded, ye cried: "Let the sacrifice of our souls, O Lord, be acceptable before Thee, for they loved Thee and disregarded temporal life, O Lover of mankind!"

O the good merchandise of yours, O holy ones! For ye gave your blood, and inherited the heavens; and having been tried for a time, ye rejoice eternally! Truly good was your merchandise: for leaving behind corruptible things, ye received incorruptible things; and rejoicing in chorus with the Angels, ye unceasingly sing unto the consubstantial Trinity!

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion: "The glory of the world..."*

### AT THE APOSTICHA

[f. 30rA] *Martyrika, Tone 1:*

O all-lauded martyrs, the earth hath not concealed you, but heaven hath received you! The gates of Paradise opened unto you, and being within, ye delight in the Tree of Life; pray Christ to grant unto our souls peace and great mercy!

*Verse: Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen and taken to Thyself, O Lord.*

*Hymn for the Departed (Поко́инъ):*

What worldly pleasure abides unpartaking of sorrow? What glory stands upon earth unchanging? All things are frailer than a shadow, all things are more deceitful than dreams: in one hour death takes all these away! But in the light of Thy countenance, O Christ, and in the delight of Thy beauty, give rest unto those whom Thou hast chosen, for Thou art the Lover of mankind!

*Verse: Their souls shall dwell among good things.*

No one is sinless, none among men hath lived without sin, save Thou alone, O Immortal One! Therefore, as the compassionate God, account Thy servants worthy of the light, in the choirs of Thine Angels, overlooking their transgressions in Thy loving-kindness, and granting them forgiveness!

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*

Truly beyond understanding are all thy wonders, and the manner of thy birthgiving, O Bride of God, which all the prophets foretold: all-glorious was thy conception and birthgiving, O all-hymned one, incomprehensible and ineffable, whereby the world was saved, for He is merciful!

## ON SATURDAY AT MATINS

[f. 30rB] *After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymns of the Martyrs, Tone 1:*

With the praise of suffering and eternal honor, O glorious passion-bearers, having bound yourselves unto the Lord; for by endurance of wounds ye conquered the lawless, and by divine power received victory from heaven. By their prayers deliver us also from the invisible enemy, O Savior, and save us!

Like good warriors, covered in blood with one mind, ye feared not the threats of the torturers, O holy ones: ye came zealously unto Christ, taking up the precious Cross; and having finished your course, ye received victory from heaven! Glory to Christ Who strengthened you! Glory to Him Who crowned you! Glory to Him Who works healings for all through you!

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*

When Gabriel proclaimed unto thee: "Rejoice!" O Virgin, with his voice the Master of all became incarnate within thee, the holy Ark, as righteous David said; thou wast revealed more spacious than the heavens, having borne thy Creator! Glory to Him Who dwelt within thee! Glory to Him Who came forth from thee! Glory to Him Who delivered us through thy birthgiving![^42]

*After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns of the Martyrs, Tone 1:*

By the wounds of the holy ones which they suffered for Thy sake, be Thou entreated, O Lord, and heal all our sicknesses and passions, O Lover of mankind, we pray!

Martyrs of Christ, entreat God for us, we all pray, coming unto you in faith: for they pray for our salvation, they [f. 30vA] pour forth the grace of healings, as divine regiments of soldiers, guardians of the faith!

*Hymn for the Departed (Поко́инъ):*

Thou didst abolish the power of death, O Christ, and those who were in corruption die no more, but live in Thee; therefore, O Lord, give rest unto the souls of Thy servants, and rank them with Thy saints, by the prayers of the Theotokos, granting them Thy mercies!

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*

O only strong and fervent protectress of the human race, Virgin Theotokos: unceasingly pray with the Prophets and Martyrs, with the Hierarchs, Ascetics, and Venerable ones, unto God the Word Whom thou, O Virgin, didst bear beyond nature, to save all!

## ON SATURDAY: CANON TO THE HOLY MARTYRS, HIERARCHS, VENERABLE ONES, AND THE DEPARTED
*Composition of Saint Joseph.*[^43]

*Ode 1, Tone 1. Heirmos:*

*With a pillar of fire and a cloud Thou didst guide Israel as God, parting the sea and covering Pharaoh with his arms in the deep: let us sing a song of victory, for He is glorified!*

Being shielded with the buckler of piety, the divine passion-bearers hastened unto the combat and destroyed all the power of the enemy, singing a song of victory unto Christ Who strengthened them!

Ye shepherded the flock of God, O divine pastors, watering it with sacred words, driving away the savage wolves, and rejoicing ye dwell in the heavenly sheepfold, where the Chief Shepherd is!

[f. 30vB] Having deadened the passions of the flesh by fasting and sufferings, through divine nodding: pray Christ Who became poor for our sake ever to have compassion on us!

*Hymn for the Departed (Поко́инъ):*

Having become dead, Thou didst grant of Thy divine life and immortal life unto the dead; make those who have departed from corruptible life in faith partakers of Thy Kingdom, as Thou art compassionate and the only greatly merciful One!

*Theotokion:*

The women martyrs bound by the love of Christ and crowned by God, and all the venerable women, faithfully honor thee, O all-immaculate one and fair among women, rejoicing as unto the holy Queen!

### Another Canon for the Departed
*We sing it in order, and where there is no Menaion. Tone 1. Heirmos: "Thy victorious right hand...":*

Thou didst smash the gates of death and its bars by Thy death, O Immortal One; open the gates of immortality that are beyond understanding unto the departed, O Master, by the prayers of Thy passion-bearers!

That we might be accounted worthy of divine life, Thou didst descend unto death; and overthrowing its treasuries, Thou didst deliver us from thence: now grant rest unto the departed, O Giver of life!

*Glory...*

Taking upon Thyself my corruptible and dead darkness, Thou didst clothe it with incorruption, and didst raise it unto endless and blessed life, where do Thou give rest, as Thou art compassionate, unto those whom Thou hast received!

*Both now... Theotokion:*

Having given birth unto God the Word of God, let us, the faithful, hymn her [f. 31rA] for thus the pure one became the way of life unto the dead: let us glorify her as the God-receiver and Theotokos!

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*

*Let my heart be established in Thy will, O Christ God: Who didst establish the second heaven upon the waters, and didst found the earth upon the waters, O All-powerful One!*

Ye endured many torments and were accounted worthy of many blessings, O sacred multitude of martyrs; therefore by your prayers destroy the immense multitude of evils!

The hierarchs, being righteously clothed with grace and fair gladness, and the assembly of venerable fathers, became like unto the bodiless ministers!

Prophets of Christ, divine martyrs, choir of sacred women who suffered manfully and were glorified in fasting: by their prayers grant Thy mercies unto all, O Savior!

*Hymn for the Departed (Поко́инъ):*

O Christ, Who by Thy hand didst voluntarily fashion man from the dust of the earth: account Thy servants who have departed unto Thee in faith worthy of heavenly blessings!

*Theotokion:*

O unwedded Mother of God, offer the petitions of all unto God our Benefactor, Who was born from thy womb, that we may find perfect deliverance from evils!

*Another Canon [for the Departed]. Heirmos: Thou Who alone knowest the weakness of human...*

As Thou alone art good, as Thou alone art greatly merciful: give rest in the heavenly mansions unto those who have piously departed unto Thee [f. 31rB] where the all-joyful assembly of the martyrs is!

Thou alone wast revealed upon earth as sinless, O my Savior, Who takest away the sins of the world as Thou art merciful; therefore give rest unto the souls of those who have departed in faith, in the courts of Thy saints, O Lover of mankind!

*Glory...*

Having destroyed the power of death, Thou didst pour forth indestructible life unto all the faithful, O Lord; place therein those who have piously departed, overlooking their transgressions and forgiving their sins, O Lover of mankind!

*Both now... Theotokion:*

Without seed thou didst conceive, O pure one, the ever-existing Word Who came unto us in the flesh and destroyed the might of death, granting rest and eternal life unto the dead through His tender mercy!

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*

*I heard, O Lord, Thy report, and was afraid; I understood Thy works, cried the Prophet, and glorified Thy power, O Lover of mankind!*

The martyrs endured all manner of wounds, being noble in disposition, and like spotless lambs were brought unto Christ, Who was slain as the Life of all!

Being taught by the words of God, they delivered their souls from the bonds of the fierce one; therefore we honor these piously-minded ones!

Made strong by the divine Spirit, O divine fast-bearers, ye powerfully conquered the spirits of malice by grace, O venerable ones!

*Hymn for the Departed (Поко́инъ):*

Thou Who didst voluntarily die upon the Tree, O our Life: account those who have departed in faith worthy of eternal life, O Lover of mankind!

*Theotokion:*

They were opened [f. 31vA] and the choir of women opened unto the Lord, suffering manfully; nor were the holy women overcome by bodily pleasures, having thee as their helper, O most pure one!

*Another Canon [for the Departed]. Heirmos: The mountain of grace...*

Having put Hades to death by Thine unconquerable power, Thou wast numbered among the dead, Who alone art free, O Christ: by the entreaties of the holy martyrs, set free the souls of those who piously departed unto Thee from condemnation!

Being the Master and Foreseer of all, Who didst give Thyself as the price and ransom of the slaughter of Adam: therefore we pray Thee by Thy compassions, give rest unto the departed, granting remission of their sins!

*Glory...*

Thou didst accept burial in the tomb, O my Savior, and as God Thou didst raise the dead who were condemned to dwell in tombs; now account the departed worthy of eternal life, as Thou alone art the Lover of mankind!

*Both now... Theotokion:*

The human race was saved through thy birthgiving, for thou didst bear for us the resurrected Life, the Destroyer of death, Who made an ascent unto life, O Theotokos, all-immaculate Sovereign Lady!

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*

*Make the bright and ever-existing Light to shine forth upon us who rise early at dawn unto the judgments of Thy commandments: for Thou art the Lover of mankind, O Christ our God!*

Being girded with piety, the martyrs were revealed unwounded by the arrows of the adversary; and becoming victorious by grace, ye received crowns!

[f. 31vB] Anointing His priests with divine ointment, O Lord, they shepherded the multitude of the faithful in holiness and guided them unto the heavenly sheepfold!

Most sacred hieromartyrs and all venerable ones: living in the fear of the Spirit and becoming partakers of the Kingdom, ye are divinely glorified!

*Hymn for the Departed (Поко́инъ):*

Account those who have now departed by Thy command, O Master Lord, worthy of Thy Kingdom with the saints, overlooking all their former transgressions!

The women who found glory through fasting and suffering, O most pure one, having thee as their protectress, destroyed the bold dominion of the enemy!

*Another Canon [for the Departed]. Heirmos: O Thou Who didst enlighten the ends of...*

Thou didst accept death and blunt the sting of death; therefore give rest unto those whom Thou hast received, O Giver of life, by the entreaties of the martyrs!

Thou Who didst free mankind from mortality: place the souls of those who have departed in faith in the courts of Thy saints, whence all sorrow hath fled and gladness abides!

*Glory...*

As Paradise was opened unto him who was hung with Thee: receive now the souls of those who have departed unto Thee in faith, O Master, granting that they may dwell in the Church of the firstborn!

*Both now... Theotokion:*

Delivering those who hold fast their hope in thee: guide them quietly unto the haven of divine will by thy maternal boldness toward thy Son, O Bride of God!

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*

[f. 32rA] *Imitating the Prophet Jonah, I cry: Deliver my life from corruption, O Good One, and save me, O Savior of the world, who cry: Glory to Thee!*

Being subjected to delay by the infliction of many wounds, ye inherited true life together, praying that we all may be saved, O holy martyrs!

Ye were recognized upon earth as radiant morning stars, illuminating the faithful with the light of piety, O glorious warriors of Christ and all-wise hierarchs!

Ye were revealed as strangers upon earth and citizens of heaven, O God-bearing ascetics, having put to death the wisdom of the flesh through abstinence and humility!

*Hymn for the Departed (Поко́инъ):*

Show those whom Thou hast translated in faith to be partakers of Thine unwaning light and true delight, O Lover of mankind, and number them with the choirs of the saints!

*Theotokion:*

Those women who suffered valiantly and strove fervently were brought unto Christ through thee, O all-immaculate and all-hymned Mother of God, the Queen of glorious deeds!

*Another Canon [for the Departed]. Heirmos: The lowest abyss hath compassed us about, and...*

As Thou art merciful, grant unto the departed remission of sins and bestow eternal delight, where the brightness of Thy countenance shines and illuminates Thy passion-bearers!

With the blood that flowed from Thy side Thou didst redeem the world; therefore deliver those who have fallen asleep in faith from corruptible passions, O Christ, for Thou didst give Thyself as a ransom for all!

*Glory...*

Thou Who in the beginning didst fashion me with Thine all-pure hands [f. 32rB] and didst bestow a spirit, and when I had fallen grievously unto the earth didst renew me most beautifully: now do Thou Thyself give rest unto the souls of the departed!

*Both now... Theotokion:*

We hymn thee, O pure one clad with glory, through whom the unwaning Sun of Righteousness shone forth unto us who sit in darkness and the shadow of death: for thou wast the Mediatress of our salvation!

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*

*The fire did not touch nor harm Thy children in the furnace, O Savior; then the three sang as with one mouth, and blessed, saying: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!*

Tried as gold in the fire by every torment, O martyrs, ye were manifestly revealed more radiant than any gold by divine grace, being preserved in the heavenly treasuries!

Being priests and divine ministers, all ye holy hierarchs offered unbloody sacrifices unto God, and shepherded the people where the Chief Shepherd is magnified!

Subduing the passions of the flesh and clad with dispassion as with strength, the venerable ones were revealed as companions of the Angels; by their prayers, O Christ, deliver us from assaults!

*Hymn for the Departed (Поко́инъ):*

Where the mystical food is, and where the light of Thy countenance shines, O Christ: settle those who have departed from among us in faith, O Benefactor, that they may piously glorify Thy goodness!

*Theotokion:*

Thee, O holy, most pure one, do all the holy women [f. 32vA] both women and the beauty of men, dancing in chorus with the Angels, joyfully praise God Who was born in the flesh of thee out of great loving-kindness!

*Another Canon [for the Departed]. Heirmos: Thee, O Mother of God, we faithful perceive...*

Grant unto those who have departed unto Thee to be illuminated with the rays of Thine all-pure glory, O Christ, that they may cry unto Thee without doubt: Blessed art Thou, O God praised by the fathers!

Thou didst truly become Adam, O Creator of Adam, and didst abolish the debt of Adam, therefore we pray Thee: grant rest unto the departed, crying unto Thee, O Christ, for Thou alone art greatly merciful!

*Glory...*

Thou Who alone knowest our natural weakness, O Christ God, good and merciful: place the departed in Thy Kingdom, where the unwaning light of Thy countenance shines, O Christ: praised by the fathers, O God highly exalted!

*Both now... Theotokion:*

The shadow of the Law and the ancient riddles passed away through thy birthgiving, O Mother of God, for thou didst cause the light of divine grace to shine forth unto us, whereby we were delivered from the ancient things, hymning God Who is highly exalted!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*

*Him before Whom Angels and all the hosts tremble as their Creator and Lord: priests, hymn Him; children, glorify Him; people, bless and highly exalt Him unto all ages!*

All the martyrs passed through the herb-potions unharmed, and steadfastly endured the boiling caldrons, being gloriously refreshed by the fire of the divine Spirit! [f. 32vB] pre-eminently of the Spirit!

Thou didst give unto Thy prophets to foresee things far off, and didst sacredly make wise Thy hierarchs; by their prayers, O Christ God, enlighten the hearts of those who faithfully hymn Thee!

Having crucified yourselves unto the world by fastings, ye truly inherited transcendent life, even as from the ages all who have pleased God have done, ever and righteously!

*Hymn for the Departed (Поко́инъ):*

Thou Who didst fashion man from the dust in a manner worthy of God: as Thou art good, account the faithful whom Thou hast translated from earth worthy of the delight of Paradise, overlooking all their transgressions!

*Theotokion:*

Knowing thee to be the beauty and undefiled among women, O pure Virgin, the women who suffered offered their prayers through thee unto God, meeting all the needs of thy servants!

*Another Canon [for the Departed]. Heirmos: The children in the furnace...*

Having justified them by faith, O Savior, by the prayers of the passion-bearers, show those whom Thou hast translated to be of the right hand, singing: Hymn the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and highly exalt Him unto all ages!

Having washed away every defilement of Thy departed servants with the dew of Thy love for mankind, grant them to praise Thee worthily, singing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, hymn and highly exalt Him unto all ages!

Thou Who hast dominion over death and life, and between all things: deign that those who have fallen asleep in faith may obtain Thy calling, crying: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, hymn and highly exalt Him unto all ages!

*Theotokion:*

Thou wast the Mediatress of salvation unto us, O all-immaculate one...

## ON SATURDAY EVENING, AT LITTLE VESPERS, AT "LORD, I HAVE CRIED"

[f. 35rA] *Resurrectional Stichera, on 4, Tone 2:*[^44]

Unto the pre-eternal Word of God born of the Father, Who was incarnate of the Virgin Mary, come, let us bow down: for having endured crucifixion, He was committed unto burial as He Himself willed; and He rose from the dead, and saved me, wandering man!

Christ our Savior, being nailed upon the Cross, tore up the handwriting against us, and abolished the dominion of death: we bow down before His third-day resurrection!

With the Archangels let us hymn the resurrection of Christ: for He is the Redeemer and Savior of our souls, and in fearful glory and mighty power He comes again to judge the world which He created!

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*

Beholding the wonders of the great mystery, I proclaim the Godhead; beholding the passions, I deny not the humanity. For Emmanuel opened the gates of nature as man, but as God He unloosed not the bars of virginity [f. 35rB] but He passed through in like manner as He was formed, even as He entered through hearing; and in like manner He was born as He was conceived: impassibly He entered, and ineffably He came forth, according to the Prophet who said: "This gate shall be shut, and no man shall pass through it, save only the Lord God of Israel, Who hath great mercy!"

### AT THE APOSTICHA

*Resurrectional Stichera, Tone 2:*

Thy resurrection, O Christ Savior, enlightened the whole universe and recalled Thine own creation: O All-powerful Lord, glory to Thee!

*Other Stichera to the Theotokos, Tone 2.*

*Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Егда́ ѡ҆ дре́ва):*

*Verse: Hear, O daughter, and see, and incline thine ear.*

The joy of all who sorrow, protectress of the wronged, feeder of the hungry, consolation of travelers, haven of the tempest-tossed, visitor of the sick, shelter and defense of the afflicted, and staff of the blind: thou art all these, O Mother of the Most High God, most pure one; hasten, we pray thee, to save thy servants! [f. 35vA] shelter and defense of the afflicted, and staff of the blind: thou art all these, O Mother of the Most High God, most pure one; hasten, we pray thee, to save thy servants!

*Verse: The rich among the people shall entreat thy countenance.*

No other refuge unto God and the Good One have we acquired, save thee, O Virgin, Bride of God: cast us not away from thy protection, nor put us to shame who run with love unto thy patronage, O Mother of God; therefore hasten to our aid, and grant relief unto us, O Savior!

*Verse: I will remember thy name in every generation and generation.*

The fear of many-formed temptations and dire distresses now tempest-toss me, and the deep [f. 35vB] of despair drowns me; the winter of my transgressions grievously troubles me: anticipate and deliver me who am tempest-tossed, O only calm of the faithful, and lead me up unto the haven of the high divine calling!

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*

Thou prayest for all, O Good One, who run with faith unto thy mighty protection: for we sinners have no other refuge unto God, in perils and sorrows an ever-present deliverance, laden with many sins, O Mother of the Most High God; therefore we fall down before thee: deliver thy servants from every distress![^45]

Then, "Now lettest Thou depart": Trisagion. Troparion: "When Thou didst descend unto death..." Theotokion: "All beyond comprehension..." And the dismissal. [f. 33rA] all-immaculate one, and abiding in brightness unto endless ages: therefore, O pure Virgin, do we ever bless and highly exalt all Thy works unto all ages!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*

*The life-receiving, ever-flowing fountain, the radiant, all-golden lampstand, the animate Church, the all-pure tabernacle more spacious than heaven and earth: as the Theotokos, let us, the faithful, magnify!*

Let us honor the sacred roots of the sacred martyrs, rejoicing: their sufferings and wounds, nailings and banishments, and blessed slaughter, whereby they were revealed as heirs of Christ!

As priests of God, the divine servants clothed themselves in righteousness, living ever in holiness; having finished their course in the midst of torments, they rejoice, magnifying Christ!

Having become the divine lips of the Lord, all the Prophets pre-announced His light unto all; with them now rejoice also the women who struggled valiantly and pleased God by fasting!

*Hymn for the Departed (Поко́инъ):*

O Power that rulest over all: show those whom Thou hast translated from earth to be partakers of Thy Kingdom with Thy saints, and in Thine exceeding goodness overlook the deeds committed by them, O God of all!

O thou who didst bear the natural and timeless Light: loose all my temporal transgressions by thy prayers, and enlighten my mind that is ever darkened by slothfulness, that I may hymn thee and faithfully magnify thee!

[f. 33rB] *Another Canon [for the Departed]. Heirmos: The image of the pure...*

Spare Thine own creation, O God, as Thou art the Lover of mankind and merciful, and give rest unto all Thy servants where all the martyrs rejoice: those who have departed from temporal things in faith, O greatly merciful One!

Possessing an abyss of mercy that overflows the transgressions of Thy servants: receive those whom Thou hast chosen, O Lover of mankind, and give them rest in the bosom of Abraham, and show them in Thy light with Lazarus!

Having become the Redeemer and Savior of the human race by reason of the Crucifixion: as the Benefactor, account those who have now departed from among us worthy of divine delight, and of incorruptible life, and gladness, and brightness!

*Theotokion:*

O the wonder of thy wonders that are beyond understanding! For thou alone, O Virgin, hast given all under the sun to understand the newest wonder, O most pure one, of thine incomprehensible birthgiving; therefore we all magnify thee!

# AT THE PRAISES: STICHERA
*Martyrika, Tone 1:*

Passion-bearers of Christ, come, all ye people, let us honor them with spiritual songs and hymns: the luminaries of the world and preachers of the faith, the ever-flowing fountains from which healings pour forth unto the faithful! By their prayers, O Christ our God, grant peace unto Thy world, and great mercy unto our souls!
