These warriors of the great King opposed the decrees of the torturers, manfully disregarding torments, and trampled down all deceit: worthily were [f. 33vA] they ask of the Savior peace, and great mercy unto our souls!

O all-lauded martyrs, neither tribulation, nor distress, nor famine, nor persecution, nor wounds, nor rage of wild beasts, nor sword, nor threatening fire were able to separate you from God; but rather by the love which ye had toward Him, as though contesting in bodies not your own, ye forgot nature and despised death! Therefore ye worthily received the reward of your labors, having become heirs of the Kingdom of Heaven: pray Christ for our souls!

All-lauded martyrs in the Lord: for ye contested with a good contest; ye opposed kings and conquered torturers; ye feared not fire nor sword, nor savage wild beasts that devoured your bodies! Sending up hymnody unto Christ with the Angels, ye received crowns from heaven: entreat that great mercy may be granted unto us!

*Hymn for the Departed (Поко́инъ):*

By Thy word, O my Savior, Thou dost reveal that Thou art the Resurrection of all; by a word, O Word, Thou didst raise Lazarus from the dead! Then the dead arose from the tombs, and the gates of Hades were shattered; then death appeared unto men as sleep! But Thou Who camest for the salvation of Thine own creation and not for condemnation: give rest unto those whom Thou hast chosen, for Thou art the Lover of mankind!

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*

Rejoice on our behalf, O holy Virgin Theotokos, pure vessel of the whole universe: [f. 33vB] unquenchable lampstand, dwelling-place of the Uncontainable One, indestructible Church: Rejoice, from whom was born the Lamb of God, Who takes away the sins of the whole world!

### AT THE APOSTICHA

*Stichera for the Departed, Tone 1.*

*Podoben: "O all-lauded martyrs" (Прехвальніи мꙋнцы):*

*Composition of Saint Theophanes.*

Unto Thee, O Savior, we pray: account the departed worthy of Thy sweet communion, and settle them in the mansions of the venerable ones, with Thy saints and in the heavenly habitations, in Thy tender mercy overlooking their iniquities and granting them rest!

*Verse: Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen and taken to Thyself, O Lord.*

Higher than visible things are Thy promises, O Savior, which eye hath not seen, and ear hath not heard, neither have entered into the heart of man; account the departed unto Thee worthy to obtain Thy sweet communion, and grant them rest!

*Verse: Their souls shall dwell among good things.*

Rejoicing in Thy Cross, and hoping in Thy Cross, Thy servants have departed unto Thee, O Lover of mankind: grant them now forgiveness of their transgressions through Thy Cross and the blood poured out for the life of the world, in Thy loving-kindness forgiving their sins and enlightening them with the light of Thy countenance!

*Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion:*

Entreat Christ, Whom thou didst bear, O Virgin Mother, to grant forgiveness of sins unto all who faithfully hymn thee!

# TONE 2: SATURDAY VESPERS, SUNDAY MATINS, AND WEEKDAY OFFICES

## ON SATURDAY EVENING, AT GREAT VESPERS, AT "LORD, I HAVE CRIED"

[f. 36rA] *Resurrectional Stichera, Tone 2:*[^46]

*Composition of Saint John of Damascus.*

Unto the pre-eternal Word of God born of the Father, Who was incarnate of the Virgin Mary, come, let us bow down: for having endured crucifixion, He was committed unto burial as He Himself willed; and He rose from the dead, and saved me, wandering man!

Christ our Savior, being nailed upon the Cross, tore up the handwriting against us, and abolished the dominion of death: we bow down before His third-day resurrection!

With the Archangels let us hymn the resurrection of Christ: for He is the Redeemer and Savior of our souls, and in fearful glory and mighty power He comes again to judge the world which He created!

*Other Eastern Stichera. Composition of Anatolius, Patriarch of Constantinople. Tone 2:*

Thee Who wast crucified and buried, the Angel proclaimed, O Master, and said [f. 36rB] unto the women: "Come and see where the Lord lay! For He is risen as He said, for He is all-powerful!" Therefore we bow down before Thee, the only Immortal One: O Giver of life, Christ, have mercy on us!

By Thy Cross Thou didst abolish the curse of the tree; by Thy burial Thou didst put to death the dominion of death; and by Thy resurrection Thou didst enlighten the human race: therefore we cry unto Thee: O Benefactor, Christ our God, glory to Thee!

The guards were terrified, O Lord, and the gates of death and the gatekeepers of Hades were afraid when they beheld Thee: for Thou didst shatter the brazen gates and didst crush the iron bars, and didst lead us forth from darkness and the shadow of death, and didst break our bonds asunder! Singing a song of victory, we cry: [f. 36vA] enter into the house of the Lord, and let us fall down, saying: Thou Who wast crucified upon the Tree, and didst rise from the dead, and art in the bosom of the Father: cleanse our sins!

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion (Dogmatikon):*

The shadow of the Law passed away when grace arrived: for as the bush burned with fire and was not consumed, so as a Virgin thou didst give birth, and a Virgin thou didst remain; instead of a pillar of fire, the Sun of Righteousness hath shone forth; instead of Moses, Christ, the Salvation of our souls![^47]

### AT THE APOSTICHA

*Resurrectional Stichera, Tone 2:*

Thy resurrection, O Christ Savior, enlightened the whole universe and recalled Thine own creation: O All-powerful Lord, glory to Thee!

*Other Stichera in Alphabetical Order:*

*Verse: The Lord is King, He is robed in majesty.*

By the Tree, O Savior, Thou didst abolish the curse of the tree; the dominion of death Thou didst put to death by Thy burial, and Thou didst enlighten our race by Thy resurrection: therefore we cry unto Thee: O Giver of life, Christ our God, glory to Thee!

*Verse: For He hath established the world, so that it cannot be moved.*

Thou wast seen nailed upon the Cross, O Christ, reforming the beauty of creation; the soldiers indeed showed cruelty, piercing Thy ribs with a spear, and the Jews asked to seal the tomb, not knowing Thy power: but in Thy tender mercy Thou didst accept burial, and on the third day Thou didst rise: [f. 36vB] O Lord, glory to Thee!

*Verse: Holiness becomes Thy house, O Lord, unto length of days.*

O Christ, Giver of life, Thou didst voluntarily endure passion for the sake of the dead; and descending into Hades as Mighty, Thou didst snatch away those who were awaiting Thy coming there, as from a mighty beast, and didst grant them to dwell in Paradise instead of Hades: therefore grant unto us also who glorify Thy third-day resurrection cleansing of sins and great mercy!

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*

O new wonder, greater than all ancient wonders! For who hath known a Mother to give birth without a man, and to carry in her arms Him Who contains all creation? Born is the Word of God, Whom as an infant, O most pure one, thou didst bear in thine arms, and having maternal boldness toward Him, unceasingly pray for those who honor thee, to have compassion and save our souls!

*Troparion, Tone 2:*

When Thou didst descend unto death, O Life Immortal, then didst Thou slay Hades with the brightness of Thy Godhead; and when Thou didst raise the dead from the nethermost parts, all the heavenly powers cried aloud: O Giver of life, Christ our God, glory to Thee!

*Theotokion:*

All beyond comprehension, all all-glorious are thy mysteries, O Theotokos: sealed in purity and preserved in virginity, thou wast known to be a true Mother, having given birth unto the true God; pray Him that our souls may be saved!

# ON SUNDAY AT THE MIDNIGHT OFFICE, TRIADICAL CANON
[f. 37rA] *Composition of Metrophanes.*[^48]

*Ode 1, Tone 2. Heirmos:*

*He Who submerged of old in the deep: let us hymn the three-personed, single-principled essence of the Godhead, singing: Possessing essentially an inexhaustible abyss of mercy: have compassion and save those who bow down before Thee, as Thou art the Lover of mankind!*

Being the cause, the source and root of the Father in the Son and Thy Holy Spirit, of the consubstantial Godhead: enlighten my soul with the three-sunned Light, and illuminate me by communion!

Divinely granting me brightness, O three-radiant Unity, single in principle: heal the passions in the wounds of my sins by Thy luminous rays, and by sweet communions make me partaker of Thine unapproachable glory, O animate womb and tabernacle!

*Theotokion:*

The stream of actions of our nature, having suffered unworthily and slipped into corruption, O most pure Virgin: the Lord the Word, being incarnate from thy womb, lovingly recalled and mystically taught the all-bright Godhead!

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*

*Establish me upon the rock of faith: the Godhead, first principle of nature, glorifying Thee with equal honor in three Persons; for Thou, proceeding as Life from Life, art without corruption our only God, and none is holy save Thee, O Lord!*

Thou hast not instructed the bodiless ranks [f. 37rB] to praise Thy goodness, O Trinity, undivided Monarchy, unceasingly unto Thee; but accept now also the praise from our clay lips!

Establish upon the rock of faith, and broaden in the ocean of Thy love, the heart and mind of Thy servants, O three-sunned Unity: for Thou art our God, hoping in Whom we are not put to shame!

*Theotokion:*

He Who constituted the substance of creation before all things: united Himself unto thy womb through unfeigned goodness, O Sovereign Lady; and He shone forth unto all in three-sunned light, of one Godhead and Dominion!

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 2.*

*Podoben: "Seeking the highest" (Вы́шнихъ и҆щѧ):*

O Holy Trinity, have mercy on that which Thou hast created, and deliver us from fire and every condemnation, for Thou canst do all things, as Thou art the compassionate and greatly merciful God; therefore we fall down before Thee, crying: We have sinned, forgive, O Lover of mankind!

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*

Thy servants are filled with many wounds, wounded by invisible arrows, and lying upon the bed of despair we cry unto thee, O Sovereign Lady, praying unceasingly on our behalf, who run unto thee in faith!

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*

*I hymn Thee, having heard, O Lord, Thy report... to understand the mystical ranks: even as the bodiless Angels cry unto Thee with fear, O unoriginate Trinity: so we also with clay tongues cry unto Thee: Creator of creation...*

[f. 37vA] ...beholding my heavenly weakness, O Almighty One: therefore have compassion on Thy servant, and lead me back unto better life!

Of the primordial Unity, let us praise the unconfused three Persons, having individual hypostases, yet united and undivided in counsel, in glory, and in Godhead!

*Theotokion:*

The Creator found thee alone from the ages as a pure and all-immaculate temple, O Virgin Theotokos; dwelling in thee, He formed human nature, as He is the Lover of mankind!

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*

*Enlightenment of those lying in darkness: as the greatness of Thy providence over all things, extending rays of salvation unto me, O King of peace: preserve us in Thy faith, for Thou art the Life and Peace of all!*

Appearing in the bush unto Moses in a fiery vision, the Word of the Father was named an Angel, foreseeing Thy coming; whereby Thou didst clearly illuminate unto all the dominion of the one Godhead in three Persons!

Not altering the natural and co-eternal glory, O single Holy Trinity: grant unto those who hymn Thee with Orthodox faith ever to behold Thy glory, unoriginate and single, in three suns!

*Theotokion:*

Being one by nature, yet tried in all things: calling unto the union of the one Dominion

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*

*Held fast in the abyss of sin, O Creator of mercy, have mercy: Thou Who art the calm of the faithful, O God of three suns: save us from innumerable transgressions and from passions!*

By the ineffable deep of goodness, by the uncontainable of Thy brightness and sent Godhead: grant me the light-giving ray!

*Theotokion:*

Ineffably, O Virgin, the Most High became man incorruptibly: clothed in the garment of man, illuminate me with three-sunned light!

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 2.*

*Podoben: "Seeking the highest" (Вы́шнихъ и҆щѧ):*

O Christ God, only Most Good, Who didst pour out Thy blood for our sake, being hung upon the Cross by the counsel of Thy Father and the Spirit: therefore we cry aloud: Remember Thy flock, O Lover of mankind!

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*

O pure one, have mercy on thy servants, and deliver from fire and every torment those who cry day and night unto thy Son, O most pure one: despise not thy flock, by thy prayers, O Mother of Christ!

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*

*Concerning the golden image on the plain of Dura: The Prophets establish that the angelic Godhead is unchanging, O Lord Who alone art immutable and in three Persons: show my heart also ever unchanging, that I may fervently glorify Thee and piously hymn Thee!*

[f. 38rA] The noetic ranks of bodiless essences are illuminated by Thy rays, O God of single dominion and three suns, being by position secondary lights; show them forth as light, as Thou art the ever-living Giver of light!

Illuminated by three-radiant rays, O Most Holy Trinity, in one dominion preserve Thy singers from adverse assaults, that we may unceasingly glorify Thee: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, in one Godhead!

*Theotokion:*

Restoring us and raising us up unto heavenly things without departure: He Who out of ineffable love for mankind became man from the Virgin's womb loved thee, and deified man, and sits with the Father upon the throne of glory!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*

*In the likeness of gold: O ever-existing Trinity, co-eternal, unoriginate, sole ruler, unchanging unto ages: apart from Thy light-bearers, destroy all the evil assaults of adversaries and disturbances among men; keep Thy servants unharmed ever, O Lord of all!*

Ever-existing and Almighty, uncircumscribed, three-sunned Monarchy, Who didst constitute the world and dost preserve it by Thy power: grant unto the all-perfect, O All-powerful One, to hymn and glorify Thee with the angelic choirs unto all ages! [f. 38rB] of falsehood, and of the divine natural and unchanging nature: Thou didst assume human nature and didst teach us to honor the Trinity as Dominion unto all ages!

Directing righteousness and wisdom: by Thy standings, therefore, singing unto God, and radiant, O most pure one: bless all ye works, hymn and highly exalt Him unto all ages!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*

*He Who before the sun was God, the Luminary... of the unoriginate Light: by His radiance the Son, Light and natural, shone forth with light; ineffably born of the earth, together appearing without departure...*

Shine forth in Orthodox hearts the light of the Godhead; rising, grant understanding, and give understanding to comprehend and behold the good and perfect hymnody, to magnify and glorify Thee!

O Trinity uncircumscribed in nature... with unsearchable joy, Who art our Creator before creation: have compassion on Thy servants! [f. 38vA] Thee: and [preserve] Thy flock, [by the prayers of the Mother of] God.[^49]

*Trisagion. After the Six Psalms:*

*God is the Lord, and hath appeared unto us: in the same Tone, Troparion: Resurrectional:*

*Glory: Both now:*

*Beyond comprehension. Then, the Kathisma of the Psalter.*

*Then, the Sessional Hymns.*

*Tone 2.*

The noble Joseph, having taken down Thine immaculate Body from the Tree: wrapped It in pure linen, and with spices, enclosed It in a new tomb and laid It to rest; but on the third day Thou didst arise, O Lord, granting great mercy unto the world. *Glory:*

When the stone was sealed at the sepulchre by the Jews: the Stone of faith, Thou didst arise, being truly existent; Thou hast granted unto all: glory to Thee! *Both now: Theotokion:*

Thou art highly glorified, O Theotokos; we hymn thee, for by the Cross of thy Son, Hades was overthrown, and death was put to death; we who were dead have arisen, and have been deemed worthy of life; we have received Paradise, the ancient delight. Therefore, giving thanks, we cry aloud unto thee: Rejoice, O Virgin full of grace, the Lord is with thee!

*After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns to the Myrrh-bearers. Tone 2:*

The angel stood by, crying aloud at the sepulchre: "[What is proper unto the dead, even myrrh, is not fitting for Him; for Christ was shown to be foreign to corruption.]" *Glory: "Nay, cry aloud: [The Lord is risen, granting great mercy unto the world!]"*

[f. 38vB] The company of Thy disciples, together with the Myrrh-bearing women, rejoices in concord: for we celebrate a common feast with them, unto the glory and honor of Thy Resurrection. And through them, O Lord, Lover of mankind, grant Thou great mercy unto Thy people.

*Both now. Theotokion:*

The laws of nature were concealed by thy divine childbearing; thou didst unite virginity with childbirth. For thou alone didst bear Him Who was timelessly begotten before thee. Therefore, O Theotokos, we magnify thee.

*Hypakoe, Tone 2:*

Having gone unto the sepulchre after the Passion to anoint Thy Body, O Christ God, the women beheld angels in the sepulchre and were dismayed; for they heard a voice from them: "The Lord is risen, granting great mercy unto the world!"

*The Gradual Hymns (Anabathmoi), Tone 2.*

*Antiphon 1:*

Unto heaven do I raise the eyes of my heart, unto Thee, O Savior: save Thou me by Thine illumination.

Have mercy upon us who have sinned greatly against Thee, at every hour, O my Christ; and give me a pattern of repentance unto Thee before the end.

*Glory: Both now:*

Unto the Holy Spirit it belongs to reign, to sanctify, and to animate creation: for He is God, consubstantial with the Father and the Word.

*Antiphon 2:*

Except [the Lord had been among us, who could have been preserved whole from the enemy] and man-slayer together?

[Deliver not Thy servant, O Savior, unto their teeth: for like unto a lion my foes rise up against me...]

[f. 39rA] [...against me] my foes rise up.

Unto the Holy Spirit belong dominion and honor:[^50] for all created things, as He is God, He by His power preserves from the Father, through the Son.

*Antiphon 3:*

They that trust in the Lord are become like unto the holy mount: which can by no means be shaken by the assaults of the enemy.

Let not them that live godly stretch forth their hands unto iniquity: for Christ will not leave His rod upon His inheritance.

Unto the Holy Spirit every wisdom pours forth; from Him comes grace unto the Apostles, and by their suffering the Martyrs are crowned, and the Prophets behold.

*Prokeimenon, Tone 2:*

Arise, O Lord my God, in the commandment which Thou hast commanded: and the congregation of the people shall compass Thee. *Verse: O Lord my God, in Thee have I put my trust. Then: Let every breath. The Gospel, and the rest in order.*

*THE RESURRECTIONAL CANON*[^51]

*Ode 1. Tone 2. Heirmos:*

*The all-conquering power submerged the entire Pharaonic cavalry in the deep of old; and the incarnate Word abolished the prevailing sin, the all-glorious Lord: for He is gloriously glorified.*

The Prince of this world, O Good One, unto whom we had enrolled ourselves, having disobeyed Thy commandments, was condemned by Thy Cross; for rushing upon Thee as mortal, [he was cast down by the dominion of Thy power, and his weakness was reproved.]

[f. 39rB] The Deliverer of mankind, and the Author of incorruptible life: Thou hast come into the world. By Thy Resurrection Thou didst tear asunder the swaddling bands of death, which all of us hymn in doxology: for He is gloriously glorified.

*Theotokion:*

Having appeared higher than all visible and invisible creation, O pure and ever-Virgin: for thou didst bear the Creator, as He well-pleased, to become incarnate in thy womb. Him do thou beseech with boldness, to save our souls.

*Another Canon, Cross-Resurrectional.*

*Ode 1. Tone 2. Heirmos:*

*Having traversed an untrodden, uncustomary, waterless sea path, the chosen Israel cried aloud: "Let us sing unto the Lord, for He is gloriously glorified!"*

Thou hast become the strength of the infirm, the Resurrection of the fallen, and incorruption for the dead, O Christ God, who didst honor Thy passion: for He is glorified.

[Having raised up] the fallen image, [O Creator, and restored that which was] broken: [O God and greatly merciful, Thou wast made manifest unto all:] for He is glorified.

The angelic [ranks marvelled at thy childbearing, which is] beyond [nature: for thou didst give birth unto God and the Lord.]

*[Another: Heirmos...]*

[f. 39vA] ...obtain: for thy Son is slaughtered as a Lamb for all.

We all cry aloud unto thee, O true Mother of God: deliver thy servants who have provoked God to wrath; for thou alone hast boldness before the Son.

*Kontakion. Tone 2:*[^52]

Thou didst arise from the tomb, O all-powerful Savior: and Hades, beholding this wonder, was dismayed; and the dead arose. And creation, beholding it, rejoices with Thee; and Adam exults together with us. And the world, O my Savior, unceasingly hymns Thee.

*IKOS:*

Thou art the Light of the darkened, Thou art the Resurrection of all, and the Life of men: and Thou didst raise all up with Thyself. Thou didst overthrow the power of death, O Savior, and didst shatter the gates of Hades, O Word; and the dead, beholding this wonder, were astonished, and all creation together rejoices in Thy Resurrection, O Lover of mankind. Therefore, we all glorify and hymn Thy condescension. And the world, O my Savior, unceasingly hymns Thee.

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*

*The god-opposing decree of the lawless tyrant raised a high flame. But Christ spread a spiritual dew upon the pious children: Blessed and highly glorified is the God of our fathers.*

[The Master did not] endure to behold man tormented by sins: but [having come,] Thou didst save [him] by Thy Blood; [together with him we praise and glorify the God of our fathers.]

[f. 39vB] The garment of vengeance: the gatekeepers of Hades shuddered at the servant of the senseless tyrant, for Thou didst come to slay him: Blessed and highly glorified is the God of our fathers.

*Theotokion:*

We know thee to be holier than the holy, for thou alone didst bear the immutable God, O undefiled Virgin, unwedded Mother: for unto all the faithful thou hast poured forth incorruption by thy divine childbirth.

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*

*The all-wise youths were revealed as orators of old; for from a god-inspired soul they theologized, singing: "O God of our fathers, transcendent in divinity, blessed art Thou!"*

He judged of old the disobedience of our forefather in Eden: but He was willingly judged, loosing the transgressions of the transgressor: O God of our fathers, transcendent in divinity, blessed art Thou!

Thou didst save him who was wounded by the tongue through the envy of the man-slayer, by voluntary biting in Eden: for by Thy voluntary passion Thou didst heal him: O God of our fathers, transcendent in divinity, blessed art Thou!

*Theotokion:*

Walking in the shadow of death, Thou hast called me unto the light: having encompassed dark-visaged Hades with the radiance of divinity: O God of our fathers, transcendent in divinity, blessed art Thou!

*Another: The same Heirmos:*

Jacob beheld in the night, as in an enigma, God incarnate: and from thee He appeared in brightness unto them that sing: "O God of our fathers, transcendent in divinity, blessed art Thou!"

[f. 40rA] [He united Himself] unto men, O pure one: O God of our fathers, transcendent in divinity, blessed art Thou!

Abominable is he who preaches Thee not as the Son of the Father and the Virgin, having sung away the Greeks, crying with unhesitating faith and tongue: "O God of our fathers, transcendent in divinity, blessed art Thou!"

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*[^53]

*The fiery furnace in Babylon once divided its operation by the divine decree: burning the Chaldeans, yet cooling the faithful as they sang: "Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!"*

Beholding the garment of Thy flesh reddened with blood, O Christ, the angelic ranks marveled with trembling at Thy great longsuffering, crying: "Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!"

Thou hast clothed my mortal nature in immortality by Thy Resurrection, O Compassionate One; therefore, rejoicing, Thy redeemed people sing in thanksgiving, O Christ, crying: "Death hath been swallowed up in victory!"

*Theotokion:*

Having conceived in thy womb without seed the inseparable Father, an impossible bridal chamber, thou didst bear ineffably, O most pure Mother of God; therefore we hymn thee as the salvation of us all.

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*

*The thrice-rich youths did not bow down unto the golden image, beholding the unchangeable living image of God; in the midst of the flames, singing together: "Let all creation praise the Lord, and supreme exalt Him unto all ages!"*

[f. 40rB] [He] was seen nailed upon the Cross, He Who is rich in mercy; He was willingly buried, and on the third day He arose; and Thou hast delivered all earthly beings, O Lover of mankind, who sing in faith: "Let all creation praise the Lord, and supreme exalt Him unto all ages!"

*Theotokion:*

Having descended into the nethermost parts, O Word of God, to deliver from corruption man whom Thou didst fashion, O Christ, by Thy divine power, and having made him incorruptible, Thou didst make him a partaker of Thine ever-existing glory: "Let all creation praise the Lord, and supreme exalt Him unto all ages!"

*Another: The same Heirmos:*

He was seen upon the earth through thee, and lived among men, He Who is ineffable in goodness and power; unto Whom all of us the faithful sing, crying: "Let all creation praise the Lord, and supreme exalt Him unto all ages!"

Truly preaching thee as pure, we glorify thee, O Theotokos; for thou alone didst bear the Incarnate One of the Trinity; unto Whom with the Father and the Spirit we all sing: "Let all creation praise the Lord, and supreme exalt Him unto all ages!"

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*

*The Lord, Who is co-unoriginate with the Father, having become incarnate from the Virgin, hath appeared unto us: to enlighten the darkened, and to gather together the dispersed; therefore the all-hymned Theotokos do we magnify.*

As in Paradise the thrice-blessed Tree was planted upon the Cross, O Savior: the fruit of Thy communion [f. 40vA] hath blossomed forth unto us.

Being crucified, Thou didst cast down the mighty, as Thou art all-powerful; and having raised up human nature that lay below in the stronghold of Hades, Thou didst seat it upon the Father's throne. Together with which, as Thou comest, we worship Thee and magnify Thee.

*Triadicon:*

Singing in Orthodox faith the Trinity consubstantial, a Unity in three Persons, we the faithful glorify: the indivisible, super-divine Nature, the thrice-radiant, unwaning Dawn, the single incorruptible Light that hath shone forth upon us.

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*

*Thou art wholly desire, Thou art all sweetness, O Word of God, Son of the Virgin, God of gods, O all-holy Lord of the holy; therefore all of us with her that bare Thee do magnify Thee.*

The knees of the heavenly ones bow unto Thee, O Jesus: and of the earthly, as unto the Creator, and of the subterranean, as unto God Who was crucified in the flesh; and all of us, theologizing, magnify Thee.

[Him Whom] Thou didst snatch from the hands of the [bonds of fetters, the Great One, do Thou now also deliver us from the present tormenting hands: that being so delivered we may magnify Thee.]

*The same Heirmos:*

[An image of strength is given unto corrupt nature, the Word of God in thy womb, O pure Virgin; and having raised this up again, which had slipped down unto Hades: therefore all of us magnify thee as the Theotokos.]

[As Thou hast willed, O Master, receive...]

[f. 40vB] ...that all of us may magnify Thee as Benefactor.

*AT THE PRAISES: STICHERA*[^54]

*Resurrectional. Tone 2:*

Let every breath and all creation glorify Thee, O Lord; for by the Cross Thou didst abolish death, that Thou mightest show unto the people Thy Resurrection from the dead, as the only Lover of mankind.[^55]

Let the Jews declare how the soldiers lost the King Whom they guarded; for why did the stone not keep the Rock of life? Either let them produce Him that was buried, or let them worship Him that is risen, saying with us: "Glory to the multitude of Thy compassions, O our Savior, glory to Thee!"

Rejoice, ye people, and be glad! An angel sitting upon the stone of the sepulchre, he brought good tidings unto us, saying: "Christ is risen, the Savior of the world, and hath filled all things with fragrance!" Rejoice, ye people, and be glad!

An angel indeed brought the greeting "Rejoice!" unto her that was full of grace before Thy conception, O Lord; and an angel rolled away the stone of Thy glorious sepulchre at Thy Resurrection. The one, in place of sorrow, brought tokens of gladness; while the other, in place of death, proclaimed unto us the Master, the Giver of life. Therefore we cry aloud unto Thee: O Benefactor of all, Lord, glory to Thee!

*Other Stichera, Eastern [Anatolian]:*

The women poured forth myrrh with tears upon Thy sepulchre: and were filled [f. 42rA] [of Christ] our God, Who willingly endured the Cross for our sake, and spent three days in Hades: and let them worship His third-day Resurrection, whereby the ends of the whole world were enlightened.

*Verse: Arise, O Lord my God, let Thy hand be lifted up; forget not Thy poor unto the end.*

Thou wast crucified and buried, O Christ, as Thou didst will; Thou didst despoil death, and didst arise in glory, as God and Master, granting eternal life unto the world, and great mercy.

*Verse: I will give thanks unto Thee, O Lord, with my whole heart; I will speak of all Thy marvelous works.*

Truly, ye lawless ones, having sealed the stone, ye have made us worthy of a greater miracle: the guards know it, having come forth today from the sepulchre; and they said: "Say ye that while we were asleep, His disciples came and stole Him." And who steals a dead body, and especially a naked one? He arose by His own power as God, leaving behind His burial wrappings in the tomb. Come, behold, O Jews, how He hath not broken the seals, He Who hath trampled down death, and granted unending life unto mankind, and great mercy!

*ON SUNDAY EVENING, AT LORD, I HAVE CRIED:*[^57]

*Penitential Stichera, Tone 2.*

*Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Егда ѡ древа):*

Having the Wellspring of loving-kindness, the inexhaustible abyss of mercy, and the torrents of compassions, O Father all-good, and Son, Word of the Father: and [f. 42rB] *AT THE LITURGY*[^56]

*The Beatitudes. Tone 2:*

We bring unto Thee the voice of the thief, and we pray: Remember us, O Lord, in Thy Kingdom!

We offer Thy Cross for the remission of transgressions, which Thou didst receive for our sake, O Lover of mankind.

By Thy death, O Lord, Thou didst slay death; and by Thy Resurrection, O my Savior, Thou didst enlighten the world.

We worship Thy burial, O Master, and Thy rising, whereby Thou didst deliver the world from corruption, O Lover of mankind.

Meeting the Myrrh-bearing women, risen from the tomb, Thou didst tell them to proclaim Thy rising unto the disciples.

As Thou didst raise Adam from the tomb, O All-Good One: so as God, by the Tree Thou didst save the world. *Glory:*

Let us glorify the Father, let us worship the Son, and let all of us the faithful hymn the Holy Spirit. *Both now:*

Rejoice, fiery Throne; rejoice, Mother unwedded; rejoice, O Virgin, who didst bear God unto men!

...and Holy Spirit, uncreated Nature: receive our supplication and prayer, granting forgiveness unto all that are in transgressions! [f. 42vA] as God, Compassionate and Lover of mankind.

Thou hast by nature, as God, a womb of compassions, and mercy of goodness. Therefore we pray Thee, O Christ our Savior, and falling down we call unceasingly, crying: grant unto Thy servants remission of their many transgressions, and forgiveness unto all, which all of us have committed: for Thou art God, compassionate and the Lover of mankind.

Wishing to save all, O Savior, as God, for whose sake Thou didst become incarnate and was revealed as man: save us who worship Thy commandments. For Thou didst not come, O Lover of mankind, to save the righteous, but to loose us who are bound in transgressions by many sins, through the grace of divine baptism: as Thou art compassionate and the Lover of mankind.

*Other Stichera to the Bodiless Hosts.*[^58]

*Podoben: "The same Tone and Podoben" (Гла́съ и҆ подо́бенъ то́йже):*

Thrones, Cherubim, and Seraphim, Dominions, Powers, honorable Authorities, Angels, Archangels, and Principalities with them: they who sing an unceasing hymn in concord unto Him Who constituted their incorruptible nature, teaching all to honor one Essence in the Trinity: equally unoriginate, equally honorable, and sharing one throne.

The first of the immaterial choirs, receiving the beams of the divine Sovereignty with glad-tidings illuminations of outpourings, according to their rank impart the divine splendors unto the rest, and bring unto us saving [f. 42vB] in purity with diligence.

On high unto the heights, O soul, on high the eye of the heart and the spiritual aspirations, having divine love, let us ever stretch forth in our souls: so that, being enlightened by the rays from thence, we may escape the darkness of passions, hoping with the Angels to stand before the dreadful throne of the Creator, and to be transformed from light to light.

*Glory: Both now: Theotokion:*

The multitude of Angels, O pure one, sings unto thy Son with thrice-holy voices: as unto Him Who hath a fiery throne and an animate palace; the divine Bridge who ever leads from earth unto Him. Rejoice, O full of grace, crying aloud unto thee in concord with the Archangel Gabriel: for thou didst bear the Wellspring of joy!

*AT THE APOSTICHA, STICHERA*

*Penitential: Tone 2:*

I have sinned against Thee, O Savior, as the Prodigal Son: receive me, O Father, as I repent, and have mercy on me, O God!

I cry unto Thee, O Christ Savior, with the voice of the Publican: cleanse me as Thou didst him, and have mercy on me, O God!

The Passion-bearers, not shaken by earthly pleasures, were accounted worthy of heavenly blessings, and became fellow-citizens with the Angels. O Lord, by their prayers, have mercy and save us!

*Glory: Both now: Theotokion:*

Rejoice, O Mother Theotokos, invincible Church, protection and rampart: as the Prophet cries: "Zion, Church of God, in which righteousness hath appeared unto us!"

[f. 43rA] *ON MONDAY AT MATINS.*[^59]

*After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymns.*

*Penitential, Tone 2:*

As waves of the sea have my iniquities risen up against me; as a ship in the abyss, I alone am submerged by many transgressions: but unto the calm haven of repentance, guide me, O Lord, and save me!

I am a barren tree, O Lord, bearing no fruit of repentance whatsoever; and I fear being cut down, and I dread that unquenchable fire. Therefore I beseech Thee: before that extremity, turn me and save me!

*Glory: Both now: Theotokion:*

Being the Wellspring of loving-kindness, vouchsafe mercy unto us, O Theotokos: look down upon a sinful people; show forth, as ever, thy power: for trusting in thee, we cry "Rejoice!" unto thee, as of old Gabriel, the Archistrategos of the Bodiless Hosts.

*After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns.*

*Penitential, Tone 2:*

"Have mercy on me," said David; and I cry unto Thee: "I have sinned, O Savior; cleanse my sins through repentance, and have mercy on me!"

"Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!" For two sins David wept; but I cry unto Thee concerning myriads of transgressions: he soaked his bed with tears, but I have not acquired a single tear. In terror I pray: Have mercy on me, O God, according to Thy great mercy!

[f. 43rB] *[Martyricon: Having yielded their body, the holy martyrs...]*

...having the holy garment in the world: they endured tortures from the lawless, and abolished the idolatrous deceit; by their prayers deliver us also from the invisible enemy, O Savior, and save us!

*Glory: Both now: Theotokion:*

We magnify thee, O Theotokos, crying: Rejoice, Cloud of unwaning Light; Him didst thou carry in thy bosom, the Lord of glory!

*After the 3rd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns.*

*Podoben: "Being the wellspring of loving-kindness" (Милосердіа сꙋщи исто):*

In ignorance and with knowledge I sin, by night and by day. Thee do I provoke to wrath, O Christ, I alone upon earth by my lawlessness; O only Good and Sinless One, turn me and save me, through the entreaties of Thine Angels, Thou Who didst come in loving-kindness to call sinners unto repentance!

*Glory: Both now: Theotokion:*

O unwedded and pure Theotokos, who without seed didst bear the Master of all: Him do thou entreat with the Angels, that we may be delivered from every perplexity, and that He may grant compunction and light unto our souls, and cleansing of transgressions, as thou alone dost swiftly protect!

*THE CANON OF REPENTANCE*[^60]

*Ode 1. Tone 2. Heirmos:*

*Come, ye people, let us sing a song unto Christ God, Who divided the sea and led the people whom He had brought out of Egyptian bondage: for He is glorified.*

Being incarnate, O Word, and not having come to call the righteous, as Thou didst say, but sinners unto repentance: receive me who have sinned greatly, and save me!

[f. 43vA] I alone am enslaved unto sin; I alone have opened the doors unto the passions. O only Good Changer, turning me, save me in Thy loving-kindness. *For the Martyrs:*

At Thy judgment-seat, O Lord, wearing crowns, the Passion-bearers stand: having vanquished the audacity of the evil one, and being enriched with immortality. *For the Martyrs:*

Pouring forth streams of healings unto us, the Passion-bearers ever dry up the corrupt passions of our flesh, by the power of the Holy Spirit. *Theotokion:*

O Maiden who didst bear the Wellspring of dispassion: heal me who am wounded by passions, and snatch me from eternal fire: O only one full of divine joy!

*Another Canon, to the Bodiless Hosts.*

*Composition of Theophanes.*

*Ode 1. Tone 2. Heirmos:*

*Having traversed an untrodden, uncustomary, waterless sea path...*

O god-bearing Coal, kindled by the radiance of Thy nature: Thou hast revealed the Bodiless choirs who glorify Thee, O Christ, as all-powerful.

The Angels acquired the power of incorruption and the granted glory of immortality, O Christ; by drawing near unto Thee they are illuminated.

The Angels appeared as light-bearers, showing forth the immaterial and natural, in forms, O Christ; sensibly fashioning purity. *Theotokion:*

The angelic ranks serve thy childbearing which is beyond nature, rejoicing, O pure one: for thou didst bear their God and Lord.

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*

[f. 43vB] *Establish us in Thyself, O Lord, Who by the Tree didst put transgressions to death: and plant Thy fear in our hearts, as Thou art the Lover of mankind.*

O Christ Who didst enter the incorruptible womb: renew my soul which is corrupted by passions through repentance, and reveal it filled with Thine ever-existing light!

I hearkened unto the enemy who provokes Thee to wrath, and I committed all sins; and senselessly I provoked Thee to wrath, O Lover of mankind, the only Long-suffering One. *For the Martyrs:*

Girt with the Cross, the invincible weapons and martyrs of the Savior, like walls, destroyed the deceitful fortifications in God. *For the Martyrs:*

Having strengthened your weakness by divine power, O noble Passion-bearers: ye surrendered the strength of the adversary unto utter destruction. *Theotokion:*

O Mary, golden Censer: drive away the stench of my passions, and establish me who am shaken by the assaults of the deceitful adversary!

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*

*The bow of the mighty is broken by Thy dominion, O Christ: and the weak are girded with strength.*

God, Who is immortal by nature, wisely working in goodness, makes manifest the immortal armies.

Standing now with supreme longing before Christ: O Angels, pray ye that all of us may be saved! *Theotokion:*

Having received a temporal beginning, truly from thee: He Who is the Maker of the ages, O Mother ever-Virgin.

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*

*I hymn Thee, for by hearing, O Lord, I heard...*

[f. 44rA] ...[He came,] seeking me who had gone astray; therefore I glorify Thy great dispensation towards me, and renewal.

I have fallen into the mire of sin, and have lost the former comeliness, O Lord, and I fear torment: therefore, by the beauty of repentance, enlighten my humble soul!

With deceitful words, the subtle one stole me away from Thee, and made me food for himself, O God of all: snatch me from his malice, and call me back by the patterns of repentance. *For the Martyrs:*

Delivered over as food unto beasts, and burned with fire, O Martyrs, and flayed, and dismembered in your limbs: ye did not deny Christ, your Helper and Might; Him do ye fervently beseech on behalf of me, the wretched one. *For the Martyrs:*

Honoring one Nature, and the Trinity in Persons, the uncreated Godhead: not honoring creation in any way, ye were known as the Martyrs of Christ; therefore ye endured great tortures. *Theotokion:*

He is incarnate of thy pure blood, and is united unto men by His will, O all-immaculate Lady: and He receives the penitent who of old were submerged in sins, being inclined by thy supplications, O pure one.

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*

*I heard, O Lord, of Thy glorious dispensation: I bring unto Thee the bodiless intercessors; receiving whom in Thy compassion, as Thou art tender-hearted, deliver me from sins!*

Drawing near unto the All-causing Mind, the divine minds being purified, are illuminated [f. 44rB] the divine ornaments of the heavenly hierarchy, being adorned by the Holy Spirit, are preserved immutably. *Theotokion:*

Perceiving thee from afar, O Virgin, carrying upon thy hands God incarnate, Isaiah foretold.

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*

*O Giver of light and Creator of the ages, Lord, in the light of Thy commandments guide Thou us: for beside Thee, we know no other God.*

Thou Who didst enlighten the eyes of the blind: enlighten my blinded soul; and strengthen it to work good deeds, taking care utterly to hate slothfulness.

Heal my soul, O only Savior, which is wounded by the grievous wound of willful sin: Thou Who of old didst heal the wounds of him that fell among thieves. *For the Martyrs:*

The assembly of honorable Sufferers put to shame the council of lawless persecutors, having endured manifold pains; and now, with the sacred angelic choirs, they ever rejoice. *For the Martyrs:*

As stars of manifold light, sending forth the radiance of endurance, and enlightening the souls of the faithful with the Holy Spirit: the most radiant Martyrs were revealed. *Theotokion:*

Newly as an Infant unto us, thou didst bear the pre-eternal Son, twofold in wills and operations: as man, and together as God, O all-hymned one.

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos: The coal of Isaiah...*

[f. 44vA] ...Seraphim, with brightness, with the exalted Thrones: god-like do they enlighten the rest.

As the Giver of all effusion of light, Thou hast drawn Thine illumination, O Word of God, unto the light-resembling mirrors, receiving it with joy and undeviating understanding.

Joy unto thee, which looses the lamentation of the ancestors, Gabriel, the sacred Archangel, having flown down from heaven, proclaimed, O pure Bride of God.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*

*Held fast in the deep of sin, I call upon the unfathomable abyss of Thy loving-kindness: lead me up from corruption, O my God!*

I have fallen by the malice of the serpent: I lie upon the bed of despair. O Christ Who didst raise the paralytic by Thy word, raise me up also!

Tossed by the serpent's winds, and ever submerged by the waves of sin: save me, as Thou didst Peter, O Lord, Lover of mankind!

Having surpassed the bounds of nature, ye endured torments that are beyond nature; therefore ye were deemed worthy of blessings that surpass the mind, O Martyrs. *Martyricon:*

As noble, as fair, as honorable: ye were united unto the fair Benefactor; ever praying on our behalf, O all-glorious Martyrs. *Theotokion:*

From all generations He chose thee, the beauty of Jacob, which the Creator loved, O all-immaculate one; and having shone forth from thee, He appeared.

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*

[f. 44vB] ...having hearkened unto my soul, O Master, deliver me from fierce things: for Thou alone art the cause of our salvation.

The divine places of Thy glory, O Master Christ, Light of the beginning, kindled with light-flashing splendors, abide eternally in light-resembling radiance.

Strengthened by divine power, the Seraphim, calling with unceasing voices the thrice-holy hymn: lifting them up to revere the three-hypostatic Nature. *Theotokion:*

As the Lord swore in truth of old unto David: having come forth from thy womb He fulfilled it; for thou, O Maiden, didst bear Him Who reigns over heaven and earth.

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*

*Unto the golden image worshipped in the plain of Dura, Thy three youths took no heed of the godless command; but cast into the midst of the flames, being bedewed they sang: "Blessed is the God of our fathers!"*

By mental perversion and demonic assaults, being filled with every shame: I was far from Thy commandments, like the Prodigal; but now turning, I cry: "I have sinned like him; abhor me not, O Jesus, Who wast incarnate for my sake!"

O God of all: the Ninevites, having repented of old, Thou didst save from the decree that brings forth death; likewise, O only Lover of mankind, deliver from fierce torments my heart defiled by manifold prodigality, which now turns unto Thee. *For the Martyrs:* [f. 45rA] blessed divine Martyrs, and remained unhealed; but unto all the faithful your wounds were revealed as healing, wounded by the assaults of the ancient deceiver.

Neither fierce beasts, nor the threats of torturers, nor fire, nor wounds, nor the cutting sword, nor incandescent vessels did ye fear: but as in alien bodies, ye endured all things, O great Martyrs; therefore ye were crowned. *Theotokion:*

A dwelling of immaterial Light was thy womb, with splendors of divine understanding, which set fire unto godlessness, O all-pure Bride of God, Maiden; Whom singing we call: "Blessed is the God of our fathers!"

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos: The youths were revealed as orators:*

Around the throne of Thine ineffable glory, the immaterial minds ever dancing, with unceasing mouths sing: "O God of our fathers, transcendent in divinity, blessed art Thou!"

When the angelic ranks beheld Thee being carried up unto heaven with the flesh, they opened the heavenly gates unto Thee, singing: "O God of our fathers, transcendent in divinity, blessed art Thou!" *Theotokion:*

Gabriel, showing thee, O Maiden, to be the beginning of the Law and the Prophets, cried aloud: "Behold, thou alone, all-hymned one, dost give birth unto the God Who is transcendent in divinity unto our fathers and us!"

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*

*Unto God Who descended into the fiery furnace unto the Hebrew children, and changed the flame into coolness: sing, all ye works, as unto the Lord, and supreme exalt Him unto all ages!*

[f. 45rB] [I have fallen unto the evil one,] and became enslaved by his wiles; and beholding me in great negligence, he boasts through deceit. Snatch me from him, O Compassionate One, Who art the conversion of them that have gone astray!

Loose me who am held fast by indissoluble bodily bonds, Thou Who didst loose the indissoluble from eternal bonds; and guide me to run unto the saved paths, O Christ, Savior of the world! *Martyricon:*

He that works passions hath wrought all malice upon me, the humble one; O blessed Martyrs, who were truly conformable unto the passions of Christ: deliver me from the adversary's injury!

Not bowing their knees unto idols, ye were cast into the furnace of wounds of old, like the youths; and being revealed unburnt by divine dew, O all-praised Martyrs, sing ye Christ unto all ages! *Theotokion:*

My wretched soul, grown weak through many assaults of the evil one, O Mother of God, make healthy by thy healing supplications, O Virgin, that I may glorify thee unto all ages!

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*

*The thrice-rich youths took no heed of the golden image, beholding the unchangeable living image; but in the midst of the flames they sang: "Let all creation praise the Lord, and supreme exalt Him unto all ages!"*

According to the likeness of Thy goodness, Thou didst constitute the Angels, fulfilling Thy commandments with strength, O Word, and helping all the faithful to cry: "Let all the works of the Lord praise the Lord, and supreme exalt Him unto all ages!"

[f. 45vA] With divine virtues Thou hast adorned the heavenly life of the holy Angels, enlightening their hierarchy unto Thee, O Christ, who cry: "Let all creation praise the Lord, and supreme exalt Him unto all ages!"

Rejoicing brightly, let us sing the divine song of the Bodiless Hosts, without failing; and blessing the Master, let us cry aloud the hymn: "Let all creation praise the Lord, and supreme exalt Him unto all ages!" *Theotokion:*

Righteousness, which wisely governs all things, worthily loved thee, the all-pure Virgin; ineffably, O all-holy Theotokos, having dwelt within thee: Whom unceasingly glorifying, as Lord and Master we supreme exalt Him unto all ages.

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*

*The Word of God, God of God, Who by ineffable wisdom came to renew Adam, who fell grievously into corruption through eating: ineffably incarnate of the Holy Virgin for our sake, we the faithful magnify in songs of one mind.*

Behold the time of working: why sleepest thou foolishly, O soul, in deep despair? Arise, illuminate thy lamp with tears; make haste, the Bridegroom of souls draws near: delay not, lest thou remain outside the divine doors!

O how dreadful is Thy judgment-seat, revealing every naked deed before Angels and men! O the fierce sentence which Thou art about to give unto them that have sinned! From which deliver me, O Christ, before the end: grant me tears of conversion. *For the Martyrs:*

[f. 45vB] Marked with the divine blood of the Lamb and Shepherd, O glorious divine Sufferers: being slaughtered ye rejoiced, like innocent lambs; and now ye enlighten the holy Church of the first-born in heaven. *For the Martyrs:*

Having appeared like lamps of solar radiance, by the rays of your sufferings ye illuminate every soul, and drive away every darkness of deceit, O noble Sufferers: therefore in faith ye are worthily blessed. *Theotokion:*

Spare me, O Lord, spare me when Thou art about to judge: and condemn me not unto fire, neither reprove me in Thy wrath; the Virgin who bare Thee, O Christ, entreats Thee, and the multitude of Angels, and the assembly of Martyrs.

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*

*Thou art wholly desire, Thou art all sweetness, O Word of God, Son of the Virgin, God of gods, O all-holy Lord of the holy; therefore all of us with her that bare Thee do magnify Thee.*

Appearing white-robed, the Angels in radiant form spoke unto Thy divine disciples, proclaiming Thy second coming, O Christ: with whom blessing Thee, we magnify Thee.

As the Benefactor of every rational nature: Thou didst make these first rays a second brightness, by reason of Thine extreme goodness; therefore, giving thanks, all of us magnify Thee. *Theotokion:*

Perceiving thy radiant virginity, O all-pure one, and marveling: the divine Archangel brought joy unto thee...

[f. 46rA] *AT THE APOSTICHA, STICHERA*[^61]

*Penitential. Tone 2:*

Contemplating the measureless evils of my deeds, I flee unto Thy compassions: resembling the Publican, the weeping Harlot, and the Prodigal Son. Therefore, I also fall down before Thee, O Merciful One: before Thou judgest me, spare me, O God, and have mercy on me!

Overlook my transgressions, O Lord Who wast born of the Virgin, and cleanse my heart, making it a church for Thy Holy Spirit; cast me not away from Thy presence, Thou Who hast immeasurable great mercy!

Ye suffered for Christ even unto death, O Passion-bearing Martyrs: for ye have your souls in the hand of God in heaven, and your relics are honored throughout the whole world; Hierarchs and kings bow down, and all people rejoicing, we cry aloud as is customary: "Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His saints!"

*Glory: Both now: Theotokion:*

In thee have I placed my hope, O Theotokos: let us not fall away from our expectation; save...

*ON MONDAY EVENING, AT LORD, I HAVE CRIED:*

*Penitential Stichera, Tone 2.*

*Podoben: "When from the Tree" ([Егда ѡ древа:]):*

I have surpassed all in sin, what repentance shall I learn? If I sigh like the Publican [f. 46rB] us from perils, O Helper of the perplexed; and overthrow the counsels of adversaries: for thou art our salvation, O blessed one.

*ON MONDAY*

*The Beatitudes, Tone 2:*

We bring unto Thee the voice of the thief, and we pray: Remember us, O Lord, in Thy Kingdom!

Save me, O Lord God, and make me a partaker of the portion of them that love Thee from the soul!

All the heavenly armies serve Thee with fear, as God; by their prayers save us! *For the Martyrs:*

With the weapon of faith, O Sufferers, ye conquered the armies of the enemy, and were brought unto God.

*Glory: Triadicon:*

The spiritual ranks with the human race honor the simple Trinity, the Godhead of one essence.

*Both now: Theotokion:*

O all-pure Lady, who without seed didst bear God: pray Him that we may be saved!

...I do not presume to weigh down the heavens. If I weep like the Harlot, with my tears I defile the earth: but grant [f. 46vA] me remission of sins, O God, and have mercy on me!

I have committed every sin; I have surpassed all in prodigality. If I desire to repent, I have no streams of tears. If I live negligently even now, I shall be condemned unto torment. But grant me correction, O only Good God, and have mercy on me!

Grant me a shower of tears of divine compunction, O Christ, as Thou art compassionate: that weeping, I may wash away the defilements of my transgressions, which come from pleasures, and be shown cleansed, when Thou, the Judge, shalt come from heaven to judge mankind: as Thou art the only righteous Judge.

*Other Stichera, to the Holy John the Forerunner.*[^62]

*Podoben: "The same Tone and Podoben" (Гла́съ и҆ подо́бенъ то́йже):*

O Preacher and Baptist of Christ, Angel, Apostle, Martyr, Prophet, Forerunner, Lamp, close Friend, Seal of the Prophets, most honorable of the born, Mediator of the Old and New grace, bright voice of the Word: by thy sacred intercessions direct our prayerful deeds unto God the tender-hearted!

"Behold the Lamb of God, that takes away the sin of the world!" didst thou cry aloud, O holy Prophet and Forerunner, when thou didst behold Christ walking upon earth. Him do thou entreat, to grant remission of sins unto them that honor thee. For thou hast, in truth, great boldness before Him, O Baptist, as mediator of the Law and grace.

Make haste, and rescue me from temptations [f. 46vB] by which the bitter demons assault me, seeking to seize the soul of thine unworthy servant, like a bird; leave me not unto the end: that they may know more from deeds that thou art my refuge!

*Glory: Both now: Theotokion:*

As having natural kinship and concord in prayer, breathing as one, O Mother of the King of all, and divine Forerunner: make supplication together on behalf of the servant who hath greatly provoked the Good and Merciful One: so that, being inclined by your intercessions, He may show compassion and save, and deliver me from kinship with fire.

*AT THE APOSTICHA, STICHERA*

*Penitential, Tone 2:*

I have sinned against Thee, O Savior, as the Prodigal Son: receive me, O Father, as I repent, and have mercy on me, O God!

I cry unto Thee, O Christ Savior, with the voice of the Publican: cleanse me, as Thou didst him, and have mercy on me, O God!

When the holy Martyrs pray for us, and hymn Christ: all deceit ceases, and the human race is saved by faith.

*Glory: Both now: Theotokion:*

O impassable Door, mystically sealed, blessed Theotokos: receive our prayers, and bring them unto thy Son and our God, that for thy sake He may save our souls.

*ON TUESDAY AT MATINS.*[^63]

*After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymns:*

[f. 47rA] ...[against] me my iniquities; and as a ship in the abyss, I alone am submerged by many transgressions: but unto the calm haven of repentance, guide me, O Lord, and save me!

I am a barren tree, O Lord: I have brought forth no fruit of repentance whatsoever; and I fear being cut down, and I dread that unquenchable fire. Therefore I beseech Thee: before that calamity, turn me and save me!

*Glory. Both now: Theotokion:*

We have become partakers of the divine nature through thee, O Theotokos Virgin: for thou didst bear God incarnate for us; therefore as is due, all of us piously magnify thee.

*After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns: Tone 2:*

"Have mercy on me," said David; and I cry unto Thee: "I have sinned, O Savior; having cleansed my sins through repentance, have mercy on me!"

"Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me!" For two sins David wept; but I cry unto Thee concerning myriads of transgressions: he soaked his bed with tears, but I have not acquired a single drop. In despair I pray: Have mercy on me, O God, according to Thy great mercy!

Apostles, Prophets, and Martyrs, Hierarchs, Venerable and Righteous: who have fought the good fight, and kept the faith, having boldness before the Savior: entreat Him on our behalf, as He is good, that our souls may be saved, we pray!

[f. 47rB] *[Glory: Both now: Theotokion:]*

...[protection] and help which comes from thee: for in thee hath my soul trusted, and have mercy on me!

*After the 3rd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns: Tone 2:*

*Podoben: "Being the wellspring of loving-kindness" (Милосердіа сꙋщи исто):*

For the sake of the mercy of loving-kindness, O Good One, Christ came to save His creation: having bowed the heavens by His descent. Therefore, hymning Thy dreadful dispensation, we cry unto Thee: by the entreaties of Thy Forerunner, grant us cleansing of sins, as Thou alone art tender-hearted. *Glory:*

Thou Who didst enlighten Thy saints more than gold, and art glorified in Thy venerable ones as Good One: being entreated by them, O Christ God, pacify our life, as Lover of mankind; and direct our prayer like incense, Thou Who alone restest among the saints. *Both now: Theotokion:*

O fervent Protectress of Christians: pray unceasingly unto thy Son, O Theotokos, to deliver us from every malicious assault and bitter grief of the adversary; and to grant us forgiveness in those things wherein we have sinned, for the sake of the mercy of His compassions: through thy prayers, O Virgin Mother.

*THE CANON OF COMPUNCTION*[^64]

*Composition of Joseph.*

*Ode 1. Tone 2. Heirmos:*

*Having received the song of Moses, cry aloud, O soul: "A Helper and a Protector is He become unto me for salvation: this is my God, and I will glorify Him!"*

Let us weep bitterly for ourselves, brethren, before our departure: that with good tears we may escape the tears of torment [f. 47vA] which will then profit nothing to them that have them.

Myriads of times, O Christ, I promised to repent: but having an unfeeling soul, I fall into transgressions; have compassion, O Savior, upon my weakness. *For the Martyrs:*

The Passion-bearers of Christ, having endured the fire of torment by divine bedewing: deliver me, who lie in grievous passions, from the fire of Gehenna. *For the Martyrs:*

Having appeared mighty against the enemies by divine power: ye cast down their unpowerful strength, O worthily blessed Martyrs. *Theotokion:*

O fiery Tongs, which Isaiah once beheld: burn up the material passions of my heart, O Virgin Mother, and consume them utterly.

*Another Canon, of the Forerunner.*

*Composition of Joseph. Heirmos:*

*The all-conquering power submerged the entire Pharaonic cavalry in the deep of old...*

O Baptist and Forerunner of Christ: being ever submerged by bodily pleasures, strengthen my mind, and calm the waves of passions: that being in divine calm, I may ever glorify thee.

Having been enlightened with incomprehensible illumination, like a star of manifold light, thou didst run before the spiritual Orient: pray Him, O Baptist, to illuminate my heart, which is darkened by all demonic assaults.

In the river, O all-wise one, thou didst once submerge the abyss, with grace that inundates every transgression: but I pray thee [f. 47vB] dry up the torrents of my transgressions, O most rich one, by thy divine intercession. *Theotokion:*

Thou wast a kinsman of the pure Virgin who bare God incarnate, O blessed Forerunner: with her we honor thee and pray, who now live in thy divine temple: make us temples of the Spirit!

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*

*Show my barren mind to be fruitful, O God: Cultivator of souls, and Planter of good things, by Thy loving-kindness.*

I have weighed down my soul with slothful slumber: raise me up, O Christ, unto the vigil of repentance, to do Thy commandments!

Reveal me not put to shame, O Jesus, in the dreadful day: but before the end, turning me, deliver me from fierce torments! *Martyricon:*

Having well imitated the passions of Christ in divine manners, O honorable Passion-bearers: heal the bitter passions of my soul! *For the Martyrs:*

That ye might be deemed worthy of the ever-existing blessings in heaven, O Passion-bearers: ye steadfastly endured every temptation of fierce things upon earth. *Theotokion:*

Mother-like thou dost feed with milk the Nourisher of all, and thou carriest Him upon thine arm, O pure one, Who ever holds all things in His hand.

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*

*Having established me upon the rock of faith, Thou hast enlarged my mouth against my enemies; for my spirit rejoiced when singing: "There is none holy as our God, and none righteous beside Thee, O Lord!"*

He that hath my mind darkened [f. 48rA] enlighten my mind darkened by slothfulness, by thine intercession, O Forerunner of the Lord: and deliver me from great adverse circumstances, I pray.

Thou didst loose the barrenness of her that bare thee, being born by the providence of God, O all-wise Prophet: make my barren heart fruitful now by thine intercession, to bring forth the blossoms of virtues.

Pray that they who with love built the temple of God may obtain the life above; and they that serve in thy temple in faith, make them temples of the Holy Spirit, O Baptist and Forerunner, by thy prayers. *Theotokion:*

The Forerunner, carried in his mother's womb, leaped and worshipped the Lord carried in thy womb, O Virgin full of divine joy: pray Him to deliver us from all sorrow.

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*

*Foreseeing Thy childbearing from the Virgin, the Prophet proclaimed, crying: "I heard Thy report and was afraid; for from Teman, from the holy shadowed mountain, art Thou come, O Christ!"*

Beholding me robbed on all sides and impoverished, O Word, the enemy rejoices in my destruction, the master of deceit; O Lord of glory and Enricher of the poor, rescue me from his malice!

I have defiled my hands and eyes, O Lord, doing things unworthy to be done; and in foolishness I have provoked Thy compassions: grievously have I tried Thy longsuffering; but having compassion, save [f. 48rB] me as God! *For the Martyrs:*

Wondrous is God in His saints, unto them that believe in Him, and who destroy the idols of destruction: and who have inherited the expanse of Paradise, from which Adam of old was cast out!

By the shedding of your blood, O blessed ones, ye stopped the blood that was once offered unto demons, a destructive error: offered by men who were deceived unto destruction; therefore ye are ever blessed. *Theotokion:*

Taught by the Spirit, the glorious choir of Prophets prefigured thy mystery which is beyond understanding, O Theotokos, in manifold forms with sacred figures; whose fulfillment we behold from afar.

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos: He came:*

Unto Him Who bowed the heavens and mingled with men, thou didst bow thy head with thy right hand, O most rich one: by which preserve me, keeping my heart in peace.

The impassable wilderness had thee as a citizen, O blessed Forerunner; therefore I cry unto thee: make my soul fruitful, which is destitute of all divine works!

Directing the divine Law, thou wast lawlessly slaughtered; therefore I pray thee: correct me who ever act lawlessly and am drowned in demonic delusions!

Having built thyself as a temple of the Queen and Lady: thou hast now departed unto the divine habitations, O Forerunner; pray that they who built this all-holy temple unto thee may obtain them! *Theotokion:*

[f. 48vA] Look down upon me who am sick, O all-immaculate one, and loose my fierce passions which are difficult to heal: that I may magnify thee who hast magnified all mankind!

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*

*Drive away the gloom of my soul, O my Savior, and enlighten me with the light of Thy commandments, as the only King of peace.*

Senselessly I add sins unto sins, and there is no lifting up in my death: woe is me, how shall I appear before Christ?

Receiving peril like a ship: I have wasted my time which Thou gavest me, O Compassionate One; and now, having become poor, I cry: despise me not, O Christ! *For the Martyrs:*

As ye despised the earthly glory which is trodden underfoot, O Passion-bearers, ye were accounted worthy of heavenly glory, abiding with Christ. *For the Martyrs:*

Separating their mind from the love of the flesh by faith, the Passion-bearers lovingly embraced tortures, having appropriated themselves unto Christ. *Theotokion:*

Daniel beheld thee in the Spirit as a great mountain, O Theotokos: from which the Stone was cut out, crushing the idols of demons.

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos: Illumination:*

In the streams of Jordan's water of incorruption, O Forerunner, having baptized Christ: pray Him to dry up the outpourings of my passions, and to inherit the torrents of delight, and the fair joy of the righteous.

Already I lament, and I shudder with fear, and am ever held fast by perplexity: considering my deeds, and the [f. 48vB] terror. O tender-hearted Lord, spare me, by the prayers of Thy Baptist!

Ordaining saving laws for the people, O Forerunner, having been in repentance of transgressions: thou didst stand between the Law and grace; therefore we pray thee: enlighten us with the patterns of repentance!

Grant me time for repentance, O Benefactor, unto me who have spent all the past in despair: having the great Forerunner John praying unto Thee for this, O Word, and all-comely preacher of repentance. *Theotokion:*

By the snare and hunting of the deceitful one I was put to death, O all-immaculate Lady: make me alive, O Theotokos who didst bear the Life constituted for all: that I may piously hymn thee, the all-hymned one.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*

*Held fast in the deep of sin, O Savior, and tempest-tossed in the sea of life: but as the Prophet Jonah, lead me up from the deep of passions, and save me!*

As of old the Canaanite woman, I cry unto Thee, O Christ: "Son of David, having had mercy, show compassion upon me!" For I have a soul suffering in fierce things, and it will not come to its senses.

The measureless waves of passions trouble me; as Thou didst rebuke the sea of old, and save Thy holy disciples: so raise me up, O Jesus, and save me! *For the Martyrs:*

The bodiless angelic choirs marveled at your endurance in the flesh, and praised Him Who gave you strength, O honorable Sufferers...

[staining...]

[f. 49rA] ...[burned] with the streams of your blood,[^65] and having your eyes gouged out, O Martyrs, and frozen by fierce cold: ye passed over unto the warmth of life, hymning Christ. *Theotokion:*

As a Table containing the mystical Bread, of Which having eaten, we hunger no more, O all-hymned one: knowing thee in truth as the Mother and Nourisher of Christ, the God of all.

*Heirmos: Held fast in the abyss of sin, O...*

Thou who didst proclaim the voice of the Word: pray that our voices may be received, and forgiveness of sins be granted unto them that sing unto thee in love.

Heal the crushing of my soul, and loose the burden of sins, and beyond hope save me, by thy prayers, O blessed Forerunner!

O glorious Forerunner, pray Him Whom thou didst baptize with thine own hand, to deliver me by His hand, Who takes away sins, unto Him lifting up my hands ever on high. *Theotokion:*

Slothful slumber holds me fast; sinful sleep weighs down my heart: by thy divine intercession, O all-pure one, raise me up and save me!

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*

*The youths resembling the Cherubim danced in the furnace, crying aloud: "Blessed art Thou, O God, for in truth and judgment hast Thou brought all these things upon us for our sins: all-hymned and highly glorified unto all ages!"*

I have forsaken Thy laws, submitting unto brutish desires [f. 49rB] [deeds] unfitting, O Christ; and I am condemned in my senselessness, as no other among men upon earth: leave me not, therefore, O Savior, to perish, for the sake of Thy love for mankind!

Behold, I was conceived in iniquities, O Lord, as David cries; and born upon earth; and as a servant provoking to wrath, I provoked Thee to wrath, the only existing true God: leave me not, therefore, O Savior, to perish, for the sake of Thy love for mankind! *For the Martyrs:*

Manfully did the assembly of Sufferers contend, and wondrously were they crowned by the life-bearing right hand: for in truth they loved God, Who created all things by His Word; and now rejoicing in heaven, they take delight in divine enjoyment. *For the Martyrs:*

Having their eyes gouged out, and the cutting off of hands and feet: the glorious ones sent forth a good course unto the heavenly journey, hindering the journeys of the single adversary; by their prayers save all, O Word, who glorify Thee! *Theotokion:*

The Cherubim glorify, the Seraphim hymn, the Thrones, Authorities, and Dominions unceasingly: thy childbearing which is beyond understanding, O all-hymned Mary: for thou alone didst bear God in the flesh; pray Him, O pure one, to save all of us who honor thee in love.

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos: The god-opposing [decree]:*

Root out with the axe of thy prayer, cutting down the instigator of the passions of my heart; plant, O Forerunner, the fear of divine dispassion, estranging me from ignorance toward God, and from every malice.

[f. 49vA] "In the streams of Jordan, as thou didst baptize the Lord Who covers with waters the upper chambers:[^66] pray Him, O glorious Forerunner, ever to grant waters of divine compunction unto mine eyes that purify."

"O Forerunner, who didst preach the Lamb of God Who takes away the sins of the world: pray Him, O glorious one, to show me a stranger to the portion of the goats, and to number me with the sheep on His right hand."

"A barren womb bears thee, O Virgin, who didst bear the Word incarnate in thy womb; Whom by divine leaping the great Forerunner recognized in the womb as the enlightenment of the barren: and rejoicing, he bowed down in worship."

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*

*"In the bush unto Moses on Mount Sinai, Him Who prefigured the virgin wonder of old: praise ye, bless, and highly exalt unto all ages!"*

"That Thou mightest deify us, Thou wast mercifully incarnate; I understand not how, being damaged by sins, by what grace; convert me, O Christ, Who art the conversion of all."

"Thou, O Word, art the Good Shepherd Who didst seek the sheep slaughtered upon the mountains of transgression: having converted my wretched soul, save me, lest the deceitful enemy devour me utterly!"

*For the Martyrs:*

"Manfully let us stand together, the stalwart Sufferers cried out one to another, being fiercely encompassed: 'Behold, Christ stretches forth crowns unto us unto ages!' *For the Martyrs:*"

"With robust sinews, by your steadfast sufferings, ye strangled the serpent who truly thought" [f. 49vB] "...to deceive you; and ye were shown forth as heirs of the delight of Paradise. *Theotokion:*"

"That God might deify us, He was incarnate of thy pure blood, and became earthly, O Virgin Theotokos: Whom pray thou ever for them that hymn thee."

*Another Canon [to the Forerunner]. Heirmos:*

*"The fiery furnace of old in Babylon divided its operation by the divine command, burning the Chaldeans, but cooling the faithful who sang: 'Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!' "*

"Grant the day-star unto me who lie upon the earth, O Forerunner, who didst stretch forth thy right hand and wash the Immaculate One with waters: and draw me out of the defilements of the flesh, purifying me entirely by repentance, and save me."

"Having time to repent, O my soul, shake off the heavy burdens of sloth, and hasten unto the struggle, crying aloud unto thy Benefactor: 'O Merciful One, have compassion upon me, by the entreaties of the Baptist of all!' "

"The torrents of passions and the waters of wickedness have entered into my soul, O blessed Forerunner: hasten quickly to deliver me, thou who by river streams didst wash the quiet abyss of dispassion."

"Woe is me who have committed many evils! Woe is me alone, who have provoked the all-good God to wrath! O Baptist of Christ, help me, and grant remission of my transgressions and a cutting off of the debt, by thine intercession. *Theotokion:*"

"Having borne the Most High God in the flesh: raise me up from the corruption of passions which afflict me and have grievously wounded me entirely, O all-pure one, and enrich me with divine virtues: that being saved, I may hymn thee."

[f. 50rA] *Ode 9. Heirmos:*

*"Who of earthborn men hath ever heard such a thing, or who hath ever seen, that a Virgin was found having conceived in the womb, and without pain gave birth to an Infant? Such is thy wonder: and thee, O pure Theotokos Mary, do we magnify!"*

"Behold Thy dread tribunal, before which I am to receive judgment, and the unquenchable fire of its terror; convert me who have spent all my years in vanity, O only King of all, Who didst convert Manasseh when he had sinned."

"Check the torrents of my measureless evils, O Christ, I cry unto Thee, granting me streams of tears for the washing of the defilements which I took upon myself in senselessness; and save me by Thy mercy, save me, O Master!"

"O ye who have repented in soul: The radiant memory of the divine Sufferers, having shone forth upon us like the sun, enlightens all the ends of the earth: and by the Divine Spirit it drives away soul-corrupting darkness. *For the Martyrs:*"

"An honorable host, victorious warriors, a chosen city, the assembly of the holy Martyrs, a blessed choir, joined together in an angel-pleasing manner with the bodiless hosts: by their prayers, O Christ, make all of us partakers of Thy Kingdom. *Theotokion:*"

"With radiant beams, from Him Who shone forth unto us from thy womb and abolished the night of godlessness," [f. 50rB] "...O all-immaculate Mother Mary: enlighten all who honor thee in faith, and deliver them from the ineffable darkness and from condemnation."

*Another Canon [to the Forerunner]. Heirmos: The Lord, Who is co-unoriginate with the Father...*

"Deliver me from the mire of sin, O Lord, sinless and only abundantly merciful One, by the entreaties of the Baptist: who proclaimed Thee unto the whole world as the Lamb of God Who takes away the sins of men."

"Like a sweet-smelling rose, like a fragrant cypress, like an unfading lily, like precious myrrh do I name thee, O Forerunner: that I may be delivered from the foul stench of my deeds by thy prayers, fleeing beneath thy protection."

"Unto me who am barren in unfruitfulness, O all-blessed one, make me ever to offer the fruits of virtues by grace, nourishing me as a child of the Lord, and a partaker of the divine Kingdom, and a fellow-citizen of the assembly of the saints."

"Unto us who love thee, and bless thee in faith, and dance in chorus in thy divine temple: grant from on high deliverance from cruel things, O Forerunner of the Lord, and direction for our life, and redemption from transgressions. *Theotokion:*"

"Leaping in the womb of the Mother of God: thou didst bow down in worship unto Him Who upholds all things by His nod; therefore pray Him, O Forerunner: that my humble soul may be saved, which falls into many transgressions day by day."

*At the Aposticha, Stichera of Repentance, Tone 2:*

[f. 50vA] "Pondering the senselessness of my committed evils, what compassions shall I neglect?[^67] I have become like unto the publican, and the harlot who wept, and the prodigal son. Therefore I fall down before Thee, O Merciful One: before Thou judgest me, spare me, O God, and have mercy upon me!"

"Overlook mine iniquities, O Lord Who wast born of the Virgin, and purify my heart, making it a temple for Thy Holy Spirit; cast me not away from Thy presence, Thou Who hast measureless great mercy. *For the Martyrs:*"

"Having taken up the Cross of Christ, an invincible weapon, the holy Martyrs abolished all the power of the devil, and received heavenly crowns; they have become a wall for us, interceding on our behalf."

*Glory: Both now: Theotokion:*

"Save Thy servants from perils, O Virgin Theotokos: for under God we all flee unto thee, as unto an unbreakable wall and protectress."

*On Tuesday at the Beatitudes (Blazhenna), Tone 2:*

*The voice of the thief we bring unto Thee, and we pray: Remember us, O Lord, in Thy Kingdom!*

"Overlook my many transgressions, O Lover of mankind, and show me a partaker of the Kingdom, of the celestial splendor; submerged in the abyss of compassion, O Forerunner, in thy goings dry up the abyss of mine evils by thy prayers."

"Having dried up the deceitful streams with streams of your blood, O Sufferers of Christ: ye are worthily glorified. *Glory:*"

*Triadikon:*

"Unto Thee, the Trinity without beginning, do we bow down in worship: Father, and Son, and upright Spirit: a Nature thrice-signified, simple, and thrice-hypostatic. *Both now:*"

*Theotokion:*

"The Fruit of thy womb, O pure one: hath again made him who slipped through the fruit to be an inhabitant of Paradise."

## ON TUESDAY EVENING, AT "LORD, I CALL:"

*Stichera of the Precious Cross, Tone 2.*

*Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Егда́ ѿ дре́ва):* [^68]

[f. 50vB] "Unable to endure the sight of the Sun, the luminaries were darkened when Thou, O Word, didst set upon the Cross; and the earth quaked, and the rocks were split; the temple's beauty was rent in twain; the tombs were opened, and the dead arose; and Hades, giving up all those below, proclaimed them in eternity, and as death was accounted unto all."

"When the noble thief beheld Thee upon the Cross, O Christ, the fruitful Vine: that man became the best and most sincere of thieves; and he received forgiveness for his ancient transgressions with a very devout and small voice, saying unto Him: 'Let us hasten to be Thine, crying out: Remember us also, O Lover of mankind!' "

"It shines like a star in heaven, in the Church the divine Cross..."

[f. 51rA] "...Thy Cross, O Christ: burning up the demons, but enlightening the faithful, and putting to shame the faces of them that crucified Thee; whose ancestors the Cross prefiguring by the tree, formerly delivered from servitude, and made honey flow from the rock, establishing them in goodness."

*Other Stichera to the Most Holy Theotokos.*

*Podoben: "The same Tone and Podoben" (Гла́съ и҆ подо́бенъ то́йже):*
