"As the protectress of all men: the present time is great; here as a good intercessor the Judge hath shown thee, who ineffably didst clothe Him Who took our mixture out of tender compassion, and endured the Cross and death for our sake; Him therefore pray unceasingly: to send down forgiveness of transgressions unto all, O Bride of God."

"Of old the Virgin and Ewe-lamb, beholding Him Who sprang from her womb suspended upon the Tree as one condemned, between two condemned ones: cried aloud, saying: 'O my Son and my God, a dread sight, a dread mystery! To comprehend the abyss of Thy wisdom, none is able: I hymn Thy longsuffering!' "

"Where is the comeliness of Thy countenance? Where hath the beauty of Thy form hidden itself, O Son? How is it that He Who in beauty made ineffable things, O God, fair in beauty, hangs upon the Tree dishonored and shameful for the sake of all men, having neither form nor comeliness, O Child?' the all-good Virgin cried aloud, groaning and weeping."

*Glory: Both now: Stavrotheotokion:*

"The beam of the luminaries set, for He Who is suspended as the Noetic Light..."

[f. 51rB] "...was stripped naked upon the Cross; for the worse is ever overcome by the greater, and the lesser gives place unto the better; how then was it not fitting for the noetic beam to be hidden when Christ shone forth? Thus with worthy voices the all-pure one cried out, beholding Thee, the Beam of luminaries."

*At the Aposticha, Stichera of the Precious Cross, Tone 2:*

"Save me, O Christ Savior, by the power of the Cross, Thou Who didst save Peter in the sea: and have mercy upon me, O God!"

"'Let Him be crucified!' they cried aloud who continually enjoyed Thy gifts; and in place of the Benefactor, they asked to receive a malefactor, a murderer of the righteous. But Christ was silent, enduring their fierceness: desiring to suffer and to save us, as the Lover of mankind."

*For the Martyrs:*

"The ranks of the Martyrs opposed the tormentors, saying: 'We do battle for the King of the heavenly powers; though ye deliver us unto fire and torments, we renounce not the power of the Trinity!' "

*Glory: Both now: Stavrotheotokion:*

"Having endured many pangs at the Crucifixion of thy Son and God, O all-pure one, she groaned with tears and cried aloud: 'Woe is me, sweet Child! How dost Thou suffer unjustly, desiring to deliver the earthborn descendants of Adam?' Therefore, O all-pure Virgin, we entreat thee in faith: make Him merciful unto us!"

*On Wednesday at Matins.*

*After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymns of the Precious Cross, Tone 2:*

[f. 51vA] "Thou hast worked salvation in the midst of the earth, O Christ God; spreading Thine immaculate hands upon the Cross:[^69] Thou hast gathered all the nations, who cry aloud: 'O Lord, glory to Thee!' "

"In the same manner as the enemy held Adam captive through the tree of eating: in like manner Thou, the Lord Himself, didst take the enemy captive through the Tree of the Cross and by Thy death; for unto this the second Adam came: to seek the lost one and to make alive him who had died. O God, glory to Thee!"

*Glory: Both now: Stavrotheotokion:*

"We magnify thee, O Theotokos, crying aloud: Rejoice, O Rod from which God budded forth without seed, and destroyed death upon the Cross!"

*After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns of the Precious Cross, Tone 2:*

"The life-giving Cross of Thy goodness, which Thou hast granted unto us who are unworthy, O Lord, we offer unto Thee in prayer: save the ruler and Thy city that entreat Thee, for the sake of the Theotokos, O only Lover of mankind."

"Thou Who didst enlighten earthly things by the Cross, and called sinners unto repentance: separate me not from Thy flock, O Good Shepherd: but seek me who am lost, and number me with Thy holy flock, O only Merciful One and Lover of mankind."

*For the Martyrs:*

"Thou Who didst enlighten Thy saints more than gold, and glorified Thy venerable ones as God: being entreated by them, O Christ God, give peace unto our life, as the Lover of mankind, and let our prayer be set forth as incense before Thee: Thou Who alone restest in the saints."

[f. 51vB] *Glory: Both now: Stavrotheotokion.*

*Podoben: "Being the wellspring of loving-kindness" (Милосе́рдїа сꙋ́щи):*

"The Virgin and Thy Mother, O Christ, beholding Thee stretched out dead upon the Cross, wept bitterly and said: 'O my Son, what is this dread mystery? Thou Who grantest eternal life unto all, how dost Thou die upon the Cross an ignominious death?' "

*After the 3rd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns, Tone 2.*

*Podoben: "Being the wellspring of loving-kindness" (Милосе́рдїа сꙋ́щи):*

"Like the thief I confess, and I cry unto Thee, O Good One: Remember me, O Lord, in Thy Kingdom, and count me worthy with them, Thou Who of Thine own will didst endure passions for our sake!"

"Thou Who didst endure crucifixion for our sake and didst become dead, O Jesus, Giver of life: that Thou mightest deliver the creation of Thine hands from the condemnation of death, as compassionate God and Lover of mankind, according to the multitude of Thy tender mercies: Thou Who alone art sinless!"

*Glory: Both now: Stavrotheotokion:*

"Preserved by the Precious Cross of thy Son, O pure Lady Theotokos, we easily overcome every assault of the adversary; therefore, as is meet, we bless thee as the Mother of God, the only hope of our souls."

# CANON TO THE PRECIOUS AND LIFE-GIVING CROSS
*Work of Joseph.*[^70]

*Ode 1. Tone 2. Heirmos:*

*"In the deep of old He drowned:"*

"The first-created man transgressed the first commandment of old, and thence found death; by Thine elevation upon the Tree," [f. 52rA] "...O Immortal One, and having tasted of death, Thou didst grant immortality unto all men."

"When the Cross was planted upon the earth, the arrogance of the enemy fell down, and he was trampled underfoot; and man, who was formerly condemned, enters again into Paradise; glory to Thee, our God, Who alone hast thus been well pleased. *For the Martyrs:*"

"Like rams, like noetic lambs, ye were all slaughtered, and pitilessly severed limb from limb, O all-praised Martyrs: and ye were brought unto Him Who was slaughtered, like sheep; and now ye enlighten the Church of the firstborn saints. *For the Martyrs:*"

"Ever exercising steadfastness in suffering, O wise ones, ye cast down the cunning enemies, being severed by the sword, and cast into fire and water; therefore, O passion-bearers, ye were deemed worthy of a blessed end. *Theotokion:*"

"The sacred company of the Prophets named thee an impassable gate, a chosen land, and an unhewn mountain, O all-pure Lady: for thou didst bear the God of the ages, Who of His own will received crucifixion in the flesh."

# ANOTHER CANON TO THE MOST HOLY THEOTOKOS
*Tone 2. Heirmos:*

*"Come, ye peoples, let us sing a song unto Christ God, Who divided the sea and led the people whom He brought out of the bondage of Egypt: for He hath been glorified!"*

"Come, all ye faithful, with one accord let us hymn the Theotokos, for she bore God beyond human understanding; and she unceasingly prays to save us all."

"He Who is the Image of the Father's hypostasis took from thee our mixture," [f. 52rB] "...O Theotokos Mary; He glorified the fallen image, and made it new."

"Thou art more honorable than the Cherubim, and higher than the heavenly circles; for in thy womb, beyond understanding, thou didst dispassionately contain God. *Theotokion:*"

"Thou didst bear the Redemption for our sins, the Benefactor and Lord; having changed the mortality of our forefather Adam, thou didst raise our nature unto the heavens."

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*

*"The barren church of the gentiles hath blossomed like a lily by Thy coming, O Lord: wherein my heart hath been established."*

"Being crucified, Thou didst shake all creation, O Lord, and didst establish it unto its ends, as it hymns Thy power and Thine ineffable condescension, O Word."

"Thou didst open Paradise by Thy Cross, O Master, and brought in the thief who recognized Thy Kingdom and the wealth of Thy divine compassion. *For the Martyrs:*"

"The Martyrs blossomed forth like fragrant roses in the spiritual valleys, and drove away the foul-smelling deceit, and made fragrant the hearts of the faithful. *For the Martyrs:*"

"Luminaries of the universe, faithful saviors: O holy ones, enlighten all with radiant beams, as they worthily bless God."

"Beholding the Giver of life lifted up upon the Tree, and of His own will dying, Who bestows life upon all: the all-immaculate one cried aloud in her maternal heart."

[f. 52vA] *Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*

*"Establish us in Thee, O Lord:"*

"As truly the golden censer, and the jar of manna, and the mountain of God, and the fair divine palace do we name thee, O Virgin."

"Being the church and sacred dwelling of the Word, O Theotokos: be thou ever an expiation for my transgressions, O all-pure Virgin."

"Neither the tongue of the earthborn nor the mind of the bodiless hosts is able to declare thy childbirth: for beyond nature and understanding, O Theotokos, thou didst bear the Creator."

"Be thou a confirmation, a refuge, and a protection, O Virgin Theotokos, unto them that flee unto thee in faith, and proclaim thee as the Mother of God."

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*

*"Thy coming from the Virgin:"*

"Thou didst abolish the dominion of the cruel prince of this world when Thou wast lifted up upon the Tree, and didst bury the curse; therefore we glorify Thee, who are saved for Thy sake, O only Lord."

"Beholding Thee stretched out upon the Tree, the sun hid its light; the mountains and the rocks were split, and the veil of the temple was rent in twain, O Almighty One."

"Being put to death, ye put the enemy completely to death; being scraped with iron, ye stripped off the thickness of carnal mortality, O divine Martyrs, and were clothed with glory. *For the Martyrs:*"

"Being dreadfully beheaded, the Martyrs cut off the heads of the cunning powers: and rejoicing, they inherited surpassing glory. *Theotokion:*"

[f. 52vB] "From thy womb the paternal Effulgence, Christ, shone forth; and being crucified, He enlightened the universe, O unwedded Maiden, and abolished the demonic darkness."

*Another [Canon]. Same Heirmos:*

"Rain down upon me a drop of compunction, O Lady, taking away all the burning heat of my heart, and checking the turbid streams of my slumber."

"Despise me not, O all-pure one, who am slain by the weapon of pleasures and lie wounded: but heal me by the spear and blood of the crucified Son of God and our God."

"Thou who hast enriched all creation with divinity: vouchsafe me who am grievously impoverished to attain divine grace, that I may magnify thee as my good protectress, O all-immaculate one. *Theotokion:*"

"Refresh me, O Maiden, by repentance, and rain down upon my heart which burns with the heat of passions, pouring out upon us the oil of healing, even thy mercies."

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*

*"Mediator between God and men:"*

"Being nailed unto the Cross, Thou didst shake the foundations of the earth; and being pierced with the spear, Thou didst slay the dragon who is the originator of evil: and Thou didst pour forth a drop of salvation unto all, O Christ."

"Enduring not to see him go astray whom Thine hands had formed: Thou didst stretch forth Thine hands upon the Tree, O Word, being put to death: and Thou didst quicken him who had died of old through the tree."

*For the Martyrs:*

"Fervent friends of Christ, intercessors for men, venerable unto the churches, all-adorned vessels of the Spirit: the wise passion-bearers" [f. 53rA] "...are worthily blessed. *For the Martyrs:*"

"Lawfully did the choir of Thy holy sufferers contend; they put the lawless to shame, O only Lawgiver, by Thy power: and having finished the course, they were victoriously crowned. *Theotokion:*"

"Thou wast shown forth incorrupt after childbirth, O pure Virgin, for God was incarnate and born of thee; beholding Whom crucified, unable to bear it, she cried aloud in maternal grief."

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*

*"O Giver of light and of the ages:"*

"We the faithful know Thee to be incarnate of thee, O Theotokos, who didst bear the Son without seed: true God, and man by nature: therefore we glorify thee."

"Fleeing ever in faith unto thy protection and intercession, O all-pure Virgin, for thy sake we are delivered from great and cruel distress."

"Deliver us from temptations, and from perilous thoughts, O all-pure one: from great wrath, and from great sin, from famine and pestilence, and from eternal torment, O Virgin. *Theotokion:*"

"Be thou our protectress, salvation, and hope, O Lady, unto Christians: save them that ever faithfully hymn thee in love, O all-praised Virgin."

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*

*"In the sea-monster, Jonah cried aloud: 'Lead me up from the depth of Hades, O Master, that as unto the Deliverer, in the voice of praise and in the spirit of truth, I may sacrifice unto Thee!' "*

"Laying his hands across their heads of old, Jacob prefigured the Cross:"

[f. 53rB] "...upon which, O Word, Thou didst stretch forth Thy palms: and from the hand of the deceitful warrior Thou didst deliver mankind, O Christ."

"When Thou of Thine own will wast crucified, O Christ, King of all, reigning sin was buried; and Adam, who of old was expelled from Paradise, is settled therein again, hymning Thee."

"Still covered with blood in sacred wounds, who were adorned with heavenly beauty: the truly beloved Martyrs of the Lord I hymn with an unwavering heart. *For the Martyrs:*"

"The divine Martyrs preserved their lamp unquenchable, having richly replenished it with their own blood: and rejoicing, they received entrance into the divine bridal chamber."

"We hymn thee, O all-praised one, who didst bear the all-hymned God, Who upon the Tree destroyed the adversary enemy: and delivered us who hymn His sufferings."

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*

*"Held fast in the deep of sin:"*

"He Who by His will fashions all things was well pleased to dwell within the womb of the unwedded Maiden: and now by a mystery He hath enriched them that cry aloud with incorruption, as an infant."

"Thou art higher than the celestial powers, and more holy, O all-immaculate one: having supernaturally received into thy womb the Word Whom nothing can contain."

"Guide me unto the path of repentance, O Lady: who have gone astray upon the way of life, and often fall into sinful trackless wastes. *Theotokion:*"

"Despise not our supplications, O pure one, who" [f. 53vA] "...hast placed the hope of thy servants upon thee: for thou art a refuge, O Lady, and comfort unto our souls."

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*

*"The god-opposing decree:"*

"The turning sword of old turns its back upon me, ever since Thou, lifted up upon the Cross, wast pierced with the spear, O compassionate Lord; therefore I magnify Thee, having found dispassion through Thy precious Passion."

"The serpent lifted up upon the tree by Moses prefigured the divine elevation of Christ; which put the deceitful serpent to death, and made all alive, putting to death our transgression."

*For the Martyrs:*

"Ye became divine sons by communion with the Son Who is without beginning from the Father without beginning, O holy ones: having been conformed unto His all-pure Passion; therefore He calls you brethren and heirs of His Kingdom. *For the Martyrs:*"

"By elevation upon the cross, like the Master, and pierced with the spear, and severed with the sword: divided between fire and water, and crushed upon wheels, the God-bearing Martyrs rejoiced. *Theotokion:*"

"Beholding the Cluster of grapes which thou didst cultivate without tillage, O pure one, hanging upon the Tree, she cried aloud: 'O sweet Wonder, drip forth sweet wine, whereby the drunkenness of passions may be taken away!' "

*Another [Canon]. Same Heirmos:*

"My strength, and hymn, and salvation, and sure protection, and unassailable wall art thou, O Lady: conquer the demons that war against me," [f. 53vB] "...who ever seek to put my soul to death."

"Thou who didst incarnate God from thy virginal blood, Who made mankind alive of old: deliver me by thy prayers, who am defiled by passions and have fallen through the wiles of the enemy."

*Theotokion:*

"The furnace prefigured thy childbirth, O all-immaculate one, for it burned not the Children; even as the divine Fire burned not thy womb; therefore pray thou to deliver thy servants from eternal fire."

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*

*"The fiery furnace of old:"*

"By the blood that dripped from Thy pure ribs, O Longsuffering One, creation was sanctified, and the rivers of polytheism were dried up: and the cloud of piety was magnified, trampling down the deluge of deceit."

"At Thy Crucifixion the sun was ashamed, and hid its beams; the rocks were split, and Hades below was terrified: and the souls of the righteous leaped for joy, awaiting utter deliverance, O Word."

*For the Martyrs:*

"The relics of the passion-bearers pour forth healings unto the faithful, and ever heal the wounds of diseases that are difficult to cure; 'Wondrous art Thou, O Lord, in Thy holy Martyrs!' we cry aloud with thanksgiving. *For the Martyrs:*"

"Having your mouths muzzled, and your limbs bound fast, and enduring the freezing cold, the weight of burning heat, the tearing of nails, bitter imprisonments, and a violent death, O passion-bearers: ye are therefore glorified with Christ."

[f. 54rA] "...*Theotokion:*"

"Desiring to take flesh from thy womb, the Invisible One becomes visible; and He Who is the curse endured crucifixion and is called a curse, delivering all from the curse, even thy Son, O Lady full of divine joy!"

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*

*"Unto Him Who of old bedewed the Hebrew Children in the fire, and wondrously burned the Chaldeans: let us sing praises, saying: 'Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; praise and highly exalt Him unto all ages!' "*

"Living and unstinting salvation unto us earthborn, O immaculate Ewe-lamb, who didst bear the Lamb of God: despise me not who cry: 'Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; praise and highly exalt Him unto all ages!' "

"Thy divine childbirth, O all-pure one, renewed us, and showed us to be children and sons of the day and of light; and being saved, we cry aloud: 'Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; praise and highly exalt Him unto all ages!' "

"From thy virginal loins thou didst pour forth remission; whence thou didst bring forth water, O pure one, for the healing of the faithful: therefore we all cry aloud: 'Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; praise and highly exalt Him unto all ages!' "

*Theotokion:*

"The ripe Cluster of life hast thou brought forth, O pure one: for thou art the Vine that waters the earth with good things; hymning which, we cry aloud: 'Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; praise and highly exalt Him unto all ages!' "

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*

*"The Son of the Father without beginning, God and Lord:"*

[f. 54rB] "...being incarnate of the Virgin, hath appeared unto us, to enlighten the darkened and to gather together the dispersed; therefore the all-hymned Theotokos do we magnify!"

"Heal my brokenness and my wretchedness by Thy wound, O only Physician: and the image buried by cunning passions, purify by Thy Passion, O Master, God of my salvation!"

"Thou wast seen lifted up upon the cypress, O Master, and upon the pine and cedar, for the sake of Thy goodness: being One of the Holy Trinity, having one Hypostasis in two natures, that Thou mightest save mankind. *For the Martyrs:*"

"Clothed with the Cross as with a shield, O Martyrs, ye were shown forth unharmed by all the arrows of the author of evil; therefore in thought ye trample him underfoot, mocking him as a feeble sparrow evermore. *For the Martyrs:*"

"The earth received your blood among earthly things, but heaven received your divine spirits, standing before the divine Throne with the fiery ranks: O passion-bearing Martyrs, unshakable pillars of the Church! *Theotokion:*"

"Thou hast renewed the corrupted nature of our forefathers, having supernaturally given birth while remaining a virgin unto the Creator of all nature: Whom beholding hanging upon the Cross of old, the all-pure Virgin Mother cried aloud."

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*

*"God the Word from God, Who by ineffable wisdom came to renew Adam, who had fallen grievously through the eating of corruption: ineffably incarnate of the holy Virgin for our sake:"*

[f. 54vA] *"...with one accord we the faithful magnify Him in hymns!"*

"Vouchsafe me divine radiance, O Maiden, who alone didst ineffably give birth to the Lover of mankind, Who borrowed flesh from thee: deliver me from the coming flame and from every torment, who glorify thee in love."

"Having acquired thee, O Theotokos, as a firm protectress, as a hope and a wall, an expectation and a steadfast shelter, an unassailable confirmation and a harbor sheltered from storms: all of us are eternally saved."

"Having borne the Divine Light: enlighten my heart, O Maiden, which is darkened by the many assaults of passions and thoughts of the stranger, ever granting me a drop that purifies me from the defilements of sin, O Virgin."

*At the Aposticha, Stichera of the Precious Cross, Tone 2:*

"The Wood of Thy Cross, O Christ God, hath been shown forth as the Tree of life unto us who believe in Thee; and thereby Thou didst abolish him that held the power of death,[^71] and didst make us alive who were dead through sin; therefore we cry aloud unto Thee: 'O Benefactor of all, Lord, glory to Thee!' "

"Having voluntarily become poor for the sake of Adam's poverty, O Christ God, Thou camest upon earth, incarnate of the Virgin; and Thou didst receive crucifixion, that Thou mightest free us from the bondage of the enemy: O Lord, glory to Thee! *For the Martyrs:*"

"Every city and country honors your relics, O holy passion-bearing Martyrs:"

[f. 54vB] "...for having lawfully contended, ye received crowns from heaven; and therefore ye are the boast of hierarchs, the victory of churches, and the beauty of churches."

*Glory: Both now: Stavrotheotokion.*

*Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Егда́ ѿ дрѣ́ва):*

"The all-ripe Cluster, Whom thou didst carry untilled in thy womb, when thou didst behold Him hanging upon the Tree, O pure one: sobbing, she cried aloud and called out: 'O Child, drip forth sweetness, whereby all drunkenness of passions may be taken away, O Benefactor: for the sake of me who bore Thee, by divine supplications, as Thou art compassionate!' "

*On Wednesday at the Beatitudes (Blazhenna), Tone 2:*

*The voice of the thief we bring unto Thee, and we pray: Remember us, O Lord, in Thy Kingdom!*

"Lifted up upon the Cross, O Savior, Thou didst raise up all human nature with Thyself, which unceasingly hymns Thee."

"The handwriting against Adam Thou didst tear in pieces with Thy spear, inscribing him in the book of the living, O Lover of mankind."

*For the Martyrs:*

"Having become imitators of Him Who endured crucifixion: ye became partakers of His glory, O Martyrs."

*Glory:*

"The Father without beginning, and the Son co-beginningless, let them be hymned in one honor and glory, together with the Spirit."

*Both now: Theotokion:*

"Beholding Him upon the Cross Whom thou didst bear without seed: the Maiden hymned His longsuffering with tears."

## ON WEDNESDAY EVENING, AT "LORD, I CALL:"

[f. 55rA] *Stichera to the Holy Apostles, Tone 2.*

*Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Егда́ ѿ дрѣ́ва):* [^72]

[f. 55rA] "Ye watered all the earth like spiritual rivers flowing forth from Eden; and having offered sacrifice, ye preached the saving preaching, and reaped a fruitful harvest, O wise ones: hiding the saved souls of these within noetic treasures, O disciples of the Lord, as a multi-instructed wealth."

"From the darkness of passions and pleasures, deliver my much-suffering heart, ye who are luminaries of the noetic East, and all-radiant enlighteners, shining forth the Sun unto all, Who dissolved the deceit of the night of malice; pray Him, as His eyewitnesses, to enlighten our minds also."

"Ye were shown forth as truly new tablets of grace inscribed by God, initiates of mysteries and sufficient witnesses: bearing the saving Word, written by the Finger of the Spirit; therefore ye traversed all the ends of the earth, clearly showing forth unto all men the Orthodox faith and the path that leads unto it."

*Other Stichera to Saint Nicholas.*

*Podoben: "The same Tone and Podoben" (Гла́съ и҆ подо́бенъ то́йже):*

[f. 55rB] "Having lived in Myra as a venerable one: thou wast truly shown forth as myrrh, being anointed with noetic myrrh, O holy Nicholas, hierarch of Christ; and exhaling an immortal fragrance of sweet savor unto them that flee beneath thy protection in faith, releasing them from misfortunes, perils, and afflictions, O father, by thy prayers unto the Lord."

"Held fast by a multitude of tribulations, and tossed by the storm of life, and most grievously submerged by waves, and encompassed with sorrows: upon thee do I place all my hope, O father Nicholas: grant me deliverance from all cruel things by thy prayers, O blessed one, which thou offerest unto our Master and God."

"Beset by the gloom and darkening of thoughts, and borne away by demonic deceits, and inflamed by carnal passions, and overcome by the law of sin: illuminate me with the light of grace, for thou art a light in the world, enlightened by a divine ray, O Nicholas worthy of all blessedness."

*Glory: Both now: Theotokion:*

"The Word, the Son consubstantial with the Father and the Holy Spirit: like a great sun shining upon earth from the Virgin's womb: in the last times sent you forth like rays, O glorious Apostles, enlightening all men with the light of faith, who were in the gloom of deceit:"

[f. 55vA] "...and bringing them unto Him by divine teachings."

*At the Aposticha, Stichera of the Apostles, Tone 2:*

"Thou hast magnified the names of the chief Apostles throughout the universe, O Savior; for they were instructed in heavenly and ineffable things, and granted healings unto earthly men; and their mere shadows healed diseases, working wonders from among the fishermen; and from among the Jews, theologically declaring the teachings of grace; for their sake, O Merciful One, grant us great mercy!"

"Being ever assailed by unjust deeds, and fleeing unto Thee, Who art truly God: we offer unto Thee the cry of Thy disciples, saying: 'Save us, O Master, we perish! Show Thyself unto our enemies, we pray Thee: for Thou coverest Thy people and savest them from perils: overlooking our sins through the prayers of the Apostles, for the sake of Thy great goodness, O Lord!' "

*For the Martyrs:*

"Great is the glory which ye acquired by faith, O holy ones; for not only in your sufferings did ye conquer the enemy, but even after death ye drive away spirits and heal the sick, physicians of souls and bodies: pray unto the Lord, that our souls may find mercy!"

*Glory: Both now: Theotokion:*

"Like a fruitful olive tree, O Virgin, thou didst put forth the Fruit of life for us, bearing great and rich mercy for the world."

*On Thursday at Matins.*

*After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymns of the Apostles, Tone 2:*[^73]

[f. 55vB] "Thou Who didst make fishermen wiser than rhetoricians, and sent them forth as preachers throughout all the earth: by Thine ineffable love for mankind, O Christ God, for their sake establish Thy Church, and send down Thy blessing upon the faithful: Thou Who alone restest in the saints."

"The all-simple disciples and eyewitnesses of God: brought to naught the unwise wisdom of philosophers and rhetors, making the nations wise by the simplicity of their preaching, O divine Apostles: that they might orthodoxly hymn the one Creator and Lord."

*Glory: Both now: Theotokion:*

"We magnify thee, O Theotokos, crying aloud: Rejoice, O Cloud of the unwaning Light, for thou didst bear the Lord of glory in thy womb!"

*After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns of the Apostles, Tone 2:*

"Having caught the nations with the net of the Spirit, the fishers taught the ends of the earth to bow down in worship unto Thee, with the Father and the Spirit, O Christ God: for their sake establish Thy Church, and send down Thy blessing upon the faithful, O only Merciful One and Lover of mankind. *For the Martyrs:*"

"O passion-bearers of the Lord, blessed is the earth that was drenched with your blood, and holy are the temples that received your bodies! For at the tribunal ye vanquished the enemy, and preached Christ with boldness: pray Him as the Good One, we entreat you, that our souls may be saved."

*Glory: Both now: Theotokion:*

"We have become partakers of the divine nature..."

[f. 56rA] "...through thee, O Theotokos, ever-Virgin: for thou didst bear God incarnate for us; therefore, as is meet, we all devoutly magnify thee."

*After the 3rd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns, Tone 2.*

*Podoben: "Being the wellspring of loving-kindness" (г҃. стїхолосїи: Гла́с, в҃. По: Милосе́рдїа сꙋ́щи):*

"Having sent forth Thy holy disciples into the world as radiant luminaries, O Word: Thou didst enlighten the world beneath the sun, delivering men from the darkness of ignorance; being ever entreated by their prayers, enlighten my soul thereby, O Lover of mankind, and save me."

"With the rays of wonders, O Nicholas, thou dost enlighten the whole universe: and thou dissolvest the gloom of sorrows and perils, driving away their assault, being a most fervent protector."

*Glory: Both now: Theotokion:*

"O unwedded and all-pure, holy Theotokos and Bride unwedded: together with the Apostles ever entreat thy Son, Whom thou didst bear in the flesh beyond nature: to grant forgiveness of transgressions, direction for our life, and a change of our passions, unto all that hymn thee."

# CANON TO THE HOLY APOSTLES
*Work of Theophanes.*[^74]

*Ode 1. Tone 2. Heirmos:*

*"In the deep of old He drowned:"*

"Having become like lightnings of the Divine Light, O radiant Apostles of the Savior: enlighten me wholly, who am darkened by the blackness of pleasures, and have spent all my life in vain pursuits."

"O disciples and friends of Christ: deliver me from the enemy whose friend I became through contact with evil things, making my spirit worthy of adoption through Him Who loved the human race out of goodness."

[f. 56rB] "O my humble soul, hasten to repent before death, and weep for thyself who art dead: that He Who raised the four-days-dead Lazarus, as He is compassionate, may raise thee also by the entreaties of the Apostles."

*Theotokion:*

"Having borne the good God Who works good in all things, O all-pure one: entreat Him, O all-immaculate one, together with the Prophets, Martyrs, and Apostles: to deliver from all perils them that are held captive by distress."

# ANOTHER CANON TO SAINT NICHOLAS
*Work of Joseph.*

*Ode 1. Tone 2. Heirmos:*

*"Come, ye peoples, let us sing a song:"*

"Ever standing before the divine Throne of grace, O Nicholas: pray that grace and mercy may be granted unto thy servants who invoke thee in faith."

"God hath shown thee forth, O father Nicholas, as a great benefactor and protector upon the earth; therefore, unceasingly night and day, preserve me from the snares of the deceiver."

"As a day-star have I known thee: by thy radiant beams may I be delivered from darkness, and temptations, and perils, and great sin, O father Nicholas. *Theotokion:*"

*Theotokion:*

"Deliver me from bodily sicknesses, and heal the unfathomable wounds of my soul, and snatch me from eternal fire, O only full of grace!"

*Ode 3. Heirmos incipit:*

*"The barren church hath blossomed:"*

[f. 56vA] *Canon to the Apostles:*

"Having acquired as their Teacher the Father's Wisdom through the Spirit: the glorious eyewitnesses condemned the wisdom of the Greeks."

"Loose the barrenness of my soul, O all-praised ones: and cause me to bear the good fruit of deeds in virtues, as worthy and blessed eyewitnesses of the Word."

"Grievously wounded by the poisonous bite of the enemy: heal me by the supplications of Thine Apostles, O abundantly Merciful Benefactor of all."

*Theotokion:*

"Entreat the all-good God, O all-pure one, with all the Apostles: that they who honor thee may be delivered from every harm, distress, and peril."

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*

*"Establish us in Thee, O Lord, Who by the Tree didst put sin to death: and plant Thy fear in our hearts, as Thou art the Lover of mankind."*

*Canon to Saint Nicholas:*

"Being a fountain of healings, O holy one: heal the passions of my soul, and preserve my life, keeping me, thy servant, unharmed."

"Save me from the unjust vanquishing of my mind, from the harm of visible and invisible foes warring against me, as my great protector, O Nicholas."

"He Who alone is good gave thee as a good intercessor unto men, O blessed one; therefore I entreat thee: free me from great evils. *Theotokion:*"

*Theotokion:*

"My strength, and joy, and gladness, and steadfast wall, and protectress art thou, O all-immaculate one, delivering me from temptations and perils."

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*

[f. 56vB] *"Thy coming from the Virgin:"*

*Canon to the Apostles:*

"Unto me who ever hunger and pine away with famine, satisfy me with the food of salvation, O only Lover of mankind, by the divine entreaties of the Apostles who preached Thee throughout the whole world."

"Upon the sea of this life Thou didst lead Thy glorious Apostles like steeds, O Lover of mankind, stirring up the salty and bitter waters of unbelief."

"Having caused Christ the Sun to shine upon them that were in darkness: enlighten me who lie in the darkness of sin, O all-praised Apostles, restraining the wicked thoughts of my heart. *Theotokion:*"

*Theotokion:*

"O all-hymned one, who didst bear the all-praised God: pray with the Apostles for them that hymn thee, that we may be delivered from sins, perils, and afflictions."

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*

*"I hymn Thee, for by hearing, O Lord:"*

*Canon to Saint Nicholas:*

"Having adorned thy throne with virtues, O Nicholas, thou wast shown forth as a precious adornment of hierarchs; therefore I entreat thee: adorn the unseemliness of my soul, and save me from worldly snares."

"Make smooth for me the path that leads yonder, O all-blessed one, lighten for me the waves of this life, and lead me unto the haven of life, O Nicholas, who have enriched myself with thee as a great protector."

"O hearer of divine words, having heard my voice: deliver me from demonic snares, and from lawless men, and from great afflictions that assail me," [f. 57rA] "...O great Nicholas. *Theotokion:*"

*Theotokion:*

"O holy Lady Theotokos: sanctify and preserve me night and day: and direct me unto salvation, who fall into many sins and am cast down by demonic assaults."

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*

*"Mediator between God and men:"*

*Canon to the Apostles:*

"The great Shepherd sent forth His divine disciples like sheep in the midst of wolves, subduing them by the divine power of baptism and the beauty of their words."

"With divine light ye enlightened the hearts of them that were in the darkness of deceit, O Apostles; therefore I entreat you: enlighten me who am darkened by sensual passions, O blessed of God."

"O wretched soul, make haste and repent before the end, crying unto the Lord: 'I have sinned against Thee, O Master, forgive me for the sake of the Apostles, and save me, as Thou art compassionate!' *Theotokion:*"

*Theotokion:*

"With Thy light illuminate me who lie in darkness, O Dwelling-place of light: and pray with the Apostles, O all-immaculate one, to deliver me from every necessity."

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos: O Giver of light:*

*Canon to Saint Nicholas:*

"Fulfiller of the law of God: entreat the good God that I may keep the divine laws, and deliver me from lawless enemies and from the most grievous harm, O all-blessed Nicholas."

"As of old Thou didst appear, O Savior, and deliver the three youths: so also deliver me from great sin by thy prayers unto God, O God-wise Nicholas."

[f. 57rB] "Sacred celebrant of Christ, surety of sinners, great wonderworker: pray unto God the Giver of good, that He put me not to shame in the hour of judgment. *Theotokion:*"

*Theotokion:*

"O pure Mother of God, who art good: stand by and deliver me who am held by many passions, that being saved, I may hymn thee with soul, heart, and tongue."

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*

*"In the deep of sin:"*

*Canon to the Apostles:*

"Bearing the water of life: water my soul which is consumed by the heat of sin, I pray you, O disciples of the Savior."

"Having become noetic heavens, O God-radiant Apostles: ye declare the ineffable glory of God; pray ye that all of us may attain unto it."

"Tossed grievously upon the deep: unto Thee, the Pilot of all, do I come; for the sake of Thine Apostles, direct me unto the haven of salvation. *Theotokion:*"

*Theotokion:*

"With all the heavenly powers, with the Prophets, Apostles, and Martyrs: entreat thy Son for our sake, O Virgin Bride of God."

*Another [Canon]. Same Heirmos:*

*Canon to Saint Nicholas:*

"Having been primate of the people of Myra, O Nicholas, thou didst establish the assemblies of the faithful with thy good deeds: deliver me from foul-smelling transgressions."

"Having acquired a heart brighter than the sun, O father: enlighten me wholly, driving away the darkness of temptations and sorrows, O Nicholas."

"Deliver me from all distress:"

[f. 57vA] "...as thou hast an abundance of mercy, O Nicholas; strengthen me to walk the narrow path that leads unto the Lord. *Theotokion:*"

*Theotokion:*

"Unto me who call upon thee at every time, O all-pure one: may I find thee as a helper, delivering me from great distress and from dread torments."

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*

*"The god-opposing decree:"*

*Canon to the Apostles:*

"Kindled by the fire of the Divine Spirit, O Apostles: ye quenched the coals of deceit, and kindled the divine love in the minds of all the faithful; therefore with loud voices we honor you."

"Ye hated the world and all that is in the world: and loved Christ, Who came into the world in the flesh as man; pray Him, O divine Apostles, to free me from all cruel things in this life."

"O righteous and compassionate Judge, Who alone knowest my hidden transgressions: in the hour of judgment condemn me not, neither cast me into the fire, by the supplications of Thine Apostles. *Theotokion:*"

*Theotokion:*

"Unconsumed by the fire of the Godhead, having ineffably given birth, O Virgin unwedded Maiden: therefore pray with the Apostles, O pure one: to free me from the eternal flame, who glorify thee."

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos: Unto the golden image:*

*Canon to Saint Nicholas:*

"Tossed every day by a storm of temptations, O father Nicholas, passing through the midst of snares like fire: beneath thy generous shelter do I flee; preserve me unharmed, entreating the good God and Lord."

[f. 57vB] "Having heard my words swiftly, O father Nicholas, hasten to come unto my aid, who am tossed by sorrows, and worldly necessities, and demonic afflictions: that being saved, I may hymn thy protection."

"Thou who of old didst appear in a dream unto the emperor, delivering the innocent who were about to die: deliver me from the perils that ever assail me, and from bodily ailments and diseases of soul, O father Nicholas. *Theotokion:*"

*Theotokion:*

"Thee alone do I offer as my helper, O all-pure one; unto thee who hast been given unto me as the guardian of all my life; despise me not, thy servant, my only protectress, but save me who sing unto thee: 'Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!' "

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*

*"The fiery furnace of old:"*

*Canon to the Apostles:*

"Descending upon you in the likeness of fire, the Comforter Spirit in fiery form made you as luminaries, burning up all godlessness: and enlightening all with the words of piety, O divine Apostles of the Word."

"Grievously tempest-tossed by passions, heal my uncorrected heart, O Compassionate One, I pray Thee; enlighten my soul and direct my mind, which hath inclined toward evil: through the entreaties of Thy disciples."

"Sigh, O my soul, and weep bitterly; and lament before the end, before inconsolable weeping overtake thee; and cry aloud unto the Creator: 'Have compassion upon me, through the prayers of Thine Apostles!' *Theotokion:*"

*Theotokion:*

"The furnace which burned not the Children of old prefigured thy childbirth, O all-immaculate Virgin;" [f. 58rA] "...therefore I entreat thee: pray with the Apostles, in the time of judgment, to deliver me from the fire of Gehenna."

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*

*"Into the fiery furnace with the Children:"*

*Canon to Saint Nicholas:*

"Having received power from God to bind and to loose, O God-wise father Nicholas: loose the bonds of my sins by thy prayers, and bind me unto the divine love of the Master Who desired to save me."

"By thy divine visitation, visit me day and night, making smooth the paths of my humble soul; and preserve me, O holy Nicholas, unharmed from the assaults of the cunning deceiver."

"Stretch forth thy hand unto divine help, snatch me from the cruel corruption of enemies, thou who of old didst deliver the youths from bitter death: that I may honor thee as a good protector."

"When Thou, O God, shalt sit upon Thy dread Throne to judge the world: enter not into judgment with Thy servant, but vouchsafe me to be among the saved, by the prayers of Nicholas. *Theotokion:*"

*Theotokion:*

"Beyond nature by thy childbirth, O Theotokos, thou hast magnified us who were brought low by great and countless evils; therefore we entreat thee, O all-pure one: magnify thy rich mercies toward us."

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*

*"The Son of the Father without beginning:"*

*Canon to the Apostles:*

"O glorious choir! O blessed Apostles!"

[f. 58rB] "Disciples of the Savior, all-wise preachers: deliver me from every harm, from great wrath, from great sin, from great transgression, and from various perils!"

"Me who am condemned, me who am uncorrected, who have neglected Thy commandments, and followed harmful deceits: turn me back, O Lord, by the prayers of Thine Apostles!"

"I bring an uncorrected soul, a conscience buried beneath the weight of transgressions, a defiled heart, and a wretched mind: I cry unto Thee, O Lover of mankind: for the sake of the Apostles, have compassion upon me by Thy mercy! *Theotokion:*"

*Theotokion:*

"The Apostles, O all-pure one, preached thy Son unto all the world as God and man; therefore with them pray thou that they who magnify thee in faith may be delivered from torments on the dread day of judgment."

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*

*"God the Word from God, Who by ineffable wisdom came to renew Adam, who had fallen grievously through the eating of corruption: ineffably incarnate of the holy Virgin for our sake: with one accord we the faithful magnify Him in hymns!"*

*Canon to Saint Nicholas:*

"A rule of priesthood and pattern of meekness do we know thee to be, O all-wise Nicholas; calm by thy prayers the storm of passions and perils that rises up day by day, and preserve me unharmed."

"As a most sacred vessel receptive of the divine myrrh, which through thy prayers was poured forth upon the earth: unto all of us" [f. 58vA] "...giving fragrance to our hearts: having been the wise primate of Myra, drive away the foul stench of temptations by thy prayers."

"Thou art the comfort of my soul, O father; invisible amidst a multitude of cruel afflictions, do thou boundless calm my temptations, which the deceitful one stirs up against me day and night, appearing as my good protector, O Nicholas."

"The dread day of the Master approaches at the doors; what wilt thou do, O my soul, having a multitude of sins? Make haste therefore before the end, and cry unto the Lord diligently: 'By the prayers of Nicholas Thy hierarch, save me!' *Theotokion:*"

*Theotokion:*

"Spare me, O Lord, spare me when Thou art about to judge; and condemn me not unto the fire, neither rebuke me in Thy fury: the Virgin who bore Thee entreats Thee, O Christ, together with the multitude of angels and the glorious Nicholas."

## ON THURSDAY EVENING, AT "LORD, I CALL:"

*Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Егда́ ѿ дрѣ́ва):* [^76]

[f. 59rA] "O Son, when Thou wast nailed unto the Cross: the sun beheld it and was darkened for fear of Thee; and the veil of the temple was rent in twain; the earth quaked, and the rocks likewise were split in trembling: unable to bear the sight of their Creator and God suffering unjustly of His own will upon the Tree, and insulted by the lawless."

"The all-cunning serpent was cast down entirely upon the earth; he was utterly brought to naught, and lies in a marvelous fall, when Thou wast lifted up upon the Tree, O Lover of mankind; and Adam is loosed from the curse and saved, who was formerly condemned; therefore we also pray: 'Save us, have compassion upon all of us, and vouchsafe us Thy Kingdom!' "

"When Thou wast lifted up upon the Cross, and Thy side was pierced with a spear, O Sinless One: the sun hid itself, not wishing to see it, O Savior; the earth was shaken, and the rocks were split in terror at that time while Thou wast insulted; and all creation cried aloud: 'Glory to Thy Crucifixion, O Word, whereby Thou hast saved all, O Lover of mankind!' "

Hasten and be glorified, that they who glorify Thy divine sufferings may obtain divine glory!' "

"When the unwedded Maiden beheld her Son taken down from the Tree, stretched out and laid lifeless upon the earth like a mortal man: embracing Him in her bosom and kissing His lips and eyes, she cried aloud unto Him in wonder: 'How is it that Thou Who quickenest all art now seen by me speechless and motionless? In truth, a great wonder!' "
