## ON FRIDAY AT MATINS

*After the 1st Psalter Stichology, Sessional Hymns (Sedalna) of the Cross, Tone 2:*[^77]

"Thou didst work salvation in the midst of the earth, O Christ God: stretching out Thine all-pure [f. 59vB] hands upon the Cross, gathering all the nations who cry: 'O Lord, glory to Thee!' "

"In the manner wherein the enemy led Adam captive, deceived by the tree, O Lord: so likewise hast Thou Thyself, the second Adam, led the enemy captive by the Wood of the Cross: seeking him who had gone astray, and quickening him who was dead; O God, glory to Thee!"

*Glory: Both now: Stavrotheotokion:*

"The Virgin and Thy Mother, O Christ, beholding Thee stretched out dead upon the Tree, weeping bitterly, said: 'O my Son, what is this dread mystery? How dost Thou, Who grantest eternal life unto all, die of Thine own will upon the Cross by a reproachful death?' "

*After the 2nd Psalter Stichology, Sessional Hymns, Tone 2:*

"Unassailable is Thy Cross, O Christ, which Thou alone hast granted unto us who are unworthy: we bring it unto Thee in prayer; save our Emperor and Thy city, who pray unto Thee."

*Other [Kathisma Hymns]: O Only Lover of mankind:*

"We bow down before Thine all-pure icon, O Good One, asking forgiveness of our transgressions, O Christ God: for of Thine own will Thou wast well pleased to ascend the Cross, that Thou mightest deliver them whom Thou hadst fashioned from the bondage of the enemy. Therefore, giving thanks, we cry aloud unto Thee: 'Thou hast filled all things with joy, O our Savior, Who didst come to save the world!' "

*For the Martyrs:*

"Fervently having Him Who decks the heavens with clouds as their raiment in the world, the holy ones endured torments from the lawless, and abolished the deceit of idols. By their prayers, deliver us also from the invisible enemy, O Savior, [f. 60rA] and save us."

*Glory: Both now: Stavrotheotokion:*

"Standing by Thy Cross, she who bare Thee without seed, unable to bear the sight of Thee suffering unjustly, wept with lamentation and cried aloud unto Thee: 'How sufferest Thou, Who art dispassionate by nature, O sweetest Son? I hymn Thine endless goodness!' "

*After the 3rd Psalter Stichology, Sessional Hymns, Tone 2:*

"Like the thief do I confess, and cry aloud unto Thee, O Good One: 'Remember me, O Lord, in Thy Kingdom, and number me with him, Thou Who didst willingly accept suffering for our sake!' "

"Thou Who didst enlighten the earthborn by Thy Cross and didst call sinners unto repentance: separate me not from Thy flock, O Good Shepherd: but seek me who have gone astray, O Master, and number me with Thy holy flock, O only Merciful One and Lover of mankind."

*Glory: Both now: Stavrotheotokion:*

"Preserved by the Precious Cross of Thy Son, O pure Lady Theotokos: we all easily conquer every assault of the adversary. Therefore, as is meet, we bless thee as the Mother of God, and the sole hope of our souls."

# CANON TO THE PRECIOUS AND LIFE-GIVING CROSS
*The Composition of Joseph. Tone 2.*[^78]

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*

*"Traversing the untrodden, unaccustomed, unwetted path of the sea, chosen Israel cried aloud: 'Let us sing unto the Lord, for gloriously is He glorified!' "*

"Having accepted crucifixion, and being nailed with nails in secret [ignominy], O Word: Thou didst will to honor all men who glorify Thy voluntary sufferings."

[f. 60rB] "Stretching out Thy palms upon the Cross, O Savior, Thou Who didst stretch out the heaven like a curtain: Thou didst embrace the nations and peoples who glorify Thy voluntary sufferings."

*For the Martyrs:*

"Taking up the Cross upon their shoulders, the fellow-sufferers firmly followed Him Who was crucified, accomplishing in their bodies the likeness of His divine sufferings."

*For the Martyrs:*

"The Angelic Powers sang praises, seeing your sufferings, and the multitude of men rejoiced, O victorious Martyrs, most ardent contemplators of the Cross."

*Theotokion:*

"The word of the honored Prophet is fulfilled: for a sword pierced through thy heart, O Lady, when thou didst behold Thy Son pierced upon the Cross."

*Another Canon, to the Most Holy Theotokos. Tone 2. Heirmos:*

*"Come, ye peoples, let us sing:"*

"Having given birth unto the fountain of immortality: heal me who am wounded by passions, O Maiden, and snatch me from eternal fire, O only one rejoiced by God!"

"Deliver me from bodily ailments, and heal the hidden wounds of my soul: and snatch me from eternal fire, O only God-graced one!"

"Unto thy grace do I now flee, O Virgin all-pure Mother: deliver thy servant from sicknesses of soul, and from soul-corrupting arrows, and from eternal fire."

"Thou art my fervent cleansing, O Lady; unto thee do I flee [f. 60vA] and I shall obtain the salvation of my soul; for thou art able to save every soul, being the Mother of God."

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*

*"Establishing me upon the rock of faith, Thou hast enlarged my mouth against mine enemies: for my spirit hath rejoiced to sing: 'None is holy as our God, and none is righteous save Thee, O Lord!' "*

"The incorruptible Cluster of Grapes hanging upon the Tree dripped divine sweetness, gladdening the hearts of men, and ever stilling the drunkenness of malice by grace: Jesus, the Redeemer of our souls."

"Thou wast lifted up upon the Tree of Thine own will, O Jesus, and didst cast down all the malice of the devil; and man who had fallen into destruction through a perverted mind, Thou hast raised up, O abundantly Merciful One."

*For the Martyrs:*

"Kindled with the fire of divine love, the valiant ones feared not the fire, and were not terrified by death, looking toward the immortal gifts to receive them, and unending joy, and unsetting light."

*For the Martyrs:*

"With the raw streams of their blood, the passion-bearers dyed their most radiant purple robe; and clothed therein, bearing the divine Cross in their right hand as a sceptre, they judge and ever reign."

*Theotokion:*

"With the mouths of the bodiless ranks: for thou gavest birth unto the Master of all in the flesh, Who loosed all who were bound by the tree, O Maiden unwedded of God, and bound the faithful in His love."

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos: The same.*

[f. 60vB] "Thou didst bear the King without beginning, O Virgin Mother, Who took on flesh incorruptibly: Him therefore entreat, as the Lover of mankind, to save His servant from every tribulation and from future condemnation."

"Dispel the perplexity of my soul, heal its wounds, and drive away its festering by thy divine power; and grant me a stream of compunction, thou who gavest birth unto the ever-flowing Fountain."

"Heal my ailing soul, which is in peril through temptations and despondency, O Mother of God; and grant tears of repentance unto mine eyes, and plant the fear of my Good One within it, O all-pure one."

"Having spent my life in slothfulness, and defiled my heart with passions, I come unto thee, O Lady, in compunction of soul, and pray: 'Have compassion and save me, establishing me in the paths of repentance!' "

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*

*"Thou camest forth from the Virgin, neither an ambassador nor an angel, but Thou Thyself, O Lord, incarnate, and hast saved all of me, a man. Therefore I cry unto Thee: 'Glory to Thy power, O Lord!' "*

"Thou wast hung upon the Tree, O All-powerful One, Who didst hang the earth upon the waters; when Thy side was pierced with a spear, Thou didst drip blood for our freedom, unto the redemption of all."

"When Thy side was pierced, my knee was healed; when Thou wast struck upon the cheek with a hand, we obtained freedom; and when Thou didst taste gall, we were delivered from sweet food [of sin], O Christ."

*For the Martyrs:*

"Having struck down the deceitful serpent with arrows, [f. 61rA] ye ever heal the wounds of our hearts, welling forth grace from the fountains of the Savior, O divine Martyrs."

*For the Martyrs:*

"Ye inflicted a bodily wound upon the enemy, O all-honored ones, being covered in blood with wounds, stretched out upon the cross and flayed, O God-illumined passion-bearers."

*Theotokion:*

"The Most High was incarnate of thy most pure blood; Whom beholding unjustly lifted up upon the Tree, the all-pure one groaned, weeping, and magnified His loving-kindness."

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos: I have heard by report:*

"Heard in truth: giving birth beyond nature unto the praised Word of God; and I pray: heal the mortal diseases of my soul, and deliver me from cruel condemnation."

"Ever deify us with thy rich mercies, O Virgin, stilling diseases and destroying the passions of rational souls; therefore loose the bonds of the sins and many sicknesses of my heart."

"I have defiled my soul with shameful things; do thou who wast the most honorable receptacle cleanse me, O Mother of God, guiding me unto the light of repentance, and delivering me from the fire to come."

"Enlighten my mind by prayer, O all-pure Lady; still the waves of my passionate heart, consuming carnal desires, and guiding me unto the divine haven."

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*

[f. 61rB] *"A live Coal having formerly appeared unto Isaiah, the Sun hath shone forth from the virginal womb, granting the enlightenment of the knowledge of God unto them that were astray in darkness."*

"Nailed unto the Cross out of loving-kindness, O Master, Thou didst tear me away from the depth of evil; and being willingly wounded, pierced with thorns, Thou Who didst crown the whole earth with flowers: Thou dost uproot the thorns of my passions from the root, O Word, and plantest Thy knowledge within me."

*For the Martyrs:*

"By the strength of your weakness, O holy Martyrs, having willingly girded and strengthened yourselves, ye brought to naught every power of the enemy."

*For the Martyrs:*

"Having striven greatly upon earth, O holy ones, ye found great glory in the heavens; and ye deliver us from great afflictions, who honor your grace."

*Theotokion:*

"He Who is carried in God-befitting manner upon the shoulders of the Cherubim in heaven, in truth, O all-pure one, sits upon thine arms, and being crucified, He delivered all from corruption."

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos: Enlightenment:*

"Slain by the snares and traps of the deceitful one: quicken me, O all-immaculate Lady Theotokos, who gavest birth unto the hypostatic Life of all, that I may piously hymn thee unto ages."

"Having shown forth the Lamb and Shepherd, O Virgin Mother, shepherd me aright who have gone astray, and vouchsafe me to be numbered with the sheep on the right hand in the day of judgment, that I may sing of thy saving grace."

[f. 61vA] of the darkening of passions, from the stumbling-blocks that ever arise through the temptations of the alien, and from the future torments of eternal sinners: deliver me, O Maiden, by thy prayers, I beseech thee."

"O Bride of God, in whom the one divine Word made His abode, enlightening the whole inhabited earth: cause the ray of true repentance to shine upon me, illuminating the darkness of my passions, O all-immaculate one."

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*

*"Hearing the voice of prayerful words from an aching soul, O Master: deliver me from cruel things; for Thou alone art the cause of our salvation!"*

"Offering Thy back unto stripes, and Thy cheeks unto buffeting, and Thy face, O Savior, unto spitting: Thou hast saved me who have sinned greatly beyond mind."

"Like a lamb led to the slaughter wast Thou, O Christ God, bringing back unto life them that were slain by the venomous bite of the noetic wolf: glory to Thy crucifixion!"

*For the Martyrs:*

"Keeping the laws of the Master, the Martyrs utterly turned away from the lawless counsel of the transgressors; and having died, they received the life to come."

*For the Martyrs:*

"Having arrayed themselves with joy against the opposing powers, O holy ones, with divine weapons ye conquered them, and received crowns of victory from God."

*Theotokion:*

"That He might deify man, God is born of the incorrupt Virgin, and is crucified, [f. 61vB] and tastes death: putting to death by the Cross him that slew me of old."

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*

*"Held fast in the abyss of sins, I ever flee unto thee; save me by thy prayers and preserve me: for whatsoever thou desirest, thou canst also perform, as the Mother of Him Who strengthens all."*

"Tempest-tossed by the storm of sorrows, and consumed by present necessities, save me, O Theotokos Virgin, thy servant."

"Vouchsafe me thy loving-kindness, me who am held fast by mercilessness and malice; and snatch me from the impending torments and eternal fire."

"Having conceived the all-pure Lamb Who takes away the sins of the world, thou gavest Him birth, O all-immaculate one: cease not to pray that He grant me forgiveness of sins."

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*

*"The God-opposing command of the lawless tyrant raised a high flame: but Christ spread spiritual dew upon the God-fearing children, He Who is blessed and supremely praised, the God of our fathers!"*

"Me who fell through transgression, Thou didst raise up, being lifted up upon the Cross, O Resurrection and Upraising of all, O Word; and having cast down the crushing adversary, Thou didst show him utterly dead: glory to Thy dominion!"

"With nails wast Thou nailed, O Christ, for the sins of our forefather, and with a reed Thou didst write freedom for all [f. 62rA] men: glory to Thy suffering, whereby we were delivered from the darkness of passions!"

*For the Martyrs:*

"Their bodies were severed by foul and murderous hands, O victorious great Martyrs of Christ, yet they remained inseparable in spirit from God, severing and slaying the deceitful enemy with the sword of courage."

*For the Martyrs:*

"Leading behind themselves an invincible army by the unconquerable strength of the Crucified Christ, they utterly destroyed the destructive host, having victory to receive crowns, and a blessed and peaceful life."

*Theotokion:*

"The ensouled Palace of the womb and the fiery-radiant Throne was the Virgin shown to be; seated upon which, He raised up all men from the first fall, and honored them by sitting together with the Father."

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos: The same.*

"Having given birth unto our hypostatic Life, and having destroyed death by death: deaden the passions of my heart, and grant me fountains of tears, O pure one, that I may ever glorify thee."

"O unashamed hope, known expectation, unassailable wall, protection and helper: be thou unto me, O all-immaculate one, a guide unto repentance, and guide me, O pure one, unto the light of repentance and compunction."

"Deliver thy servant from every demonic malice and sorrow, and from condemnation and eternal fire, entreating thy Son, that I may ever glorify thee with faith."

"An all-pure conception and an incorrupt [f. 62rB] childbearing didst thou alone display, remaining a Virgin: for having conceived Christ, the pure God Who is over all, Who became man, thou art the salvation and redemption of the faithful."

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*

*"Unto the golden image the thrice-blessed youths bowed not down: seeing the immutable living image of God, in the midst of the flame they sang: 'Let all creation sing unto the Lord, and highly exalt Him unto all ages!' "*

"The disobedient people, doing all lawless things without fear: lifting Thee up upon the Tree, O Compassionate One, Who dost justify the lawless, they crucified Thee in the midst of the lawless; Whom all creation glorifies as God and Master, singing of Thy long-suffering."

"Thou didst redden Thy fingers, O Christ, when nailed upon the Tree; the blood formerly offered unto demons unto the destruction of those who brought it, Thou didst cause to cease; therefore all creation glorifies Thee unto ages, singing of Thy love for mankind."

*For the Martyrs:*

"Filled with the appearance of living creatures, O Martyrs: having poured forth streams of blood in divine currents, ye cry with unwavering faith: 'Let all creation sing unto the Lord, and highly exalt Him unto all ages!' "

*For the Martyrs:*

"The innumerable multitude of your blood, O holy ones, extinguished the fire of impiety, and destroyed the manifold deceit of the seducers; and it enlightened all the faithful who sing: 'Let all creation sing unto the Lord, and highly exalt..."

[f. 62vA] Him unto all ages!' "

"The immaculate Ewe-lamb, the adornment of Prophets and Martyrs: beholding Thee, the Word without beginning, lifted up as a Lamb upon the Tree, wept bitterly and said: 'Let all ensouled creation sing unto the Lord, and highly exalt Him unto all ages!' "

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*

*"Unto Him Who descended into the fiery furnace unto the Hebrew children, and turned the flame into dew, God: sing, all ye works of the Lord, and highly exalt Him unto all ages!"*

"A haven unto Christians and a helper art thou; despise me not who am held fast by cruel things, O all-pure Virgin, who am ever surrounded by tribulations and by many assaults of cunning demons."

"Condemn not the voice of my prayerful armies, O dread protector, but snatch me from every disease and great rebuke by thy supplications; for thy maternal prayer inclines God."

"A tempest of passions of the most cruel sorrows hath arisen, O pure and blessed one; and conquer, O Maiden, all the bodiless enemies who unsparingly attack my poverty, that I may glorify thee."

"From the unquenchable fire, and the flame of sins, and the fire of passions and Gehenna, and the assault of demons, snatch me at the hour of death, O only Mother of God, protectress of the faithful."

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*

*"Every tongue is at a loss to praise thee as is meet, and even a transcendent mind is dazed to sing [f. 62vB] thee, O Theotokos; yet, being good, accept our faith, for thou knowest our divine love; for thou art the protectress of Christians, and thee do we magnify!"*

"Of old did Isaac prefigure Thy passion; being bound as a type, yet not enduring death, the ram was offered in his stead as a true sacrifice; but when Thou wast sacrificed of Thine own will, we were loosed from evil."

"Fair in beauty beyond the sons of men, O Christ, yet having neither beauty nor comeliness in Thy passion, hanging upon the Wood of the Cross, Thou didst adorn the ugliness of the whole human race: glory to Thy tender compassion, O only Merciful Lord!"

*For the Martyrs:*

"Having truly become fellow-citizens of the heavenly inhabitants, O divine Martyrs, equal in honor with the Angels, like shining fellow-citizens, and the Church of the holy firstborn: ye joyfully enlighten them that shine with divine light, being adorned with crowns of martyrdom."

*For the Martyrs:*

"O beloved friends of Him Who loved you most gloriously: deliver me from deceitful companions, who have a worldly image and service; and grant enlightenment and remission of cruel sins unto all who celebrate your memory without ceasing."

*Theotokion:*

"The radiant beauty of the natural course withdrew, when it beheld Thee, the Sun of righteousness, lifted up upon the Cross of Thine own will; and the Virgin, with the virginal disciple, cried aloud with weeping: 'Woe is me!' crying: 'What is this strange sight?' "

[f. 63rA] *Another [Canon]. Heirmos: He Who was begotten without beginning:*

"The Lord Who loves mankind, the only abundantly Merciful One, beyond mind and Word didst thou bear; Him entreat, O Virgin, at the dread hour of judgment, to deliver thy servant from eternal fire."

"Unto them that hymn thee there, and glorify thee with faith, and ever flee unto thy divine protection: grant from heaven remission of cruel things, O Bride of God, and from tormenting passions, and deliver them from torment and judgment."

"Having tasted of the fruit of sin, which was sweet in days, but most bitter in tasting, which hath slain me: of which I drank to satiety, snatch me from that dread judgment, O all-pure Virgin Mother."

"Bless my humble heart, O Lady, which is injured by pleasurable bars, as the Mother of the Good One, and being good unto all; and lead me unto the doors of good repentance."

### AT THE APOSTICHA, STICHERA OF THE CROSS

*Tone 2:*[^79]

"Thy Cross, O Christ God, a tree of life hast Thou shown unto us who believe in Thee; and thereby having abolished the dominion of him that had the power of death, Thou hast quickened us who were dead through sin; therefore we cry aloud unto Thee, O Benefactor of all: 'O Lord, glory to Thee!' "

"Willingly having become poor, for the sake of Adam's cleansing, O Christ God, Thou camest upon the earth, incarnate of the Virgin; and Thou didst accept crucifixion, that Thou mightest free us from the bondage of the enemy: O Lord, glory to Thee!"

[f. 63rB] "Having suffered for Christ even unto death, O passion-bearing Martyrs: your souls indeed are in the hand of God in the heavens; and throughout all the world your relics are honored: Hierarchs and Kings bow down, and all peoples rejoicing, we customarily cry aloud: 'Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His venerable ones!' "

*Glory: Both now: Stavrotheotokion.*

*Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Егда́ ѿ дре́ва):*

"When the immaculate Ewe-lamb beheld her Lamb led of His own will unto the slaughter like a man: weeping, she said: 'Dost Thou now hasten to leave me childless, O Christ, who gave Thee birth? What is this that Thou hast done, O Redeemer of all? Yet I hymn and glorify Thy supreme loving-kindness, which is beyond mind and word, O Lover of mankind!' "

# ON FRIDAY, THE BEATITUDES (BLAZHENNA)
*Tone 2:*

"We bring unto Thee the voice of the thief, and pray: 'Remember us, O Lord, in Thy Kingdom!' "

"Thou didst uproot the malicious thorn, O Master, willingly wearing the crown of thorns, O Long-suffering One."

"Crucified, O Sinless One, upon Golgotha: Thou didst crush the head of the cunning one, and hast saved all creation."

"By their crushing, the Martyrs crushed all the power of the enemy, and received crowns of victory. *Glory:*"

"By the sprinkling of divine blood, the faithful are enlightened, worshiping the one Godhead in three Persons. *Both now:*"

"Beholding Christ as a Lamb hung upon the Tree, the all-immaculate one, weeping, magnified Him."

## ON FRIDAY EVENING, AT "LORD, I CALL:"

[f. 63vA] *Stichera to the Holy Martyrs, Hierarchs, and Venerables. Tone 2.*

*Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Егда́ ѿ дре́ва):* [^80]

[f. 63vA] "Yielding their flesh unto wounds, and enduring most bitter torments, and a violent death, O all-praised Martyrs: ye put the tormentors to shame, and utterly abolished the honor of idols; preaching Christ as the only God and Master, before Whom, crowned with crowns, O glorious ones, ye stand together with the Angelic ranks."

"Preachers of the Word Who appeared upon the earth were ye shown to be, O divine ones, and ye taught all men piety; and setting forth the Orthodox divine teachings, whereby ye drove heresy far away from the Church of Christ: therefore, as sacred ministers of the Trinity, lead all men into the mansions that abide ever, O blessed ones."

*Other Stichera to the Martyrs.*

*Podoben: "The same Tone and Podoben" (Гла́съ и҆ подо́бенъ то́йже):*

"Having not loved earthly pleasures, O passion-bearers: ye were counted worthy of heavenly good things, and became fellow-citizens with the Angels. By their prayers, have mercy upon us and save us."

"When the holy Martyrs pray for us and hymn Christ: all deceit ceases, and the human race is saved through faith."

"The ranks of the Martyrs opposed [f. 63vB] the tyrants, saying: 'We fight for the King of hosts: even if ye deliver us unto fire and torments, we reject not the power of the Trinity!' "

*Glory: Both now: Theotokion:*

"The shadow of the law hath passed away..."

### AT THE APOSTICHA, STICHERA

*Tone 2. For the Martyrs:*

"Great is the glory which ye acquired through faith, O holy ones: for not only did ye conquer the enemy in your sufferings, but even after death ye drive away spirits and heal the sick, being physicians of souls and bodies; pray ye unto the Lord, that our souls may find mercy."

*Verse: Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen and taken to Thyself, O Lord.*

*Hymn for the Departed (Поко́инъ):*

"Like a flower fades, and like a shadow passes by, and every man is dissolved; but again when the trumpet sounds, the dead, as in an earthquake, shall all arise to meet Thee, O Christ God; then, O Master, those whom Thou hast translated from among us, establish in the courts of Thy Saints: the spirits of Thy servants, O Christ."

*Verse: Their souls shall dwell among good things.*

"Woe is me! What a struggle hath [f. 64rA] the soul when separating from the body! Woe is me! How much it weeps then, and there is none to have mercy upon it! Lifting up its eyes unto the Angels, it prays in vain; stretching out its hands unto men, it hath none to help. Therefore, my beloved brethren, knowing our short life, let us ask rest from Christ for the departed, and for our souls great mercy."

*Glory: Both now: Theotokion:*

"Save Thy servants from perils, O Theotokos Virgin: for under God we all flee unto thee, as unto an unbreakable wall and protectress."

## ON SATURDAY AT MATINS

*After the 1st Psalter Stichology, Sessional Hymns (Sedalna) to the Martyrs, Tone 2:*[^81]

"Fervently having Him Who decks the heavens with clouds as their raiment in the world, the holy ones endured torments from the lawless, and abolished the deceit of idols. By their prayers, deliver us also from the invisible enemy, O Savior, and save us."

*Apostles, Prophets, and Martyrs, Hierarchs, Venerables, and Righteous:*

"Who have finished the course well, and kept the faith: having boldness toward the Savior, entreat Him for our sake, we pray, that our souls may be saved."

*Glory: Both now: Theotokion:*

"All thy mysteries are beyond comprehension, all most glorious, O Theotokos: sealed with purity and preserved in virginity, thou wast known to be a true Mother, having given birth unto the true God; Him entreat, that our souls may be saved."

[f. 64rB] *After the 2nd Psalter Stichology, Sessional Hymns, Tone 2:*

"Thou Who didst enlighten Thy saints more than gold, and didst glorify Thy Venerables as Thou art good: being entreated by them, O Christ God, pacify our life, as Thou art the Lover of mankind, and set forth our prayer as incense, Thou Who alone restest in the saints."

"Passion-bearers of the Lord, blessed is the earth that drank your blood, and holy are the temples that received your bodies; for at the judgment-seat ye denounced the enemy, and preached Christ with boldness; Him entreat as the Good One, we pray, that our souls may be saved."

*For the Dead:*

"Remember Thy servants, O Lord, as Thou art good, and forgive whatsoever they sinned in life; for none is without sin save Thee alone, Who art able to grant rest unto the departed."

*Glory: Both now: Theotokion:*

"O Virgin Mother Mary, who didst bear Christ the Redeemer and Savior: pray His tender compassion, together with the Apostles, and Martyrs, and Prophets, and with the Venerables, and Hieromartyrs: to grant us cleansing of sins and great mercy."

# CANON TO THE HOLY MARTYRS, HIERARCHS, VENERABLES, AND THE DEPARTED
*The Composition of Joseph. Tone 2.*[^82]

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*

*"Taking up the song of Moses, cry aloud, O my soul: 'A helper and protector was He unto me for salvation: this is my God, and I will glorify Him!' "*

[f. 64vA] Cruel persecutions and severe plunderings did ye endure with patience, O Sufferers; every deceit from the ends of the earth did ye drive away by divine power."

"O ministers of God and Hierarchs: shining brightly with noetic radiance, ye guided the multitudes of all the pious unto the light of piety."

"Having humbled your proud mind, O Venerables, ye bowed down well unto the earth; being lifted up by divine types, ye ever help all the humble. *For the Dead:*"

"Show forth as partakers of the most radiant light and heavenly joy, O God, Thy faithful servants whom Thou hast translated from temporal things, O supremely Good One. *Theotokion:*"

"Having striven valiantly in fasting, and patiently cast down the enemy, the honored women stand before thee, O Mother of God, rejoicing."

*Another Canon, for the Departed. Tone 2. Ode 1. Heirmos:*

*"Traversing the untrodden wave:"*

"Having trampled down death by Thy death, Thou didst pour forth the ever-flowing stream of divine life; which grant, O Good One, unto the souls of the departed, by the supplications of Thy Martyrs, granting them remission of transgressions."

"Ever welling forth rich mercy, O Christ, unto them that piously receive Thee: in Thy house, in Thy sole tabernacle, grant a place of refreshment, O Master, unto Thy servants, as Thou art tenderly compassionate."

"Thou wast stronger than death, O Christ; therefore having bound it, Thou didst lead it captive unto the heavenly [f. 64vB] realms; and now deliver from this prison the departed, as Thou art good, and grant them participation in Thy radiance. *Theotokion:*"

"Establishing the wavering of my mind, O Mother of God, strengthen me by the divine commandments of Him Who came forth from thy sanctified womb, O Lady, and destroyed the gloomy kingdom of Hades."

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*

*"Show my barren mind to be fruitful, O God, Husbandman of souls and Planter of good things, by Thy tender compassion."*

"Kindled with the fire of the love of Christ, O passion-bearers, ye extinguished the coals of the torments by the dew of the All-Holy Spirit."

"O sanctified Hierarchs of Christ, and honored assemblies of the righteous: entreat the God Who loves mankind on behalf of us all."

"The most sacred choir of divine Prophets was magnified, and the multitude of women who suffered valiantly obtained glory."

"Slain upon the Cross, Thou didst grant immortality unto the dead; which vouchsafe them to obtain, who have passed over unto Thee in faith, O Christ."

"With all the Prophets and sacred women, fervently entreat God now, O Virgin, Who was born of thee, to have compassion upon us."

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*

*"Establishing me upon the rock of faith, Thou hast enlarged my mouth against mine enemies; for my spirit hath rejoiced to sing: 'None is holy as our God, and none is righteous save Thee, O Lord!' "*

"To be illuminated with the radiance of Thy beauty [f. 65rA] vouchsafe them that have fallen asleep in faith, with Thy Martyrs, O Thou Who art rich in mercy; for Thou art our God, and none is righteous save Thee, O Lord."

"In a place of refreshment, in the bosom of Abraham, vouchsafe Thy servants to abide, who cry unto Thee: 'For Thou art our God, and none is righteous save Thee, O Lord!' "

"To abide in the heavenly bridal chambers together with the wise virgins who carried lamps, receive Thy crown-bearing servants whom Thou hast translated by Thy will from temporal things, as Thou art the only Lover of mankind. *Theotokion:*"

"Me who was dead and returned unto the earth: thou didst resurrect, having given birth unto the Giver of life; thou didst raise me up from the lowest Hades, O most immaculate one, who with faith glorify and honor thee, O all-hymned Lady."

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*

*"Foreseeing Thy birth from the Virgin, the Prophet proclaimed, crying aloud: 'I have heard Thy report and was afraid: for from the south, from the holy shadowed mountain, Thou art come, O Christ!' "*

"Well assimilated unto the sufferings of Christ, O God-proclaimed passion-bearers, being stretched out in many torments, ye rejoiced, looking unto the eternal rewards, which having obtained, ye are ever blessed."

"Keeping the laws of the Spirit, O chief hierarchs, ye most wisely shepherded the people like chosen helmsmen, [f. 65rB] guiding them unto the divine haven, and translating them from the waves of this life, they passed over unto the stillness of life."

"As strangers on earth were ye shown to be, having translated your life unto the heavens, as it is written, piously and wisely; and having bridled the carnal passions by the labors of abstinence, through the power of Christ. *For the Dead:*"

"Those whom Thou hast translated from temporal life, a numerous multitude, having followed Thy most glorious faith, O Word: uniting them with all the multitude of the saved, vouchsafe them eternal life. *Theotokion:*"

"Desiring divine deadness, which truly mediated unending life, the honored women were vouchsafed it, O all-pure Lady Mother of God, entreating Thy Son and God on our behalf."

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos: I sing unto Thee, hearing:*

"Having lived in repentance and love, and in Orthodox understanding: vouchsafe Thy servants Thy glory which is beyond mind, O Christ, through Thy great love for mankind and the supplications of Thine elect Martyrs."

"As Thou hast an ever-flowing stream of delight: Thou dost ever water Thine elect, O Lord; with these also now feed them that have been translated unto Thee, O Christ, by Thine ineffable tender compassion, beside the waters of rest."

"That Thou mayest reign over the living and rule over the dead, Thou didst resurrect even the dust of the earth by Thy power; therefore unto Thee" [f. 65vA] who have passed over unto Thee, settle them in Thy courts, O Savior. *Theotokion:*"

"Thou didst not hide the shadow of mystery and ancient wretchedness; for thou gavest birth unto the Creator Who is able to fill us who were cast down by transgressions, O Mother of God, only Virgin Mother."

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*

*"Having dispelled the gloom of my soul, O my Savior: enlighten me with the light of Thy commandments, as Thou art the only King of peace!"*

"Loving Thee, O Compassionate One, the valiant Passion-bearers hated all worldly things, mingling with torments by the casting off of the flesh."

"Hierarchs, Prophets, Venerables, and Cross-bearers, enlightening all creation with the rays of the Spirit: ye dispel the darkness of passions."

"Most hymned Martyrs, Prophets, and Chief Priests, and ever-glorious women: fervently pray unto the Master for our sake. *For the Dead:*"

"We pray Thee, O Word: uniting them whom Thou hast taken from among us unto the choir of Thine elect, show them to be partakers of the better life. *Theotokion:*"

"O all-pure Virgin, boast of Martyrs, and of Venerables and Righteous ones: deliver me from every torment of the evil one."

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos: Giver of light:*

"Having slain us and laid us in corruption, Thou didst raise us from the gloomy recesses of Hades, and didst number us, O Good One, and unite us with the armies of the holy Angels."

"Since Thou didst come to save us, O Christ, receive now them that have piously [f. 65vB] departed unto Thee, as Thou art the only Good One, and settle them in the bosom of Abraham and with Lazarus."

"Thou hast loosed, O Master, my seasonal and long war, having formerly been a mediator and petitioner of peace toward Thee; and now of Thy will give rest and have compassion upon Thy servants. *Theotokion:*"

"Beneath thy protection, hoping in thee, we are saved, O Mother of God; for thou gavest birth unto the Giver of life, Who quickens all things of His own will."

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*

*"Held fast in the depth of sin, O Savior, and tempest-tossed in the sea of life: yet as Jonah from the sea-monster, so lead me up from passions, and save me!"*

"With strength of heart the sufferers, having arrayed themselves against the enemy, cast him down, and received crowns of victory from God; and now they fervently pray for all the earthborn."

"Let us faithfully honor the divine Hierarchs, and bless His Venerables, being saved by their supplications from all wrath, and tribulation, and snare of the enemy."

"The divine choir of women suffered and pleased God in asceticism, and obtained the Heavenly Kingdom; by their prayers, save Thy world, O only Jesus. *For the Dead:*"

"O Giver of life, Who didst fashion man from the earth: give rest unto them whom Thou hast translated from among us, granting them remission of evils, as Thou art tenderly compassionate and the Lover of mankind. *Theotokion:*"

"Holy Theotokos, cleanse our thoughts and strengthen our mind, and save [f. 66rA] us unwounded from the arrows of the evil one, who unceasingly glorify thy greatness."

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*

*"Held fast in the abyss of sins, I call upon the unfathomable abyss of Thy tender compassion: lead me up from corruption, O my God!"*

"In ineffable divine brightness, where the choirs of Martyrs dwell: vouchsafe them whom Thou hast translated from the earth by Thy all-effecting will, O Lover of mankind."

"To be illuminated with the beauty of Thy glory, vouchsafe them that have left this life, and give rest unto them that have passed over into Thine ineffable light, O Master."

"Show thyself delivering fervently them that call upon thee, O all-pure one full of grace, who gavest birth unto God Who hath dominion over life and death."

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*

*"Imitating the Cherubim, the Children rejoiced in the furnace, singing: 'Blessed art Thou, O God, for in truth and judgment hast Thou brought all these things upon us because of our sins, Thou Who art supremely hymned and glorified unto all ages!' "*

"By endurance the holy ones cast down the enemy, enduring every painful disease of torments: for they utterly loved God Who suffered for our sins; by their prayers, O Savior of all, Word, deliver from temptations and perils them that glorify Thee."

"Radiant Hierarchs, and Venerables, and Prophets, and Hieromartyrs, an all-admirable multitude, and the sacred assembly of holy women who shone brightly in asceticism: ever make supplication for our sake, [f. 66rB] that we may find mercy."

"The multitude of Martyrs entreats Thee, O Christ our Benefactor, on behalf of all in sorrow and affliction, and cruel temptations, and all transgressions, and from harm: save me, O Christ, who am perished. *For the Dead:*"

"Where sickness hath fled away, and sighing and sorrow; and where the light of Thy countenance shines, O Christ, and where the choirs of the saints dance around: establish forever the souls of them that have passed over unto Thee, O Lover of mankind, overlooking all their transgressions, as Thou art the only Merciful One."

"With the Martyrs, O all-pure one, with the Venerable Fathers, and all the Prophets, with the holy Women: entreat Him Who alone rests in the saints, to cleanse all of us who glorify thee with sacred voices, O pure one, unto all ages."

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos: The God-opposing command:*

"Thou Who art in heaven, having descended to save the human race that was deceived of old, O Lord: therefore the Martyrs entreat Thee: give rest in the land of the meek unto these whom Thou hast translated from the earth, O Savior."

"Abolishing the mortification of mortality, having Thyself alone become free among the dead: deliver Thy servants also now from the mortification of sin, showing them to be heirs of Thy Kingdom."

"Thy great and ineffable tender compassion, the measureless abyss of Thy love for mankind: grant remission of transgressions unto the departed, O Christ, and show them cleansed by Thy goodness. *Theotokion:*"

[f. 66vA] Thou wast a lamp of divine glory, carrying the radiance, O Maiden, of Him Who appeared unto us in the flesh by the Spirit, and destroyed the gloom of Hades by the brightness of His Godhead, O full of God's joy!"

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*

*"Unto Him Who prefigured of old the virgin wonder unto Moses in the bush on Mount Sinai: sing, bless, and highly exalt Him unto all ages!' "*

"The stream of your blood, O holy passion-bearing Martyrs, having cleansed all creation like an outflow of deceit, richly watered souls with eternal life."

"The ascetic choir, the assembly of Hierarchs, and holy Women, and glorious Prophets were shown to be equal in honor with the Angels, having lived on earth angelically in the Spirit."

"Deliver all of us from the passions, O chief priests of the Lord, and Prophets, and multitude of Venerables, and holy women: from the arrows of the enemy, who praise you. *For the Dead:*"

"Those whom Thou hast received from among us, O Savior, establish in the bosom of Abraham, and grant rest with Lazarus: give remission of all their sins, as Thou art all-compassionate. *Theotokion:*"

"O pure Mother of God, together with all the holy Prophets, and Martyrs, and ascetic Women, and Hieromartyrs: pray the Savior to have compassion upon us."

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*

*"The fiery furnace of old in Babylon divided its operation by the divine command: burning the Chaldeans, but cooling the faithful [f. 66vB] who sang: 'Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!' "*

"Thou hast shown unto us the untrodden paths of hostile death, as Thou art immortal, by Thy divine power, and hast revealed the entrances of life, O Immortal One; which Thy Martyrs have now worthily obtained."

"Vouchsafe the departed to enjoy Thy noetic beauty, driving away from thence the ugly sorrow of sin, O Master, as Thou art the Lover of mankind; for Thou alone wast shown to be free from sin."

"Thou hast set upright us who had fallen into the dust of death, O Christ: granting life by Thy death, and endless food, and everlasting joy; which vouchsafe the departed now to obtain, as Thou art merciful."

"Great and dreadful is the mystery of thy birthgiving, O Mother of God; for thou gavest birth unto God, Whom death could not endure, and the grave could not corrupt: therefore all nations glorify thee, O all-pure one."

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*

*"Unto Him Who shone forth from the Father before all ages, the Word conceived in the womb beyond nature in the flesh: in unceasing hymns do we the faithful magnify!"*

"Strong against passions, mighty against enemies were ye shown to be, O passion-bearers: ye carried away the victory, having suffered lawfully, and were crowned by Christ."

"Having been divine ministers of God, and imitators of the Good Shepherd: ye shepherded His sheep piously, O glorious chief hierarchs."

[f. 67rA] "With the Venerable ascetics, and the sacred Churches, let us honor the multitudes of women who suffered, and cast down the enemy by fasting."

"The most glorious multitude of Thy saints, O Christ, unceasingly entreats Thee: them whom Thou hast translated in faith, O Lord, show to be partakers of eternal life. *Theotokion:*"

"Having given birth in the flesh unto the tenderly compassionate God, together with all the saints ever entreat Him to save us from perils, O pure Virgin Mother."

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*

*"She who shone forth before the sun, the Dayspring, Who came unto us in the flesh from her womb, having ineffably incarnate God: O blessed and all-pure one, thee, O Theotokos, do we magnify!"*

"Having authority over the living and the dead, O Prince of life: grant a heavenly inheritance unto them that have passed over from the earth unto Thee, and the brightness of the Saints, O Master, and of Thy most glorious passion-bearers."

"Being the Word, Who gavest me being of old, most life-originating; and gavest again well-being: in the beloved bosom of Abraham the Forefather settle Thy departed servants, as Thou art merciful."

"Thou art all sweetness, O my Savior, the desire of all, an insatiable longing; with the streams of Thy food and the waters of forgiveness, prepared, water them that unceasingly glorify Thee. *Theotokion:*"

"Thee who art worthy do we the faithful now bless: following thy God-inspired words, for Thou alone didst bear God for the earthborn, [f. 67rB] Who destroyed the power of death, O Virgin Mother."

# AT THE PRAISES (LAUDS): STICHERA TO THE MARTYRS
*Tone 2:*[^83]

"Having suffered for Christ even unto death, O passion-bearing Martyrs: your souls indeed are in the hand of God in the heavens; and throughout all the world your relics are honored: Hierarchs and Kings bow down, and all peoples rejoicing, we customarily cry aloud: 'Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His venerable ones!' "

"Great cities and countries honor your relics, O passion-bearing Martyrs; for having suffered lawfully, ye received heavenly crowns: and for this reason ye are the boast of Priests, the victory of Kings, and the beauty of Churches."

"Taking up the Cross of Christ, an invincible weapon, the holy Martyrs abolished all the power of the devil, and received heavenly crowns; they became a wall for us, praying for our sake."

"The multitude of Thy saints entreats Thee, O Christ: have mercy and save us, as Thou art the Lover of mankind."

*Glory: Both now: Theotokion:*

"All my hope do I place in thee, O Mother of God: preserve me beneath thy protection."

### AT THE APOSTICHA, STICHERA FOR THE DEPARTED

*Tone 2.*

*Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Егда́ ѿ дре́ва та):*

"The onset of death and corruption hast Thou cast down by Thy life-giving death, O Master; and unto all Thou dost well forth eternal life, and unto the dead of the earth Thou hast granted resurrection."

[f. 67vA] unto them. Therefore we pray Thee, O Savior: give rest unto them that have departed unto Thee in faith, and vouchsafe them Thine incorruptible glory, O Lover of mankind."

*Verse: Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen and taken to Thyself, O Lord.*

"That Thou mightest make men partakers of Thy divine Kingdom, O Christ: Thou didst endure crucifixion and willingly accept death; therefore we pray: by Thy tender compassion show them that have departed in faith to be partakers of Thy Kingdom, and vouchsafe them the beauty of Thy glory, O Lover of mankind."

*Verse: Their souls shall dwell among good things.*

"Desiring to save Thine own creation, Thou didst joyfully accomplish the dread mystery of the dispensation in truth, as Thou art supremely Good, and by Thy precious blood Thou didst ransom the whole world; therefore we pray: vouchsafe them that have departed unto Thee redemption with all the Saints."

*Glory: Both now: Theotokion:*

"When my soul is about to be separated from life from the bond of the flesh:

[f. 67vB] then stand by me, O Lady, and destroy the counsels of bodiless enemies, and crush their jaws who seek to devour me unsparingly: that I may pass without hindrance through the princes of darkness who stand in the air, O Bride of God!"

# ON SATURDAY, THE BEATITUDES (BLAZHENNA)
*Tone 2:*

"We bring unto Thee the voice of the thief, and pray: 'Remember us, O Lord, in Thy Kingdom!' "

"Having been assimilated unto the sufferings of Christ, O Martyrs: ye ever heal the diverse passions of men."

"With the Prophets, Apostles, and Venerable teachers: they well pleased the Creator of all."

"With all Thy saints, O Lord Who lovest mankind, we pray: establish all Thy servants who have departed in faith."

*Glory:*

"O consubstantial Trinity, have compassion upon them that honor Thee; snatch them from the deceit of the enemy, ever delivering them."

*Both now: Theotokion:*

"Despise not the supplications of thy servants, O all-immaculate one, saving us from all tribulations and sorrows."

**END OF THE SECOND TONE.**[^84]
