# TONE 3: SATURDAY VESPERS, SUNDAY MATINS, AND WEEKDAY OFFICES

## ON SATURDAY EVENING, AT GREAT VESPERS

[f. 69rA] *At "Lord, I call:" Stichera of the Resurrection, Tone 3:*[^85]

[f. 69rA] "By Thy Cross, O Christ Savior, the dominion of death was destroyed, and the deceit of the devil was brought to naught; and the human race, being saved through faith, ever brings a hymn unto Thee."

"All things were enlightened by Thy Resurrection, O Lord, and Paradise was opened again; and all creation, praising Thee, ever brings a hymn unto Thee."

"I glorify the power of the Father and the Son, and hymn the authority of the Holy Spirit: the undivided, uncreated Godhead, the consubstantial Trinity, reigning unto ages of ages."

*Other Stichera, Anatolian (Eastern), Tone the same:*

"Before Thy precious Cross we bow down, O Christ, and Thy Resurrection do we sing and glorify; for by Thy wound were we all healed."

"We hymn the Savior Who was incarnate of the Virgin; for for our sake was He crucified, and on the third day He arose:

[f. 69rB] granting unto us great mercy."

"Having descended unto them that were in Hades, Christ proclaimed good tidings, saying: 'Be of good cheer, now have I conquered! I am the Resurrection, I will lead you up, having destroyed the gates of death!' "

"Standing unworthily in Thine all-pure house, we send up an evening hymn, crying from the depths, O Christ God, Who didst enlighten the world by Thy three-day Resurrection: deliver Thy people from the hand of Thine enemies, O Lover of mankind."

*Glory: Both now: Theotokion (Dogmatikon):*

"How should we not marvel at thy God-manbearing childbearing, O all-honored one? For not having accepted the trial of man, O all-immaculate one, thou gavest birth in the flesh without a father unto a Son Who was begotten of the Father without a mother before the ages, having suffered neither change, nor mingling, nor division; but preserving intact the property of each nature."

[f. 69vA] Therefore, O Virgin Mother and Lady, pray Him to save the souls of them that orthodoxly confess thee to be the Mother of God."

### AT THE APOSTICHA, STICHERA OF THE RESURRECTION

*Tone 3:*[^86]

"By Thy passion, O Christ, Thou didst darken the sun, and by the light of Thy Resurrection Thou didst enlighten all things: accept our evening hymn, O Lover of mankind."

*Other Stichera, Alphabetical:*

"Thy life-giving arising, O Lord, enlightened the whole inhabited world, and recalled Thine own corrupt creation. Therefore, loosed from the curse of Adam, we cry aloud: 'All-powerful Lord, glory to Thee!' "

"Being God immutable, Thou didst change in suffering flesh, which creation unable to bear to see, bent down in fear; and groaning, it hymned Thy long-suffering; and having descended into Hades, Thou didst arise on the third day, granting life unto the world and great mercy."

"That Thou mightest deliver our race from death, O Christ, Thou didst endure death, and having arisen as the firstborn from the dead, Thou didst raise up with Thyself them that acknowledged Thee as God; and Thou didst enlighten the world, O Lord, glory to Thee!"

*Glory: Both now: Theotokion:*

"Without seed, from the Holy Spirit, by the Father's good pleasure, thou didst conceive the Son of God, Who is from the Father without mother before all ages; and for our sake, without father from thee, thou didst bear Him in the flesh, and didst nourish the Infant with milk: therefore cease not [f. 69vB] to pray, that our souls may be delivered from tribulations."

*Then: "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart..." Trisagion. After "Our Father...":*

*Resurrection Troparion, Tone 3:*

"Let the heavenly things rejoice and the earthly things be glad, for the Lord hath wrought dominion with His arm: He hath trampled down death by death, He hath become the firstborn from the dead; He hath delivered us from the belly of Hades, and hath granted unto the world great mercy."

*Glory: Both now: Theotokion:*

"Thee who didst mediate the salvation of our race do we hymn, O Theotokos Virgin: for in the flesh assumed from thee, Thy Son and our God, having accepted suffering through the Cross, hath delivered us from corruption, as He is the Lover of mankind."

# ON SUNDAY, AT THE MIDNIGHT OFFICE
*Triadical Canon. The Composition of Metrophanes [of Smyrna]. Tone 3.*[^87]

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*

*"He Who of old by His nod gathered the waters into one gathering: and O one Trinity, source of Godhead, vouchsafe me the light of Thy thrice-radiant light, that I may sing of Thee in unceasing hymns. Triadikon:"*

"The immaterial ranks sacredly sing, standing with trembling before the primary Light of the Trinity, as written in the book of creation, and we earthborn with one mouth faithfully glorify Thee with sacred sacrifices."

"Of the Mind, and the Word, and the Spirit, [f. 70rA] so great as they call the unoriginate and eternal generation unto Thy Word, from the unbegotten Father: O Son, signifying God, Son of the sole beginning, together with the procession of the Holy Spirit."

"The supreme Light of the one Godhead, having most gloriously shown forth unto all, O pure Virgin who gavest Him birth."

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*

*"He Who brought all things out of nothing: to divide the waters of old, He commanded, watering the earth; prefiguring unto all the Trinitarian hypostasis of the sole Godhead and Dominion."*

"The nature of earthborn minds sings of Thee, the one and thrice-radiant immutable Creator, and we cry unto Thee: 'Deliver me from every assault, and save me!' *Glory:*"

"As in the utterances of prophetic words, and of the all-wise Apostles, preachers of the faith, we glorify Thee as the equal-acting Trinity in one God of all. *Both now:*"

"From the exalted throne descended the Word, lifting up man, as He is the Lover of mankind, through thee, O all-pure one, and the thrice-sunny light shone forth upon all."

*Sessional Hymn (Sessional Hymn), Tone 3.*

*Podoben: "Beholding the beauty of thy virginity" (Красотѣ̀ дѣ́вства твоегѡ̀):*

"O undivided and inseparable Trinity, remember us who bow down before Thee, and who piously hymn and unceasingly call upon Thee: save them whom Thou [f. 70rB] hast fashioned for the sake of the abundance of Thy tender compassion, in Thy holy Church, which Thou didst acquire by Thy power; for Thou knowest, O Merciful One, the weakness of our heart."

*Glory: Both now: Theotokion:*

"I am wholly changed through my lack of self-control, and through my senseless fearlessness I have become wretched; I cannot bear the day whereat all visible and invisible things tremble; O Lady, help me, and dispel the perplexity of my heart; for thou thyself art the hope and protectress of thy servants."

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*

*"Thou hast set firm love toward us: the Father indeed toward Thee, O Father, as a shoot from the root, the Son and the right Spirit, natural shoots and God-planted flowers without beginning, so as to be luminaries of the Godhead in spiritual essences; unceasingly they hymn Thee, the unfathomable God, with whom we also glorify, saying: 'O transcendent Trinity, preserve Thy servants, as Thou art merciful!' "*

*Both now:*

"Thou didst save us from great peril, O abundantly merciful Word of God, Who wast incarnate for our sake, and mystically revealed the thrice-sunny Godhead, Whom we glorify."

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*

*"As Isaiah saw:"*

"The image of the one Sovereign Ruler, as Isaiah saw God: the ranks of three Angels..." [f. 70vA] Persons. Join my voices thereto: a Seraph was sent to proclaim the thrice-radiant Essence and the thrice-sunny Unity.[^88]

*Glory:*

"O Thrice-sunny Unity, Who of old didst bring into being out of non-existence the nature of things visible and invisible: deliver from every assault them that cry unto Thee in faith as the one God, to Whose glory Thou art like."

*Both now:*

"Having become a light-bearing lantern and vessel of honor unto God, O Virgin, we sing of thee with love and bless thee: for from thee was Christ born, in two natures and two wills, Who is One of the Trinity; and the Lord is glorified with Him."

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*

*"The lowest depth of sins..."*

"Through the figures of the most glorious Powers, in a manner resembling an image, to receive an image of the Lord in three Persons, material in human forms."

*Glory:*

"Being the purifier of the hearts of Thy servants, unto the unapproachable light, O Thrice-sunny Lord, and the radiance of Thy glory, vouchsafe unto our souls that which is desirable by Thine unutterable divine beauty."

*Both now:*

"Open unto me the gates of the light born of thy womb, O all-pure one: that I may behold the thrice-radiant light of the Godhead, and glorify thee as Lady of all."

[f. 70vB] *Sessional Hymn, Tone 3.*

*Podoben: "Beholding the beauty of thy virginity" (Красотѣ дѣвства):*

"Having cleansed him as Thou art merciful, deliver Thy righteous servant from those ages, and cast him not into the fire of Gehenna: for Thou alone, O Christ, art abundantly merciful."

*Glory: Both now: Theotokion:*

"Grant me teaching of groaning, as unto the Publican, O Virgin, and tears of the harlot: that bringing forth Thy judgment, I may cry: 'Have mercy on me, O all-merciful one, and lead me forth from my perplexity by this thy grace, granting me a stream of compunction; for unto thee have I fled, O all-pure one!' "

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*

*"As of old the pious..."*

"Show forth the God-originating, divine Abraham of threefold Person, whose good is higher than grievous sinful darkening and passions; by which grace-bestowing mysteries: 'O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!' "

"Let us alone desire the harvest of Thy life for me, in three Hypostases and distinct properties, of Father and Son and Spirit, crying together: 'O God of our fathers!' "

*Glory:*

"Abraham of old, seeing God in three Hypostases near the oak of Mamre, received Isaac as the reward of hospitality for mercy, Whom we also now glorify as the God of our fathers."

*Both now:*

"Having been born on earth, a man, the Creator: in a God-befitting manner and in virginity, O all-pure one, of thy womb, and He deified us, O blessed, all-immaculate, and all-pure Theotokos."

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*

*"In the unenduring fire..."*

"The unoriginate Father, as root, the Word, and the Spirit, being co-unoriginate [f. 71rA] by nature, as the clarity of the super-essential Godhead, showed forth the one glory and power of the Trinity, Whom we all sing of, strengthen unto the ages."

*Glory:*

"Thou dost direct by Thy bright ranks the heavenly orders to sing unceasingly with thrice-holy divine hymns: O Father, Word of like form, and Spirit, the thrice-radiant and equal-in-power dominion; therefore we sing of Thee unto all ages."

*Both now:*

"The prophetic utterances, having seen thy childbearing from afar, O Theotokos, praised it as unutterable, and the God born above nature: and in harmony with this we sing of Him as the Lord, and we honor thee who gavest Him birth, O Virgin, unto all ages."

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*

*"A new wonder and God-befitting..."*

"The God-beholding ranks of the incorporeal ones, wishing to ascend on high as with material wings to behold the glory of the Thrice-radiant One: yet being greatly unable to comprehend that Godhead by reason of the light, they unceasingly cry out a hymn, with whom in harmony, O unique Trinity, we glorify Thee."

*Glory:*

"With love, the nature upon earth, having received Thee with an intelligent soul in speech, we hymn Thee, O Master, God Almighty, the one nature in truth and the Trinitarian Persons, from our whole heart; therefore, O Bountiful One, as Thou art abundantly merciful, have compassion on us."

*Both now:*

"Show me forth as a temple of Thy monarchical and all-bright Godhead, O Knower of all things: teach me to serve Thee, the Creator [f. 71rB] of the ages, and spiritually to behold Thine unutterable glory, through the intercessions of the only Theotokos, whom worthily, as most glorious, we magnify."

### AT MATINS

*After the Six Psalms:*

*"God is the Lord, and hath appeared unto us..." in Tone 3. And we say the Resurrection Troparion:*

"Let the heavenly things rejoice..." *Glory: Both now: Theotokion:* "Thee who didst mediate..." *Then the customary reading of the Kathismata of the Psalter.*

*After the First Kathisma, Resurrection Sessional Hymns, Tone 3:*[^89]

"Christ is risen from the dead, the firstfruits of them that slept, the firstborn of creation, and Maker of all things that have come to be; the corrupted nature of our race hath He renewed in Himself. No longer dost thou have dominion, O death; for the Master of all hath destroyed thy dominion."

*Glory:*

"At Thine immutable Godhead and voluntary passion, O Lord, Hades was dismayed and wailed aloud, saying: 'I tremble at the flesh of an incorruptible hypostasis; I behold the Invisible One secretly warring against me; therefore also those whom I hold cry out: Glory, O Christ, to Thy Resurrection!' "

*Both now: Theotokion:*

"With great love the heavenly ranks were refreshed, and the earth was dismayed with trembling, when the all-pure voice came upon thee, O Theotokos; for it became a single festival unto both, when the bodiless joy was brought unto thee; therefore with the Angel we cry unto thee: 'Rejoice, O pure dwelling-place of God!' "

*After the Second Kathisma, Resurrection Sessional Hymns:*

[f. 71vA] *Resurrectional, Tone 3:*[^90]

"Having tasted death in the flesh, O Lord, Thou didst cut off the bitterness of death by Thy rising, and didst strengthen man against it, calling back the overthrow of the ancient curse, O Defender of our life: O Christ God, glory to Thee!"

*Glory:*

"Thy comprehension-surpassing Crucifixion and unutterable Resurrection do we faithful glorify, an ineffable mystery; for today death and Hades have been despoiled, and the human race hath put on incorruption; therefore also with thanksgiving we cry aloud: Glory, O Christ, to Thy Resurrection!"

*Both now: Theotokion:*

"Incomprehensible and uncircumscribed, consubstantial with the invisible Father, thou didst secretly contain in thy womb, O Theotokos; one and unconfused Godhead of the Trinity, we have recognized how to glorify thy childbearing in the world; therefore also with thanksgiving we cry unto thee: 'Rejoice, full of grace!' "

*Hypakoe, Tone 3:*[^91]

"Marveling in appearance, dewing with words, the Angel shining forth said unto the Myrrh-bearing women: 'Why seek ye the Living among the dead? He is risen, having emptied the tombs! Understand the Transformer of corruption, and say unto God: How awesome are Thy works, for Thou hast saved the human race!' "

*The Anabathmoi (Antiphons of the Steps), Tone 3.*

*Antiphon 1:*

"The captivity of Sion hast Thou delivered from Babylon: and draw Thou me also out of passions unto life, O Word."

[f. 71vB] "They that sow in the south with divine tears shall reap sheaves of life with joy and singing."

"To the Holy Spirit is every thanksgiving, as He shines forth together with the Father and the Son, in Whom all things live and move."

*Antiphon 2:*

"Except the Lord build the house of virtues, in vain do we labor; and unless He protect the soul, no one can destroy our city."

"Of the fruit of the womb, by the Spirit, are the saints made Thy sons, O Christ, as unto the Father, at all times."

"By the Holy Spirit is all holiness and wisdom foreseen; for He brings every creature into being: let us serve Him, for He is God, as unto the Father and the Word."

*Antiphon 3:*

"Blessed are they that fear the Lord, walking in the way of the commandments; for they shall eat the life-giving, great fruitfulness."

"Round about Thy table rejoice, seeing Thy offspring, O Chief Shepherd, bearing the branches of good works."

"By the Holy Spirit is all wealth of glory, from Whom is grace and life unto every creature; for He is sung together with the Father and with the Word."

*Prokeimenon, Tone 3:*[^92]

"Say among the heathen that the Lord reigns, for He hath established the world so that it cannot be moved."

*Verse: Praise God in His saints; praise Him in the firmament of His power.*

*The Gospel. And the rest in order.*

*Canon*

# CANON OF THE RESURRECTION
[f. 72rA] *Tone 3.*[^93]

*Ode 1. Tone 3. Heirmos:*

*"He Who of old by His divine nod gathered the waters into one gathering, and divided the sea for the people of Israel: this is our God, and He is exceedingly glorious; unto Him alone let us sing, for He hath been glorified."*

"He Who judged the earth to bring forth thorns for the transgressor by the sweat of his brow: from thorns a crown at the hands of the lawless, this is our God, He received in the flesh, and He hath loosed the curse, for He hath been glorified."

"A victor and defeater of death, having clothed Himself in death, He appeared, having received passible, ensouled flesh: this is our God, and having fought against the tormentor, He raised up all with Himself, for He hath been glorified."

"All nations glorify thee, the true Theotokos, who gavest birth without seed; for having descended into thy sanctified womb: this is our God, Who became consubstantial with us, and as God and man was He born incorruptibly."

# ANOTHER CANON, OF THE CROSS AND RESURRECTION
*Tone 3.*[^94]

*Ode 1. Tone 3. Heirmos:*

*"Let us sing a new song, O ye peoples:"*

"The human race falling under the sin-catching tormentor, Christ redeemed with His divine blood, and He hath renewed them that were His own creation, for He hath been glorified."

"Christ was seen mortal indeed, willing death, He Who is the treasury of life; and as immortal in Godhead, He hath quickened the dead, for He hath been glorified."

# ANOTHER CANON TO THE ALL-HOLY THEOTOKOS
[f. 72rB] *Tone 3. The same Heirmos:*

"Every nature of heavenly beings bows the knee, O Virgin, unto Him Who was incarnate incorruptibly, together with earthly beings and suitably the nethermost, for He hath been glorified."

"The changes which are in thee: the ungrudging Giver of good things, God the Father: having given us the divine Spirit, and from thee, O Maiden, having received flesh, for He hath been glorified."

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*

*"He Who brought all things out of nothing by His Word, which are fashioned and perfected by the Spirit: O Almighty Master, establish me in Thy love."*

"By Thy Cross was the ungodly one put to shame; for the pit which he dug and made, therein did he fall; but Christ raised up the horn of the humble in His Resurrection."

"The preaching of the Gospel unto the nations, as water covers the sea, O Lover of mankind; for having risen from the tomb, Thou didst reveal the Trinitarian light."

*Theotokion:*

"Most glorious things have been spoken of thee, O ensouled city of the Ever-Reigning One; for through thee, O Lady, hath God lived together with them that are upon the earth."

*Another Heirmos:*

*"Thou hast shattered the bow of the enemy:"*

"Thou art the all-pure purity of the Cross against idolatrous impurities; for Christ the pre-eternal stretched out His hands upon thee, and all we faithful bow down before thee, the God-receiving tomb of Him that buried thee," [f. 72vA] "unto Thy glory, and Christ is risen, for He is the true God."

*Another Canon. The same Heirmos:*

"A rod from the root of Jesse, having prophetically budded forth, O Virgin: Christ as a flower hath shone forth upon us, Thou art the Savior, O Lord."

"That Thou mightest make earthborn mortals partakers of the divine nature, taking our flesh from the Virgin, Thou hast renewed it: Thou art the Savior, O Lord."

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*

*"Thou hast set firm love toward us, O Lord; for Thine Only-begotten Son didst Thou give unto death for our sake; therefore we cry unto Thee with thanksgiving: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!"*

"Wounds and stripes, O Christ, didst Thou mercifully endure, suffering blows upon Thy cheeks with insults, and bearing spitting with long-suffering: by which Thou hast wrought salvation for me; glory to Thy power, O Lord!"

"In mortal body, O Life, didst Thou become partaker of death, for the sake of the affliction of the poor and the groaning of the needy; and having corrupted the corrupter, O Glorified One, Thou didst raise up all with Thyself, as Thou art glorified."

*Theotokion:*

"Remember, O Christ, the flock which Thou didst acquire by Thy passion: accepting the merciful supplications of Thine all-glorious Mother, and having visited the afflicted, deliver it by Thy power, O Lord."

*Another Heirmos:*

*"Strange and unutterable:"*

"Having fashioned [man] according to Thine image..."

[f. 72vB] "...crucified on the Place of the Skull, Thou hast saved."

"The dead whom death swallowed up in Hades, and the corruptive kingdom of Hades was destroyed, when Thou didst arise from the tomb, O Lord."

*Theotokion:*

"O pure Mary, golden censer, unconfusedly as One of the Trinity the Word of God descended into Thee and was incarnate, filling the world with sweet fragrance."

*Another Heirmos:*

*"He Who set fast the mountains, O Master, by the balance of divine understanding, Thou hast found from the Virgin a Stone cut without hands: glory to Thy power, O Lover of mankind."*

"Thou didst heal our diseased nature, O Master, having rooted it out from the Virgin, becoming incarnate as a companion; O Word, Thy precious Godhead."

"Thou art my portion, O Lord, and desired inheritance, Who didst unite me from the Virgin, O Word, into Thy Hypostasis, having become a Hypostasis in the flesh."

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*

*"Unto Thee do I rise early in the morning, surpassing all immaterial angelic mind, a small world; for Thy commandments are light: wherein guide Thou me."*

"Handed over to an unjust judge through the envy of the Hebrews, Thou Who seest all things and judgest all the earth with righteousness, didst deliver ancient Adam from condemnation."

"Grant Thy peace unto Thy Churches, O Christ, by the invincible power of Thy Cross, Thou Who didst arise from the dead, and save our souls."

"A holy Tabernacle, and more spacious than the heavens, far more God-chosen than the cedars in Lebanon, didst thou appear" [f. 73rA] "ever, having been shown forth alone, O Ever-Virgin."

*Another Heirmos:*

*"The Invisible One appeared upon earth, and willingly lived with men, the Incomprehensible One: and rising early unto Thee, we cry unto Thee, O Lover of mankind."*

"Pierced with a spear in Thy side, O my Christ: from the rib fashioned of man, the mediatress of ruin that was unto all men, didst Thou free from the curse."

"Equal to the Father in essence, the Son, the consecrated temple of His assumed and incorruptible body: from the dead didst Thou raise up, O Christ our Savior."

*Another Heirmos:*

"O Word of God, thy Son, O Virgin, the Fashioner of Adam the first-formed, uncreated, though He fashioned ensouled flesh for Himself from thee."

"Equal to the Father, thy Son, O Virgin, the Word of God, a perfect Hypostasis in every nature, Jesus the Lord, perfect God and man."

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*

*"The lowest depth of sins hath compassed me, and my spirit fails; but stretch forth Thy high arm, O Master, and as Thou didst Peter, O Pilot, save me."*

"The abyss of mercy and compassions hath compassed me by Thy merciful condescension; for having been incarnate, O Master, and being in the form of a servant, Thou didst deify and glorify me together with Thyself."

"The slayer of death endured slaying, beholding the slain One revived; O Christ Savior, the images of Thy Resurrection and the wounds" [f. 73rB] "of Thy most pure sufferings."

*Theotokion:*

"O all-pure one, who alone didst mediate beyond mind between the Creator and men: pray thy Son to be merciful unto thy servants that have sinned, and to be their defender."

*Another Heirmos:*

*"At the descent of Jonah into the nethermost parts of Hades, having become an image of nature, he cried aloud: Lead up my life from corruption, O Lover of mankind."*

"Thou wast wounded with wounds, and them that were wounded from Hades didst Thou raise up together with Thyself by the passion of the Cross; therefore I cry unto Thee: Lead up my life from corruption, O Lover of mankind."

"The gates of Hades shrank back in fear before Thee, O Christ, and the vessels of the enemy were despoiled; therefore the women met Thee, receiving joy instead of sorrow."

*Another Heirmos:*

"He Who is after our likeness from the incorrupt Virgin is depicted, Who in an inseparable form, having become in form and in deed, is man without change in Godhead."

"Deliver me, O all-pure one, from the abyss of sins and the storm of passions; for thou art a haven and an abyss of wonders unto them that flee unto thee in faith."

# KONTAKION
*Tone 3.*

*Podoben: "The works of the day" (Дѣла дніа):* [^95]

"Thou didst arise today from the tomb, O Compassionate One, and hast led us up from the gates of death; today Adam dances and Eve rejoices, and together the prophets and patriarchs [sing unceasingly of the divine power of Thine authority]."

# IKOS
[f. 73vA] *Tone 3:*[^96]

"Let heaven and earth today keep festival, and with one mind sing of Christ God; for having raised up the prisoners from the tomb, all creation rejoices together, offering worthy hymns unto the Creator of all and our Redeemer: for as the Giver of life He hath freed them, and raised them up with Himself unto the heavens, and cast down the loftiness of the enemy, and shattered the gates of Hades by the divine power of His authority."

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*

*"As of old Thou didst bedew the three pious Children in the Chaldean furnace: with the bright fire of the Godhead enlighten us also, who cry: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!"*

"The bright veil of the temple was rent at the Crucifixion of the Creator, revealing unto the faithful the truth hidden in the Scripture, who cry: 'Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!' "

"A drop of divine, life-creating blood from Thy pierced side, O Christ, dripping upon the earth by Thy dispensation, hath renewed them that are of the earth, who cry: 'Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!' "

*Triadikon:*

"Let us glorify the good Spirit with the Father, and with the Only-begotten Son, we faithful honoring one Principle in three, and one Godhead, crying: 'Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!' "

[f. 73vB] "having trampled the sevenfold flame, they sang: 'Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers!' "

"Not simply seeing a man suspended upon the Cross: but beholding God incarnate, the sun was darkened, unto Whom we also sing: 'Blessed art Thou who criest, O God of our fathers!' "

"Hades turning away having received Him Who was mighty in Godhead, the Giver of incorruption, He led forth the souls of the righteous that cried: 'Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers!' "

*Theotokion:*

"A hidden treasure of great price hast thou become, O all-pure one, unto us who wish to honor thee, confessing thee to be the Mother of God; for He was pleased to be incarnate: 'Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!' "

*Another Heirmos:*

*"He Who possesses the power of the heavenly hosts, Who sits in the Father's bosom, and is borne upon the cherubic wings: blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers."*

"Fierce was death, but it destroyed itself by drawing near; and Adam having become a body fashioned by God, we cry: 'Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!' "

"All we have known thee who gavest birth to God; for One of the Trinity, Who was incarnate incorruptibly, hast thou borne: blessed, O all-pure one, is the fruit of thy womb."

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*

*"Gathered together in the unenduring fire, yet unharmed by the flame, the youths pre-eminent in piety sang a divine hymn: 'Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing and exalt Him above all unto the ages!' "*

[f. 74rA] "The brightness of the temple was rent when Thy Cross was planted on Calvary, and creation bowed down in fear, singing: 'Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing and exalt Him above all unto the ages!' "

"Christ is risen from the tomb, and him that fell through the deception of the tree hath He set upright by this His divine power, crying and saying: 'Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing and exalt Him above all unto the ages!' "

"Thou didst appear as the temple of God, an ensouled dwelling-place, and an Ark; for unto the Creator didst thou reconcile mankind, O all-pure Theotokos; and worthily do all works sing of thee, who even after childbearing wast preserved a Virgin."

*Another Heirmos:*

*"The God-bearing Children, having quenched the material flame of fire with an immaterial flame, and the company sang: 'Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto the ages!' "*

"The passionless Word, passionless indeed in Godhead, yet God suffers in the flesh, unto Whom we also sing: 'Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing and exalt Him above all unto the ages!' "

"Thou didst wither away as mortal, and didst arise as immortal, O Savior, and Thou dost save from death them that sing: 'Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing and exalt Him above all unto the ages!' "

*Triadikon:*

"We piously worship the three-hypostatic Godhead, unutterably united in one, and we sing: 'Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing and exalt Him above all unto the ages!' "

*Another Heirmos:*

[f. 74rB] "O Mother, thou hast surpassed the intelligent ranks, and having come near unto God, O blessed Virgin, the faithful [extol] thy childbearing, and we exalt it above all unto all ages."

"Thou hast shown forth the natural beauty most pre-eminent, the flesh of the Godhead shining brightly, O blessed Virgin, the faithful [extol] thy childbearing, and we exalt it above all unto all ages."

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*

*"A new wonder and God-befitting: for through the closed virginal gate the Lord manifestly passes; bare at His entrance, and flesh-bearing God appeared at His going forth, and the gate remains shut: her unceasingly as Mother of God do we magnify."*

"Awesome is it to behold Thee, O Creator, lifted up upon the Tree, O Word of God, and suffering in the flesh as God for Thy servants, and lying breathless in the tomb, yet loosing the dead from Hades: therefore Thee, O Christ, as Almighty do we magnify."

"From mortal corruption hast Thou saved the forefather, O Christ, having been laid dead in the tomb; and Thou hast caused life to blossom forth, having raised the dead; with Thy hand Thou didst lead up human nature unto the light, and clothed it in divine incorruption: therefore Thee, the Fountain of ever-living light, do we magnify."

*Theotokion:*

"The all-pure one was shown forth as the receptacle of light; for God, Who was incarnate ineffably and immutably, having lifted up the nature of Adam upon the Cross, appeared as the firstborn from the dead, and God remains in the highest," [f. 74vA] "and together with the Father and the Divine Spirit do we glorify Him."

*Another Heirmos:*

*"Wounded with the arrow by the glory of thy most pure childbearing, O pure one, and marveling at thy most fitting beauty, with angelic hymns worthily do we magnify thee as Mother of God."*

"Death withered away; from the nature of death Thou didst pour forth life unto all, even by Thy Crucifixion didst Thou ascend, O Savior; unto me, mortal by nature, as God Thou didst grant incorruption, O Lover of mankind."

"Thou hast saved me, rising from the tomb, O Christ; and ascending, Thou didst bring me unto the Father, Thy Begetter, and didst seat me at His right hand, O tender-hearted Mother of God the Lord."

*Another Heirmos:*

"Thou art the praise of the sanctity of thy servants, O Virgin, unto pious believers; sight heals, for receiving ever the divine and spiritual desire: as Mother of God do we magnify thee."

"Thou hast set her who bare Thee as an unashamed intercessor, O Christ; by her supplications mercifully give us the Spirit, granting us the comforting Spirit, the Giver of goodness, Who proceeds from the Father through Thee."

# AT THE PRAISES
*Stichera of the Resurrection, Tone 3:*

"Come, all ye nations, understand the power of the awesome mystery: for Christ our Savior, Who was in the beginning the Word, was crucified for our sake and was willingly buried, and He arose from the dead to save all" [f. 74vB] "things: let us worship Him!"

"All Thy wonders did Thy guards recount, O Lord, but the vain council filled their right hands with bribes, thinking to conceal Thy Resurrection, which the world glorifies: have mercy on us!"

"All things were filled with joy, having received the proof of the Resurrection; for Mary Magdalene came unto the tomb and found an Angel sitting upon the stone, gleaming in his raiment, and saying: 'Why seek ye the Living among the dead? He is not here, but is risen, as He said, going before you into Galilee!' "

"In Thy light, O Master, shall we see light, O Lover of mankind; for risen from the dead, Thou didst grant salvation unto the human race, that all creation may hymn Thee, the only Sinless One: have mercy on us!"

*Other Stichera, Eastern, Tone 3:*

"A morning hymn did the myrrh-bearing women bring unto Thee with tears, O Lord; for having sweet fragrances, they reached Thy tomb, striving to anoint Thy most pure body; but the Angel sitting upon the stone announced good tidings unto them: 'Why seek ye the Living among the dead? For He hath trampled death, and is risen as God, granting great mercy unto all!' "

"Shining brightly upon Thy life-bearing tomb, the Angel said unto the Myrrh-bearers: 'The tombs are emptied by the Redeemer; He hath cast down Hades and is risen on the third day, as the only God and Almighty!' "

[f. 75rA] "Mary Magdalene came on the first day of the week, seeking Thee in the tomb; and not finding Thee, she wept and cried aloud with lamentation: 'Woe is me, my Savior! The King of all hath been stolen away!' But two life-bearing Angels within the tomb cried out: 'Why weepest thou, O woman?' 'I weep,' said she, 'because they have taken away my Lord from the tomb, and I know not where they have laid Him.' But turning round, when she beheld Thee, she immediately cried: 'My Lord and my God, glory to Thee!' "

*Glory:*

"The race of the Jews were wounded with envy, and they shut up Life in the tomb; but the Thief opened Paradise with his tongue, crying and saying: 'He Who with me and for my sake was crucified, let us be crucified together on the Tree; and He that sits with me upon the Throne, sitting with the Father: for He is Christ our Savior, Who hath great mercy!' "

# AT THE DIVINE LITURGY
*The Beatitudes (Makarismoi), Tone 3:*[^97]

"Adam our forefather, who rejected Thy commandment, O Christ, didst Thou cast out of Paradise; but the Thief, O Bountiful One, who confessed Thee upon the Cross, didst Thou settle therein, who cried: 'Remember me, O Savior, in Thy Kingdom!' "

"Under the sentence of death wast Thou condemned, O Life-Giver Christ, and all creation was visibly transformed, seeing Thee its Master in human nature; therefore with the Thief we cry unto Thee: 'Remember me when Thou comest into Thy Kingdom!' "

"Thou didst condemn us who sinned under the curse of death; but our Life-Giver, having borne our body sinlessly, O Lord, Thou didst quicken the dead" [f. 75rB] "who cried: 'Remember us in Thy Kingdom!' "

"Moses stretched forth his hands upon the mountain, prefiguring the Cross, overcoming Amalek; and we faithful, having received this mighty weapon against demons, faithfully cry: 'Remember us also in Thy Kingdom!' "

"Risen from the dead, Thou didst raise us up together from passions by Thy Resurrection, O Lord, and all the power of death hast Thou destroyed, O Savior; therefore in faith we cry unto Thee: 'Remember us also in Thy Kingdom!' "

"Unto the Myrrh-bearing women didst Thou first appear, risen from the dead, O Savior, crying out: 'Rejoice!' and through them Thou didst announce Thy rising unto Thy friends, O Christ; therefore in faith we cry unto Thee: 'Remember us also in Thy Kingdom!' "

*Triadikon:*

"Unto the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit let us faithful bow down, the uncreated Trinity, Who is in three Persons and in one Godhead, ever praised faithfully by the incorporeal powers in thrice-holy hymns."

*Both now: Theotokion:*

"Rejoice, O Door of God, through which the Creator passed incarnate, preserving thee sealed! Rejoice, light Cloud, bearing Christ the divine Rain! Rejoice, Ladder and heavenly Throne! Rejoice, mountain of God, holy, fertile, and unhewn!"

# ON SUNDAY EVENING, AT VESPERS
[f. 75vA] *On "Lord, I have cried", Penitential Stichera, Tone 3.*

*Podoben: "Great is the power of Thy martyrs" (Веліа мчникъ твои):* [^98]

"Greatly sinning and provoking Thee, the good Master Who art merciful by nature: receive me returning as the Prodigal, and make me as one of Thy hired servants, O heavenly Father."

"Through slothfulness have I passed the measure of life, and unto the end have I now drawn near, wretched that I am, not considering the judgment that awaits me and my wretched fall; but turning me back, O Savior, save me from the condemnation of unendurable torments."

"Deliver my humble soul from Gehenna and the gnashing of teeth, and from every other torment of eternal endurance, that in meekness I may sing of Thee, the merciful God and Lover of mankind by nature."

*Other Stichera, to the Bodiless Powers, Tone 3:*

"Thou didst establish the choirs of the Bodiless Powers, O Lord, displaying unto all the wealth of Thy goodness, and bringing them from non-existence into being, who now praise Thy glory which surpasses mind with unceasing voices."

"Great is the power of Thine Angels, O Christ; for being incorporeal, they guard the world, preserving the Churches by the strength which is from Thee, O Master; and they pray unto Thee for the universe, beholding the thrice-sunny meekness of Thy unique powers," [f. 75vB] "as secondary lights, unique in the world, and shining abundantly, they bestow upon us divine splendors."

*Glory: Both now: Theotokion:*

"O Lady over all creatures, all-pure one, free my mind which is grievously held captive by passions, through thy warm intercession and maternal prayer unto thy Son and God."

*At the Aposticha, Penitential Stichera, Tone 3:*

"An evening hymn do we offer unto Thee, O Christ, with incense and spiritual songs: have mercy, O Savior, on our souls."

"Save me, O Lord my God, for Thou art the salvation of all; the storm of passions troubles me, and the burden of my transgressions drowns me: give me a helping hand, and lead me up unto the light of compunction, as Thou alone art compassionate and the Lover of mankind."

*Martyrion:*

"Great is the power of Thy Cross, O Lord; for it was planted in one place, yet it works in the world, and it showed forth Apostles from fishermen, and Martyrs from the nations, that they may pray for our souls."

*Glory: Both now: Theotokion:*

"O Theotokos, protectress of all that pray unto thee, in thee do we dare, and in thee" [f. 76rA] "do we boast, and in thee is all our hope: pray Him that was born of thee for thine unprofitable servants."

## ON MONDAY AT MATINS

*After the First Kathisma, Penitential Sessional Hymns, Tone 3:*[^99]

"Dwelling upon the earth, O my soul, repent; for the dust in the grave sings not, nor delivers from transgressions; cry aloud unto Christ God: 'O Knower of hearts, I have sinned against Thee; before Thou judgest me, spare me, O God, and have mercy on me!' "

"How long, O my soul, abidest thou in transgressions? How long dost thou receive postponement of repentance? Take to mind the coming judgment; cry aloud unto Christ God: 'O Knower of hearts, I have sinned; O Sinless Lord, have mercy on me!' "

*Glory: Both now: Theotokion:*

"At the beauty of thy virginity and the exceeding brightness of thy purity Gabriel was amazed, and cried unto thee, O Theotokos: 'What worthy praise can I offer unto thee? Or what shall I name thee? I am at a loss and dismayed; therefore, as I was commanded, I cry unto thee: Rejoice, full of grace!' "

*After the Second Kathisma, Penitential Sessional Hymns, Tone 3:*

"At the dread judgment seat I am convicted without accusers, and condemned without witnesses; for the books of conscience are opened, and secret deeds are revealed; therefore, before on that universal spectacle Thou shalt examine the things" [f. 76rB] "wrought by me: O God, cleanse me and save me!"

"Thou knowest the depth of my transgressions, O Lord; give me a helping hand, as Thou didst unto Peter, and save me!"

*Martyrion:*

"The noble patience of your endurance conquered the craft of the evil-originating enemy, O all-praised Passion-bearers; therefore ye were counted worthy of eternal blessedness; but pray the Lord, O Christ-loving ones, to save the flock of people, being true luminaries."

*Glory: Both now: Theotokion:*

"Rejoice, Virgin Mother, holy mountain, Edenic paradise, from whom was born Christ God, the Seedless Word, through Whom life blossomed forth unto the world."

*After the Third Kathisma, Sessional Hymns, Tone 3.*

*Podoben: "Beholding the beauty of thy virginity" (Красотѣ̀ дѣ́вства твоегѡ̀):*

"When we shall stand before Thine unbribable tribunal and divine judgment, and the heavenly powers shall stand before Thee with trembling: how then shall I appear unto Thee, O most righteous Judge, having deeds worthy of condemnation and fire? But by the prayers of Thine Angels, spare and save me!"

"The heavenly and earthly things didst Thou bring into being by Thy word as Almighty, and the angelic ranks standing before Thee with trembling: unceasingly offer praise unto Thee, O Master, Who illuminest the ends of the earth with Thy light; with them we also cry unto Thee: Save us by Thy tender compassion!"

*Glory: Both now: Theotokion:*

"As the uncultivated vine, O Virgin, thou didst bud forth the most beautiful" [f. 76vA] "Cluster, pouring forth for us the wine of salvation which gladdens all, both souls and bodies; therefore, ever blessing thee as the cause of good things, with the Angel we cry unto thee: 'Rejoice, full of grace!' "

# CANON OF COMPUNCTION
*The Composition of Joseph [the Hymnographer]. Tone 3.*[^100]

*Ode 1. Tone 3. Heirmos:*

*"Pharaoh's chariots didst Thou cover in the deep, having divided the sea, and Thou didst save the people of Israel who sang unto Thee with hymns."*

"From the darkness of transgressions deliver me, O Sinless One, which I have committed foolishly; grant me tears of compunction, as once unto the harlot."

"Having become a den of robbers by improper deeds, by virtues make me Thy temple, O Lover of mankind, Who willingly wast born in a cave."

*Martyrion:*

"By the guidance of the Divine Spirit ye passed through the storm of tortures, O God-inspired Martyrs, and reached the divine haven."

*Martyrion:*

"Enlightened by the grace of the Spirit, O Martyrs, ye fled from the exceeding deep darkness of idolatry, rejoicing, O all-praised ones."

*Theotokion:*

"O all-holy, all-pure one, helper of sinners, restoration of the fallen, grant me, who have greatly sinned, compunctionate repentance."

# ANOTHER CANON TO THE HOLY BODILESS ANGELS
*The Composition of Theophanes. Tone 3.*[^101]

*Ode 1. Tone 3. Heirmos:*

*"Let us sing a new song, O ye peoples:"*

[f. 76vB] "Unoriginate of ages, and Giver of all God-befitting beauty, O Christ God, enlighten my thought by the nod of Thy Powers."

"Rejoicing in an angel-befitting manner, by the most rich communion the angelic choirs are secretly enlightened by Thy fair splendors, O Savior, of the hidden mystery."

"As God and Life-Creator, the beneficent Spirit, proceeding from the Father, established the heavenly Hosts with untouchable divine graces."

*Theotokion:*

"O divine leader Gabriel, with the choir of the Bodiless ones, and now most rich, cry out a joyful voice unto her that is full of grace: 'Rejoice, all-immaculate one!' "

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*

*"Establish me, O Lord, Who alone art abundantly merciful, and stretch forth a helping hand, as Thou art the Lover of mankind."*

"As Thou didst save Peter who was sinking, O Lover of mankind: so also lead me up from the depth of my transgressions."

"Slain by deceptions and killed by passions, do Thou, O Life-Giver, quicken me by the forms of repentance."

*Martyrion:*

"Burned unjustly with material fire, O Martyrs, ye were immaterially inflamed with immaterial desire."

*Martyrion:*

"O Martyrs, being torn asunder, ye destroyed the tearing and mocking of the deceiver, and were counted worthy of crowns."

*Theotokion:*

"O Mary, named after the Lord, held fast am I by many soul-corrupting passions: free me by thy prayers."

[f. 77rA] *Another Heirmos:*

*"Thou hast shattered the bow of the enemy, and crushed the shield by Thy might, O Master Christ, our confirmation: holy art Thou, O Lord!"*

"Streaming brooks of grace and rivers of goodness hast Thou revealed the angelic choirs, secretly shining with Thy dawn."

"That Thou mightest show forth, O Master Christ, the treasures of Thy wealth and might, Thou didst bring into being the intelligent powers, partakers of Thy glory."

"With trembling the angelic splendors, standing before Thee in ministry, ever sing of Thy power which is unreckonable in might, O Christ."

*Theotokion:*

"Incorruptibly and immutably did He assume the whole man, He Who is Master of all, O Mother of God: incorruptibly didst thou reveal the overflowing fountain of grace."

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*

*"Wast Thou wroth against the rivers, O Lord? Wast Thy wrath against the rivers, or Thine onset against the sea?"*

"Loose the bonds of my passions, O Lord; and having bound me with repentance, make me a partaker of Thy good things."

"Cry unto me the light-bearing forms of repentance, O Christ Who art the Sun, driving away the deep darkness of my evils."

*Martyrion:*

"Ye appeared as wise sufferers, like coals of fire, burning up the matter of godlessness and enlightening souls in darkness."

*Martyrion:*

"Ye were assimilated unto the death of Christ, O Martyrs, having partaken of various pains; therefore ye inherit divine life."

*Theotokion:*

[f. 77rB] "Grant me, O pure one, true repentance; still the tumult of my passions, O protectress of them that sin."

*Another Heirmos: "Strange and unutterable:"*

"O rays, receiving the thrice-sunny radiance, ye were brought by divine will into the Trinitarian adornment, guided by the power of the Spirit."

"Sent into the world unto them that are about to believe in God: as guardians of salvation unto the pious, O Angels, fashioning Thy glory, O Savior."

"The Angels are secretly enlightened by pure approach unto Thy Godhead, O Christ all-holy, crying: 'Glory to Thy power, O Lover of mankind!' "

"Beholding the inextinguishable radiance of the super-divine Godhead, manifestly enriched, the angelic ranks proclaim."

*Theotokion:*

"As a slavish suppliant I now come beneath thy shelter, O all-immaculate one; but deliver me, O Theotokos, from the turmoil of passions, who gavest birth to the Author of sinlessness."

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*

*"Thy light that knows no evening, O Christ, shine forth, O God, upon my humble soul, and guide me in Thy fear; for light are Thy commandments."*

"Set me not naked of good deeds at Thy judgment seat, O Lover of mankind; but clothe me in the garment of divine actions through repentance."

*Martyrion:*

[f. 77vA] "I am wounded by the weapon of passions, and into the pit of despair have I fallen; overlook me not, O Master, but heal me by the radiance of conversion."

"Cruelly scraped with claws, and cut down with the sword, O sufferers, and exhausted with wounds, ye bowed not the knee unto the idol."

"The world is ever adorned by your sufferings, O holy Martyrs; for ye found a transcendent abode with the Angels."

*Theotokion:*

"O thou who alone on earth didst give birth in the flesh unto the Word by a word, and didst remain a Virgin: deliver me from irrational deeds, that with honorable words I may sing of thee."

*Another Heirmos: "The Invisible One appeared upon earth:"*

"With the Father, the Son, and the Spirit: enlightened by the thrice-radiant light, let us faithful sing of the one Godhead together with the angelic hosts."

"The Seraphim teach to honor one pre-unoriginate Principle, crying aloud manifestly the thrice-holy voice."

"Divinely, O Maiden, did the Archangel Gabriel, descending from heaven, announce unto thee the birth of the Giver of life, O all-pure Theotokos."

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*

*"Thou Who hast reached unto the end of the ages, O Lover of mankind, and hast them that are engulfed in the storm-tossed thoughts of wrath: despise not them that cry: Save, O Savior, as Thou didst save the Prophet from the beast."*

"Lifted up in mind like the ancient Pharisee, by transgressions" [f. 77vB] "have I fallen grievously; and seeing me, the deceiver rejoices, O Christ, Who didst humble him by the Cross: have compassion on me who have humbled myself."

"Having been a lover of sin like no other in life, O Master, wretched that I am, I await Thy long-suffering, yet am not worthy thereof; but turn me back by Thy tender compassion."

*Martyrion:*

"By fierce slaughter the lawless ones condemned the God-wise, with fire and burning and piercings: yet they proved them truly brighter than gold and heirs of Christ."

"The tribunal was filled with struggles and exceeding great contests, and having surpassed wounds beyond nature, ye conquered the prince of darkness and received crowns from God, O sufferers."

"The Ark of the Covenant, the truly holy Table, our Propitiatory, the ensouled Church of God, to praise her in all things, let us sing of the true Mother of the Creator."

*Another Heirmos: "At the descent of Jonah into the nethermost parts of Hades:"*

"Sing mightily of the first and all-bright radiance of the Godhead, O Archangels and Angels, crying with Principalities, Authorities, and Powers, with unceasing voices unto the Lord."

"He Who by the all-sunny order invisibly strengthens the intelligible world in order: vouchsafe us to be assimilated unto this in a God-pleasing manner through the honorable Church."

*Theotokion:*

"Heal..."

[f. 78rA] "...as an ever-flowing fountain of healing did the Word Who dwelt in thee show thee forth; pray therefore, O Virgin Theotokos, heal the wounds of my soul."

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*

*"The three Children in the furnace, prefiguring the Trinity, trampled the threat of fire, and singing, cried aloud: 'Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers!' "*

"Thy time is ending, O my soul; the departure hath drawn near: show forth the fruits of repentance before the doors are shut; cry aloud unto Christ: 'O Lord, save me!' "

"The plow of incorruptible knowledge, let us sow the wheat of repentance, O alas, that we may reap the sheaf of righteousness, rewarding our souls in Christ."

*Martyrion:*

"Luminaries of piety, adversaries of impiety, enrichers of the poor, O Martyrs of the Lord: enrich with virtues my most wretched soul that is destitute."

"Thou Who didst save the Publican who groaned from the depths: accept also my small groaning, and save me for the sake of the Passion-bearers who glorified Thee in their members, O Christ."

"O Fountain that driest not up the waters of forgiveness, dry up the streams of my transgressions, granting me streams of tears, that I may sing of Thee as God."

*Another Heirmos: "The proud tormentor:"*

"With steadfast mind and valiant eye beholding the primal splendors: by participation ye become secondary lights, crying: 'Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!' "

"Guided by unswerving desire and ineffable love," [f. 78rB] "by the beauties of the Creator, by ordination ye became secondary luminaries, O angelic choirs, crying: 'Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!' "

*Theotokion:*

"Thou didst give birth unto the incarnate Word, unoriginate, Who was begotten of the Father without mother before all ages, a divine birth, O Lady, blessed is the fruit of thy womb."

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*

*"He Who descended into the flame unto the Hebrew Children by divine power, and appeared as the Lord: praise Him, ye priests; exalt Him above all, ye peoples, unto the ages."*

"For the sake of mockery Ham became a servant by his father's sentence; what wilt thou do, O my soul, having enslaved thyself unto passions, and behaving foolishly, and not fearing the heavenly Father?"

"Cain the fratricide became a fratricide foolishly; thou hast appeared like unto him, not slaying another, but thine own self, O my soul, through love of pleasure and the deceits of life."

*Martyrion:*

"Chosen pearls of the Lord, precious stars, luminaries shining with the dawn of divine grace, Passion-bearers of Christ: assembling in faith, let us worthily honor them."

"Receiving the blood of the wise Passion-bearers above incense, O Word, by their prayers save them that fall down before Thee in repentance, as Thou alone art merciful."

*Theotokion:*

"By the defilement of a prodigal life have I now drawn near unto Hades; having the promptest nod, O Maiden, as thou gavest birth unto God the merciful" [f. 78vA] "unutterably, have compassion on me and save me."

*Another Heirmos:*

*"The God-bearing Children, having quenched the material flame of fire with an immaterial flame, and the company sang: 'Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing and exalt Him above all unto the ages!' "*

"As Maker of all, Thou didst conceive the Angels; and standing before Thee with fear, crying with trembling: 'Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing and exalt Him above all unto the ages!' "

"By participation in the divine fire, having become as flame, the heavenly minds cry: 'Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing and exalt Him above all unto the ages!' "

"The immaterial and intelligent Angels didst Thou establish before all visible things, unceasingly crying unto Thee: 'Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing and exalt Him above all unto the ages!' "

*Theotokion:*

"The Word of the Father, incarnate beyond word, didst thou bear, O Virgin Theotokos, Whom we sing of: all works unceasingly as the Lord, and we exalt Him above all unto all ages."

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*

*"On Mount Sinai Moses saw Thee in the bush, O Lord, conceiving in thy womb the fire of the Godhead unburnt; and Daniel saw thee, an unhewn mountain, a rod that budded forth from the root of David."*

"Jacob received the birthright on account of temperance of old, but Esau surrendered his seniority, not" [f. 78vB] "restraining his belly; how evil is intemperance, and how great is temperance in the similitude of fasting: love, O my soul, the attraction of good things."

"Having endured much like the blameless, everlasting Job; for the torrents of temptations rushing together shook not the pillar of his heart; emulate him always, remaining immutable, O my soul, against the wiles of the evil one."

*Martyrion:*

"Kindled by the fire of the Divine Spirit, ye appeared as swords cutting down the opposing hosts, O Trophy-bearers of Christ, and glorified by great victories, ye are crowned by the almighty hand of the King of all."

*Martyrion:*

"O blameless multitude of Martyrs, pray the Master and God, Who accepted your unutterable labors and united you unto the incorporeal hosts, to abate the multitude of mine immeasurable evils."

*Theotokion:*

"O bright bridal chamber of the prodigal, show me forth as a house of light; O impassable gate, open unto me the way of repentance; O holy Land, guide me into the land of the meek, O Lady, freeing me from the great mastery of passions."

*Another Heirmos:*

*"Wounded with the arrow by the glory of thy most pure childbearing, O pure one, and marveling at thy most fitting beauty, with angelic hymns worthily do we magnify thee as Mother of God."*

"O choirs now standing before the great and primal Light, ye have become most mighty intercessors for all of us who magnify you as Angels of God with divine might."

[f. 79rA] "Counted worthy to glorify the Trinity with divine hymns, being brightly illuminated with Her first radiance, vouchsafe us to be illuminated with the second radiance, who piously magnify you."

*Theotokion:*

"We all know thee as the foundation of our salvation; for thy holy childbearing hath saved our nature, O Mother of God, who sing of thee, O Theotokos, and faithfully glorify thee."

*At the Aposticha, Penitential Stichera, Tone 3:*

"Gather my scattered mind, O Lord, and cleanse my frozen heart; give me repentance as unto Peter, groaning as unto the Publican, and tears as unto the harlot, that with a great voice I may cry unto Thee: 'O God, cleanse me, as Thou alone art compassionate and the Lover of mankind!' "

"Many a time when completing the singing, I have found myself full of sins; with the tongue indeed I utter the singing, but in soul I ponder improper things; but amend both, O Christ God, through repentance, and save me."

"Come, all ye peoples, let us honor the memory of the holy Passion-bearers; for having become a spectacle unto Angels and men, they received crowns of victory from Christ, and pray for our souls."

*Glory: Both now: Theotokion:*

"O pure praise of maidenhood, being the order of heaven, the song of Apostles, and the fulfillment of the Prophets, O Lady, receive our prayers."

# ON MONDAY, THE BEATITUDES
*Tone 3:*[^102]

[f. 79rB] "Adam our forefather, who rejected Thy commandment, O Christ, didst Thou cast out of Paradise; but the Thief, O Bountiful One, who confessed Thee upon the Cross, didst Thou settle therein, who cried: 'Remember me, O Savior, in Thy Kingdom!' "

"Looking down upon the multitude of my sins according to the multitude of Thy mercy, O Christ, save me, and in the day of judgment deliver me from eternal torment, as God, that I may hymn Thy goodness."

"Cherubim and Seraphim, Thrones, Archangels, Powers and Principalities, Dominions, Angels and all Authorities: pray the Creator to overlook my transgressions then, when He shall come to judge the earth, as He is the Lover of mankind."

*Martyrion:*

"Having dipped their purple robe in sacred blood, the sufferers of Christ were counted worthy to reign together in a God-befitting manner with the King of hosts, and they ask for us the remission of transgressions, who ever honor them worthily with peace."

*Glory:*

"Faithfully singing of the one Godhead in three Persons: Father, Word, and Holy Comforter Spirit, let us cry out angelically unto the end unceasingly: 'Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, O God, Who savest our souls!' "

*Both now: Theotokion:*

"O light Cloud, who gavest birth to Light from Light, guide and direct me, darkened by passions and the pleasures of life, unto the light, O pure one; and pray that I may attain the glory which they who have lived well have now obtained."

*Toward Monday [Evening]:*

## ON MONDAY EVENING, AT VESPERS

[f. 79vA] *On "Lord, I have cried", Penitential Stichera, Tone 3.*

*Podoben: "In the likeness of the Cross" (Кртаѡбразно):*

"The multiform serpent, seeing the slothfulness within me toward profitable deeds, and transforming itself by a nod toward evil and worse things, showed forth the sweetness of sin; but its own bitter working is contrary to the divine commandments; therefore it strikes me in disposition, to accept evil as good, O deceitful one, O Christ."

"Having walked zealously upon the great path of sinful iniquity, and forsaken the right path unto the end, now have I drawn near unto the gates of death, crying in compunction: 'O Path of our life, my good Jesus: turning me back unto the breadth of true repentance, save me; grant me correction, and before death vouchsafe me divine forgiveness!' "

"I have slain myself with diverse sins and many transgressions, and through great impropriety I lie dead and helpless in truth; yet my only hope lives, which is toward Thy tender compassion, O Christ, Who givest breath, sight, and life unto the dead, and slayest the passions that have made us wretched; therefore anticipate and snatch me from eternal death!"

[f. 79vB] *Other Stichera, to the Holy Forerunner John, Tone 3:*[^103]

"O Forerunner, who in thy birth didst loose thy mother's childlessness and thy father's muteness: loose the childlessness of my heart and the irrationality of my soul by thy acceptable prayers unto the young Child, the Son, the God-Child and God of all, Whom as the Word of the Mind thou didst bear without passion; and strengthen me both to speak and to do the things pleasing unto Him."

"O thou who didst prepare the paths of Christ and make straight His paths, before Whose face thou wast sent: show forth my heart well-trodden unto Him by thy prayers and manifest help; for thou wast shown worthy to walk with His honorable feet upon the heavenly land, where the feet of the meek do walk, that with love [f. 80rA] I may honor thee as an intercessor."

"Thou didst emulate the life of Angels upon earth, the perfection of the Prophets, and the first martyr of the New Covenant, and first preacher unto the holy ones beneath the earth, of the Divine Word's coming in the flesh, attested friend of Christ, of the Lamb and Redeemer: from all snares of the enemy and his manifold temptations, deliver thy servant, O Baptist John, by thy prayers."

*Glory: Both now: Theotokion:*

"O Cloud of the light that knows no setting, Maiden full of the joy of God, blessed Mary: shine upon me the light of repentance, held foolishly in sinful darkness, and by thy prayers deliver me from the fire of Gehenna and unknowable darkness; and make me a partaker of the day that knows no evening, O Virgin, who flee beneath thy shelter, O all-pure one."

*At the Aposticha, Penitential Stichera, Tone 3:*

"An evening hymn do we offer unto Thee, O Christ, with incense and spiritual songs: have mercy, O Savior, on our souls."

"Save me, O Lord my God, for Thou art the salvation of all; the storm of passions troubles me, and the burden of iniquities drowns me: give me a helping hand, and lead me up unto the light of compunction, as Thou alone art tender-hearted and the Lover of mankind."

*Martyrion:*

"Great is the power of Thy Martyrs, O Christ; for lying in tombs, they drive away spirits, and have abolished the power of the enemy through Trinitarian faith, having contended for piety."

*Glory: Both now: Theotokion:*

"O holy Theotokos among women, unwedded Mother: pray Him Whom thou didst bear, the King and God, that He may save us, as He is the Lover of mankind."

## ON TUESDAY AT MATINS

*After the First Kathisma, Penitential Sessional Hymns, Tone 3:*

[f. 80rB] "Dwelling upon the earth, O my soul, repent; for the dust in the grave sings not, nor delivers from transgressions; cry aloud unto Christ God: 'O Knower of hearts, I have sinned; before Thou judgest me, have mercy on me!' *Glory:*"

"How long, O my soul, abidest thou in transgressions? How long dost thou receive postponement of repentance? Take to mind the judgment that is to come; cry aloud unto Christ God: 'O Knower of hearts, I have sinned; O Sinless Lord, have mercy on me!' "

*Both now: Theotokion:*

"Our refuge and strength, O Theotokos, mighty helper of the world: by thy prayer save thy servants from every affliction, O only blessed one."

*After the Second Kathisma, Sessional Hymns, Tone 3:*

"At the dread judgment seat I am convicted without accusers, and condemned without witnesses; for the books of conscience are opened, and secret deeds are uncovered; before therefore in that universal spectacle Thou shalt demand an account of the things wrought by me: O God, cleanse me and save me!"

"Thou knowest the depth of my transgressions, O Lord; give me a helping hand, as Thou didst unto Peter, and save me!"

*Martyrion:*

"Ye shine by faith, O all-bright luminaries, holy physicians of piety, all-praised Passion-bearers; for ye feared not the wounds of the tormentors, and cast down the wickedness of idols, having the invincible victory of the true Cross. *Glory:*"

[f. 80vA] *Glory: Both now: Theotokion:*

"Receive, O Lady, him who flees with faith beneath thy shelter; and abhor me not, nor despise, O good one, him who prays in repentance; receive the supplication from mine unworthy lips, and by thine intercession deliver me from afflictions, that with boldness I may cry unto thee: 'Rejoice, full of grace!' "

*After the Third Kathisma, Sessional Hymns, Tone 3:*[^104]

*Podoben: "Of the divine faith" (Бжтвенныя вѣры):*

"Fleeing unto thy protection, with faith we cry from the depth of the soul, O divinely blessed Prophet and Forerunner: quiet the confusion of temptations and afflictions, and the tempest of diseases, and make of no effect the wickedly crafty counsels of the enemies, asking great mercy for us."

*Glory.*

*Podoben: "Beholding the beauty of thy virginity" (Красотѣ дѣвтва):*

"Shake off thine apathy, O wretched soul, before thy departure through repentance, and turn back with weeping, crying unto the guileless Jesus, the Lover of mankind: 'I have sinned against Thee, O Master, but as Thou art compassionate, save me through the prayers of the holy Forerunner, Who alone art sinless!' "

*Both now: Theotokion:*

"Incomprehensible and unsearchable, O Virgin Lady full of the joy of God, is the dread mystery of God wrought concerning thee; for having conceived Him without seed, thou didst bear Him invested with flesh from thy most pure blood; Whom do thou earnestly pray, O pure one, together with the Forerunner, that our souls may be saved."

## ON TUESDAY AT MATINS

# PENITENTIAL CANON TO OUR LORD JESUS CHRIST
[f. 80vB] *A Composition of Joseph.*

*Ode 1, Tone 3. The Heirmos:*[^105]

*"Marvelous in glory, Who workest wonders, art Thou, O God, Who didst dry up the abyss, and drown the chariots, and save the people who sing unto Thee as unto our Deliverer and God."*

"Within thyself before the end, believe, that we may weep over earthly things; when we shall kindle our deeds like bright candles, so that we may attain the divine bridal chamber yonder."

"Thou didst show forth salvation of old unto Manasseh and unto all souls, when he cried out from the midst of bonds, bound unto Thee, the only Good One; emulate him, O soul, and thou shalt be saved."

*Martyrion:*

"Blindness of eyes, loss of hands, cutting out of the tongue, cutting off of feet, breaking of ribs and arms did the divine sufferers endure, giving thanks unto Christ."

*Martyrion:*

"The shrine of your relics hath appeared unto us as a place of healing, O holy Martyrs, unto all the faithful, from which we draw healings for souls and bodies, who ever honor you as is due."

*Theotokion:*

"Carrying Christ, the Manna of immortality, O spiritual Vessel: deliver me from the bitterness of soul-destroying passions, O Virgin fed from on high, that with faith I may piously glorify thee."

# CANON TO THE HOLY FORERUNNER JOHN
*Tone 3. The Heirmos:*[^106]

*"He Who of old by His divine nod gathered the waters into one gathering, and divided the sea for the people of Israel: this is our God, Who is exceedingly glorified; unto Him alone let us sing, for He hath been glorified."*

"Grant me to bud forth divine fruits of virtues, praying unto the Baptist, loosing the barrenness of my sin, and driving away the gloom from my mind, O Forerunner of the Lord."

[f. 81rA] "As a star that ran before, thou didst appear upon earth, of the great Sun of glory Who hath enlightened the whole earth; Him do thou pray, O Forerunner, to enlighten my soul darkened by evil thoughts."

"Unto those once in Hades, preaching by the Divine Spirit, thou didst foreannounce, O Forerunner; quicken my slain soul by thy supplications, and raise me up from the tomb of transgressions, I pray thee, O glorious Forerunner."

*Theotokion:*

"With the Archangels and Angels, O Virgin, and with all the Saints, pray the Lord Who was begotten of thee for us, we pray thee who entreat thee, who confess thee in truth to be the Theotokos, that we may be delivered from afflictions."

# PENITENTIAL CANON
*Ode 3. The Heirmos:*[^107]

*"O barren and childless soul, acquire blessed fruit, and becoming joyful in children, cry aloud: 'I have been established by Thee, O God; there is none holy, and there is none righteous beside Thee, O Lord!' "*

"I have foolishly rejected the law of God, and I am to be condemned; and what shall I do? I know not. O most righteous Judge, have compassion and save me in Thy tender-heartedness."

"Being the Orient unto the orients, O Lover of mankind: shine upon me, I pray Thee, the light of righteousness, delivering me from the darkening of passions and from the darkness of my sins, O Most Merciful One."

*Martyrion:*

*Theotokion:*

"O all-pure Mother, unto us who repent and flee unto Christ, and desire to receive remission of transgressions: make Him merciful unto all, O Lady of all."

"O Christ Who of old didst pour forth water from the rock for the disobedient and murmuring people, a healing of thirst: pour forth from my dry soul, O God, a drop of compunction that cleanses me."

# PENITENTIAL CANON

"I have been wounded by the weapon of sin, and I lie wholly disabled; O Christ God, Who wast once wounded with a lance for my sake: heal me by Thy tender mercy."

"I groan, and abide in evils, yet even then I bring no tears, suffering from insensibility; O Word of God, have compassion on me and save me by Thy good judgments."

*Martyrion:*

"Like lambs neither crying out, nor uttering a word, nor emitting a voice, O all-glorious sufferers, ye came unto slaughter and wounds, singing unto Christ."

[f. 82rB] *Martyrion:*

*Theotokion:*
