# CANON TO THE FORERUNNER
*Ode 6. The Heirmos:*[^109]

*"The lowest depth of sins hath surrounded me, and my spirit fails; but stretching out Thy high arm, O Master, save me, O Helmsman, as Thou didst Peter."*

"Having baptized Him with waters who bowed beneath thy hand, the stream of delight: pray Him, O wise one, to send down unto me the water of compunction, who have sinned much."

"The abyss of tender mercy didst thou wash in the river, O Forerunner, even Jesus the Lover of mankind, Who covers the heavens on high with waters; pray Him to pour forth remission for me."

" 'Repent!' cried the Forerunner; 'the Kingdom of heaven is at hand!' Count those worthy to attain it, who honor thee with love and flee beneath thine honorable shelter."

*Theotokion:*

"O all-pure one, who gavest thy flesh on loan unto the Creator: with the heavenly hosts, and with all the Prophets, Apostles, and Martyrs, pray Him to have compassion on thy servants."

# PENITENTIAL CANON
*Ode 7. The Heirmos:*[^110]

*"Having cooled the flame of the furnace, and saved the children unburnt: blessed art Thou unto ages, O Lord God of our fathers."*

[f. 82vA] "I have stripped myself of the garments of incorruption, and clothed myself in deeds of dishonor; therefore I cry unto Thee, O Bountiful God: enlighten me with the garments of virtues."

"With prodigal eyes I have defiled myself, and by the slackness of intemperance I have become unclean, and became an abomination before Thee, O Jesus; receive me as the prodigal."

*Martyrion:*

"Having loved the life on high, ye endured many afflictions, O armorbearers of Christ, treasures of the martyrs; therefore with faith we call you blessed."

*Martyrion:*

"Illuminated with the radiance of martyrdom, ye shine brighter than the sun, and drive away the great darkness of nature, O holy Martyrs."

*Theotokion:*

"Having given birth to the Creator of all, Who holds back the gloom of ignorance: deliver me from sin, O Theotokos, pure ever-Virgin."

# CANON TO THE FORERUNNER
*Ode 7. The Heirmos:*

*"The three children in Babylon..."*

"As a luminary of the Light, illuminate my spirit darkened by slothfulness and blinded; directing me unto the path of repentance, O Baptist and Forerunner of Christ."

"Pondering the hour of judgment, I am wholly terrified, being conscious of a multitude of countless deeds; O Forerunner of the Lord who standest before Him: deliver me from the fire that lies before me."

"O protector of my life, my defender, O Forerunner: preserve and shelter me from enemies visible and invisible, and make me a partaker of the heavenly Kingdom."

*Theotokion:*

"As the Mother of God, pray Thy Son with the Prophets, Apostles, and Martyrs, to deliver us from future necessity, who ever honor thee."

# PENITENTIAL CANON
[f. 82vB] *Ode 8. The Heirmos:*

*"God Who is unceasingly glorified by the Angels, the heaven of heavens, the earth and mountains, hills and the depth, and all the race of mankind: with hymns bless Him as Creator and Deliverer."*

"Having not Thy fear dwelling in my heart, I, foolish one, have fulfilled all carnal pleasure, and I tremble before Thy judgment, O Christ the King: condemn me not now who repent."

"Vouchsafe me, O Most Merciful One, to pass over unto the spiritual land, wherein the meek do dwell, washing me by repentance from earthly sin, O Thou Who for this cause wast born of the Virgin upon earth."

*Martyrion:*

"Having washed your feet in your own blood, tripping up the enemy, and ever making your journey unto the heavens, O all-glorious sufferers of Christ, the God of all."

*Martyrion:*

"Ye stripped yourselves for sufferings and great struggles; ye stripped the enemy and clothed him with shame; therefore as crown-bearers ye dance in the heavens, O glorious Passion-bearers."

*Theotokion:*

"The Lord, beautiful in beauty, having desired the beauty of thy loveliness, took up His abode in thy womb, O all-immaculate one, and enlightened human nature with beauties, even with gifts beyond the mind."

# CANON TO THE FORERUNNER
*Ode 8. The Heirmos:*

*"In the unsteady fire..."*

"Thou didst preach the Lamb of God, Who takes away the sins of men, O John, divine Forerunner; pray Him that the time of my sins may be loosed, and that I may be counted worthy of the portion of those who are saved."

[f. 83rA] "Deliver me from the burning flame of the furnace, from the outer, unilluminated darkness, who am wholly held in the darkness of evil deeds; I pray Thee, O pre-eternal Word of God, for the sake of Thy glorious, divine Baptist."

"Unto empty and barren souls didst thou preach fruitfulness through repentance, O divine Forerunner of the Lord; cut down my thorn-bearing soul, and cleanse it with tears, that I may yield an ear of good deeds."

*Theotokion:*

"As the Mother of God, pray with the holy Angels, Prophets, Apostles, and Martyrs, to deliver those who confess thee to be God's Mother from afflictions and sorrows, and from the torments of the age to come."

# PENITENTIAL CANON
*Ode 9. The Heirmos:*[^111]

*"Blessed is the Lord God of Israel, Who hath raised up an horn of salvation for us in the house of David His servant, through the tender mercy of His loving-kindness, whereby the dayspring from on high hath visited us, and hath guided us into the way of peace."*

"Behold, now is the acceptable time, and the day of purification; desire henceforth to turn back, O my soul, and reap intelligent fruits, lest the dread scythe of death find thee unfruitful, and cut thee down like the ancient fig tree, and send thee unto the fire yonder."

"As once the rich man, making merry in luxury, had no great compassion toward his neighbor, and feared not the unquenchable fire: therefore, O Master, soften the stony hardness of my soul, that at least at the end I, the darkened one, may be enlightened by tender mercy."

[f. 83rB] *Martyrion:*

"Signed with the divine blood of Christ, O Martyrs, and suffering valiantly with the signs of faith, ye put down the enemies of the unbelievers; and snatching many people from foul delusion, ye enlightened them with divine rays, with the light of His understanding."

*Martyrion:*

"Ye appeared as sharpened swords, cutting through the enemy's battle-lines, O divine Martyrs of Christ; and as vessels containing the radiance of the Holy Trinity, and luminaries shining the light of piety upon the faithful, and true citizens of the spiritual Sion."

*Theotokion:*

"The Prophets foresaw thee as a light-bearing cloud, from which the great Sun appeared unto us, Christ God, and enlightened those who were formerly darkened; Him do thou pray, O good one, to drive away the clouds of my passions, and to enlighten me with divine light."

# CANON TO THE FORERUNNER
*Ode 9. The Heirmos:*

*"In the shadow of the law and the Scripture..."*

"Looking into the shadow of the law, I beheld the radiance of divine grace from afar, wisely enlightening the ends of the earth and driving away the darkness of ignorance, O Forerunner; therefore we honor thee."

"As a Martyr of Christ, as the divine Baptist, as the luminary of repentance, and as the dawn of piety, mediator of the Old and New: vouchsafe my humble soul, which hath walked in malice, to partake of divine understanding."

"In the dreadful hour, in the fearful hour, in the hour of condemnation, when I am condemned: deliver me, O wise one, from the threatening that awaits me there, having the Savior of our souls as One Who gives ear unto thy supplications as the Friend of the Bridegroom."

[f. 83vA] *Theotokion:*

"As the Mother of God, as the Mother of Him Who was born in the flesh without corruption, O pure one: with the Bodiless Powers, the Apostles and Prophets, with the Hierarchs and Martyrs, pray Him unceasingly to grant peace unto the world, O all-pure Virgin Mother."

*At the Aposticha, Penitential Stichera, Tone 3:*

"Cleanse my dispersed mind, O Lord, and purify my frozen heart; give me repentance as unto Peter, groaning as unto the Publican, and tears as unto the harlot, that with a great voice I may cry unto Thee: 'O God, save me, as Thou alone art compassionate and the Lover of mankind!' "

"Many a time when offering a song, I have found myself committing sins; with the tongue indeed I utter the singing, but in soul I ponder improper things; but amend both through repentance, O Christ God, and have mercy on me."

*Martyrion:*

"The soldiers of Christ cast away the fear of kings and torturers, and boldly and manfully confessed Him, the Lord God and King of all; and they pray for our souls."

*Glory: Both now: Theotokion:*

"Without seed didst thou conceive of the Holy Spirit; and glorifying thee, we hymn thee: 'Rejoice, O all-pure Virgin!' "

# ON TUESDAY, THE BEATITUDES
*Tone 3:*[^112]

"Adam our forefather, who rejected Thy commandment, O Christ, didst Thou cast out of Paradise; but the Thief, O Bountiful One, who confessed Thee upon the Cross, didst Thou settle therein, who cried: 'Remember me, O Savior, in Thy Kingdom!' "

[f. 83vB] "I possess a soul defiled by dark passions; I come unto Thy compassions, being in despair, and earnestly cry unto Thee, O Christ: 'Have compassion on me, as Thou art merciful, O Lord!' "

"Having become the mediator of the Old and New, O Baptist, renew me who have walked in transgressions; grant by thy supplications, O all-praised one, that I may walk steadfastly in the paths of repentance which lead up well into the heavenly Kingdom."

*Martyrion:*

"Having fought the good fight, O valiant sufferers, ye endured countless pains, and ye ever relieve the proud illnesses of all, and drive away the afflictions of souls; therefore with faith we glorify you, O Saints."

*Glory:*

"Light, and life, and sight, a Trinity in three Persons truly exists; all of us glorify Father, Son, and Spirit: in unity and conjunction, Master and Lord of all, one God is known in three Persons."

*Both now: Theotokion:*

"Have compassion, O Virgin Mother, on me who sin continually and provoke the good God; and establish in me now the models of repentance, O good one, that having escaped future torments, I may earnestly hymn thy prayers, O Maiden."

## ON TUESDAY EVENING, AT VESPERS

[f. 84rA] *On "Lord, I have cried", Stichera of the Cross, Tone 3.*

*Podoben: "Great is the power of Thy martyrs" (Веліа мункъ твои):* [^113]

"Creation hath been sanctified, O only Long-suffering One, by the precious blood that dripped from Thy ribs, and the rivers of polytheism have been dried up, and Adam hath been delivered from condemnation by Thy crucifixion, O Word."

"He Who is Creator and Lord of all, and God of all, voluntarily sanctifies: Thou didst endure suffering for men, lifted up upon the Cross; by the curse of the law, Thou art crucified by Thy will, O Benefactor and Lord; and pierced in Thy ribs with a lance, O Giver of life, Thou didst pour forth two fountains of immortality; therefore unceasingly all of us faithfully glorify Thy sufferings, O Bountiful One."

*Other Stichera to the Most Holy Theotokos, Tone 3:*

"Beholding Him Who was born of thee hanging upon the Tree, O all-immaculate one, thou didst cry aloud, weeping: 'My sweetest Child, whither hath Thy light-bearing beauty departed, Who didst adorn human nature?' "

"Wounded by the weapon of the serpent, the beginner of evil, and lying half-dead upon the bed of despair: heal me speedily, O Maiden, by the medicine of thy prayer, and save me, my hope and protection."

[f. 84rB] "Lay aside, O soul, the hard-to-bear burdens of thy grievous transgressions, and bow thy neck unto the light yoke of thy Lord, Who shone forth from the Virgin at the angelic voice, as in a light cloud."

*Glory: Both now: Theotokion:*

"With the light of thy prayers, O Virgin, enlighten my humble soul, as Mother of the Most High; and let me behold the path of salvation, which I, the wretched one, cannot see because of the sin that overshadows me."

*At the Aposticha, Stichera of the Cross, Tone 3:*[^114]

"We bow down before Thy precious Cross, O Christ, the guardian of the world, salvation unto us sinners, great purification, victory of kings, and praise of the whole universe."

"In the form of the Cross, Moses on the mountain lifted up his hands on high and conquered Amalek; and Thou, O Savior, having stretched out Thy hands upon the precious Cross, didst embrace and save me from the slavery of the enemy, and gavest me the sign of life, to flee from the bow of mine adversaries; therefore, O Word, I bow down before Thy precious Cross."

"The Prophets, Apostles of Christ, and Martyrs taught us to sing of the consubstantial Trinity, and enlightened the deceived nations," [f. 84vA] "and made the sons of men partakers with the Angels."

*Glory: Both now: Stavrotheotokion:*

"When thou didst see the Sun that knows no setting, Who shone forth from thy womb, setting upon the Cross, and darkening the rays of the sun, thou didst cry aloud, weighed down in soul with the darkness of grief: 'O Thou Who didst voluntarily set, shine forth again, for my enlightenment and that of the whole world!' "

## ON WEDNESDAY AT MATINS

*After the First Kathisma, Sessional Hymns of the Cross, Tone 3:*[^115]

"The Cross was lifted up upon the earth, and reached unto the heavens, not as a tree attaining height, but because of Thee Who upon it fillest all things: O Lord, glory to Thee!"

"Upon the cypress, the pine, and the cedar was the Lamb of God lifted up, that Thou mightest save those who faithfully bow down before Thy voluntary crucifixion: O Christ God, glory to Thee!"

*Glory: Both now: Stavrotheotokion:*

"Having acquired the Cross of Thy Son as a rod of strength, O Theotokos, thereby do we cast down the insolence of the enemy, who unceasingly magnify thee with love."

*After the Second Kathisma, Sessional Hymns of the Cross, Tone 3:*

"Having chosen to suffer the Cross and death, Thou didst establish it in the midst of creation, when Thou, O Savior, wast well-pleased to nail Thy body; then also the sun hid its rays; then also the Thief, beholding these things upon the Cross, cried unto Thee, crying reverently:"

[f. 84vB] " 'Remember me, O Lord!' and through faith received Paradise."

"At Thine unsearchable goodness and voluntary crucifixion, the angelic hosts marvelled, seeing how the Invisible One was wounded in the flesh, wishing to deliver mankind from corruption; therefore as unto a Benefactor we cry unto Thee: 'Glory, O Christ, to Thy tender compassion!' "

*Martyrion:*

"Having girded yourselves with the whole armor of Christ, and clothed yourselves in the armor of faith, as sufferers ye cast down the enemy's battle-lines; for zealously with the hope of life ye endured all the threats and wounds of the tormentors; therefore also ye received crowns, O patient-minded Martyrs of Christ."

*Glory: Both now: Stavrotheotokion:*

"Reproach and death through crucifixion didst Thou voluntarily endure, O Bountiful One; seeing which, she who bore Thee was wounded, by whose supplications, in the tender mercy of Thy loving-kindness, O only all-good Lord and Lover of mankind: have compassion and save the world, Who takest away the sins of the world."

*After the Third Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 3:*

*Podoben: "Beholding the beauty of thy virginity" (Красотѣ̀ дѣ́вства твоегѡ̀):*

"Having accepted crucifixion and death, Thou didst pour forth immortal life for us, O Christ Savior, and freed the world from corruption; therefore voluntarily we glorify Thy saving passions, O Giver of life and Lover of mankind, whereby we all are saved, having the peace of Thy precious Cross as an invincible weapon. *Glory:*"

"Dishonorably didst Thou endure the Cross, O Lord, Who art the Creator of all creation, that Thou mightest honor me who was formerly grievously dishonored; and pierced in Thy rib with a lance, O Long-suffering One, wishing to deliver me, Thy creation, from corruption: I hymn Thy great mercy and grace, O Lover of mankind."

[f. 85rA] *Both now: Stavrotheotokion:*

"Thy pure, unblemished Mother, O Christ, seeing Thee hanging dead upon the Tree, weeping maternally, said: 'What hath the lawless and ungrateful Hebrew assembly rendered unto Thee, which inherited many and great gifts of Thine, O my Son? I hymn Thy divine condescension!' "

# CANON OF THE PRECIOUS AND LIFE-GIVING CROSS
*A Composition of Joseph.*

*Ode 1, Tone 3. The Heirmos:*[^116]

*"He Who of old by His divine nod gathered the waters into one gathering, and divided the sea for the people of Israel: this is our God, Who is exceedingly glorified; unto Him alone let us sing, for He hath been glorified."*

"The painful passions hast Thou quenched, O Word, through the sufferings of Thy precious flesh, and saved men from the adversary who of old was slain, who piously bow down before Thine incomprehensible dispensation."

"The enemy who by deceit told man to transgress the commandment, bound him with unbreakable bonds, O Lord, in which, being incarnate by Thy will, Thou wast bound, loosing our transgressions, O Lover of mankind."

[f. 85rB] *Martyrion:*

"Beholding creation in distress through drowning in divine deceits, the Passion-bearers were shown to be storm-free harbors, having drowned all the power of the evil one in streams of blood, O great martyrs."

*Martyrion:*

"The choir of Martyrs was brightly joined unto the assemblies on high, ever illuminated with the radiance of the uncreated Godhead, and it illuminates those upon earth who faithfully glorify His wonders."

*Theotokion:*

"Thou wast shown to be higher than the heavenly ranks, having given birth upon earth unto God the Word, O all-pure one, Who by His sufferings and precious Cross raised us up unto the heavens, for the sake of His goodness."

# CANON TO THE MOST HOLY THEOTOKOS
*Tone 3. The Heirmos is the same:*[^117]

"Grant tears abundantly like rains unto the furrows of my soul, O Virgin, and vouchsafe me, O Lady, to bring forth saving fruit; and fill my heart with joy, that I may glorify thee."

"For the sake of the mercy of thy compassions, O Lady of all: have mercy on my passionate soul, and deliver me from eternal fire and from the invasion of the age, O Theotokos, who now flee beneath thy shelter."

"As an undefiled temple of Christ, my heart having been defiled with improper passions: I pray thee, O all-pure one, cleanse it by thy prayers, and enrich it with deeds of a pure life, O one full of the joy of God."

"Why, O passionate soul, dost thou pass through life in slothfulness, and fearest not the day of the dread judgment? But arise henceforth from the sin of despondency, and zealously and warmly cry unto the Lady: 'Save me, O pure Lady!' "

# CANON OF THE CROSS
*Ode 4. The Heirmos:*[^118]

*"Thou hast placed toward us steadfast love, O Lord, for Thou didst give Thine Only-begotten Son unto death for us; therefore we cry unto Thee thankfully: 'Glory to Thy power, O Lord!' "*

*Martyrion:*

*Martyrion:*

# CANON TO THE THEOTOKOS

"When the Bridegroom comes in the night to judge the earth: then vouchsafe me, O all-pure one, to go forth to meet Him with a bright lamp, and to bow down before His coming."

"By the tempest of trials and the surge of evil thoughts I am wholly drowned, and ever dragged down into the depth of despair; save me, O Lady, I cry unto thee, thy servant."

*Theotokion:*

# CANON TO THE THEOTOKOS
*Ode 8. The Heirmos:*

*"Gathered together in the unsteady fire..."*

"Unceasingly pray for those who honor thee in compunction, that they may be delivered from the snares of the devil, crying unto thy Son: 'Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing and exalt Him above all forever!' "

"When by God's command my soul is about to depart from life: snatch me from the snares of the hunters, O Theotokos, who sing: 'Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing and exalt Him above all forever!' "

"The dark night holds me, for I am enslaved by dark deeds; but do thou thyself, who art the door of the Light, illuminate me with thy light, who sing: 'Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing and exalt Him above all forever!' "

"Grant thy mercy, O Lady, unto the world; pray for thy servant, and deliver thy people from the expected punishment, O all-pure one, that we may cry unto thee, giving thanks: 'Glory to thee, O Queen of all!' "

*Ode 9. The Heirmos:*

[f. 87vA] *Ode 9. The Heirmos:*[^119]

*"Thee, Who wast prefigured in the Bush and the fire upon Sinai unto Moses the lawgiver, and Who didst conceive the divine fire in thy womb unburnt, the all-bright and unquenchable lamp: with faith and songs do we honor, magnifying thee."*

"That Thou mightest find the lost drachma, O Christ, Thou didst kindle Thy flesh upon the Cross, O Good One, and makest Thy heavenly hosts partakers of joy, O Giver of life; with them, as unto our Benefactor, honoring Thee in songs, we magnify Thee."

"As Thou didst lift up Thy hands upon the Cross, O Christ: my hands that were formerly weakened by many passions, and my knees truly weakened for the divine race, hast Thou strengthened by Thy power; therefore thankfully we magnify Thee."

*Martyrion:*

"Burning with the flame of immeasurable wounds, Thy valiant and marvelous sufferers found Thee, O Christ, as cooling dew; therefore rejoicing, they finished the race through desire of honors, unceasingly magnifying Thee in hymns, O Most Merciful One."

*Martyrion:*

"The multitude of sufferers, the choir of Saints, prays Thee, O Christ, for the assembly of the people who have provoked Thee much: through the multitude of Thy compassions, O Bountiful One, cleanse the multitude of our iniquities, as Thou art the Lover of mankind."

*Stavrotheotokion:*

"A new human likeness didst thou bear from thy blood, O Virgin; Whom, when He was lifted up upon the Cross, the sun could not bear to behold and was darkened, and the darkness of idolatry departed; therefore in hymns we magnify thee."

# CANON TO THE THEOTOKOS
[f. 87vB] *Ode 9. The Heirmos:*

*"In the shadow of the law and the Scripture, we the faithful see an image: for every male that opens the womb is holy unto God; therefore the firstborn Word of the unoriginate Father, the Son Who is the firstborn of the Mother that knew not man, do we magnify."*

"The end draws near, O soul; the judgment is at hand; shake off the deeds of shame, and lay hold of the good life, for thou hast a helper, the Theotokos, who delivers thee from great afflictions."

"I, the wretched one, have fallen among spiritual thieves, and by their wiles I was harmfully stripped of the robe of my virtues; and filled with soul-destroying passions, I cry unto thee: 'O good, all-immaculate one, despise me not!' "

"My whole life, O all-pure one, is spent in despondency, and Hades draws near unto me through despair; but grant me correction, O pure one, and leave me not to be afflicted therein, who flee unto thy shelter."

"Thou knowest the weakness of my humble body, the wounds of my soul, the groaning of my heart, and the wandering and delusion of my mind; therefore in thy tender compassion, grant healing unto both."

*At the Aposticha, Stichera of the Cross, Tone 3:*

"The tree of disobedience budded forth death unto the world; but the Tree of the Cross brought forth life and incorruption; therefore we pray Thee, the crucified Lord: let the light of Thy countenance be signed upon us."

[f. 88rA] "Through the forgetfulness of food was man cast out, having fallen by a grievous fall; but Thou, O Master, didst not despise him, but taking me up, Thou savest me and leadest me up into glory: O my Deliverer, glory to Thee!"

*Martyrion:*

"The hosts of holy Angels marvelled at the sufferings of the martyrs, how, being clothed in the flesh, they disregarded torments, having become emulators of the passions of Christ the Savior; and they pray for our souls."

*Glory: Both now: Stavrotheotokion:*

"When the much-hymned Ewe-lamb, even the Virgin Thy Mother, beheld Thee lifted up upon the Cross, O my Christ, she cried aloud with weeping: 'O my Son and my God, childless hast Thou shown me to be, Who didst preserve me pure even after childbearing!' "

# ON WEDNESDAY, THE BEATITUDES
*Tone 3:*[^120]

"Adam our forefather, who rejected Thy commandment, O Christ, didst Thou cast out of Paradise; but the Thief, O Bountiful One, who confessed Thee upon the Cross, didst Thou settle therein, who cried: 'Remember me, O Savior, in Thy Kingdom!' "

"Thou wast crucified for my sake, and pierced in the rib with a lance, O my Jesus; two fountains of salvation didst Thou pour forth for me; therefore, being saved by Thy passion, O Christ, I sing and glorify Thy tender mercy: 'Remember me, O Savior, in Thy Kingdom!' "

[f. 88rB] "Counted with the transgressors, Thou didst take away the transgressions of all, O Jesus, and wast crowned with thorns as King of all; the sinful thorns of our forefather dost Thou root out and cut down, O Christ; therefore with faith we now glorify Thy passions: 'Remember me, O Savior, in Thy Kingdom!' "

*Martyrion:*

"Having emulated the passions of Christ, O valiant sufferers, all-glorious Martyrs, ye cast down the enemy's delusion by the power of Christ, and obtained heavenly glory; pray for all of us, O Saints."

*Glory: Trinity:*

"O Trinity in three Persons, and undivided, all-creating Trinity, one essence and power: shelter Thy singers from the great harm of the enemy, and count them worthy of the Kingdom, which they who have lived well have obtained."

*Both now: Stavrotheotokion:*

"Beholding upon the Cross Him Whom she had incarnate of her pure blood, weeping she cried aloud: 'O Virgin Theotokos, what is this, O Child, that the wicked assembly hath rendered unto Thee, putting Thee to death Who art the life of the faithful and the resurrection of all?' "

## ON WEDNESDAY EVENING, AT VESPERS

[f. 88vA] *On "Lord, I have cried", Stichera to the Holy Apostles, Tone 3.*

*Podoben: "Great is the power of Thy martyrs" (Веліа мункъ):* [^121]

"By the prayers of Thine honorable and divine Apostles, O Lover of mankind, Bountiful One, only Merciful One: grant Thy peace unto Thy people, and deliver from fierce evils those who sing of Thee and faithfully bow down before Thee."

"When ye shall finally sit upon thrones to judge every creature together with the Judge of all: show me forth uncondemned, and deliver me from darkness and all torment, O my benefactors, divine Apostles."

"Deliver me, O eyewitnesses of God, from the arrows of the ungodly one, quenching his wiles, and bedew me with spiritual dew, I pray you, my wise benefactors, divine Apostles."

*Other Stichera to Saint Nicholas, Tone 3.*

*Podoben: "The same" (то́йже):*

"I, the wretched one, have been wounded by the bite of the serpent, and lie cast down, dead and breathless; by thine active prayer raise me up speedily, O all-blessed Hierarch, that I may glorify thy swift-to-hear grace."

"My mind having been darkened by evil thoughts, and lying uncared for, never ceases to be trapped by the deceitful enemy; but as God, have compassion and save me, through the prayers of Nicholas."

[f. 88vB] "A great salvation hast thou appeared unto all of us, O all-blessed Nicholas; for thou deliverest thy servants from all kinds of afflictions and temptations, from diseases, illnesses, and circumstances, and from invisible enemies."

*Glory: Both now: Theotokion:*

"Great is the power of thy wonders, O pure one; for thou deliverest from afflictions, and savest from death, and snatchest away from unexpected temptations, and quickly loosest sorrows, and takest away sins from men."

*At the Aposticha, Stichera to the Apostles, Tone 3:*

"Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth, O holy Apostles; ye destroyed the delusion of idols and preached the knowledge of God; this is your good fight, O blessed ones; therefore we sing and glorify your memory."

"Being branches of the life-bearing vine, O glorious Apostles, ye brought yourselves as fruit of piety unto Christ; therefore, having boldness, pray that peace and great mercy may be granted unto our souls."

*Martyrion:*

"The soldiers of the Martyrs, O Lord, established by faith and strengthened by hope, being spiritually united in the love of Thy Cross," [f. 89rA] "destroyed the enemy's tyranny and obtained crowns; with the Bodiless Powers they pray for our souls."

*Glory: Both now: Theotokion:*

"Snatch me, who have sinned exceedingly, O Maiden, by thy great prayer, from the distressing flame; and guide me, O pure one, by thy supplications, unto saving paths, directing me by thy maternal prayers."

## ON THURSDAY AT MATINS

*After the First Kathisma, Sessional Hymns to the Apostles, Tone 3:*[^122]

"Come, let us all praise the Apostles as helmsmen who abolished the delusion of idols, and led us unto the light of life, and taught us to believe in the Trinity; therefore today, honorably celebrating their memory, we the faithful glorify Christ our God."

"Thou hast made the memory of Thine Apostles bright, O Lord, as Almighty, for Thou didst strengthen them to emulate Thy passions; for manfully they conquered the power of the enemy; therefore also they received gifts of healings; by their prayers, O Lover of mankind, grant peace unto Thy people."

*Glory: Both now: Theotokion:*

"Pondering in mind the boundless wealth of thy tender mercy and the unutterable dominion of thy compassion: I flee unto thy protection, held fast by sorrow, and grievously despairing, I cry from the depth of my heart with tears: 'O Virgin Theotokos, save me, save me, the unworthy one!' "

[f. 89rB] *After the Second Kathisma, Sessional Hymns to the Apostles, Tone 3:*

"The Apostles watered all the earth with the word as with divine medicine, and brought forth the ear of faith, and filled the ends of the universe with Thy goodness, O Lord, and cut down all the tares; therefore they brought all unto Christ God, baptizing them into the uncreated Trinity."

*Martyrion:*

"Holy Passion-bearers, pray the merciful God, that He may grant the remission of transgressions unto our souls."

*Glory: Both now: Theotokion:*

"The Prophets foretold, the Apostles taught, the Martyrs confessed, and we have believed that thou art truly the Theotokos; therefore also we magnify thy childbearing, O all-pure one."

*After the Third Kathisma, Sessional Hymns, Tone 3:*

"As merciful, O Christ, Thou didst send Thine Apostles unto the ends of the earth, as sharpened, mighty arrows, slaying all ungodliness and evil teaching, and planting saving teachings; by their prayers, O Bountiful One, grant peace unto our souls."

*Glory: To Saint Nicholas:*[^123]

"Praising thee as a preacher of truth and an all-bright luminary unto the world, we hymn thee, O Nicholas, and cry out praying with faith: as thou didst snatch the innocent from death, even so, O holy one, deliver us also from afflictions, sorrows, and every cruel oppression."

[f. 89vA] *Both now: Theotokion:*

"Quicken my soul, slain by many transgressions, O all-immaculate Lady, as thou hast maternal boldness toward thy Son; for thou alone, beyond mind and understanding, didst give birth unto the Word, co-unoriginate with the Father and the Spirit, Who ever grants life and incorruption unto the world, and great mercy."

# CANON TO THE HOLY APOSTLES
*A Composition of Theophanes.*

*Ode 1, Tone 3. The Heirmos:*[^124]

*"He Who of old by His divine nod gathered the waters into one gathering, and divided the sea for the people of Israel: this is our God, Who is exceedingly glorified; unto Him alone let us sing, for He hath been glorified."*

"Pillars of the Church, foundations of the faith, pious confirmation, and they that establish all things for the faithful: come, let us bless the sacred Apostles, that by their prayers we may be saved."

"Immovable pillars of piety: set me upright who have been tripped up by the enemy's deceit, and lie upon the earth in distress and helplessness, that I may find remission of the things wherein I have sinned."

"Before the judgment, I, the prodigal, fear and condemn myself, for I have acquired countless evil deeds; therefore I pray Thee, O righteous Judge: save me who am in despair, through the divine prayers of Thine Apostles."

*Theotokion:*

"With the holy Prophets, with the Apostles and Martyrs, earnestly pray the Lord Who was incarnate of thee, O pure one, that He may put to death all our carnal passions, and grant us eternal life."

# CANON TO SAINT NICHOLAS
[f. 89vB] *A Composition of Joseph.*

*Ode 1, Tone 3. The Heirmos:*[^125]

*"Let us sing unto the Lord, Who wrought marvelous wonders in the Red Sea; for with the deep He covered the adversaries, and saved Israel; unto Him alone let us sing, for He hath been glorified."*

"As an all-bright, unquenchable luminary, a pillar upon the earth, and one who calls unto the heavenly harbor those who are ever drowned by the waves of life: let us all honor Nicholas, and bless him with love."

"Strengthened by the power of God, O all-blessed one, thou didst acquire zeal for piety according to knowledge; therefore thou didst deliver those who were unjustly about to be given over to death; for this cause we pray thee: deliver us from all unjust affliction, O Nicholas."

"Offer prayers unto the Lord, O holy father, without ceasing: that He may deliver us from sins, and from the flame of eternal torment, and from afflictions and sorrows, as He is the only All-good One."

*Theotokion:*

"The divine Ark that contained the Lawgiver Who takes away all our iniquities for the sake of the unutterable deep of divine mercy: O all-pure Mother, let us sing in concord."

# CANON TO THE APOSTLES
*Ode 3. The Heirmos:*

*"O Most High Ruler of all, Who from non-existence didst bring all things by the Word, which are built and perfected by the Spirit: establish me in Thy love."*

"Ye who filled the ends of the world with divine teaching: fill my soul with virtuous deeds and good thoughts, O eyewitnesses of Christ."

[f. 90rA] "From the many snares of the evil one, and from every sorrow, and constraint, and great tribulation: as disciples of Christ, deliver me."

"Understand, O my wretched and humble soul, that often sinnest and provokest God: how dost thou, a sinner, ask forgiveness, being unwilling to cease from evil?"

*Theotokion:*

"O divine ladder which Jacob saw, since God descended thereon, raising us up: earnestly pray with the Apostles to have compassion on us."

# CANON TO SAINT NICHOLAS
*Ode 3. The Heirmos:*

*"O barren and childless soul, acquire fruit from God, and becoming joyful, cry aloud: 'I have been established by Thee, O God; there is none holy, and there is none righteous beside Thee, O Lord!' "*

"A sharpened spiritual sword wast thou shown to be, O wise one, cutting down the evil tares of heretics, and smoothing the saving path for the faithful, O father Nicholas."

"A flowing and cleansing fountain, washing away the defilement: we pray Thee, O Savior, wash away the filth and passions of all of us by his prayers."

"Delivering from afflictions and sorrows, casting down the enemy by thy mighty prayers: strengthen now our ailing thoughts against the assaults of passions, by thy prayers, O father Nicholas."

*Theotokion:*

"The mind cannot comprehend the birth which is beyond the mind, of thy marvelous childbearing, O Theotokos, Virgin Mother; therefore I pray thee: endow my mind with grace, that I may ever glorify thee."

# CANON TO THE APOSTLES
*Ode 4. The Heirmos:*

*"Thou hast placed toward us steadfast love, O Lord..."*

[f. 90rB] "Heralds of the Sun that knows no setting, the Apostles enlightened all by the words of cosmic knowledge, and drove away the darkness of godlessness."

"A sea of fierce sin holds me fast, O Word, and the surges of foolish thoughts trouble my humble soul; O Helmsman and Lord, save me by the prayers of Thy disciples."

"Pondering the terrible things of Thy dread coming, O Master: I have before the judgment my conscience within me convicting me, and before the torment tormenting mine insensibility."

*Theotokion:*

"O Word of God, Who wast born of the Virgin, the Maiden of God: by her sacred intercessions and those of Thy wise Apostles, O Savior, deliver Thy servants from every tribulation and every distress."

# CANON TO SAINT NICHOLAS
*Ode 4. The Heirmos:*

*"Habakkuk foresaw the overshadowed mountain, even thy pure womb, O pure one; therefore he cried: 'God shall come from the south, and the Holy One from the thick and shadowy mountain!' "*

"Every believer ever presents thee as an intercessor before God, O Nicholas; therefore we pray thee: deliver us from cruel temptations and sinful falls, O father."

"Having living water in thy heart, even the grace of the Lord: thou ever bedewest, O wise one, those who burn with the heat of sorrows and whose souls are consumed with sins, who are about to perish wretchedly, O all-blessed one."

"O thou who didst once deliver those led unto unjust death, O all-blessed one: now also save us from strange, soul-destroying condemnation," [f. 90vA] and from every demonic deception.

Thou hast ineffably given birth unto the incarnate Word, the plenitude of tender-compassion: pray Thou unto Him, O Most-pure One, that we be delivered from all carnal passions and defilements, and from all tribulations of this life.

Ode 5. Heirmos.

The Invisible One was seen upon earth, and being incomprehensible, He voluntarily lived among men; therefore, rising early at the dawn unto Thee, we praise Thee, O Lover of mankind.

Having become incarnate upon earth, Thou hast made Thy disciples as heavens declaring Thy glory; for their sake, therefore, O Lord, have mercy upon our souls.

From passions and from every constraint, from dire distress, O Word, deliver Thy servants through the acceptable intercessions of Thine Apostles.

Woe is me, O my all-passionate soul! How wilt thou appear before the dread judgment seat, being destitute of fruit? Hasten to repent, bringing forth the fruits of virtues.

Unto Him Who ineffably appeared upon earth in the flesh from Thy pure blood, O Pure One, pray Thou ever as unto Thine own Son, that He may grant us cleansing.

Another [Canon]. Heirmos.

With Thine unwaning light, O Christ, illumine, O God, my humble soul, and guide it into Thy path; for Thy commandments are light.

O father, illuminated by the pure throne and by the beams ever proceeding from the venerable [mysteries], entreat cleansing and mercy for all.

Unto me, who more than all men have provoked Thee to wrath with an unreasoning mind, O Most-good One, show tender mercy through the fervent prayers of Nicholas.[^126]

[f. 90vB] In slothfulness all my life hath been spent; by thy prayer, O father Nicholas, raise me up unto repentance, taking pity on my defilement. Theotokion:

As the singular joy of the Angels, O Lady full of divine grace, fill my soul with joy, which mourns and is submerged in indolence.

Ode 6. Heirmos.

The lowest depth of sins hath surrounded me:

O apostolic choir, thou unfailing abyss of spiritual wisdom, dry up the stream of the worldly wisdom of the nations, and water the assemblies of the pious.

Sigh and weep, O my humble soul, and cry aloud unto the Lord, saying: I have sinned against Thee; cleanse me, O Tender-hearted One, by the intercessions of Thine all-wise Apostles.

The torrents of passions have overflowed and submerged the tabernacle of my soul; O Apostles, being spiritual rivers, renew me who am crushed, restoring me unto life. Theotokion:

The assembly of the Apostles, O Christ, together with Her that bare Thee, entreats Thee: send down cleansing unto us, and peace unto Thy servants, as Thou art the Lover of mankind and God Who art easily reconciled.

Another [Canon]. Heirmos.

The depth of passions hath risen against me, and the tempest of contrary winds; but preventing me, save me, O Savior, and deliver me from corruption, as Thou didst save the Prophet from the beast.

Having mortified thy members through abstinence, thou hast acquired ageless life; make us also partakers thereof by thy prayers, O wise one, by fleeing from evil deeds.

[f. 91rA] By the sail of thy sacred prayers, draw us forth from the deep abyss of manifold temptations and from the gulf of sins; and guide us unto the haven of life, O wise hierarch.

Having adorned the throne of Myra in Lycia, thou hast appeared as the beauty of chief hierarchs; but by thy prayers, O Hierarch, preserve us unharmed from worldly misfortunes. Theotokion:

The Word took up His abode within Thy womb, O Pure Mother; He Who of old dwelt among men cast out corruption through transgression, as He alone is God, through the mercy of His tender-compassion.

Ode 7. Heirmos.

Of old the three children bowed not down before the golden image of Persian honor, singing in the midst of the furnace: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers.[^127]

Christ, Who is the Light of the world, hath shown forth the light-bearing Apostles as a second light, dispersing the darkness of deception and enlightening the minds of the faithful.

Break in pieces the snares of the enemy set against us, O sweet-voiced Apostles, and smooth for us the path of repentance, who flee unto you.

My soul, made barren through carnal passions, do ye cleanse, O divine heralds and Apostles of the Lord, being divine salt, reviving the faithful. Theotokion:

O beauty of Jacob, enlighten, I pray Thee, the eyes of my heart with goodly form; pray for me together with the Apostles unto Him Who was born of Thy pure blood.

[f. 91rB] Another [Canon]. Heirmos.

The three children in the furnace prefigured the Trinity; they trampled upon the threat of fire, and praising they sang: Blessed art Thou, O Lord, God of our fathers.

Arius, who of old raged against the Lord's people, thou hast strangled with the sinews of thy words, O father Nicholas, as a true prince of pastors.

Having holily passed thy venerable life, thou dwellest with the saints, O father Nicholas, sending down sanctification and enlightenment unto those who piously call thee blessed.

As a ready deliverer, as a fervent protector, we ever invoke thee, O father Nicholas: deliver us from passions and from unexpected temptations that come upon us. Theotokion:

Unto me who through negligence have darkened my soul, do Thou grant light, O Pure One, who hast given birth unto the Light, kindling the lamp of my heart, that with zeal I may praise Thee, O Good One.

Ode 8. Heirmos.

In the unsettled fire:

I have been wounded by the weapon of passions, and have pierced my heart with folly, acting wickedly against the Creator; O glorious Apostles, heal me entirely unharmed, being physicians of souls and bodies.

The divine proclamation of the preachers hath gone forth into all the earth, teaching orthodoxly concerning the singular Priesthood, and to honor the singular Essence of the Holy Trinity, and the one true Lordship, one Kingdom, unto ages of ages.

[f. 91vA] Turn me back, O Master, who have sinned much and have awaited Thy divine long-suffering in the persistence of transgressions, and let not my weakness, O Word, turn into negligence and scorn. Theotokion:

O divine tongs, who ineffably received the divine coal, O Mother of God: quench the burning coal of my passions, O Most-pure One, with the dew of Thy prayers, and of all the glorious and divine Apostles.

Another [Canon]. Heirmos.

Bless the Lord, Who is unceasingly glorified in the highest by the Angels: the heavens, the earth, the mountains, the hills, the deep, and all the race of mankind, with hymns bless Him as Creator and Maker.

Thou hast inherited the land of the meek, having become meek, O venerable one; therefore I pray thee faithfully: by thy prayers assuage the tempest of the crafty one that is ever stirred up against us.

Even as thou didst deliver the generals who were about to die unjustly, so deliver us from the affliction of wicked men, and from every demonic assault, O Nicholas, praying unto the Savior.

Thou hast shown unto men the upright and saving path; guide us thereon who traverse this life, O most-blessed Nicholas, through thy prayers, that together we may enter into the gates of life. Theotokion:

My strength and my song is He Who was born of Thee, O All-immaculate One; entreat Him earnestly, O Virgin, to strengthen me who am weakened by passions, [f. 91vB] to perform His saving commandments.

Ode 9. Heirmos.

In the shadow and letter of the Law, we the faithful perceive a figure: every male that opens the womb is holy unto God; therefore the Firstborn Word of the unoriginate Father, the Son Who is the firstborn of a Mother that knew not man, do we magnify.[^128]

O Word of the unoriginate Father, Who by the words of Thy disciples hast established the ends of the earth: through their supplications show mercy also unto me, who have slipped into irrational passions and have fallen into demonic delusions.

O my soul, enslaved to the impulses of passions, offer supplications unto Him Who suffered for our sake, that He may deliver thee from tribulations, when the glorious and sacred disciples pray, having in their flesh imitated His sufferings.

O disciples of Christ, when ye shall sit upon thrones to judge those guilty before the tribunal, keep my soul uncondemned, which is defiled by improper deeds, as my good advocates and intercessors for the world. Theotokion:

O Most-pure Virgin, pure palace of Christ, O Most-pure Virgin, who beyond cause and word gavest birth unto God, the Holy of Holies: pray for all together with the holy Apostles.

Another [Canon]. Heirmos.

Seen upon Mount Sinai:

As a divine bulwark and confirmation and pre-eminent excellence, the earthly world hath acquired thee; by thine intercessions, O father Nicholas, it is ever delivered from every temptation and distress; therefore in praise we faithfully call thee blessed.

[f. 92rA] Being weighed down by many tribulations, I flee unto the breadth of thy fervent prayers, O all-blessed hierarch; transform the afflictions of my soul, I cry unto thee, calm the waves of despair, and quiet the agitation of my mind.

The advent of the Creator is at hand to judge the whole earth; and being unprepared, wretch that I am, I am terrified, contemplating the multitude of mine evils. O Lord, Long-suffering One, show tender mercy and save me, through the divine prayers of Nicholas, Thy venerable servant.

O Thou who hast given birth unto the Light, cause saving enlightenment to dawn upon me, dispersing the many and dark clouds of my soul, that by Thy prayers I may become a child of the day, ever performing what is good, so that in hymns I may ever call Thee blessed.

At the Aposticha, Stichera

to the Apostles, Tone 3.

Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth, O holy Apostles; ye abolished the deception of idols, having proclaimed the knowledge of God; behold, this is your goodly contest, O blessed ones; therefore we sing and glorify your memory.[^129]

Having kept the commandments of Christ blamelessly, O holy Apostles, ye received from Him, and therefore ye distribute, healing the passions of our souls and bodies; therefore, having boldness, pray unto Him that He may have mercy upon our souls. Martyrion:

As luminaries ye shine in the world, and after death, O holy martyrs, having fought the good fight, having boldness, pray unto Christ that He may have mercy upon our souls.

[f. 92rB] Glory... Both now... Theotokion:

Without seed hast Thou conceived by the Holy Spirit; and glorifying Thee, we sing: Rejoice, O Most-pure Virgin.

ON THURSDAY

The Beatitudes, Tone 3.

The forefather Adam, who rejected Thy commandment, O Christ, didst Thou cast out of Paradise; but the thief, O Tender-hearted One, who confessed Thee upon the Cross, didst Thou lead therein, crying: Remember me, O Savior, in Thy Kingdom.

O Apostles, who with the rod of the Cross drew forth people ensnared by ignorance, and drove away the Hellenic deception from the earth: ye have truly become sincere deliverers unto the faithful; therefore ye are called blessed.

Having become mystical rays and luminaries of the Sun of righteousness, O glorious Apostles, ye drove away the darkness of impiety, and guided all people unto the light of the knowledge of God; therefore we honor you.

Having endured the burning of tortures, ye suffered and received the dew of grace, and as servants of Christ, O wise martyrs, ye ever piously heal human passions; therefore we faithfully honor you, O holy ones.

Glory...

Sacred preachers of the Trinity: Peter and Paul, Mark and Luke, Matthew, Simon, James, Andrew, John, Bartholomew, Philip, Thomas: earnestly pray ye ever that we may be delivered from every affliction.[^130]

Both now... Theotokion:

[f. 92vA] O beauty of the Apostles, and rejoicing of the holy passion-bearers, O Lady most full of divine grace, pray unto the Savior and God for us all, that we may receive forgiveness of sins, and all become partakers of divine life.

ON THURSDAY EVENING, AT "LORD, I HAVE CRIED"

*Stichera of the Cross, Tone 3.*

*Podoben: "They weighed thirty pieces of silver" (Поста́виша три́десѧте):*

O Lord, being passionless in Thy divine nature, Thou didst endure suffering according to Thy bodily nature, being nailed unto the Cross; and Thy lance-pierced side, immovably steadfast, poured forth two rivers for me in ineffable mysteries.[^131]

Crowned with an unwoven crown of thorns, the King of all was clad in a purple robe; not tearing the barrier of thorny sin, O Savior, but receiving Thy name with Thy hands, Thou hast written all of us who have believed in God in the heavenly book.

In no wise did the unjust envy of the Hebrews cease, neither against Thee Who wast crucified, O Guileless One, nor when Thou wast dead, O Christ; but even so they slandered Thee as a deceiver, and the cruel ones asked Pilate to guard Thy tomb, because of their incurable wrath.

Other Stichera to the Most-holy Theotokos.

Tone the same.

When She that bare Thee saw Thee, the unwaning Sun Who shone forth from Her womb, setting upon the Cross—Thee Who holdest the rays of the sun— [f. 92vB] She cried aloud with a soul pierced through with the darkness of sorrows: Voluntary setting, and dawning again, for my enlightenment and the world's!

O Lady, who gavest birth unto Him Who is to judge the living and the dead: quicken my soul which is deadened through illness by repentance, and by the divine Blood that flowed from the side of Thy Son, make me a doer of His commandments.

When I bare Thee without travail, O Child, said the Ewe-lamb and Mother, I escaped affliction and the mist of sorrows; but now, beholding Thee lifted up upon the Cross, O my Womb, my heart is encompassed by bitter arrows, and I am submerged in boundless sorrow, O Master.

Glory... Both now... Theotokion:

To Thy Christian people Thou hast given Him Who was born of Thee, as a great champion against darkness and a mighty refuge; for having no boldness toward Thee, O Christ, because of our many sins, we offer this prayer unto Thee through His Mother, and Thy most-pure sufferings.

[f. 93rA] At the Aposticha, Stichera

of the Cross, Tone 3.

We venerate Thy Cross, O Christ, the precious guardian of the world, the salvation of us sinners, the great cleansing, the victory of the Church, and the praise of the whole universe.

Moses upon the mountain, lifting up his hands toward the height in the figure of the Cross, overcame Amalek; and Thou, O Savior, stretching out Thy palms upon the precious Cross, embracing me, hast saved me from the bondage of the enemy, and hast given me the sign of life, to flee from the bow of those who oppose me; therefore, O Word, we venerate Thy precious Cross.[^132]

Great is the power of Thy Cross, O Lord: for it was planted in one place, and works throughout the world, and made Apostles out of fishermen, and martyrs out of the nations, that they may pray for our souls.

Glory... Both now... Staurotheotokion:

Beholding Thee, O my Christ, the All-good One, lifted up upon the tree, the All-immaculate One cried aloud, weeping maternally: O my most-beloved Son, how hath the lawless assembly lifted Thee up upon the Cross?

ON FRIDAY, AT MATINS

After the First Kathisma, Sessional Hymns

of the Cross, Tone 3.

The Cross was planted upon the earth, and reached unto the heavens, not as a tree attaining height, but because Thou Who wast upon it dost fill all things: glory be to Thee.[^133]

Thou Who didst deign to suffer the Cross and death: Thou didst endure in the midst of creation beneath the sun, when Thou wast pleased, [f. 93rB] O Savior, to crucify Thy flesh; then the sun hid its rays, and the thief beholding Thee upon the Cross cried out reverently: Remember me, O Lord, and was received into the heavenly mansions, O Lord.

Glory... Both now... Staurotheotokion:

The spotless Ewe-lamb of the Word, the incorrupt Virgin Mother, seeing Him Who sprouted from Her without travail suspended upon the Cross, weeping maternally, cried aloud: Woe is me, my Child! How dost Thou suffer voluntarily, wishing to deliver mankind from the dishonor of passions?

After the Second Kathisma, Sessional Hymns, Tone 3.

From the cypress, the pine, and the cedar, Thou didst ascend, O Lamb of God, that Thou mightest save those who venerate Thy voluntary crucifixion with the Cross; O Christ God, glory be to Thee.

At Thine unsearchable power and voluntary crucifixion, the angelic hosts marvelled, seeing how the Invisible One received wounds in the flesh, wishing to deliver mankind from corruption; therefore, as unto our Benefactor, we cry unto Thee: Glory to Thy tender-compassion, O Christ! Martyrion:

The noble endurance of your patience overcame the snares of the evil-originating enemy, O all-praised martyrs; therefore ye have been accounted worthy of eternal blessedness; but pray ye unto the Lord to save the flock of the people named after Christ, being witnesses of the truth.

Glory... Both now... Staurotheotokion:

Unto death with reproach, O Tender-hearted One, didst Thou voluntarily submit in Thy crucifixion; seeing which, She that bare Thee, O Christ [f. 93vA] was wounded, by whose prayers, for the sake of Thy Mother's tender-compassion, O only Most-good Lover of mankind, O Lord: show mercy and save the world, Thou Who takest away the sins of the world.

After the Third Kathisma, Sessional Hymns, Tone 3.

Thou didst endure the Cross, O Sinless One, as a vessel of the curse, through ineffable tender-compassion; and the first-formed man hast Thou delivered from the original curse; therefore we the faithful venerate Thy passions, glorifying Thy dispensation, O Savior, which Thou alone hast accomplished through the tender-compassion of Thy Mother: Thou hast saved Thine own creation.

Struck on the cheek for the sake of the human race, and not being angered, deliver our life from corruption, O Lord, and have mercy upon us, as the Lover of mankind.

Glory... Both now... Staurotheotokion:

Having acquired the Cross of Thy Son as a rod of power, O Mother of God, therewith we cast down the insolence of the enemy, who with love unceasingly magnify Thee.

CANON of the Precious and Life-giving Cross of the Lord.

Composition of Joseph.

Ode 1. Tone 3. Heirmos.

The sun once traversed the dry, deep-rooted earth; for the water solidified on both sides like a wall for the people traversing the deep on foot, and singing in a manner pleasing unto God: Let us sing unto the Lord, for He is gloriously glorified.[^134]

Thou didst congeal the sea waves with a rod, and didst divide them for the people, prefiguring Thy Cross, through which Thou hast swallowed the bitter water, and hast brought them unto the land [f. 93vB] of divine knowledge, O Tender-hearted One, saving all who sing with faith of Thy power.

Thou didst make the abyss by Thy command, covering the proud depths with waters, O Mighty One; Who didst hang the earth upon the waters: hanging upon the tree, Thou dost shake all creation by Thy nod, and dost establish the souls of all in Thy fear. Martyrion:

Ye have become partakers of the Son, O divine martyrs of Christ, and citizens and heirs of the Sion on high; wherein also wearing crowns, ye cry aloud with brightness: Let us sing unto the Lord, for He is gloriously glorified! Martyrion:

Ye gave your hands and feet to be cut off, O martyrs, being cruelly scraped; and mingling with the fire, ye in no wise denied Christ, the God of all, but fervently cried aloud: Let us sing unto the Lord, for He is gloriously glorified! Theotokion:

O prefigured Virgin, Gate of salvation, seeing Thy Son voluntarily lifted up upon the wood of the Cross, weeping Thou didst cry aloud: O Tender-hearted Lord of glory, how dost Thou suffer these things, O Master?

Another Canon to the Most-holy Theotokos.

Tone 3. Heirmos.

He Who of old by His nod:

Grant me cleansing of transgressions by Thy divine supplications, O Virgin; for Thou hast mighty prayer, O Most-pure One; and being a disciple of Thy prayers, deliver me from sins, from passions, from tribulations, and from distresses.

With the waters of Thy prayers, O Virgin, refresh my soul in compunction, melted by the drought of my measureless [f. 94rA] sins and passions, that having attained divine refreshment, we may magnify Thee in hymns as our fervent protector.

Being entirely submerged in sins, and having no one, wretch that I am: do Thou, O Pure Lady, stretching forth the hand of Thy tender-compassion, swiftly draw me unto repentance, granting me a fountain of tears.

Tear asunder, O Most-pure One, the handwriting of my sins through Thy prayers, as Thou hast boldness toward Thine own Son to pray earnestly for us; for Thee alone do we Christians have as our protectress.

Ode 3. Heirmos.

Establish, O Lord, upon Thyself Who art the foundation, Thy Church which Thou hast acquired by Thy precious Blood.

Bearing a single compound hypostasis, O Word, Thou didst endure the most dishonorable crucifixion, preparing incorruptible honor for those who honor Thee.

Earthborn mortals have been released from the curse, when Thou, O Master, becamest a curse, pouring forth blessing through the Cross. Martyrion:

Having become sojourners in all the earth, ye have truly appeared as citizens of heaven, O all-praised ones, singular companions of Christ. Martyrion:

Having acquired the Cross as a most mighty weapon, the martyrs completely conquered all the power of the destroying enemy. Theotokion:

He preserved Thee as a Virgin even after childbirth, O Pure One, having given birth unto the incarnate God, Who was nailed upon the Cross of His own will.

[f. 94rB] Another [Canon]. Heirmos.

He Who brought all things from non-being:

Open unto me swiftly, I pray Thee, the treasury of Thy tender-compassion, O Most-pure Mother of God, and appear unto me as a fervent helper in temptations, and as salvation.

Deliver me from every surrounding cruel storm of sin, O Most-pure One, Thy servant; and guide me unto the saving haven by Thy prayers.

Restrain, O Pure Virgin Mother, the turbid floods of my passions that assault my humble soul and grieve it.

Grant me a stream of tears, O Good One, and therewith quench the furnace of my passions, and wash me clean from all spiritual defilement, O Mother of God.

Ode 4. Heirmos.

Thy virtue, O Christ, hath covered the heavens; for proceeding from the Ark of Thy sanctification, Thine incorrupt Mother, Thou didst appear in the temple of Thy glory as an infant borne in arms, and all things were filled with Thy praise.[^135]

Thou Who alone didst raise up the fall of Adam, O Christ, being the new Adam, didst nail Thy hands unto the Cross, and being struck on the cheek of Thine own will, Thou didst taste vinegar and gall, being exalted by the height of Thy kingdom.

As a sheep led to the slaughter did the Prophet foresee Thee, and as a Lamb, O Word of God, not resisting at all, nor crying aloud, Thou didst endure to be crucified of Thine own will, that Thou mightest deliver and save those who have sinned voluntarily, O Merciful Lord. Martyrion:

[f. 94vA] Having renewed their souls with the plow of faith, the martyrs of Christ sowed the seed of patient endurance of tortures, and reaped the abundant ear of martyrdom, nourishing the assemblies of the faithful; therefore ye are ever glorified.

From the abyssal oppression of cruel unbelievers, through the expectation of good things, the holy martyrs attained unto the expanse of the kingdom on high, that our mouths might be enlarged unceasingly to hymn their struggle.

Having received the divine coal, as with tongs, which was in no wise burning, but rather dewing, O Virgin Mother, within Thy divine womb, seeing Him voluntarily suspended in the flesh upon the tree, we glorify Him in hymns.

Another [Canon]. Heirmos.

Thou hast placed toward us:

All my hope have I placed upon Thee, O Mother of God; falling down before Thee, my soul prays: deliver me from deadly diseases, raising me up unto the life of salvation, O Thou who gavest birth unto Life.

O Pure Lady, mighty helper of the world, cast me not away from Thy presence, nor send me away ashamed from Thy countenance, nor show me as a mockery unto the ages.

Entirely naked have I become, wretch that I am, of divine deeds, and I have been wounded by the sharp arrows of pleasures, and covered with sores; therefore I cry unto Thee, O Lady: save me, O Most-pure One.

The waters of improper deeds have come, O Pure One, unto my wretched soul, and holding it fast with earthly thoughts, [f. 94vB] I cry unto Thee with pain: despise not Thy servant, O Lady.

Ode 5. Heirmos.

When Isaiah saw God symbolically upon a throne high and lifted up, escorted by the Angels of glory, he cried: Woe is me, wretched one! For I have foreseen God becoming incarnate, possessing unwaning light and peace.[^136]

Thou didst give me rest, O Word, who was overburdened by the labor of transgressions, having rested upon the tree, O Master; and Thou didst take away my reproach, whereby Thou didst suffer reproaches, O Christ; I hymn Thy dominion and divine sufferings.

Having kindled Thy flesh upon the Cross as a lamp, Thou didst seek the lost coin, O Lover of mankind; and Thou dost summon all the spiritual powers to the finding; being overcome by slothfulness, beneath the feet of the impious passion-bearers of Christ, the enemy is seen dead and inactive; while they themselves are numbered with the heavenly Angels, filled with ineffable joy. Martyrion:

The holy ones, being frozen by cruel tortures, afflictions, and wounds through unjust condemnation, passed over unto the divine warmth of the heavenly kingdom; and they ever appear as advocates of hymns for the faithful. Theotokion:

Beholding Thee crucified upon the tree, and Thy side pierced with a lance—Thee Who of old formed Eve from a rib—the Most-pure Virgin cried maternally: How dost Thou die, O my Son, [f. 95rA] my immortal Life?

Another [Canon]. Heirmos the same.

O divine vine, that budded forth the fair cluster, and gavest unto souls to drink of the divine drink, O Virgin: from bitter drunkenness and the intoxication of passions and pleasures deliver my soul, and from eternal fire.

Root out the nest of my sins, O Most-pure Bride of God, who have fallen into the mire of passions; and cleanse me by Thy prayers, washing me clean from the defilements of passions, clothing me in the radiant robe of salvation.

O Thou who gavest peace and salvation unto all the world, having given birth unto the divine Peace, O Virgin: appease the present warfare of passions of my soul and body, O Pure One.

In fear and love of the Savior Christ, heal my soul that is struck with sins, O Most-pure One, by Thy tender-compassion; and grant me, guiding me, ever to perform in humility the commandments of Thy Son, that I may receive His grace.

Ode 6. Heirmos.

The elder, having seen salvation with his eyes, which came unto the people from God, cried aloud unto Thee: O Christ, Thou art my God!

Voluntarily wast Thou slaughtered as a Lamb, O Christ, raising up again unto life him who had died through the eating of the tree.

Having been lifted up upon the Cross, the demonic deception fell down; and the multitude of the faithful was exalted, singing of Thee, O Giver of life.

Washed in the purple dye of their own blood, the martyrs now stand before the King of all, [f. 95rB] adorned with radiant crowns. Martyrion:

The relics of the precious martyrs pour forth healing unto all who have recourse unto them, and drown the multitude of passions. Theotokion:

The human mind cannot comprehend, O Maiden, the mystery of Thy birth-giving which is beyond nature; for beyond understanding hast Thou given birth unto God.

Another [Canon]. Heirmos.

The lowest depth of sins:

Grant forgiveness of transgressions, as Thou art good, unto Thy servant, O Most-pure One, who with faith asks for Thy protection; and snatch me from the future judgment.

O Good One and Mother of the Deliverer, stand Thou by me at the hour of my departure, when I am examined by the spirits of the air concerning what I have committed with an unreasoning mind.

Wretched have I become within myself, ever encompassed with uncleannesses; and now beholding death standing before my feet, I cry aloud unto Thee, O Mother of God: help me!

The waves of passionate thoughts ever agitate me, O Most-pure One, and the crafty spirits barely keep from drowning me; but establish me upon the rock of passionlessness.

Ode 7. Heirmos.

We hymn God the Word, praising Him piously: Who in the fire bedewed the Hebrew children, and took up His abode in the incorrupt Virgin: Blessed art Thou, O Lord, God of our fathers.[^137]

Thou didst ascend upon the cedar, the pine, and the cypress, O Blessed One, Who art One of the Trinity; and Thou hast exalted those who had fallen into the depth of many pleasures: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

[f. 95vA] With Thy precious Blood, O Lord, Thou didst cleanse creation from the blood offered unto abominable demons; and Thou didst destroy defiled sacrifices, O Word of God, being sacrificed as a guileless Lamb: glory to Thy dominion! Martyrion:

Standing before the torturers as immovable pillars, the sufferers shook deception and established the hearts of the faithful, singing: Blessed art Thou, O Lord, God of our fathers! Martyrion:

Ye were not consumed by the fire, having acquired a resolve more fervent than fire, O victorious passion-bearers of Christ, crying: Blessed art Thou, O Lord, God of our fathers! Theotokion:

Thou alone didst have an ineffable conception, O Pure One, and an unutterable birth-giving, having given birth unto the incarnate God Who was crucified in the flesh; singing unto Whom, we cry: Blessed art Thou, O Lord, God of our fathers!

Another [Canon]. Heirmos: As of old:

Praying unto Thee, the pure and immaculate Mother of God, defiled in body and soul, and wretched with unclean deeds: I place my hope in Thy mercy, O Lady; do Thou have tender-compassion on me, O Most-pure One.

The multitude of my transgressions and the fullness of evils fill me with great perplexity, and drag me down into the depth of despair. O Most-pure Lady, save me who am perishing and cruelly submerged.

Have mercy, O Good One, on my soul that is humbled by evil deeds; [f. 95vB] and guide me unto the path of repentance, and direct me to do the will of Thy Son, and deliver me from torment.

O Good One, overlook the multitude of our sins through the multitude of the compassions of Thy goodness; and be Thou easily reconciled unto those who unceasingly cry: Blessed, O Most-pure One, is the fruit of Thy womb!

Ode 8. Heirmos.

In the unsettled fire:

The disobedient and unreasoning people condemned Thee to die, Who wast pleased to be crucified on the place of the skull of Thine own compliant will, that by Thy will Thou mightest quicken those who were mortified, O Word, who sing of Thee and exalt Thee unto the ages.

Stretching out Thy palms upon the Cross, Thou didst heal, O Master, the hands of the first-formed man unrestrainedly stretched forth unto the tree of eating. And seeing Thee with fear, the sun hid its rays, and all creation was shaken. Martyrion:

Having dried up the roots of impiety with sacred healing, the passion-bearers poured forth fountains of healings, washing away the defilements of passions, and richly watering the hearts of the faithful. Martyrion:

O passion-bearers, fellow citizens with the Bodiless Hosts, having accomplished the precious sufferings and fulfilled the divine commandments: pray ye unto God that those who honor you may be written in the city on high unto ages of ages.

The golden urn, the table of the priest, the rod, the divine mountain, [f. 96rA] the cloud, the royal palace, and the fiery throne do all we the faithful call Thee, O Mother of God, who remained a Virgin after childbirth.

Another [Canon]. Heirmos.

Unto Him Who descended into the flame unto the Hebrew children by divine power, and appeared unto them: all ye men, worship the Lord; ye priests, sing and exalt Him unto the ages.

The bitterness of pleasures, having passed through all my bodily senses, immeasurably defiles my soul and drags it into death; O Lady of the world, be Thou my salvation.

I have committed both soul and body and heart unto Thee, for I have no other hope save Thee, O Lady, through whom I shall obtain mercy; therefore grant me Thy rich grace.

The serpent crawled near me with venom, and through carnal pleasure cruelly killed my wretched soul; but revive it with contrary remedies, O Pure One, through Thy prayers.

The cruel night of transgressions covers me, O Pure Lady, for I have no lamp of good deeds enlightening my soul; therefore I have been deprived of the unwaning light on high.

Ode 9. Heirmos.

In the shadow and letter of the Law:

Thou wast nailed upon the Cross, O Jesus, Who didst establish the whole earth upon nothing, and didst deliver me from the corruption of sin, who was held fast by evil darkness; as Thou art good, show tender mercy and deliver me, O Christ; and by Thy dishonorable death Thou hast honored me, O Plenteous in mercy.

[f. 96rB] God, invisible by nature, appeared crucified in the flesh, that Thou mightest deliver the visible world from the invisible enemy; and having descended below, O Christ, Thou madest the heavenly ones fellow worshippers of the dominion of Thy great power. Martyrion:

The sacred army of the saints, the chosen holy host, having the Tree of life, Christ, in their midst, O Lord: the Church of divine beauty, the venerable assembly, the all-glorious passion-bearers of the Savior, have appeared. Martyrion:

Remember us who remember you upon earth, O holy ones, standing joyfully before the throne of the Master, richly illuminated with sacred beams from His radiance, that we may receive release from our debts. Theotokion:

Seeing Thy crucifixion, O my Son, the two luminaries went down; and how did the faithless Hebrew assembly not sink into darkness, having betrayed Thee unto death, the Prince of life? cried the Mother of God, whom we unceasingly magnify.[^138]

Another [Canon]. Heirmos.

Thee, the unburnt Bush, and holy Virgin, Mother of the Light, and Mother of God, the hope of us all, do we magnify.

Having cleansed the defilement of passionate thoughts from my mind, O Pure One, clothe me in the radiant garment of passionlessness.

Open unto me the divine entrances of repentance, O Virgin, blocking the incursions of my passions and pleasures, and restoring me by Thy power.

Hear the voice of my groaning, and the voice of my weeping, O All-immaculate Virgin, and grant cleansing [f. 96vA] and salvation unto my wretched soul.

Entirely in despair am I, wretched one, and in perplexity, contemplating my evil deeds; therefore show tender mercy, O Lady, and save me.

At the Aposticha, Stichera

of the Cross, Tone 3.

The tree of disobedience budded forth death for the world; but the tree of the Cross sprouted life and incorruption; therefore we pray unto Thee, the crucified Lord: let the light of Thy countenance be signed upon us.

As food for oblivion was I, Adam, having fallen by a cruel fall; but Thou didst not despise me, O Master; taking pity on me, Thou wast crucified for my sake, and Thou savest me and bringest me unto glory: O my Deliverer, glory be to Thee! Martyrion:

Come, all ye people, let us honor the memory of the holy passion-bearers; for they became a spectacle unto Angels and men, received crowns of victory from Christ, and pray for our souls.

Glory... Both now... Staurotheotokion:

Seeing Him Who was born of Thee, O All-immaculate One, suspended upon the tree, Thou didst cry aloud, weeping: O my sweet Child, whither hath Thy light-bearing beauty departed, Who didst work good for the human race?

ON FRIDAY

The Beatitudes, Tone 3.

The forefather Adam, who rejected Thy commandment, O Christ, didst Thou cast out of Paradise; but the thief, O Tender-hearted One, who confessed Thee upon the Cross, didst Thou lead therein, crying: Remember [f. 96vB] me, O Savior, in Thy Kingdom.

Beholding Thee upon the Cross, the unwaning Sun, the sun of light was darkened; the rocks were rent, and all the earth was shaken; the veil of the Temple was torn in twain in the midst, seeing Thee suffering unjustly, O Savior, Incomprehensible to all.

Thou wast led unto death as a sheep, O Jesus, the Life of the living, that by Thy divine sufferings Thou mightest save as God those who had been mortified by the ancient eating; and Thou showest them as citizens of the Lord; therefore with faith we glorify Thy passions.

Having voluntarily suffered for our sake, and taken upon Himself the reproach of men: O martyrs who imitated His passions, through many tortures ye cast down the enemy, and obtained the glory on high; therefore ye are divinely glorified. Glory...

Unto the Father, and the Son, and the All-holy, true, and upright Spirit: let all we the faithful bow down, praising the one Principle and divine glory, crying with pious and orthodox understanding: Remember us in Thy Kingdom. Both now...

Seeing Her Son voluntarily enduring passions in the flesh upon the Cross, the All-immaculate One was troubled in all Her being, and weeping, the Pure One cried aloud: Woe is me, my Child! How art Thou put to death, Who wishest to quicken those who died cruelly?

[f. 97rA] ON FRIDAY EVENING, AT "LORD, I HAVE CRIED"

Stichera to the Holy Martyrs, Hierarchs, and Venerable Monastics.

*Tone 3.*

*Podoben: "Great is the power of Thy martyrs" (Веліа му́никъ твоихъ):*

Suffering bravely, O noble martyrs, and having endured wounds and bonds and diverse tortures, ye have been led unto the painless and blessed inheritance, according to the measure of your sufferings.[^139]

Having wisely uttered the word of piety and divinity, O Hierarchs of the Lord, ye destroyed all the contradictions of heretics; and ye appeared as chief hierarchs unto all the faithful; therefore ye are honored.

Ye imitated the immaterial and bodiless ones, O God-bearing ascetics, having shown forth a glorious life in the material body; therefore ye dwell in celestial mansions.

Other Stichera of the Martyrs.

*Podoben: "The same Tone and Podoben" (Гла́съ и҆ подо́бенъ то́йже):*

Great is the power of Thy Cross, O Lord: for the Cross was planted for us, and works in the world, and made Apostles out of fishermen, and martyrs out of the nations, that they may pray for our souls.

Great is the power of Thy martyrs, O Christ: for lying in the tombs, they drive away evil spirits, and have abolished the power of the enemy, through faith in the Trinity, having contended for piety.

[f. 97rB] Prophets, Apostles of Christ, and martyrs: ye taught how to praise the consubstantial Trinity, and enlightened the deceived nations, and made the sons of men partakers with the Angels.

Glory... Both now... Theotokion:

Unto Him Who is invisible...

At the Aposticha, Stichera,

Tone 3. Of the Martyrs.

The martyrs of the Lord, established in faith and strengthened in hope, united in soul through the love of Thy Cross, destroyed the tyranny of the enemy; and having obtained crowns, they pray with the Bodiless Hosts for our souls.

For the Departed.

All human existence, howsoever much it may be, passes away after death: riches remain not, nor doth glory descend; for when death comes, it destroys all these things; therefore unto Christ the Immortal let us cry: Unto those translated from among us, grant rest, where the dwelling of all who rejoice is found, O Consolation![^140]

O mortals, why do we trouble ourselves in vain? The path on which we run is brief; life is smoke, vapor, earth, and ash; for a little while it appears, and quickly perishes; therefore [f. 97vA] unto Christ the Immortal let us cry: Unto those translated from among us, grant rest, where the dwelling of all who rejoice is found, O Consolation!

Glory... Both now... Theotokion:

Holy Mother of God among women, unwedded Mother: pray Thou unto Him Whom Thou didst bear, our King and God, that He may save us, as the Lover of mankind.

ON SATURDAY, AT MATINS

After the First Kathisma, Sessional Hymns

of the Martyrs, Tone 3.

The noble endurance of your patience overcame the snares of the evil-originating enemy, O all-praised passion-bearers; therefore ye have been accounted worthy of eternal blessedness; but pray ye unto the Lord to save the flock of the people named after Christ, being true martyrs.[^141]

Ye shine with faith, O holy ones, most radiant luminaries, physicians of piety, all-praised passion-bearers; for ye feared not the wounds of the torturers, and cast down the impiety of idols, having the true Cross as an invincible victory.

Glory... Both now... Theotokion:

As the advocate of the salvation of our race, we hymn Thee, O Virgin Mother of God; for Thy Son and our God, having taken flesh from Thee, and received the suffering of the Cross, hath delivered us from corruption, as the Lover of mankind.

After the Second Kathisma, Sessional Hymns

of the Martyrs, Tone 3.

Having armed yourselves strongly with the weapon of Christ, and clad yourselves in the armor of faith, ye cast down the hosts of the enemy, O sufferers; [f. 97vB] for fervently, through the hope of life, ye endured all the threats and wounds of the torturers; therefore ye also received crowns, O long-suffering martyrs of Christ.

O holy passion-bearers, pray unto the merciful God, that He may grant remission of sins unto our souls.

For the Departed.

When we shall stand before Thy word, at Thy free judgment seat, O Lord: put not to shame those who have believed in Thee, O our Savior; for we all have sinned, yet we have not departed from Thee; therefore we pray Thee: in the bosoms of Thy righteous ones, O Christ, whom Thou hast received, give rest, for Thou alone art sinless.

Glory... Both now... Theotokion:

The Prophets proclaimed, the Apostles taught, the Martyrs confessed, and we have believed, that Thou art truly the Mother of God; therefore we magnify Thy birth-giving, O Most-pure One.

CANON to the Holy Martyrs, Hierarchs, Venerable Monastics, and the Departed.

Composition of Joseph.

Ode 1. Tone 3. Heirmos.

Thou art God Who art manifest in glory, working wonders: Who didst dry up the abyss, and didst drown the weapons, and didst save the people who sing unto Thee as the Deliverer, our God.[^142]

All ye sufferers, O all-wise ones, have found the glory of martyrdom; bravely did ye endure manifold tortures, O passion-bearers; therefore ye are ever glorified.

[f. 98rA] Possessing the life on high, ye appeared as divine servants, O all-wise sacred mystics of the incarnate Word, having pastured the Lord's flock well through divine power.

Having crucified yourselves unto the world in the flesh, O venerable ones, ye cast away all pleasures; and having appeared as vessels of the Spirit, ye destroyed the deceitful spirits together through divine power.

*Hymn for the Departed (Поко́инъ):*
