Those who have been translated from the earth by Thy command, O Lord, in pious faith, O Tender-hearted One: account worthy of endless life and unwaning light, and grant them rest, as Thou art good.

As having given birth unto God in the flesh, O Most-pure One, we piously honor Thee unceasingly with righteous disposition, together with the venerable women who shone forth in fasting, and by their sufferings cast down the enemy.

Another Canon to the Departed.

Composition of Theophanes.

Tone 3. Heirmos.

Unto the sea divided with a rod: and cast down the tyranny of Hades; having ascended unto the heavens, O Most-pure One, Thou didst raise up the choir of passion-bearers with Thyself; and now give rest unto the souls of those translated unto Thee, O Christ.[^143]

O Thou Who dost strengthen the divine martyrs, and by them didst overthrow deception: through their supplications, as God, deign that those who have finished their course in Thee, O Savior, may obtain immortality and the blessed inheritance.

For the sake of Thy servants, O Master, Thou didst pour forth Thine own Blood, being slaughtered as a compassionate One, and didst pay the debt for them; [f. 98rB] therefore, O Merciful One, we pray Thee: give rest unto Thy servants who have been translated unto Thee. For the Departed.

Purely let us hymn the Mother of God, who bare God: Who by His death overthrew our death, and poured forth ageless life, and blessedness enduring unto the ages.

Ode 3. Heirmos.

O barren and childless soul, acquire fruit from God, and rejoicing cry aloud: I am established through Thee, O God; there is none holy, and none righteous, save Thee, O Lord.

Strengthened by the power of God, O glorious martyrs, ye completely destroyed the ruinous power of the enemy who was mighty in wickedness, and received divine crowns of victory.

Thou hast shown forth the venerable ones, O Master, as conquerors of the enemy; and with the most-holy anointing of hierarchs, O Christ, through their supplications, enlighten those who sing of Thee.

Together with all the Prophets, let us praise the divine choir of women who shone forth in fasting, and suffered through faith, and trampled upon the manifold-wiled serpent. For the Departed:

Those whom Thou hast translated from among us, O God, according to Thy natural will, O Christ: number with the saints, overlooking their transgressions in this life, O Tender-hearted One, through the prayers of Thy saints.

Having been saved, O Most-pure One, by Thy venerable birth-giving, with eloquent voice we faithfully cry unto Thee: Rejoice! And we pray: through Thy prayers entreat forgiveness of transgressions for us all.

[f. 98vA] Another [Canon]. Heirmos.

He Who brought all things from non-being:

Thou Who didst create me from the earth, and when I, wretched one, was returned unto the earth, didst renew me by Thy Cross: give rest unto the souls of the departed, through the prayers of the martyrs.

Being entreated by the divine wounds, afflictions, and tortures of the passion-bearing martyrs: number the souls of Thy servants in the dwellings of the saints, O Tender-hearted One.

Deliver Thy servants, O Lover of mankind, from the fire of Gehenna and from the dark dwellings of Hades, who have fallen asleep in Thee, O Good One, in hope of Thee, O Most-venerable One, as Mother of the Creator of creation, Who hast destroyed death, O All-honored Mother of God, and granted us incorruption.

Ode 4. Heirmos.

Foreseeing the overshadowed mountain, even Thy pure womb, O pure one, Habakkuk cried aloud: God shall come from the south, and the Holy One from the thick and shadowy mountain.[^144]

Like sheep were ye all brought, being slaughtered as lambs, O wise sufferers, unto the Lamb, the Word of God, Who deigned to be slaughtered upon the tree of the Cross for the human race.

Together with the venerable ones we honor the glorious chief hierarchs, who became luminaries unto the faithful, who abolished heresies and the deep darkness of passions, and through faith drew men unto the unwaning Light.

With the beauty of words, the divinely-speaking Prophets enlighten the souls of the faithful; [f. 98vB] and with the brightness of their contests and the outpourings of miracles, the God-bearing women illuminate our hearts. For the Departed:

Make those who have left this life partakers of celestial glory, O Word of God, granting them deliverance from transgressions, O Good One, which they committed upon earth, in knowledge and in ignorance.

As the divine ornament of martyrs, the steadfast confirmation of the venerable, and the proclamation of the Prophets, let us hymn the all-praised Mother of the Lord.

Another [Canon]. Heirmos.

Thou hast placed toward us steadfast love:

Thou didst mercifully take up Thine abode in the tomb for our sake, O Master; Thou didst empty the graves, as God; and having shown the martyrs as trophy-bearers, number Thy departed servants in the place of refreshment.

Thou Who didst joyfully accept the mighty contests, wounds, and swift cuttings of the limbs of the sufferers which they endured for Thy sake, O Master: deliver from torment those whom Thou hast received.

Thou Who by Thy nod holdest the keys of life: account worthy of Thine endless life and incorruptible glory those whom Thou hast now translated, breaking down the middle wall of sin. Theotokion:

Truly hast Thou appeared as Mother and Virgin, O All-immaculate One, having uniquely united an incorrupt conception and birth-giving in virginity; for Thou gavest birth unto God, Who destroyed the power of death.

Ode 5. Heirmos.

Light [f. 99rA] With Thine unwaning light, O Christ, illumine, O God, my humble soul, and guide it in Thy fear, for Thy commandments are light.

Your wounds and bruises appeared unto the enemy as incurable wounds; and now do ye, O sufferers of the Lord, heal the wounds of all the faithful.

Let us hymn the multitude of the venerable, and call blessed the hierarchs of Christ, and honor His Prophets, who ever pray for us.

Loving God Who became incarnate for our sake, the glorious women suffered with an upright disposition, and having contested, they now abide in the heavens. For the Departed:

In the delight of Paradise, in the land of the living, O Christ, where Thy light shines: settle Thy faithful servants whom Thou hast translated from the earth.

The Father's Word became incarnate from Thee, O Most-pure One, and showed Thee forth as higher than the Angels, surpassing all creatures; therefore we hymn Thee.

Another [Canon]. Heirmos: Rising early at the dawn unto Thee:

In the Church of the firstborn, O Blessed One, number those who have passed away from among us with the righteous, for the sake of the martyrs and by the supplications of the sufferers.

For the deliverance of many transgressions, O Christ, Thou didst pour forth Thy most-holy Blood; and now, through the supplications of Thy martyrs, O Savior, give rest unto those who have piously fallen asleep.

Direct, O Word, the souls of the departed unto the eternal place of Thy delight, which is beyond understanding; and account them worthy of the divine brightness of the saints.

Thee, O Virgin, who beyond word didst conceive in Thy womb the uncontainable Word, [f. 99rB] Who gives life unto the dead, do we worthily call blessed.

Ode 6. Heirmos.

The depth of passions hath risen against me, and the tempest of contrary winds; but preventing me, save me, O Savior, and deliver me from corruption, as Thou didst save the Prophet from the beast.

O luminaries of the dread divine manifestation, lambs of the Lamb and most-sacred Pastor, all-glorious sufferers of Christ: let them be honored with sacred hymns.

The assembly of the venerable was exalted, having exalted God in humility; and the multitude of chief hierarchs was glorified, having glorified the holy Trinity in good works.

By the judgment of divine commands, and by perfect endurance of suffering, the sacred choir of women overcame the lawless enemy, having contested valiantly. For the Departed:

Number those who have been translated from the earth in faith with the assemblies of the righteous, and establish them in the bosom of faithful Abraham, O Christ, ever to glorify Thy great tender-compassion. Theotokion:

Thou art the praise of martyrs, Prophets, and venerable ones, and of all the righteous from of old, O Most-pure One; therefore with joyful voices we honor Thee and glorify Thee.

Another [Canon]. Heirmos.

Raise me up from corruption, O Lord my God, Jonah cried aloud; and I cry unto Thee: deliver me from the depth of my many evils, O Savior, and direct and guide me unto the light of Thy commandments.

Turn the weeping of those who have fallen asleep in faith into joy, O Christ, through the prayers of the passion-bearers, [f. 99vA] with divinely-befitting gladness, O Christ, as the blessed God Who didst strengthen them, guiding and directing them unto Thy light.

By the multitude of Thy compassions, O God, give rest unto the departed in the bosom of the Patriarchs, where the radiant light of Thy countenance shines, O Christ, overlooking all their transgressions.

Pour forth, O Christ, upon those who have departed from among us and been delivered from the cruelties of this life, the marvelous mercy of Thy love for mankind, and satisfy them with Thy joy and meekness. Theotokion:

From deadness, corruption, and death have we been delivered through Thy glorious birth-giving, O Mother of God; for Thou, O Pure One, gavest birth unto the Fountain of incorruption, and hast enlightened the whole world with Thy light.

Ode 7. Heirmos.

The three children in the furnace prefigured the Trinity; they trampled upon the threat of fire, and singing they cried: Blessed art Thou, O Lord, God of our fathers.[^145]

Standing in the midst of the fire, O all-glorious passion-bearers, ye received divine dew; and having mortified the manifold-wiled enemy by your tortures, ye made him dead.

The divine hierarchs, having steered the Church of Christ as a ship, preserved her un-submerged, having truly escaped the evil waves of deception.

Having mortified the flesh through sacred ascetical labors, O true fasters, ye inherited ageless life and passionlessness, together with the holy Prophets and sacred women.

[f. 99vB] For the Departed.

Show not Thy faithful servants guilty who hoped in Thee, whom Thou hast translated; but give them rest, O Word, in the brightness of Thy saints, to sing of Thy tender-compassion. Theotokion:

Unto the martyrs, venerable ones, and Prophets, O All-immaculate One, and holy women, and all chief hierarchs who lived holily: Thou art truly the glory; therefore with them we honor Thee.

Another [Canon]. Heirmos: As of old:

O Word of God, Who art the life-originating Cause and creating Power of all: account the souls of Thy departed servants worthy of the delight of the most-sacred disciples, O God of our fathers.

The glorious martyrs of Christ bravely disregarded their bodies as corruptible; and now with boldness they pray unto Thee: give rest unto the souls of Thy departed servants, O God of our fathers.

With the rod of the Cross Thou didst write forgiveness of sins for all the faithful; account the souls whom Thou hast now translated unto Thee worthy to partake thereof, and to sing of Thee in gladness, O God of our fathers.

Glory...

O Word of the Father, Who of Thine own will dost accomplish all things: as God Thou didst renew human nature which was buried in passions; blessed, O Most-pure One, is the fruit of Thy womb!

Ode 8. Heirmos.

Bless the Lord, Who is unceasingly glorified in the highest by the Angels: the heavens, the earth, the mountains, the hills, the deep, [f. 100rA] and all that is manifest, and all the race of mankind, with hymns bless Him as Creator and Deliverer.

Inflicted with wounds and subjected to diseases, being exceedingly afflicted, ye did not deny the true Life, O passion-bearers of the Lord, nor did ye offer deceitful honor unto idols.

As lamps set upon candlesticks of venerable virtues, ye enlighten all men, O sacred passion-bearers, fellow citizens with the heavenly minds.

Let us worthily hymn the praiseworthy Prophets, and the theological discourse of the venerable, and the praiseworthy multitude of all beneficent women, who pray for us unto the Savior and God.

*Hymn for the Departed (Поко́инъ):*

O Thou Who mystically rulest over the living: number those faithful whom Thou hast translated from the earth with the saints in the light of Thy countenance, granting forgiveness of transgressions for the sake of Thy great tender-compassion, O Savior.

Theotokion:

Let the much-hymned Virgin, the proclamation of the Prophets, the ornament of hierarchs, sufferers, and venerable ones, and the joy of holy women, be sung unto the ages.

Another [Canon]. Heirmos.

The children in Babylon, having endured to serve the living God, disregarded the musical instruments; and standing in the midst of the flame, singing a hymn of divine beauty, they said: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, sing and exalt Him:

Thou Thyself art the Treasure of immortality, O Prince of life; Thou didst cause incorruption to bud forth for the dead, which [f. 100rB] Thou didst grant unto Thy disciples, O Christ, who piously sing unto Thee: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, sing and exalt Him unto the ages.

Through spiritual wisdom and patient endurance of works, the strong sufferers disregarded tortures; they ask refreshment from Christ for the souls that have been translated, crying: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, sing and exalt Him unto the ages.

Cleanse, O Good One, through the lance of Thy side, tearing up the handwriting of those translated unto Thee, and the partition-wall of their transgressions; deign that they may softly hymn Thee, O Savior: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, sing and exalt Him unto the ages.

Theotokion:

Thou hast appeared as a mystical cloud, O pure Virgin, unto those who are parched with the thirst of mortification, pouring forth living water of forgiveness and immortality for the dead, unto all who sing with faith, crying: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, sing and exalt Him unto the ages.

Ode 9. Heirmos.

Moses saw Thee upon Mount Sinai in the Bush, who didst unburnt conceive the fire of the Godhead in Thy womb; and Daniel saw Thee as the unhewn mountain; and Isaiah cried aloud, calling Thee the rod that sprouted from the root of David.

Like sheep were ye brought unto Him Who was slaughtered for our sake, and ye filled the divine choirs of Angels with joy, O passion-bearers of Christ; therefore, by your prayers on high, establish all men, and deliver them from the harmful deception of the enemy.

[f. 100vA] As luminaries possessing the living Word, enlighten our souls, O most-sacred High Priests of Christ, having received the fire of the Spirit; ye consumed the passions of deception and destroyed the generation of idols.[^146]

With the holy members of the Church let us honor the multitude of the Venerable, who cried aloud before the Law and under the Law through pure life; and let us praise the choir of holy women, crying aloud: O Lord, by their prayers save us all.

*Hymn for the Departed (Поко́инъ):*

Thy burial, O Christ, and Thy Resurrection became life unto all. Therefore, taking courage, we cry aloud unto Thee: together with Thine elect servants, give rest unto the faithful servants whom Thou hast received, and forgive all their transgressions, as the all-good God.

Theotokion:

Dreadful is this place! cried Jacob aloud when he beheld Thy prefiguration in the Ladder, O Mother of God, un-deceiving glory of the martyrs, praise of the venerable, proclamation of all the Prophets, and salvation of the faithful.

Another [Canon]. Heirmos.

Her who was prefigured by the bush and by fire on Sinai unto Moses the lawgiver, and who without being burned conceived the divine Fire in her womb: the all-radiant and unquenchable lamp, the true Mother of God, we honor in hymns, magnifying her.

Troparion:

Now as the only good and mankind-loving God, by the supplications of the martyrs, give forgiveness of transgressions unto those who have been translated unto Thee, O Merciful One, in the land of the meek, the land of gladness, [f. 100vB] unto those who unceasingly magnify Thee with hymns.

In the holy tabernacles, in the bosom of Abraham, number those whom Thou hast received, O Christ, with the righteous, where the light of Thy countenance shines, the ineffable and divine, and true everlasting joy that abides unto the ages.

Make Thy servants whom Thou hast translated by Thy will worthy of Thy blessed life, eternal good things, unceasing delight, and true gladness, O Giver of life, in a place of pasture, beside the waters of rest.

Theotokion:

As the holy Ark and candlestick of the Tabernacle of the Lawgiver, O all-immaculate Lady, Thou didst receive in Thy womb Thy Creator, Who by His death overthrew the ancient weapon found against us and the law of death.

AT THE PRAISES: STICHERA

Martyric. Tone 3.[^147]

Come, all ye peoples, let us honor the memory of the holy passion-bearers; for they became a spectacle unto Angels and men, and received crowns of victory from Christ; and they pray for our souls.

The soldiers of Christ cast away the fear of kings and tyrants, and with holy boldness and courage confessed Him, the Lord God of all and our King; and they pray for our souls.

The powers of the holy Angels were astonished at the contests of the martyrs, how being clothed in flesh they disregarded tortures, having become imitators of the passions of Christ the Savior; and they pray [f. 101rA] for our souls.

Ye shine as luminaries in the world, and even after death, O holy martyrs, having fought the good fight and possessing boldness, pray unto Christ that our souls may find mercy.

Glory... Both now... Theotokion:

Without seed Thou didst conceive of the Holy Spirit; and glorifying Thee, we sing: Rejoice, O most-holy Virgin!

AT THE APOSTICHA, STICHERA

*For the Departed. Tone 3.*

*Podoben: "Great is the power of Thy Cross, O Lord" (Ве́ліа Кр́та твое́го Гди):* [^148]

I glorify Thy precious Cross, by which life was bestowed and the enjoyment of delight unto those who sing of Thee in faith and love, O only abundant in mercy; therefore we cry unto Thee, O Christ God: Give rest unto those translated from among us, where there is a dwelling of all who rejoice in Thee.

*Verse: Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen and taken to Thyself, O Lord.*

O only Merciful and Tender-compassionate One, Who possessest an unfathomable abyss of goodness, and knowest human nature which Thou didst fashion: we pray Thee, O Christ God, give rest unto those translated from among us, where there is a dwelling of all who rejoice in Thee.

*Verse: Their souls shall dwell among good things.*

Thou didst abide in the tomb as a man; but by invincible power as God Thou didst raise up those who sleep in the tombs, who offer unceasing hymns unto Thee; therefore we pray Thee, O Christ God:

[f. 101rB] give rest unto those translated from among us, where there is a dwelling of all who rejoice in Thee.

Glory... Both now... Theotokion:

We all know Thee, O Mother of God, as an intelligible lamp bearing the light of the Godhead united unto the coarseness of human nature; pray Thou unto Thy Son and God to give rest unto those translated from among us, where there is gladness for all who rejoice.

ON SATURDAY, THE BEATITUDES

Tone 3.[^149]

Thou didst cast out our forefather Adam from Paradise when he set aside Thy commandment, O Christ; but the thief who confessed Thee upon the cross Thou didst bring into it, O Compassionate One, as he cried: Remember me, O Savior, in Thy kingdom.

Mingling yourselves with fiery wounds, O passion-bearers of Christ, ye found heavenly dew which refreshed and strengthened you to endure the bitter bodily pains; therefore ye ease every pain continually for our souls.

O sacred hierarchs, glorious Prophets, multitude of the venerable, and choir of divine women, through fasting ye received heavenly glory, trampling down the deception of the enemy; by their prayers, O Savior, have mercy upon Thy servants.

*Hymn for the Departed (Поко́инъ):*

Where Thy light shines in the mansions of Thine elect, O God, where delight flows evermore, establish those who have been translated from among us in faith, O Jesus, overlooking their transgressions, O Savior, that we may diligently glorify Thee.

Glory...

[f. 101vA] Glory... Triadicon:

To the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, the divine Trinity: we the faithful bow down before the uncreated Trinity, Who art in three Persons and in one Godhead, ever faithfully glorified by the bodiless powers in thrice-holy hymns.

Both now... Theotokion:

Enlightenment and cleansing, and deliverance for all through Him Who was revealed from Thee, [f. 101vB] O Lady full of the grace of God, fervently beseech Him to deliver us from all condemnation at the dread future judgment, O Most-pure One, who ever faithfully hymn Thee.

[Woodcut: The Golgotha Crucifixion scene, depicting the Cross of Christ on Mount Golgotha flanked by the spear on the left and the reed with sponge on the right, bearing the titulus inscribed "Jesus Christ, King of Glory" (*ІС ХС ЦРЬ СЛВЫ*), with the walled city of Jerusalem in the background and the skull of Adam in the cavern below.][^150]

[f. 102rA] ON SATURDAY EVENING, AT LITTLE VESPERS:

Resurrection Stichera, Tone 4.[^151]

Unceasingly bowing down before Thy life-creating Cross, O Christ, we glorify Thy three-day Resurrection; for thereby Thou hast renewed corrupted human nature, O Almighty One, and hast renewed for us the ascent into heaven, as the only good and mankind-loving God.

Thou didst loose the condemnation of the tree of disobedience, O Savior, by willingly being nailed to the wood of the Cross; and descending into hades, O Mighty One, Thou didst tear apart the bonds of death as God; therefore we bow down before Thy Resurrection from the dead, crying aloud with joy: O Almighty Lord, glory to Thee!

Thou didst shatter the gates of hades, O Lord, and by Thy death didst destroy the kingdom of death; and Thou didst set free the human race from corruption, granting life, incorruption, and great mercy unto the world.

Glory... Both now... Theotokion:

Great and most-glorious is the miracle wrought in Thee! And who is able to speak of the mighty acts of the Lord? For the wonders wrought in Thee, [f. 102rB] O Mother of God, surpass our understanding, being worthy of great astonishment; for being unable to speak of Thy mystery which cannot be comprehended, who hath ever heard from the ages of a Virgin nursing, and a Mother appearing on earth without a man, and carrying her Creator as an infant upon her arms? Therefore, O Lady, all generations unceasingly bless Thee.

AT THE APOSTICHA, STICHERON

Resurrectional. Tone 4.[^152]

Ascending the Cross, O Lord, Thou didst wipe away our ancestral curse; and descending into hades, Thou didst set free the eternal prisoners, granting incorruption unto the human race. Therefore, singing we glorify Thy life-creating and saving Resurrection.

Other Stichera to the Most-holy Mother of God,

*Same Tone.*

*Podoben: "Being called from on high" (Зва́нный бы́вше):*

*Verse: Virgins shall be brought unto the King after her, her companions shall be brought unto Thee.*

Save everyone who piously bows down down before Thy birth-giving, [f. 102vA] save from the assault of the enemy, O all-immaculate Mother of God, as the Protectress of our race; having now obtained Thee as our helper, we all possess a refuge and confirmation, and an advocate before the Master, Christ God; whom pray Thou to grant peace unto the world, we beseech Thee, and forgiveness of transgressions unto those who flee unto Thy protection.

*Verse: Hear, O daughter, and see, and incline thine ear.*

Behold, I lay bare unto Thee the sores of my soul, and show Thee the wounded afflictions which robbers have inflicted upon me through wicked thoughts and demonic agitations, O all-immaculate Mother of God, who gavest birth to the Physician of souls and bodies; grant me healing of these by Thy supplication, pouring forth the oil of Thy compassion and goodness according to the dignity of salvation and deliverance.

*Verse: I will remember thy name in every generation and generation.*

I, wretched one, do not hide my ways, for I have acquired all things that God hates; I have defiled flesh [f. 102vB] and my spirit, and the intellectual thoughts, with unfitting deeds and vile words, with tongue and deeds, senses, and most-grievous acts. O Mother of God, grant me amendment of all these, that I may not be put to shame by my evil customs; I fall down and weep for the wretched deeds I have committed walking through this life.

Glory... Both now... Theotokion:

All the sins I have committed and my iniquities which I have practiced, therefore I fall down before Thee: have mercy upon me, O Mother of God, all-immaculate Lady; cast me not away, nor put me to shame, O Helper of sinners; enlighten my humble and darkened heart; cleanse it with tears, weeping, sighing, and thoughts of compunction, that I may escape the unendurable fire and the worm; before the end, O all-wretched soul, hasten and repent fervently, and crying aloud with tears, say: O Mother of God, have compassion upon me!

Then: Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart: Trisagion. Troparion: The radiant proclamation of the Resurrection: Theotokion: The mystery hidden from the ages: and Dismissal.

# TONE 4: SATURDAY VESPERS, SUNDAY MATINS, AND WEEKDAY OFFICES

## SATURDAY EVENING: VESPERS (TONE 4)

[f. 103rA] Tone Four.

ON SATURDAY EVENING, AT GREAT VESPERS:[^153]

Resurrection Stichera, Tone 4.

Unceasingly bowing down before Thy life-creating Cross, O Christ, we glorify Thy three-day Resurrection; for thereby Thou hast renewed corrupted human nature, O Almighty One, and hast renewed for us the ascent into heaven, as the only good and mankind-loving God.

Thou didst loose the condemnation of the tree of disobedience, O Savior, by willingly being nailed to the wood of the Cross; and descending into hades, O Mighty One, Thou didst tear apart the bonds of death as God; therefore we bow down before Thy Resurrection from the dead, crying aloud with joy: O Almighty Lord, glory to Thee!

Thou didst shatter the gates of hades, O Lord, and by Thy death didst destroy the kingdom of death; and Thou didst set free the human race from corruption, granting life, incorruption, and great mercy unto the world.

[f. 103rB] Other Stichera, Anatolian.

Composition of Anatolius.

Come, ye peoples, let us sing of the Savior's three-day rising, whereby we have been delivered from the unbreakable bonds of hades, and have received incorruption and life, crying aloud: O Thou Who wast crucified, buried, and hast risen: save us by Thy Resurrection, O only Lover of mankind!

Angels and men, O Savior, sing of Thy three-day rising, whereby the ends of the universe have been enlightened, and we all have been delivered from the bondage of the enemy, crying aloud: O Life-creator, Almighty Savior, save us by Thy Resurrection, O only Lover of mankind!

Thou didst shatter the brazen gates and crush the iron bars, O Christ God; and Thou didst raise up fallen mankind; therefore in unison we cry aloud: O Lord Who didst rise from the dead, glory to Thee!

O Lord, Thy birth from the Father is timeless and co-eternal; [f. 103vA] and Thine incarnation from the Virgin is ineffable and inexplicable unto men; and Thy descent into hades was dreadful unto the devil and his angels; for having trampled down death, Thou didst rise on the third day, granting incorruption and great mercy unto mankind.

Glory... Both now... Theotokion:[^154]

David, the forefather of God, through Thee, O Prophet, musically proclaimed concerning Thee unto Him Who hath done great things for Thee: The Queen stood at Thy right hand; for God, Who willed to become man from Thee without a father, showed Thee as the Mother and mediatress of life, that He might renew His own image corrupted by passions; and having found the wandering sheep, caught by wolves, taking it upon His shoulders, He brought it unto the Father, and according to His own will united it with the heavenly powers; and Christ, Who possesses great and abundant mercy, saved the world through the Mother of God.

AT THE APOSTICHA, STICHERON

Resurrectional. Tone 4.[^155]

Ascending the Cross, O Lord, Thou didst wipe away our ancestral curse; and descending into hades, Thou didst set free the eternal prisoners, granting incorruption unto the human race. Therefore, singing we glorify Thy life-creating and saving Resurrection.

Other Stichera, Alphabetical.

*Verse: The Lord is King, He is robed in majesty.*

Suspended upon the wood, O only Mighty One, Thou didst shake all creation; and laid in the tomb, Thou didst raise up those dwelling in the tombs, granting incorruption and life [f. 103vB] unto the human race. Therefore, singing we glorify Thy three-day rising.

*Verse: For He hath established the world, so that it cannot be moved.*

The lawless people, O Christ, having betrayed Thee unto Pilate, condemned Thee to be crucified, appearing ungrateful toward their Benefactor; but of Thine own will Thou didst endure burial, and by Thine own sovereign power didst rise on the third day as God, granting unto us unending life and great mercy.

*Verse: Holiness becomes Thy house, O Lord, unto length of days.*

Reaching the tomb with tears, the women sought Thee; and not finding Thee, they wept and cried aloud with lamentation, saying: Woe unto us, our Savior, King of all! How wast Thou stolen away? What place contains Thy life-bearing body? An Angel answered them, saying: Weep not, but go and proclaim that the Lord is risen, granting us joy, as the only Compassionate One!

Glory... Both now... Theotokion:

Grant consolation unto Thy servants, O All-immaculate One, putting down the fierce risings against us, delivering us from every affliction; for Thee alone do we hold as a firm and sure hope, and we have acquired Thy protection; let us not be put to shame, O Lady, who call upon Thee; hasten Thou unto the supplication of those who faithfully cry unto Thee: Rejoice, O Lady, helper of all, joy and protection of our souls!

Troparion, Tone 4.

The joyful news of the Resurrection having been learned from the Angel by the disciples of the Lord, and having cast away the ancestral condemnation, [f. 104rA] they spoke exultantly unto the Apostles: Death is overthrown, and Christ God is risen, granting great mercy unto the world!

Theotokion:

The mystery hidden from the ages and unknown unto Angels was revealed through Thee, O Mother of God, unto those on earth, God being incarnate in unconfused union, and willingly accepting the Cross for our sake; whereby having raised up the first-fashioned, He saved our souls from death.

ON SUNDAY, AT MIDNIGHT OFFICE,

Triadicon Canon. Composition of Metrophanes. Tone 4.[^156]

Ode 1. Heirmos.

The deep of the Red Sea:

Let us glorify the Persons of the divine-originating Trinity, the one Nature equal in essence of the Three, co-eternal and enthroned together, praying and saying: Save those who faithfully glorify Thee!

Thou wast anointed by the Father with the oil of gladness through the Spirit, O God-crowned One, as Son; and becoming man, Thou didst teach the co-essential nature of the one Godhead.

The Seraphim, unable to endure the beauty of the inaccessible glory of Thy three-sunned Unity, cover themselves with their wings, and unceasingly glorify Thee with thrice-holy hymns.

Theotokion:

Ineffably Thou gavest birth unto the Creator of all, O Most-pure One, Who delivers mankind from the ancient curse and from mortal corruption; through Thee have we come to know the one co-essential God.

Ode 3. Heirmos.

Not by wisdom nor by power:

[f. 104rB] Having shown power unto Thy holy Apostles of old, in that Thou didst send the Comforter from the Father, O Christ, Thou didst reveal the one three-sunned Nature.

The Patriarch Abraham, when he beheld the appearance in the form of men, revealed the lordship of Thy goodness, O Trinity.

The one God believed in three Persons, uncircumscribed in heaven, unsearchable in time: deliver our souls from every affliction.

Theotokion:

Having been translated through Thy Son, as ones taught: glorify the co-essential and most-radiant Godhead, and ever bless Thee, O Virgin.

Sessional Hymn, Tone 4.

To: Speedily anticipate:

O Thou Who by Thine only beckoning and the pure counsel of Thy Father and the Spirit didst create all things, O Christ abundant in mercy, Thou didst accept crucifixion for the human race; therefore giving thanks, singing we cry aloud: Have mercy upon Thy flock, O only Lover of mankind!

Glory... Both now... Theotokion:

We sing of Thee, O Bride of God, Mother of Christ God, glorifying Thy birth-giving which cannot be comprehended, whereby we were delivered from the deception of the devil and from all perils, O Lady Mother of God; therefore in faith we cry aloud: Have mercy upon Thy flock, O only All-immaculate One!

Ode 4. Heirmos.

Sitting in glory upon the throne:

The transcendent Trinity, in the unity of the Godhead, [f. 104vA] and Lordship, with the Seraphim we glorify Thee as indivisible essence, as unmingled, as equal in dignity of glory, O God, Who art unsearchable.[^157]

Divided ineffably in the Persons of the Godhead, and united in the dominion of one Lordship, the unchangeable Father without beginning begat the uncircumscribed Word, and the divine Spirit equal in power proceeded from Him; therefore we piously proclaim the Trinity equal in essence as God.

Prefigured of old in types, the Word of God prefigured Thine incarnation from Thee, O Virgin; but afterward, having appeared unto men, He was revealed in truth as the three-hypostatic Unity.

Ode 5. Heirmos.

All things were amazed:

Understanding by faith the all-creative Godhead to be one inaccessible Essence, we sing of three life-originating and co-enthroned Hypostases: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, the co-eternal Unity.

O three-sunned Light of Thy substantial light, shine upon me, O unique Godhead, uncreated Nature, and Fountain of every light-giving ray, that I may behold Thine ineffable beauty.

As unto the one Father, Creator and Upholder of all, and all-wise Helmsman, the true Giver of life: falling down, [f. 104vB] preserve those who sing of Thee. Theotokion:

Willing to deify the man corrupted of old, whom He fashioned out of goodness, Thy Son, O Virgin, showing the image of the divine likeness, truly became man, and proclaimed the one three-sunned Godhead.

Ode 6. Heirmos.

Crying aloud, he prefigured:

The Father Who spoke was wholly revealed, and the Spirit was seen as Christ was baptized; therefore we glorify the one Trinitarian Godhead.

As Isaiah beheld Thee sung with thrice-holy voices, sitting upon a high throne, he knew the Hypostases of the one Trinitarian Godhead.

Show an exalted heart toward Thy servants, O exalted King co-essential, that the brightness of Thy glory may be seen.

Theotokion:

I have sinned, yet I have not departed from Thee, wretched as I am; have compassion upon me, O co-essential, one honorable Godhead, and deliver me from grievous condemnation, through the supplications of the maiden of God.

Sessional Hymn, Tone 4.

To: Lifted up on the Cross:

O incomprehensible God and inaccessible, Who art one by nature, good and tender-compassionate: O Father, Son, and most-holy Spirit, preserve and cleanse those who in faith cry aloud in Thy holy Church by night and by day; and deliver us not, O Master, unto the enemies who seek our destruction, [f. 105rA] that Thy servants may ever sing from the heart of Thy mercy, O Lady, calling and saying: O most-holy Virgin, hasten and deliver us from enemies visible and invisible, and from every threat, for Thou art our protection.[^158]

Ode 7. Heirmos.

In the furnace the Abrahamic children:

Imitating the heavenly natures and the ranks of the bodiless beings who dive into the depths, all we earthborn piously glorify the one Godhead in three equal-working Hypostases.

The sayings of the holy Prophets revealed Thee of old in types as the single Creator of all, the ineffable God and Lord in three divine Hypostases.

Theotokion:

The Word, invisible by nature and all-creative, appeared in flesh unto men, becoming man from the pure Mother of God, calling man unto communion with Thy Godhead, O Christ.

Ode 8. Heirmos.

Daniel stretched forth his hands:

O unique and thrice-radiant Light, beginningless Essence, incomprehensible Beauty: dwell within my heart, and show me to be a radiant and pure temple of Thy Godhead, as I cry: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing and exalt Him unto the ages!

From various passions, O indivisible Trinity, unmingled Unity, deliver me from the darkening of transgressions; and enlighten me with Thy deifying Spirit, that I may behold Thy glory and sing of Thee, [f. 105rB] the glory of the Lord.

Theotokion:

The Mind unbegotten is the Father, and the Word co-beginningless, and the Spirit co-enthroned: one Essence, Power, and Being, transcendent and ineffable, the great-working Trinity and Unity; preserve Thy flock through the prayers of the Mother of God, as the only Lover of mankind.

Ode 9. Heirmos.

Let every earthborn:

Unto Thee now I direct my heart and thought, and both day and night my whole soul and body unto my Creator and Deliverer, O three-radiant Ruler of all; and I cry unto Thee: Save me Thy servant from perils and great afflictions!

Exalt our mind and thought unto Thee on high, enlighten us with Thy most-pure radiances, O Father, Word, and Comforter, dwelling in inaccessible light, O Sun of glory holding the light: ever to glorify Thee, the one-originating God in three Persons.

One Light in three properties, divided in Persons: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, by Whom all creation subsists; Whom the Son, descending, renewed, suffered, and rose on the third day.

Save those who believe in Thee as God, who proclaim the transcendent beginningless Essence as one God: the three Persons, equal in beginning and dominion, of Thy Lordship, and worthy of divine glory, through the prayers of the pure Mother of God.

## SUNDAY MATINS (TONE 4)

At Matins, after God is the Lord: Troparion:

God is the Lord, and hath appeared unto us: and the rest...

[f. 105vA] Tone 4. Then the Troparion: The radiant proclamation of the Resurrection: Glory... Both now... Theotokion: The mystery hidden from the ages: Then the customary reading of the Psalter.

After the First Kathisma, Sessional Hymns:

Resurrectional. Tone 4.[^159]

Gazing upon the entrance of the tomb, and unable to endure the angelic flame, the Myrrh-bearers marvelled with trembling, saying: Was He stolen away, He Who opened Paradise unto the thief? Or is He risen, Who proclaimed His rising before His passion? In truth Christ is risen, granting life and resurrection unto those in hades!

Rising as immortal from hades, O Savior, Thou didst raise up Thy world with Thyself by Thy Resurrection, O Christ our God; Thou didst shatter in Thy might the dominion of death; Thou didst show forth the resurrection unto all, O Merciful One; therefore we glorify Thee, O only Lover of mankind!

Glory... Both now... Theotokion:

We magnify Thee, O Mother of God, crying aloud: Thou art the mountain from which the stone was cut out ineffably, which shattered the gates of hades.

After the Second Kathisma, Sessional Hymns:

*Resurrectional, Tone 4.*

*Podoben: "Joseph was amazed" (По: [Оу҆диви́ся І҆ѡ́сифъ]):*

By Thy voluntary counsel Thou didst endure crucifixion, O Savior, and in a new tomb mortal men laid Thee, Who by Thy word didst establish the ends of the earth; therefore the enemy was bound, and death was grievously despoiled, and all those in hades cried out unto Thy life-bearing rising: Christ is risen, [f. 105vB] the Giver of life, abiding unto the ages!

Gabriel descended from the heights on high, and approaching the stone where the Stone of life lay, shining in white he cried aloud unto the weeping women: Cease your cries of lamentation, ye who ever have grace; for Him Whom ye seek weeping, take courage, for He is truly risen; therefore cry aloud unto the Apostles that the Lord is risen!

Glory... Both now... Theotokion:

Joseph was astonished, beholding that which was beyond nature, and meditating upon the rain upon the fleece in Thy seedless conception, O Mother of God: the Bush unburnt by fire, Aaron's rod that budded; and he bore witness, as Thy betrothed and guardian, crying unto the priests: A Virgin gives birth, and after giving birth remains still a Virgin!

Hypakoe, Tone 4.

Running swiftly unto Thy glorious rising, the Myrrh-bearers proclaimed unto the Apostles, O Christ: that Thou art risen as God, granting great mercy unto the world.

Hymns of Degrees [Anavathmoi], Tone 4.

Antiphon 1.[^160]

From my youth many passions war against me; but do Thou Thyself help me and save me, O my Savior.

Ye who hate Zion, be put to shame by the Lord; for ye shall be withered up by fire even as grass.

By the Holy Spirit every soul is quickened, and exalted in purity; it is illumined by the Trinitarian Unity in sacred mystery.

[f. 106rA] Antiphon 2.

I cried unto Thee, O Lord, fervently from the depth of my soul, and let Thy divine ears be attentive unto my hearing.

Whosoever hath acquired hope in the Lord is higher than all who cause sorrow.

Through the Holy Spirit the streams of grace gush forth, watering all creation unto life.

Antiphon 3.

Let my heart be lifted up unto Thee, O Word, and let none of the beauties of the world sweeten me unto pleasure.

As one hath love toward his mother, so are we bound to have warmer affection toward the Lord.

Through the Holy Spirit comes the wealth of the knowledge of God, contemplation, and wisdom; for from Him the Word reveals all the Father's commandments.

Prokeimenon, Tone 4: Arise, O Lord, help us, and deliver us for Thy name's sake. [Ps. 43:26] Verse: O God, we have heard with our ears. [Ps. 43:1] Let every breath praise the Lord. Resurrection Gospel, and the rest in order.

THE RESURRECTION CANON.

Ode 1. Tone 4. Heirmos.[^161]

Traversing of old the deep of the Red Sea with dry feet, Israel conquered the power of Amalek in the wilderness by Moses' hands stretched out in the form of the Cross.

He was lifted up upon the most-precious wood of the Cross, correcting our fall, healing the ancient total ruin, [f. 106rB] O Master, as good and almighty.

In the tomb bodily, in hades with the soul as God, in Paradise with the thief, and on the throne wast Thou, O Christ, with the Father and the Spirit, filling all things, Thou Who art uncircumscribed.

Theotokion:

Without seed by the Father's will, from the divine Spirit, Thou didst conceive the Son of God and gavest birth unto Him in the flesh: Who is from the Father without a mother, and for our sake from Thee without a father.

Another Canon, of the Cross and Resurrection.

Tone 4. Heirmos: I will open my mouth:

Healing the shattered nature of mankind, O Lord, Thou didst renew it by Thy divine blood, and shattering him who was mighty in strength, who of old shattered Thy creation.

The rising of the dead came to pass through Thy being put to death; for the strength of death was taken away, being surpassed by eternal life, when God, Who rules over all, became incarnate.

Theotokion:

Remaining glorious above the heavenly hosts, Thy divine temple became animate; Thou didst bear in Thy womb, O Virgin, holy mountain, our Lady.

Another Canon, to the Most-holy Mother of God.

*Tone 4. Heirmos: The three mighty captains: He Who was born...*

The peoples were shaken, the nations were troubled, and the mighty kingdoms were bowed down, O Pure One, from fear of Thy birth-giving; for my King came, cast down the tyrant, and delivered the world from evil.

Descending unto men, Christ cleansed the dwelling where He Who dwells in the highest dwelt, and showed it to be unshakable, the only [f. 106vA] vessel of virginity after childbearing, having preserved her who gave birth unto the Creator.[^162]

Ode 3. Heirmos.

Thy Church rejoices in Thee, O Christ, crying aloud: Thou art my strength, O Lord, my refuge, and my confirmation!

The wood of life, the spiritual and true Vine, hangs upon the wood, pouring forth incorruption unto all.

As great, as dreadful, He cast down the insolence of hades; and as incorrupt God, He is now risen bodily from the tomb.

Theotokion:

Thou alone, O Mother of God, wast the mediatress of goods beyond nature for those on earth; therefore we cry unto Thee: Rejoice!

Another [Canon]. Heirmos: Thy singers, O Mother of God:

The serpents full of poison for me, O Savior, who bit bitterly, Thou, O Almighty Lord, didst shatter by the nails of Thy hands; for there is none holy among the saints above Thee, O Lord!

Willingly seen in the tomb as dead, O Lover of mankind, Giver of life, Thou didst break open the gates of hades for the souls from the ages; for there is none holy among the saints save Thee, O Lord!

Theotokion:

Thou wast shown forth as the unploughed field, having brought forth the living Ear of grain Who is the mediator of immortality for all who partake, resting holily in the Holy of Holies.

Another [Canon]. Heirmos: Let the heavens rejoice:

Earthly creation marvelled at the wonders, having been united through Thee unto the unendurable divine Fire, [f. 106vB] as bread baked well in clay, O Most-pure Virgin, having preserved human nature uninjured.

Who is she that is truly near unto God, as having surpassed the angelic ranks, alone in the beauty of virginity, as the Mother who bore the Almighty?

Ode 4. Heirmos.

Beholding Thee, the Sun of righteousness, lifted up upon the Cross, the Church stood in her station, worthily crying aloud: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

Ascending the Cross, Thou didst compel the death of Thy life-creating Body; worthily was it put to death, and we cry aloud unto Thee: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

Thou didst descend, healing my passions, suffering upon the Cross in Thy most-pure flesh, in which Thou didst willingly clothe Thyself; therefore we cry unto Thee: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

Theotokion:

Without knowing wedlock Thou gavest birth, O Virgin, and after childbearing wast shown forth remaining a Virgin; therefore with unceasing voices we cry aloud unto Thee with unwavering faith: Rejoice, O Lady!

Another [Canon]. Heirmos: The unsearchable:

Israel, the son according to the law, knew Thee not as God, O Christ Who wast without iniquity; but as a lawbreaker, transgressing the law, he nailed Thee unto the Cross, being unworthy of the giving of the law.

Having deified Thy soul, O Savior, Thou didst despoil the treasures of hades, raising up the souls from the ages; and Thy life-bearing body poured forth incorruption for all time.

[f. 107rA] incorruption.

Theotokion:

Truly we glorify Thee, O Virgin, as the only Mother of God, whom the Bush unburnt prefigured unto Moses the beholder of God, mingled with fire, O Most-pure One.

Another [Canon]. Same Heirmos.

He lived with men, the Invisible One became visible, being in the form of the incomprehensible Godhead; and taking form from Thee, O Virgin, of the Father's flesh, unto those who know Thee as the pure Mother of God.

The Virgin received the Immaterial One materially in the midst of matter, an infant wrapped in swaddling clothes; therefore the incarnate God is known in two natures, both earthly and above essence.

After childbearing He Who dwelt as God in the Virgin preserved Thee a Virgin; and being born without seed, He remained the Word and God, and preserved the Virgin in childbearing, as God and Creator.

Ode 5. Heirmos.[^163]

Thou, O Lord, art my light, Who camest into the world, the holy Light turning back from gloomy ignorance those who sing of Thee in faith.

Thou, O Lord, didst mercifully come down unto the earth; Thou didst lift up fallen human nature, being exalted upon the wood.

Thou didst take away for me the condemnation of transgressions, O Christ; Thou didst loose the pangs of death, O Compassionate One, by Thy divine Resurrection.

We offer Thee as an invincible weapon against enemies; we have acquired Thee as confirmation and the hope of our salvation, O Bride of God.

[f. 107rB] Another [Canon]. Heirmos: All things were amazed:

Senseless hades prepared to receive Thee entirely, for beholding Thee nailed to the Cross, pierced with the lance, breathless, the living God: it thought Thee to be a mere man; but experiencing the might of Thy Godhead, it came to know Thee.

The tomb and hades, O Lover of mankind, divided the ruined temple of Thy body, having gone thither unwillingly unto those who had decayed; so that the souls of Thy saints and their bodies, O all-mortal One, were quickened.

Lo, now the prophetic utterance is fulfilled; for Thou, O Virgin unwedded, didst receive in Thy womb the God Who is over all, and gavest birth unto the timeless Son, Who grants peace unto all who sing of Thee.

Another [Canon]. Heirmos: Unto those walking in darkness:

A house of glory, and a holy mountain of God, O Pure One, a bridal chamber, a temple of sanctification of the Son of God Who dwelt in Thee, and made for us the eternal wounds of delight.

Thou didst take flesh from virginal blood, O Christ, a thickened substance and composition, endowed with speech and intellect, animate, effective, having will, self-determining, and sovereign.

The virginal womb put to shame the mind of tyrants; for as an infant He tested the soul-destroying viper's den with His hand, and cast down the proud whisperer, subjecting him under the feet of the faithful.

Ode 6. Heirmos.

I will sacrifice unto Thee with the voice of praise, O Lord, the Church cries unto Thee, having been cleansed from the blood of demons by the mercy [f. 107vA] flowing from Thy side.

Thou didst ascend the Cross, girded with power, and grappling with the tyrant as God, Thou didst cast that adversary down from on high; and Adam Thou didst raise up by Thine invincible power.

Rising radiant and beautiful from the tomb, O Christ, Thou didst scatter all Thine enemies by divine power, and as God didst fill all things with gladness.

Theotokion:

O wonder newest of all wonders! For a Virgin, having conceived without a man, contained without confinement in her womb Him Who upholds all things by His word.

Another [Canon]. Heirmos:

I came into the depth of the sea:

Hades opened its throat and swallowed me, and expanded its soul, being unavoidable; but Christ, descending, brought up my life, as the Lover of mankind.

Death perished by death; for He Who was put to death is risen, granting me incorruption; appearing unto the women, the Immortal One proclaimed joy.

Theotokion:

Thy pure womb was shown forth as the spacious dwelling-place of the incomprehensible Godhead, O Mother of God, which the other ranks are unable to behold without fear.

Another [Canon]. Same Heirmos:

The evil and venomous serpent slew me, because of my foremother Eve; but now, O Pure One, He Who fashioned me called me back from corruption through Thee.

The abyss of ineffable beauty, O Maiden, clearly showed Thee forth as chosen, in whose womb Christ the Savior formed the lightning of the Godhead...

[f. 107vB] KONTAKION, Tone 4.[^164]

To: Thou hast appeared today:

My Savior and Deliverer from the tomb, as God, raised up the earthborn from their bonds, and shattered the gates of hades; and as Master He is risen on the third day!

IKOS

Let all we earthborn praise Christ, the Giver of life, Who is risen from the dead on the third day from the tomb, Who today shattered the gates of death by His power, put hades to death, crushed the sting of death, and set free Adam with Eve, gratefully crying aloud diligent praise; for He alone, as the mighty God and Master, is risen on the third day!

Ode 7. Heirmos.

In the fiery furnace the Persian children of Abraham, burned rather by the desire of piety than by the flame, cried aloud: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord!

Human nature was brought unto incorruption, washed by the divine blood of Christ, gratefully singing: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord!

As life-bearing, as truly more beautiful than Paradise, and brighter than any royal bridal chamber, O Christ, Thy tomb was shown forth: the fountain of our resurrection.

Theotokion:

Rejoice, O holy divine dwelling of the Most High! For through Thee joy was given unto those who cry unto Thee, O Mother of God: Blessed art Thou among women, O all-immaculate Lady!

[f. 108rA] Another [Canon]. Heirmos:

The god-wise ones did not serve creation:

Lifted up upon the wood, Thou didst humble the haughty eye, and the exalted pride Thou didst cast down unto the earth; and Thou didst save man, O praised God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

By Thy power Thou didst exalt the horn of those who serve Thee, Who art risen from the dead; and Thou didst empty the rich storehouse of hades, O praised God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

Triadicon:

Shining with divine rays, we glorify the one Godhead, as in three lights, unmingled, undivided, the eternal flame enlightening all who cry: O praised God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

Another [Canon]. Heirmos:

The three youths in Babylon:

Virginal love draws me unto singing, the fire unto rest in the Mother and Virgin: Blessed art Thou, O Lord, Who art.

Thou art higher than all creatures, for Thou gavest birth unto the Creator and Lord; therefore I cry unto Thee, O blessed Mother of God: The Lord of hosts is with Thee!

Triadicon:

I honor one Nature indivisible in three Hypostases, and I sing of the three-hypostatic Nature: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers!

Ode 8. Heirmos.[^165]

Daniel stretched forth his hands and shut the mouths of lions in the pit; and the youths, lovers of piety, girded with virtue, quenched the power of the fire, [f. 108rB] crying: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing and exalt Him unto the ages!

Stretching forth Thy hands upon the Cross, Thou didst gather all nations from the ends of the earth, and didst show forth one Church, O Christ, unto those who sing of Thee, both earthly and heavenly, singing in unison: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing and exalt Him unto the ages!

Shining in white, the Angel appeared unto the women with the untouchable light of the Resurrection, crying: Why seek ye the living in the tomb as dead? In truth Christ is risen, unto Whom we cry: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing and exalt Him unto the ages!

Theotokion:

Thou alone in all generations, O Virgin Most-pure, wast shown forth as the Mother of God; Thou, O all-immaculate One, becamest the dwelling of the Godhead, unburnt by the fire of the inaccessible Light; therefore all of us bless Thee, O Mother, Bride of God!

Another [Canon]. Heirmos: The godly youths:

Beholding Thine unjust slaughter, creation darkened and lamented; for the earth was troubled, and the sun clothed itself in gloom as a dark garment; and we sing of Thee, O Christ, and exalt Thee unto all ages!

He Who descended with me even unto hades, and made a way of resurrection for all, raising me up again upon His shoulders, brought me unto the Father, crying: Sing unto the Lord, all ye works, and exalt Him unto the ages!

Glory...

From the first and single Principle of all, the one Father, [f. 108vA] we glorify: proclaiming Thee the beginningless Begetter of the Word, and the Producer of the Spirit, God and Creator of all; in unison we bow down before the Trinity, and exalt Him unto all ages.[^166]

Another [Canon]. Heirmos: In the furnace:

He Who fashioned Thee from the rib of Adam is incarnate from Thy virginity; He Who is the Cause of all ages, Whom singing we cry aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing and exalt Him unto all ages!

In the tent Abraham beheld the mystery wrought in Thee, O Mother of God; for he received Thy bodiless Son, singing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing and exalt Him unto the ages!

Triadicon:

The prefiguration of Thine equal-honored Trinity, O Savior, the children trampled down the flame with virginal fire, crying aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing and exalt Him unto all ages!

Ode 9. Heirmos.

A cornerstone cut out without hands from an unhewn mountain, from Thee, O Virgin, was Christ cut out, uniting the separated natures; therefore rejoicing, we magnify Thee, O Mother of God!

Wholly didst Thou receive me in Thine incarnation, granting salvation unto all of me, O my Savior, Who didst endure bodily upon the Cross, O Christ of abundant grace; hades was shown to be desolate, and the holy God-bearing ones Thou didst raise up, manifestly by Thy rising, [f. 108vB] as the Angel spoke: In truth the Lord is risen!

Triadicon:

The Unity of the divine Essence, and the Trinity in Hypostases, let all we faithful praise: in unconfused Hypostases, the Father without beginning, the Son, and the All-holy Spirit.

Another [Canon]. Heirmos: Let every earthborn:

Cunningly creeping forth from Eden, the serpent swallowed me as a captive; but upon the firm rock of the skull Thou wast crushed, O Almighty Lord, as an infant; and by the wood of the Cross Thou didst open again for us the entrance to delight.

The strong pride of the enemy is now laid in desolation; and with an all-derisive hand, when he was broken, Thou didst deliver me from the entanglements of hades, O Christ; and now, as of old, Thou hast shown him who boasted to be subject to mockery.

Come, visiting the affliction of Thy poor people, with a merciful and mighty hand strengthen the Cross-bearing King against boastful enemies, to deliver Thine elect inheritance, as the Lover of mankind.

Another [Canon]. Heirmos: The mystery of God:

We behold Thee as a lily, O Pure One, clothed by the divine Spirit, O Most-pure One, in the midst of briars, filling with sweet fragrance those who faithfully magnify Thee.

Receiving corruptible earthly nature, from which, O all-immaculate Pure One, the Incorrupt One placed it in Himself incorruptibly, through His tender-compassion, [f. 109rA] therefore we magnify Thee as the Mother of God.

O Thou Who rulest over all creatures, grant victorious triumph unto Thy people, putting down the unsubmissive under the feet of the Church, that we may magnify Thee as the Mother of God.

AT THE PRAISES: STICHERA

Resurrectional. Tone 4.[^167]

O Thou Who didst endure crucifixion and death, and didst rise from the dead: O Almighty Lord, we glorify Thy Resurrection!

By Thy Cross, O Christ, Thou hast freed us from the ancient curse; and by Thy death Thou didst destroy the devil who tormented our nature, and by Thy rising Thou didst fill all things with joy. Therefore we cry aloud unto Thee: O Lord Who didst rise from the dead, glory to Thee!

By Thy Cross, O Christ Savior, guide us unto Thy truth; and deliver us from the snares of the enemy, O Thou Who didst rise from the dead; raise us up who have fallen into sin, stretching forth Thy hand, O mankind-loving Lord, through the prayers of Thy saints.

Without being separated from the Father's bosom, O Only-begotten Word of God, Thou camest down unto earth through love of mankind, becoming man without change; and Thou didst endure crucifixion and death in the flesh, being impassible in Thy Godhead; and rising from the dead, Thou didst grant immortality unto the human race, as the only Almighty One.

Other Stichera, Anatolian.

Thou didst take death in the flesh, mediating immortality for us, O Savior; and Thou didst dwell in the tomb, that Thou mightest free us from hades, raising us up together with Thyself. Thou didst suffer as man, [f. 109rB] yet Thou didst rise as God; therefore we cry aloud: Glory to Thee, O Giver of life, O Lord, only Lover of mankind!

The rocks were split asunder, O Savior, when Thy Cross was planted upon Golgotha; the gatekeepers of hades were terrified when Thou wast laid in the tomb as dead; for Thou didst destroy the power of death, granting incorruption unto all the dead by Thy Resurrection, O Christ, Giver of life, Lord, glory to Thee!

*Verse: Arise, O Lord my God, let Thy hand be lifted up; forget not Thy poor unto the end.*

The women longed to see Thy Resurrection, O Christ God; Mary Magdalene came beforehand, and found the stone rolled away from the tomb, and an Angel sitting and saying: Why seek ye the living among the dead? He is risen as God, that He may save the universe; let us bow down before Him!

*Verse: I will give thanks unto Thee, O Lord, with my whole heart; I will speak of all Thy marvelous works.*

Where is Jesus, Whom ye intended to guard? Tell us, O Jews: where is He Whom ye laid in the tomb, having sealed the stone? Give up the dead man, ye who rejected life; give up the buried One, or believe in Him Who is risen! Even if ye keep silence concerning His rising, the stones shall cry aloud, and especially the stone rolled away from the tomb. Great is Thy mercy, great is the mystery of Thy dispensation, O our Savior, glory to Thee!

Glory... The Morning Gospel Sticheron.

Both now... Theotokion: Most blessed art Thou: The Great Doxology: and Dismissal.

[f. 109vA] AT THE LITURGY.

## SUNDAY LITURGY: THE BEATITUDES (TONE 4)

The Beatitudes, Tone 4.[^168]

Through the tree Adam became an exile from Paradise; but through the tree of the Cross the thief dwelt in Paradise. For the one, having tasted, transgressed the commandment of Him Who made him; but the other, being crucified with Thee, confessed Thee as the hidden God, crying aloud: Remember me in Thy kingdom!

Having the Cross of Christ in our thoughts, let us strive to put to death the pleasures of life, making our souls a resting-place for the Holy Spirit; and raising the voice of the wise thief, let us cry aloud in faith: Remember us also in Thy kingdom!

O faithful, let us beseech Him Who is risen from the dead, Who despoiled the dominion of hades, and appeared unto the Myrrh-bearing women, crying aloud unto them: Rejoice! that He may deliver mankind from corruption, ever crying unto Him with the voice of the wise thief: Remember us also in Thy kingdom!

Unto Thy tomb, O Christ, the Myrrh-bearers came to anoint Thee; and not finding Thy life-bearing and most-pure body, O Good One, they were in perplexity, seeking Thee with tears and weeping; but beholding Thee, the beloved Master, they cried unto Thee: Remember us in Thy kingdom!

In truth Christ is risen! And the tomb bears witness, O transgressors [f. 109vB] of the law; for leaving the grave-clothes, He is risen on the third day, though ye sealed the stone; and the guards stood before the tomb; hades was despoiled, death was put to death; Christ was not stolen away: believe with us in His Resurrection!

Coming unto the Disciples, and granting them peace, and convincing doubting Thomas by the showing of the wounds, Thou didst raise up all the ends of the earth, O Lord, to glorify Thee; and being now entreated, O Master, save those who cry: Remember us in Thy kingdom!

Glory... Triadicon:

To the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, let all we faithful pray worthily with one mind to glorify the Unity of the Godhead, existing in three Hypostases, abiding unmingled, simple, indivisible, and inaccessible, whereby we are delivered from the fiery torment.

Both now... Theotokion:

Thy Mother, O Christ, who bore Thee in the flesh without seed, and truly remained a Virgin incorrupt after childbearing: we offer her unto Thee in prayer, O Master, abundant in mercy, to grant forgiveness of transgressions unto those who ever faithfully cry aloud: Rejoice, O truly living Treasure!

## SUNDAY EVENING VESPERS (TONE 4)

[f. 110rA] ON SUNDAY EVENING, AT "LORD, I HAVE CRIED":

*Penitential Stichera, Tone 4.*

*Podoben: "Thou hast given a sign" (Да́лъ есѝ зна́менїе):* [^169]

I have sinned, O Lover of mankind: not according to nature as a man, that I might ask forgiveness; but beyond man, and contrary to nature, and beyond forgiveness; but Thou, my Savior, having become higher than natural understanding, and possessing love for mankind beyond mind: have mercy upon me who turn unto Thee!

Thou didst establish repentance for sinners, O Christ, and not for the righteous, having the examples of the thief, the prodigal, Manasseh, the harlot, the persecutor, the publican, and the fornicator; knowing Thy love for mankind and all-goodness, my Savior, I do not despair, but I turn and pour forth tears, and I am confident that Thou wilt receive me.

Grant me compunction, estrangement from evils, and complete amendment, unto me who am now plunged in bodily passions and far estranged from Thee, O God and King of all; and having no hope at all, save me who am hungry for the sake of Thine abundant goodness: O all-powerful Jesus, Savior of our souls!

Other Stichera, to the Holy Angels.

*Tone 4.*

*Podoben: "As one valiant among martyrs" (Я҆́кѡ до́бля):*

[f. 110rB] Thou didst make the angelic hosts acceptable dwellings and all-radiant receptacles of divine radiances, O Immortal One, and spectators of the divine constitution, and ministers of Thy glory; Thou didst establish them in strength to accomplish Thy word, fulfilling Thine all-creative and simple will.

Willing to possess an abyss of goodness, being beginningless Good, Thou didst first fashion by immaterial beckoning the choirs of Angels and the ranks of the Powers; for in truth it was fitting that good things should be poured forth and proceed, that many might be benefited, O Master.

The six-winged Seraphim, the many-eyed Cherubim, the exalted Thrones surrounding Thee, partaking without mediation of Thine all-creative action, the Dominions, Principalities, Powers, Archangels, and Angels, divine Powers praising Thy glory, O Almighty One: pray unto Thee for us.

Glory... Both now... Theotokion:

Surpassing the angelic ranks, O All-immaculate One: together with the Angels ever pray [f. 110vA] Thou unto Him Who rules over the Angels and all creation, to grant us remission of transgressions, and deliverance from passions, and to make us then worthy singers of His glory and heirs of incorruptible food.

AT THE APOSTICHA, STICHERA

Penitential, Tone 4.

With tears I desired to wash away the handwriting of my transgressions, O Lord, and for the rest of my life to be well-pleasing unto Thee through repentance; but the enemy beguiles me, and battles against my soul. O Lord, before I perish utterly, save me!

Who that is tempest-tossed and flees unto this harbor is not saved? Or who that is diseased and falls down before this remedy is not healed? O Creator of all, and Physician of the sick: O Lord, before I perish utterly, save me!

Glorified in the memory of Thy saints, O Christ God, and entreated by them: send down upon us great mercy.

Glory... Both now... Theotokion:

Rejoice, O radiant Cloud! Rejoice, O luminous Lampstand! Rejoice, O Urn containing the Manna! Rejoice, O Rod of Aaron! Rejoice, O Unburnt Bush! Rejoice, O Bridal Chamber! Rejoice, O Throne! Rejoice, O holy Mountain! Rejoice, O Refuge! Rejoice, O Divine Table! Rejoice, O mystical Gate! Rejoice, the Joy of all!

## MONDAY MATINS: REPENTANCE AND THE BODILESS POWERS (TONE 4)

[f. 110vB] ON MONDAY AT MATINS.

After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymns.

Penitential, Tone 4.

Visit my humble soul, O Lord, which hath spent its whole life in sins; receive me as the harlot, and save me.

Crossing the deep of the present life, I contemplate the abyss of my many evils; having no helmsman for my thoughts, with the voice of Peter I cry unto Thee: Save me, O Christ God; save me, as Thou art the Lover of mankind!

Glory... Both now... Theotokion:

An invincible rampart art Thou unto us Christians, O Virgin Theotokos; for fleeing unto Thee, we remain unharmed, and when we sin again, we have Thee as an intercessor. Therefore giving thanks, we cry aloud unto Thee: Rejoice, Thou who art full of grace: the Lord is with Thee!

After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns.

Penitential, Tone 4.

Let us swiftly enter together into the Bridal Chamber of Christ, that we all may hear the blessed voice of Christ our God: "Come, ye who love heavenly glory, and receive it together with the wise virgins, having enlightened your lamps with faith!"

Weighed down by the multitude of my transgressions, I am troubled with fear of torment, O Christ our God; I offer tears of repentance of heart unto Thee Who hast dominion over life and death, and I cry unto Thee in compunction: I have sinned, O Lord, save me!

Today the angelic hosts [f. 111rA] to enlighten the minds of the faithful, and to make them radiant with divine grace. Therefore, O God, being entreated by them: grant us great mercy.

Glory... Both now... Theotokion:

Having received the word from the Angel in Thy womb, O Virgin, and having given birth unto Christ God incarnate, Emmanuel: O Theotokos, intercede for our souls.

After the 3rd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns, Tone 4.[^170]

To: Swiftly anticipate:

With immaterial lips, O Supradivine Trinity, the choirs of the Bodiless Powers stand before Thee with fear, unceasingly singing unto Thee, crying aloud: "Holy! O Tri-hypostatic Nature, have mercy on Thine own creation, the work of Thy hands!" By their supplications, O only Lover of mankind.

Glory...

The angelic ranks stand with fear before Thy throne, O Master, and being enlightened by the radiances proceeding from thence unto singing, they unceasingly chant a hymn of victory unto Thee. By their holy prayers, grant peace unto the world and remission of our transgressions, O Lord.

Both now... Theotokion:

O all-immaculate Virgin, who didst bear the transcendent God: together with the Bodiless Powers unceasingly pray unto Him to grant us remission of transgressions and amendment of life before the end, unto us who faithfully and lovingly praise Thee as is meet, O only all-praised one!

CANON, Penitential.[^171]

Tone 4, Ode 1. Heirmos:

The three mighty captains: He Who was born of the Virgin hath drowned the tripartite soul in the deep of impassibility; by prayer, as upon a timbrel, in the mortification of the body, let me sing a hymn of victory unto Thee!

[f. 111rB] O my Savior Jesus, Who didst save the prodigal, and didst receive the weeping of the harlot, and the sigh of the publican, justifying him by Thy nod who had sinned without number: receive also me who turn, and save me.

Like combustible material, the malignant fire devours my soul, and the flame of the torment to come: O Lover of mankind, extinguish it with the dewing drops of Thy mercies, O Long-suffering One, granting me tears of repentance.

Martyricon:

Filled with great understanding, the choir of holy Sufferers wisely rejected the foolish counsel and contrary wisdom of all the lawless, and received honor from God.

Leaving the fair things of the world, O all-lauded and patient sufferers, ye followed the holy end of every struggle; therefore deliver me, who ever call you blessed, from every worldly confusion.

Theotokion:

O most-radiant Lamp of the Sun of glory: rekindle my soul, which hath quenched its fire through slothfulness, watering it with the sweetness of divine deeds, O Most-pure One, that with faith and love I may glorify Thee.

Another Canon to the Bodiless Powers.

Tone 4, Same Heirmos.

As pure minds standing before the great and primal Mind, and filled with divine radiance, O Angels, [f. 111vA] illumine me with your ray as I sing, O most-glorious ministers of the Word, the Cause of all!

Incline with love unto the Son on high, and fashioned in the heavens with divine beauties, O glorious Archangels, ye stand in tenderest dwellings, crying: "A song of victory unto the Creator!"

Theotokion:

O Thou who alone didst receive in Thy womb the Word Whom the angelic hosts ever glorify: heal my soul, loose the shame of sin, O all-immaculate one, and enlighten me with understanding of Thy childbearing.

Ode 3. Heirmos:

From on high He descended willingly upon the earth, He Who is exalted above every principality and power, and hath lifted up from nethermost hades the humble nature of mankind; for there is none holy save Thee, O Lord!

The darkness of passions of the night of this life hath encompassed me, O Christ God; O Thou Who art the Unwaning Light, illumine me with the rays of repentance, and save me, as Thou art the Lover of mankind, that I may glorify Thee.

Show me to be of the portion of Thine elect, O Christ, having separated me from the adversary's part, O Savior, cleansed by tears and almsgiving, that in praise I may glorify Thee evermore.

Martyricon:

Your feet were truly reddened with blood, and having stepped forth, they ran unto heaven; having forsaken the earth together with sin, O Martyrs, companions of divine glory, while your body dissolved under wounds, O Sufferers of Christ, [f. 111vB] the power of your soul was strengthened, being joined inseparably with love unto Him Who created all things by His will.

Theotokion:

O Lady Mary, who didst bear the Lord of Hosts as a sacred one: deliver and enlighten my soul, which is weakened by passions of the mind and blackened by malice.

Another Canon to the Bodiless Powers.[^172]

Tone 4, Same Heirmos.

O Word of God, Who art praised by heavenly choirs: make the assemblies of the faithful to resemble them in harmony of mind; for there is none holy save Thee, O Lover of mankind!

With warm love and zealous affection, partaking of the primal Source, the divine Archangels stand ministrant before Him, unceasingly singing: "One is the essence of the beginningless Godhead!"

Theotokion:

O pure Mother who didst bear Christ: Thou hast radiantly abolished the ancient curse of grief, for He crowns all with blessings; for there is no helper save Thee, O Most-pure Lady!

Ode 4. Heirmos:

Sitting in glory upon the throne of the Godhead:

As before the most righteous Judge, I now fall down before Thee, O Lord: deliver me who am condemned from condemnation of despair, and free me from Thy righteous judgment, making me worthy of the fountain of Thine elect.

Look upon me, O Lover of mankind, who have fallen among thieves; and heal me who am wounded by evil deeds, O Christ, pouring out for me the wine and oil of repentance, and clothe me with the garment of salvation.

Martyricon:

Clothed from on high with the robe of distinction in the stripping off of your bodies, O praiseworthy Martyrs, [f. 112rA] ye stripped bare him who of old puffed up our forefather, making his sighs dead.

Martyricon:

Flourishing before the lawless, O Martyrs, adorned with the understanding of the Word of God and with piety, ye wise ones submerged the ungodly in snares and silenced the enemies.

Theotokion:

Like rain dropping into the deep of wisdom, Jesus descended, finding Thee alone pure, O Virgin Mother of God, and by divine grace He stemmed the fierce torrents of impiety.

Another Canon. Same Heirmos.

By Thine incomprehensible power, O Word of God, All-good One, Thou didst incline the celestial minds from non-existence, and didst enlighten them with ineffable glory, as they cry unto Thee: "Glory to Thy power, O Christ!"

Guided by the Spirit and His grace, and rustling with divine rays, the exalted Powers inherited non-falling ranks, honoring the one Principle and Godhead of all.

Thy ministrant radiances were accounted worthy to behold the most-clear beauty of Thy face, and receiving understanding from thence, they cry unto Thee: "Glory to Thy power, O Christ!"

Theotokion:

Adorned with golden raiment, the Queen Virgin ever stands before the Son, incomparably higher than the Angels, who cry: "Glory to Thy power, O Lord!"

Ode 5. Heirmos:

"Now will I arise," prophetically saith God; "now will I be glorified; now will I be exalted, taking up him who fell from the Virgin, and I will lift him up unto the marvelous light of My Godhead."

[f. 112rB] As one condemned, I must stand before Thee, the only Judge, O Savior, and give an account of all the evil things wherein I have sinned utterly of my own will, and defiled myself entirely.

Save me, O Lord, for I am filled with many evils; heal, I pray Thee, my infirmities and fierce wrath, and do not abandon me alone according to Thy wrath, O my Jesus, who have sinned greatly against Thee.

Martyricon:

The Martyrs found a blessed end and obtained glory in heaven, glorifying Christ their combat-master with their limbs, courageously partaking beforehand in wounds and stripes.

Martyricon:

O blessed Sufferers of Christ: by your divine and fair life, with the unfading crown, the unwaning light, and the dwelling not made with hands, which cannot be shaken, ye have inherited the heavenly riches.

Theotokion:

Prophetic voices foretold Thy wonders, calling Thee, O Most-pure One, the Mountain, the Gate, and the luminous Candlestick, from whence in truth the marvelous Light enlightens the whole world, O pure Lady!

Another Canon. Same Heirmos.

With trembling the Cherubim and Seraphim together with the Thrones glorify Thee, and the divine Archangels, Dominions, Powers, Principalities, and Authorities together with the Angels: the honorable, single, and Triune Godhead.

[f. 112vA] The most-exalted Angels, having appeared in radiant form, O Christ, proclaiming Thy Resurrection unto the venerable women, and crushing the mind of the enemy with the flashes of Thy Godhead.

Now preserve Thy Church by the encampment of the Archangels, as she glorifies Thee with orthodox voices, O Thou Who wast ineffably born of the Virgin, and deliverest mankind from evil.

Ode 6. Heirmos:

I came into the deep of the sea, and the tempest of many transgressions overwhelmed me; but as God, lead up my life from corruption, O Plenteous in mercy!

Being dead in mind and unfeeling, wretch that I am, I ever defiled the counsel of my feet. O God Who didst create me, destroy me not utterly!

O Compassionate One, my deeds are ready to slander me like enemies before Thy child; therefore, O Christ, deliver me swiftly from them, guiding me unto repentance.

Martyricon:

The lawless assembly crushed the bones of the Passion-bearers, but crushed not their faith, for the sake whereof they appeared as heirs unto God and the Savior of our souls.

Martyricon:

Like precious stones upon an immovable rock, the Passion-bearers were divinely built up, and were established as temples of the Holy Spirit in the Church of God.

Theotokion:

O Bride of God, who didst bear Christ the Sun: enlighten my darkened heart with the rays that shine from Thee, through the dark assaults of sin.

Another Canon to the Bodiless Powers.

Tone 4, Same Heirmos.

Standing around the good Throne, O angelic hosts, now [f. 112vB] enjoying the radiance of the Primal Light: enlighten those who sing of you in faith!

Having created the angelic choirs by Thy wisdom, the Dominions, Powers, and Seraphim, Thou hast shown them forth as Master, praised in wonders.

Theotokion:

O Master Christ, resting upon exalted thrones, and preserving all things by divine providence: Thou didst rest as manna upon the virgin arms of the Maiden.

Ode 7. Heirmos:

The three children in Babylon turned the tyrant's command into foolishness, and in the midst of the fire they cried aloud: "Blessed art Thou, O Lord, God of our fathers!"

Unto whom shall I liken thee, woe is me, O wretched soul, loving unbecoming things and not loving the good? Therefore, before the end, hasten to show forth good examples.

Grant me a shower of tears, O Christ, that I may wash away my fierce offenses; and leave me not to perish, O Savior, who have sinned against Thee far more than any man.

Martyricon:
