Bearing in your body the mortification of the slain Word, ye put deceit to death; and though dead, O glorious ones, ye live, and heal those slain by passions, O Martyrs!

Martyricon:

What place doth not now possess you as enlighteners and protectors, O Martyrs? What land is not sanctified by your sufferings, O glorious ones, and by the torrents of your healings?

Theotokion:

Thou alone remainest a Virgin even after childbearing, O Lady, [f. 113rA] shining with virginal beauty; Thou alone knewest not maternal pangs, for Thou didst bear God, the Deliverer of our souls.

Another Canon to the Bodiless Powers.[^173]

Tone 4, Same Heirmos.

Having been made lights, the spiritual Angels led a pure life, crying aloud: "Blessed art Thou, O Lord, God of our fathers!"

Purified by a live coal, Isaiah beheld the Seraphim standing before Thy throne, crying aloud: "Blessed art Thou, O Lord, God of our fathers!"

Theotokion:

As Thou surpassest the ranks of the Bodiless Powers, O Virgin, having given birth unto the Son and Lord the Creator: blessed art Thou, O Most-pure Lady, and blessed is the Fruit of Thy womb!

Ode 8. Heirmos:[^174]

O Almighty Deliverer of all: descending into the midst of the flame, Thou didst bedew the pious ones, and didst teach them to sing: "Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, sing and exalt Him unto all ages!"

Lassoed together with beasts, having submitted to irrational passions, O Word of God, transcendent and beginningless: turn me and save me as I cry: "Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, sing and exalt Him unto all ages!"

The wild boar of evils hath devoured me alone, O Savior, like a vineyard cultivated by the Spirit; deliver me from it, O Word, and show me forth fruitful in virtues.

Martyricon:

The sprinkling of blood reddened [f. 113rB] for you a purple robe woven by God, wherewith ye were adorned, O Martyrs, wearing crowns of victory; and now warring for Christ, ye stand before the eternal King.

Martyricon:

The holy company of the Martyrs dissolved the unholy gathering that commanded them to act lawlessly; and having suffered lawfully, they were lawfully crowned by the Master of all.

Theotokion:

All creation blesses Thy childbearing, which crowned us with blessings and took away the curse, O only all-praised and glorified one, who hast bestowed grace upon our race!

Another Canon to the Bodiless Powers.

Tone 4, Same Heirmos.

As partakers of immortal life, O Creator, Thou didst make the Angels to share in this deathless life, and didst teach them to sing: "Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, sing and exalt Him unto all ages!"

Lovingly chanting hymns unto Thee, the Archangels cry with unceasing voices, divinely honoring Thee as Master of all: "Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, sing and exalt Him unto all ages!"

Theotokion:

Legal types prefigured Thee, O all-blessed one, who didst bear God united unto material flesh, Who before was immaterial divine essence: bless, O Virgin, Thy childbearing!

Ode 9. Heirmos:[^175]

Eve indeed, through the disease of disobedience, brought in the curse; but Thou, O Virgin Theotokos, through the blossoming of Thy childbearing, didst bud forth blessing unto the world. Therefore we all magnify Thee.

[f. 113vA] Behold, the time of repentance, O my soul! Why art thou idle? Why art thou weighed down with sleep? Let us cast off despondency, let us adorn our lamp with the oil of good deeds, as it is written, lest we stand outside the doors weeping!

While there is yet time to repent, turn away from the evils thou hast committed, knowingly and unknowingly, O my soul, and cry aloud unto Him Who knows all things: "I have sinned! Forgive me, O Master, and be not angry with me, who am unworthy!"

Martyricon:

Christ gathered the holy Sufferers from every land and glorious city into honorable resting-places, and now they joyfully enlighten the Church of the firstborn.

Martyricon:

The all-honorable shrine of Thy precious Martyrs, being gloriously irradiated with the rays of the Holy Spirit, beams forth healings abundantly and dispels the darkness of disease, O Lord, only Plenteous in mercy!

Theotokion:

Enlighten my soul with the rays that are in Thee, O Bride of God, and raise me up who lie in the pit of perdition, crushing the waves that ever afflict my heart and stir me up unto passions.

Another Canon to the Bodiless Powers.

Tone 4, Same Heirmos.

A divine mystery is accomplished in Thee, O most-pure Virgin; for God was incarnate of Thee through tender mercy. Therefore we magnify Thee as the Mother of God.

As ye sing unto the Parent of the Mind, and the Son, and the Spirit:

[f. 113vB] O Angels, hasten now to bring unto us the gifts of divine grace!

Beautifully adorned with the gift of incorruption and grace, the divine Archangels, running unto Thee, O Christ, the Fountain of the Godhead, magnify Thee in song as Benefactor.

Theotokion:

Bridal chamber of the ineffable Incarnation, living palace unto all the sanctified, and Ark of the law of grace art Thou, O Mother of God: therefore we unceasingly magnify Thee!

AT THE APOSTICHA, STICHERA

Penitential, Tone 4.

Wash me with my tears, O Savior, for I am defiled with many sins; therefore I fall down before Thee: I have sinned, have mercy on me!

I am a sheep of Thy rational flock, and I flee unto Thee, the Good Shepherd; seek me out who have gone astray, O Christ, and have mercy on me.

Who would not marvel, beholding the good fight wherein ye contended, O holy Martyrs? How, being in the flesh, did ye vanquish the bodiless foe, confessing Christ and arming yourselves with the Cross? Therefore ye were worthily revealed as expellers of demons and conquerors of barbarians, unceasingly praying that our souls may be saved.

Glory... Both now... Theotokion:

O Lady and Queen of all, praise of the Orthodox: shatter the insolence of heretics, and put to shame the faces of those who bow not down before, nor honor, [f. 114rA] O Most-pure One, Thine honorable icon!

ON MONDAY, THE BEATITUDES.

Tone 4.

Through the tree Adam was cast out of Paradise; but through the tree of the Cross the thief dwelt in Paradise. For the one, having tasted, transgressed the commandment of Him Who made him; but the other, being crucified with Thee, confessed Thee as the hidden God, crying aloud: "Remember me in Thy kingdom!"

When Thou comest to judge thus, I who have sinned on earth more than all men, and fear the unbribable judgment-seat there: preserve me then uncondemned, O All-good One, and deliver me from torment, granting me repentance that washes away great defilements, as Thou art the Lover of mankind!

Cherubim and Seraphim, Authorities, Thrones, Archangels, Dominions, and all Powers, holy Angels, and most exalted Principalities: now standing before the Master of all, entreat remission of transgressions and direction of life for all who faithfully cry: "Remember us in Thy kingdom!"

Having approached the fire, ye burned up deceit as brushwood, O holy Passion-bearers of Christ; [f. 114rB] and with the multitude of your blood, O all-lauded ones, ye choked the ancient serpent; having taken the victory, ye rejoice with the hosts on high, praying earnestly that we may be saved.

Glory... Triadicon:

O three-sunned Radiance shining in the fullness of the world: having driven away the fierce passions of my soul, send down upon me the illumination of light and cleansing, unto me who now cry in faith: Unto the beginningless Father, the co-enthroned Son, and the Spirit: O Trinity, all-creating Power, save us!

Both now... Theotokion:

Cleanse me who sin evermore and am wholly held fast by slothfulness, O pure Lady, and adorn me with forms of repentance, granting compunction unto my humble soul, O Most-pure One, unashamed hope of those who lovingly praise Thee, and who faithfully cry aloud: Remember us also, O all-hymned Virgin!

## MONDAY EVENING VESPERS (FOR TUESDAY) (TONE 4)

ON MONDAY EVENING, AT "LORD, I HAVE CRIED":[^176]

*Penitential Stichera, Tone 4.*

*Podoben: "With tears I desired" (Хотѣ́хъ слеза́ми):*

I ought ever to remember the last hour of my departure, and the coming of the Angels, and the assaults of demonic thoughts; but the enemy, casting into my mind the fall of my intellect, ever entices me deceitfully unto worse things. O Lord, before I perish utterly, save me!

It behooves me ever to keep in mind the fearful judgment-seat [f. 114vA] O Lord, Thy judgment-seat: how shall I stand before Thy throne, having not kept Thy commandments, nor a single ordinance, and unable to tear away evil thoughts? But as Thou Thyself knowest, grant me amendment, and save me!

The gloom of sin covers me, a wave of vile thoughts, a tempest of passions troubles me and betrays me to destruction; but as my Creator and Maker, and my merciful God and Lord, deliver me from future calamity and affliction!

Other Stichera, to the Holy Forerunner John. Same Tone.

Having boldness toward the Lord, O Forerunner who surpassest all born of women: unceasingly pray unto Him for those who in faith entreat thee, to give us conversion and forms of repentance, that being ever saved, we may praise thee.

Thou wast named a Prophet from the womb, and a preacher from the belly, O Forerunner and Apostle of the Lord's coming. Unto demons am I surrendered, and a slave unto many sins: set me upright from both, as thou didst baptize the Lord, that I may proclaim Thy swift protection.

Thou art the winnowing-fan of the Divine Spirit: blow away the tare-like manners from my heart, gathering the divine deeds from me, as wheat into the granary of God, that I may be acceptable food unto the Master, enriched with eternal rest, O blessed Baptist of Christ!

[f. 114vB] Glory... Both now... Theotokion:

Grant me tears from the heart, and sighing from the deep, O Maiden, and contrition of soul, and the forgiveness of transgressions committed by me in life, that by Thy help I may pass through this life in peace, and attain everlasting rejoicing.

AT THE APOSTICHA, STICHERA

Penitential, Tone 4.

With tears I desired to wash away the handwriting of my transgressions, O Lord, and for the rest of my life to be well-pleasing unto Thee through repentance; but the enemy beguiles me, and battles against my soul. O Lord, before I perish utterly, save me!

Who that is tempest-tossed and flees unto this harbor is not saved? Or who that is sick and falls down before this remedy is not healed? O Creator of all, and Physician of the sick: O Lord, before I perish utterly, save me!

O Thou Who didst accept the endurance of the holy Martyrs: receive from us also our singing, O Lover of mankind, and grant us their prayers and great mercy.

Glory... Both now... Theotokion:

Deliver us from our afflictions, O Mother of Christ God, who didst bear the Creator of all, that we all may cry unto Thee: Rejoice, the only protectress of our souls!

## TUESDAY MATINS: REPENTANCE AND ST. JOHN THE FORERUNNER (TONE 4)

ON TUESDAY AT MATINS.[^177]

After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymns.

Penitential, Tone 4.

Visit my humble soul, O Lord, [f. 115rA] which hath spent its whole life in sins; receive me as the harlot, and save me.

Crossing the deep of the present life, I contemplate the abyss of my many evils, and having no helmsman for my thoughts, with the voice of Peter I cry unto Thee: Save me, O Christ, save me, as Thou art the Lover of mankind!

Glory... Both now... Theotokion:

As Thou art truly the Mother of God, praying with boldness unto Thy Son and our God, as His Mother: preserve the city, especially those who run unto Thy protection, who have Thee as their dominion, and who flee unto Thee, the harbor and rampart, the only protectress of the human race.

After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns.

Penitential, Tone 4.

My mind is darkened by the gloom of passions and worldly vanities, wretch that I am, and there is no thought of repentance in me; but have compassion, O Savior, on me the wretched, and grant me thoughts of compunction, that being saved, before the end I may cry unto Thy tender mercy: O Lord, Christ, my Savior, save me who am despairing and unworthy!

Let us swiftly enter into the Bridal Chamber of Christ, that we all may hear the blessed voice of Christ our God: "Come, ye who love heavenly glory, and receive it together with the wise virgins, having enlightened your lamps with faith!"

Martyricon:

Armed with the Cross, Thy holy Passion-bearers [f. 115rB] conquered the wiles of the primal-evil enemy, O Christ our God; they shone forth as luminaries, guiding those on earth, and they grant healings unto those who ask in faith. By their prayers, save our souls!

Glory... Both now... Theotokion:

The Word of the Father, Christ our God, incarnate of Thee have we known, O Virgin Theotokos, only pure, only blessed one! Therefore unceasingly praising Thee, we magnify Thee.

After the 3rd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns, Tone 4.

Repent, O soul, before thy departure: judgment is inexorable for those who sin, and unstable; cry aloud unto the Lord with compunction of heart: "I have sinned knowingly and unknowingly, O Compassionate One: by the prayers of Thy Baptist, have mercy and save me!"

The turtledove loving song, the sacred Baptist, who preached repentance and showed forth Christ to be the Son of man, became an advocate for all who sin, and an ever-present helper unto all the tempest-tossed. By his prayers, O Christ, save Thy world!

Glory... Both now... Theotokion:

By Thy divine childbearing, O pure Lady, Thou hast renewed the mortal nature of earthborn men that had decayed in passions, and hast raised all up from death unto the life of incorruption. Therefore as is meet, we all call Thee blessed, O all-glorified Virgin, even as Thou didst foretell.

[f. 115vA] CANON, Penitential.[^178]

Composition of Joseph.

Tone 4, Ode 1. Heirmos:

He Who smote Egypt and drowned the tyrant Pharaoh in the sea, and saved the people from bondage, as Moses sang a hymn of victory: for He is glorified!

To me who secretly commit deeds of darkness, O Lord: do not rebuke me openly, nor put me to shame before all; but enlighten me with the light of true repentance, O Savior, and save me.

I, the prodigal, ever add sins unto sins, and never feel Thy fear, O Lord. Therefore before the end save me and have mercy on me!

Martyricon:

Protected by the shield of piety, O holy ones, and carrying the weapon of the Cross like a spear, ye went forth against the root of the enemy, O glorious ones, and cast him down.

Martyricon:

Blood-drinking lions, the cutting sword, boiling cauldrons, tearing out of nails, rending and painful torments: the divine Martyrs feared none of these.

Theotokion:

An Ark gilded with the Holy Spirit wast Thou revealed, O Most-pure One: carrying not the tables of the law, but Christ the Lord, Whom the law and the Prophets foretold of old.

Another Canon, to the Holy Forerunner John. Tone 4.

*Heirmos: The three mighty captains: He Who was born...*

As a great star unto the sun, O Forerunner, thou didst enlighten the earth with thy radiances, O Baptist. Therefore I cry unto thee: Enlighten [f. 115vB] my heart, blinded by fierce darkness from countless transgressions!

Thou didst once loose the bonds of barrenness when thou wast born, O blessed one. Therefore I pray thee: show my soul, barren of commandments, to be fruitful through thy prayers, bearing the grace of virtues.

Preparing the way, going forth in the power of Elijah unto the Deliverer: direct the movements of my soul unto Him, O ever-glorious Baptist, removing every stumbling-block and stone of offense by thy prayers.

O luminous cloud, disperse the many and dark clouds of my soul by thy radiant intercession, that I may see the radiance of Him Who shone forth from the Virgin, and receive unwaning light through light.

Ode 3. Heirmos:

Thou Who dost establish the thunder and create the spirit: establish me, O Lord, that I may sing unto Thee in truth, and do Thy will; for there is none holy as Thou, our God!

O Thou Who didst enlighten the eyes of the blind, O Christ: enlighten my eyes darkened by pleasures and worldly cares, which look not at all upon Thy judgments.

Behold the time: arise, O my soul, from the evils thou hast committed, and cry with fear unto the Key, the Deliverer: "Open unto me the doors of repentance!"

Martyricon:

The divine instruments were shown forth in divine struggles by the Passion-bearers, and trampled under them [f. 116rA] he who of old boasted is seen dead and inactive.

Martyricon:

Having finished the course of martyrdom, the company of Saints, by divine power, cast down the darkness of spiritual tyrants utterly, and obtained glory.

Theotokion:

By joy Thou hast loosed sorrow, having given birth unto our joy, the Giver of life and Deliverer, O Most-pure Theotokos: Whom earnestly entreat to save our souls.

Another Canon to the Forerunner.

Tone 4, Same Heirmos.

The bow of the mighty is broken, and the weak have girded themselves with strength; therefore my heart is magnified in the Lord.

Thou hast fulfilled every virtue, and every malice hast thou hated and cast away, and shown forth the narrow path of repentance, O blessed one; thou hast shown forth the Word incarnate, O great Forerunner: therefore I pray thee, deliver me from irrational passions, guiding me unto good passionlessness.

Having lived sacredly in the body, thou didst show forth the life of the Bodiless Powers, O Forerunner: establish me by thy prayers to become like unto him, O God-bearer!

Theotokion:

Mercy was shown unto me through Thee, who through transgression became unprofitable, O Virgin Mother: therefore with songs I call Thee blessed as is meet.

Ode 4. Heirmos:

I heard, O God, Thy report, and was afraid; I understood Thy works, said the Prophet, and was terrified, O Lord, for the earth was filled with Thy praise.

I was stripped of virtue, and [f. 116rB] clothed with malice, and I am full of judgment, O Jesus, Lover of mankind: enlighten me with divine garments!

Sailing across the water of the worldly sea, O Word: through slothfulness I fell into danger by bodily pleasures; guide me unto the harbor of repentance!

Martyricon:

Having truly cleansed all the filth of godlessness, the noble Martyrs, by the divine power of endurance, granted salvation unto all.

Martyricon:

Being rolled upon the ground like stones, O Passion-bearers, ye utterly overthrew the strongholds of deceit, and attained the city on high.

Theotokion:

Thee, our salvation, at every time and place do I invoke: despise me not, O all-immaculate one, who didst bear God, the Deliverer and Savior of us all.

Another Canon to the Forerunner.[^179]

Tone 4. Heirmos: For love's sake, O Compassionate One:

Having known thee as a turtledove, announcing the springtime of truth unto the world with most honorable words, we ever call thee blessed, O glorious Forerunner!

Renew me who am crushed by deceitful crushings, O Forerunner, as thou art the mediator between the Old and the New, who sing of thee!

O thou who didst dwell in the desert with blameless life: renew my mind, desolated by all manner of transgressions, with divine prayers, O Forerunner!

Theotokion:

Thy Son, O Virgin, was known as cleansing and deliverance for us: pray unto Him to save those who glorify Thee with compunction of soul.

[f. 116vA] Ode 5. Heirmos:

Shine forth upon me, O Lord, the light of Thy commandments; for early in the morning my spirit seeks Thee, O Christ, and sings unto Thee. For Thou art our God, and unto Thee have I fled, O King of peace!

I who have come naked into human life, and am darkened by the deceitful commandments of the deceiver: O Jesus, have compassion on me, and guide me unto the light of the life of repentance!

My heart was lifted up by the assaults of the serpent, and fell with a great fall; O Jesus, the restoration of the fallen, raise me up and save me, for the sake of Thy many compassions!

Martyricon:

With drops of blood ye extinguished the furnace of the deceit of polytheism, O blessed ones, and with showers of healings ye ever quench the flame of passions, O Sufferers of the Savior!

Martyricon:

Standing before the judgment-seat, scraped with claws, and pelted with stones, O Martyrs: though a multitude of fierce torments drew near, ye remained unbent by divine beckoning.

Theotokion:

Shine forth upon me, O Lady, the ray of Thy tender mercy, who am in the darkness of my transgressions, O Virgin, and guide me unto the light of repentance, O Most-pure One, that in faith I may sing of Thee.

Another Canon to the Forerunner.

Tone 4. Heirmos: Thy light, O Lord:

Burnt with the coal of the desert, and inflamed by the assaults of passions, O child of the desert: bedew me with thy prayers, and keep me unharmed by injury.

By the holy right hand of thy baptism, O divine and all-blessed right hand of the Father, [f. 116vB] which saves us from the hand of the deceiver: give ear through holy intercessions!

As a refuge, a mighty protection, and a great rampart doth the whole world possess thee, O Forerunner: deliver us by thy prayers from every distress!

Theotokion:

God loved the beauty of Jacob, O Virgin Maiden, Who through Thee adorned all things that of old were darkened by transgression.

Ode 6. Heirmos:

In the deep of life I tossed upon the waves of my soul; but like Jonah from the whale, thus I cry: "From the depth of my evils lead me up, I pray, O Savior God, and Word!"

Through the slumber of neglect I have weighed down my wretched soul, and have fallen into sin: raise me up unto the light of repentance, O Lord, and by Thy tender mercy save me!

How did I fall, wretch that I am? How did I depart from the All-good God? How do I not grasp in feeling that terrible judgment-seat whereon I must be condemned? O my Creator, have compassion on me!

Martyricon:

Ye were revealed as citharas, sounding forth a saving voice unto us, delighting the hearts of the faithful, and utterly driving away the drunkenness of deceit, O enlightened Sufferers!

Martyricon:

Having surpassed human bounds, O Martyrs of Christ, looking unto the Creator with honorable gaze: ye endured the pains of torments rejoicing, as in foreign bodies.

Theotokion:

O all-immaculate Virgin, [f. 117rA] protectress and shelter unto all the faithful: stand forth and deliver me from future judgment, and from the terrible tribunal in the hour of judgment, that in faith I may ever praise Thee.

Another Canon to the Forerunner.

Tone 4, Same Heirmos.

I came into the deep of the sea, and the tempest of my many transgressions overwhelmed me; but as God, lead up my life from corruption, O Plenteous in mercy!

Standing and baptizing in the streams Him Who takes away the sins of men: cease not to pray unto Him, O Forerunner, to have compassion and save our souls!

Thou wast revealed as a preacher of repentance: keep my heart from being defiled by harmful sins, O Forerunner, having no uprising!

Thou didst cry aloud, O blessed one, unto the deserts of unfruitful souls, concerning the coming of the Word: therefore with unceasing voices every Church calls thee blessed.

The law changed types by Thy fearful childbearing, O Bride of God: beholding now its concealment, O Lady, we honor Thee as is meet.

Ode 7. Heirmos:[^180]

The children of Abraham, having not bowed down unto the golden image, being unconsumed like gold in the furnace, danced in the fiery furnace as in a radiant bridal chamber, singing: "Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!"

Thou didst appear as a young child, willing to deliver the world from ancient condemnation, O Christ, as Thou art tender-hearted. Therefore I cry: Renew me now, who have grown old through many sins, O Compassionate One, and save me as I sing: "Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!"

[f. 117rB] O Thou Who didst once save Manasseh when he repented, and didst show compassion on the harlot and justify her through tears: save me who have committed many and fierce sins, and receive me as I cry: "Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!"

Martyricon:

When the fierce tempest of polytheism held the universe, making piety your ship, O Passion-bearers, steered by Christ, ye reached the harbor, crying: "Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!"

Having blossomed openly like gold in the furnace through unsparing torments, O Sufferers, and appeared as precious seals of the Sufferings of Christ: ye are now hidden in heavenly treasuries for much confirmation.

Theotokion:

Having borne the Son and God, the Deliverer and Master in the flesh, O Most-pure Lady: ever pray unto Him, O Most-pure One, that we may receive deliverance from fierce deeds and remission of our many sins, who glorify His mercies that are beyond mind.

Another Canon to the Forerunner.

Tone 4. Heirmos: The children of Abraham of old:

Greater than all born of women wast thou revealed, O Forerunner: deliver me who sin greatly from the great flame and eternal darkness, through thy greatest prayer!

The barren fig tree was revealed, and fearing cutting down: establish me by thine intercession, O Forerunner of the Word, and make me fruitful!

[f. 117vA] that I may call thee blessed.

Put to sleep every tempest of the enemy stirred up against him who flees unto thee in faith, by thy vigilant prayers unto the Deliverer of all, O Forerunner John!

Theotokion:

From the assault of the evil one, and his portion, O Virgin, and from demonic servitude, deliver Thy servants, who with soul and tongue ever glorify Thee.

Ode 8. Heirmos:

In fiery flame the Cherubim and Seraphim stand before Thee, O Lord, and all creation sings unto Thee a fair song: Sing, bless, and exalt Christ, the only Creator, unto all ages, ye people!

I remained not in Thy fear, I listened not unto Thy commandments, and I never submitted unto Thy will. What shall become of me, wretch that I am? O Thou Who art the Lover of mankind, have compassion on me freely, O Savior, and cast me not away!

O Good Husbandman, I cry unto Thee: with the sickle of Thy fear reap from the roots all the thorny thoughts of my wretched soul, and grant me to sprout the seed of repentance, O Christ, a saved wheat-ear!

Martyricon:

Widened by grace, the Passion-bearers distressed in wounds narrowed the paths full of snares for the enemy; and now they guide us unto the paths of God in faith and love.

Martyricon:

The deceiver was taken, falling into the depths of your endurance and suffering, O Martyrs; and the foolish one lies mocked by all, [f. 117vB] while ye are adorned with crowns of victory!

Theotokion:

Thy womb, O all-immaculate one, was shown to be from the honorable threshing-floor, bearing unto the world the Wheat of life, which feeds all things. Therefore we, the faithful, call Thee blessed as is meet.

Another Canon to the Forerunner.

Tone 4, Same Heirmos.

O Almighty Deliverer of all: descending into the midst of the flame, Thou didst bedew the pious ones, and didst teach them to sing: "Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and exalt Him unto all ages!"

Held fast by the sleep of despondency, and darkened by the gloom of malice: set me upright by thy radiant prayer, O Forerunner, and grant me to walk decorously in virtues as in the day!

The winter of temptations holds me, and the tempest of passions troubles me: stretch forth thy hand unto me, O Forerunner, guiding the ship of my soul unto the harbor of repentance by thy prayers!

Thou didst baptize in the streams of the river Him Who takes away the sins of the world: dry up the abyss of my evils through the efforts of thy prayers, O blessed John the Forerunner!

Having seen the Holy Spirit, thou didst hear the Father's voice bearing witness, O Forerunner, unto Jesus ineffably baptized by thee: Whom pray to save us!

Theotokion:

As the fountain of our renewal, renew me wholly who am crushed by the assaults of the serpent, that with faith and love I may call Thee blessed, O all-immaculate Virgin Theotokos!

[f. 118rA] Ode 9. Heirmos:

He hath showed strength with His arm; He hath put down the mighty from their seats, and exalted them of low degree, the God of Israel; whereby the Dayspring from on high hath visited us, and hath guided us into the way of peace.

Behold, the mystical bridal chamber is opened: come, having adorned your lamps with the oil of virtues, and go forth radiant. Put off the sleep of despondency from thy soul, that thou mayest enter with Christ, bearing radiance!

Like the harlot holding Thy feet in thought, and washing them with tears, O Word: wash me, O Savior, from the darkness of passions! "Thy faith hath saved thee": say now unto me also, that I may sing of Thy countless tender mercy!

Martyricon:

With merry heart and joyful soul the Martyrs dwell on high, bearing the wounds of Christ like beautiful adornment; and they ask peace for us, deliverance from fierce deeds, and remission of transgressions.

Martyricon:

Every place that hath your relics, O Sufferers, like another ark of Israel, is delivered from evils; the heavens rejoice with the honorable Angels, having gained your souls, O blessed ones!

Theotokion:

O comely Maiden, who didst bear the comely God: I cry unto Thee, bless my soul that is fiercely harmed by passions and the assaults of wicked demons, that in faith I may sing of Thee, the hope of all!

Another Canon to the Forerunner.

Tone 4, Same Heirmos:

[f. 118rB] Eve indeed, through the disease of disobedience, brought in the curse; but Thou, O Virgin Theotokos, through the blossoming of Thy childbearing, didst bud forth blessing unto the world. Therefore we all magnify Thee.

Christ the Lord is my strength and song: pray unto Him, O blessed Forerunner, to strengthen me against passions and every demonic assault, doing the divine will, that I may ever glorify thee with love!

A fair Turtledove and sweet-speaking Swallow wast thou revealed, O divine Forerunner, announcing the divine spring, Christ: Whom pray to deliver me from the soul-corrupting winter and the storm of sin, through thine intercessions!

Leaping in the maternal womb, thou didst announce Him Who shone forth from the Virgin: pray unto Him to put to death my bodily leapings that mortify me, and to fill my heart with joy, that I may sing of thee, O divine Forerunner!

Judgment is without mercy, O soul, unto those who show no mercy; look and attend, receive oil that can keep thy lamp unquenched; the Bridegroom draws near: be watchful, that thou mayest have an unquenchable resolve!

Theotokion:

O blessed Theotokos, who didst bear the blessed God: pray unto Him to deliver me from all malice, and make my heart zealous for Him, hating bodily voluptuousness, that in hymns I may magnify Thee!

[f. 118vA] AT THE APOSTICHA, STICHERA

Penitential, Tone 4.

Wash me with my tears, O Savior, for I am defiled with many sins; therefore I fall down before Thee: I have sinned, have mercy on me, O God!

I am a sheep of Thy rational flock, and I flee unto Thee, the Good Shepherd; seek me out who have gone astray, O God, and have mercy on me.

Martyricon:

Ye became partakers with the Angels, O holy Martyrs, courageously confessing Christ before the tribunal. For ye left all the fair things of the world as though they were not, and held fast the faith as a firm hope. Therefore, having driven away deceit, ye pour forth gifts of healing unto the faithful, unceasingly praying that our souls may be saved.

Glory... Both now... Theotokion:

Preserve Thy servants from all evils, O blessed Theotokos, that we may glorify Thee, the hope of our souls!

ON TUESDAY, THE BEATITUDES.[^181]

Tone 4.

Through the tree Adam was cast out of Paradise; but through the tree of the Cross the thief dwelt in Paradise. For the one, having tasted, transgressed the commandment of Him Who made him; but the other, being crucified with Thee, confessed Thee as the hidden God, crying aloud: "Remember me in Thy kingdom!"

O Christ, Who didst accept the weeping of Peter, and the tears of the harlot, and the mere sigh of the publican, having had compassion as Thou art merciful: have mercy also on me who fall down [f. 118vB] and ask forgiveness of transgressions, O All-good Lord, and deliver me from eternal torment!

O great Forerunner, who didst loose the bonds of barrenness: destroy the barrenness of my humble heart, and by thine intercession make it bring forth assemblies of virtuous deeds, whereby I may receive unfailing food, crying evermore: "Remember me, O Lord, when Thou comest into Thy kingdom!"

Martyricon:

Crushed by torments, strangled with ropes, pressed down, O wise ones, cast into the deep of the sea, O all-glorious Martyrs, burned with fire, and scraped with sharp bones: ye denied not God; therefore ask peace, enlightenment, and great mercy for us, O holy ones!

Glory... Triadicon:

The Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit: let all we faithful pray worthily to glorify with one mind the Unity of the Godhead, existing in three Hypostases, abiding unmingled, simple, indivisible, and unapproachable, whereby we are delivered from the fiery torment.

Both now... Theotokion:

Thou didst receive in Thy womb Him Who is co-beginningless with the Father and co-enthroned with the Holy Spirit, and beyond mind and word didst bear Him Who became man through benevolence toward mankind, O Mary, Bride of God, spacious dwelling-place of our God: Whom earnestly entreat to save us!

## TUESDAY EVENING VESPERS (FOR WEDNESDAY) (TONE 4)

[f. 119rA] ON TUESDAY EVENING, AT "LORD, I HAVE CRIED":[^182]

*Stichera of the Cross, Tone 4.*

*Podoben: "As one valiant among martyrs" (Я҆́кѡ до́бля):*

Lifted up upon the Cross, pierced with a spear, and reddening Thy fingers with blood, O Christ: Thou didst write our freedom, O All-good One, and didst tear up the handwriting against our forefather Adam, and didst set free the human race. Therefore we praise Thine understanding-transcending goodness, O Compassionate One!

We praise Thy sufferings, O Master Jesus: the Cross, the Spear, the Reed, the Nails, the Sponge, the Purple Robe, the Crown of thorns, the spitting, and the mocking, which Thou didst endure willingly; we magnify Thy harmlessness, O only Giver of life, Thy long-suffering, and in faith we glorify Thee, O Lover of mankind!

We bow down before Thy precious Cross, O All-good One, kissing it with love, and I glorify Thy descent that is beyond mind, Thy boundless mercy, Thine ineffable compassions, and Thy rich goodness, therefore Thou didst save human nature held fast in the darkness of transgressions. Glory to Thy Crucifixion, O Christ!

Other Stichera to the Most-holy Mother of God.

*Tone 4.*

*Podoben: "The same" (то́йже):*

When she beheld Thee nailed upon the Cross, O Lord, the Ewe-lamb and Thy Mother marveled, crying aloud: "What a sight is this, O my beloved Son?

[f. 119rB] Is this what the disobedient and lawless assembly repays unto Thee, which enjoyed Thy many wonders? But glory to Thine ineffable condescension, O Master!"

When the Ewe-lamb who bore Thee beheld Thee, the Lamb and Shepherd, upon the tree, she wept and maternally said unto Thee: "O most-beloved Son, how art Thou lifted up upon the tree of the Cross, O Long-suffering One? How are Thy hands and feet nailed by the lawless, O Word, and Thou didst pour out Thy blood, O Master?"

When the Virgin and Thy Mother saw Thee hanging upon the Cross, O Lord, she marveled and weeping said: "What have they repaid unto Thee, who enjoyed Thy many gifts, O Master? But I pray Thee: leave me not alone in the world, but hasten to rise, raising up our forefather with Thyself!"

Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion:

To: Called from on high:

Weep not for Me, O Mother, beholding hanging upon the tree Thy Son and God, Who suspended the earth upon the waters and created all creation! Behold, I will arise and be glorified, and will crush the kingdoms of hades with power, and destroy its might, and deliver those bound from its malice, as I am tender-hearted, [f. 119vA] and will bring them unto My Father, as I am the Lover of mankind!

AT THE APOSTICHA, STICHERA

Of the Cross, Tone 4.

An invincible weapon hast Thou given unto us, O Christ, Thy Cross, and thereby we conquer the assaults of the stranger. Ever having Thy Cross for our help, O Christ, we easily trample upon the snares of the enemy.

Martyricon:

Having boldness before the Savior, O holy ones: unceasingly pray for us sinners, asking remission of transgressions and great mercy for our souls.

Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion:

To: As one noble:

Beholding Thee crucified, and Thy side pierced with a spear, O Most-pure One, Christ the Lover of mankind: weeping, she cried aloud: "What is this, O my Son? What have the ungrateful people repaid unto Thee for the good things Thou didst for them? And art Thou in haste to make me childless, O Most-beloved One? I marvel at Thy voluntary crucifixion, O Compassionate One!"

## WEDNESDAY MATINS: THE PRECIOUS CROSS AND THE THEOTOKOS (TONE 4)

ON WEDNESDAY AT MATINS.[^183]

After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymns.

Of the Cross, Tone 4.

Thou hast redeemed us from the curse of the law by Thy precious Blood; being nailed to the Cross and pierced with a spear, Thou didst pour forth immortality unto mankind: O our Savior, glory to Thee!

The Jews nailed Thee to the Cross, O Savior, Who didst summon us from corruption, O Christ our God; Thou didst stretch forth Thy palms upon it of Thine own will, [f. 119vB] and wast pleased to be pierced in Thy side with a spear, according to the multitude of Thy compassions, O only Lover of mankind.

Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion:

When Thine immaculate Mother saw Thee lifted up upon the Cross, weeping maternally, she cried aloud: "What is this new and strange wonder, O my Son? How doth the lawless assembly nail Thee to the Cross, O Life of all, my sweetest Light?"

After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns.

Of the Cross, Tone 4.

Swiftly anticipate, before we are enslaved to the enemies who blaspheme Thee and threaten us, O Christ our God; destroy by Thy Cross those who war against us, that they may know how mighty is the faith of the Orthodox, through the prayers of the Theotokos, O only Lover of mankind.

Nailed upon the Cross on Golgotha, O Master, of Thine own will Thou didst heal my ancient wound of sin, according to the greatness of Thy goodness. For Thou didst submit Thyself willingly as man, O our Savior, for the sake of the human race, and from Thy side didst pour out blood and water for those who sing of Thee in faith.

Martyricon:

Having struggled nobly by the power of the Cross, ye mightily cast down the adversary enemy by your endurance, O holy Passion-bearers. Therefore, celebrating your memory in blood, we are healed by the operation and grace of the All-holy Spirit. By your prayers, O sacred warriors of Christ: pray unto the Savior for the world!

[f. 120rA] Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion:

The Virgin and Ewe-lamb, beholding upon the Cross the Lamb Who was born of her without seed, and pierced with a spear, wounded with the arrows of grief, cried out, exclaiming with anguish: "What is this new mystery? How dost Thou die, Who alone art the Lord of life? Therefore arise, raising up our fallen forefather!"

After the 3rd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns.

Of the Cross, Tone 4.

When I had bitterly fallen in Paradise through the evil counsel of the murderer of man: Thou didst lift me up again on the place of the Cross, O Christ, healing by the tree the curse of the tree, having slain the serpent who through deceit put me to death, and Thou didst grant me divine life: glory to Thy divine Crucifixion, O Lord!

Having recognized Thee hanging upon the tree, O Christ, the Sun of righteousness: the sun darkened its light, and creation was shaken; and the dead arose swiftly from the tombs as from sleep, O Word, singing of the majesty of Thy glory by divine power.

Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion:

O all-immaculate Virgin, Mother of Christ God: a sword pierced Thy most-holy soul when Thou didst behold Thy Son and God crucified of His own will: Whom, O all-blessed one, unceasingly pray to grant remission of our transgressions!

CANON, to the Precious and Life-giving Cross of the Lord.[^184]

Composition of Joseph.

Tone 4, Ode 1. Heirmos:

[f. 120rB] Traversing of old the deep of the Red Sea with dry feet, Israel, with Moses' hands stretched out crosswise, vanquished the might of Amalek in the wilderness.

Thou Who didst stretch out the heaven, O Jesus, didst stretch out Thy palms, gathering brightly unto Thyself the nations that had departed far from Thee, as Thou art God and merciful.

Surround me with Thy Cross, O my Christ, that I may not become the prey of the wolf, O Word, who seeks my perdition and prepares to devour and swallow me every day!

Martyricon:

By sufferings ye overthrew the author of sufferings, and now ye enjoy life free from suffering; and ye ever lighten every disease of our souls and bodies, O blessed ones!

Martyricon:

By patient bonds ye bound the manifold-cunning one, O blessed Martyrs, being bound willingly for the sake of Christ, and having loosed all deceit. Therefore ye are worthily called blessed!

Theotokion:

Thou didst remain a Virgin even after childbearing, for Thou didst bear God, O Most-pure One, Who was lifted up upon the Cross and raised up the earthborn. Therefore in faith we all magnify Thee with a loud voice.

Another Canon to the Most-holy Mother of God.

Same Heirmos.

As Thou art truly more honorable and holy than all creation, O Most-pure One: my heart, defiled fiercely with unclean passions [f. 120vA] with Thy pure prayer, O Theotokos, cleanse!

Deliver me from tears and sighings, which await me at the dread future Judgment, by Thy God-pleasing entreaties, O Virgin Mother and [Mother of] our God.

As Thou alone beyond mind by Thy childbearing didst free the human race from the curse: me who am enslaved to carnal passions, O Most-pure One, free by Thine intercessions.

Ode 3. Heirmos:[^185]

Thy Church doth rejoice in Thee, [O Christ...]:

Lifted up upon the Cross: Thou didst raise up those cast down into corruption, and didst cast down the enemy, as Thou art Christ our God.

The enemy's sword was blunted when Thou wast pierced in the side with a spear, and Eden was opened: O Co-consubstantial Word of the Father.

Martyricon:

The fiery rivers, the deceptive streams the Martyrs stopped, and extinguished the flame of polytheism.

Martyricon:

Being crucified and scraped with claws, O Martyrs of Christ: ye slew the serpent enemy with the sword of endurance.

Beholding Thee, the spotless Ewe-lamb, lifted up upon the Cross, mournfully lamenting, O Master: praising Thy dominion.

Another Canon. Heirmos:

Not in wisdom, nor in power, nor in riches do we boast: but in Thine, O Father, hypostatic Wisdom of God: for there is none holy save Thee, O Lover of mankind.

More exalted than the Cherubim, I pray Thee, O Lady: show my mind that hath fallen into [f. 120vB] the serpent's snares, to have departed from carnal passions.

At the dread scrutiny, when the Lord will judge me who have sinned much: may I find Thee, O all-immaculate one, delivering me from condemnation.

By Thy compassions transform my unmerciful ways by Thine intercessions, O Christ: and me who am unmerciful, save, by the supplications of Her who bore Thee.

Ode 4. Heirmos:

Beholding Thee lifted up [upon the Cross...]:

Beholding Thee willingly lifted up upon the tree, the sun of the Sun of glory was clad in darkness, and the rocks were split, and the veil of the temple was rent in twain.

When Thou wast crucified and pierced with a spear, O Lord, the weapon turned back, giving its back at Thy command; the wise thief hymns Thy dominion.

Martyricon:

Armed with the weapon of Thy Cross, Thy Passion-bearers, O Lord: were shown unwounded by the arrow of malice, and destroyed the unstable walls of the idols.

Martyricon:

As spotless sheep, in sacrifices and spiritual oblations, O Martyrs of the Lord, ye were brought unto Him Who was crowned for our youth, receiving the recompense of sufferings.

Theotokion:

Having in time brought forth the Timeless One, and alone having obtained virginity spotless: when She beheld the Lord lifted up upon the tree, Her soul was rent with griefs.

Another Canon. Same Heirmos:

Thou only dwelling-place of the divine Sanctification, which was not emptied in bestowing grace upon [f. 121rA] His creation, O Most-pure One: sanctify my soul, and enlighten my mind.

My mind being overwhelmed by every wind of malice, and all cruel storms: strengthen it by Thine intercessions, O Lady, and snatch me from assaults.

Theotokion:

O Virgin Palace of the Temple, adorned with grace, now I pray Thee: show me, who have become a den of thieves, to be the house of the Holy Trinity by Thine intercessions.

Ode 5. Heirmos:[^186]

Thou, O Lord, art my light, [Who camest into the world...]:

When Thy side was pierced, O Master, Thou didst pour forth for me divine streams of incorruption, for him who slipped into corruption through the transgression of the rib.

Thy precious Cross is victory over enemies, which Thou hast given unto us, O Word, and for the salvation of the souls of those who sing unto Thee in faith.

Martyricon:

Together with fiery ministers, mortals have now been joined: having passed through material fire, the great Martyrs, as most-radiant Sufferers.

Martyricon:

While the flesh was dissolving through many sufferings, the Martyrs' love of soul toward the Creator was confirmed unbroken.

Theotokion:

He Who alone is good, having entered Thy womb incorruptibly, O Most-pure One, was manifest incarnate and was crucified, that He might deliver us from corruption.

Another Canon. Heirmos:

The ungodly shall not see Thy glory, [O Christ...]:

O Ewe-lamb, who didst bear the Lamb of God: seek out my soul that hath been deceived by the serpent's deceit, and that wanders upon [f. 121rB] the mountains through transgression, O Lady.

By Thy warm prayer, O ever-Virgin Lady: vouchsafe my soul, which freezes in cruel frost, to draw near in piety unto the warmth of the Creator of divine love.

Thou who alone art good and spotless among women, O Pure One: free my wretched soul from passionate blemish, and dispose me to live purely by Thine intercessions.

Preserve my soul as the apple of Thine eye, O Most-pure One, under the cover of Thy wings, O Good One, and deliver me from the torment of spiritual wickedness and from torments.

Ode 6. Heirmos:

I will sacrifice unto Thee with the voice of praise, O Lord:

Thou Who art greater than all magnificent honor didst endure to be dishonored, that Thou mightest honor me who was evilly dishonored, and save me by the Cross.

Thou wast dead indeed, lifted up upon the tree: but make dead the slayer of my soul, who is now full of all shame, O my Creator, as I sing of Thy power.

Martyricon:

Wounded with incurable torments, O all-glorious ones: and by your fingernails, O Martyrs, the wounded enemy was cast down, and is seen put to shame by faith.

Martyricon:

The dust of the Martyrs' relics lying in the tomb works sleep-granting rest, and blows away the demons like dust, and heals diverse sicknesses.

Theotokion:

The lawless assembly nailed Thee with nails, and the Virgin lamented, crying [f. 121vA] [...now] with a sword I rend my heart, O my Son!' the Virgin cried aloud with tears.

Another Canon. Same Heirmos:

Thy childbearing was the destroyer of death, O Virgin, and life and redemption unto those put to death. Therefore I pray Thee: resurrect my dead soul!

Stretch forth a hand of help unto me, O Lover of mankind, who am tossed on the tempest of life: through the supplications of Thy Mother and the higher immaterial Powers.

O Field that didst sprout forth the heavenly Wheat: despise not my weakened soul, languishing from famine of divine deeds, but nourish it with God's grace.

Lull to sleep the passionate movements of the body and my carnal wantonness; calm my mind as a rest, having put it to sleep with the slumber of Thy prayers, O Pure One.

Ode 7. Heirmos:[^187]

In the furnace the Abrahamic Children [trampled the flame...]:

Desiring to be crucified naked upon the tree, O only Immortal One, Who clothest the heaven with clouds: Thou clothest in eternal shame him who of old stripped the forefather naked.

Thou wast lifted up upon the Cross, and fallen Adam arose. When Thou wast pierced in the ribs with a spear, O Master, the crafty one received a mortal wound. Blessed is Thy dominion, O Lord!

Martyricon:

Most fairly united unto the most fair Word, O all-lauded Sufferers, ye were separated from the world, being burned and crushed, and [f. 121vB] ever tripping up the enemy.

Martyricon:

Ye cast down the fortifications of deceptive walls by your sacred sufferings, O glorious Sufferers: and became a wall, fortress, and protector unto the faithful who piously glorify you.

Theotokion:

As the dew in the furnace cooled the youths, O Virgin Maiden, and in no wise burned Thy womb, so when Thou didst see Christ hanging upon the tree, Thou didst praise His condescension which transcends the mind.

Another Canon. Same Heirmos:

O divine Mountain from which the Stone was cut, O Maiden, which crushed the idols of the idolatrous: heal my sculpted soul, and drive away the stony perplexity of my heart.

O unshakable Maiden, who didst receive in Thy midst Him Who by His glance shakes the earth, and now when He wills shakes us: therefore strengthen me who am shaken by the enemy's assaults.

Casting down my carnal mindsets, show me, O Theotokos, wholly spiritual, adorned with virtues: whom the all-cunning one darkened through the unseemliness of pleasures.

O divine Lily of mercy and goodness, pour forth abundantly the wealth of Thy compassions: and washing away the filth of my transgressions, quench the carnal inflammation.

Ode 8. Heirmos:

Daniel, stretching out his hands, [stopped the mouths of the lions in the pit...]:

Stretching out Thy palms upon the Cross, O Good One, desiring to heal the unrestrained hands of our transgressions, Thou wast nailed with nails, O Lord [f. 122rA] [...for him who cried]:[^188] 'Remember me, crying in Thy kingdom!'

Nailed upon the Cross, O Christ, Goodness of many wounds, pierced in the side, Thou didst pour forth two streams of remission; and the earth, not enduring to see the boldness, shook; the rocks were split, the sun was darkened, the mountains and hills trembled. Glory to Thy dominion!

The hands of the forefather formerly stretched out unrestrainedly toward the food of the tree, Thou didst make right, O Christ, their slip, stretching out Thyself willingly, and Thy hands were nailed, O Long-suffering One, Who didst fashion man with Thy hand, for the sake of Thine immeasurable goodness. Glory to Thine arrangement which transcends the mind!

Martyricon:

Like blazing lands, O holy ones, by the most-radiant beams of your honorable struggles, whereby ye destroyed all the darkness of vanity, and dwelt in the unwaning Light, being [f. 122rB] deified by participation, and ye illumine all with spiritual light who worthily call you blessed.

Glory... Triadicon:

Rendering praise, glory, and honor unto the all-causing Trinity, and offering with thrice-holy voices the angelic song unto the beginningless Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, we lift up the voice of the wise thief, singing and crying aloud unto It: 'Remember us in Thy kingdom!'

Both now... Theotokion:

Beholding Her Son and God willingly lifted up upon the Cross, the Most-pure One marveled, weeping and saying unto Him Who adorned all things: 'Whither hath Thy beauty set, O Lord? What is this that the ungrateful assembly hath repaid unto Thee instead of good things? I sing of Thy goodness which transcends the mind!'

## WEDNESDAY EVENING VESPERS (FOR THURSDAY) (TONE 4)

ON WEDNESDAY EVENING, AT 'LORD, I HAVE CRIED':[^189]

*Stichera to the Holy Apostles, Tone 4.*

*Podoben: "As one valiant among martyrs" (Я҆́кѡ до́бля):*

Strongest in mind, the holy ones, taking the field against the alignment of the cunning one, armed with the whole weapon of the spiritual word: ye destroyed all demonic might, and cut down human souls like roots. Therefore unto the ages we honor your weapons.

The net of faith stretched out in cruciform manner, the Twelve of Thy divine Apostles: drew all nations unto Thy comprehension, O Christ, and drove away the salty sea of passions. Therefore I pray Thee: lead me up from the depth of transgressions, through their all-acceptable supplications.

[f. 122vA] Let us hymn the glorious Twelve of the Apostles: Peter and Paul, preachers of Christ, Bartholomew, James, Andrew, Simon, and Matthew, with Luke, John, and Mark together, with Philip and Thomas let us praise, and the other Seventy let us honor, as the Savior's well-pleasers.

*Other Stichera to Saint Nicholas, Tone 4.*

*Podoben: "The same" (то́йже):*

With divine myrrh the divine spiritual grace anointed thee, and as primate of Myra, anointing the ends of the world with most-sacred virtues, driving away stinking passions with fragrant prayers: therefore in faith we glorify thee, and we honor thy grace, O Saint Nicholas.

As an unquenchable luminary, and as a universal lampstand, shining upon the firmament of the Church, O glorious one, enlightening the world, driving away the mist of cruel tribulations, embracing the winter of griefs, and granting profound tranquility: worthily we call thee blessed, O Nicholas.

Thy most-glorious life everywhere showed thee exceedingly fair, O God-wise one, most sacred ornament of hierarchs and adornment of ways, spreading forth beams upon the earth like the sun, and thou didst enlighten the hearts of the faithful who celebrate thy light-bearing and divine memory, O all-blessed Nicholas.

Glory... Both now... Theotokion:

[f. 122vB] From every unconfessed sin and crafty snaring deliver me, O all-immaculate one, and bridle the raging of passions, I pray: drive away the mist and darkening of my mind, and guide me unto the harbor of the divine commandments of Thy Son, O Mother of God, that unceasingly I may honor Thee.

AT THE APOSTICHA, STICHERA

To the Apostles, Tone 4.

The choir of the Apostles Thou didst enlighten with the Holy Spirit, O Christ; and through them wash away our sinful filth, O Lord, and have mercy on us.

Unlettered disciples the Holy Spirit showed forth as teachers, O Christ God; and by the much-speaking melodious harmony of tongues, Thou didst abolish deception, as Thou art all-powerful.

Martyricon:

Living sacrifices, rational whole burnt offerings, Martyrs of the Lord, perfect slaughters of God, sheep knowing God and known by God, whose sheepfold cannot be entered by the wolf: by your prayers may our hearts be shepherded beside waters of rest.

Glory... Both now... Theotokion:

Having Thee, O Theotokos, as our hope and protectress, we fear not the enemy's assaults, for Thou savest our souls.

## THURSDAY MATINS: THE HOLY APOSTLES AND ST. NICHOLAS (TONE 4)

ON THURSDAY AT MATINS.[^190]

After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymns.

To the Apostles, Tone 4.

As luminaries unto the ends of the earth Thou didst reveal Thy disciples, O Christ, by the mystery of preaching, enlightening souls in darkness, and the dark idolatrous deception [f. 123rA] [...taking away] all understanding of the first-fashioned from the passionate, as I sing:[^191] Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing and exalt Him supremely unto all ages!

The handwriting of the first-fashioned Adam is torn up by the piercing of Thy divine ribs; and with drops of blood, O Master, the whole earth is sanctified, crying unceasingly with voices of thanksgiving: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing and exalt Him supremely unto all ages!

Martyricon:

Standing in the midst of fire, as though bedewed and not burned, the all-glorious Martyrs, singing in mysterious voice the children's truly divine song: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing and exalt Him supremely unto all ages!

Martyricon:

Enduring the unstable fire by their own free will, the Martyrs were not shaken by the darkness of torments; but being strengthened by the Cross, they ran unto the unwaning Light, crying: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing and exalt Him supremely unto all ages!

Theotokion:

Beholding Christ put to death, O all-hymned Lady, Who put to death the enemy that had slain mankind, falling down and weeping like a spring, and marveling at His long-suffering, She cried aloud: 'Woe is me, my Son, how dost Thou die, O Immortal Life?'

Another Canon. Same Heirmos:

A fruit of life didst Thou bear, O Lady, by which the poison of death perished. Therefore I cry unto Thee: me who am slain by the fruit of sin, graciously [f. 123rB] quicken as I sing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing and exalt Him supremely unto all ages!

Lull the passionate movement of my mind by Thine unsleeping prayer, O Most-pure Lady, and raise me up from the sleep of slothfulness, to sing in spiritual vigilance: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing and exalt Him supremely unto all ages!

Tear up the bonds of my transgressions, and calm the bodily uprisings, O Theotokos; destroy evil thoughts, and quickly cleanse Thy servant from secret imaginations, O protectress and defense of all the faithful!

Fear not, O my wretched soul, the darkness of slander of those who slander my countless evil deeds; therefore repent, and take the only Most-pure One as an ally unto good, for She is the refuge of mankind!

Ode 9. Heirmos:

The stone cut without hands from the mountain:

Behold, Life hanging upon the Cross hath appeared unto all; the sun, not enduring it, withholds its beam, and the earth shakes, and thoughts are confirmed in the purity of piety.

How doth the lawless assembly condemn Thee, my Jesus, the Lawgiver, to die upon the tree: Who art the Life and Lord of all, and Who through sufferings bestows incorruptible impassibility upon all mankind!

With your blessed mouths, O all-wise ones, ye proclaimed the incarnation of the Word: in the midst of the lawless enemies, O all-praised ones [f. 123vA] [...and sacredly] having suffered, ye were crowned with crowns of victory.

As luminaries, the daystars, ye enlighten all creation with the radiances of sacred sufferings, and with divine splendors of healings, and ye dispel the deep night of passions, O divine Martyrs.

Enlighten my soul, O Pure One, darkened by sin, and drive away the clouds of my evils, O Cloud of Light, who of old didst behold the darkened sun when the Immortal One was crucified.

Another Canon. Same Heirmos:

Break asunder the bonds of my evils, by the divine spear of Thy Son, and loose my wretched soul, chained and in distress: and lead it unto the love of God, O Virgin Mother of our God.

O Virgin wider than the heavens, my heart being exceedingly straitened by the action of the cunning one: lead it out unto the breadth of impassibility, ever strengthening me to walk upon the narrow path.

That I may glorify Thee, O truly glorious Virgin, deliver me from great sinful irrationality: and make me a partaker of heavenly glory, who flee unto Thy mercy.

Stop all the counsels of those armed against us, O Mother of God the Most-high, and fill with joy those who trust in Thee, that fervently we all may proclaim Thy protection.

AT THE APOSTICHA, STICHERA

Of the Cross, Tone 4.

Be Thou a wall unto us, Thy Cross, [f. 123vB] O Jesus our Savior, for no other consolation have we faithful, save Thee, Who in the flesh wast nailed upon it, and Who grantest us great mercy.

Thou hast given a sign unto those who fear Thee, O Lord: Thy precious Cross, whereby Thou didst put to shame the Principalities of darkness and powers, and didst lead us back unto the first blessedness. Therefore we glorify Thy dispensation, the Lover of mankind: O all-powerful Jesus, Savior of our souls!

Martyricon:

As in fields we marvel not at the struggles of the holy Martyrs, for being surrounded by a body that dies, ye conquered the incorporeal enemies; for the torturers' threats terrified you not, nor did the application of torments dismay you; truly worthily ye were glorified by Christ.

Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion:

To: As one noble:

Beholding Thee crucified, O Christ, the Most-pure Lady, putting to death the deceiver: as Master, weeping She praised the Tender-hearted One Who had come forth from Her, and marveling at His long-suffering, She cried aloud: 'O My most-beloved Child, forget not Thine handmaid! Tarry not, O Lover of mankind, my consolation!'

ON WEDNESDAY, THE BEATITUDES

Tone 4.[^192]

Through the tree Adam was cast out of Paradise; but through the tree of the Cross the thief dwelt in Paradise. For the one, having tasted, transgressed the commandment of Him Who made him; but the other, being crucified with Thee, confessed Thee as God...

[f. 124rA] Ode 4. Heirmos:[^193]

Beholding Thee lifted up [upon the Cross...]:

Thou didst send Thy chosen horses into the sea, O Lover of mankind: stirring up the waters of ignorance, and proclaiming Thy true knowledge unto all.

Stars that enlightened the spiritual firmament of the Church with piety, O glorious Apostles: deliver me from the night of ignorance and transgressions.

Flying like sharpened arrows of the Mighty One, O Apostles, quench now the inflamed arrows of my heart, and strengthen my mind.

Theotokion:

Heal my soul, embittered with venom by the bite of the adversary, with effectual remedy, O Christ, through the supplications of Her who bore Thee, and of Thy sacred Apostles.

Another Canon [to St. Nicholas]. Heirmos: Sitting in glory [upon the throne of the Godhead...]:

Thy most-glorious life, exalted, showed thee most-glorious by divine wonders, and glorified, the adornment of First Hierarchs, and the praise of all who honor thee with joyful songs, O Nicholas.

The throne of God is sweet with praise, O glorious one: with divine splendors of humble-mindedness; gather us together to be partakers of it, through thy God-pleasing supplications, O father Nicholas.

Those led unjustly unto death thou didst deliver: being kindled with divine zeal, O father, in priestly dignity. Therefore we cry unto thee: likewise deliver us from entanglements which bitterly put to death, by thy prayers.

[f. 124rB] Unseen in our midst: thou comest unto all who call upon thee, lightening the diseases of our souls, and granting their alleviation readily.

Theotokion:

The angelic hosts, being filled with awe, O Most-pure One, praise the greatness of Thy divine childbearing, with whom pray, O Lady, that all may be saved who with pure faith call Thee blessed.

Ode 5. Heirmos:

Thou, O Lord, art my light, [Who camest into the world...]:

Living vines, blossoming forth clusters of grapes, have given all to drink of the wine of spiritual joy, O glorious Apostles.

Guide me unto the light of the commandments of God, O Apostles: who foolishly abide in the darkness of spiritual sloth.

Deliver me from spiritual transgressions, and the future judgment, and passions and tribulations, O blessed Apostles.

Save me, O God, as Thou art the Lover of mankind, save me, by the prayers of Her who ineffably bore Thee, and of all Thy divine Apostles.

Another Canon [to St. Nicholas]. Heirmos: The ungodly shall not see [Thy glory...]:

Thou hast set like the sun, O wise father, and hast shone forth from Christ with light-bearing splendors of thy wonders, enlightening all under the sun, O father Nicholas.

Holy Nicholas, hear us in the day of the onset of tribulations and sorrows, and drive away every strait by the grace of the Spirit dwelling within thee.

My soul crushed by worldly passions by prayers: to help [f. 124vA] [...I call upon thee], O holy Nicholas; make haste, and grant me perfect healing, entreating Christ for me, a sinner.[^194]

Theotokion:

With spiritual eyes, O Virgin, Isaiah beholding Thee, the unwedded Embers, cried aloud: 'Behold, from the Virgin Maiden the Lord Jesus will be born, for the regeneration of mankind!'

Ode 6. Heirmos:

I will sacrifice unto Thee with the voice of praise, [O Lord...]:

The God-chosen sheep of the Good Shepherd, scattered throughout the world, by faith transformed the great savagery of wolves into the gentleness of sheep.

Trees of the divine Paradise bearing good fruit, O Apostles, bring all the barrenness of my most-wretched soul into the fruitful harvest of virtuous character.

I was wounded with the weapon of passions and died: O glorious ones who received from Christ the grace to raise the dead, quicken my dead and wretched soul!

O Thou Who art compassionate unto all: cause the storm of filthy passions of my soul to cease, through the supplications of Her who bore Thee, the Theotokos, and of Thy Martyrs.

*Another Canon [to St. Nicholas]. Heirmos: I came into the deep of the sea...*

Being strengthened by the power of the Savior, O God-wise one, thou wast able to destroy the invisible enemy; from his bitter injury deliver us, by thy supplications, O father Nicholas.

[f. 124vB] From torment in Gehenna, and from the harmful sentence of the cruel bonds, deliver us, by thy sacred prayers, O most-glorious Nicholas.

Having of old delivered the generals who were unjustly to die, by thine intercession, as from harm, O worthily blessed one.

Theotokion:

Thy people and Thy city entreat Thee, O Mother of God: deliver us from every tribulation, O all-immaculate one, and from eternal condemnation there.

Ode 7. Heirmos:

In the furnace the Abrahamic Children [trampled the flame...]:

By the power of the preaching of all the world, the true Apostles of Christ destroyed the winter of deception, and warmed the minds of the faithful with divine knowledge.

Ever pouring forth fragrant myrrh, O divine Apostles: fill with the fragrance of spiritual myrrh those who run unto God, and drive away stinking passions.

Me who am dissipated in carnal improprieties, O glorious disciples of the incorruptible Word: save me as I sing: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord!

Theotokion:

Choirs of Angels, choirs of Martyrs and Apostles: ever entreat Thee, O Word, according to the multitude of Thy compassions, to cleanse sins, for Her sake, as Thou art wise.

Another Canon [to St. Nicholas]. Heirmos: Three youths [in Babylon...]:

O Saint Nicholas, who restest in the only Holy God Who rests in the saints: pray that He may sanctify us, and send down upon us rich mercies [f. 125rA] [...having darkened them, by the teachings of piety thou didst enlighten the world; by their supplications, save our souls.][^195]

As Moses led Israel from bondage through the Red Sea by Thy right hand, drowning Pharaoh: so in wonders Thy wise disciples parted the sea of bitter godlessness, and guided the people unto Thee, O beginningless Word, only Lover of mankind.

Glory... Both now... Theotokion:

Fleeing with our souls in distress, a reconciliation unto God for sinners, O Most-pure Lady: save us from every oppression and malice of men, and dread torments and foolish passions, who with unhesitating faith ever call upon Thee, O all-hymned Virgin.

After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns.

To the Apostles, Tone 4.

Preachers of faith, Thy disciples, O Savior, Thou didst reveal unto the world, guiding the nations through them unto knowledge of Thee: for with the radiances of the word they enlightened all, driving away the darkness of ignorance by faith. By their prayers save our souls.

Martyricon:

Manfully having endured, ye worthily received the incorruptible crown of Christ's kingdom, for being drawn with desire toward ageless life, ye endured torments in the flesh, O Passion-bearers. Therefore pray that our souls may be saved.

Glory... Both now... Theotokion:

We magnify Thee, O Theotokos, crying aloud: 'Thou [f. 125rB] art the only blessed one, from whom was ineffably born Christ our God.'

After the 3rd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns, Tone 4.

As a beam of the Sun of righteousness, Christ sent you forth to enlighten all the earth, O glorious Apostles, by your divine prayers; for with the unwaning divine Light ye illumine all, and enlighten those who in faith celebrate your holy memory.

Swiftly anticipate, O father Nicholas, and save thy servants from the tribulations and sorrows that come upon us: for thou hast boldness before the Creator and God; therefore stand forth swiftly, unto those who faithfully call upon thee: grant now thy protection and defense.

Glory... Both now... Theotokion:

Unashamed hope of those who trust in Thee, who alone beyond nature didst bear in the flesh Christ our God: entreat Him together with the holy Apostles to grant the universe cleansing of transgressions, and unto us all amendment of life before the end.

CANON to the Holy Apostles.

Tone 4, Ode 1. Heirmos:

Traversing of old the deep of the Red Sea with dry feet, Israel, with Moses' hands stretched out crosswise, vanquished the might of Amalek in the wilderness.

Luminaries, organs of the divine Disciples, ever sounding Him forth with divine spiritual songs, have sung a song for us, as truly saved, O glorious Apostles of Christ!

[f. 125vA] [...Upon the bed of slothfulness] lying, and ailing in the death of sin, my soul is bitterly swallowed up: vouchsafe me your visitation, O glorious eyewitnesses of Christ![^196]

Ye who by the word loosed the nations from irrationality, O Apostles: enlighten my heart, bitterly darkened by irrational deeds, by the grace of the Paraclete, O glorious ones!

A Virgin even after childbearing didst Thou remain incorruptible, and didst bring forth Him Who for our sake appeared beyond word; Whom earnestly entreat to enlighten our souls.

ANOTHER CANON, TO SAINT NICHOLAS.

Composition of Joseph.

Tone 4, Ode 1. Heirmos:

The three mighty captains:

Having inherited a life free of care, O father, and being ever filled with spiritual joy: drive away great sorrow from my soul, I pray, that rejoicing I may glorify thee.

Most sacred father Nicholas: thou wast placed spiritually upon the lampstand of virtues, and like a luminary thou dost enlighten the hearts of the faithful, O hierarch Nicholas; therefore in faith I pray thee: by thy light-bearing prayers drive away the darkness of my soul.

Now filled with great assaults of this corruptible life, I ever cross the deep, that I may find thee, O venerable pilot, calming the tempest into tranquility, through thy divine prayers.

Theotokion:

Having an unsleeping prayer, O pure one: lull our spiritual passions to sleep by thy sacred intercession, divine [f. 125vB] and granting saving vigilance unto the fulfillment of God's commandments.

Ode 3. Heirmos:

Thy Church doth rejoice in Thee, [O Christ, crying: Thou art my strength, O Lord...]:

Thy city, O God, the streams of the rivers of Thy disciples, O Master, sacredly make glad.

Heavenly citizens, fellow-guests of the spiritual ranks, O all-glorious Apostles: deliver us from every tribulation!

Thou Who didst establish Thy rational sheep, O Christ: establish me through their prayers upon the rock of Thy desires, as Thou art tender-hearted.

As Thy Mother entreats Thee together with the choir of the Lord's Disciples, who purely bore Thee: grant us Thy mercies.

Another Canon. Heirmos:

Not in wisdom, nor in power, nor in riches do we boast: but in Thine, O Father, hypostatic Wisdom of God: for there is none holy save Thee, O Lover of mankind.

Thou wast revealed as a weapon, slaying the subduing enemies; from whom, O Nicholas, keep us unharmed and spotless, performing the divine will.

Heal the crushing of my soul, O hierarch, who didst crush the enemy's snares and trappings, that in faith I may magnify thee as my protector.

Thou who didst destroy the lifeless temples of Artemis: consume the passionate idols of my mind by thy divine intercessions, O father Nicholas.

Theotokion:

Having obtained Thee as our protectress, O Most-pure Virgin: turn our sorrow into joy, and deliver us from griefs that bring forth death!

[f. 126rA] [...of His mercy.][^197]

True, righteous, and meek, gentle, and humble wast thou, O glorious one; thou wast taken up unto the most-glorious height of priesthood, performing wonders and signs.

Having kept the divine laws, thou wast revealed as a most honorable temple of God. Therefore we cry aloud unto thee, O all-blessed father: deliver us from all lawlessness by thine intercession.

Theotokion:

From the uprising of passions in my soul, by Thy living prayer give me vigilance, O Maiden, driving far away the slumber of despondency.

Ode 8. Heirmos:

Daniel, stretching out his hands, [stopped the mouths of the lions in the pit...]:

Fiery breathings of Christ: who stopped lawless mouths and everywhere sowed the saving preaching: deliver from the mouth of the spiritual wolf those who cry: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing and exalt Him supremely unto all ages!

Sound the trumpet over my dead soul, O melodious trumpets of Christ, glorious Apostles: and raise it up from the grave of despair and cruel despondency, to sing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing and exalt Him supremely unto all ages!

Despise not me who have trampled upon Thy laws, O Christ, through corruption of mind, me who have slipped into passions, O good Master, and who ever slave for evil custom, through the supplications of Thy sacred disciples.

Theotokion:

O Mary, who rulest over all, [f. 126rB] free me who am held by the serpent and who ever sin, by Thy prayers, and make me a servant unto Christ in a pure life, to sing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing and exalt Him supremely unto all ages!

Another Canon [to St. Nicholas]. Heirmos:

O all-powerful Redeemer of all:

When Thou didst bedew the faithful in the midst of the flame, and didst teach them to sing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing and exalt Him supremely unto all ages!

Eloquently speaking divine things, O Nicholas, thou didst truly close the unstopped mouths of the lawless, and delivering many from the ruin of Arius, who rightly sing: Sing unto the Lord, and exalt Him supremely unto all ages!

Named after victory, O holy one: show us to be victors through thy prayers over the passions that bring forth death, and over the flattering tongue of lawless men, who faithfully and ever call thee blessed.

Be entreated to send us now all saving help, O wonderworker Nicholas, in the day of tribulation, when asking of thee in faith, we pray.

Triadicon:

With equal glory let us faithful bow down before the Holy Trinity of one nature: unto the beginningless Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, crying aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; sing and exalt Him supremely unto all ages!

Theotokion:

Vouchsafe me to be of Thy people, O blessed Lady who didst bear God the compassionate; and standing before Him in the hour of judgment, deliver me from condemnation there, O Most-pure One!

[f. 126vA] Ode 9. Heirmos:[^198]

The stone cut without hands from the mountain:

Chosen stones laid as the chief corner stone, ye built up the hearts of all the faithful; by the rock of faith, O Apostles, ye destroyed the enemy's buildings.

Having received power from Christ to bind and to loose: loose the bond of my evils, and draw me unto the love of God, and make me a partaker of the Kingdom, O divine Apostles!

Divine good clouds, water now with divine showers my heart which hath become dry through great wicked action, and show it forth fruitful, O glorious Apostles!

With the holy Angels, with the divine Apostles, with the glorious Martyrs: entreat Thy Son and God, O all-immaculate Mother of God, to deliver Thy servants from tribulations.

Another Canon [to St. Nicholas]. Heirmos:

Eve, through the disease of disobedience, [brought in the curse...]:

The curse was introduced; but Thou, O Virgin Theotokos, through the sprout of Thy dwelling, didst blossom forth blessing unto the world. Therefore we all magnify Thee.

Working healings, thy tomb, O venerable one, pours forth fragrant myrrh unto those who approach with faith and love, O Nicholas, and who honor thy memory. Therefore we all magnify thee.

Like the sun thou dost enlighten the whole northern region, O all-blessed Nicholas, by the beams of divine wonders driving away the darkness of cruel circumstances, through thy sacred intercessions, O adornment of hierarchs!

As is thy wont, show compassion upon us, O Nicholas:

[f. 126vB] who are ever bitterly afflicted by worldly assaults, and demonic deceits, and temptations of wicked men: that with love we may call thee blessed.

Remember the dread day and hour, O my soul, when the Master will bring thee unto judgment and reprove thy secret deeds; cry aloud unto Him: O Savior, save me through the prayers of Nicholas!

Theotokion:

Joyfully we offer unto Thee the voice of the divine Gabriel, and we cry aloud: Rejoice, O Paradise, ever having the Tree of Life in Thy midst, most glorious Palace of the Word! Rejoice, O all-immaculate Virgin!

AT THE APOSTICHA, STICHERA

To the Apostles, Tone 4.

The choir of the Apostles Thou didst enlighten with the Holy Spirit, O Christ; and through them wash away our sinful filth, O Lord, and have mercy on us.

Unlettered disciples Thy Holy Spirit showed forth as teachers, O Christ God; and by the much-speaking melodious harmony of tongues, Thou didst abolish deception, as Thou art all-powerful.

Precious is the death of Thy saints, O Lord; for by sword and fire and contrite soul they poured out their blood, having hope and power from Thee to receive the reward of labors, and having endured, they received great mercy from Thee, O Savior.

Glory... Both now... Theotokion:

Having obtained Thee as a wall, O Most-pure Theotokos, and a calm harbor and confirmation: therefore we pray, steer me who am tempest-tossed in life, and save me!

[f. 127rA] ON THURSDAY, THE BEATITUDES

Tone 4.[^199]

Through the tree Adam was cast out of Paradise; but through the tree of the Cross the thief dwelt in Paradise. For the one, having tasted, transgressed the commandment of Him Who made him; but the other, being crucified with Thee, confessed Thee as God, crying aloud: Remember me in Thy kingdom!

Spiritual sheep of the Shepherd and Lamb, as wise lambs ye were sent forth by Him into the midst of wolves, transforming their savagery into gentleness by divine preaching; crying in faith with unwavering mind: Remember us also in Thy kingdom!

Having traversed the ends of the earth, O Apostles of the Lord, like radiant stars: ye destroyed the darkness of deception, and shone forth the saving light unto the deceived. Therefore we call you blessed, preachers of Christ, asking: pray unto the Lord for us!

Being crushed by torments, and burned with material fire: ye burned up the bitter matter of polytheism, [f. 127rB] O all-blessed ones, and now ye pour forth streams of healings unto those who come unto you with warm faith, O preachers of Christ, and who cry unto Christ: Remember us in Thy kingdom!

Glory... Triadicon:

With unwavering thought, with sober mind, lifting up our hands unto Him Who sits on high with the Father and the Holy Spirit, O indivisible Trinity, Who didst establish all things by Thy word, and Who dost enlighten all who call in faith and ever cry: Remember us also in Thy kingdom!

Both now... Theotokion:

Joy of the Apostles, and unfading crown of the Passion-bearers, art Thou truly, O all-immaculate Virgin Theotokos. With them ask for us, O Lady, remission of transgressions, and amendment of life, who sing of Thee in faith and faithfully cry: Save us, O Mother of God, who bow down before Thee!

## THURSDAY EVENING VESPERS (FOR FRIDAY) (TONE 4)

ON THURSDAY EVENING, AT 'LORD, I HAVE CRIED':

*Stichera of the Cross, Tone 4.*

*Podoben: "Thou hast given a sign" (Да́лъ єсѝ зна́ме):*
