When all creation beheld Thee crucified, it was transformed and trembled; the earth shook, being all in commotion, O Long-suffering Word, and the veil of the temple was rent in twain with fear. When Thou wast insulted, the rocks were split from fear, and the sun hid its beams, knowing Thee to be its Creator.

[f. 127vA] [...that the most lawless assembly dared to condemn Thee, the immortal Judge: Who of old gavest the Law in the wilderness unto Moses the God-seer! Seeing the Life of all dead upon the tree, how did they not tremble with knees shaking, knowing Thee to be King and Lord of all, and Creator of the universe?][^200]

The handwriting of our forefather Adam from ages past is torn up by the piercing of Thy ribs, O Most-merciful One, and renewed human nature is sanctified by the sprinkling of Thy blood, crying aloud: Glory to Thy compassion! Glory to Thy divine Crucifixion, O all-powerful Jesus, Savior of our souls!

Other Stichera to the Most-holy Theotokos.

*Tone 4.*

*Podoben: "As one valiant among martyrs" (Я҆́кѡ до́бля):*

When the Ewe-lamb and Thy Mother beheld Thee nailed upon the Cross, O Lord, She marveled and cried aloud: 'What a sight is this, O my beloved Son? Is this what the disobedient and lawless assembly hath repaid unto Thee, which enjoyed Thy many wonders? But glory to Thine ineffable condescension, O Master!'

When the Ewe-lamb who bore Thee beheld Thee, the Lamb and Shepherd, upon the tree: She wept maternally and said unto Thee, O most-beloved Son: 'How art Thou lifted up upon the tree of the Cross, O Long-suffering One? How are Thy hands and feet nailed by the lawless, O Word, and Thou didst pour out Thy blood, O Master?'

Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion:

When the Virgin and Thy Mother saw Thee hanging upon the Cross, O Lord:

[f. 127vB] She marveled and weeping said: 'What have they repaid unto Thee, who enjoyed Thy many gifts, O Master? But I pray Thee: leave me not alone in the world, but hasten to rise, raising up our forefather with Thyself!'

AT THE APOSTICHA, STICHERA

Of the Cross, Tone 4.

An invincible weapon hast Thou given unto us, O Christ, Thy Cross, and thereby we conquer the assaults of the stranger. Ever having Thy Cross for our help, O Christ, we easily trample upon the snares of the enemy.

Martyricon:

Glorified in the memory of Thy saints, O Christ God, and entreated by them: send down upon us great mercy.

Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion:

To: Called from on high:

Weep not for Me, O Mother, beholding hanging upon the tree Thy Son and God, Who suspended the earth upon the waters and created all creation! Behold, I will arise and be glorified, and will crush the kingdoms of hades with power, and destroy its might, and deliver those bound from its malice, as I am tender-hearted, and will bring them unto My Father, as I am the Lover of mankind!

## FRIDAY MATINS: THE PRECIOUS CROSS AND THE THEOTOKOS (TONE 4)

ON FRIDAY AT MATINS.

After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymns.

Of the Cross, Tone 4.

Thou hast redeemed us from the curse of the law by Thy precious Blood; being nailed to the Cross and pierced with a spear, Thou didst pour forth immortality unto mankind: O our Savior, glory to Thee!

[f. 128rA] The Jews nailed Thee to the Cross, O Savior, Who didst summon us from corruption, O Christ our God; Thou didst stretch forth Thy palms upon it of Thine own will, and wast pleased to be pierced in Thy side with a spear, according to the multitude of Thy compassions, O only Lover of mankind.[^201]

Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion:

O all-immaculate Virgin, Mother of Christ God: a sword pierced Thy most-holy soul when Thou didst behold Thy Son and God crucified of His own will: Whom, O all-blessed one, unceasingly pray to grant remission of our transgressions!

After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns.

Of the Cross, Tone 4.

Swiftly anticipate, before we are enslaved to the enemies who blaspheme Thee and threaten us, O Christ our God; destroy by Thy Cross those who war against us, that they may know how mighty is the faith of the Orthodox, through the prayers of the Theotokos, O only Lover of mankind.

When Thou wast wounded with a spear in Thy divine side, the weapons of the invisible enemy failed utterly, and all violence of his malice ceased. Therefore we bow down before Thy saving Passions, glorifying Thy divine dispensation.

Martyricon:

Today the angelic hosts approach at the memory of the Passion-bearers, to enlighten the minds of the faithful and make radiant the universe with grace. Being entreated through them, O God: grant us great mercy.

Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion:

[f. 128rB] When Thine immaculate Mother saw Thee lifted up upon the Cross, O Word of God, weeping maternally, She cried aloud: 'What is this new and strange wonder, O my Son? How dost Thou, the Life of all, taste of death, desiring to quicken the dead, as Thou art merciful?'

After the 3rd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns.

Of the Cross, Tone 4.

The Cross and death for our sake, which for the sake of Thine immeasurable mercy Thou didst endure willingly, and an unjust judgment, that Thou mightest free all from condemnation and the ancient curse, who through deceit fell into burning. Therefore we bow down before Thy Crucifixion, O Word!

Beholding Thee hanging upon the tree, O Christ, the Sun of righteousness, the sun darkened its light; and creation was shaken, and the dead arose swiftly from the tombs as from sleep, O Word, singing of the divine dominion of Thy glory!

Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion:

Thine immaculate Mother, O Christ, when She beheld Thee lifted up upon the Cross, weeping maternally, said: 'What is this new and strange wonder, O my Son? How doth the lawless gathering nail Thee to the Cross, O Life of all, my sweetest Light?'

CANON to the Precious and Life-giving Cross of the Lord.

Tone 4, Ode 1. Heirmos:

I shall open my mouth, and it will be filled with the Spirit, and I will utter a word unto the Queen Mother: and I will appear radiantly celebrating, and I will sing rejoicing of Her wonders.

Upon the Cross Thou didst stretch out Thy divine palms, O Long-suffering One, and didst recall the perishing world unto knowledge of the dominion of all the Kingdom. Therefore we magnify Thy compassion.

Moses lifted up the serpent, prefiguring Thy divine Crucifixion, O beginningless Word, whereby the venomous serpent fell, which was the author of Adam's fall.

Martyricon:

Ye were vouchsafed now to dwell in the splendors of the saints, having received the unshakable kingdom, as Paul said, and ye became partakers of Christ's glory.

Martyricon:

The surging waves of your unbearable torments submerged not your ship, O Martyrs; for by the helm of the King of all, ye reached the haven of rest.

Theotokion:

A sword, as Simeon said, pierced Thy heart, O Virgin Lady, when Thou didst behold Christ crucified and pierced with a spear; therefore weeping, Thou didst endure griefs.

Another Canon to the Most-holy Theotokos.

Tone 4, Same Heirmos:

Thou alone art the protection, refuge, and guardian of Thy servants, O pure Mother of God. Therefore falling down, we cry unto Thee: Save us, O Lady, yea, Mary!

Cleanse, O Lady, my defiled heart, who didst bear the most-holy Word, [f. 128vB] and who art holier than all the higher hosts, O all-hymned Maiden!

The recall of the fallen and confirmation of those who stand art Thou, O all-immaculate one. Therefore I pray Thee: set upright my mind that hath fallen into sin, O Lady, that I may glorify Thee!

Me who lie dead with griefs and weighed down with diseases: stretch forth a hand of help and raise me wholly up, and show me filled with divine joy, O Mother of God!

Ode 3. Heirmos:

Establish Thy singers, O Theotokos, as a living and copious fountain, who have gathered together in spiritual choir, and in Thy divine glory vouchsafe them crowns of glory.

As a sheep, the lawless people led Thee to slaughter, O Christ, the Lamb of God and Son, Who desired to deliver from the bitter wolf the sheep whom Thou didst love, O Lover of mankind.

Thou didst stand before the judge, judged unjustly, Who judgest all the earth righteously, and Thou didst endure a blow on the cheek, desiring to free me who was enslaved to the evil ruler of the world, O Lord!

Martyricon:

Having suffered lawfully, O holy ones, ye put to shame the lawless enemies; and being willingly slain for Christ's resurrection, ye vanquished the serpent that authored death.

Martyricon:

Fellow-citizens against the plotter: having passed through the fire truly unto praise, O suffering Martyrs, mortals were united with immaterial ranks, being filled with joy ineffable [^203]

Thy Son was truly revealed as incorruptible renewal, O Virgin, God born in the flesh, lifted up upon the Cross, and casting down demons, O joyful Lady!

Another Canon. Same Heirmos:

Remember, O Most-pure Virgin, him who is drowning in the deep of bitter worldly things, and guide me unto the calm harbor of salvation, for Thee alone have we obtained as our hope.

Dispel the darkness of my mind, O Theotokos, by the Light within Thee, as Thou art good, and establish me in ways of repentance, as Thou art merciful, that being saved, I may call Thee blessed.

By the sprinkling of Thy mercy, O Virgin, extinguish the flame of my passions, O full of grace, and cleanse the filth of my heart, O all-immaculate one.

Visit my wretched soul, O Mother of God, which is bitterly pierced by passions, as Thou art merciful, and save me by Thy prayers, that having obtained the better life, I may magnify Thee!

Ode 4. Heirmos:

Sitting in glory upon the throne of the Godhead, on a swift cloud came Jesus the transcendent God, with incorruptible palm, and saved those who cry: Glory to Thy power, O Christ!

Marveling at the hidden counsel of God concerning Thine incarnation from the Virgin, O Most-high, the Prophet Habakkuk cried aloud: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

To deliver me from the bonds of sin, O Lover of mankind, Thou wast bound willingly, and didst die upon the Cross as an evildoer: glory to Thy great compassion!

O Word of God, tasting the fruit of transgression, [f. 129rB] and enduring a reproachful death, granting immortality unto the nature of mortals slain by passions: glory to Thy great mercy!

Martyricon:

Desiring to inherit the joy of God in the All-holy Spirit, with glad soul the Martyrs endured wounds, and wounded the cunning one.

Martyricon:

Having hands and heads cut off, tongues severed, O God-proclaiming Martyrs, deprived of sight, and burned upon coals: yet by God ye remained unharmed!

Theotokion:

The handwriting against Adam was rent in twain when Thou wast pierced with a spear, O Master, the Lady cried aloud, standing by the Lord's Cross and lamenting in pain.

Another Canon. Same Heirmos:

O all-marvelous Mother of God: shine forth upon me the dawn of repentance, dispel the darkness of my wretched soul, and drive away evil thoughts from my heart, O Virgin!

Having brought forth the timely and readily entreatable Good One, O Most-pure Virgin Mother: as Thou art good, ever pray for us, to deliver us from grievous burdens.

Thee, the Comforter of all men, in faith I entreat and implore, O blessed one: make Thy Son a merciful Judge unto me, that in praises I may glorify Thee!

Having Thee as my helper, whom shall I ever fear or dread? Who desiring to bring sorrow upon Thy servant will not be afraid, O Most-pure One?

Ode 5. Heirmos:

All creation was amazed [at Thy divine glory...]:

Beholding Thee, the Sun, stretched out upon the Cross, the sun drew in its rays, unable to shine when Thou, O Savior, didst set, enlightening those asleep in the night of deception, who bow down before Thy dominion.

Crucified and spat upon for my sake, O merciful Lord, Thou didst accept the tasting of vinegar and gall: delivering me, as Thou art good, from that tasting of pleasure whereby we were condemned and fell under corruption.

Martyricon:

Ye dispelled the winter of deception, O divine Martyrs, by the warmth of the Holy Spirit, and rejoicing ye attained together unto the spring of rest, helping all who are in tribulations.

Martyricon:

With showers of divine blood ye watered the earth, drying up the torrents of godlessness, O holy Martyrs. Therefore ye have now dwelt beside the living water, praying for all.

Theotokion:

When She beheld Her Son Whom She had borne in the flesh, O full of God's grace, lifted up upon the tree, She was filled with weeping, and truly marveled at His long-suffering. Therefore She magnified His condescension.

Another Canon. Same Heirmos:

Slain by passions, O all-immaculate one: I flee unto Thy compassions, and I hasten unto Thy warm protection and help, O Lady; having alone borne Life, quicken my heart!

[f. 129vB] Enlighten my darkened heart, O Most-pure One, who didst bear the Giver of light, God and man together; Whom as His Mother entreat to grant me redemption from sins before the dread day.

Heal the crushings of my mind, O all-immaculate one: cure the passions of my soul, and drive away the darkness of despondency, that in praise I may hymn Thee, who didst receive blessedness, O all-hymned Theotokos!

Cast down, O Lady, the insolence of my enemies, for Thee alone do we have as protectress, Thee our hope and mighty help; preserve us, O Pure One, delivering me from all their oppression.

Ode 6. Heirmos:

Celebrating this divine and all-honorable festival of the Mother of God, O God-wise ones, come, let us clap our hands, glorifying in faith God Who was born of Her.

By the pains which Thou didst endure being crucified, Thou didst stop the pains of mankind, and dost translate all unto a painless life, O compassionate Lord!

The sun drew in its rays, the veil of the temple was rent in twain, and the earth shook; the rocks were split from fear, unable to behold the Creator upon the Cross.

Martyricon:

The serpent became dead, being slain by your torments, O divine Martyrs, and ye truly inherited together life by divine grace.

Martyricon:

Many torments ye endured, and many crowns ye obtained, [f. 130rA] O countless multitudes of ever-rejoicing Martyrs: therefore drive away the multitudes of my evils![^205]

Theotokion:

Be Thou a harbor unto me who sail in the deep of tribulations, O all-immaculate one, who by Thy childbearing, O Mother of God, hast now saved the Benefactor of all creation!

Another Canon. Heirmos:

Prefiguring the three-day burial, the Prophet Jonah cried aloud, praying in the whale: From corruption save me, O Jesus, King of hosts!

Shine forth upon me the dawn of repentance, O Lady, and dispel the clouds of my evil thoughts, O Cloud of the Sun of righteousness, ever Virgin!

Give me to drink of the beverage of compunction, O Lady, and grant me now rivers of tears, wherewith I may quench the eternal flame, O only all-praised one!

Deliver me from the strong deep of my evils, who didst bear the true deep of goodness, and guide me unto the haven of God's will.

Ode 7. Heirmos:

The God-wise youths worshipped not the creature rather than the Creator, but manfully trampling upon the threat of fire, they rejoiced, singing: Blessed art Thou, O all-hymned Lord and God of our fathers!

The adversary was conquered and fell with a marvelous fall, when Christ was lifted up upon the tree, and he that was formerly condemned was saved, [f. 130rB] crying unto Him: Blessed art Thou, O Lord and God of our fathers!

Me who was slain by the tree, Thou didst quicken, having died upon the tree, O Christ, and by divine wounds Thou didst heal the stripes of my heart. Blessed art Thou, O all-hymned Lord and God of our fathers!

Martyricon:

The subduer, suffering drowning in your blood, was swallowed up with his myriads, as ye, O all-lauded Martyrs, rejoicing sing: Blessed art Thou, O Lord and God of our fathers!

Martyricon:

Though your bodies were burned, wounded with measureless wounds, yet the beauty of your soul was shown truly most fair, O Martyrs of Christ, as ye ever cry: Blessed art Thou, O Lord, the God of our fathers!

Theotokion:

An immaculate palace, a palace unto the Creator, untilled earth, a fiery-radiant throne wast Thou revealed, O Most-pure One. Therefore we cry unto Thee: Rejoice, O Lady, who didst deify mankind by Thy divine childbearing!

Another Canon. Heirmos:

Those in the fire:

With great love I flee under Thy protection; send me not away empty, but grant me, O Most-pure One, remission of transgressions, and save me, that my enemies, seeing it, may be put to shame.

I shall not fear evil, for Thou art with me, O Virgin; pursue the enemies who mercilessly persecute me, and vanquish them, strengthened by Thy power, O Mother of God!

Thou hast the power ever to do all things, having borne the Good One of all: deliver me from the dominion of pleasure and passions [f. 130vA] that rejoicing I may sing: Rejoice, O Throne of the Most High, O blessed one!

Thee alone upon earth have I as protectress and help in truth, I Thy servant: a secure and firm [refuge], O Pure One, glorified of God; and unto Thee do I flee: save me from the snares of those who hunt [after my soul], O Mother of God!

Ode 8. Heirmos:[^206]

The pious youths in the furnace, the childbearing of the Theotokos saved: then prefigured, but now fulfilled; it raises up the whole universe to sing: Chant unto the Lord, all ye works, and exalt Him above all unto the ages!

Having loosed me from temporal bonds, Thou didst become subject to time, Who art timeless; being bound by Thine own will, Thou didst bind the proud one with unlooseable bonds, that Thou mightest save me by the Cross and Passion. Therefore, we bless Thee, O Christ, unto the ages!

Being lifted up upon the tree by Thine own will, all creation was lifted up with Thee, O all-hymned Word, unoriginate and invisible, O Christ; by Thy Passion Thou didst expose [the enemy]. Therefore, we sing unto Thee unto the ages!

Martyricon:

Ye mounted upon your blood as upon a chariot, O all-comely Martyrs, and were taken up unto supramundane dwellings, receiving worthy honors from Christ; and crying aloud, ye sing: Chant, and exalt Him above all unto the ages!

Lifted up upon the tree, surrendered unto wild beasts, and shedding your blood, being dismembered, O Passion-bearing Martyrs, rejoicing ye sang: Chant unto the Lord, all ye works, and exalt Him above all unto the ages!

[f. 130vB] Theotokion:

Beholding Thee wounded upon the tree, Who grantest unto all divine and saving vigilance, the all-immaculate Mother wept aloud with lamentation and cried: What is this newest wonder, O God-fighting arrogance, that desires to put to death [the Author of life]!

Another Canon. Same Heirmos:

Having led a prodigal life, and committed every uncleanness: I tremble before the judgment seat, I tremble at the scrutiny, I tremble also at the portion of my condemnation, O Pure One, who didst bear the Judge; stand by me then, and deliver me from distress!

Upon Thee have I placed all the hope of my salvation, O unwedded Mother of God, and Thee do I summon to my help at all times: save me from sorrows and assaults of enemies, loose the bonds of my evils, and snatch me from eternal darkness!

At the hour of my demise, O Virgin, snatch me from demonic hands, and deliver me from judgment, dispute, dread scrutiny, bitter toll-houses, and the cruel prince, O Mother of God, and from eternal condemnation!

Preserve Thy servant, O Virgin, from every foreign assault: for Thee do I have, O Lady, as protection and intercession, refuge and confirmation; and through Thee do I hope to escape the snares of the enemy, O only Protectress of the human race!

Ode 9. Heirmos:

Let every earthborn mortal...

[f. 131rA] Ode 9. Heirmos:

Let every earthborn mortal leap for joy in spirit, being enlightened; and let the nature of the bodiless minds celebrate, honoring the sacred festival of the Mother of God, and let them cry out: Rejoice, O all-blessed one, pure Theotokos, ever Virgin!

He Who desires to judge mankind stood as One judged, O Lover of mankind; and He was willingly crowned with a crown of thorns, O Savior, not enduring that the briars of disobedience remain unrooted, O Christ, but planting in all the knowledge of Thy loving-kindness!

O how did a lawless people condemn the righteous and blameless One! Darkened by a curse, they deliver Thee, O Light-giver, unto the Cross, at Whose Passion the sun was darkened, and the splendor of the temple was rent in twain, and the foundations of the earth were shaken!

Martyricon:

Conformed unto the Passion of Christ, O holy Martyrs, and looking upon the heavenly Kingdom and its brightness: therefore enlighten your chanters, delivering them from sinful darkness and manifold cruelties!

Martyricon:

Having hated all worldly things, O all-wise ones, ye received eternal glory, and were deified by sacred communion. Remember us all, who with faith honor your all-holy and honorable memory, O ever-glorious ones!

Theotokion:

Enlighten, O Pure One, those who with love honor and magnify Thee; loose the darkness of our passions, O Maiden, calm the storm, and remove from our midst the stumbling-blocks of the evil one; and by Thine intercessions subdue the Hagarenes unto the pious Ruler!

[f. 131rB] Another Canon. Same Heirmos:

Rejoice, O all-pure one, who in truth didst bear joy unto those upon earth! Rejoice, saving haven and protection of those who flee unto Thee! Rejoice, pure Ladder that didst raise up the fallen! Rejoice, all-blessed Theotokos, hope of our souls!

Quench the flame of my sin, O all-pure Lady, which hath defiled my soul and body, O Thou full of divine grace, through the power of Thy prayer, O all-immaculate one, granting saving healing: the divine fear of the Master!

Thou art my enlightenment, Thou art my deliverance and joy, Thou art my glory, praise, and the expectation of my salvation, O all-immaculate one; and in faith I bow down before Thee and cry unto Thee: Save me, Thy servant, and snatch me from the gates of hades!

Save me, O Pure One, who didst bear the Savior and All-compassionate One; have compassion upon me, Thy servant, and guide me unto the path of repentance; drive far from our midst the stumbling-blocks of the evil one, and deliver me from his snare and from eternal fire, O all-immaculate one!

At the Aposticha, Stichera of the Cross. Tone 4:

Be Thou a wall unto us, O Cross of Christ our Savior, for we, the faithful, have no other hope save Thee, Who in the flesh wast nailed upon it, and Who grantest unto us great mercy!

Thou hast given a sign unto them that fear Thee, O Lord: Thy precious Cross, wherewith Thou didst put to shame the principalities of darkness [f. 131vA] and power of darkness, and hast raised us up unto our primal blessedness. Therefore we glorify Thy loving dispensation, O all-powerful Jesus, Savior of our souls.

Martyricon:

Who will not marvel, seeing, O holy Martyrs, the good fight which ye have fought? How, being in the flesh, ye conquered the bodiless enemy, confessing Christ, and arming yourselves with the Cross? Therefore ye were worthily revealed as expellers of demons and vanquishers of barbarians, unceasingly praying that our souls may be saved.

Glory... Now and ever... Stavrotheotokion:

*Podoben: "As one valiant among martyrs" (Я҆́кѡ до́бля):*

When the Ewe-lamb and Thy Mother beheld Thee nailed upon the Cross, O Lord, She was amazed, and cried out: What is this sight, O beloved Son? Hath this unfaithful and lawless assembly repaid Thee thus, which enjoyed Thy many wonders? But glory to Thine ineffable condescension, O Master!

On Friday, the Beatitudes. Tone 4:[^207]

Through the tree Adam was driven out of paradise; but through the tree of the Cross the thief took up dwelling in paradise. For the one, having tasted, transgressed the commandment of Him Who made him; but the other, being crucified with Thee, confessed Thee as the hidden God, crying out: Remember me in Thy kingdom!

Beholding Thee stretched out upon the tree, O only Long-suffering One, the heavenly Powers were in doubt, marveling with trembling; the earth was shaken [f. 131vB] and the beauty of the luminaries was extinguished; while condemned Adam, when Thou, O Lover of mankind, wast unjustly condemned, was justified, glorifying Thy tender compassion.

Lifted up upon the Place of the Skull, Thou didst crush the enemy's head; and having died upon the tree, Thou didst quicken those who died through the fruit of the tree, O Master, and didst reveal them as dwellers of paradise, who unceasingly glorify Thy tender compassion, and cry out: Remember us in Thy kingdom!

Martyricon:

Taking up the Cross as a weapon, O holy Martyrs, ye went forth against the battle-array of enemies with valiant resolve, and having destroyed them, ye were crowned with incorruptible wreaths, and obtained the highest glory, O richly-blessed ones, rejoicing. Therefore in faith we bless you as good [servants].

Glory... Triadicon:

That we may worship the divine compassion of Thy loving-kindness toward us, O Savior, Thou wast nailed upon the Cross, Who art united with the Father and the Spirit; Thou didst endure the sponge and the reed, the mocking and the wounds, desiring to deliver from eternal fire those who cry: Remember us in Thy kingdom!

Now and ever... Theotokion:

He Who is uncontainable everywhere, Who cannot be circumscribed by place, took up dwelling within Thy womb, O Mother of God, all-pure Lady; and being suspended upon the tree, He was revealed as the fountain of life unto the world. Entreat Him therefore to mortify the carnal mind of our flesh, and to save us all by His goodness.

## FRIDAY EVENING VESPERS (FOR SATURDAY) (TONE 4)

[f. 132rA] ON FRIDAY EVENING, AT "LORD, I HAVE CRIED":[^208]

*Stichera to the Holy Martyrs, and Hierarchs, and Venerables. Tone 4.*

*Podoben: "Thou hast given a sign" (Да́лъ єсѝ зна́менїе):*

Having zealously emulated the sufferings of the Lover of mankind, O Passion-bearers, ye surrendered your bodies unto wounds and bitter torments, and unto myriads of afflictions, as seeing beforehand the divine enjoyment of paradise, the unfailing nourishment, and the everlasting blessing; which having obtained, pray ye for those who praise your goodness.

All-sacred Shepherds, having become imitators of the glorious Chief Shepherd, Christ the King of all, ye readily laid down your soul for the sheep; ye endured cruel tribulations, as pilots against grievous wolves, O richly-blessed ones, preserving unharmed the God-gathered flock.

*Other Stichera to the Holy Martyrs.*

*Podoben: "The same Tone and Podoben" (Гла́съ и҆ подо́бенъ то́йже):*

Living sacrifices, rational whole-burnt offerings, O Martyrs of the Lord, perfect oblations unto God, knowing God and sheep known of God, whose fold wolves cannot penetrate: pray that we also may be pastured by you beside the water of repose.

Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His saints; for with sword and fire and contrite soul they poured forth [f. 132rB] their blood, having hope in Thee, to receive the reward of their labors; having endured, they received from Thee, O Savior, great mercy.

Having boldness toward the Savior, O holy ones, pray unceasingly for us sinners, asking remission of transgressions and great mercy for our souls.

Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion:

He who for thy sake, O God-ancestor Prophet [David]...

At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 4. Martyricon:

Glorified in the memory of Thy saints, O Christ God, and entreated by them, send down upon us great mercy.

Martyricon:

Thou Who didst accept the endurance of the holy Martyrs, accept also from us our singing, O Lover of mankind, and grant us through their prayers great mercy.

*Hymn for the Departed (Поко́инъ):* [^209]

With the spirits of the righteous who have been made perfect, give rest to the souls of Thy servants, O Savior, preserving them in the blessed life which is with Thee, O Lover of mankind.

Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion:

Unquenchable Lamp, righteous Throne, all-pure Lady, pray that our souls may be saved!

## SATURDAY MATINS: ALL SAINTS, MARTYRS, AND THE DEPARTED (TONE 4)

[f. 132vA] ON SATURDAY AT MATINS:[^209]

After the 1st Kathisma: Sessional Hymns to the Martyrs, Tone 4:

Today the angelic hosts have assembled at the commemoration of the Passion-bearers, to enlighten the minds of the faithful, and to illumine the universe with grace. Entreated by them, O Christ, grant us great mercy!

Armed with the Cross, Thy Passion-bearers, O Christ our God, overcame the wiles of the author of evil; they shone forth as luminaries, instructing mankind, and bestowing healings upon those who ask in faith. By their entreaties, save our souls!

Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion:

The mystery hidden from all ages, and unknown even to the Angels, was manifest through Thee, O Theotokos, unto those upon earth: God incarnate in unconfused union, willingly accepting the Cross for our sake; whereby, having resurrected the First-fashioned, He saved our souls from death!

After the 2nd Kathisma: Sessional Hymns to the Martyrs, Tone 4:

Thy Martyrs, O Lord, in their sufferings received incorruptible crowns from Thee, our God; for possessing Thine invincible strength, they put down the tormentors, and crushed the feeble insolence of the demons. By their prayers, O Christ God, save our souls!

As with purple and fine linen, Thy Church hath been adorned with the blood of Thy Martyrs throughout the whole world; therefore She cries aloud unto Thee, O Christ God: Send down Thy compassions upon Thy people, grant peace unto Thy city [f. 132vB] and unto our souls great mercy!

*Hymn for the Departed (Поко́инъ):*

The souls of those whom Thou hast translated from temporary things unto Thyself, O Savior, give rest, as Thou art immortal and all-powerful, and the only Lover of mankind. Forgive as Thou art compassionate the things committed by them; have mercy, O Merciful One, upon the works of Thy hands, through the prayers of the Theotokos, O only Lover of mankind!

Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion:

O Pure, All-immaculate, and Unwedded One, who alone in time didst bear the Son and Word of God full of grace: Him, together with the holy and honorable Patriarchs, Martyrs, Prophets, and Venerables, entreat to grant us cleansing and great mercy!

Canon to All Saints (Martyrs, Hierarchs, Venerables) and for the Departed.[^210]

Ode 1. Tone 4. Heirmos:

O Thou Who wast born of the Virgin, drown the tripartite nature of my soul in the deep of passionlessness, I pray Thee, O mighty Captain, that as on a timbrel, in the mortification of the body, I may sing unto Thee a song of victory!

The honorable Church is enlightened continually by the radiant struggles of the Lord's Passion-bearers; and She glorifies in festive dance Christ the Sun Who shone forth from the Virgin and dispersed the darkness of deception!

Let us in faith praise the High Priests of Christ, who well pastured the chosen people; and let us brightly extol the holy assembly of the Venerables who lived godly lives and mortified carnal pleasures by the Spirit!

Strength from God was granted unto women, who in asceticism and valiant [f. 133rA] suffering trampled underfoot the enemy by grace; by their supplications, O Lord, and of all Thy Saints, send down Thy mercies upon us all!

Justify, O Christ, those whom by Thy righteous providence Thou hast translated from this corruptible life unto incorruptible life, Thy servants; and vouchsafe them to dance with all Thy righteous ones, overlooking their transgressions. Theotokion:

Thou hast delivered us from the ancient condemnation, O Son of God, having well-pleased, O Pure One, to become also Thy Son; therefore receiving adoption as sons, we sing praise unto the good Father, hymning Thee!

Another Canon for the Departed.

Ode 1. Tone 4. Heirmos:

The surge of the Red Sea:

Taking Thy servants by their right hand, guide them unto eternal life, O Christ, unto the vision of Thy comeliness, being entreated by the Passion-bearing Martyrs!

Vouchsafe those who have reposed in faith to inherit Thine ineffable and blessed glory, O Christ, overlooking their transgressions, and justifying them by grace, through the shedding of Thy blood!

By Thy life-bearing mortification Thou didst put to death the slayer, Who didst grant life unto the dead, O Christ God; do Thou Thyself now give rest unto Thy faithful servants whom Thou hast received. Theotokion:

Surpassing in comeliness of highest beauty as the Son of God, yet as Thou wast incarnate of the Virgin, O Maiden, and wast suspended upon the tree, Thou hadst no comeliness, accepting death for all!

[f. 133rB] Ode 3. Heirmos:

The bow of the mighty hath grown weak, and the feeble have girded themselves with strength; therefore my heart is established in the Lord!

As well-victorious lambs having been slain, O Martyrs, ye were brought unto Christ, unto the Lamb and Word of God Who was slain for the deliverance of all!

Having preserved the divine doctrines, O Mystagogues, ye led forth the worthy from among the unworthy, enlightening them with sacred teachings!

The pride of the adversaries was crushed by your temperance, being nourished with unfailing food, through visions and divine ascents!

All those whom in faith Thou hast translated, O Christ, give rest, through the supplications of all Thy Saints, overlooking their transgressions committed in this life!

Let us bring praise unto God, Who was willingly born of the Virgin, and Who joined the choirs of women unto the angelic choirs!

Another Canon. Heirmos: Not in wisdom:

Having quenched the deception of idols, the Martyrs now entreat the Good God to grant divine rest unto those who have reposed before us!

Vouchsafe to turn back the turning sword, and grant Thine reposed servants, O Master, to obtain the choice participation of the Tree of Life!

In paradise, O Christ, vouchsafe Thy servants to dwell, where the voice of those who feast is pure, granting them remission of sins!

[f. 133vA] Unto divine childbearing Thou didst join virginity, O All-pure One; for Thou didst ineffably bear the Creator of all magnificent things, Whom all things willingly obey!

Ode 4. Heirmos:

Sitting in glory upon the throne of the Godhead, Jesus most divine came upon a light cloud, and by an incorruptible arm He saved those who cry: Glory to Thy power, O Christ!

Having extolled the all-sacred choir of Martyrs, they sacredly glorified the Lord in their bodies, Who is glorified by all the Angels; and they pray that we may be delivered from all affliction!

Possessing the light of immaterial understanding, the divine Hierarchs dispersed the night of all deception, and by unerring guidance they guide the God-chosen flock of Christ unto comprehension!

The venerable multitude of the holy ascetics was adorned, and the unique festivity of godly women was magnified; the holy choir of Prophets was honored, being united with the angelic hosts, rejoicing!

Having become fellow citizens with the Angels, O holy Martyrs, ask relief for all who entreat you, and dwelling in the spiritual paradise, and perfect remission of transgressions!

Thou Who didst preserve Her as a Virgin after childbearing unblemished, the Virgin choir glorifies Thee Who standest before all; with them unceasingly intercede, that our souls may be saved from all affliction and assault!

*Another Canon. Heirmos: Beholding Thee, the Sun of righteousness, lifted up...*

The Martyrs were seen as luminaries, enlightening the firmament of the Church; they ask of Christ the Savior to grant relief unto the reposed!

[f. 133vB] Having the Cross of Christ as a rod of strength, Thy servants traversed the sea of this life; settle them upon Thy holy mountain, O Lord, wherein Thou hast established holiness!

The beloved dwellings of the departed, which Thou hast chosen, O Master, and which Thou hast received, Thy servants: vouchsafe to dwell therein, as Thou art compassionate, where the righteous spirits abide. Theotokion:

He Who delivers those held by cruel death, having been incarnate as man from Thee, O Mother of God, the Immortal One endured death in the flesh, destroying the power of death!

Ode 5. Heirmos:[^211]

Thou, O Lord, art my light, Who camest into the world, a holy light turning those who sing unto Thee in faith from the darkness of ignorance!

Being lifted up upon the Cross, and crushed with clubs, and severed limb from limb, the valiant Martyrs did not deny the God Who gave them life!

Having become faithful saviors, O Hierarchs, ye followed the Lamb and Shepherd, having received to save those who were entrusted unto you!

Ye separated yourselves from worldly tumults, O Venerables; ye mortified your hearts from passions, and became sons unto the God of all. For the Departed:

Divine Patriarchs, and the assembly of women who pleased God: ask repose for those who have reposed before us!

God dwelt within Thee, O All-pure One; He made mortals into divine dwelling-places of His glory!

Another Canon. Same Heirmos:

Thou, O Lord, of Thy tender compassion didst glorify the Martyrs, and for their sake give rest unto the reposed, as Thou art tender-hearted!

[f. 134rA] Grant unceasing life, beautiful joy, and unending gladness unto those who have died before us, O Many-merciful One!

O Sun of the day and fountain of goodness: give rest unto those who have reposed in faith! Theotokion:

We sing of Thee, O Mother of God, through whom the ineffable and unapproachable beauty shone forth unto those in darkness, and in love we call Thee blessed!

Ode 6. Heirmos:

I came into the depths of the sea, and the storm of my many transgressions submerged me; but as God, raise up my life from corruption, O Many-merciful One!

As precious stones rolled wisely across the earth, O Martyrs, ye cast down the whole structure of impiety and became temples of God!

All the imitators, the Hierarchs, Righteous, and Venerables join hands like olive branches, who rule the flock in Christ; therefore ye are called blessed!

Following the prophetic teachings, the multitude of women pleased God the Word, both in sufferings and in ascetic struggles, Who is praised by the Virgin Maiden. For the Departed:

O Life of all the dead, who in faith have departed from this naked world unto Thee the Creator: vouchsafe them to dwell in light with Thy Saints, O Merciful One! Theotokion:

With mouth, tongue, and heart I confess Thee, O Maiden, as the pure Mother of our God; and by Thine intercession deliver me from eternal condemnation!

[f. 134rB] Another Canon. Heirmos:

I shall sacrifice unto Thee with a voice of praise, O Lord:

The divine spear that pierced Thy side, having blunted the turning sword, O Savior: give rest unto Thy servants, through the supplications of Thy Passion-bearers!

Suspended upon the tree, O my Savior, Thou didst open paradise; lead therein those who have reposed in faith, as Thou art compassionate, and show them to be partakers of Thy life!

Vouchsafe those who in piety have passed away by death unto Thee, O Lady, to enjoy the pasture of life, and number them with the Venerables from all ages! Theotokion:

The Word, being the invisible Son of God, became ineffably incarnate of the Virgin Maiden, and by His death destroyed death!

Ode 7. Heirmos:

The Abrahamite youths of old in Babylon trampled upon the flame of the furnace, crying aloud in hymns: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

As sacred vessels unto Christ, ramparts and pillars of the Church, let us in gladness of soul sing harmoniously of the Lord's Martyrs!

The Hierarchs of Christ and the divine choir of all the Venerables rejoice with the hosts on high; by their prayers, O Christ, save those who sing unto Thee!

Ye followed what is good, O holy women, and shining forth valiantly in suffering, ye cast down the deceiver who had wounded our race!

Thou Who didst despoil hades and trample upon death by Thy death: give rest unto those whom Thou hast translated in faith!

[f. 134vA] give rest, and show them to be dwellers of paradise, O Compassionate One! Theotokion:

Beholding the flame which of old did not consume the bush, the Lawgiver was instructed concerning the image of Thy childbearing, O ever-blessed Virgin Mother of God!

Another Canon. Heirmos:

In the furnace the Abrahamite youths:

Accepting the endurance, patience, and blood of all the Martyrs, O Savior, give rest unto those who in piety have reposed, as Thou art merciful and a changer of wills!

O Savior, Who didst number with Thy firstborn and righteous ones the souls of Thy servants translated unto Thee: vouchsafe them unceasingly to enjoy Thee, Who rulest over all!

In gladness, boldness, and radiant light, O Word of God, our Deliverer: well-please that those whom Thou hast received in mercy may meet Thee upon the clouds! Theotokion:

Rejoice, O blessed Virgin Mother of God, for through Thee destruction of death in truth took place, and unassailable life was granted unto mortals!

Ode 8. Heirmos:

O Deliverer of all, all-powerful One, Who didst descend into the midst of the flame and bedew the holy youths, and didst teach them to sing: All ye works of the Lord, bless the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto the ages!

Hierarchs, Prophets, and Martyrs, having finished the sacred contest, ye obtained a sacred dwelling with the Angels; with them ask cleansing and great mercy for us all!

[f. 134vB] Illumined by the Spirit, the Venerables destroyed the demonic darkness; together with them, the Hieromartyrs, Hierarchs, Rulers, and Righteous praise God in songs of laudation!

He who formerly boasted in godlessness to destroy the earth and sea is ever trampled underfoot by women, who with zealous devotion follow Christ in suffering and fasting!

For all who have reposed in faith we entreat Thee, O Christ: as Thou art tender-hearted, number them among the choir of the saved, who unceasingly cry out: All ye works of the Lord, bless the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto the ages! Theotokion:

Vouchsafe me Thy mercy, O Mother of God and Lady, who didst bear the all-merciful Word, and save me who cry: All ye works of the Lord, bless the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto the ages!

Another Canon. Heirmos:

Daniel stretched out his hands:

Receiving the supplications of the Martyrs and Thy mercy toward our kinsmen, O Master, give rest unto the souls of those who have reposed in Thy faith, overlooking their sins, who cry aloud unto Thee: All ye works of the Lord, bless the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto the ages!

Thou wast numbered among the lawless as dead; yet Thou didst pour forth immortal life unto the dead; therefore vouchsafe Thy translated servants, who hope in the Resurrection, to obtain Thy Kingdom, O Savior, who cry unto Thee: All ye works of the Lord, bless the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto the ages!

O [f. 135rA] fountain of grace, receive in Thy heavenly dwellings Thy servants who have passed away and left this corruptible life, O Savior, receiving in reconciliation those who cry unto Thee: All ye works of the Lord, bless the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto the ages!

Thou alone wast revealed upon earth, O Pure Virgin, an unwedded Mother; for Thou didst bear God, O Lady, beyond word and understanding, and didst pour forth common life unto the dead; therefore we all bless Thee, O Mary, Bride of God!

Ode 9. Heirmos:[^212]

Eve indeed, through the disease of disobedience, brought in the curse; but Thou, O Virgin Theotokos, through the blossoming of Thy childbearing, hast made blessing to flower forth unto the world; therefore we all magnify Thee!

Beholding the divine gifts, O Martyrs, and receiving great recompense for their sufferings, they rejoice, magnifying Christ, Who in truth hath magnified them and shown them to be victorious!

As ones appointed to shepherd the people, O Hierarchs, heralds of God, and as ones enlightened by fasting, O Venerables, ye shone forth more consolingly than the sun, illuminating the faithful by the manifestation of great works!

Together with the Hieromartyrs and with all the Prophets, let us bless all the Venerables, righteous ones, and women who brightly pleased God; by their prayers, O Christ, deliver our souls from gehenna! For the Departed:

Of that joy which the Saints obtained who well-pleased Thee: vouchsafe those who have reposed in Thee with faith [f. 135rB] to be partakers, O Christ, overlooking their sins, O Lord, Who alone art many-merciful! Theotokion:

Higher than the Cherubim on high, O all-immaculate one, as Thou didst bear the Upholder of all: make my mind higher than carnal passions, strengthening me, O Lady, to do His will!

Another Canon. Same Heirmos:

Thou hast given unto the true sufferers and Martyrs boldness to entreat Thee; grant therefore divine deliverance unto those who have reposed in faith, through their supplications, granting great things in the dwelling-place of the Saints, O Lord!

By Thine all-effective beckoning, Who orderest all things for good, possessing authority over the living and ruling over the dead as all-powerful: place Thy servants whom Thou hast translated beside the waters of repose!

Thou Who art good by nature, and rich in mercies and goodness, deliver from outer darkness those who call upon Thy Name; having justified them by faith, enlighten them by grace, as Thou art the Lover of mankind! Theotokion:

The Prophets proclaimed the types of Thy childbearing, O all-immaculate one, while others pre-eminently composed titles for Thee; for Thou didst bear Life unto those in hades, destroying the dominion of death!

At the Praises: Stichera to the Martyrs, Tone 4:

Who will not marvel, seeing [f. 135vA] O Martyrs, the good fight which ye have fought? How, being in the flesh, ye conquered the bodiless enemy, confessing Christ, and arming yourselves with the Cross? Therefore ye were worthily revealed as expellers of demons and vanquishers of barbarians, unceasingly praying that our souls may be saved!

Ye became partakers with the Angels, O holy Martyrs, having manfully preached Christ as heirs. For having forsaken all pleasant things in the world as non-existent, ye held fast unto the Cross as firm hope; therefore having driven away deception, ye grant unto the faithful gifts of healing, unceasingly praying that our souls may be saved!

How can we fail to marvel at your struggle, O holy Martyrs? For being clad in a mortal body, ye conquered bodiless foes. The threats of the tormentors terrified you not, nor did the infliction of tortures frighten you; therefore ye are worthily glorified by Christ!

Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His saints; for with sword and fire and contrite soul they poured forth their blood, having hope in Thee, to receive the reward of their labors; having endured, they received from Thee, O Savior, great mercy!

In Thy resting-place, O Lord, where all Thy Saints repose: give rest unto Thy reposed servants, as Thou art the only Lover of mankind!

O only pure and all-immaculate Virgin, who didst bear God without seed: pray that our souls may be saved!

[f. 135vB] *At the Aposticha, Stichera for the Departed, Tone 4.*

*Podoben: "Thou hast given a sign" (Да́лъ єсѝ зна́менїе):*

Truly dread is the mystery of death, how the soul is violently parted from the body, severed from the harmony and natural bond by divine will! Therefore we pray Thee: grant repose unto the translated, in the tabernacles of Thy righteous ones, O Life-giving Lover of mankind!

Death appears as sleep unto those who grieve; for Thou wast placed in the tomb, Who rulest over all, and didst shatter the dominion of death, bringing to naught its ancient violence! Therefore we pray Thee: place the translated in the light of Thy Saints, and in the splendor of the righteous!

Thou wast made righteousness and sanctification unto us, and deliverance for our souls; for Thou didst bring us justified and redeemed unto the Father, having taken upon Thyself our due condemnation. And now we pray Thee, grant repose unto the translated, in the joy and brightness of Thy Saints, O Benefactor and Lover of mankind!

Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion, Tone 4:

Following the words of the God-inspired Prophets, O All-immaculate One, we profess Thee as Mother of God; for Thou didst ineffably give birth unto God incarnate, Who delivered us from burning transgressions; Whom now entreat to illumine with His radiance Thy reposed servants, O All-pure One!

# TONE 5: SATURDAY VESPERS, SUNDAY MATINS, AND WEEKDAY OFFICES

## TONE 5 [^213]

## SATURDAY EVENING: VESPERS (TONE 5)

[f. 137rA] ON SATURDAY AT LITTLE VESPERS:[^214]

We set 4 verses, and we sing Resurrectional Stichera, Tone 5:

[f. 137rA] By Thy precious Cross, O Christ, Thou didst put the devil to shame; and by Thy Resurrection Thou didst blunt the sting of sin, and didst save us from the gates of death. We glorify Thee, O Only-begotten One!

He Who grants Resurrection unto the human race was led as a sheep to the slaughter; the princes of hades were terrified of Him, and the gates of sorrow were lifted up. For Christ, the King of glory, entered in, saying unto those in bonds: Come forth! and unto those in darkness: Uncover yourselves!

A great wonder! The Creator of the invisible, having suffered in the flesh through love of mankind, the Immortal One is risen! Come, all ye families of the nations, let us worship Him; for having been delivered from deception by His compassion, we have learned to hymn one God in three Hypostases!

Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion:

Rejoice, noetic door, through which the Chief Illuminator, God, passed! Rejoice, rod of Aaron, that didst blossom forth a flower from the root of Jesse! Rejoice, Table that didst provide the Bread of Life as food [f. 137rB] unto all the human race, O Virgin Pure Mother!

At the Aposticha, Resurrectional Sticheron, Tone 5:

Thee, Who wast incarnate, Christ the Savior, and yet wast not separated from heaven, we magnify with voices of song; for as the Lover of mankind, O Lord, Thou didst accept the Cross and death for our race, and having crushed the gates of hades, Thou didst rise on the third day, saving our souls!

*Other Stichera to the Most-holy Theotokos, Tone 5.*

*Podoben: "Rejoice, O life-bearing Cross" (Ра́дꙋйся живоно):*

*Verse: Virgins shall be brought unto the King after her, her companions shall be brought unto Thee.*

Accept, O tender-hearted Mother of God, this singing from unworthy souls and from our defiled lips, as the widow's two mites, brought thankfully with love. Bestowing great things in return for small by Thy grace, deliver Thy suppliants from every assault and malice, O Lady, dissolving the walls of present approaching affliction; as Thou art wise, calm them by Thy glorious prayers, and [f. 137vA] granting great mercy!

*Verse: The rich among the people shall entreat thy countenance.*

Truly a Cherubic Throne wast Thou revealed, being higher than creation; for having received God the Word, Who desired to renew our form, He dwelt in Thee, O All-pure One, and came forth from Thee clad in flesh, as He is tender-hearted; He accepted the Cross and Passion for our sake, and as God granted the Resurrection. Therefore, knowing that Thou hast reconciled our condemned nature unto the Creator, O Virgin, thankfully we pray: through Thine intercessions may we obtain forgiveness and remission of transgressions!

*Verse: I will remember thy name in every generation and generation.*

My soul having been continually burdened with darkness, O Lady, from the multitude of sins and cruel bonds: I dare not look up unto the height of God. Therefore, prostrate upon the earth...

<!-- Physical Woodcut: The Crucifixion of Christ with the Theotokos and St. John the Theologian; inscribed IC XC, MP OY, ICWA, NI KA --> [f. 137vB] I cry aloud unto Thee: Have mercy on me! O Thou Who didst cause the all-merciful God to shine forth from Thy most-pure womb, show forth Thy wonders now ineffably; and lifting up Thy hands unto Thy Son, O All-pure One, send down great mercy upon me who pray!

Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion:

Who can worthily call Thee, O pure Mother of God? Shall I name Thee the God-receiving Church? Or the Garden of Eden? Or Noah's glorious Ark of salvation? The Dominion of God the King of all? The Holy Nation? The Abode of Christ our God? For Thou wast likened unto the Ark of Moses, having within the cleansing and the blossomed Rod, the Candlestick, the Urn, and the all-golden Censer; unto which every believer flees and asks great mercy!

[f. 138rA] ON SATURDAY AT GREAT VESPERS:[^215]

Resurrectional Stichera, Tone 5.

Work of John of Damascus.

[f. 138rA] By Thy precious Cross, O Christ, Thou didst put the devil to shame; and by Thy Resurrection Thou didst blunt the sting of sin, and didst save us from the gates of death. We glorify Thee, O Only-begotten One!

He Who grants Resurrection unto the human race was led as a sheep to the slaughter; the princes of hades were terrified of Him, and the gates of sorrow were lifted up. For Christ, the King of glory, entered in, saying unto those in bonds: Come forth! and unto those in darkness: Uncover yourselves!

A great wonder! The Creator of the invisible, having suffered in the flesh through love of mankind, the Immortal One is risen! Come, all ye families of the nations, let us worship Him; for having been delivered from deception by His compassion, we have learned to hymn one God in three Hypostases!

[f. 138rB] Other Stichera, Anatolian (Eastern), Tone the same:

We offer evening worship unto Thee, the Unwaning Light, Who at the end of the ages, as in a glass, didst shine forth in the flesh unto the world, and descended even unto hades, and shattered the darkness therein, and showed forth the light of the Resurrection unto the nations. O Light-giver, Lord, glory to Thee!

Let us glorify Christ, the Author of our salvation; for when He was risen from the dead, the world was saved from deception. The angelic choir rejoices, and demonic deceit flees away; fallen Adam is raised, and the devil is brought to naught!

The guards who were instructed by the lawless to conceal the Resurrection of Christ received pieces of silver and said: While we slept, the dead man was stolen from the tomb [f. 138vA] Who hath ever seen, or who hath heard, that a corpse was stolen at any time, especially one anointed with myrrh and naked, leaving behind his grave-clothes in the tomb? Be not deceived, O Jews! Learn the sayings of the Prophets, and understand that He is in truth the Redeemer of the world, and All-powerful!

O Lord, Who didst despoil hades and trample upon death, our Savior, and didst enlighten the world by Thy precious Cross: have mercy on us!

Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion (Dogmatikon), Tone 5:[^216]

In the Red Sea of old an image of the unwedded Bride was prefigured. There Moses was the divider of the water; here Gabriel was the minister of the wonder. Then Israel traversed the deep dry-shod; now the Virgin hath borne Christ without seed. The sea, after the passage of Israel, remained impassable; the Immaculate One, after the childbearing of Emmanuel, remained incorrupt. O Thou Who art, and Who wast before, and hast appeared as man, O God: have mercy on us!

At the Aposticha, Resurrectional Stichera, Tone 5:

Thee, Who wast incarnate, Christ the Savior, and yet wast not separated from heaven, we magnify with voices of song; for as the Lover of mankind, O Lord, Thou didst accept the Cross and death for our race, and having crushed the gates of hades, Thou didst rise on the third day, saving our souls!

Other Stichera according to the Alphabet:

*Verse: The Lord is King, He is robed in majesty.*

[f. 138vB] When Thy side was pierced, O Life-giver, Thou didst pour forth streams of forgiveness unto all, life and salvation; and having accepted death in the flesh, Thou didst bestow immortality upon us. And taking up dwelling in the tomb, Thou didst set us free, co-resurrecting us with Thyself gloriously, as God. Therefore we cry aloud: O Lover of mankind, Lord, glory to Thee!

*Verse: For He hath established the world, so that it cannot be moved.*

Strange is Thy Crucifixion, and Thy descent into hades, O Lover of mankind! For having despoiled it, and co-resurrected with Thyself gloriously the ancient prisoners, as God, Thou didst open paradise, and vouchsafed them to enjoy it. Therefore, unto us who glorify Thy three-day rising, grant cleansing of sins, making us dwellers of paradise, as Thou alone art tender-hearted!

*Verse: Holiness becomes Thine house, O Lord, unto length of days.*

Thou Who for our sake didst accept suffering in the flesh, and on the third day didst rise from the dead: heal our carnal passions, and raise us up from cruel transgressions, O Lover of mankind, and save us!

Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion:

Thou art the Temple and the Door, the Palace and the Throne of the King, O all-pure Virgin; from whom my Deliverer, Christ the Lord, appeared unto those sleeping in darkness, being the Sun of righteousness, desiring to enlighten those whom He fashioned according to His own image with His own hand. Therefore, O All-hymned One, as Thou hast acquired maternal boldness toward Him: unceasingly pray, that our souls [f. 139rA] may be saved!

Resurrection Troparion, Tone 5:

Let us, the faithful, hymn and worship the Word, co-unoriginate with the Father and the Spirit, Who was born of the Virgin for our salvation; for He was well-pleased to ascend the Cross in the flesh, to endure death, and to resurrect the dead by His glorious Resurrection!

Theotokion:

Rejoice, impassable gate of the Lord! Rejoice, rampart and protection of those who flee unto Thee! Rejoice, unstormed haven, rejoice, O unwedded Mother, who didst bear in the flesh Thy Creator and God! Pray unceasingly for those who praise and worship Thy childbearing!

## SUNDAY MIDNIGHT OFFICE (TONE 5)

On Sunday at the Midnight Office:[^217]

Canon to the Holy and Life-giving Trinity.

Work of Metrophanes.

Ode 1. Tone 5. Heirmos:

The steed and rider into the Red Sea:

Singing of the light of the single and tri-hypostatic countenance, we pray: Enlighten our mind, O Almighty God, and raise it up unto Thine ineffable glory!

The choir of immaterial angelic beauties unceasingly sings of Thee with thrice-holy hymns: the tri-radiant Unity and the perfect Trinity!

O pre-eternal and all-powerful One, grant unto my soul the paternal drink of Thy sweet, light-giving love, O Trinity, light-originating Unity; and divine, purifying compunction, as Thou art many-merciful unto all creation!

[f. 139rB] As rain upon the fleece, O Virgin, the divine dew descended invisibly into Thy womb from heaven, and saved parched human nature, O All-pure One!

Ode 3. Heirmos:

Thou Who upon nothing didst establish the noetic essences by Thy thought, and didst constitute them as unceasing chanters of Thy Godhead, O Tri-radiant God and Creator of all: receive also from mortals and earthborn beings praise and supplication, as Thou art tender-hearted!

Inaccessible unto any natural change, unto us who are mutable and lost: O unfathomable fountain of Thy goodness, grant remission of transgressions, O three-sunned Sun of glory!

We glorify the Father, the Son, and the Spirit: in the unchangeable countenance of the Godhead, the Trinity, the single and thrice-shining Lord of all; as the Prophets and Apostles were clearly instructed by Thee. Theotokion:

Thou didst appear unto Moses in the bush as the Angel of Great Counsel of the Almighty, prefiguring Thine incarnation from the Virgin, O Word of God, through which Thou didst refashion us, and didst lead us up unto heaven!

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 5.*

*Podoben: "The Word co-unoriginate" (Собезнача́лно Сло́во):*

Thou art merciful, O undivided Trinity, and Thou hast compassion upon all as Thou art all-powerful, and as Thou art all-compassionate God and many-merciful. Therefore we flee unto Thee, weighed down by many transgressions, crying aloud: Purify Thy servants, deliver from every torment, and save us all!

[f. 139vA] O all-hymned Virgin, have mercy on us who flee with faith unto Thee Who art tender-hearted, and who ask Thy warm intercession; for Thou art able, as Thou art good, to save all, being the Mother of the Most High God, ever offering holy prayers, O Thou full of divine grace!

Ode 4. Heirmos:

Understanding Thy divine condescension with foresight, O Christ, Habbakuk cried aloud unto Thee with trembling: Unto salvation of Thy people, to save Thine anointed, art Thou come!

Daniel was secretly instructed concerning the one Tri-hypostatic Lord, seeing Christ as Son of Man going unto the Father, and prefiguring the vision of the Spirit!

With clay lips we hymn Thee, the pre-essential God in three Hypostases; vouchsafe us, being of a unified nature, angelic glory: one power and one Lordship in three Persons we indivisibly glorify: O Father, Son, and Spirit, enlighten us Thy servants! Theotokion:

The holy and overshadowed mountain which Habbakuk foresaw of old, from whence the Holy One came forth, foretold the inviolable childbearing of Thy conception, O Virgin!

Ode 5. Heirmos:[^217]

Clothed with light as with a garment, rising early unto Thee I cry aloud: Enlighten my darkened soul, O Christ, as Thou alone art compassionate!

Thou Who out of goodness didst fashion man, and didst assemble him according to Thine own image: renew in me, O thrice-holy my God, as Thou art good and tender-hearted!

Do Thou Thyself guide me, O thrice-radiant Unity, unto the divine paths of salvation, and fill me with Thy radiance, as by nature God is unmeasured in power!

To behold the indivisible Light [f. 139vB] of Thy nature, distinguished by hypostatic characteristics, thrice-shining, unwaning: enlighten my heart with Thy rays! Theotokion:

As the Prophet foresaw Thee of old, O Pure and All-holy Virgin, as an open door unto the unwaning light, O Maiden, he recognized the dwelling-place of God!

Ode 6. Heirmos:

Surging with the storm of soul-corrupting passions, O Master Christ, calm the tempestuous sea, and lead me up from corruption, as Thou art compassionate!

O Tri-radiant Unity in three Persons, single in nature, conformed and equal in power, and in essence and will, as the Prophets foresaw, show forth the light of the Son unto Thy light!

O Tri-hypostatic Unity, possessing in three Persons one power and dominion: for by It all creation was constructed, and is renewed! Theotokion:

Deliverance from transgressions and from afflictions, as Thou art God, single and tri-radiant, send down unto Thy singer, through the supplications of the Mother of God!

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 5.*

*Podoben: "The Word co-unoriginate" (Собезна́чално Слово):*

Have mercy on me, O my Savior, have mercy on me! And reprove me not in Thy wrath, O Merciful One, nor enter into judgment with Thy servants in Thy compassions! For in truth, my countless transgressions appear before us; therefore I cry unto Thee: O Compassionate One, have mercy on me!

Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion:

In doubt concerning all things, I flee unto Thee, the hope of all and refuge of sinners and [f. 140rA] the humble, crying: I have sinned, and I remain in evils, unfeeling, wretch that I am! Have mercy on me before the end, convert me, and deliver Thy servant from every torment!

Ode 7. Heirmos:

The Lord God of our fathers, praised above all, extinguished the flame and bedewed the youths who sang with one accord: Blessed art Thou, O God!

Possessing an abyss of mercy, O Lord, and an unfathomable ocean of compassions: have mercy upon us who sing of Thee as the One God!

The thrice-radiant God of all, the sacredly sovereign, single and tri-hypostatic: Thee as God and Lord we hymn; grant remission of transgressions, as with boldness in faith we distinguish, yet divide not, the essence of God!

In the midst Thou didst glorify the Father, the Son, and the All-holy Spirit, co-unoriginate with the Father, the Blossom of the Godhead, co-eternal with the Spirit, granting life unto all mankind through the Virgin!

Ode 8. Heirmos:

Unto Thee, Creator of all, in the furnace, the youths, weaving a world-wide choir, sang: All ye works, chant unto the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto the ages!

Thou didst appear of old, O my God, unto Abraham in the form of three men, prefiguring the Trinity of the Godhead, as he sang of Thy single dominion!

Vouchsafe me now to look upon Thy beneficent rays, O Unapproachable Light, Father of compassions, Word, and Spirit, that I may render thanks unto Thee, singing unto the Lord of all!

From the Father God is pre-eternal; the Son is the Son born of the Father; and the Holy and Life-giving Spirit proceeds from the Father, being manifest through the Son!

[f. 140rB] Thou didst shine forth unto us from the three-sunned glory the single, all-radiant Christ the Lord, secretly teaching all to hymn one Godhead in three Persons unto the ages!

Ode 9. Heirmos:

Isaiah, dance! A Virgin hath conceived in the womb, and hath borne a Son, Emmanuel, God and man; Orient is His name: Whom magnifying, we call the Virgin blessed!

Human deeds cannot worthily hymn the Sovereign Unity; yet as we are able, daring through faith, O Sovereign, Co-enthroned Trinity, we offer glory and praise unto Thy dominion!

With hypostatic glory, the Cherubim and Seraphim praise the single-origin, tri-radiant God with unceasing mouths; receive also us sinners, O Lord, who magnify Thy dominion!

Three lights today upon the Cherubic Throne, and the Seraphim standing round about Thee, covering their faces with wings, cry aloud: Holy, Holy, Holy, Thrice-holy God, glorified in Thy three holy Persons! Theotokion:

As pure, immaculate, and Virgin, Thou didst bear the unchanging Son and God, Who delivers us from temptations; entreat Him now to send down remission of transgressions upon us!

## SUNDAY MATINS (TONE 5)

At Matins, after the Gospel: "God is the Lord and hath appeared unto us" in Tone 5. And we chant the Resurrection Troparion: "The Word co-unoriginate"; Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion: "Rejoice, impassable gate of the Lord"; then the usual Kathisma reading of the Psalter [f. 140vA] After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymns: Resurrectional, Tone 5:[^218]

Let us praise the Cross of the Lord, honor His holy Burial with songs, and glorify His Resurrection! For as God He raised the dead from the tombs, having despoiled the dominion of death and the might of the devil, and shone forth light unto those in hades!

Glory:

O Lord, after Thy three-day Resurrection and the worship of the Apostles, Peter cried aloud unto Thee: The women took courage, but I was afraid; the thief confessed Thee as God, but I denied Thee. Wilt Thou then call me still to be Thy disciple, or wilt Thou show me again as a fisher drawing men from the deep? But receive me in repentance, O God, and save me!

Now and ever... Theotokion:

Dread is the wonder of Thy conception, and ineffable the manner of Thy childbearing, made known in Thee, O Pure Ever-Virgin: my mind is astonished, and my thought is seized with awe, at Thy glory, O Theotokos, spread abroad unto all for the salvation of our souls!

After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns: Resurrectional, Tone 5:

O Lord, Thou wast called dead, Who didst put death to death; Thou wast placed in the tomb, Who didst empty the tombs. Above, the soldiers guarded the tomb; below, Thou didst resurrect the dead from all ages. O Almighty and Incomprehensible Lord, glory to Thee!

O Lord, between the condemned the lawless nailed Thee, and with a spear they pierced Thy side [f. 140vB] O Many-merciful One; and Thou didst accept burial, Who didst destroy the gates of hades, and didst rise on the third day! The women ran to see Thee, and announced the rising unto the Apostles. O Savior praised above all, Whom the Angels sing: Blessed art Thou, O Lord, glory to Thee!

Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion:

Rejoice, holy mountain, impassable to man! Rejoice, animate and unburned Bush! Rejoice, only bridge of the world unto God, leading mortals unto eternal life! Rejoice, incorrupt Maiden, who without knowing man didst bear the Salvation of our souls!

Hypakoe, Tone 5:

Terrifying the mind with angelic appearance, yet enlightening their souls with the divine rising, the Myrrh-bearing women proclaimed the good tidings unto the Apostles: Announce among the nations the Resurrection of the Lord, Who works wonders with you, and grants us great mercy!

Hymns of Ascents (Anavathmoi), Tone 5:[^219]

Antiphon 1:

When I am in affliction, like David I sing unto Thee, O my Savior: Deliver my soul from a deceitful tongue!

Unto those in the wilderness life is blessed, being borne aloft by divine desire!

By the Holy Spirit all things are upheld, visible and invisible; for being self-sovereign, He is truly One of the Trinity!

Antiphon 2:

[f. 141rA] Let us be lifted up unto the mountains, O my soul; go thither, whence help shall come!

May Thy right hand, O Christ, stretched forth over me, preserve me from all deception!

Unto the Holy Spirit, speaking of God, let us say: Thou art God, Life, Desire, Light, Mind; Thou art Goodness, Thou reignest unto the ages!

Antiphon 3:

Concerning those who said unto me: We will go into the courts of the Lord; being filled with great joy, I send up prayers!

In the house of David dread things are accomplished; for there fire burns every defiled mind!

Unto the Holy Spirit belongs the life-originating dignity: from Whom every living creature is animated, as in the Father, together with the Word!

Prokeimenon, Tone 5:

Arise, O Lord my God, let Thy hand be lifted up; for Thou reignest unto the ages!

*Verse: I will give thanks unto Thee, O Lord, with my whole heart; I will speak of all Thy marvelous works.*

Let every breath praise the Lord!

*Verse: Praise God in His saints; praise Him in the firmament of His power.*

Resurrection Gospel. We sing: Psalm 50 ("Have mercy on me, O God"). And the rest in order.

RESURRECTION CANON.

Ode 1. Tone 5. Heirmos:

The steed and rider into the Red Sea: Christ Who shatters warfare with a high arm shook them off; but He saved Israel, as they sang a song of victory!

[f. 141rB] The thorn-bearing Hebrew assembly, not preserving maternal love toward Thee, their Benefactor, O Christ, crowned Thee with thorns, Who didst loose the thorn-bearing sentence of the First-fashioned!

Having bowed down, O sinless Life-giver, Thou didst raise me up who had fallen into the pit; and without experiencing sin, O Christ, Thou didst endure my foul corruption, and didst perfume me with the myrrh of Thy divine essence! Theotokion:

The curse is dissolved, sorrow hath ceased; for the Blessed and Rejoicing One hath made joy to shine forth unto the faithful, bearing Christ the Blossom, a blessing unto all the ends of the earth!

Another Canon, of the Cross and Resurrection. Heirmos: Unto God the Savior:

Unto Him Who was willingly nailed upon the Cross in the flesh, and freed man who had fallen through the tree of the ancient sentence: unto Him alone let us sing, for He hath been glorified!

Unto Christ Who raised the dead from the tomb, and raised our nature with Himself, and adorned it with the Father's union: unto Him alone let us sing, for He hath been glorified! Theotokion:

O All-pure Mother of God, unceasingly pray unto God Who became incarnate of Thee and was not parted from the bosom of the Father, to deliver from every circumstance those whom He fashioned!

Another Canon to the Most-holy Theotokos.

*Heirmos: The steed and rider into the Red Sea...*

O All-pure One, pray unto Christ, the Light that dwelt within Thee and enlightened the world with the rays of His Godhead, to enlighten all who sing of Thee, O Virgin Mother!

[f. 141vA] Adorned with the beauty of virtues, O favored one, with the good-working, comely beams of the Spirit, all creation sings unto Him Who hath beautified all things.

The Bush on Sinai prefiguring Thee of old was not consumed, O Virgin, when united with the fire; for as a Virgin Thou didst give birth, and a Virgin Thou didst remain, beyond understanding, O Bride of God!

Ode 3. Heirmos:

Thou Who didst establish the earth upon nothing by Thy command, and didst suspend its uncontainable weight: upon the unshakable rock of Thy commandments, O Christ, establish Thy Church, O only Good and Lover of mankind![^220]

Gall indeed they offered Thee, O Jesus Christ, Who didst pour forth honey from the rock and didst work wonders in the wilderness; and vinegar they gave Thee in return for the manna, the ungrateful children of Israel!

They who of old were covered with a light-bearing cloud placed Christ the Life in a tomb; but having risen by Thine own power, Thou didst grant unto all the faithful the mystical overshadowing of the Spirit's radiance from on high.

Thou wast revealed without corruption to be the Mother of God, Who didst shine forth from the incorrupt Father without maternal travails; therefore we confess Thee in orthodox manner to be the Mother of God, having given birth unto the incarnate Word.

[f. 141vB] Another [Canon, of the Cross and Resurrection].

Heirmos: By the power of Thy Cross, O Christ:

Thou didst rise from the tomb, O Christ, delivering from corruption the dead who sing of Thy three-day Resurrection, O Life-giver!

The Myrrh-bearing women hastened to anoint Thy body, O Christ; and not finding it, they returned, singing of Thy rising!

Pray unceasingly, O pure one, unto Him Who came forth from Thy womb, to deliver from the deceit of the devil those who hymn Thee as the Mother of God!

Another [Canon to the Theotokos].

*Heirmos: Thou Who upon nothing didst establish the noetic...*

The ladder whereby the Most High came down unto us to restore corrupted nature: having truly appeared unto all as the gateway unto the portals of Heaven, the All-good One was well-pleased to share with the world.

The mystery prepared of old, O Virgin, foreseen before the ages by God Who knows all things, in these latter days hath received its fulfillment in Thy womb, O all-immaculate one.

The curse, the ancient condemnation, is loosed through Thy mediation, O all-pure Virgin; for the Lord, having appeared from Thee, hath poured forth blessing unto all as the All-good One, the only adornment of mankind!

Ode 4. Heirmos:

Perceiving Thy divine condescension with prophetic insight, O Christ, Habakkuk cried aloud unto Thee in trembling: Thou art come for the salvation of Thy people, to save Thine anointed ones!

Prefiguring in image Thy most-pure Cross, O Good One, which puts to death the sinful taste, Thou didst sweeten with wood the bitter waters of Marah!

The Cross in place of the tree of knowledge, gall in place of sweet food didst Thou receive, O my Savior; and in place of mortal corruption Thou didst pour forth Thy divine Blood!

[f. 142rA] Without union Thou didst conceive incorruptly in Thy womb, and without travail Thou didst give birth; and after childbirth Thou wast preserved a Virgin, having borne God in the flesh!

Another [Canon, of the Cross and Resurrection].

Heirmos: I heard the report of Thee:

At the place of the waters upon earth, the Cross was fixed on Golgotha; all the powers were shaken, and the veils in the heights were rent; and they cried: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

When the Savior descended unto those below as one dead, those who were dead from all ages arose with Him; and they cried: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

Thou didst bear the Good One, unknown unto mothers; yet Thou art indeed a Mother, and remainedst a Virgin; whom singing, we cry aloud: Rejoice, O Mother of God!

Another [Canon to the Theotokos].

*Heirmos: Perceiving Thy divine condescension with prophetic insight, O...*

With pure heart and mind, and action and contemplation, grant me invincible and unconquerable grace, O pure one, that embracing the fruit of salvation from God, I may be saved through Thy prayers, O Virgin!

He Who created all things from the unseen was well-pleased as Benefactor to be created in the flesh from Thee, unto the salvation of those who sing of Thee in faith and love, O all-immaculate one!

The supramundane choirs sing of Thy childbirth, O all-immaculate one, rejoicing in the salvation of those who truly confess Thee in godly wisdom, O undefiled Virgin!

The rod of Jesse named Thee, from which blossomed forth unto us the fair flower, Christ God, unto the salvation of those who sing of Thee in faith and love, O all-immaculate one!

[f. 142rB] Ode 5. Heirmos:

Thou Who clothest Thyself with light as with a garment, unto Thee I rise early and unto Thee I cry: Enlighten my darkened soul, O Christ, as the only Merciful One!

The Lord of glory, in inglorious form, hangs willingly dishonored upon the Tree, ineffably devising divine glory for me!

Thou didst reclothe me in incorruption, tasting mortal corruption in the flesh without corruption, and shining forth from the tomb on the third day!

Having given birth without seed unto Christ, our Righteousness and Redemption, Thou didst make the nature of the forefather free from the curse, O Mother of God!

Another [Canon, of the Cross and Resurrection].

Heirmos: Rising early we cry unto Thee:

Thou didst stretch forth Thy hands upon the Tree, O our Savior, calling all unto Thyself as the Lover of mankind!

Having risen from the tomb on the third day, O Life-giver, Thou didst pour forth most beloved immortality unto all!

Unceasingly pray unto Him Whom Thou didst bear, O Mother of God, to save our souls, who sing of Thee in godly wisdom!

Another [Canon to the Theotokos].

*Heirmos: Thou Who clothest Thyself with light as with...*

All the most-pure choirs, seeing that Thou wast to become the Mother of God, O most-pure Theotokos, found Thee alone to be pure and completely immaculate!

As a bright cloud of living water, raining down upon us Christ, the dew of incorruption, we know Thee, O pure one!

As the Good One, God Who dwelt in Thee, the only Compassionate One, loved all Thy beauty and undefiled maidenhood sealed with virginity!

[f. 142vA] Ode 6. Heirmos:

Calming the sea of passions, tossed by the soul-destroying tempest, O Master Christ, lead me up from corruption, as Thou art compassionate![^221]

Placed in corruption, the forefather, having tasted of the forbidden tree, O Master Christ, was led up unto life by Thy Passion!

Thou didst become Life, and wast crucified through corruption, O Master Christ; and through corruption Thou didst pour forth resurrection!

A Virgin gave birth, and having given birth remained pure: holding in her arms Him Who upholds all things, truly Thou didst bear Him, O Virgin Mother!

Another [Canon, of the Cross and Resurrection].

Heirmos: The deep surrounded me:

Thou didst stretch forth Thy hands, gathering together those scattered far off, through the congregation of Thy wounds, O Christ our God, by Thy life-bearing Cross, as the Lover of mankind!

Death was overthrown, and the gates of hades Thou didst shatter; and Adam who was bound, being loosed, cried aloud: Thy right hand hath saved me, O Lord!

Theotokion: As the unburned Bush, and the Mountain, and the animate Ladder, and the heavenly Gate, we worthily glorify Thee, O glorious Mary, praise of the Orthodox!

Another [Canon to the Theotokos].

Heirmos: Tossed by the tempest:

He Who is the Cause of all things, Who grants life unto all, received Thee as cause, becoming incarnate for our sake from Thee, O Mother of God, all-immaculate one!

Pouring forth a soul-nourishing fountain of healings, we know Thee, O all-immaculate one, who hasten with faith unto Thy glorious protection!

[f. 142vB] Thou didst give birth unto the Life-giver, the Cause of salvation, Who grants eternal redemption unto us who truly confess Thee to be the Mother of God!

Kontakion, Tone 5:
