*Podoben: "The Word co-unoriginate" (Собезнача́льное Сло́во):*

Unto hades, O my Savior, didst Thou descend, and having shattered its gates as Almighty, Thou didst resurrect the dead with Thyself as Creator; and Thou didst break the sting of death, and Adam was delivered from the curse, O Lover of mankind! Therefore we all cry: Save us, O Lord!

Ikos:

Hearing the angel's voice, the women put away their lamentation; becoming joyful and trembling, they beheld the vision; and behold, Christ stood before them, saying: Rejoice, take courage! I have conquered the world and freed the prisoners! Hasten therefore unto the disciples, announcing unto them: I go before you into the city of Galilee to preach. Therefore we all cry unto Thee: Save us, O Lord!

Ode 7. Heirmos:

The Lord praised by the fathers quenched the flame and bedewed the children, as they sang in unison: Blessed art Thou![^222]

Clothed in the flesh as bait upon a hook, by Thy divine power Thou didst draw down the serpent, leading up those who cry: Blessed art Thou!

The inaccessible nature of earth, being compounded in sin, the flesh covers, not bound by measure; unto Whom we all sing: Blessed art Thou!

In one hypostasis, yet in two natures, O all-immaculate one, Thou didst bear the incarnate God; unto Whom we all sing: Blessed art Thou!

Another [Canon, of the Cross and Resurrection].

Heirmos: In the fiery furnace:

He Who through the wood of the Cross destroyed the idolatrous deceit: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

Christ, Who by His own death destroyed the dominion of death: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

He Who was born of the Virgin, Whom He made the Mother of God: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

Another [Canon to the Theotokos].

*Heirmos: The Lord God of our fathers, praised above...*

Remaining uncircumscribed and immutable, in the flesh He united Himself hypostatically unto Thee, the most-holy, as Compassionate: the only blessed God of our fathers!

As undefiled and all-immaculate, O pure Mother of God, in unison we glorify Thee and the Throne of Thy Creator, unto Whom we all sing: Blessed art Thou!

Save me, O Lord, Who wast clothed from the Virgin Mother of God in the garment of the flesh; unto Whom we all sing: O God, blessed art Thou!

Ode 8. Heirmos:

Unto Thee, the Creator of all, the youth in the furnace, forming a universal choir, sang: All ye works of the Lord, sing praise unto the Lord, and exalt Him above all forever!

[f. 143rA] Mystically clothed in the passion of salvation, Thou didst pray concerning the cup, as voluntary; two wills, in two essences Thou dost bear, O Christ, unto the ages!

By Thy creative descent, O Christ, hades was mocked and cast forth all those put to death of old by deceit, who exalt Thee unto all the ages!

Thee Who beyond understanding didst give birth unto the Word, God and Man, and remainest a virgin, all ye works, O Virgin, we bless and exalt unto all the ages!

Another [Canon, of the Cross and Resurrection].

Heirmos: Him Who of old before the ages:

Him Who stretched forth His hands upon the Cross and shattered the dominion of death, Christ God: ye priests, sing praise, ye people, exalt Him above all forever!

Him Who shone forth from the tomb as a bridegroom, Christ God, and appeared unto the Myrrh-bearing women, proclaiming joy unto them: ye priests, sing praise, ye people, exalt Him above all forever!

Thou wast revealed higher than the Cherubim, O pure Mother of God, having carried in Thy womb Him Who is borne upon them; Whom with the bodiless hosts we earthborn bless and exalt unto all the ages!

Another [Canon to the Theotokos].

*Heirmos: Unto Thee, the Creator of all, the youth...*

O most-holy, pure one, sorrow is loosed, since Thou, the Mother of God, didst receive joy; therefore unceasingly we sing of Thee, and exalt Him above all forever!

The assembly of the bodiless hosts sings with us, O Virgin who didst bear God, the incomprehensible Unity [f. 143vA] forming a choir in love: and we exalt Him above all forever!

As a fire blossoming forth immortality, O incorrupt maiden, the Lord of all was revealed from Thee, washing away the defiled who sing in faith and exalt Him unto the ages!

The truly divine and light-bearing Throne, and tables of grace we confess Thee to be, O Virgin, who didst receive the Word; Whom we exalt unto the ages!

Ode 9. Heirmos:

Rejoice, O Isaiah! For a Virgin hath conceived in her womb and borne a Son, Emmanuel, God and Man; the Dayspring is His name; Whom magnifying, we call Thee blessed, O Virgin![^223]

Fallen man Thou didst take upon Thyself, O Master Christ, from virginal loins, uniting Thyself wholly; yet in no sin didst Thou share; from all passions Thou didst free him by Thy most-pure passions!

By the pouring forth of streaming blood from Thy most-pure and life-creating side, O Master, the idolatrous sacrifice ceased, and all the earth offers unto Thee the sacrifice of praise!

Neither as bodiless God nor merely as simple man did the pure and undefiled Maiden bring Thee forth, but as perfect man and truly perfect God; Whom magnifying, we call Thee blessed, O Virgin!

Thy childbirth is beyond understanding, O Mother of God; for conception was without a man in Thee, and virginal was Thy childbirth; for God is the One born; Whom magnifying, we call Thee blessed, O Virgin!

Another [Canon, of the Cross and Resurrection].

Heirmos: Thee Who art beyond understanding:

Him Who endured upon the Cross, slain in the flesh, and Who destroyed death by death, O Christ: we the faithful magnify with one mind!

Thee Who didst accept passion without dishonor, and didst despoil hades, and didst deliver the world from deceit, O Lover of mankind: we the faithful magnify with one mind!

Rejoice, O all-immaculate Mother of God, who didst bear Christ God; pray unto Him to grant remission of transgressions unto me who sing of Thee in faith!

Another [Canon to the Theotokos].

*Heirmos: Rejoice, O Isaiah! For a Virgin hath conceived...*

In streams of Thy blood let us extinguish the flesh beyond nature; giving birth unto the only-begotten Son, Creator of all, not of man, but without seed, an intelligent and animate Bush, O Virgin!

Thou didst prepare an entrance, the unrestrained assault of death being stayed; having truly given birth in the flesh, beyond understanding, unto eternal Life; by whose bitter assault hades was abolished, O most-holy Virgin Mother!

Sitting upon the throne, Thy Son, Who hath adorned Thee with the golden virtues of divine beauty, shining openly, placed Thee at His right hand, O pure one, giving honor unto Thee as His Mother, O Lover of mankind!

At the Praises: Resurrectional Stichera. Tone 5:

O Lord, though the tomb was sealed by the transgressors of the law, Thou didst come forth from the tomb, even as Thou wast born of the Mother of God! Thy bodiless Angels understood not how Thou wast incarnate; the soldiers who guarded Thee perceived not when Thou didst rise; for both were sealed unto those who examined them, but the wonders were revealed unto those who worship the mystery in faith and sing praise unto it: Grant unto us joy and great mercy!

[f. 144rA] O Lord, having shattered the eternal bars and broken the bonds, Thou didst rise from the tomb, leaving behind Thy grave-clothes as a testimony of Thy true three-day burial; and Thou didst go before into Galilee, Thou Who wast guarded in the cave! Great is Thy mercy, O incomprehensible Savior, have mercy on us!

O Lord, the women ran unto the tomb to see Thee, O Christ, Who didst suffer for our sake; and having come, they found an Angel sitting upon the stone, struck down with fear; and he cried aloud unto them, saying: The Lord is risen! Say unto His disciples that He is risen from the dead, saving our souls!

O Lord, even as Thou didst come forth from the sealed tomb, so didst Thou enter, while the doors were shut, unto Thy disciples, showing them the bodily passions which Thou didst endure, O long-suffering Savior; for as from the seed of David Thou didst endure wounds, and as the Son of God Thou didst free the world! Great is Thy mercy, O incomprehensible Savior, have mercy on us!

Other Stichera, Eastern:

O Virgin-born King of the ages and Creator of all, Who didst accept crucifixion and burial in the flesh for our sake, that Thou mightest free us all from hades: Thou art our God; besides Thee, we know no other!

O Lord, who shall declare Thy transcendent wonders, or who shall proclaim Thy dread mysteries?

[f. 144rB] For having become man for our sake as Thou Thyself didst will, Thou didst manifest the dominion of Thy power! By Thy Cross Thou didst open paradise unto the thief, and by Thy burial Thou didst shatter the bars of hades, and by Thy Resurrection Thou didst enrich all creation! O Compassionate Lord, glory to Thee!

*Verse: Arise, O Lord my God, let Thy hand be lifted up; forget not Thy poor unto the end.*

The Myrrh-bearing women, having reached Thy tomb very early, sought to anoint Thee, the immortal Word and God, with myrrh; and instructed by the voices of the Angel, they returned with joy to announce openly unto the Apostles that the Life of all is risen, granting purification and great mercy unto the world!

*Verse: I will give thanks unto Thee, O Lord, with my whole heart; I will speak of all Thy marvelous works.*

At Thy God-receiving tomb the guards said unto the Jews: O your vain-minded counsel! Compelling us to guard the Uncircumscribed One, in vain have ye labored! Wishing to conceal the Resurrection of the Crucified One, ye have preached it clearly! O your vain-minded gathering! Why do ye take counsel again to conceal what cannot be concealed? Rather hear from us and be willing to believe the truth that hath come to pass: The lightning-bearing Angel, descending from heaven, rolled away the stone, and from fear of him we were held fast as dead! And crying aloud unto the resolute Myrrh-bearing women, he said unto them: See ye not the guards become dead, and the seals loosed, [f. 144vA] and hades emptied? Why do ye declare Him as dead Who hath abolished the victory of hades and shattered the sting of death? Go quickly, announcing without fear unto the Apostles: Truly the Lord is risen, He Who hath great mercy![^224]

AT THE DIVINE LITURGY.

The Beatitudes (Makarismoi). Tone 5:

The thief upon the cross, believing Thee to be God, O Christ, confessed Thee purely from the heart: Remember me, O Lord, crying aloud in Thy kingdom!

Unto Him Who from the wood of the Cross caused life to blossom forth for our race, and dried up the curse that came from the tree, as Savior and Creator let us sing!

Crucified with Thee, O Christ, between two condemned thieves: the one indeed blaspheming Thee was justly condemned; but the other, confessing Thee to be God, was settled in paradise!

By Thy death, O Christ, Thou didst destroy the power of death, and didst raise up [f. 144vB] those dead from all ages, who sing of Thee, the true God and our Savior!

Having come unto Thy tomb, O Christ, the venerable women sought to anoint Thee, the Life-giver, with myrrh; and an Angel appeared unto them, crying aloud: Truly the Lord is risen!

The preaching of Thine Apostles hath filled the whole earth, O Christ, and driven away the night of godlessness, illumining all the faithful with the light of understanding!

Glory... Triadikon:

We worship Thee, O Trinity, Unity unoriginate and consubstantial, and we glorify Thee with the heavenly ranks: Thou art the Savior, the unoriginate God, the invincible Trinity!

Now and ever... Theotokion:

Having shown us joy in deed by Thy childbirth, O all-immaculate one, we cry unto Thee: Rejoice! crying aloud with the Angel: Rejoice, Mother of the true God and our Savior!

## SUNDAY EVENING VESPERS (TONE 5)

ON SUNDAY EVENING, AT "LORD, I HAVE CRIED":

Penitential Stichera, Tone 5.

*Podoben: "Rejoice, O container of ascetics" (Ра́дꙋйся по́стникѡвъ):* [^225]

I weep and lament bitterly, contemplating the dread retribution of the Word; having no answer from my deeds, not even a small one, against my guilt, wretched that I am! Therefore I pray: before the unknown hour of my end shall overtake me, before the sickle of death [f. 145rA] before I am to receive condemnation where the fire is unquenchable and the outer darkness, and where is the worm, and the gnashing of teeth, and the burning of those who have sinned: grant me deliverance from my transgressions, O my Christ, and great mercy!

Despising Thy laws and commandments, wretched that I am, O my God, my Creator, how shall I escape henceforth the torment there, O Savior? Therefore, before my end, O Savior, grant me forgiveness, giving me tears through the prayers of Thy saints, driving far from me the demon hosts that seek to bring me down into the abyss of hades! Therefore I pray Thee: take not Thy sovereign right hand away from me!

Woe is me, how have I been blinded in mind! How have I departed from Thee, and worked passionately for sin and the passion of the flesh! I have delivered up my whole self, wretched that I am! And now I await my departure from life, and the torment that is to be reaped by such as I, a passionate one! O All-good Lord, grant me tearful repentance and remission of my countless transgressions, I faithfully pray Thee, Who grantest great mercy unto the world!

Other Stichera to the Bodiless Hosts. Same tone and melody:

O honorable Trinity-bearers of the divine Principality, of the most-bright and single Godhead, who unceasingly offer a hymn with bodiless voices and tongues of fire: offer our supplications and prayers which we send up from defiled lips, and ask remission of our transgressions! For He knows our infirmity, having clothed Himself with it; and being merciful by nature, He will receive your supplications, healing those who have sinned, unto Whom we sing:

[f. 145rB] Granting great mercy unto the world!

O divine multitude of Angels, who draw near unto my Master and stand with fear before His divine Throne, and are filled with ineffable brightness: guide unto the light of salvation him who hath wandered into the darkness of sin, by the command of the merciful God! Drive away the dark and alien gloom of crafty demons by your protection and grace; for they cannot endure the bright coming, but are driven away!

When ye stand with the saints of God before the Throne of grace, being in divine peace and receiving true enlightenment from the divine Light: look down from thence, O lovers of mankind, upon those who wander in the fierce confusion of the world-ruler and sleep in darkness! Come therefore, O Archangels, unto our aid, and deliver us from the snares of the origin-of-evil enemy; for unto your protection we all flee, O all-praised ones!

Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion:

Having truly been revealed as the Cherubic Throne, being higher than the Angels, for the divine Word of God, wishing to renew the form of man, dwelt in Thee, O pure one, coming forth from Thee bearing flesh, as He is merciful! He accepted the Cross and death for our sake, and granted the Resurrection as God! Therefore, as the most glorious renewal of fallen nature, with faith we pray unto the Creator, giving thanks: that through Thy prayers we may obtain forgiveness of transgressions and great mercy!

[f. 145vA] At the Aposticha, Penitential Stichera. Tone 5:

O Lord, I cease not from sinning; yet being deemed worthy of Thy love toward mankind, I perceive not my lack of understanding! Overcome my darkness, O only Good One, and have mercy on me!

O Lord, I fear Thy terror, yet cease not from doing evil! Who, standing before the tribunal, fears not the judge? Or who, wishing to be healed, provokes the physician to wrath, as I do? O long-suffering Lord, have compassion upon my weakness, and have mercy on me!

To the Martyrs: Despising all earthly things and manfully daring the torments, ye missed not the blessed hopes, but became heirs of the heavenly Kingdom, O all-praised Martyrs! Having boldness toward God, the Lover of mankind, ask peace for the world, and for our souls great mercy!

Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion:

A dread and most-glorious and great mystery! The Uncontainable One was contained in the womb, and the Mother remained a Virgin after childbirth; for she gave birth unto God, incarnate of her! Unto Him let us speak a song, singing with the Angels: Holy art Thou, O unoriginate Christ, Who for our sake didst become man: glory to Thee!

## MONDAY MATINS: REPENTANCE AND THE BODILESS POWERS (TONE 5)

ON MONDAY AT MATINS.[^226]

After the 1st Kathisma, Penitential Sessional Hymns. Tone 5:

When the Judge shall sit and the Angels stand by, the trumpet sounding and the flame burning: what wilt thou do, O my soul, led [f. 145vB] unto judgment? For then thy fierce deeds shall confront thee, and thy secret transgressions shall be exposed! Therefore, before the end, cry aloud unto the Judge: O God, cleanse me and save me!

Let us all be watchful and meet Christ with abundance of oil and with bright lamps, that we may be accounted worthy of the bridal chamber within; for he who is found outside the doors shall cry in vain unto God: Have mercy on me!

Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion:

Holier than the Cherubim and higher than the Seraphim, O most-pure one, truly confessing Thee to be the Mother of God, we sinners have Thee as protectress, and find salvation in time of temptations! Therefore unceasingly praying unto her, she is a sovereign protection and refuge for our souls!

After the 2nd Kathisma, Penitential Sessional Hymns. Tone 5:

O soul, the things here are temporal, but the things there are eternal! Behold the tribunal, and the Judge upon the throne, and tremble at the reckoning! Turn back henceforth with diligence; the judgment grants no pardon!

Upon the bed I lie of many transgressions, despoiled of the hope of my salvation; for the sleep of my slothfulness procures torment for my soul! But do Thou, O Christ, born of the Virgin, raise me up unto Thy praise, that I may glorify Thee!

To the Martyrs: The memory of the passion-bearers shines today, for it hath radiance from Heaven! The angelic choir celebrates, and the race of men keeps feast together!

[f. 146rA] Therefore they pray: O Lord, have mercy on our souls!

Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion:

With the heavenly Angels and with earthly men, in the voice of rejoicing, O Mother of God, we cry aloud unto Thee: Rejoice, O Gate, wider than heaven! Rejoice, only salvation of earthborn men! Rejoice, pure favored one, who didst bear the incarnate God!

After the 3rd Kathisma, Penitential Sessional Hymns. Tone 5.

*Podoben: "The Word co-unoriginate" (Собезнача́льное Сло́во):*

I tremble exceedingly at the dread tribunal and the righteous Judge's sentence: I shall not be justified, my conscience convicts me! Living in negligence, I am perplexed and held fast with fear; but by your holy supplications deliver me from the fire, O ye Archangels, keepers and beacons unto the ends of the earth!

Cast down by irrational passions, having squandered my life in prodigality: call me back, O Savior, as the prodigal, and in the mercy of Thy compassions stretch forth Thy fatherly embrace and receive me: through the prayers of the Bodiless Hosts, grant me mine ancient honor!

Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion:

O fervent protectress, invincible hope, firm and unashamed, wall and protection and haven of those who flee unto Thee, O ever-virgin pure one: with the Angels pray unto Thy Son and God to grant peace unto the world, and salvation, and great mercy!

[f. 146rB] PENITENTIAL CANON.

Work of Joseph.

Ode 1. Tone 5. Heirmos:

Let us sing unto the Lord, Who wrought marvelous miracles in the Red Sea, a song of victory, for He hath been glorified!

Seduced and deceived by many guiles of the alien, O Christ: turn me back and have compassion on me, as Thou art almighty!

O Christ, Who didst open the ears of the deaf man: open the deafened ears of my soul, that I may give ear unto Thy words!

To the Martyrs: Being unshakable stars of the righteous Sun, Christ, O Martyrs: drive away the darkness from our hearts!

Ye quenched the fiery darts with the divine fire of the Spirit, appearing as sufferers, shattering all the darts of the serpent!

Theotokion: O Gate of divine glory, open unto me the gates of repentance, and snatch my humble soul from the gates of hades, I pray Thee!

Another Canon to the Bodiless Hosts.

*Heirmos: The steed and rider into the Red Sea...*

Initiates of the light-bestowing Divine Principality, ignited foremost by Its beams: pray unto the Master, O Angels, to enlighten my soul with light!

Having boldness as those who stand before the lofty Throne: deliver those who sing of you in godly manner, O leaders of the immaterial rank, O Chief Commanders!

The curse is loosed and sorrow hath ceased; for the Blessed and Favored One, joy of all the faithful, bearing Christ the Blossom, is a blessing unto all the ends of the earth!

[f. 146vA] Ode 3. Heirmos:

The Lord reigns over the nations; God sits upon His holy throne: and let us sing unto Him with understanding, as King over all!

Thou Who art well-pleased not that the wretched should perish, O good Lord: have compassion upon him who perishes and save me, by the all-merciful nod of Thy mercy!

In knowledge and in ignorance have I sinned against Thee, O Christ the Lord; unto Thee Who knowest all things I come and fall down before Thee: receive me as the prodigal!

To the Martyrs: That ye might put to death him who lives in sin, and show the enemy dead, O Martyrs, ye took no thought for bodily death, O blessed ones!

To the Martyrs: Diversified with sufferings, O Martyrs, and adorned with garments dipped in blood: ye stand now crowned before the King of all!

Theotokion: As Mother Who didst bear God incarnate, receive the voices of those who ever cry unto Thee, and deliver us from various temptations!

Another [Canon to the Bodiless Hosts].

*Heirmos: Thou Who upon nothing didst establish the noetic...*

Thou Who by Thy Word didst wisely establish the choirs of the heavenly hosts, showing forth Thy goodness to be powerful without measure: establish Thy Church, O Son, through their intercessions, O only Good and Lover of mankind!

Adorning the Angels with ineffable brightness, O Christ, and through them establishing Thy Church, O Compassionate One: enlighten my wretched soul through their prayers, remembering not my countless sins, O Master!

Ineffably Thou wast revealed to be the Mother of God, Whom the bodiless choirs of the single Divine Principality unceasingly praise [f. 146vB] in three holy mysteries and dominions, O most-holy, all-immaculate Virgin!

Ode 4. Heirmos:

The works of Thy dispensation, O Lord, struck awe into the Prophet Habakkuk; for Thou wentest forth for the salvation of Thy people, to save Thine anointed ones!

The deeds which I have committed in life are a crafty and fierce snare; from them deliver me, O Christ my God, granting me sincere repentance!

Every honorable commandment have I neglected, casting away Thy fear, O Christ, and the inevitable judgment of Thy tribunal: wherein condemn me not, O Compassionate One!

To the Martyrs: Suffering insults visibly spoken against you, cast down by wounds, O blessed ones, and scraped with claws, O Word, Thy sufferers rejoiced in faith!

To the Martyrs: The crafty one was unable to shake you, O sufferers, from the fiery pillar! Therefore, unto many who were shaken, ye were shown forth as a divine foundation, O noble ones!

Theotokion: The Lord was incarnate of Thy pure blood, O All-praised one, granting repentance unto those who honor Thee through Thy good intercession, as He is compassionate and the only Lover of mankind!

Another [Canon to the Bodiless Hosts].

*Heirmos: Perceiving Thy divine condescension with prophetic insight, O...*

Thou didst establish the light-bearing ranks of the Angels, enlightening them with divine beams as the Giver of good, as Thou art mighty in strength, O Word, fulfilling Thine unseen purpose!

[f. 147rA] Let us lay aside earthly bodily thoughts, O faithful, imitating the life of the bodiless Angels, and lifting our mind unto the primal things in the Spirit!

Be Thou my protectress, O all-immaculate one, refuge and advocate, calming the tempest of passions: Thou who didst surpass the angelic choirs in incomparable beauty!

Ode 5. Heirmos:

O True Light, Christ God, unto Thee my spirit rises early from the night: shine upon us Thy face!

Lift thyself up, O my soul! Awake from sinful sleep and bitter sloth, and be illumined with the light of repentance!

Let us renew the spirit with diligence, and be watered with streams of compunction, that we may sprout the wheat-ear of repentance!

To the Martyrs: Kindled with coals of love, ye appeared as unburned swords, O passion-bearers, cutting down the hostile legions!

Ye were undefiled by the enemy, subduing him, O passion-bearers, and were shown forth as close friends unto Christ!

Theotokion: O Virgin, blessed among women, grant Thy mercies unto Thy people; for through Thy prayers Thou wast revealed to be His Mother!

Another [Canon to the Bodiless Hosts].

*Heirmos: Thou Who clothest Thyself with light as with...*

Encompassing all the ends of the earth, ye bring good benefactions unto the faithful, and preserve them, obeying the Word of God and the Father in all things, O glorious ornaments of the immaterial [f. 147rB] hierarchy, illumined by the Light of His brightness!

Direct all my desire unto Thee, who beyond speech didst bear the Sweetness of desire, unto those who know Thee as the Mother of God, O pure one!

Ode 6. Heirmos:

As Thou didst save the Prophet from the whale, so lead me up from the depths of transgressions, O Lord, and save me!

Sunk in life am I in sin, which I alone have committed, wretched that I am: O only Sinless One, have compassion on me!

Winged with the strength of zeal, let us hasten unto the saving haven of repentance, that we may be saved!

To the Martyrs: Together with the Prophets and Apostles, creation is illumined by the sufferings of the Martyrs: through whom enlighten us also, O Lover of mankind!

All ye faithful, let us honor the Martyrs, vessels that contained the beam of the divine and honorable effusion of light!

Theotokion: O Mother of God, salvation of the faithful: pray unto the Lord for deliverance from every sin for Thy servants!

Another [Canon to the Bodiless Hosts].

Heirmos: Tossed by the tempest:

Hierarchically adorned, O chosen angelic assemblies, ye are enlightened by light-giving radiances, openly imitating the divine illuminations!

Richly adorned with three-sunned radiances, O Angels and Archangels of godly countenance: enlighten my wretched soul by your prayers!

Thou didst conceive, O Most-pure One, the Creator of all and God, unto Whom with trembling [f. 147vA] the all-blessed Angels who stand before Him sing with fear, rejoicing!

Ode 7. Heirmos:

Blessed art Thou, O God, Who seest the depths and sittest upon the throne of glory: praised and exalted above all forever![^227]

Heal my many passions, O compassionate Christ, Who knowest my weakness: praised and glorified above all forever!

Blessed art Thou, O God, Who in mercy watchest over all and receivest them: praised and glorified!

To the Martyrs: Strengthened by divine power, O noble passion-bearers, ye conquered the enemies, crying: Praised and exalted above all forever!

To the Martyrs: O Word, Who didst strengthen the wise passion-bearers to endure manifold torments: through their prayers have compassion on us, as Thou art very merciful!

Theotokion: Blessed art Thou, O God, Who didst dwell in the Virgin among women, and didst save man: praised and glorified above all forever!

Another [Canon to the Bodiless Hosts].

*Heirmos: The Lord God of our fathers, praised above...*

Endowing you with unreckoned power, O Christ, Thou didst appoint the Archangels, teaching them to sing: O God, blessed art Thou!

Adorning the unnumbered multitude of bodiless ranks with goodness, account the assemblies of the faithful worthy to sing unto Thee, O God, forever!

Shaken by passions, do Thou now establish me, O Thou who didst pour forth dispassion unto all the faithful, who cry: O God, blessed art Thou!

Ode 8. Heirmos:

The King of all creation, before Whom the Angels tremble: praise ye, O people, and exalt Him above all forever!

[f. 147vB] Being dead through transgressions, quicken me, O Lord, that I may glorify Thee unto all the ages!

Having enlightened me with repentance, deliver me from the darkness of sin, O Lord, that I may glorify Thee unto all the ages!

To the Martyrs: The passion-bearing Martyrs trampled upon the flame of deceit, receiving dew from heaven in most-glorious manner!

To the Martyrs: As fertile earth, O Holy Ones, ye truly brought forth fruit a hundredfold unto Christ the Arbiter of the contest!

Theotokion: Thou didst bear the true God incarnate, O Virgin, and didst enlighten those darkened outside the light!

Another [Canon to the Bodiless Hosts].

*Heirmos: Unto Thee, the Creator of all, the youth...*

The angelic assemblies now invite me to sing in hymns, and with heartfelt desire I sing with them: Bless the Lord, and exalt Him above all forever!

O initiates of the most-bright, three-sunned radiance: pray that they may be saved who sing in faith: All ye works of the Lord, bless the Lord, and exalt Him above all forever!

O Gate of Light, Virgin Mother, maiden: illumine with Thy light those who sing in faith: All ye works of the Lord, bless the Lord, and exalt Him above all forever!

Ode 9. Heirmos:

Thee Who art blessed among women and blessed by God, the race of mankind doth magnify in songs!

Be Thou my prayer, O Lord, who have foolishly sinned without number, and grant me a portion of repentance, O Word!

As Thou didst save the Ninevites of old who repented, O only Savior:

[f. 148rA] save us also who sing of Thee, by Thy mercy!

To the Martyrs: Enduring every manner of wound, ye preserved your soul unsoftened, O Passion-bearers, partakers of divine glory!

To the Martyrs: As unwaning stars upon earth, illuminating the souls of all, ye appeared as passion-bearers unto the Master of all!

Theotokion: Thou bearest as a fiery throne Him Who upholds all things by His nod, and with Thy breast dost nourish Him Who nourishes all, O Virgin!

Another [Canon to the Bodiless Hosts].

*Heirmos: Rejoice, O Isaiah! For a Virgin hath conceived...*

Having become leaders of the angelic rank, O most-bright Michael, and divine Gabriel, who wast truly the preacher of the divine incarnation: preserve all who sing of you, O glorious ones!

O Master, Who overflowest with rich gifts in Thy treasures, Who leadest the ranks of the Angels, with whom Thou comest as Judge and King of all: save me who flee unto the mercy of Thy hosts!

O intelligent Archangels, Dominions and Thrones, Cherubim, Powers and Seraphim, bright Angels, Principalities and Authorities: with trembling they serve Thy Son, O all-immaculate, pure one, all-blessed Mother of God!

At the Aposticha, Penitential Stichera. Tone 5:

Overlook the multitude of my transgressions, O Lord born of the Virgin, and cleanse every defilement of sin, granting me the thought of repentance, as Thou art the only Lover of mankind: and I pray Thee, have mercy on me!

Woe is me, unto what have I become like? Unto the barren fig tree! And I fear the curse of being cut down:

[f. 148rB] but O heavenly Husbandman, Christ God, show my dried-up soul to be fruitful, and receive me as the prodigal son, and have mercy on me!

To the Martyrs: O divine army of the heavenly King! For though ye were of earthborn rank, ye strove to attain, being deemed worthy of the honors of the bodiless hosts! Therefore through their prayers, O Lord, save our souls!

Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion:

O favored one, intercede by Thy prayers, and ask for our souls an abundance of compassions and cleansing from our many transgressions, we pray!

ON MONDAY, THE BEATITUDES (MAKARISMOI). Tone 5:

The thief upon the cross, believing Thee to be God, O Christ, confessed Thee purely from the heart: Remember me, O Lord, crying aloud in Thy kingdom!

Two thieves meeting me on the path of life have wounded me; but unto Thy compassion I now flee: heal me, O Christ, and save me, I pray!

To the Martyrs: Shaken by passions, O sufferers of Christ, ye remained unmoved; by the honor of your endurance, O blessed ones, shake the passions of my heart!

Theotokion: Forming an armed host in angelic manner today, the bodiless hosts sing of Thee with the faithful: Blessed Virgin, Mother of God, the only adornment of mankind!

Triadikon: In godly manner, ye earthborn, let us sing the Thrice-Holy hymn unto God Who is hymned in the highest: Holy art Thou, O unoriginate Father, Son, and Spirit!

Theotokion: Having received into Thy womb the joy of the Angels, O pure one: with light-bearing deeds fill my soul with joy, guiding me unto the Light!

## MONDAY EVENING VESPERS (FOR TUESDAY) (TONE 5)

[f. 148vA] ON MONDAY EVENING, AT "LORD, I HAVE CRIED":

Penitential Stichera, Tone 5.

*Podoben: "Rejoice, O container of ascetics" (Ра́дꙋйся по́стникѡвъ):* [^228]

Woe is me, who have angered the good and merciful God, my Lord! How many times have I promised to repent, O Christ, and have been found false, condemned that I am! First, indeed, I defiled the garment of Baptism, and transgressed the covenant and my vow unto Thee; and this second covenant which I confess unto Thee before Angels and men, being clothed in mournful form, having cast it aside henceforth, O Savior, leave me not to perish utterly!

What manner of repentance is thine, O my wretched soul, in the day of judgment? Or who shall deliver thee from eternal torment and the rest? No one, unless thou thyself shalt appease the Compassionate One, forsaking thine evil deeds, and acquiring a life pleasing unto God: weeping each day, as a sinner, over thine immeasurable transgressions, which thou committest at every hour, in deed, and in word, and in thought: praying unto Christ, that He grant forgiveness unto my sinful soul!

Let not the attraction of sinful habit hold me fast, O Savior; neither let the age, having taken pride, lead me unto its will; but snatch me from its dominion by Thy mighty [f. 148vB] hand, O Almighty One, and do Thou reign within me, O Lover of mankind: grant that I may be wholly Thine, and live according to Thy will, O Word, and have rest in Thee: and find salvation, and cleansing, and great mercy!

Other Stichera to Saint John the Forerunner:

Same tone and melody:

When God bowed down unto the earth and ineffably humbled Himself, thou didst adorn Him, O Forerunner of Christ and Martyr, and thou dost shelter him who flees with faith into thy divine protection, O blessed one! Therefore snatch me from the dread day, wherein I must stand before the tribunal and be given over unto torments! I pray thee, deliver me then from the condemnation there, as thou hast boldness without shame, O wise one, praying unto Him Who grants great mercy unto the world!

Thou art a most radiant lamp unto the Sun, O wise Forerunner of Christ: shine upon me, who have fallen into the darkness of immeasurable evils, the beam of light, I pray thee; and raise me up from the pit of sin, guiding me by saving words: O thou who of old didst loose the voice of thy father by thy birth, do thou now rectify my voice, I pray thee, that with songs I may brightly glorify today God the Lover of mankind and our Savior, [f. 149rA] Who grants great mercy unto the world!

A divine temple of God, the Life-giver of all, didst thou become, O blessed Prophet, Forerunner, and Preacher; for thou hadst Him living in thy heart! Whom unceasingly beseech, O all-wealthy John, for those who flee unto thy holy temple and honor thee: pray that we may become temples of the Spirit and draw near unto God, that in songs we may honor the protection and fervent prayer of the Prophet, O praiseworthy one, greater than whom none hath been testified among those born of women!

Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion:

Having changed since childhood, unceasingly committing sins, I have been grievously wounded in mind, and defiled by dwelling in it with much love! And now, lamenting, I weep over the bitterness of my deceit, and my evil habit, and foolishness, and the perdition of my soul! O Sovereign Lady, despise me not who am perishing miserably; but having compassion, deliver me by Thy protection from the great assault and passions, that at least now in old age I may repent, O Bride of God!

At the Aposticha, Penitential Stichera. Tone 5:

O Lord, I cease not from sinning; yet being deemed worthy of Thy love toward mankind, I perceive not my lack of understanding! Overcome my darkness, O only Good One, and have mercy on me!

O Lord, I fear Thy terror, yet cease not from doing evil! Who, standing before the tribunal, fears not the judge? Or who, wishing to be healed, provokes the physician to wrath, as I do?

[f. 149rB] O long-suffering Lord, have compassion upon my weakness, and have mercy on me!

To the Martyrs: Armed with the shield of faith, and strengthened by the sign of the Cross, ye manfully dared the torments, and cast down the deceit and pride of the devil, O Thy holy ones, O Lord! Through their prayers, as Almighty God, send down peace unto the world, and unto our souls great mercy!

Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion:

Assuage the diseases of my much-sighing soul, and stay every tear from the face of the earth: for Thou drivest away diseases from men, and loosest the sorrows of sinners; for Thee have we all acquired as hope and confirmation, O most-holy Virgin Mother!

## TUESDAY MATINS: REPENTANCE AND ST. JOHN THE FORERUNNER (TONE 5)

ON TUESDAY AT MATINS.[^229]

After the 1st Kathisma, Penitential Sessional Hymns. Tone 5:

When the Judge shall sit and the Angels stand by, the trumpet sounding and the flame burning: what wilt thou do, O my soul, led unto judgment? For then thy fierce deeds shall confront thee, and thy secret transgressions shall be exposed! Therefore, before the end, cry aloud unto the Judge: O God, cleanse me and save me!

Let us all be watchful and meet Christ with abundance of oil and with bright lamps, that we may be accounted worthy of the bridal chamber within; for he who is found outside the doors shall cry in vain unto God: Have mercy on me!

[f. 149vA] Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion:

Strange is the virgin mystery! Salvation hath appeared unto the world; for from her was He born without seed, and appeared in the flesh without corruption, the joy of all! O Lord, glory to Thee!

After the 2nd Kathisma, Penitential Sessional Hymns. Tone 5:

When thy deeds shall be uncovered, O my soul, while myriads of Angels stand before the Judge: what answer wilt thou find from thence, unless before the end thou shalt cry aloud with tears: I have sinned, O good Lord, have mercy on me!

Upon the bed I lie of many transgressions, despoiled of the hope of my salvation; for the sleep of my slothfulness procures torment for my soul! But do Thou, O Christ, born of the Virgin, raise me up unto Thy praise, that I may glorify Thee!

To the Martyrs: An unbreakable wall of the wonders of Thy holy Martyrs hast Thou granted us, O Christ God; through their supplications destroy the counsels of the heathen, and strengthen the scepters of the Kingdom, as Thou art the only Good Lover of mankind!

Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion:

Show Thy swift protection and help and mercy upon Thy servant, and calm the waves of unclean thoughts, O pure one, and raise up my fallen soul, O Mother of God; for I know, yea, I know, O Virgin, that Thou canst do whatever Thou desirest!

After the 3rd Kathisma, Sessional Hymn. Tone 5.

*Podoben: "The Word co-unoriginate" (Собезнача́льное Сло́во):*

Slipped into the depth of sin, the tempest of despair holds me fast:

[f. 149vB] but come quickly, O Christ, as the almighty Pilot of all, and direct me unto the calm haven of dispassion: through the prayers of Thy Forerunner, in Thy compassions, O Savior, save me!

Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion:

O animate holy Table, who didst sprout the divine Flower from the root, the Ark and Lampstand, all-golden Urn, bearing the Bread of Life: as Thy Son and God, pray unto Him together with the holy Forerunner, to have compassion and save those who confess Thee to be the Mother of God!

PENITENTIAL CANON.

Work of Joseph.

Ode 1. Tone 5. Heirmos:

The land upon which the sun never shone nor did it ever see: the deep which the bare sky-flying monster did not behold: Israel passed through dryshod, O Lord, and Thou didst lead them up unto Thy holy mountain, as they sang and chanted a song of victory!

Grant me cleansing for the things committed by me, O Christ; grant me relief before I depart hence; cleanse the much putrefaction, O Lord, as the holy lepers; and account me worthy to stand without blemish before Thee, Who art to come to judge the living and the dead!

The putrefaction that lies upon the eyes of my soul, preventing me from beholding Thy beams, which Thou didst manifest upon earth, Thou unwaning Sun: cleanse this, O Savior, and grant me to contemplate, O compassionate Lord, the light of Thy judgments!

To the Martyrs: Being watchful keepers of the commandments of Christ, [f. 150rA] ye put to sleep all the malice of the enemy, O blessed sufferers! Therefore, weighed down with the sleep of sin, unto repentance, I pray, by your divine vigilance, raise me up also!

To the Martyrs: Contending in the flesh against the adversary enemy, O Martyrs: ye conquered him with the weapon of the Cross, and drowned him in streams of blood, and received the crowns of victory from God, singing and chanting a song of victory!

Theotokion: Wounded and overwhelmed by evil, O pure Virgin: establish me upon the rock of the commandments, shaken as I am by the snares of the ancient deceiver, O good one; and account me worthy to be well-pleasing unto Christ, Who is to come to judge the living and the dead!

Another Canon to the Holy Forerunner John. Tone 5.

*Ode 1. Heirmos: The steed and rider into the Red Sea...*

A purified way of life and an immaterial life didst thou show forth in a material body, O Forerunner! Therefore we pray thee: make those who praise thee in faith imitators of thyself!

Having immersed the Abyss of compassion, Christ, in the streams of the river: pray unto Him, O Forerunner, to dry up the abyss of my evils, I pray thee, and enlighten my understanding!

O Forerunner of the Savior, mediating for me the cause of repentance: grant me unceasing compunction, washing away the stench of sin with tears, I pray thee!

Theotokion: Ineffably Thou didst give birth without [f. 150rB] travail unto Him Whom the Father begat incorruptly before the ages, O all-hymned Sovereign Lady! Pray unto Him to save from every harm those who flee unto Thee!

Ode 3. Heirmos:

My heart shaken by the waves of life: steer Thou unto a calm haven, guiding me as God!

I promise Thee, O God, to repent, and again I sin: what shall become of me? How shall I appear when Thou judgest the earth?

By the nod of the Lord let us bow down, let us sigh, let us shed tears to cleanse our defilements, that we may be delivered there!

To the Martyrs: With deadened mind the transgressors of the law, who loved life, slew the victorious Martyrs who confessed Christ!

To the Martyrs: The choirs of Martyrs were numbered with the choirs of intelligent Angels, becoming equal unto the Angels by the grace of the Holy Spirit!

Theotokion: Open unto me the gates of repentance, O Gate of Light, Virgin; and close the entrances of passions against my humble soul!

Another [Canon to the Forerunner].

*Heirmos: Thou Who upon nothing didst establish the noetic...*

Ever pouring forth healings unto those who hasten with faith unto thy temple, O admirable Forerunner: heal the passions of my heart, I pray thee, which negligent carelessness hath nurtured in all-wretched manner, O all-wealthy one!

Ever held fast by sighing and lamentations, contemplating Thy strict tribunal, O only Sinless One:

[f. 150vA] O most-righteous Judge, preserve me uncondemned therein through the prayers of Thy Baptist, O Lord my God!

Having become the mediator of the New and the Old, by divine intercessions, O glorious Forerunner: renew me, who have grown old through many sins, I cry unto thee, by repentance, that in praise I may honor thee!

O holy Virgin Mother, only all-immaculate one: alter our defilement of transgressions, enlighten our thoughts, cleanse our hearts, and deliver all from eternal condemnation, we pray!

Ode 4. Heirmos:

I heard the report of Thee, O Lord, and was afraid; I understood Thy dispensation, and glorified Thee, O Lover of mankind!

Neglecting the voice of Thy commandments which enlighten, O Lord, I have committed dark deeds, and fear the end of Thy dread tribunal there!

Winged with the sail of divine fear, let the ship of our soul reach the haven of repentance, escaping the tempest of passions!

To the Martyrs: Dripping sweetness wisely, ye appeared as divine mountains, and truly as hills having the Lord as the God-planted Tree of Life!

To the Martyrs: With the arrows of endurance and struggle ye shot down the adversary demon, and received the crowns of glory!

Theotokion: O most-holy Sovereign Lady, advocate of those who sin, and sure correction of the fallen: blessed art Thou, who didst bear God!

Another [Canon to the Forerunner].

*Heirmos: Perceiving Thy divine condescension with prophetic insight, O...*

Thou didst dwell in the highest Kingdom, [f. 150vB] as truly a noble soldier of Christ the King, O Baptist! Pray unceasingly unto Him to have compassion upon the people who honor thee!

The Lord, foreseeing thee as a true beacon, blessed father of thanksgiving: pray unto Him to cleanse us all, we pray!

Thou didst announce unto the dead the coming of Him Who was put to death for our sake: pray unto Him, O Forerunner, to quicken and save me also who am deadened by sins!

Theotokion: Have mercy on me, O only all-immaculate one, who ineffably didst give birth unto the merciful God, the most-merciful Goodness: deliver me from eternal torment!

Ode 5. Heirmos:

Coming before me, have compassion upon my wretched soul that sins by night in the darkness of passions, and grant within me the bright rays of the day, O spiritual Sun, having enlightened the night with Light!

From my deeds there is no salvation for me; for much have I sinned upon earth, wretched that I am: and I tremble at Thy dread tribunal, when Thou shalt judge the transgressors of Thy commandments, O God!

How foolish have I become! How darkened in committing evil deeds! How have I not understood Thy fear, O Christ! But I have bowed down unto the earth, and become like unto brute beasts: but do Thou turn me back, O God, Lover of mankind!

To the Martyrs: The cloud of Martyrs dispersed the clouds of many torments: it illumined the day of true understanding, and destroyed the mist of polytheism, and attained unto the unwaning Light!

To the Martyrs: Cleanse my mind through the supplications of Thy holy [f. 151rA] Martyrs, O Christ, I pray Thee, and show it full of enlightenment, and a partaker of their glory, that in songs I may glorify Thee, O Savior!

Theotokion: By the ineffable Word, O Virgin Mother, Thou didst bear upon earth God, Who grants repentance unto all who have sinned greatly: through Thy good mediation, Thou art a refuge and haven for the fallen!

Another [Canon to the Forerunner].

*Heirmos: Thou Who clothest Thyself with light as with...*

A barren womb brought thee forth, O Forerunner, adorning the barren deeds of the heart, showing them well-pleasing with fruitful words; therefore we call thee blessed!

Thou didst blossom forth as a gracious lily, a renewal in the deserts; therefore I cry unto thee: O Forerunner, drive away the great stench of evil from my soul!

Thou wast found in the midst of the Law and of grace, O all-wise one; therefore I cry aloud: being cut down by the law of sin, have compassion on me, O Forerunner, who act so wretchedly!

Theotokion: O unapproachable Gate of glory, pure one, open unto me the gates of repentance, mediating for me divine entrances and the resting-place there!

Ode 6. Heirmos:

As Thou didst deliver the Prophet from the beast, O Lord: so lead me up from the depths of unclean passions, I pray Thee, that I may look again toward Thy holy temple!

Behold, the time of repentance is at hand, yet I lie prostrate continually, ever held fast by much insensibility: having loosed the darkness of my heart, O Word, have compassion in Thy mercy!

[f. 151rB] Have compassion on me who sigh as once on the Publican, O compassionate Christ, and grant me to weep warmly as the Harlot, that I may wash away, O Word, the filthy accumulation of my many transgressions!

To the Martyrs: O Great Martyrs of Christ, deliver me, who have sinned greatly, from the great flame that awaits me there in Gehenna, that I may ever glorify your universal memory!

To the Martyrs: Having contested well, Thy sufferers were brightly crowned by Thy life-originating right hand, O God and Lord! Through their honorable supplications save all Thy people!

Theotokion: O sacred Tabernacle, divine city, honorable Ark, lampstand of the Divine Light, table of the Bread of Life, animate palace of the Word: show me to be a temple for the Spirit!

Another [Canon to the Forerunner].

Heirmos: Tossed by the tempest:

Shining with ineffable beams, O Forerunner of Christ, thou dost ever enlighten by grace those who praise thee in godly manner!

Held fast by the sleep of slothfulness, O holy Prophet and Forerunner of Christ, raise me up by thine effectual prayer, diligently to do the divine will!

Blessed one: Deliver us from every affliction of adversaries, who have acquired thee as a divine advocate and intercessor with the Sovereign Lady, O blessed one!

Theotokion: The tempest of sin troubles me, O Most-pure Mother of God: make haste to deliver me, guiding me unto the haven of repentance, O All-immaculate one!

[f. 151vA] Ode 7. Heirmos:

The prayer of the Children quenching the fire, a dewy furnace, a proclaimer of wonders, not burning up nor consuming the singers of praise: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers![^230]

Pardon my numberless transgressions, O Christ, and deliver me from future torment, for the multitude of Thy compassions, O God!

Like the Prodigal Son, I have squandered the riches which I received, and I melt away with hunger, deprived of divine nourishment; receiving me who repent, O Savior, save me!

To the Martyrs: Ye made abominable the adversary enemy, having your members put to death by many torments, O highly blessed Martyrs of the Lord! Therefore, O faithful, we piously sing your praise!

To the Martyrs: Ye put to death the demon ranks and the whole multitude of the tyrants by the arrows of your suffering, and through endurance and courage ye have now passed over unto true life.

Theotokion: A haven of salvation hast Thou appeared unto all, O pure one, calming the tempest of passions and leading all the humble upon earth unto tranquility, O pure Mother of God!

[f. 151vB] Another [Canon to the Forerunner]. Heirmos:

The Lord exalted above all by the fathers:

With words we entreat thee who art the Forerunner of the Word: as thou didst loose the silent voice at thy birth, so loose the bond of our sins and transgressions.

O Sun of many lights, cause the saving dawn of repentance to shine upon me, and deliver me from the darkness of passions which darkens my darkened heart!

Having a barren soul and barrenness of deeds, O divine offshoot of the barren womb: pray unceasingly unto Christ, O Baptist, that I may bring forth fruits of repentance!

Triadikon: Equal unto the Begetter we glorify the Son, and the Holy Spirit, the undivided Trinity, singing in godly manner: Blessed art Thou, O God!

Theotokion: In youth Thou didst bring forth a young child, Christ, O all-immaculate one, Who works our renewal, O Bride of God, who were grown old through the ancient transgression!

Ode 8. Heirmos:

The angelic host and the council of men, the King and Creator of all, ye priests hymn, ye Levites bless, ye peoples exalt above all unto all the ages!

Behold, my wounds have become loathsome and festered, O Christ, and my soul hath suffered and been humbled utterly; through years of repentance, O Savior, heal me!

The deceitful and most wicked serpent, having stealthily robbed me, filled me with evil; and sighing, I cry aloud: Cast me not away, O Word, who am condemned and brought low!

To the Martyrs: Ye turned not aside from the better standing; but the strong and boastful enemies who thought to cast you down, ye threw down, having conquered them utterly, O most-wise ones!

To the Martyrs: You, O all-praised Martyrs of the Lord, neither fire, nor sword, nor wild beasts, nor hunger, nor the breaking of wheels, nor any other torment was able to separate from Christ, the Lover of mankind!

Theotokion: The praise of Angels, the salvation of men, and my surety be Thou, O Mother [f. 152rA] of God, that I may turn and receive forgiveness of my former sins, committed in knowledge and in ignorance!

Another [Canon to the Forerunner]. Heirmos: Unto Thee, the Seer:

Thou dost wash the congregation of the people with the streams of the Jordan, preaching repentance, O glorious Forerunner! Therefore I cry unto thee: Dry up the arrows of my evils, sending me fountains of tears!

Trembling before the great judgment, O soul, contemplating the tribunal of the Almighty, cry aloud: O Compassionate One, for the sake of Thy Baptist, have compassion and save me, and deliver me from torments!

Unclean lips and a defiled tongue do I move unto supplication, O holy Forerunner: make haste to help me quickly, who am fiercely and unceasingly shaken by great assaults!

Triadikon: Let us hymn the Father, the Son, and the Spirit, the consubstantial Trinity, that having obtained the forgiveness of sins and perfect salvation, we may exalt Thee above all unto all the ages!

Theotokion: By Thy lofty Childbirth Thou didst raise us up from the pit of the fall, O full of God's grace! Therefore, with thankful voices, in faith we hymn Thee, O Maiden, unto all the ages!

Ode 9. Heirmos:

He Who is mighty hath magnified Thee, showing Thee a pure Virgin after childbirth, as having borne without seed the Creator of all: therefore, O Mother of God, we magnify Thee!

I magnify Thy long-suffering, O Jesus: be long-suffering still toward [f. 152rB] me, and cut me not down like the barren fig tree, I sigh unto Thee, that I may bring forth fruits of repentance unto Thee!

How terrible art Thou, O only Sovereign and Mighty One! And who shall stand against Thy dread rebuke, O Christ, when Thou shalt sit upon the judgment seat? Wherein preserve me uncondemned!

To the Martyrs: Bodily sicknesses ye take away by your divine sufferings, O sufferers of the Lord! Therefore heal the cruel passions of my soul, O most assured physicians of the sick!

To the Martyrs: Brighter than the sun's rays shines from the shrine of your relics the radiance of divine grace, enlightening hearts and illuminating souls, O passion-bearers who praise you in faith!

Theotokion: A light-bearing Cloud leading the new people unto the promised land hast Thou truly appeared, O full of God's grace, and a Gate leading unto life: therefore, O Mother of God, we magnify Thee!

Another [Canon to the Forerunner]. Heirmos: Rejoice, O Isaiah:

Behold, the splendor of thy temple is known as heaven upon earth, O Forerunner of the Lord, which approaching, thou dost enlighten with divine radiances those who now glorify thee therein day by day!

As a genuine and intimate friend of God, O Baptist: strengthen me, O all-blessed one, to love Him unswervingly with an upright mind, and to abhor corruptive passions which impel me toward destruction!

[f. 152vA] by contrary winds, O most-wise one, shaken: unto our divine establishment and the unshakable strengthening of the Church, which preserve unbowed by thy prayers from so many great scandals!

The coming of the Creator is at the doors: why then dost thou not weep for thyself, O passionate soul? Living in carelessness, arise, crying aloud: Spare me, O Savior, through the supplications of the Forerunner, as Thou art the Lover of mankind!

Theotokion: A light-bearing Carriage of the Sun hast Thou truly appeared, Who shone forth from Thy most-pure, immaculate womb, and loosed the cruel darkness of deceit; therefore in faith we magnify Thee as is meet!

At the Aposticha, Penitential Stichera, Tone 5:

Despise the multitude of my transgressions, O Lord Who wast born of the Virgin, and cleanse all my sins! Grant me the thought of conversion, as Thou art the only Lover of mankind, I pray Thee, and have mercy on me![^231]

Woe is me! Unto what have I likened myself? Unto the barren fig tree, fearing the reproach of the curse! But, O heavenly Husbandman, Christ God: show my languishing soul to be fruitful, and receive me like the Prodigal Son, and have mercy on me!

[f. 152vB] Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion:

On Tuesday, The Beatitudes, Tone 5:

Even as Thou didst justify the Harlot who wept, O Christ, illuminating her soul: so also cleanse me, O Master, from defiled sin, by the nod of Thy love for mankind!

## TUESDAY EVENING VESPERS (FOR WEDNESDAY) (TONE 5)

[f. 153rA] ON TUESDAY EVENING, AT "LORD, I HAVE CRIED":

*Stichera of the Cross, Tone 5.*

*Podoben: "Rejoice, O container of ascetics" (Ра́дꙋйсѧ по́стникѡвъ):*

Thou wast lifted up like a Lamb upon the Cross, and didst cast down the haughtiness of the deceiver, being slain; by Thy Blood Thou didst sanctify all the earth, and being pierced with a Lance, Thou didst straightway command the flaming sword to turn its back before me, O Christ, and openedst the entrance to Paradise, and grantedst me to enjoy the Tree of Life unshakably. Therefore, having been saved by Thy Passion, I cry rejoicing: Glory to Thy Cross, O Christ, whereby we have been delivered from the ancient curse, and embrace the blessing from the Tree, and great mercy!

Willing to extinguish human pains and reproaches, O all-good Lord, my Savior: Thou didst endure a reproachful crucifixion, and didst taste gall, O Guileless One, taking away our bitter wickedness. The piercing of Thy side struck terror, O Word, for it was done as unto an unresisting Master! Therefore we also sing of Thy glorious purpose, and worshipping, we honor the Lance, the Sponge, and the Reed, whereby Thou didst grant unto Thy world peace and great mercy!

How did the lawless assembly of the Hebrews condemn Thee, O Jesus, to be crucified upon the Cross? Not pitying Him Who had healed the whole man, floating in deeds of wickedness, she said of old, when she beheld Him uplifted upon the Cross, Whom her [f. 153rB] womb had incorruptly brought forth: What hath the lawless assembly done unto Thee, O my longed-for Child, my most-beloved Son? Make haste and save those who in faith glorify Thy crucifixion, and who magnify me, even as Thou didst promise, as the only All-bountiful One!

Other Stichera to the Forerunner together [with the Cross], same Tone:

Willing to wipe out the handwriting against Adam the First-formed unto the end, O magnificent Lover of mankind: as the Creator of Adam, Thou wast nailed with nails, O sinless Christ, and with a Lance was Thy divine side wounded for our sake, forbidding the flaming sword, O Word, to bar against us the entrance to Thy delights! Therefore, glorifying Thee, we sing of Thy dominion, and we honor Thy Cross, and we hymn Thee, O Lover of mankind, whereby great nature hath found a painless heritage and great mercy!

Beholding Her Lamb of old hastening unto slaughter, the Ewe-lamb followed earnestly, crying aloud unto Him: Whither goest Thou, my sweetest Child, O Christ? For what cause dost Thou run this course, O long-suffering, sinless One? O Jesus most-beloved, sinless and most-merciful Lord, [f. 153vA] grant a word unto Thine handmaid, O most-beloved Son! Despise me not, O Compassionate One, keeping silence, who strangely gave Thee birth, O all-compassionate God, granting great mercy unto the world![^232]

Truly a Cherubic Throne hast Thou become, as being higher than creation; for within Thee, O pure one, the divine Word, willing to renew our form, took up His abode; and coming forth as a flesh-bearer, in divine compassion He accepted the Cross and Passion for our sake, and as God granted the Resurrection. Therefore, giving thanks unto God Who hath delivered our condemned nature, we pray unto Thee, O Virgin: that we, Thy servants, may obtain salvation through Thy divine prayers!

Glory... Now and ever... Stavrotheotokion:

A redemption for our sake, and a great ransom, didst Thou pour forth in Thy most-pure Blood, O Virgin-born, sinless Christ, my God, willing that all should obtain salvation! Therefore, beholding Thee nailed, Thy Mother, weeping and tearing Her hair, lamented, saying: O Child, all-immaculate Lamb, willing to deliver the world by Thy precious Blood: O my Eyes, how hast Thou set, O Savior, unwaning Sun, Who grantest enlightenment unto all, and peace, and great mercy!

At the Aposticha, Stichera of the Cross, Tone 5:

O Lord, in the time of Moses the Prophet of old, the mere image of Thy Cross being shown conquered Thine enemies; but now, having the help of Thy Cross itself, we entreat: Strengthen Thy Church, and grant [f. 153vB] unto our rulers victory as unto Constantine, for the multitude of Thy mercy, O Lover of mankind!

Thy Cross, O Christ, though visible in substance as wood, is yet clothed with divine power; and being sensibly revealed unto the world, it noetically works the wonder of our salvation; worshipping which, we glorify Thee, O Savior: have mercy on us!

To the Martyrs: Offer prayer for us, O holy Martyrs, that we may be delivered from our iniquities; for unto you is grace given to pray for us!

*Glory... Now and ever... Stavrotheotokion.*

*Podoben: "O venerable father" (Преподо́бне ѻ҆́ч҃е):*

Having taken upon Himself my whole form, the Creator and God of great voice, willing to restore the form of Adam which had fallen of old, was lifted up upon the Cross willingly as one guilty; and having stretched out His hands, He now heals what was anciently tasted at the tree in Eden; Whom the all-immaculate and most-pure Virgin beholding, cried aloud: What is this Thine ineffable long-suffering, O my Son? Unable to bear seeing Thee uplifted upon the Cross, Who holdest all the ends of the earth in Thy hand!

ON WEDNESDAY, AT MATINS:

After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymns of the Cross, Tone 5:

The Place of the Skull became Paradise; for no sooner was the wood of the Cross planted, than it straightway sprouted the cluster of life: Glory to Thee, O Savior, unto our joy!

The crucified Savior and our Deliverer, Who suffered willingly as He willed and was well-pleased, we the faithful sing [f. 154rA] and glorify; for He nailed earthly sins unto the Cross, delivering the race of mankind from deceit, and making them worthy to receive Him!

Glory... Now and ever... Stavrotheotokion:

Seeing Thee uplifted upon the Tree, O Savior, She who bore Thee without travail wept with lamentation and cried aloud: Woe is me, sweetest Son! I am wounded in soul, beholding Thee upon the Cross between two thieves, nailed as an evildoer!

After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns of the Cross, Tone 5:

Having endured the Cross by voluntary counsel, and freed the children of corruption, O Savior: we the faithful sing and worship Thee, for Thou hast enlightened us by the power of the Cross, and all of us glorify Thee, O compassionate Lover of mankind, as Life-giver and Lord!

The Tree of Thy Cross, O our Savior, was revealed as salvation unto the world; for nailed willingly upon it, Thou didst deliver all earthborn from all sorrow: O Lord, glory to Thee!

To the Martyrs: Zealous for the cup of Thy Passion, O Lord, Thy passion-bearers left behind worldly beauty and became partakers with the Angels. By their supplications, grant unto our souls peace, O Christ, and great mercy!

Glory... Now and ever... Stavrotheotokion:

By the Cross of Thy Son, O full of God's grace, all idolatrous deceit hath been abolished, and the demonic power hath been trampled down. Therefore we the faithful unceasingly sing and bless Thee as is meet, and confessing Thee truly to be the Mother of God, [f. 154rB] we magnify Thee!

*After the 3rd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns of the Cross, Tone 5.*

*Podoben: "The Word co-unoriginate" (Собезнача́льное Сло́во):*

The prophetic predictions are already fulfilled; Thine ancient counsel hath received its end! For Thou, the King of all, didst willingly impoverish Thyself in flesh, O Christ, and didst come for our sake to ascend the Cross and undergo death. Therefore we glorify Thy condescension which is beyond understanding, O Word!

Beholding Thee nailed upon the Cross, O Jesus, King of all, the angelic ranks were terrified; and straightway the demonic hosts were cut down, and the gates of hades were shattered, and the tyranny of death was cast down, and the dead who were in the tombs arose!

Glory... Now and ever... Stavrotheotokion:

Beholding Thee upon the Cross, O Christ, having hung willingly between thieves, Thy Mother, smiting Her maternal breast, cried: O sinless Son, how art Thou unjustly nailed upon the Cross like an evildoer, willing to give life unto the race of mankind, as Thou art All-good?

Canon to the Precious and Life-giving Cross of the Lord.

A Composition of Joseph.

Ode 1. Tone 5. Heirmos:

The horse and the rider into the sea:

The Jew's lawless gathering hid Him Who is understood in incomprehensibility, Who was incarnate and appeared bodily unto the world, Who anciently willed to be hung upon the Tree!

[f. 154vA] When the faithful hung Thee, O Christ, the fruitful Vine, upon the wood of the Cross, raging in madness: then didst Thou distill the wine of joy, taking away all the drunkenness of evils, O Word![^233]

To the Martyrs: Your endurance, O praiseworthy Martyrs, falls not under human laws; for beyond great human nature ye endured pains, and rejoicing, ye took up your abode in passionless repose!

To the Martyrs: Having crossed the waves of torments by the guidance of the Word, O all-praised sufferers of Christ, ye reached the untroubled harbors of divine tranquility, now truly taking delight therein!

Stavrotheotokion: When Thou didst behold the Lord, born from Thy womb, unjustly lifted up upon the Tree, O Virgin, Thou didst weep; and Thou didst hymn His truly ineffable condescension!

Another Canon to the Most-pure Mother of God.

*Heirmos: The steed and rider into the Red Sea...*

O Gates of divine glory, who didst open the gates of Paradise: open unto me the gates of repentance, I pray Thee, and enlighten my mind, that I may sing of Thee, O full of God's grace!

Thou didst stay the course of death, having given birth unto Him Who hath dominion over life and death, O all-immaculate one! Pray Thou therefore unto Him to grant assurance and to save my soul which transgressive sins put to death!

The Word, co-beginningless with the Father, chose Thee alone, the offshoot, the beauty of Jacob; and being incarnate from Thy [f. 154vB] blood, O Mother of God, save me by Thine intercessions!

Like dew upon the fleece, the heavenly Rain came down upon Thee, O all-pure one; therefore dry up the showers of my passions, I pray Thee, O Virgin Mother!

Ode 3. Heirmos:

Thou Who didst establish the earth upon nothing:

When Thou art crucified, Paradise is opened again, and the Thief enters first, rejoicing; and Thou, O my Jesus, diest, and the deceitful enemy is slain, while slain Adam is brought to life: Glory to Thy great compassion!

Having quenched the flame of sin by Thy crucifixion upon the Tree, O Jesus, in Thy goodness Thou loosest deceit while being bound; being stripped naked, Thou clothest man with the garment of glory: Glory to Thy great compassion!

The Martyrs appeared as radiant stars, scattering the darkness of impiety. By their supplications, O Christ, have compassion upon the night of my evils, and enlighten my darkened heart!

Having lawfully contested with valor, O praiseworthy Martyrs: ye wisely turned away from the counsels of the lawless lawgivers, and received divine nourishment and the habitation of Paradise!

Stavrotheotokion: The angelic choirs hymn Thee, O all-hymned one, who transcendest these incorporeal ones; for Thou didst bear God in the flesh, Who abolished the curse of the tree by the Tree, and poured forth blessing!

Another [Canon to the Theotokos]. Heirmos: The same.

[f. 155rA] Wounded by sinful arrows, heal me wholly by the remedy found in Thee, and deliver me from the disease that holds me fast, O pure one, who by Thy Childbirth didst change the suffering of mankind!

Let the invisible enemies who everywhere afflict my humble heart and seek to put me to death now, O Mother of God, be cast down by Thy protection, remaining powerless and filled with shame!

Fill me with life-giving waters, O Mother of God, who didst pour forth the divine Water unto the world; dry up the fierce torrents of my iniquities, and calm the waves of my heart by Thy divine tranquility!

The shadowy ordinances fulfilled under the Law have passed away, for Thou didst bear Christ the Lawgiver, Who ordains grace, cleansing, and enlightenment for us, and takes away the curse, O all-immaculate Virgin Mother!

Ode 4. Heirmos:

Perceiving Thy divine condescension:

Working perfect redemption for souls, O Christ: hanging willingly upon the Tree, Thou didst commit Thy most-holy soul into the hands of the Father!

The unjust judge condemns Thee, O righteous Judge Jesus, to die upon the Tree, that Thou mightest justify us who had bowed down unto the unjust adversary!

Ye were counted worthy to see the eternal good things, O Martyrs, having manifestly partaken upon earth of many perils, afflictions, and countless [f. 155rB] torments!

To the Martyrs: Ye passed through the winter of temptations, and reached the spring of heavenly rewards, and were numbered with the angelic choirs, O honorable Martyrs!

Stavrotheotokion: The sword of the divine Passion pierced Thy blessed soul, when Thou beheldest Thy Son crucified and committing His spirit into the hands of the Father!

Another [Canon to the Theotokos]. Heirmos: The same.

There is no salvation for me from judgments; but having fled unto Thy protection, my hope: save me, a wretch, by Thy prayers, O all-immaculate Virgin!

O pure Dwelling of Light, honorable Carriage of the Sun: illuminate my heart darkened by the gloom of cruel things, and save me, I pray!

With the garment of incorruption from Thy virginal blood, do Thou clothe me who am stripped naked by deceit, O Maiden, who clothest Him that covers heaven with clouds!

The Creator received Thee as a lily in the valleys of life, and breathed forth spiritual fragrance unto the world, O all-pure Virgin, Bride of God!

Ode 5. Heirmos:

Thou Who clothest Thyself with light as with a garment:

The righteous Judge stood to be judged, O Christ, and condemned enmity in the flesh, granting me straightness and perfect ascension!

When the sun beheld Thee hanging in the flesh upon the Tree, O Christ, it turned its light into darkness; and the earth was shaken, and the rocks were split asunder!

[f. 155vA] Ye left behind the fullness of the earth, as fulfillers of the divine laws, O all-praised Martyrs, and suffering, ye fulfilled holiness!

Most fair and God-radiant, clothed with divine glory and having exposed the malice of the enemy, let the Martyrs be honored!

We bless Thee, the all-immaculate Mother of God, for whose sake the curse became sterile, and redemption and blessing were given!

Another [Canon to the Theotokos]. Heirmos: The same.

May I find Thee as my help, delivering me in that hour of judgment, when I shall stand before the tribunal of Him Who was born of Thee, O Virgin![^234]

Vanquished by the law of sin, O pure one, and often seduced by the deceits of the stranger, and driven unto the brink of transgressions: do Thou convert me!

Having given birth unto the Coal which Isaiah beheld: consume the matter of my transgressions, O all-immaculate one, and enlighten me, I pray!

Having lent flesh from Thy blood unto Christ: cleanse my carnal passions utterly, O Virgin, and show unto me the path of dispassion!

Ode 6. Heirmos:

Tossed by the tempest, O soul:

Uplifted in long-suffering upon the Tree: Thou didst cast down all the haughtiness of the enemy, and savedst the fallen one, for the sake of Thy great goodness!

When Thou didst deliver up Thy spirit upon the Tree of old, how did the souls of the righteous perceive it: they were loosed from eternal bonds, O Word!

[f. 155vB] Like hard adamants, ye endured the great burning of torments with steadfastness of mind, and having gained strength, ye cast down the enemy!

To the Martyrs: Ye appeared as a many-flowered paradise, O all-glorious and wise ones, breathing forth the fragrance of the Spirit and driving away foul-smelling passions from men!

Stavrotheotokion: Wonderful is Thy Childbirth, O Mother of God, Who workest great wonders and art glorified among the saints, O only all-marvelous Sovereign Lady!

Another [Canon to the Theotokos]. Heirmos: The same.

Let not the abyss of slothfulness swallow me up, O Sovereign Lady, and let not the wave of sin cover me; but by Thy solitary prayer may I be saved, O pure one!

Having given birth unto the good Benefactor and Creator, O all-hymned Sovereign Lady, loving goodness: make my afflicted soul blessed!

The sacred writers prefigured Thee under the Law, O most-pure one, who didst bear the Light that enlightens all things; therefore I cry unto Thee: Enlighten me who am darkened!

Thou didst bear unto us the Cause of salvation, the Life-giver, Who truly grants eternal redemption unto those who proclaim Thee as the Mother of God!

Ode 7. Heirmos:

The Lord exalted above all by the fathers:

Israel tasted corruption in the thorns, the assembly of the lawless transgressing the steps; but Thou, cutting down the deceitful thorns from the roots: Blessed art Thou, O God!

That Thou mightest clothe me with the garment of incorruption, O Word, Thou wast stripped naked willingly; and Thou didst endure spitting, and crucifixion, [f. 156rA] and death, being immortal in essence!

To the Martyrs: Conformed unto the sufferings of the Holy One Who rules over all: ye were gloriously made sons and heirs of the unshakable Kingdom!

To the Martyrs: Ye gave no honor unto trees, being most irrational, but honoring Christ Who stretched out His hands upon the Tree, O Martyrs, the King and Good God of all!

Stavrotheotokion: Strange was Thy Childbirth, O all-immaculate one; for Thou didst bear God, Who withered the flame of deceit by the Tree, and enlightened the world!

Another [Canon to the Theotokos]. Heirmos: The same.

All creation sings Thy praise; for without seed Thou didst bear the all-hymned God, O most-pure Virgin, deifying those who sing: Blessed art Thou, O God!

Deadened by my passions, raise me up who lie fallen, O Bride of God, who didst bear Life from Thy womb without knowing man, that in love I may glorify Thee!

Look down upon the supplications of Thy servants, O Sovereign Lady, delivering from harms and saving from tribulations those who sing in faith: Blessed art Thou, O God!

Thou didst bear the Countless One Who bore our weakness, O pure one; entreat Him to heal my soul which is fiercely weakened!

Ode 8. Heirmos:

Unto Thee, the Creator of all, in the furnace:

O God on high, uplifted upon the Cross, given gall to drink, O Sweetness of Life, pierced with a Lance, Thou didst slay the serpent who cast down Adam in Paradise!

Thou Who didst loose me from the bonds of sin, [f. 156rB] O Word, being bound by Thine own will, and binding the hostile Belial unto eternal bonds: therefore I glorify Thy Passion unto all the ages!

To the Martyrs: Ye were revealed as partakers of the immaterial Light, being secondary lights, O holy Martyrs, taking away the darkness of deceit and divinely enlightening the hearts of all the faithful!

To the Martyrs: Ye were made sons of the free Jerusalem on high, O Martyrs, enlightening the Church of the firstborn, and exalting Christ above all unto the ages!

Stavrotheotokion: The Maiden stood by the Cross, beholding Christ nailed, Whom She had borne, O Good One; therefore She cried aloud: Leave Me not alone, O Thou Who art without beginning, Son and Word of the Father without beginning!

Another [Canon to the Theotokos]. Heirmos: The same.

O Virgin most-fair and God-radiant: beautify me by the vision of good things and enlighten me, that I may cry: Hymn the Lord and exalt Him above all unto the ages!

Open unto me the gates of light, the radiant gates of repentance, showing me the great and straight path of righteousness, which leads unto the entrance of the divine will!

Thou didst ineffably give birth unto the Word, O pure and most-holy one, the Word overshadowing with wings of God; entreat Him to cleanse now my humble soul, which is defiled with malice!

The Lord of all, O Maiden, pierced the clear arrow of immortality into incorruption; therefore I cry unto Thee: Dry up the evil arrows of my passions by the showers of Thy prayers, O pure one!

[f. 156vA] Ode 9. Heirmos:

Rejoice, O Isaiah! For the Virgin hath received:

Uplifted as a Lamb upon the Tree, O Master Christ, Thou didst crush the jaws of the noetic wolf, snatching away Thy rational sheep from his mouth, and bringing them unto Thyself![^235]

Thou wast crowned with a crown of thorns, O Christ, King of kings, casting down the kingdoms of the evil one, and cutting down from the roots the thorns of deceit; therefore in faith we glorify Thee!

To the Martyrs: Ye shone forth as the sun, having become a steadfast defense, and scattered all the mist of the adversaries, O unconquerable Martyrs, enlighteners of all the faithful, unshakable pillars of piety, O highly blessed ones!

To the Martyrs: A God-chosen company, an honorable army, a chosen assembly, a holy host were ye shown to be, O all-praised Martyrs, destroying the malignant ranks of the enemy by the divine grace of the Savior!

Stavrotheotokion: Thou didst bear the Planter of the Garden, the Author of piety, Who plants true understanding upon earth, and looses the curse that came forth from Eden; Whom magnifying, O Virgin, we call Thee blessed!

Another [Canon to the Theotokos]. Heirmos: The same.

Thou didst bear the immovable Foundation, the Savior, O pure one, Who by divine command founded the earth upon the waters; we pray Thee to establish us upon Him, that we may honor those who glorify Thee!

Gather me, O pure one, to walk without stumbling in the path of humility according to the divine commandments, [f. 156vB] driving away demonic confusion and the assault of passions, and granting me tranquility!

Held fast by the slumber of slothfulness, the enemy shamelessly beholds me, hoping to strengthen himself against me with the sleep of pleasure; but do Thou Thyself preserve me, O pure one, by Thy sleepless prayer, O Virgin Mother!

As one self-condemned, I contemplate the multitude of my sins, and the dread tribunal before which alone I must be judged; but O Thou Who alone didst bear God, preserve me uncondemned at that time, O Mother of God!

At the Aposticha, Stichera of the Cross, Tone 5:
