No sooner was the wood of Thy Cross planted, O Christ, than idolatrous deceit was driven away and grace blossomed forth; no longer is there the tyranny of condemnation, but the victory of our salvation hath appeared! For the Cross is our boast; the Cross is our strengthening; the Cross is our joy!

Led as a sheep unto sacrifice for our sake, O Christ, and as a guileless Lamb, Emmanuel went unto voluntary slaughter, and was numbered among the transgressors! Come, ye tribes of the nations, sing and worship Him Who conquered upon the Cross, the Life without end!

To the Martyrs: The holy Martyrs contested upon earth; they endured frost, they were delivered unto fire, they received cruel water; their voice is: We went through fire and water, and Thou leddest us out into a place of rest! By their prayers, O God, have mercy on us!

[f. 157rA] *Glory... Now and ever... Stavrotheotokion.*

*Podoben: "Rejoice, O container of ascetics" (Ра́дꙋйсѧ по́стникѡмъ):*

Standing by the Cross, O Jesus, She who bore Thee wept and lamented, crying aloud: I cannot bear to see Him nailed upon the Tree, Whom I brought forth, escaping the pains of childbirth as without a husband! And how am I now held fast by pain, and torn in heart, O immaculate one? For now is fulfilled the word which Simeon spake: A sword shall pierce through mine own heart! But now, O my Son, arise and save those who hymn Thee!

ON WEDNESDAY, The Beatitudes, Tone 5:

The Thief, believing Thee to be God upon the Cross, O Christ, confessed Thee purely from the heart: Remember me, O Lord, in Thy Kingdom!

Having ascended the Cross, Thou didst shake all the demonic host, and cast down the ruinous dominion [f. 157rB] of the tyrant, as Thou art Christ, and savedst mankind!

Pierced in the side, Thou didst pour forth streams of remission unto us, O Christ; and nailed upon the Tree, Thou didst cleanse all passionate human understanding!

To the Martyrs: Having become imitators of Christ's Sufferings, ye endured every torment, O passion-bearers of the Lord; therefore ye were counted worthy of the fair things in Heaven!

Glory...

Upon the Cross, O Christ, inseparable from the Father and the divine Spirit, Thou didst willingly endure the Passion, receiving and taking away all our corruptions!

Now and ever... Theotokion:

Standing before the Cross, O full of God's grace, and beholding Thy Son with wounds, Thou wast wounded in soul, singing of His manifold and supreme condescension!

## WEDNESDAY EVENING VESPERS (FOR THURSDAY) (TONE 5)

ON WEDNESDAY EVENING, AT "LORD, I HAVE CRIED":

*Stichera to the Holy Apostles, Tone 5.*

*Podoben: "Rejoice, O container of ascetics" (Ра́дꙋйсѧ по́стникѡмъ):*

Having traversed all the earth, ye illuminated it with divine teachings, having the Word alone as a lamp; and all your wealth, O disciples of the Lord, served for our benefit! Ye put sorcerers and tyrants to shame, and tore apart the cunning webs of those who practiced deceit; and ye called all men unto the knowledge of the Creator, taking away idolatrous demonic services! Therefore I pray: Deliver me from irrational passions by your prayers![^236]

From the tumult of temptations, and cruel defeat, and lawless heresies, from demonic malice, and the bitter assault of men, and all kinds of perils, from immaterial fire, and the eternal worm, and gnashing [f. 157vA] of teeth, and every other torment, deliver all of us by your supplications unto the Lord; and praying unto Him, entreat that we may obtain the reward of abstinence, labors, and virtues, and the inheritance of the heavenly Kingdom, and great mercy!

Receiving the second Trinity light of ineffable dispensation brightly and clearly, as was truly possible for human nature: the all-praised Twelve appeared in perfection, leading the assembly born of one mother, having the company of the Seventy and two; enlightening all the ends of the world, and darkening the gloom of malicious heresies, entreating Christ, Who grants great mercy unto the world!

*Other Stichera to Saint Nicholas.*

*Podoben: "The same Tone and Podoben" (Гла́съ и҆ подо́бенъ то́йже):*

Rejoice, O sacred head, pure dwelling of virtues, divine rule of the immaculate priesthood, great and radiant shepherd, whose very name is bright: mercifully inclining unto those who pray, bending down unto the supplications of the weak, ready deliverer, saving refuge for all who honor thy most-glorious memory in faith: entreat Christ to send down upon us great mercy!

Rejoice, O most-sacred mind, pure dwelling of the Trinity, pillar of the Church, strengthening of the faithful, helper of the afflicted: star that by favor of acceptable prayers [f. 157vB] scatters unexpected perils and the darkness thereof, O holy hierarch Nicholas, calm haven wherein those who take refuge are saved from the surging waves of the temptations of earthly life: entreat Christ to send down great mercy unto our souls!

Rejoice, O rule among the saints, inexhaustible deep of divine wonders, marvelous beauty, bright star that by the holy Gospels, O blessed one, enlightenest each of us, most-holy refuge stretched forth by prayers, unconquerable pillar, step of faith: entreat Christ to grant great mercy unto our souls, who honorably celebrate thy memory in love!

Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion:

Rejoice, O most-pure Seal, God-proclaiming herald of the Apostles; for Thou didst bear God truly incarnate, O pure one, beyond mind and word; whereby having received our first nobility and enjoying the food of Paradise, we honor Thee in songs as the mediatress of such good things and most acceptable intercessor; enriched by Thee, O most-pure one, we are counted worthy of the everlasting life of Thy Son, Who richly grants great mercy!

At the Aposticha, Stichera of the Apostles, Tone 5:

O Disciples of the Savior, having been eyewitnesses of the mysteries of Him Who is invisible and hath no beginning, ye proclaimed, saying: In the beginning was the Word, uncreated before the Angels; [f. 158rA] nor were ye taught by men, but by the wisdom from on high! Therefore, having boldness, pray ye for our souls!

Let us praise the Apostles of Christ with one accord in songs; for having girded themselves with the weapon of the Cross, they abolished idolatrous deceit, and were revealed as victorious crown-bearers. By their supplications and those of all the saints, O God, have mercy on us!

To the Martyrs: With insatiable love of soul, ye abandoned all things for Christ, O holy Martyrs; having endured diverse wounds and passions, ye cast down the pride of the tyrants, and having preserved the faith unswerving and uninjured, ye passed over into the Heavens; whence having boldness toward Him, ask that great mercy be granted unto us!

Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion:

We bless Thee, O Virgin Mother of God, and we the faithful glorify Thee as is meet: the unshakable city, the impregnable wall, the steadfast protectress, and refuge of our souls!

ON THURSDAY, AT MATINS:

After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymns of the Apostles, Tone 5:

As eyewitnesses and ministers of the Word, let us all the faithful praise the most-wise Apostles with spiritual songs; for they pray diligently for us who sing of their sacred memory and bow down before their relics!

Let us praise the all-hymned Apostles as eyewitnesses of the Word, divine preachers, and spiritual fishers of the nations; [f. 158rB] for they have thus brought us unto the knowledge of Christ, Who hath delivered the human race from deceit, and made them worthy of the Kingdom!

Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion:

I am condemned by the judgment of my conscience, and before the judgment I contemplate the judgment; I tremble, wretch that I am, remembering the multitude of my evils; but unto Thee, the unconquerable one, I cry in compunction, and unto my protectress and veil: Deliver me from that shame, and save me by Thy prayers!

After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns of the Apostles, Tone 5:

Let us praise the Apostles with one accord, who preached the Orthodox doctrine of the Lord unto all, extinguished the gloom of heresies, and caused spiritual enlightenment to shine in the world by the grace of teaching, and who pray that we may be saved!

To the Martyrs: At the achievements of the holy Martyrs the heavenly powers were wondrously amazed; for in mortal flesh, through the power of the Cross having contested well, they invisibly conquered the bodiless enemy. And they pray unto the Lord that our souls may find mercy!

Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion:

Having found Thee as a haven, and wall, and refuge, and hope, and protection, and fervent defense, we the faithful flee unto Thee, and cry earnestly, and call out in faith: Have mercy, O Mother of God, upon those who hope in Thee, and deliver from transgressions!

*After the 3rd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns of the Apostles, Tone 5.*

*Podoben: "The Word co-unoriginate" (Собезнача́льное Сло́во):*

O Disciples of the Savior, divine [f. 158vA] Apostles, who made the saving word to shine forth in the ends of the earth, and enlightened those who sat in darkness and the shadow of death: enlighten my soul, darkened by the blackness of passions, through your supplications, O all-praised ones![^237]

O Lord, preaching the ineffable mystery of Thine Incarnation, unlearned men put philosophers to shame; fishermen silenced orators, and became most-wise teachers of the nations, enlightening the ends of the world with the light of divine knowledge; and through them grant unto us great mercy!

Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion:

Having an unshakable hope in Thee, O all-pure Virgin, and possessing Thee as our protection: deliver us from diverse perils, tribulations, and cruel afflictions, praying unto Thy Son, together with His Apostles, to save all who hymn Thee!

Canon to the Holy Apostles.

Ode 1. Tone 5. Heirmos:

The horse and the rider into the sea:

Enriched with the light-bestowing radiance of the Author of Light, O glorious Apostles, who was well-pleased to commune with men in the flesh: scatter all the gloom of my soul, O divine Apostles!

Having strung you as arrows upon the divine bow, the divine Apostles were sent into all the world, breaking all the arrows of Belial and healing the wounds of the faithful!

Having Wisdom Itself as your Teacher, O Apostles, ye made all the ends of the earth wise; therefore enlighten me to repel every evil deed of the enemy!

[f. 158vB] O only blessed and God-favored one, who didst bear Christ among blessed men: pray Thou unto Him, together with the divine Apostles, that we may find mercy!

Another Canon to Saint Nicholas.

A Composition of Joseph.

Heirmos: The same.

In faith and love, O father, thou didst join thyself unto God, fulfilling His desires in every way; therefore we cry aloud: Holy hast thou been, O God-bearer Nicholas!

Possessing thee as an advocate with the Compassionate One, O blessed one, surrounded by tribulations and afflictions, we flee unto thee: Stretch forth a hand of salvation, delivering from great distress!

Christ showed thee as a Hierarch unto the people of Myra, sweetening us with the fragrance of wonders; therefore we pray thee: Deliver us from the foul stench of sin, O Nicholas!

Of old the prophetic choir named Thee the divine Mountain, O Maiden, and the impassable Gate; therefore we pray Thee: Open unto us the divine gates of repentance, O Virgin!

Ode 3. Heirmos:

Thou Who didst establish the earth upon nothing:

He Who became poor in the flesh through His great goodness enriched you who became poor for His sake, O glorious Apostles, with all kinds of gifts, who have enriched the ends of the world with divine and honorable signs from God!

I have been wounded by the venomous bite of passions, and have acquired a wounded heart; therefore I cry unto Thee, O Christ, Who wast wounded for my sake:

[f. 159rA] heal me by the supplications of Thine Apostles, and save me, I pray!

By the net of your prayers, O all-blessed ones, draw me up from the depths of the malice of the tempter and from the tempest of deadly passionate thoughts; and bring me, saved, unto Christ!

O Thou Who didst receive the heavenly Rain, pray Thou unto Him together with the Apostles to stay the shower of my passions, drying up the deep of my sin, and to save me who purely glorify Thee!

Another [Canon to Saint Nicholas]. Heirmos: The same.

Thou didst blunt the arrows of the evil one, O venerable one, by the resistance of thy divine righteousness; but by thy most-wise supplications, O Nicholas, preserve us uninjured, overcoming his evil deeds!

Having shown an angelic life upon earth, thou now standest unceasingly with the Angels before the Thrice-holy Throne; ask cleansing for our transgressions and release from perils, O father and Chief-hierarch Nicholas!

Drive away all the gloom of my darkness by thy light-bearing prayers, O Nicholas; calm the tempest of passions, and steer me, O father, unto the haven of dispassion, I pray thee, that in praise I may glorify thee!

Clothed in divine vesture, O Christ, as a Queen, adorned with golden fringe, the all-immaculate Mother of God intercedes by Her supplications to make us citizens of the heavenly Kingdom!

Ode 4. Heirmos:

Perceiving Thy divine condescension:

[f. 159rB] The beloved Son, Jesus, my God and Lord, made known His Father unto the Apostles, and opened the door unto all nations through their teachings!

O Son of God, Who didst reveal the Apostles as sons by adoption unto Thy heavenly Father: by their supplications make all of us sons of the light!

Ye who are to sit gloriously upon thrones with the Judge and King at the end: deliver me, O Apostles, from that dread and fearful judgment!

Theotokion: O Ark of divine sanctification, cleanse my soul, enlighten my mind, when Thou prayest unto Christ with the Apostles that He may save me!

Another [Canon to Saint Nicholas]. Heirmos: The same.

Thou hast been delivered from diverse perils, and by thy holy prayers make us also heirs thereof, O Nicholas, delivering our life from great tribulations!

Having been the First-enthroned of Myra, O Nicholas: sweeten all the senses of my heart with chrism, O Savior, driving away foul-smelling passions therefrom at all times!

Crushing the wiles of the enemy, O Nicholas: crush our visible and invisible enemies forever, and deliver them unto utter ruin!

Theotokion: O holy Mother of God, help me who am ever drowned in carnal pleasures; for I lie willingly upon the bed of slothfulness and affliction!

Ode 5. Heirmos:

Thou Who clothest Thyself with light as with a garment:

Spiritual luminaries, most-wise Apostles, who received the fire from the upper room, when the Holy Spirit came unto us, [f. 159vA] ye sang with fearful awe!

Christ sent you, the Apostles, as chosen arrows, shattering the arrows of wickedness; therefore heal me who am wounded by the arrows of the enemy![^238]

Ye who tilled the earth of impiety, and loosed the thoughts of my sins: heal me, O Apostles, with the dew of healing!

Theotokion: Condemn me not, nor cast me away from Thy presence, O Most-merciful One; for She who gave Thee pure birth entreats Thee, together with the company of the Apostles!

Another [Canon to Saint Nicholas]. Heirmos: The same.

Thou didst cast down the idol shrines, O holy one, and showedst the counsels of heretics to be of no avail, O Nicholas, and didst snatch away those who were being led unto death!

Thou didst rise early unto the Lord from childhood, O venerable one, and wast wholly illuminated with divine radiance; therefore I pray thee: Disperse the clouds of my soul!

We pray thee, O father Nicholas: Be present in the midst of all who call upon thee, granting us those petitions which lead unto salvation!

Theotokion: Incomprehensible to the mind, the Word becoming a flesh-bearer received Thee as His dwelling, O full of God's grace, delivering mankind from the sorrows that encompass them!

Ode 6. Heirmos:

Tossed by the tempest of the soul:

Seasoning with the salt of teachings the souls of the nations which had opened wide their mouths unto rot of malice, O Lover of mankind, through Thy sacred Disciples!

From the depth of perils and my evils, O Master Christ: stretch forth Thy hand, and save [f. 159vB] me, O Lover of mankind, through the supplications of Thy sacred Apostles!

O most-righteous Judge, deliver me from condemnation on the dread and fearful day of judgment, by the prayers of Thy glorious Apostles!

Theotokion: Count me worthy of the salvation of the Lord, who am estranged by the multitude of my iniquities, through the supplications of the Disciples and Thy Mother!

Another [Canon to Saint Nicholas]. Heirmos: The same.

Offer acceptable prayer by thy supplications, O Nicholas, for all who honor thee, that forgiveness may be granted unto our sins!

Deliver us from diseases and the scandals of this life, and uproot tribulations, O Nicholas, who possess thee as an intercessor with the Lord!

Christ showed thee as an excellent and good physician; therefore heal the infirmities of those who piously flee unto thee, O Nicholas!

Theotokion: A Mother without husband, Thou didst become the pure Mother of God; therefore in faith I pray Thee: Disperse the grief of my soul!

Ode 7. Heirmos:

The Lord exalted above all by the fathers:

The God-seeing Disciples of Christ exalted Him, and cast down all the power of the enemy!

Wash away the filth of my heart with streams of repentance, O Apostles, by your prayers, having taught us to cry: Blessed art Thou, O God!

With the fire of the Holy Spirit ye burned up the substance of great demonic delusion; therefore deliver me from burning Gehenna, O Disciples of God the Word!

O Thou Who didst correct the fall of Adam: raise me up who have fallen into the pit of malice, by Thy prayers, O Virgin, [f. 160rA] and those of the divine Apostles!

Another [Canon to Saint Nicholas]. Heirmos: The same.

Having committed thyself wholly unto God, O Nicholas: save me wholly, who am ever cast down by worldly passions, O God-wise one!

O most God-radiant luminary, illuminate my mind, which is ever darkened by the gloom of passions, and grant that I may walk decorously in life!

By thy prayers, O Nicholas, close the evil mouths that open wide against us, and deliver me from visible and invisible enemies!

Theotokion: From Thee hath arisen the unwaning Sun, O all-radiant cloud, Christ our God, enlightening those who sit in the darkness of ignorance!

Ode 8. Heirmos:

Unto Thee, the Creator of all, in the furnace:

As noetic clouds, O Word, Thou didst spread abroad the Apostles, showering down upon us the vehement rain of wise and divine teachings, watering us unto all the ages!

O most-excellent pillars of the Church, who hold fast the teaching of the faith: by your divine skill strengthen the decayed temple of my soul, O God-seers!

Offer sighing of soul and streams of tears earnestly unto the Lord, crying: O only Compassionate One, cleanse me and save me, through the prayers of the all-praised Apostles!

Theotokion: O chosen Company, imperial City: make me a citizen of the city on high, praying with the divine Disciples, O all-pure Virgin, unto Thy timeless Son!

Another [Canon to Saint Nicholas]. Heirmos: The same.

[f. 160rB] Thou didst put to silence the blasphemous streams of Arius, O most-wise one, with the streams of thy holy tongue; therefore I cry unto thee: Dry up the torrents of my evils by thy prayers, O blessed Nicholas!

Having become the great Chief-hierarch in Myra, O Nicholas: sweeten the senses of my soul with chrism, that I may escape the wickedness of passions and receive the grace of the Comforter!

Deliver us from sins by thy prayers, from Egyptian affliction, and heathen captivity, and the evil harm of all men, that we may praise thee as our deliverer!

Theotokion: Having clothed Himself in incorrupt flesh for our sake, O pure one, God revealed Thee, the all-immaculate Virgin, as a divine protectress for all our race; therefore we honor Thee unto all the ages!

Ode 9. Heirmos:

Rejoice, O Isaiah! For the Virgin:

Not deceived in mind, ye were revealed as radiantly shining with the radiances of divine virtues, having Christ in your midst as the Sun, and ye enlightened the ends of the earth, O most-wise ones; therefore ye are called blessed!

Bearing the wounds of Christ upon your divine bodies as an all-comely adornment, O most-wise ones: heal my soul, wounded with the arrows of the viper, by your prayers unto the Lord!

Lying in the lowest pit of sin, O Christ, and having weighed down my soul with the sleep of slothfulness: raise me up as Thou didst Lazarus, for the sake of Thy Disciples, O Word, and save me, O Lord!

[f. 160vA] Direct the steps of my soul, O Word of God, unto the unerring paths of Thy commandments, having Her who bore Thee praying for me, the all-immaculate and pure Virgin, and Thy most-wise Apostles, O Most-merciful One![^239]

Another [Canon to Saint Nicholas]. Heirmos: The same.

Having become a divine Hierarch, thou didst keep all the commandments of Christ; therefore, having become a divine guardian for the faithful, preserve them, O father Nicholas, from every affliction and torment!

Even as thou didst of old feed thy city in time of famine when bread failed, as a good and venerable shepherd: so also nourish my soul with spiritual bread, O father Nicholas, who possess thee as an advocate!

Praising thee in faith as a great luminary set high in the Church of Christ, O venerable pastor: by thy light-bearing, powerful prayers drive away the deep darkness of sin from our souls!

The day of manifestation, the coming of Christ, hath drawn near, as it is written; put off slothfulness, O barren soul, and cry aloud earnestly unto Christ: Save me, O Lord, through the supplications of Nicholas!

Theotokion: The Prophet foresaw Thee as a light-bearing Lampstand, O most-pure one, carrying the noetic Candle, Christ, by Whom we who lie in the darkness of passions are enlightened, magnifying Thee as the Mother of God and ever-virgin!

At the Aposticha, Stichera of the Apostles, Tone 5:

O Disciples of the Savior, having been eyewitnesses of the mysteries of Him Who is invisible and hath no beginning, ye proclaimed, [f. 160vB] saying: In the beginning was the Word; ye were not created before the Angels, nor were ye taught by men, but by the wisdom from on high! Therefore, having boldness, pray ye for our souls!

Let us praise the Apostles of Christ with one accord in songs; for having girded themselves with the weapon of the Cross, they abolished idolatrous deceit, and were revealed as victorious crown-bearers. By their prayers and those of all the saints, O God, have mercy on us!

To the Martyrs: Being in torments, the Saints cried out rejoicing: This is a gain for us unto God! In place of wounds upon our bodies, the radiant garment of the resurrection shall blossom forth for us; in place of dishonor, crowns; for prison bonds, Paradise; and in place of condemnation with evildoers, life with the Angels! Therefore, by their prayers, O Lord, save our souls!

Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion:

We bless Thee, O Virgin Mother of God, for from Thee hath shone forth Christ the Sun of Righteousness, Who hath great mercy!

ON THURSDAY, The Beatitudes, Tone 5:

The Thief, believing Thee to be God upon the Cross, O Christ, confessed Thee purely from the heart: Remember me, O Lord, in Thy Kingdom!

Like bright clouds, ye traversed the earth, sprinkling life-bearing water, and richly watering hearts made barren by sin, O divine Disciples!

Like mystical rays of the Sun that shone forth from the pure Virgin, ye enlighten those who sit in the darkness of ignorance, [f. 161rA] O divine Disciples of Christ our God!

To the Martyrs: Having endured the fierce burning of torments with zealous soul, O most-wise ones, ye burned up idolatrous deceit, and passed over unto divine rest, O holy Martyrs!

Glory... Triadikon:

O Most-holy Trinity, Father without beginning, co-beginningless Son, and Holy Spirit: one Godhead, by the prayers of all the preachers, preserve Thy Church!

Now and ever... Theotokion:

Adornment of the Apostles, O only God-favored one: enlighten me with the radiances of repentance, who am darkened by worldly pleasures, that I may magnify Thee!

## THURSDAY EVENING VESPERS (FOR FRIDAY) (TONE 5)

ON THURSDAY EVENING, AT "LORD, I HAVE CRIED":

*Stichera of the Cross, Tone 5.*

*Podoben: "O venerable father" (Преподо́бне ѻ҆́ч҃е):*

Let all the trees of the forest rejoice, beholding the all-honorable Wood made glad by the Passion of Christ, distilling grace like a flame of fire, and driving away passions, bestowing gifts upon all: enlightening souls and thoughts, healing diseases, driving away passions, casting far away invisible demons, and manifestly conquering barbarian nations: ever granting victories unto our rulers over barbarians, blessing unto the faithful, and great mercy!

Worshipping in faith the place where the feet of the Lord stood, even as the Prophet spake: we glorify Christ Who was crucified and Who crucified our transgressions, Who loosed the curse of the tree, and reconciled mankind wholly unto the Father by His thoughts, kissing the nails of His hands and feet, the Lance, the Reed, the Sponge, and [f. 161rB] the Crown, honoring with reverence the spittings and mockings, and all other things which the hymn sings, whereby we have been saved!

Crucified together in all the members of Christ, and having died unto the world and the world-ruler: desiring to walk in the footsteps of Christ, let us bear the same divine Cross upon our shoulders, casting away carnal wantonness and evil lusts which draw the soul unto sin! Deeming that we stand before Him and behold Him nailed upon the Cross, and committing His spirit unto His Father with a sigh: that we may ever be inseparable from Him!

Other Stichera to the Most-holy Theotokos, same Tone:

When the unplowed Vine bloomed forth the Cluster unto the Father: beholding Him hung upon the Tree, pierced [f. 161vA] and pierced with a spear in Thy Life-giving Side. What is this, She cried, O my Son and my God? How dost Thou, Who healest all diseases and passions, endure passions, being impassible according to Thy Divine nature? What have the ungrateful people rendered unto Thee, their Benefactor, in return for Thy benefactions? cried the Most-pure One. But by His Passions, pray unceasingly that I may be delivered from passions, that I may glorify Thee![^240]

Let us all weep, and stretch forth our hands, looking up unto Him with fervent tears; and bowing the knee, beating our faces earnestly unto the earth, let us send up sighs unto the height, who by our improper deeds have angered God through the rejection of His commandments, crying aloud: Deliver us from the coming woes and every torment! As for those who have grieved Thee and turned away in shame, for whose sake Thou didst endure the Cross, having become incarnate: through the supplications of Thy Mother, make them partakers of Thy Kingdom!

Unto whom hast thou become likened, O my soul, ever advancing in what is worse, and senselessly adding multiple sores unto thy wounds, so that the wound is over all the body, not considering that the Judge draws near, before Whom thou shalt stand to receive punishment and torment according to thy deeds? But turn back and fall down before the Virgin, crying: O Sovereign Lady, O Sovereign Lady! Despise me not, who have angered the most-beneficent God, Who was born of Thee for the salvation of men, and was crucified in the flesh!

[f. 161vB] *Glory... Now and ever... Of the Cross.*

*Podoben: "Rejoice, O container of ascetics" (Ра́дꙋйсѧ по́стничкѡмъ):*

As a ransom for our sake and as a great price, Thou wast well-pleased to give Thy most-pure Blood, O my sinless Christ, desiring that we should obtain salvation in due time. Therefore, beholding Thee nailed fast, the Mother of God wept and tore Her hair, saying: O Child, all-immaculate Lamb, Who desirest to redeem the world by Thy precious Blood! O my womb, how hast Thou set, O Savior, the unsetting Sun, Who bestowest upon all enlightenment, and peace, and great mercy?

At the Aposticha, Stichera of the Cross, Tone 5:

Lord, in the time of Moses the Prophet of old, the mere image of Thy Cross being shown forth conquered Thine enemies; and now, having Thy Cross itself, we ask for help: establish Thy Church, and grant victory unto our rulers, as unto Constantine, for the sake of Thy manifold mercy, O Lover of mankind!

Thy Cross, O Christ, even if it is visible wood in essence, is clothed in Divine power; and being visibly shown forth unto the world, it noetically works our salvation. Worshipping it, we glorify Thee, O Savior: have mercy on us!

To the Martyrs: Caring naught for all earthly things, and manly daring to enter into torments, ye missed not the blessed hopes, but became heirs of the heavenly Kingdom, O all-praised Martyrs! Having boldness before God Who loves mankind, entreat peace for the world, [f. 162rA] and for our souls great mercy!

Glory... Now and ever... Of the Cross:

Beholding of old Her Lamb and Her Son, the Virgin Mother and all-blessed Maiden, uplifted upon the Cross, cried aloud weeping: Woe is Me, O My Son! How dost Thou die, Who art God immortal by nature?

## FRIDAY MATINS: THE PRECIOUS CROSS AND THE THEOTOKOS (TONE 5)

ON FRIDAY AT MATINS.

After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymns of the Cross, Tone 5:

The Place of the Skull became Paradise; for as soon as the Wood of the Cross was planted, straightway it budded forth the Life-bearing Cluster, even Thee, O Savior, unto our gladness. Glory to Thee!

Hymning the Savior and Redeemer Who was crucified for our sake, Who willingly went up upon the Cross as He was well-pleased, we the faithful glorify Him, for He nailed the sins of men upon the Cross, delivering the human race from deception, and vouchsafed us the Kingdom.

Glory... Now and ever... Of the Cross:

Standing of old by the Cross of the Lord, weeping, the Pure One cried aloud: Woe is Me, O My Divine Child! Woe is Me, O sweetest Light unto My eyes! How art Thou stretched upon the Cross, Who stretchedst out the heaven like a curtain, and Who liftest up the fountains of waters from the sea by Thy command?

After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns of the Cross, Tone 5:

Having endured crucifixion by Thy free will, Thou didst deliver mankind from corruption, O Savior! We the faithful hymn Thee and worship Thee; [f. 162rB] for Thou didst illumine us by the power of the Cross, and we all glorify Thee, O Lover of mankind and Compassionate One!

As the Giver of Life and the Lord, O Compassionate One, Thou didst willingly endure the Cross, and as almighty God Thou didst destroy the ancient curse incurred through eating. Therefore we hymn and worship Thy Divine and precious Passions, O Christ, unceasingly glorifying Thy dispensation which surpasses understanding!

To the Martyrs: Today shines the memory of the Passion-bearers, for it hath illumination from the heavens; the angelic choir keeps festival, and the human race celebrates with them. Therefore they pray unto the Lord that our souls may find mercy!

Glory... Now and ever... Of the Cross:

By the Cross of Thy Son, O Thou full of God's grace, all idolatrous deception was abolished, and demonic power was trampled down. For this cause we the faithful ever hymn and bless Thee as is due, confessing Thee truly to be the Mother of God, and we magnify Thee!

*After the 3rd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns of the Cross, Tone 5.*

*Podoben: "The Word co-unoriginate" (Собезнача́льное Сло́во):*

Seeing Thee nailed upon the Cross, the angelic ranks were seized with dread, O Jesus, King of the sun! The demonic hosts wandered in defeat, the bars of hades were shattered, the tyranny of death was cast down, and the dead in the tombs arose!

Bitterness took hold of Adam through the tree, when he stumbled at the secret command; but when Thou wast nailed fast, O Jesus, Adam tasted of life, [f. 162vA] and through the Wood of the Cross was brought back again into heaven; the serpent was abolished, corruption was swallowed up, and we all offer glory unto Thee![^241]

Glory... Now and ever... Of the Cross:

Beholding Thee, O Christ, hanging willingly upon the Cross between thieves, Thy Mother, moved with maternal sorrow, cried aloud: O sinless Son, how art Thou unjustly nailed upon the Cross like an evildoer, desiring to make alive the human race, as Thou art all-good?

CANON TO THE PRECIOUS AND LIFE-CREATING CROSS OF THE LORD.

Composition of Joseph.

Ode 1. Tone 5. Heirmos:

Unto God the Savior, Who guided the people through the sea with dryshod feet, and drowned Pharaoh with all his army: unto Him alone let us sing, for He hath been glorified!

Enduring suffering by Thine own will, O Christ, Thou didst endure the Passion, and didst bind him who of old slew us in Paradise. Therefore we glorify Thy goodness!

Thou wast uplifted upon the Cross, and the enemy fell down, and the fallen arose; and we were made citizens of Paradise, O Christ, glorifying the dominion of Thy Kingdom!

To the Martyrs: Having well armed yourselves with the shield of faith, ye stood in battle array against the great strife of the tyrants, O all-wise Great Martyrs, and having conquered them, ye received glory!

To the Martyrs: As precious lambs, O precious Passion-bearers, ye offered yourselves unto the Lamb Who was slain for our sake, manifestly forsaking detestable sacrifices; [f. 162vB] therefore we call you blessed, O all-praised ones!

Theotokion: Thou didst bring forth for us a new Child, ancient of days, O pure Virgin, Who renews human nature that had grown old, O all-immaculate one, by His Divine Passion!

Another Canon to the Most-holy Theotokos. Heirmos: The same.

Knowing Thee to be a fountain of tender compassion and a firm protectress for all, O all-immaculate Virgin Mother Mary, we send up cries unto Thee: Have mercy and take pity upon my humble soul!

Thou didst hold in Thy womb the Son of God, O pure one, and He assumed human nature as He is all-good, and delivered all men from the corruption of death!

Be Thou my enlightenment and the hope of my salvation, O all-immaculate Mother of God, loosing the bonds of my transgressions, and delivering me from future torment and condemnation!

Deliver my humble soul from evil thoughts, O Mother of God, and make it a dwelling place of God, that I may ever glorify Thee as is due!

Ode 3. Heirmos:

By the power of Thy Cross, O Christ, establish my understanding, that I may hymn and glorify Thy saving crucifixion upon the Cross!

Thou didst sweeten the fruit of corruption when uplifted upon the Tree, O Savior, and didst pour forth unto us from Thy side fountains of incorruption!

Thou wast slain as a lamb upon the Cross, [f. 163rA] marking the doorposts of our houses with Thy Divine Blood, O Master; therefore with fear we glorify Thee!

To the Martyrs: Strengthened by Christ, O Passion-bearers, and fortified in diverse manners, ye remained unshaken, like towers against missiles!

To the Martyrs: Like clusters of the living Vine, the Martyrs of Christ our God distilled the wine of suffering, gladdening the hearts of the faithful!

Theotokion: Thou Mediatress of life unto us, O pure one: Thy Son and Lord was shown forth dead upon the Tree, glorifying those who hymn Thee!

Another [Canon to the Theotokos]. Heirmos: The same.

Rescue me who have fallen into the pit of destruction of cruel sins, O Mother of God, by Thy compassionate goodness!

Having arrived at the evening of life, and being held fast by evil deeds, I cry unto Thee, O all-immaculate one: Show Thyself to be my helper!

Holy Mother of God, pure one: grant remission of my transgressions by Thy prayers, and entreat for me salvation and eternal joy!

Grant me a drop of tears, O pure one, that I may wash away the perplexity from my heart, and purely hymn Thee!

Ode 4. Heirmos:

I heard the report of the power of the Cross, how Paradise was opened unto us; and I cried aloud: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

When Thou, the Sun of Righteousness, O Christ, didst set upon the Cross, Thou didst cause unwaning light to shine upon us who sing of Thy dread condescension, O Word!

When Thou didst stand before the judgment seat, O Christ, [f. 163rB] Thou didst condemn the unjust enemy; and Thou wast crucified in the midst of transgressors, justifying us!

To the Martyrs: Victorious in wonders, the Passion-bearers of the Lord trampled down the invisible enemy, and cried aloud: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

To the Martyrs: Let us in faith honor the unfading flowers of the noetic Paradise, the precious vessels of Christ, the gathering of the Passion-bearers!

Theotokion: When She beheld Christ upon the Cross Whom She had brought forth, the Pure One marvelled at His ineffable condescension; for which cause together with Him we glorify Thee!

Another [Canon to the Theotokos]. Heirmos: The same.

For my evil deeds and manifold transgressions, who shall be able to entreat the Judge, unless it be Thou, O pure one, the only protectress of sinners?

Raise me up who have fallen into manifold transgressions and enslaved my soul to sins, by Thy powerful prayer, and loose me from slavery, O Most-pure One!

As Thou gavest birth unto the Creator and King of all things, O all-immaculate and pure Mother of God: deliver me from every defiled transgression!

I weep for myself when I consider the multitude of my transgressions and the unquenchable fire, and I pray: Grant me time for repentance, O Most-pure One!

Ode 5. Heirmos:

Rising early we cry aloud unto Thee, O Lord: Save us! For Thou art our God, and beside Thee we know no other!

The rocks split asunder when Thou wast uplifted upon the Wood, O Christ, [f. 163vA] and the foundations of the earth were shaken![^242]

The sun was darkened, O Sun of Righteousness, long-suffering One, when Thou wast uplifted upon the Tree!

To the Martyrs: The choir of the holy Passion-bearers shines with wonders, driving away the gloom of diseases by the Spirit!

To the Martyrs: Swords cleaved your bodies, but ye possessed the spirit of Divine love unsevered, O Martyrs!

Theotokion: Beholding Thee uplifted upon the Cross, O Master, the all-immaculate Virgin Mother cried aloud weeping!

Another [Canon to the Theotokos]. Heirmos: The same.

Unto me who have received the natural wound of sin, heal me with the oil of Thy tender compassion, O Sovereign Lady!

Thou didst stem the flux of corruption of old by Thy Divine birth-giving; and now stem the flood of my transgressions, O all-immaculate one!

Have mercy and take pity upon my soul, O Sovereign Lady, and deliver me from condemnation and eternal torment! Look down and hear my voice, O Sovereign Lady, and pray that I may be delivered from eternal torment!

Ode 6. Heirmos:

The abyss surrounded me, and the whale became a grave for me; but I cried aloud unto Thee, the Lover of mankind, and Thy right hand saved me, O Lord!

The Cross was planted upon the earth, and the demons were cast down; the faith received the foundation of establishment, and malice was driven away from our midst!

The sun was extinguished when Thou wast nailed in the flesh upon the Tree, O Lord; and the lost drachma was found, that had been buried [f. 163vB] by dark passions!

Uplifted upon the Tree, O Lover of mankind, Thou hadst a choir of Martyrs following in Thy footsteps, imitating Thy Passion, who intercede for impassibility!

To the Martyrs: Ye dried up the streams of deception by the outpourings of your blood, and quenched the alien fire of demons with Divine dew, O crowned Martyrs!

Theotokion: A sword pierced Thy heart, O all-immaculate one, when Thou didst behold the Creator crucified, and His Divine side pierced with a spear!

Another [Canon to the Theotokos]. Heirmos: The same.

The abyss of sins hath surrounded me, casting me down into the depth of despair, O pure one; therefore lead me up from nethermost hades who glorify Thee!

Raise me up who lie upon the bed of sins, O Most-pure Sovereign Lady, and grant me salvation worked through repentance!

Cleanse me, O Lover of mankind, by the prayers of Her who purely gave Thee birth, and deliver Thy world from every affliction, and vouchsafe us eternal glory!

Ever promising to turn away from evil deeds, I am ever found a liar, and my heart is hardened; O Most-pure Sovereign Lady, grant me amendment!

Ode 7. Heirmos:

He Who saved the singing Children in the fiery furnace: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

That we might be delivered from sweet-tasting sin, Thou didst taste of gall, O Christ, the Sweetness of Life!

When Thou wast wounded upon the Cross, O Jesus, [f. 164rA] the ancient wounds of Adam were healed!

To the Martyrs: Ye honored God through the dishonor of wheel-tortures, and received the honor on high, O Passion-bearers!

To the Martyrs: Daring with resolute fervor to enter into suffering, the Passion-bearers were revealed as conquerors!

Theotokion: After giving birth, O pure one, Thou remainest even as Thou wast before giving birth; for Thou gavest birth unto God Who is before the ages, that He might make mankind alive!

Another [Canon to the Theotokos]. Heirmos: The same.

Pure Mother of God, despise me not who ever flee unto the shadow of Thy protection!

Drying up the pasture of my passions, grant me to pour forth drops of tears, O Mother of God!

Loose me who am bound with chains of sins, by Thy prayers, O all-immaculate one, who gavest birth unto the all-hymned God!

Unto Thee I flee in faith, and Thee, O pure one, do I invoke: deliver me, O Virgin, from eternal fire!

Ode 8. Heirmos:

Him Who before the ages was begotten of the Father as Son and God, and in the last times became incarnate of the Virgin Mother: ye priests hymn, ye people supremely exalt Him unto all the ages!

O All-good One, Who didst heal the curse of the tree by the Tree, and didst become a fountain of blessing unto men: unto Thee, O Savior, we sing, and Thee we glorify unto all the ages!

Thou didst slay the haughty serpent by Thy Cross, and didst lift up him who had grievously fallen through pride, singing unto Thee, O Savior, and supremely exalting Thee unto all the ages!

[f. 164rB] The destroyers of deception and champions of the Divine faith, the pillars of the Church, truly firm adamants, the warriors of Christ: let us in faith honor the Passion-bearers in songs!

To the Martyrs: The glorious Passion-bearers shone forth like the sun, and by grace drove away the gloom of diseases, and destroyed the darkness of impiety through faith in the Trinity!

Theotokion: Gabriel the bridal escort was sent unto Thee, O Virgin, crying aloud unto Thee: Rejoice, bright chamber of Christ, the King of all, dwelling in which He deified all mankind!

Another [Canon to the Theotokos]. Heirmos: The same.

Being in perplexity of both heart and mind, not fearing the menace of Gehenna, and sinning continually: do Thou, O Virgin, resolve my perplexity, and deliver me from the fire!

I am often dragged down by the pleasures of my flesh and sold as a captive, ever provoking God to anger; O Mother of God, the only hope of the hopeless, do Thou Thyself have mercy on me!

For Thy prayer is unashamed, O all-immaculate one; for whatsoever Thou desirest Thou bestowest, entreating Thy Son and God. Therefore I pray Thee: Have mercy and save my humble soul!

Cruelly tormented by bodily diseases, the uprising of passions, and wounds of soul: make me whole by Thy supplications, O Thou who gavest birth unto the only Benefactor!

Ode 9. Heirmos:

Thee, the Mother of God surpassing understanding and word, who ineffably in time gavest birth unto the Timeless One: we the faithful with one mind magnify in hymns!

[f. 164vA] Thee, the Mother of God surpassing understanding and word, who ineffably in time gavest birth unto the Timeless One: we the faithful with one mind magnify in hymns![^243]

The strength and dominion of the enemy were taken away, O only mighty Lord, when Thou wast lifted up upon the Cross, and wast crimsoned upon it with blood!

They pierced Thy hands and Thy feet, O my Christ, and the lawless who crucified Thee numbered Thy bones, and gave Thee gall with vinegar to drink!

As holy luminaries ye preached Christ Who became man, O all-wise Passion-bearers, and ye inherited glory!

To the Martyrs: The enemies received sorrow, while ye, afflicted with wounds and diverse torments, O all-honorable ones, were revealed as Divine physicians of diseases, O Martyrs!

Theotokion: Christ Jesus, the True Light, shone forth unto us from Thee, O pure one, and by His crucifixion illumined the world, and drove away the darkness of demons!

Another [Canon to the Theotokos]. Heirmos: The same.

Grant me tears of repentance, O Most-pure One, that I may bewail my cruel and unjust deeds before the arrival of the end of my life!

Thou defilest thyself in every way, O my soul, committing unrighteous deeds in thy fornication, and dost not repent! Therefore, before the end, make haste to repent!

Deliver me from evil drownings and afflictions, and grant me mercy, O all-hymned Virgin, and Divine communion of incorruptible life!

We have acquired Thee as our protectress, who ineffably gavest birth unto God, and an invincible wall, and the salvation of our souls, and a fountain of wonders!

At the Aposticha, Stichera of the Cross, Tone 5:

[f. 164vB] No sooner was the Wood of Thy Cross planted, O Christ, than idolatrous deception was driven away, and grace blossomed forth! For no longer is there the tyranny of condemnation, but the victory of salvation unto us; for the Cross is our praise, the Cross our confirmation, the Cross our rejoicing!

Thou wast led for our sake unto the sacrifice, O Christ, as a sheep, and as a harmless Lamb, Emmanuel, unto voluntary slaughter, and wast numbered among the lawless. Come, ye nations, sing with honor, and bow down before the endless Life Who hung upon the Cross!

To the Martyrs: Blessed is the army of the Heavenly King; for even if ye were earthborn, O Passion-bearers, yet ye attained unto angelic dignity: taking no care for the flesh, for the sake of sufferings ye were vouchsafed the honor of the bodiless! By their prayers, O Lord, save our souls!

*Glory... Now and ever... Of the Cross.*

*Podoben: "Rejoice, O container of ascetics" (Ра́дꙋйся по́стничкѡмъ):*

Standing by the Cross, O Jesus, She who gave Thee birth wept and wailed, crying aloud: I cannot bear to see Him nailed upon the Wood Whom I brought forth! How am I now held fast by sorrow and torn in heart, O immaculate one, for now is fulfilled the word which Symeon spake: A sword shall pierce My heart! But now, O My Son, arise, and save those who hymn Thee!

ON FRIDAY, The Beatitudes, Tone 5:

[f. 165rA] The Thief, believing Thee to be God upon the Cross, O Christ, confessed Thee purely from the heart, crying: Remember me, O Lord, in Thy Kingdom!

Put to death upon the Cross, Thou didst make alive Adam who had died through eating, O compassionate Giver of Life, and didst make him again a citizen of Paradise, O Good One!

Thou wast nailed upon the Cross, O Christ, the true Vine, and didst distill the drink of salvation, watering the souls of all the faithful with grace!

To the Martyrs: Being beaten and cleaved limb from limb, O wise ones, ye looked upon the Master's slaughter; therefore, [f. 165rB] O Martyrs of Christ, ye are ever called blessed!

Glory... Triadikon:

We worship Thee in faith in three Persons, one God, indivisible and supreme Divine Nature, crying unto Thee: Glory to Thee, O Trinity, Unity, our God!

Now and ever... Theotokion:

She beat Herself with wailing, O Master, beholding our Life dead willingly upon the Wood of the Cross. Therefore we all ever call Thee blessed with our divine voices!

## FRIDAY EVENING VESPERS (FOR SATURDAY) (TONE 5)

ON FRIDAY EVENING, AT "LORD, I HAVE CRIED":

*Stichera to the Holy Martyrs, Hierarchs, and Venerable Monks, Tone 5.*

*Podoben: "Rejoice, O container of ascetics" (Ра́дꙋйся по́стничкѡмъ):*

The Passion-bearers quenched the flame of cruel impiety with the streams of their blood, and radiant with piety they kindled the light in all the world, O Martyrs! They utterly burned up the falsely-named gods, their wickedness, and their temples, shining forth as lights upon the earth; enlightened by whom, we flee the darkness of godlessness, turn away from idolatrous deception, and worship Christ Who bestows great mercy upon the world!

Ye were warriors of the unbeginning Father, [f. 165vA] the co-beginningless Son, and the Holy Spirit, wisely and piously teaching the faithful the unity of the Godhead in three Persons, and confirming the Orthodox preaching, having easily shattered the words of impious heretics and their snares! Therefore ye are blessed, O all-sacred pastors, for ye shepherded Christ's flock away from ravenous beasts, for whose sake ye endured all diseases and diverse afflictions![^244]

The assembly of the venerable ascetics readily trampled down carnal passions to the end, receiving the rule of the mind through the practice of virtues, whereby they valiantly conquered all demonic wiles and were revealed as companions of the Angels, having lived as bodiless ones; rejoicing in whom now, they dwell radiantly in heavenly mansions and stand before Christ, asking Him to grant great mercy unto our souls!

Other Stichera to the Martyrs. Same Tone:

Clothed with the shield of faith, taking the image of the Cross as their strength, and manly giving themselves up unto torments, Thy saints, O Lord, abolished the devil's deception and pride. Through their supplications, as almighty God, send down peace upon the world, and upon our souls great mercy!

Taking no care for all earthly things, and manly daring to enter into torments, ye missed not the blessed hopes, but became heirs of the heavenly Kingdom, O all-praised Martyrs! Having boldness before God Who loves mankind, ask peace for the world, and for our souls great mercy!

Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion: In the Red Sea:

At the Aposticha, Stichera of the Martyrs, Tone 5:

Pray for us, O holy Martyrs, that we may be delivered from our iniquities; for grace hath been given unto you to pray for us!

With insatiable love of soul, not having denied Christ, O holy Martyrs, and having endured diverse torments of sufferings, ye cast down the pride of the tyrants, and having kept the faith unyielding and unharmed, [f. 165vB] ye passed over into the heavens! Therefore, having obtained boldness before Him, pray ye that He grant unto us great mercy!

*Hymn for the Departed (Поко́инъ):*

I remembered the Prophet crying: I am earth and ashes! And again I looked into the graves and beheld the bare bones, and I said: Who then is this? A king or a beggar? A righteous man or a sinner? But give rest, O Lord, unto Thy servants with the righteous!

Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion:

O Thou full of grace, intercede by Thy prayers, and entreat for our souls a multitude of compassions and the cleansing of our many transgressions, we pray Thee!

## SATURDAY MATINS: ALL SAINTS, MARTYRS, AND THE DEPARTED (TONE 5)

ON SATURDAY AT MATINS.

After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymns of the Martyrs, Tone 5:

Today shines the memory of the Passion-bearers, for it hath a radiance from heaven; the angelic choir keeps festival, and the human race celebrates with them. Therefore they pray unto the Lord that our souls may find mercy!

The wonders of Thy holy Martyrs Thou hast granted unto us as an indestructible wall, O Christ God! By their prayers scatter the counsels of the heathen, and establish the scepters of the Kingdom, as Thou alone art good and the Lover of mankind!

Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion:

Rejoice, impassable gate of the Lord! Rejoice, wall and protection of those who flee unto Thee! Rejoice, storm-free haven, and unwedded one, who in the flesh gavest birth unto Thy Creator and God, unceasingly praying [f. 166rA] for those who hymn and worship Thy birth-giving!

After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns of the Martyrs, Tone 5:

Lord, Thy Passion-bearers, having zealously desired the cup of Thy Passion, forsook the beauty of this life, and were made companions of the Angels. By their supplications, grant peace and great mercy unto our souls!

At the achievements of the holy Martyrs the invisible powers were wondrously amazed; for in mortal body, having contested through the power of the Cross, they well and invisibly conquered the bodiless enemy. And they pray unto the Lord that our souls may find mercy!

*Hymn for the Departed (Поко́инъ):*

Give rest, O our Savior, unto Thy servants with the righteous, and settle them in Thy courts, as it is written: overlooking as God their transgressions, voluntary and involuntary, and all those done in knowledge and ignorance, O Lover of mankind!

Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion:

O Christ God, Who didst shine forth upon the world from the Virgin, and didst make us sons of light for Her sake: have mercy on us!

CANON TO THE HOLY MARTYRS, HIERARCHS, VENERABLE ASCETICS, AND THE DEPARTED.

Composition of Joseph.

Ode 1. Tone 5. Heirmos:

The earth upon which the sun never shone nor saw, the abyss which the expanse of heaven never beheld naked: Israel passed through dryshod, O Lord, and Thou didst lead them up unto the mountain of Thy sanctuary, praising and singing the hymn of victory!

[f. 166rB] Surrendering your bodies unto burning wounds, ye endured intolerable blows, O valiant Passion-bearers, desiring to obtain the honors from above; and He led you into eternal mansions, rejoicing and singing the hymn of victory!

Venerable and Righteous ones, and glorious Hierarchs: having fulfilled the commandments of God, ye shepherded the people and guided them well unto the water of understanding, and ye worthily received the torrent of delight, unceasingly pouring forth rivers of healings by grace!

Direct us, O Lord, unto the life-giving havens, through the prayers of the all-glorious Prophets, the all-wise Hierarchs, and the holy women who suffered with patience and trampled down the enemy with manly mind, who was manifested upon earth by Divine grace!

For the Departed: Thee we entreat, O compassionate God: give rest in the bosom of Abraham unto Thy servants, O Christ, whom Thou hast translated unto Thyself from the turmoil of life, and vouchsafe them eternal light, overlooking their transgressions as Thou art good!

Theotokion: Rejoice! we cry aloud unto Thee, who gavest birth unto Joy, O all-hymned one; enlighten our mind and soul, and guide us all unto the paths of understanding, O pure one; and ask Thy Son and God to grant unto all the cleansing of transgressions, O only Bride of God!

Another Canon for the Departed. Composition of Theophanes.

Ode 1. Tone 5. Heirmos: Unto God the Savior, Who in the sea:

Inflamed with Divine love, the Passion-bearers of Christ [f. 166vA] trampled down the pride of the tyrants, and ask merciful remission and repose for the reposed faithful![^245]

In the holy tabernacles, in Thy courts, O Christ, settle the reposed, O Master, Who didst pay the debt for them with Thine all-precious Blood!

O Wisdom of God, bearing the eternal imprint of the Father: give rest unto those whom Thou hast received, O Compassionate One, bestowing upon them everlasting blessedness!

Light-bearing Tabernacle, golden Ark, containing the Divine Word Who became incarnate for our sake and destroyed the power of death: do Thou entreat Him, O all-immaculate one!

Ode 3. Heirmos:

My heart shaken by the waves of life, O Lord: establish it, guiding me unto a calm haven, as Thou art God!

Spared not when beaten with clubs and cleaved with swords, O all-praised warriors, ye Martyrs were strengthened by the hope of eternal beauty!

Ye brightened the garment of the hierarchic office with forms of virtues, shepherding the flock of Christ upon the pasture of life!

Mortifying the flesh through abstinence, O Venerable ones, ye became partakers of Divine life; through their sacred prayers, O Christ, graciously deliver us!

For the Departed: Grant unto the departed the repose of that other world, O Lover of mankind, forgiving as God the debts they contracted upon the earth!

[f. 166vB] Theotokion: Beholding Thee as purple-clad among women, the assembly of holy women suffered, and was brought unto Thy Son, O Virgin Mother!

Another [Canon for the Departed]. Heirmos: By the power of the Cross:

Establish us, O Christ Savior, by Thy power, and lift up the horn of Thy Church, which orthodoxly praises Thee!

Manfully resisting the fury of the tyrants, the Passion-bearers contested, and pray unto Christ for the reposed!

Receive and give rest in Thy bright habitations, O All-good One, unto the reposed who were nurtured on Christ's laws!

O only merciful God, vouchsafe those whom Thou hast chosen unto the radiance of the saints, overlooking their transgressions!

Theotokion: We hymn Thy birth-giving, O pure one, whereby we have been delivered from the former condemnation and curse, and have been set free from death!

Ode 4. Heirmos:

I heard report of Thee, O Lord, and was afraid; I understood Thy dispensation, and I glorified Thee, O only Lover of mankind!

By Thy power, O Lord, the Passion-bearers trampled down the enemy's strength, and became the fortification and great confirmation of the faithful!

Rejoice with joy, all ye Venerable ones, and let the priests be clothed with righteousness, as was said!

Give rest in the haven of Thy Kingdom, O Master, unto those whom Thou hast translated from this present earthly life!

Sing, all ye people, of the God-speaking Prophets of God, and honor the company of women who well finished the course!

[f. 167rA] The Timeless One was made subject to time from Thee, O Virgin; entreat Him to loose all the temporal sins of my soul!

Another [Canon for the Departed]. Heirmos: I heard report:

Piously confessing Thee to be co-everlasting with the Father, the Martyrs were slain, O Christ, and they cry unto Thee: Deliver the servants whom Thou hast received!

Thou Who alone among the dead art free from death, and Who didst grant eternal life unto the dead: grant repose now unto Thy reposed servants!

Thou Who camest to save the lost, O Christ: vouchsafe those whom Thou hast translated in faith to live, having justified them by grace!

Theotokion: The power of the Highest overshadowed Thee, O Maiden, and the Lord accomplished it, having in the midst the Tree of Life, our Mediatress and Lord!

Ode 5. Heirmos:

My wretched soul burning in the night with the darkness of passions: prevent and pity me, and cause the noetic Sun to shine upon me with daytime rays, so as to illumine light in the night!

The bones of the Martyrs pour forth healing unto the sick, for they are undefiled by wickedness; and they lighten our afflictions, while all the bones of impiety are like dust!

Observing the laws of God, the Hierarchs shepherded the people and guided them generously unto ever-abiding life; and the Venerable ones mortified the tyranny of passions with perfect mind!

Let the Prophets be honored, and with them all the righteous through faith; and let those who lived venerably be praised, [f. 167rB] and the holy women who received torments upon earth as servants of Christ!

Those whom Thou hast taken from the earth, settle in heavenly habitations, O Christ, overlooking the transgressions of Thy faithful servants through Thine exceeding goodness, for Whose sake Thou wast incarnate unto the dead!

Theotokion: We hymn Thee, O Virgin, for whose sake God appeared upon the earth, becoming man, crying: Rejoice, fruitful earth, bringing forth the mystical Ear of Corn that nourishes every breath!

Another [Canon for the Departed]. Heirmos: Rising early:

Accepting the supplications of the Martyrs, O Lord: number the souls of those whom Thou hast translated among Thine elect!

Thou didst promise that those who believe in Thee shall not see death; therefore, O Master, give rest unto the reposed!

Vouchsafe Thy servants to obtain the beauty of Thy house, O Lord, and sweet communion with Thee!

Theotokion: The Word Who is co-everlasting with the Father became incarnate of the Virgin and by His death slew death!

Ode 6. Heirmos:

Even as Thou didst deliver the Prophet from the beast, O Lord, so also lead me up from the depth of unclean passions, I pray Thee, that I may look again toward Thy holy temple!

Surrendering their bodies unto wounds at the hands of the tyrants, the Divine Martyrs rejoiced in soul, considering their end as an entrance unto ever-abiding delight and honorable rewards!

Thou art the glory of Thine all-wise Hierarchs and Venerable ones, O Christ; [f. 167vA] by their prayers take pity upon Thy people whom Thou hast acquired with Thine own Blood, O Word, as Thou art the Lover of mankind![^246]

The Prophets glorified the image of Thee, O Lord, Who wast manifested truly as good; and by Thy power holy women destroyed the enemy's dominion through fasting and suffering!

For the Departed: Number Thy faithful servants who have passed away from us among the choir of Thine elect, O Good One; give them rest, O Lord, overlooking all their transgressions for the sake of Thy tender compassion!

Theotokion: The Lord Who created the heavens in the beginning entered into the womb of the Virgin, working our renewal, and clothed Himself in the form of a servant; Whom we magnify unto all the ages!

Another [Canon for the Departed]. Heirmos: The abyss surrounded me:

The armies of Thy Martyrs, imitating the powers on high, O Christ, pray unto Thee: Grant repose and the delight that is from Thee unto the departed!

In places of refreshment, in holy places of radiance, in pleasant places, O Christ, as the Lover of mankind, settle Thy servants whom Thou hast received!

Cleanse Thy servants, and grant forgiveness of transgressions unto them, O Lover of mankind, and make them worthy of incorruptible life and blessed delight!

Theotokion: What word can declare the wonder of Thy seedless conception, O all-immaculate one? For Thou gavest birth unto God, Who came unto us through tender mercy!

Ode 7. Heirmos:

The prayer of the Children quenching the fire, a dewy furnace, a proclaimer of wonders, not burning up nor consuming the singers of praise:

[f. 167vB] Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

In the flame of glowing torments, O glorious and all-sacred Martyrs, ye showed yourselves as loving God, cooling yourselves with pious thoughts!

Adorned with the wisdom of the Spirit, O all-wise ones, ye lived radiantly, ministering the Gospel of grace; and we praise you as ministers of Christ!

Having mortified the flesh through manifold hardships, ye were vouchsafed future life, O Venerable ones, praying that we who are deadened in diverse manners by the assaults of passions may obtain it!

Let the blessed choir of God's Prophets and the company of women who conquered through fasting and suffering and cast down the enemy be praised in faith!

Theotokion: Praying unto Him Who was from of old together with the Father: may we be delivered from eternal fire and darkness and from the invisible enemies that war against us, through Thy mediation, O Mother of God!

Another [Canon for the Departed]. Heirmos: In the fiery furnace:

Grant unto the reposed to enjoy the unapproachable light, O Savior, through the supplications of Thy Passion-bearers!

Number all those who have died in faith in the Church of the firstborn, O Compassionate One!

Adorned with garments of incorruption, give rest unto Thy reposed servants in Thee, O Savior!

Theotokion: Having seedlessly and most-sacredly conceived Life, O all-immaculate one, Thou didst cut short the assault of death!

[f. 168rA] Ode 8. Heirmos:

The choir of Angels and assembly of men: ye priests hymn the King and Creator of all, ye Levites bless Him, ye people supremely exalt Him unto all the ages!

Having sailed across the deep sea of torments, fed by the Word, O Passion-bearers, ye drowned all the hosts of the deceiver with streams of blood, and ye live unto all the ages!

Having become all-wise sacred celebrants, ye nourished the holy flock entrusted unto you upon the waters of Orthodoxy; therefore the beautiful torrent of delight cheers you unto all the ages!

Ye were revealed as luminaries of the faithful, O Venerable ones, having accomplished works of light; and ye passed over unto Divine radiance: pray unto the Sovereign Lady to deliver us from darkness!

The company of women traversed the stadium full of great wounds; and the choir of Prophets and the Righteous, rejoicing, pleased Christ unto all the ages!

For the Departed: Grant unto Thy reposed servants, O Master, to pass without fear through the flaming turning sword, settling them within Paradise, as Thou alone art merciful!

Theotokion: As the gate leading unto the Divine way, as the easily-ascended Ladder of God, as the unerring guide of those who are being saved: let us hymn the favored Virgin Mary!

Another [Canon for the Departed]. Heirmos:

Him Who before the ages was begotten of the Father as Son and God, and in the last times became incarnate of the Virgin Mother: ye priests hymn, ye people [f. 168rB] supremely exalt Him unto all the ages!

Accepting the contests of the holy Martyrs, for their sake give rest unto Thy servants who have died in faith, who hymn Thee, O Savior, and supremely exalt Thee unto all the ages!

Vouchsafe those who have passed away from us to be illumined with the rays of Thy glory, as Thou art compassionate, who hymn Thee, O Savior, and supremely exalt Thee unto all the ages!

Settle in the habitations of the saints those whom Thou hast translated, and number them in Abraham's bosom with Lazarus, who hymn Thee, O Savior, and supremely exalt Thee unto all the ages!

Theotokion: Adorned with the beauty of purity, O Virgin Mother, Thou becamest the dwelling place of beneficent splendor; therefore we hymn and bless Thee unto all the ages!

Ode 9. Heirmos:

For He that is mighty hath magnified Thee, showing Thee a pure Virgin after birth-giving, as having seedlessly given birth unto the Creator of all; therefore, O Mother of God, we magnify Thee!

The sacredly celebrant Pastors, the choir of holy Prophets, the countless multitude of the Righteous, and the assembly of the Martyrs: we call blessed in sacred songs, as they pray that our souls may be saved!

Wondrous art Thou, O Lord, in Thy saints! Practicing abstinence, O Venerable ones, a virginal assembly, ye amazed us by showing forth many wonders! By their supplications, O Lord, make Thy mercy marvelous unto all!

Together with the hieromartyrs who finished the good course, let the multitude of all-honorable women who suffered and through love lived ascetically be called blessed in faith, [f. 168vA] co-dwelling with angelic choirs! For the Departed:[^247]

Through the prayers of the multitude of all Thy saints, O Word: give rest unto the multitude of those who have passed away from the earth in faith, according to the multitude of Thy mercy, overlooking the sins they committed in this life!

Theotokion: I have been deadened by manifold sin, O all-honorable unwedded one; deliver me from it who flee in faith unto Thy Divine and precious protection!

Another [Canon for the Departed]. Heirmos:

Thee, the Mother of God surpassing understanding and word, who ineffably in time gavest birth unto the Timeless One: we the faithful with one mind magnify in hymns!

Receiving the rewards of the sufferings of the holy Martyrs, grant unto us, O Savior, through their prayers, repose for those who have died in faith!

Thou didst endure death, O only Immortal One; bestow repose and the radiance of immortality upon the dead, as Thou art compassionate!

Thou didst raise us who had fallen into death, and didst teach us to hope for eternal life; grant unto Thy servants to obtain it, O Savior!

Theotokion: The shadows of the Law passed away through Thy birth-giving, and Divine truth and grace were granted, O Mother of God; therefore we magnify Thee!

AT THE PRAISES: Stichera of the Martyrs, Tone 5:

Blessed is the army of the Heavenly King; [f. 168vB] for even if the Passion-bearers were earthborn, yet they attained unto angelic rank: taking no care for their bodies, through their sufferings they were vouchsafed the honor of the bodiless! By their prayers, O Lord, save our souls!

Thy Passion-bearers, O Lord, being made like unto the angelic ranks, endured torments as though bodiless, having a steadfast hope of enjoying the promised blessings! By their prayers, O Christ, have mercy on us!

The holy Martyrs, having contested upon the earth, endured frost, were surrendered unto fire, and the water received them. Their voice cries: We went through fire and through water, and Thou broughtest us out into rest! By their prayers, O God, have mercy on us!

Sleeping together in torments, they cried aloud rejoicing: Slain by wounds, for the sake of the blows inflicted upon our bodies a radiant garment shall blossom forth for us in the heavenly Kingdom; for bonds, crowns of honor; for prison bonds, Paradise; and for condemnation with evildoers, life with the Angels! Therefore, by their prayers, O Lord, save our souls!

*Hymn for the Departed (Поко́инъ):*

Thou didst create me, O Lord, and lay Thy hand upon me; and Thou didst command and say: Unto the earth shalt thou go again! Guide me into the right way, forgiving my transgressions; remit and save me who pray, as Thou art the Lover of mankind!

Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion:

We bless Thee, O Virgin Mother of God, for from Thee hath shone forth Christ the Sun of Righteousness, Who hath great mercy!

[f. 169rA] *AT THE APOSTICHA, Stichera for the Departed, Tone 5.*

*Podoben: "Rejoice, O container of ascetics" (Ра́дꙋйся по́стникѡ):*

*Composition of Theophanes:*

Illumine the reposed with the light of Thy countenance, O Christ, as Thou art compassionate; settle them in a place of pasture, beside the waters of Thy pure and Divine rest, in the longed-for bosom of the Forefather Abraham, where Thy pure light shines and the fountains of grace pour forth, where the choirs of the universe dance, joyfully surrounding the righteous! Number Thy servants together with them, granting them great mercy!

*Verse: Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen and taken to Thyself, O Lord.*

Be Thou pleased, O Compassionate One, that those who have passed away from fleeting things unto Thee, the Benefactor of all and Lover of mankind, may sing with unceasing voices, glorifying Thy dominion: granting them to be enlightened with the beauty of Thy goodness, and to receive and purely enjoy sweet and lovely communion with Thee, where Angels dance around Thy throne and the assemblies of the saints joyfully surround it! Together with them, grant repose and great mercy unto Thy servants!

*Verse: Their souls shall dwell among good things.*

Where the choir of the Prophets, the ranks of the Apostles and the Martyrs, and all who from the beginning of the world have been justified by Thy saving Passion and [f. 169rB] Blood, wherewith Thou didst redeem captive man: there give rest unto those who have reposed in faith, as the Lover of mankind, forgiving their transgressions! For Thou alone didst live upon earth sinless, truly the Savior, and Thou alone art free among the dead. Therefore grant repose and great mercy unto Thy servants!

Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion:

From the law of sin which held us captive, Thou hast set us free, O Sovereign Lady, having conceived in Thy womb the Lawgiver and King, Christ, O only Virgin Mother, through Whom we are justified; for which cause also by grace entreat Him now to inscribe in the Book of Life the souls of those who hymn Thee as the Mother of God, that being saved by Thine intercession, O all-immaculate one, we may obtain the beloved redemption of Thy Son, worshipping Him Who bestows great mercy upon the world!

ON SATURDAY, The Beatitudes, Tone 5:

The Thief, believing Thee to be God upon the Cross, O Christ, confessed Thee purely from the heart: Remember me, O Lord, when Thou comest into Thy Kingdom!

Having slain and destroyed the author of evil, O Martyrs, ye ascended unto the heights, crowned with Divine victories, and ye stand before the King of all!

Enlightened with the light of the priesthood, the Hierarchs were glorified, and the multitudes of the Venerable obtained ever-existing [f. 169vA] life; therefore they are called blessed![^248]

Settle with the choirs of Thine elect in a place of refreshment, O Master, those whom Thou hast translated, O Word, overlooking their sins committed upon earth, O Christ!

Glory... Triadikon:

O Holy Trinity, be Thou entreated by the contests of the Hierarchs and Martyrs, and grant unto those who have died in faith salvation for their souls, and great mercy!

Now and ever... Theotokion:

Having given birth beyond understanding and word unto Him Whom naught can contain, O Thou full of God's grace: entreat Him to be merciful unto us all, O Sovereign Lady!

END OF TONE 5.

# TONE 6: SATURDAY VESPERS, SUNDAY MATINS, AND WEEKDAY OFFICES

[f. 169vB] [Woodcut: The Crucifixion of the Lord upon Golgotha — the Cross with the Title I.N.C.I., the Crown of Thorns, the Spear and the Reed with Sponge, the walls of Jerusalem, and the skull of Adam at the base].

## SATURDAY EVENING: VESPERS (TONE 6)

[f. 170rA] ON SATURDAY AT LITTLE VESPERS:

Resurrectional Stichera, Tone 6:

[f. 170rA] Holding victory over hades, O Christ, Thou didst ascend upon the Cross, that Thou mightest resurrect with Thyself those who sit in darkness and the shadow of death, Thou Who art free among the dead, pouring forth life from Thine own light, O almighty Savior: have mercy on us!

Today Christ trampled down death, even as He said, and arose, and granted joy unto the world! That all of us crying aloud in hymns may say: O Fountain of Life, unapproachable Light, almighty Savior: have mercy on us!

From Thee, O Lord, Who art present throughout all creation, whither shall we sinners flee? In heaven Thou Thyself dwellest; in hades Thou didst trample down death; into the depths of the sea, there is Thy hand, O Master! Fleeing unto Thee, and falling down before Thee, we pray: O Thou Who art risen from the dead, have mercy on us!

Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion:

Come, all ye nations, in a voice of rejoicing let us hymn the Most-holy Virgin and Mother of God, the furnace of human nature, the refuge of ineffable wonders! For through Her new things came to pass: the Unbeginning One hath a beginning; the Word becomes dense; God becomes man, that He may make man divine, not by confusion of natures, but by union of hypostases! For He comes forth, One from two opposites, in each nature being perfect, indivisibly known, willing and acting according to each essence; for which cause we believe without doubt that for the sake of the saving dispensation, O Christ our God:

[f. 170rB] grant unto the world cleansing, peace, and great mercy!

At the Aposticha, Resurrectional Sticheron, Tone 6:

Thy Resurrection, O Christ Savior, the Angels hymn in the heavens; and vouchsafe us on earth with pure heart to sing and glorify Thee!

*Other Stichera to the Most-holy Theotokos.*

*Podoben: "Having laid aside all earthly hope" (Всѐ ѿло́жше):*

*Verse: Virgins shall be brought unto the King after her, her companions shall be brought unto Thee.*

As Thou gavest birth unto the incarnate Word, Who before the ages was co-everlasting with the Father, O undefiled Virgin: loose the bonds of my humble soul!

[f. 170vA] Unto Thee I cry, the help of the world: deliver me from the grip of passions and sinful woes, and pray, O all-immaculate one, save me from the snares of the alien, granting the great gift of Thy mercy![^249]

*Verse: Hear, O daughter, and see, and incline thine ear.*

Save me who am struck with dread in fornications, stripped of good deeds, and alienated from the grace of the Master, O Thou who alone gavest birth unto salvation for the world! Deliver me from perils and assaults who was willingly bound, and who through lack of understanding was cast into the pit of destruction, O Sovereign Lady, as Thou art merciful and profitable unto souls!

*Verse: I will remember thy name in every generation and generation.*

Be Thou my speedy defense, O Mother of God, and attend unto the prayer of Thy suppliant, O pure one! Stretch forth unto me the mighty hand of Thy help, O Mother of God; receive the groaning from my defiled heart, O Most-holy One, and bear it unto Thy Son and our God, O blessed Sovereign Lady, for the sake of Thy great mercy!

[f. 170vB] Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion:

Pure one, who alone gavest birth unto God: deliver me from transgressions of soul, O Virgin, and save me, I pray, who am deadened! For Thou art the hope of the hopeless and the helper of the world; Thou hast the power, O Maiden, as Mother of the Lord! Despise not my supplication, nor forsake me, O all-ruling Sovereign Lady, but as Thou art gracious and loving, save me!

[Tailpiece: Medallion depicting the face of the Savior / Angel within a floral wreath].

[f. 171rA] ON SATURDAY AT GREAT VESPERS:

Resurrectional Stichera, Tone 6.

Composition of John of Damascus.

[f. 171rA] Holding victory over hades, O Christ, Thou didst ascend upon the Cross, that Thou mightest resurrect with Thyself those who sit in darkness and the shadow of death, Thou Who art free among the dead, pouring forth life from Thine own light, O almighty Savior: have mercy on us!

Today Christ trampled down death, even as He said, and arose, and granted joy unto the world! That all of us crying aloud in hymns may say: O Fountain of Life, unapproachable Light, almighty Savior: have mercy on us!

From Thee, O Lord, Who art present throughout all creation, whither shall we sinners flee? In heaven Thou Thyself dwellest; in hades Thou didst trample down death; into the depths of the sea, there is Thy hand, O Master! Fleeing unto Thee, and falling down before Thee, we pray: O Thou Who art risen from the dead, have mercy on us!

Other Stichera: Anatolian. Same Tone:

In Thy Cross, O Christ, do we boast, and Thy Resurrection do we hymn and glorify:

[f. 171rB] for Thou art our God, and beside Thee we know no other!

Glory to Thy power, O Lord, for Thou didst destroy the one that had the dominion of death! Thou didst renew us by Thy Cross, granting us life and incorruption!

Ever blessing the Lord, we hymn His Resurrection; for having endured crucifixion, by death He destroyed death!

Thy burial, O Master, shattered and rent asunder the bonds of hades! And Thy Resurrection from the dead enlightened the world: O Lover of mankind, glory to Thee!

Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion:

Who shall not call Thee blessed, O Most-holy Virgin? Or who shall not hymn Thy most-pure birth-giving? For the Only-begotten Son, Who shone forth timelessly from the Father, the Same came forth from Thee, O pure one, having ineffably become incarnate: being God by nature, and for our sake having become man by nature, not divided into two Persons, but [f. 171vA] natures, known without confusion. Entreat Him, O pure and all-blessed one, that our souls may be saved.

AT THE APOSTICHA, RESURRECTIONAL STICHERA. Tone 6.

Thy Resurrection, O Christ Savior, the Angels hymn in the heavens; and vouchsafe us on earth with pure heart to sing and glorify Thee!

Other Stichera in alphabetical order.

*Verse: The Lord is King, He is robed in majesty.*

Having shattered the brazen gates and smashed the bars of hades as God almighty, Thou didst resurrect the fallen human race! Therefore we also with one accord cry aloud: O Thou Who art risen from the dead, Lord, glory to Thee!

*Verse: For He hath established the world, so that it cannot be moved.*
