Desiring to right us from ancient corruption, O Christ, Thou art nailed to the Cross and laid in a tomb; Whom the Myrrh-bearing women seeking with tears, weeping said: "Woe is us, O Savior of all, how didst Thou accept to dwell in a tomb? And having dwelt therein willingly, how wast Thou stolen away? How wast Thou moved? What place hath concealed Thy life-bearing body? But, O Master, even as Thou didst promise us, appear, and still our weeping lamentation!" And as they wept, an Angel cried aloud unto them: "Cease from weeping, say unto the Apostles that the Lord is risen, granting the world cleansing and great mercy!"

[f. 171vB] *Verse: Holiness becomes Thine house, O Lord, unto length of days.*

Thou wast crucified even as Thou didst will, O Christ, and by Thy burial Thou didst take death captive; on the third day Thou didst rise as God with glory, granting unto the world unending life and great mercy!

Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion:

My Maker and Redeemer, O most pure one, Christ the Lord, having come forth from Thy womb, clothed in me, hath freed Adam from the first curse. Therefore unto Thee, O all-undefiled one, as truly God's Mother and Virgin, we cry unceasingly with the Angel's "Rejoice!": say, Rejoice, O Sovereign Lady, protectress, shelter, and salvation of our souls![^250]

Troparion, Tone 6:

The Angelic Hosts were upon Thy tomb, and the guards became as dead men; and Mary stood at the grave, seeking Thy most pure body. Taking hades captive yet untouched by it, Thou didst meet the Virgin, granting life. O Thou Who art risen from the dead, Lord, glory to Thee!

Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion:

He Who called Thy Mother blessed came unto the Passion by voluntary counsel, shining forth upon the Cross, desiring to seek out Adam, saying unto the Angels: "Rejoice with Me, for the lost drachma is found!" O Thou Who hast wisely ordered all things, Lord, glory to Thee!

ON SUNDAY AT MIDNIGHT OFFICE.

## SUNDAY MIDNIGHT OFFICE (TONE 6)

Canon to the Holy and Life-Originating Trinity. Composition of Metrophanes.

[f. 172rA] Ode 1. Tone 6. Heirmos:

Traversing the deep as on dry land, Israel...

We hymn the three co-originate Persons of single nature, changeless form, God good and Lover of mankind, Who grants unto us cleansing of transgressions.

Supersubstantial One, single and threefold-sunlit in delineations, O Lord, existing in one Godhead: [direct] us in the knowledge and likeness of Thy Divine radiance!

Truly Paul, the light of the Church of the Gentiles, clearly taught us to worship the one three-hypostatic God, from Whom, and through Whom, and unto Whom all things were made.

The noetic Sun arose and shone forth early, O Theotokos, and delivered our eyes from the gloom of sin by His rays; hymning Whom, we piously call Thee blessed.

Ode 3. Heirmos:

There is none holy as Thou, O Lord...

Adorned with threefold light, O God, having established the ranks of immaterial beings to hymn Thee with thrice-holy voices: together with them receive also us who praise Thy goodness!

Singing of the one changeless Trinity, conformable, singly-natured Godhead, we pray Thee, O Lover of mankind: send down upon us forgiveness of our many transgressions!

O Mind, unoriginate Father; O Word of God, consubstantial Image; O Divine Spirit, good and right: preserve in Thy dominion those who hymn Thee, for Thou art tender-hearted! Theotokion:

Having become man in substance, my God, having driven away corruption through Thee, O pure one, alone set free the forebears from the former condemnation.

[f. 172rB] Sessional Hymn, Tone 6.

*Podoben: "Fulfilling the dispensation for our sake" (Е҆́же ѡ҆ на́съ):*

O Master God, look down from heaven, behold our lowliness, O merciful One, and show compassion, O all-good Lover of mankind! For from nowhere else do we hope to receive pardon for the evil things we have committed; therefore be Thou with us, and none can be against us!

Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion:

O all-undefiled Theotokos, look down upon the wound of my affliction and heal it, O most pure one; and cure the burning of my conscience, dew-cooling it with Thy prayer, crying aloud unto Thy servants: "I am with you, and none can be against you!"

Ode 4. Heirmos:

Christ is my power, God and Lord...

Exalt our understanding, O Unity threefold-radiant, and swiftly raise up the souls and hearts of Thy chanters; take away our wickedness, and fashion us unto likeness of Thy brightness, and transform us by the prayers of Thy initiates!

O single, uncircumscribed, and immutable Trinity: [enlighten] Thy suppliants with Thy rays!

In wisdom didst Thou of old join the ranks of ministering Angels of Thy goodness, O three-hypostatic Unity: through them receive also my praise!

He Who is intangible by nature, God communicating with us, having assumed created human nature, was fashioned in Thy womb, O Theotokos, O Virgin!

Ode 5. Heirmos:

By Thy Divine light [f. 172vA] Understanding the Divine-originating nature, providential and saving of all that is, as one radiant light, we rise at dawn, entreating forgiveness of our sinful falls.

O unoriginate God, and co-eternal Son, and Holy Spirit: strengthen Thy chanters, O monarchical Trinity, and deliver them from surrounding perils and afflictions!

Directing me by Thy benefactions alone, and guiding me ever unto pleasing Thy three-hypostatic Godhead, O Sun of Glory, make me a partaker of Thy Divine Kingdom! Theotokion:

O changeless Word of God, Who upholdest and preservest all things by Thine almighty hand: preserve and protect those who glorify Thee, by the prayers of the Mother of God who bare Thee!

Ode 6. Heirmos:

Beholding the sea of life...

Grant wisdom and understanding, O three-hypostatic Godhead, unto those who hymn Thee this day; and vouchsafe us to be illumined together by the rays of beauty of Thy light-giving goodness, who are enlightened by indivisible faith!

O threefold-shining, almighty, unapproachable One: illumine the hearts of those who with faith praise Thy dominion, and raise them up unto Divine love!

God, the Sustainer and Lord of all, dwelt ever in Thee, O pure Virgin: teach Thy children to worship the one Godhead in three Persons!

Sessional Hymn, Tone 6:

With the Holy Spirit: [f. 172vB] look down upon us who repent in faith and glorify Thy dominion, O tender-hearted One; we of clay together with the fiery ones, for we know no other God beside Thee; and cry aloud unto those who sing to Thee: "I am with you, and none can be against you!"

Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion:

Look down upon us, O all-hymned Theotokos, raising up enlightenment for darkened hearts, and illuminate Thy flock, O most pure one! For whatsoever Thou desirest Thou art able to do, as Mother of Thy Creator; and cry aloud unto those who love Thee: "I am with you, and none can be against you!"

Ode 7. Heirmos:

The Angel made the furnace sprinkle dew...

Establish in me a steadfast mind, O Unity threefold-radiant in attributes, to keep and observe Thy Divine commandments, and ever to chant unto Thee with faith: "Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!"

Hymned ineffably in identity of essence, O singly-natured God, yet bearing the number of Trinity in Persons: preserve us all from diverse temptations and adversities!

We glorify Thee, the one God in essence, shining forth unconfusedly in personal properties as Trinity, co-unoriginate and co-reverenced, changelessly revealed in the heavens. Theotokion:

The supersubstantial God accepted our human mixture from Thy pure womb, O all-undefiled Mother, in His love for mankind, and taught all to cry aloud: "Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers!"

[f. 173rA] Ode 8. Heirmos:

From the flame Thou didst pour forth dew for the venerable ones...

Swiftly grant me cleansing of my transgressions, delivering me from the multifaceted arrows [of the enemy], O consubstantial Trinity, three-hypostatic Unity, that I, Thy servant, may warmly glorify Thee!

O merciful God, Source of mercy unto those who worship Thee in truth: have mercy on all, O threefold-radiant Unity, all-good Trinity, as we praise Thy majesty!

With faith we glorify and supremely exalt the one God unto all ages: the Father co-eternal Light, Who bare the co-eternal Light the Word, together with the proceeding Spirit!

Unto mankind, O most pure one, Thou gavest birth to the almighty Word, Christ the Lord, Who heals all the wounds of the forebears; supremely exalting Whom, O Virgin, we hymn Thee!

Ode 9. Heirmos:

It is impossible for men to see God...

The Cherubic ranks, O Master, unable to endure the splendor of Thy glory, covering themselves with their wings, unceasingly cry aloud unto Thee the Thrice-holy hymn, glorifying the single glory of the three-hypostatic Godhead!

O unsetting Sun of creation, grant goodness into the hearts of Thy servants, light in their souls, and deliver me from many transgressions who sing threefold-sunlit hymns unto Thee; [f. 173rB] who hymn Thee, and deliver us from dark villainy, and vouchsafe us Thy radiant dwellings, for Thou art all-good! Theotokion:

Having in wisdom created man in the beginning, Thy Son, O Virgin, renewed him through Thee when corrupted, O all-undefiled one, and filled with the threefold-sunlit ray of Divine light all who in true faith glorify Thee as Theotokos!

## SUNDAY MATINS (TONE 6)

AT MATINS, AFTER THE PSALMS.

"God is the Lord, and hath appeared unto us", in Tone 6. And we chant the Resurrectional Troparion: "The Angelic Hosts", twice.

Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion: "He Who called Thy Mother blessed". Then the usual Kathisma reading of the Psalter.

After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymns.

Resurrectional. Tone 6.

Beholding the tomb opened and hades lamenting, Mary cried aloud unto the Apostles in hiding: "Come forth, O workers of the vineyard, preach the Word of the Resurrection: the Lord is risen, granting the world great mercy!"

Life was laid in the tomb, and a seal was placed upon the stone; as a sleeping King the soldiers guarded Christ: and having smitten His enemies with blindness, the Lord is risen!

Glory... Now and ever...

Theotokion: Entreat Thy Son and our God, Christ [to deliver us from perils and afflictions, O pure one!][^251]

[f. 173vA] Resurrectional [Sessional Hymns]. Tone 6.

O Lord, standing at Thy tomb, Mary Magdalene wept, crying aloud; supposing Thee to be the gardener, she said: "Lord, where hast Thou laid the eternal Life? Where hast Thou hidden Him Who sits upon the Cherubic throne? For those who guarded Him became as dead men from fear! Either give me my Lord, or cry aloud with me: O Thou Who wast among the dead and hast resurrected the dead, Lord, glory to Thee!"

Jonah foretold Thy tomb, and Symeon revealed Thy Divine resurrection, O immortal Lord! For Thou didst descend as dead into the grave, Who didst destroy the gates of hades; and Thou didst rise without corruption as Master unto the salvation of the world, O Christ our God, Who hast enlightened those who sat in darkness!

Glory... Now and ever... Theotokion:

Gideon depicted Thy conception, and David declared Thy birth-giving, O pure Theotokos Virgin! For as dew upon the fleece did the Word descend into Thy [womb]; without seed hast Thou budded forth, O holy earth, salvation unto the world, Christ our God, O full of grace!

Hypakoe, Tone 6:

By Thy life-giving death, having shattered the gates of hades, O Christ, as God Thou didst open ancient Paradise, and rising from the dead, Thou hast delivered our life from corruption!

[f. 173vB] [Unto heaven do I lift up mine eyes,] unto Thee, O Word: show compassion unto me, that I may live unto Thee!

Have mercy upon us who are set at naught, fashioning us into vessels well-pleasing unto Thee, O Word!

By the Holy Spirit is every saving cause: if He blow upon anyone according to worthiness, swiftly He lifts him from earthly things, wings him, leads him, and causes him to prosper on high!

Antiphon 2:

If the Lord had not been with us, not one of us could have withstood the combatant, overcoming the assaults of the enemy; for they who overcome are exalted from hence!

Let not my soul be caught in their teeth as a fledgling, O Word: woe is me, how shall I escape from the enemies, being a lover of sin?

By the Holy Spirit is deification unto all, good will, understanding, peace, and blessing; for He is equal in operation to the Father and to the Word!

Antiphon 3:

They who trust in the Lord are terrible to enemies and marvelous unto all, for they look on high!

Having Thee as Helper, O Savior, the lot of the righteous will not stretch forth its hands unto iniquities!

Through the Holy Spirit is dominion over all: Whom the hosts on high worship, together with every breath below!

Prokeimenon: [O Lord, stir up Thy strength, and] come to save us [LXX Ps. 79:3].

Let every breath... Matins Resurrectional Gospel, Psalm 50, and the rest in order.

[f. 174rA] SUNDAY RESURRECTIONAL CANON:

Ode 1. Tone 6. Heirmos:

Traversing the deep as on dry land, Israel, beholding Pharaoh the pursuer drowned, sang unto God a triumphant song!

With hands outstretched upon the Cross, O good Jesus, Thou didst fulfill the Father's good pleasure in all things; therefore we all sing unto Thee a triumphant song!

In dread as a handmaid commanded, death drew near unto the Master of life; through Whom unending life and the Resurrection are granted unto us!

Having received Thy Creator, as He Himself willed, ineffably incarnate beyond mind from Thy seedless womb, O pure one, Thou wast truly revealed as Sovereign Lady of creatures!

Another Canon: of the Cross and Resurrection.

Heirmos: Beneath the sea surge:

In awe unto Thee the gates of death open, and the eternal bars are rent asunder; by Thy precious descent the ancient dead were resurrected, thankfully chanting Thy Resurrection, O Christ!

Laid in the lowest pit, O Christ, having become dead, Thou didst put to death the slayer, and didst set free the prisoners in hades who glorify Thy precious Resurrection! Theotokion:

Rejoice, O light-bearing tabernacle, sanctification, Church, Table, and holy Mountain! Rejoice, O palace [f. 174rB] of glory, and Throne of our God! Rejoice, O unconquerable wall unto those who hymn Thee!

Another Canon to the Most-holy Theotokos.

Heirmos: Traversing the deep as on dry land:

Partaking of the forbidden food, our forebears brought in the curse; but Thou, O pure one, didst loose it, having given birth unto Christ the Author of blessing!

Having brought forth Christ, the lightning-flash of the Divine abyss, O pure one, disperse the gloom of my passions and the confusion of my transgressions by the light of Thy radiance!

Jacob foresaw with noetic eyes the Expectation of the nations secretly taking flesh in incorruption, God Who delivers us through Thine intercession!

When the rulers from the tribe of Judah had failed, O most pure one, Thy Son and God came forth as Leader, and hath now truly become King unto the ends of the earth!

Ode 3. Heirmos:

There is none holy as Thou, O Lord my God, Who hast exalted the horn of Thy faithful, O Good One, and established us upon the rock of Thy confession!

Beholding God crucified in the flesh, creation dissolved in dread; yet by the almighty hand of Him Who was crucified, it was held firm!

By death is death destroyed, and wretched it lies breathless; for unable to endure the Divine assault of Life, the strong one is slain, and the Resurrection is granted unto all! Theotokion:

The wonder of Thy Divine birth-giving, O pure one, transcends every order of nature[^252] [f. 174vA] wonder: for beyond nature Thou didst conceive God in Thy womb, and having given birth, Thou remainest ever Virgin!

Another Heirmos:

Confessing Thee Who didst rise on the third day and appeared unto the Myrrh-bearing women, O Savior, saying unto them: "Rejoice!", we say: "There is none holy save Thee, O Lord, Lover of mankind!"

Glory to Thy resurrection, O our Savior, for as almighty Thou didst deliver us from secret hades and death; and singing, we say: "There is none holy save Thee, O Lord, Lover of mankind!" Theotokion:

Glorifying Thee divinely, the Word incarnate of the holy Maiden, Who didst save our forefather from deception, we cry: "There is none holy save Thee, O Lord, Lover of mankind!"

Another [Canon of the Theotokos]. Heirmos:

There is none holy as Thou, O Lord:

Having ineffably assumed my corruptible and mortal flesh from Thy womb, O all-pure Mother of God, the Good One divinized it and united it unto Himself!

Unable to gaze upon God taking flesh, O Virgin, the Angelic choirs were struck with dread; and as Mother of God they glorified Thee with unceasing hymns!

The Prophet Daniel saw Thee revealed as the noetic mountain, from which the Stone was cut without hands, mightily shattering the temples of the demons!

What human word and tongue, O Virgin, can worthily praise Thee? For in incorruption, without seed, God the Giver of life was pleased to take flesh [f. 174vB] of Thee, O most pure one!

Ode 4. Heirmos:

"Christ is my power, God and Lord!" the venerable Church divinely cries aloud, keeping feast in the Lord from a pure understanding!

The Tree of true life hath blossomed, O Christ, for the Cross was set up; and watered by the Blood and Water from Thy corruptless side, life hath budded forth for us!

No longer doth the serpent falsely whisper deification unto me; for Christ, the Deifier of human nature, hath now opened unhindered unto me the path of life! Theotokion:

Truly ineffable and incomprehensible unto those on earth and in heaven are the mysteries of Thy divine birth-giving, O Theotokos, Ever-Virgin!

Another [Canon of Cross and Resurrection]. Heirmos:

He Who co-abides divinely with the Father on high is bodily nailed to the Tree for our sake, destroying the curse as Lord, as almighty!

The all-pure flesh of the Redeemer lying in the grave was not separated [from the Godhead]; but as almighty, Christ shattered the bars of hades, and arose in glory on the third day! Theotokion:

Risen from the dead, our Savior cried aloud unto the Myrrh-bearers, "Rejoice!", and called unto them: "Go forth and announce the good tidings unto My Apostles!"

Another [Canon of the Theotokos]. Heirmos: Christ is my power:

We who are saved through Thee hymn Thee, O most pure and all-undefiled one, and chanting piously, cry aloud:

[f. 175rA] "Blessed art Thou, O Ever-Virgin, who didst give birth to God!"

Thou didst give birth unto the unsetting Light, O Virgin, shining in the flesh unto those who sit in the darkness of this life, O all-blessed one, and Thou hast poured forth joy unto those who hymn Thee, O Ever-Virgin!

Grace hath blossomed, the Law hath ceased through Thee, O all-hymned one! For Thou, O pure one, gavest birth to the Lord Who ever grants us remission, O Virgin!

Tasting the poison showed me dead; but do Thou, O most pure one, Who didst bring forth the Tree of Life, revive me, and make me an inheritor of the delight of Paradise!

Ode 5. Heirmos:

With Thy Divine light, O Good One, illumine, I pray Thee, the souls of those who rise early unto Thee with love, to behold Thee, O Word of God, the true God, Who deliverest us from the gloom of sins!

The Cherubim give way before me now, and the flaming sword turns back from me, beholding Thee, O Word of God, the true God, Who didst open the way into Paradise for the Thief!

No longer do I fear the return unto the earth, O Christ; for from the earth Thou didst raise me up when forgotten, by reason of Thy manifold compassion, unto the height of incorruption by Thy Resurrection! Theotokion:

We have acquired Thee as an unconquerable protectress, O true Theotokos, and we praise Thee unashamed, O Lady!

Another [Canon of Cross and Resurrection]. Heirmos:

In compassion, O Good One, having taken our likeness, Thou wast willingly nailed to the Cross [f. 175rB] for my sake, who of old rejected Thy holy commandment for the sake of food; and having been put to death as man, Thou dost grant me life!

Beholding Thee on the throne with the Father, yet among the dead as dead in subterranean places, hades vomited forth those whom the wretched one held of old; and on the third day in power Thou didst resurrect fallen nature, and didst illumine the world, O Christ, for Thou art compassionate! Theotokion:

Without corruption of Thy womb didst Thou bring forth Thy Virgin birth, remaining as before, O Theotokos, unwedded Mother! Therefore pray fervently for Thy flock, that those who hymn Thee may be delivered from temptations!

Another [Canon of the Theotokos]. Heirmos: By Thy Divine light:

A divine radiant dwelling wast Thou prepared for the Master, O all-hymned one! For Thou alone wast revealed as the pure Mother of God, holding Him in Thine arms as an infant!

Bearing noetic beauty, Thy most comely soul was called Bride of God, sealed with virginity, O pure one, and enlightening the world with the light of purity!

Let the congregation of the wicked lament, who confess Thee not as the pure Mother of God! For Thou didst reveal unto us the door of Divine light, dispelling the gloom of our sins!

Ode 6. Heirmos:

Beholding the sea of life[^253] [f. 175vA] swelled by the tempest of temptations: fleeing unto Thy calm haven, I cry unto Thee: Lead up my life from corruption, O greatly merciful One!

When crucified with nails, O Master, Thou didst wipe out the curse that was against us; and pierced in the side with a spear, Thou didst tear up Adam's handwriting, setting the world free!

Adam was brought down, tripped by deceit into the abyss of hades; but as God and merciful by nature, Thou didst descend to seek him, and taking him upon Thy shoulders, Thou didst resurrect him with Thyself! Theotokion:

O most pure Sovereign Lady, who didst bear for mortals the Helmsman and Lord: still the unstable and fierce tumult of my passions, and grant calm unto my heart!

Another [Canon of Cross and Resurrection]. Heirmos:

How didst Thou endure wounds, insults, and mockery, O Word? For willingly as man Thou didst suffer passion in the flesh; yet being God, Thou didst remain impassible! Crucified upon the Tree between two thieves, Thou didst save our nature from corruption, for Thou art almighty!

Willingly wast Thou laid in the tomb for my sake as dead, O Savior; and Thou didst recall all who were held in darkness and the shadow of death! On the third day Thou didst shine forth, and meeting the Myrrh-bearing women, Thou didst cry aloud unto them: "Rejoice indeed, and tell the rest unto My Apostles!" Theotokion:

Thee, O Mother of God full of grace, pure Virgin, who didst receive in Thy womb and give birth in the flesh unto Him Who is before the ages unoriginate of the Father, do we entreat:

[f. 175vB] pray that He send down the multitude of His compassions upon us!

Another [Canon of the Theotokos]. Heirmos: Beholding the sea of life:

Great among the Prophets, Moses prefigured Thee as the Ark, the Table, the Lampstand, and the Jar, symbolically signifying the incarnation of the Most High from Thee, O Mother Virgin!

Death is slain, corruption is abolished, and Adam's condemnation is dissolved by the blessed Fruit that blossomed from Thee; for Thou didst give birth unto Life, delivering from corruption those who hymn Thee!

The Law grew weak and the shadow passed away, when the grace surpassing mind and understanding appeared through Thy birth-giving of God and Savior, O Virgin all-hymned!

KONTAKION, TONE 6:

Having raised up all the dead from the dark valleys with His life-originating hand, Christ God the Giver of life hath granted Resurrection unto the human race; for He is the Savior of all, the Resurrection, and the Life, and God of all!

IKOS:

Thy Cross and Burial, O Giver of life, do we the faithful hymn and worship; for Thou didst bind hades, O Immortal One, as God almighty, and didst raise the dead with Thyself, and didst shatter the gates of death, and didst cast down the dominion of hades as God! Therefore we the earthborn lovingly glorify Thee Who art risen and hast cast down the enemy's dominion [f. 176rA] all-ruinous, and Who didst resurrect all who have believed in Thee, and didst deliver the world from the arrows of the serpent and the deception of the enemy, as God of all!

Ode 7. Heirmos:

The Angel made the furnace sprinkle dew for the holy children, but the command of God consumed the Chaldeans, persuading the tyrant to cry: "Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!"

Lamenting at Thy Passion, the sun clothed itself in gloom, and by day the light was darkened over all the earth, O Master Christ: "Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!"

By Thy descent, O Christ, the nethermost regions were robed in light; and the Forefather, filled with gladness, danced rejoicing, crying: "Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!" Triadicon:

Hymning the unified nature that rules over all, the three-hypostatic Good, and the boundless abyss of light, we the faithful cry aloud: "Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!"

Another [Canon of Cross and Resurrection]. Heirmos: Ineffable wonder:

The lawless and impious children crucified Thee, the Savior, upon the Tree, Who didst shatter the brazen gates and iron bars unto salvation for us who sing: "O God our Redeemer, blessed art Thou!"

Thou didst destroy the dominion of death, and rising, didst grant resurrection unto those who truly glorify Thee as Lord, and cry unto Thee in Orthodox faith: "O God our Redeemer, blessed art Thou!" Theotokion:

One of the Trinity didst Thou bring forth, O all-pure one, [f. 176rB] Who in compassion appeared willingly on earth in our nature: Him unceasingly entreat to save our souls!

Another [Canon of the Theotokos]. Heirmos: The Angel made the furnace sprinkle dew:

The furnace did not consume the three youths, prefiguring Thy birth-giving; for the Divine Fire did not burn Thee, but dwelt in Thee, and enlightened all to cry: "Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!"

The ends of the earth call Thee blessed, O all-pure Mother, even as Thou didst foretell, enlightened by Thy light-bearing radiances, and shining with grace, cry aloud: "Blessed art Thou who barest God in the flesh!"

The all-deceitful serpent struck ruinous wounds into me; but Thy Son, O Mother of God, shattered them, mightily granting me to cry: "Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!"

Thou alone didst become the mercy-seat of nature, O divinely-blessed one! For bearing in Thine arms God Who sits upon the shoulders of the Cherubim, Thou criest: "Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers!"

Ode 8. Heirmos:

From the flame Thou didst pour forth dew for the holy youths, and with water didst burn up the sacrifice of the righteous man; for Thou dost all things, O Christ, whatsoever Thou desirest: Whom we supremely exalt unto all ages!

The Jewish people of old that slew the Prophets have now committed God-slaying, lifting Thee up upon the Cross, O Word of God: Whom as Lord we supremely exalt unto all ages![^254] [f. 176vA] Without leaving the vault of heaven, and descending into hades, Thou didst raise up man lying wholly in the dung-heap, O Christ! Therefore we hymn Thee unto all ages! Triadicon:

We ever preach in Orthodox faith and supremely exalt unto all ages the one uncircumscribed nature of the Trinity, greatly surpassing every word and comprehension of nature!

Another [Canon of Cross and Resurrection]. Heirmos:

Be astonished and afraid, O heaven:

Every hearing was astonished: how the Most High willingly descended to earth to destroy the stronghold of hades by Crucifixion and Burial, and raised all up to sing: "Ye children bless, ye priests hymn, ye people supremely exalt Him unto all ages!"

O Thine ineffable condescension, Christ, and unspeakable goodness! For seeing me rotting in the prison-house of hades, Thou didst suffer passion and deliver me; therefore we hymn Thee, Master of all, and supremely exalt Thee unto all ages!

Rejoice, O gate of God; rejoice, O immaterial portal; rejoice, O rampart of the faithful, Mary; rejoice, O most pure one; rejoice, who alone didst give birth unto God for mortals, unto Whom we cry: "Ye children bless, ye priests hymn, ye people supremely exalt Him unto all ages!"

Another [Canon of the Theotokos]. Heirmos:

From the flame Thou didst pour forth dew:

In a vesture of gold, as a Queen, Thy Son, having illumined Thee with the radiance of the Spirit, placed Thee at His right hand, O most pure one: Whom as Lord we supremely exalt unto all ages!

[f. 176vB] He Who by His will alone established the world assumed flesh from Thy most pure womb, desiring to fashion it anew from above: Whom we supremely exalt unto all ages of ages!

A hidden wonder of the Word unto me, Thou wast made a Divine dwelling, O most pure one, having shone forth beyond virginity in brightness; therefore we the faithful hymn Thee unto all ages!

The golden lampstand prefigured Thee who didst ineffably receive the unapproachable Light, illumining the ends of the earth with Thy radiance; therefore we hymn Thee, O pure one, unto all ages!

Ode 9. Heirmos:

It is impossible for men to see God, upon Whom the ranks of Angels dare not gaze; but through Thee, O most pure one, the Word incarnate was revealed unto us: Whom magnifying, together with the heavenly hosts we magnify Thee!

Untouched by passions didst Thou remain, O Word of God, though in the flesh Thou didst share in passions; yet Thou dost loose man from passions, having become the death of passions, O our Savior, for Thou alone art impassible and almighty!

Having accepted mortal corruption, Thou didst deliver Thy body from corruption, unseen; and Thy life-giving and Divine soul, O Master, was not left in hades; but rising as from sleep, Thou didst raise us up with Thyself! Triadicon:

God the Father and the co-unoriginate Son do all we earthborn glorify with pure lips, reverencing the ineffable and all-glorious power of the all-holy Spirit; for one is the almighty, indivisible Trinity!

[f. 177rA] Another [Canon of Cross and Resurrection]. Heirmos:

Lament Me not, O Mother:

Though Thou didst descend into the grave as dead, O Giver of life, yet Thou didst rend asunder the strength of hades, O Christ, raising up the dead whom it had swallowed up of old; and as God Thou didst grant Resurrection unto all who in faith and love magnify Thee!

Let creation put on white robes, let all earthborn shine forth! For the enemy hades hath been plundered, Christ is risen, and the First-fashioned hath arisen in glory, delivered from corruption, as the Angel cried aloud unto the Myrrh-bearing women!

Creation rejoices with Thy birth-giving, O Virgin! For it hath opened Eden unto our sight, and granting us to enjoy the good fruit of the Tree of Life, fulfill our supplications, O Sovereign Lady!

Another [Canon of the Theotokos]. Heirmos:

It is impossible for men to see God:

The Star shining with rays of Jacob's Godhead arose unto us through Thee from the gloom that held us, Christ God the Word incarnate; enlightened by Whom, together with the heavenly hosts we magnify Thee!

Strengthened by Thy power and grace, I offer Thee a hymn fervently from my heart: do Thou receive it, O pure Virgin, giving in return the grace of Thy many-splendored treasures, O divinely-blessed one!

Thou wast shown forth as the gentle loom, O Mother, upon which the Word wove the garment of the body, divinizing my form, O Virgin, in which having clothed Himself He saved all! [f. 177rB] who magnify Thee from a pure understanding!

Resurrection is now granted unto the dead by Thine ineffable and unspeakable birth-giving, O all-pure Theotokos! For Life having clothed Himself in corruptless flesh arose for all, and faithfully destroyed the decay of death!

AT THE PRAISES: RESURRECTIONAL STICHERA. TONE 6.

Thy Cross, O Lord, is life and Resurrection unto Thy people; and trusting in it, we hymn Thee our risen God: have mercy on us!

Thy burial, O Master, opened Paradise unto the human race; and delivered from corruption, we hymn Thee our risen God: have mercy on us!

Together with the Father and the Spirit let us hymn Christ, Who is risen from the dead, and cry aloud unto Him: "Thou art our Life and Resurrection, have mercy on us!"

On the third day Thou didst rise from the tomb, O Christ, even as it is written, and didst raise our Forefather with Thyself; therefore the human race glorifies Thee and hymns Thy Resurrection!

Other Stichera: Anatolian. Same Tone.

Lord, great and terrible is the mystery of Thy Resurrection; for in such manner didst Thou come forth from the tomb as a bridegroom from his bridal chamber, by death destroying death that Thou mightest set Adam free! Therefore in the heavens the Angels dance, and on earth men glorify Thy tender compassion shown toward us, O Lover of mankind![^255]

[f. 177vA] O lawless Judeans: where are the seals and the pieces of silver that ye gave unto the soldiers? The treasure was not stolen, but He arose as One mighty! But ye yourselves have been put to shame, having rejected Christ the Lord of glory, Who suffered, was buried, and arose from the dead: let us bow down before Him!

*Verse: Arise, O Lord my God, let Thy hand be lifted up; forget not Thy poor unto the end.*

When the tomb was sealed, how were ye robbed, O Judeans? Having set a watch and placed seals, the King came forth through closed doors! Either show Him forth as dead, or bow down before Him as God, singing with us: Glory to Thee, O Lord, to Thy Cross and to Thy Resurrection!

*Verse: I will give thanks unto Thee, O Lord, with my whole heart; I will speak of all Thy marvelous works.*

Weeping, the Myrrh-bearing women reached Thy life-receiving tomb, O Lord; and carrying myrrh, they sought to anoint Thy most pure body. But they found a light-bearing Angel sitting upon the stone, and speaking unto them, and saying: "Why do ye weep for Him Who poured forth life unto the world from His side? Why do ye seek in the tomb as dead Him Who is immortal? Run rather and announce unto His disciples His glorious Resurrection and world-wide joy, through which having illumined us also, O Savior, do Thou grant cleansing and great mercy!"

[f. 177vB] Glory: Gospel Sticheron: Others: Tone 3. Most Blessed art Thou: The Great Doxology: And the Dismissal.

AT THE DIVINE LITURGY.

The Beatitudes. Tone 6.

Remember me, O God my Savior, when Thou comest into Thy Kingdom: and save me, as the only Lover of mankind!

When Adam was deceived by the tree, by the Tree of the Cross Thou didst again save the Thief, who cried aloud: "Remember me, O Lord, when Thou comest into Thy Kingdom!"

Let us draw near unto Christ our God Who was willingly crucified and buried, and let us cry aloud unto Him Who arose on the third day: Thou didst shatter the gates of hades and its bars; and Thou alone didst raise all in hades who cry: "O compassionate Savior, glory to Thy rising!"

Let us all with one accord hymn Christ Who arose from the tomb, even as He said before His Passion, and rescued Adam who had been taken captive!

Having shone forth as a light unto the world, the Apostles drove away all the darkness of delusion by the divine rays of their teachings!

Glory:

We bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, saying: O Holy Trinity, save our souls!

Now and ever: Theotokion.

Rejoice, O gate opened unto God, through which God ineffably dwelt and passed incorruptibly, O ever-Virgin!

## SUNDAY EVENING VESPERS (TONE 6)

[f. 178rA] ON SUNDAY EVENING, AT "LORD, I HAVE CRIED":

*Penitential Stichera, Tone 6.*

*Podoben: "The Angelic Powers" (А҆́гг҃лскїѧ си́лы):*

A Composition of Joseph.

Grant me tears of repentance with a contrite mind, O Savior, that I may wash away the filth of my soul, which I have evilly defiled, committing unrighteousness at every hour; having to intercede for this Her who bore Thee, the angelic choirs, and Thy love for mankind!

Take heed, O my soul, and repent of the many sins which thou hast committed; and pray unto the multitude of heavenly hosts with sighing and tears, that time of repentance may be granted thee, lest like the barren fig-tree thou be cut down into the fire of Gehenna, unrepentant, having done nothing worthy upon earth, nor kept the commandment of Anyone! How shalt thou appear before Thee [Christ] Who sittest upon the throne, to give account and to endure judgment for the evils, wanderings, and harms that each of us hath committed, O my Christ? Therefore I cry unto Thee: By the supplications of Thy ministers, save me, O Good One!

Other Stichera: To the Bodiless Powers.

*Podoben: "Having risen on the third day" (Тридне́вно воскре́слъ є҆сѝ):*

O Angelic hosts, standing before Thy throne, O Christ, they pray for the human race: by their supplications, therefore, granting peace unto all, do Thou tame the power of the heathen!

[f. 178rB] Circling about the throne of the King of all, ever dancing, all the angelic ranks protect us also who call upon you beneath your shelter: deliver us from torments!

Unto the Father, Who is God over all, the powers of immaterial minds, shapeless and bodiless singers of His thrice-holy glory, brought praise; and likewise unto the one Word and the Spirit!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion.

Having conceived in Thy womb with the Archangel's voice the Word Who is co-unoriginate with the Father and the Spirit, O Theotokos, Thou art exalted higher than the Cherubim, the Seraphim, and the Thrones!

At the Aposticha, Stichera:

Penitential. Tone 6.

At Thy dreadful coming, O Christ, let us not hear: "I know you not!" For we have placed our hope in Thee, O Savior, even if through our negligence we kept not Thy commandments; but spare our souls, we pray Thee!

I have acquired neither repentance nor tears; for this cause I pray Thee, O Christ God: before the end turn me back and grant me compunction, that[^256] [f. 178vA] I may be delivered from torment!

Thy Martyrs, O Lord, denied Thee not, neither did they depart from Thy commandments: by their supplications have mercy on us!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

Archangelically let us the faithful hymn the bridal chamber of manna and the truly sealed door: Rejoice, O Sovereign Lady, through whom Christ the Giver of life and God sprang up for us, the Savior of the universe; overthrow the tormentor, our godless enemies, by Thy hand, O most pure one, the hope of Christians!

ON MONDAY, AT MATINS.

After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymns:

Penitential. Tone 6.

I ponder the dreadful day, and I weep over my evil deeds: how shall I answer the immortal King? Or with what boldness shall I, a prodigal, look upon the Judge? O compassionate Father, only-begotten Son, and Holy Spirit, have mercy on me!

In the valley of weeping, and in the place which Thou hast appointed, when Thou sittest, O Merciful One, to execute righteous judgment: magnify not my secret deeds, neither put me to shame before the Angels; but spare me, O God, and have mercy on me!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

Unceasingly with heart and lips let us hymn the most glorious Mother of God, more holy than the holy Angels, confessing Thee to be the Theotokos, as having truly given birth unto God incarnate for us, and praying unceasingly for our souls!

[f. 178vB] After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns:

Penitential. Tone 6.

Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us: for being at a loss for any defense, we sinners offer this petition unto Thee as Master: Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us!

Lord, have mercy on us, for in Thee have we put our trust: be not exceedingly wroth with us, neither remember our iniquities; but look upon us even now as compassionate, and deliver us from our enemies; for Thou art our God, and we are Thy people, all the work of Thy hands, and we call upon Thy name!

Martyrs:

A light unto the righteous ever shines: for the Saints, having been illumined by Thee, ever shine as luminaries, having extinguished the lamps of the unfaithful; by their supplications, O our Savior, Thou dost illumine my lamp, O Lord, and save me!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

Standing in the temple of Thy glory, we deem ourselves to stand in heaven! O Theotokos, heavenly gate, open unto us the door of Thy mercy!

After the 3rd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns:

*Tone 6.*

*Podoben: "Having laid aside all earthly hope" (Всѐ ᲂу҆пова́нїе):*

At the coming of Thy dreadful day I am terrified, O Christ, and I fear the inexorable judgment seat and tremble, having a multitude of transgressions; but before the end turn me back and save me, as merciful God, by the supplications of Thine Angels, O compassionate Savior, only Lover of mankind!

O soul, spending thy whole life in slothfulness, thou dost not bear in mind the dread day of judgment [f. 179rA] Arouse thyself, therefore, and choose repentance! Turn back and cry aloud unto Christ: "O Compassionate One, remember not our many transgressions in the hour of condemnation!"

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

O good Parent of God, protectress of the world, hope, shelter, and refuge of those who place their trust in Thee: intercede fervently with the Bodiless Powers unto the human-loving God Whom Thou didst bear, that our souls may be delivered from all wrath, O only blessed one!

Penitential Canon.

A Composition of Joseph.

Ode 1. Tone 6. Heirmos:

The hard-hearted Pharaoh was swallowed up with his army, but Israel passed through the midst of the sea, crying aloud: "Let us sing unto the Lord our God, for He hath been glorified!"

Having fallen into the hands of cruel thieves, O Christ, and become completely dead through wounds of soul: having had compassion on me with the oil of mercy, heal me, that I may glorify Thee!

Forasmuch as I have sinned greatly, cast down robber-like, O Christ Who wast born in a cave: grant me tears of those who repented and cleanse me, that I may become a marvel unto Thy holy work!

Having youthfully overthrown the enemy, O sufferers, ye are adorned with divinely-woven crowns; and ye stand before God in the highest with the Angels, filled with glory!

Having drowned the spiritual Pharaoh in the depth of their blood of old, [f. 179rB] the all-wise Great Martyrs passed over into the heavenly Promised Land, glorifying Christ!

Theotokion:

With the Martyrs, O pure one, with the divine Prophets, and with all the Saints, pray unto the Creator of all: to save those who in faith glorify and magnify Thee!

Another Canon: To the Bodiless Powers.

A Composition of Theophanes.

*Same Tone.*

*Podoben: "Having walked as on dry land" (Я҆́кѡ посꙋ́хꙋ ходи́въ):*

I praise the choir of the heavenly ones, the fair adornment: and I cry aloud, entreating to be illumined by their bright lightnings: I pray Thee, O Christ, Who alone art tender-hearted!

Adorned by the Word, and by the all-holy Spirit Who proceeded, O Trinity: as almighty, Thou didst establish the angelic choirs to hymn Thee, the Cause of all!

Theotokion:

Having received Thine own Creator as He willed, incarnate from Thy seedless womb beyond understanding, O pure one: Thou wast truly shown forth as Sovereign Lady over creation!

Ode 3. Heirmos:

Confirming my thoughts upon the firm rock of Thy faith, confirm my soul, O Lord; for I have Thee, O Good One, as refuge and confirmation!

I have promised repentance, O Christ, yet I depart not from evils in any wise! What shall become of me, enveloped by the multitude of adversaries? O Son of God, have compassion on me!

I ponder the forbearance of God, and yet I spend my life in slothfulness, wretch that I am; and I fear lest the sudden stroke of death overtake me![^257]

[f. 179vA] Desiring persecutions, sufferings, and perils as delicacies, the Martyrs rejoiced, beholding with spiritual eyes the everlasting enjoyment!

Having most wisely established your thoughts upon the firm rock of piety, O Martyrs, by strength of a most pure soul ye feared not the manifold wounds!

Theotokion:

A new Paradise was revealed unto us, O pure one, having the Tree of Life in its midst; eating of which, O most pure one, man is loosed from the ancient death of Adam!

Another [Canon to the Bodiless Powers]. Heirmos: There is none holy:

The Nature that by His will created every rational nature of the invisible ones, is sung by thrice-holy voices by all angelic orders, and is faithfully glorified!

Thou didst not hide goodness now, as a magnificent One, and pouring forth richly through participation in blessings, Thou didst reveal the bodiless angelic choirs, O Lover of mankind!

Theotokion:

Release from the law unto eternity was given unto us through Thee, O Theotokos, by Him Who was incarnate: Who endured sufferings for our sake and delivered all!

Ode 4. Heirmos:

Thy virtue hath covered the heavens, O Christ, and with Thy praise, O Lord, all things are filled!

Condemn us not, who have sinned much against Thee: but having sanctified us, O Master, have compassion by Thy mercy!

Being Thyself the Way of life, O Savior, vouchsafe me ever to turn away from the death-bearing ways of sin!

Scorched by the blows of burning wounds, ye quench the fire with the dew of the divine Spirit, [f. 179vB] O Martyrs, remaining unburnt!

Martyrs:

Ye are brightly filled with the stream of divine nourishment, O Martyrs, having inherited it by the shedding of your blood!

Theotokion:

In the mystery of the Incarnation, God and Lord, O Most Pure One: I flee unto all Thy protection, have compassion and save me!

Another [Canon]. Heirmos:

Christ is my power, God and Lord:

The heavenly nature, divine minds, receiving not corruption, Thy honorable throne and dwelling: enjoying Thee the Fountain of incorruption, O Lover of mankind!

By the illumination of the Holy Spirit, the angelic assemblies remained unmoved toward evil, being divinized by ascents toward the Primal Good!

Theotokion:

The curse of our first mother was loosed through Thee, O Theotokos; for Thou, O most pure and all-immaculate one, didst bear for us the ever-flowing fountain of blessing!

Ode 5. Heirmos:

O Christ, Who didst cause the light to dawn upon the world: illumine my heart, crying unto Thee early in Thy night, and save me!

O Christ, Who didst shoot forth from the root of Jesse: condemn not the flourishing of my passions, planting in me Thy fear!

Direct me to acquire the sighing of the Publican and to pour forth tears, that terrified I may escape the sighing of condemnation!

Martyrs:

Wounded by divine desire, being slain with joy, Thy Martyrs rejoiced, O Lord!

Martyrs:

To the very end of the body, O Martyrs, ye received custody; and Christ heard the prayer of your glory!

[f. 180rA] Theotokion:

Let us hymn the Theotokos, the heavenly gate: through which all sinners enter unto the ascents of forgiveness!

Another [Canon]. Heirmos: By Thy Divine Light:

Seeing Thee, O all-seeing Prophet, sitting upon the Cherubic throne as Ruler and Lord, they rejoice in the sign of Thy dominion and lordship!

Daniel beheld Thee surrounded, O Master, by tens of thousands and thousands of thousands of Angels; seeing Them united with men, he is mystically instructed in the dominion of Thy glory!

Theotokion:

Thy Son is comely in beauty beyond the sons of men, O heavenly, all-immaculate Sovereign Lady; for He is the Word of God Who is over all, even if He assumed human nature incorruptibly!

Ode 6. Heirmos:

Being swallowed up by the abyss of sins, I cry unto Thee, O Christ, with the Prophet: Lead me up from corruption!

In the gloom of despondency, O Christ: open the eyes of my soul, that I may behold Thy light and be delivered from the darkness of passions!

Make my soul abundant with the life-giving waters of repentance, O Compassionate One: grant me rivers of tears!

The valleys of the Martyrs brought forth the lilies of trials, and they fill the hearts of all the pious with fragrance!

Severed by swords in body, O Martyrs, ye united to Christ man who was crushed by the wounds of passions!

Theotokion:

O Holy Mother of God, my heart that hath been defiled [f. 180rB] by impure deeds: cleanse it by Thy supplications!

Another [Canon]. Heirmos: The Sea of Life:

Beholding with purity of mind Thy Angels descending upon the ladder, Jacob brightly foretold Thine all-divine coming in the flesh!

Understanding the bright host of divine Angels dancing in good order, Thy servant Israel rejoiced, beholding them standing about Thine ineffable glory!

Theotokion:

Exalted above the mountains of heavenly hosts and angelic powers, the Maiden Sovereign Lady was revealed as the mountain of prayer, having divinely contained in Her womb the God of all!

Ode 7. Heirmos:

He Who heard the singing of Thy holy Children and cooled the burning furnace: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers!

I was blinded in mind by vain malice, and I looked not up unto the light of repentance, O Christ my Savior!

Trusting in Thy tender compassion, I fall down before Thee, O Compassionate One: grant me the pardon of my evils, despise me not, O Master!

Martyrs:

Clothed in otherworldly glory through holy tribulations, having suffered in the world: by their prayers, O my Christ, save me!

Martyrs:

Being divine guardians of the righteous law, ye spat upon the statutes of the unrighteous in faith, suffering lawfully, beholding in joy the good [garment] with which ye were clothed![^258] [f. 180vA] Thou didst bear, O Maiden: Whom do Thou pray, O pure one, to deliver me from the slavery of passions!

Another [Canon]. Heirmos: Granting dew:

All ye holy Angels, ye are illumined with all-sustaining beauty, drawing near unto the ineffable glory of Christ, and ever crying in love: "Blessed art Thou, O God, unto the ages!"

The Angels abiding spiritually round about Thee, O Master: Thy incomprehensible majesty do they alone ever receive, singing together and saying: "Blessed art Thou, O God, unto the ages!"

Theotokion:

The Lord is with Thee, O blessed one! Even as the fruit-bearing Angel said, desiring to renew fallen nature: Thy dwelling was blessed, O pure one: blessed is the Fruit of Thy womb!

Ode 8. Heirmos:

Thy venerable Children in the furnace were likened unto the Cherubim, crying aloud the Thrice-Holy hymn: "Bless, hymn, and supremely exalt Him unto the ages!"

In my disposition I have rivaled the unmercifulness of the rich man; and I despise my humbled mind rotting in malice before the doors of repentance. O Christ, cast me not into the unquenchable fire!

Having soothed the wintry cold of sin, O Word, grant me divine conversion, good consciousness of righteousness, lest Thou seize me unprepared unto condemnation!

Martyrs:

Having trampled underfoot delusion by unbeguiled faith, O Martyrs, and having endured every tempest of torments, blessing, hymning, and supremely exalting [f. 180vB] Christ unto the ages!

Martyrs:

Having quenched the burning flame of torments by the dew of endurance, O holy ones, ye burnt up all godlessness, kindled with the zeal of divine love, O right-victorious Martyrs!

Theotokion:

Since Thou art more honorable than the Angels, Thou didst bear the all-holy God, supersubstantially existing, O Virgin Theotokos; therefore cleanse my soul!

Another [Canon]. Heirmos: Filled with the Holy [Spirit]:

Even as of old, O Good One, Thou didst surround Thy servant with bodiless hosts: so also now, O Christ, protect Thy Church which supremely exalts Thee unto all ages!

Intercede for the remission of sins, O divine Archistrategoi, as standing before the dread throne, for those who in love glorify and supremely exalt Christ unto all ages!

As Mother and Virgin, we cry unto Thee: "Rejoice!" with divine Gabriel, O full of grace; for Thou didst bear for us the Word of God in the flesh, Whom we supremely exalt unto all ages!

Ode 9. Heirmos:

She who received the "Rejoice" from the Angel, and bore her own Creator: O Virgin, save those who magnify Thee!

Joseph indeed, having practiced chastity, was known as a dispenser of wheat; but I, having lived prodigally, am held fast by a famine of virtuous deeds!

Like Peter having repented, O Christ, I offer tears; like the Publican I groan; like the Prodigal I cry from the depths: "I have sinned, forgive me!"

[f. 181rA] O gracious Lady, who by Thy birth-giving didst crush the arrogance of demons: raise me up from the dung-heap of passions, and fill me with Thy grace as I cry: "Praise the works of the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!"

Ode 9. Heirmos:

Conception without seed, ineffable birth-giving of a husbandless Mother, incorrupt birth; for the birth-giving of God makes nature new! Therefore in Orthodox faith do all generations magnify Thee as the Mother and Bride of God!

Behold, O Lover of mankind, Thou alone knowest our weakness; for in it Thou didst clothe Thyself for tender mercy's sake, desiring to cleanse it! Therefore cleanse the evil filth and the rotting of my passions, and save me!

As the Prodigal I offer Thee tears, O Lover of mankind; as the Publican groaning I call unto Thee: "Cleanse and save me!" As the Canaanite woman I cry: "Have mercy on me!" and like Peter who repented, vouchsafe me forgiveness!

Martyrs:

Having wrestled in the flesh against the bodiless ruler of this world, by the struggles of your sufferings ye cast him down, and worthily received the crown of victory! Therefore pray fervently, O holy ones, for all who sing of you in faith!

Martyrs:

Thou didst sanctify the earth, O Lord, with the holy blood of Thy Saints, and their joyful spirits Thou didst unite with the ranks of the holy spirits; and Thou shinest upon all with crowns, who in incorruptible faith glorify Thee!

The Archangel of the Angels bringing Thee the greeting, [f. 181rB] O all-pure one: "Rejoice, O Virgin! Rejoice, who didst contain the uncontainable God! Rejoice, loosening of the curse and restoration unto blessing! Rejoice, who alone didst open the gate of Paradise!"

ON TUESDAY, AT MATINS. CANON TO THE FORERUNNER.

Another [Canon]. Heirmos:

Come, ye faithful, let us enjoy the Master's hospitality and the immortal banquet in an elevated place, with uplifted minds, having learned from the Word of the Word Who hath ascended, Whom we magnify!

Restrain my mind, severely wounded by worldly pleasure-seeking, and soothe the storm of demons that disturbs me, and show me the right paths of repentance, O Forerunner of the Lord!

Standing in the midst of the Old and New, O Prophet, thou wast seen causing the Law to cease and revealing the light of Grace; by which guide us to walk swiftly by divine counsel, that we may be delivered from everlasting darkness!

Thou hast been joined with the immaterial hosts, O divinely-wise one: with them pray unto Christ to save us who are on earth, who honor thee in this thy holy temple, O Baptist John, Forerunner of the Lord!

A day of darkness, filled with wrath, awaits those who have works of darkness! O dreadful Baptist of Christ and Forerunner: by thy prayers then deliver from great condemnation those who honor thee!

Theotokion:

Thou wast shown forth as more holy than the Cherubim, O Virgin, as having borne the all-holy God: in these latter days do Thou illumine all of us who sing to Thee in faith with holy voices...[^259]

[f. 181vA] AT THE APOSTICHA, STICHERA

Penitential. Tone 6.

Finding me stripped of virtues, the enemy wounded me with the arrow of sin; but do Thou, as the Physician of souls and bodies, heal the wounds of my soul, O God, and have mercy on me!

Heal the wounds of my heart, grown great within me from many transgressions, O Savior Who art the Physician of souls and bodies; and unto those who ask, grant ever the forgiveness of offenses! Grant me tears of repentance, giving me the release of my debts, O Lord, and have mercy on me!

Lord, if we had not Thy Saints as intercessors, and Thy goodness showing mercy upon us, how should we dare, O Savior, to hymn Thee, Whom the Angels unceasingly glorify? O Knower of hearts, spare our souls!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

Thou hast been accounted worthy of a great gift, O only most pure Virgin Mother of God, for Thou didst bear for us One of the Trinity, Christ the Giver of life, unto the salvation of our souls!

## TUESDAY EVENING VESPERS (FOR WEDNESDAY) (TONE 6)

ON TUESDAY EVENING. AT "LORD, I HAVE CRIED":

*Stichera of the Cross. Tone 6.*

*Podoben: "Having risen on the third day" (Тридне́вно воскре́слъ е҆сѝ):*

Thy longsuffering was crucified, O Lord; Thou didst shake the whole earth, and the faithful Thou didst establish; therefore we hymn Thee and worship Thee [f. 181vB] ON TUESDAY,

The Beatitudes. Tone 6.

Remember me, O God my Savior, when Thou comest into Thy Kingdom, and save me, as Thou alone art the Lover of mankind!

O Thou Who didst receive the weeping of Peter: receive also my repentance, O Christ, and grant me the remission of my transgressions!

O Baptist and Forerunner of the Lord, who didst preach repentance unto men: pray that I, a sorrowful soul, may repent!

Martyrs:

Having endured most painful sufferings, O holy ones, ye deliver those in perils from afflictions; therefore ye are called blessed!

Glory: Triadicon:

O my Savior Who art glorified upon the throne in the Trinity: enlighten me, and by the supplications of the Forerunner, save me without stumbling!

Now and ever: Theotokion:

O strong Protectress of those in tribulations: protect me from the assault of worldly passions, and save me, O Sovereign Lady!

...Thy incomprehensible Cross, O Savior!

In the cheek wast Thou struck, O Savior, and spat upon; and Thou didst strike down the idolatrous enemy of malicious counsel, abolishing the fall that Adam suffered, having been robbed [f. 182rA] by reason of sight!

The sun was darkened, and all the earth was shaken, and the stones split asunder, when they beheld Thee, O Savior, unjustly suspended upon the Tree, releasing us from our desires!

Other Stichera to the Most Holy Theotokos.

Same Tone.

Standing by the Cross of old at the time of the Crucifixion, the Virgin, with the virgin Disciple, wept and cried aloud: "Woe is me! How sufferest Thou, O Christ, Who art Thyself the impassibility of all?"

"Pondering Thy conception without seed and Thy most pure birth-giving, I was exceedingly astonished! How is it that Thou hast willed to die as an evildoer, O Savior?" the all-pure one cried aloud!

Being crucified upon the Tree and nailed as a man, and laid in a tomb as one dead, the pure Virgin Mother hoped that as God, Thou wouldst rise again in glory!

Glory: Now and ever: Cross-Theotokion:

Beholding the people of the most lawless unjustly nailing Thee upon the Tree, the Virgin and Thy pure Mother was wounded in her maternal womb, O Savior, even as Simeon foretold!

At the Aposticha, Stichera

Of the Cross. Tone 6.

Thy Cross, O Lord, is life and protection unto Thy people; and hoping upon it, we hymn Thee our God Who wast crucified: Have mercy on us!

Thy Cross, O Lord, opened Paradise unto the race [f. 182rB] of mankind; and delivered from corruption, we hymn Thee our God Who wast crucified in the flesh: Have mercy on us!

Martyrs:

Having suffered for Thy sake, O Christ, the Martyrs endured many torments, and received perfect crowns in the heavens, that they may pray for our souls!

Glory: Now and ever: Cross-Theotokion:

Beholding our Life hanging upon the Tree, the all-undefiled Theotokos wept with maternal lamentation, crying aloud: "O my Son and my God, save those who hymn Thee with love!"

ON WEDNESDAY, AT MATINS.

After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymns

Of the Cross. Tone 6.

Thy Cross, O Lord, is sanctified, for by it healings are granted unto those suffering in sins; therefore we fall down before Thee: Have mercy on us!

As soon as the Tree of Thy Cross was set up, O Christ, the foundations of death were shaken, O Lord; for the mortal whom hades had swallowed up with greed, it released with trembling! Thou hast shown forth unto us Thy salvation, O Holy One: we glorify Thee, O Son of God, have mercy on us!

Glory: Now and ever: Cross-Theotokion:

O Virgin, the hope, protection, and refuge of Thy people, from whom salvation was born for the uttermost parts of the world: even as thou didst weep by the Cross of thy Son, so now bless and save those who place their trust in thee; entreat Him to deliver from evil all who hymn thee!

After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns

Of the Cross. Tone 6.

Today...[^260]

[f. 182vA] Today the word of the Prophet is fulfilled! For behold, we worship at the place where Thy feet stood, O Lord; and having tasted of the Tree of salvation, we have obtained freedom from sinful passions, by the intercessions of the Theotokos, O Thou Who alone art the Lover of mankind!

O Lord, the Judeans condemned Thee unto death, Who art the Life of all! They who passed through the Red Sea with a rod nailed Thee to the Cross; and they who sucked honey from the rock brought Thee gall! But Thou didst willingly endure, that Thou mightest free us from the bondage of the enemy: O Lord, glory to Thee!

Martyrs:

The valiant struggles at the judgment tribunal, the tormenting wounds upon the Martyrs, and the standing ranks of the Bodiless Powers holding crowns of victory, terrified the most wise tyrants and kings: they cast down Belial by the confession of Christ! O Lord Who didst strengthen them, glory to Thee!

Glory: Now and ever: Cross-Theotokion:

Standing by the Cross, the Mother unwedded, who without seed gave birth unto Him Who came forth from her, cried aloud: "A sword hath pierced my heart, O my Son, unable to endure beholding Thee upon the Tree, before Whom all creation trembles as Maker and God! O longsuffering Lord, glory to Thee!"

After the 3rd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns

*Of the Cross. Tone 6.*

*Podoben: "Having laid aside all earthly hope" (Все оу҆пова́нїе на нб҃сѣхъ):*

Beholding Thee willingly nailed upon the Cross for our sake, O Christ, creation shook with fear! The sun again darkened its light [f. 182vB] the stones were split asunder, and the inner veil of the temple of the Ark was rent, unto the conviction of the cruel and lawless Hebrews!

The tree brought corruption in Eden unto the forefather; but the Tree of the Cross blossomed with life upon the place of a skull! For the malice of the enemy was trampled down, and Adam, finding mercy through the crucifixion of Christ, found Paradise, crying aloud: "O blessed Tree!"

Glory: Now and ever: Cross-Theotokion:

The ever-virgin Maiden who bare Christ, beholding Thee lifted up upon the Cross for our sake, was wounded in soul by the sword of sorrow, and wept, lamenting as a mother: by her prayers have mercy on us, O merciful Lord!

CANON TO THE HONORABLE AND LIFE-CREATING CROSS OF THE LORD.

Composition of Joseph.

Ode 1. Tone 6. Heirmos: When Israel walked on dry land:

Stretching forth Thy palms upon the Cross, O Master, Thou didst embrace the cast-off human race, and didst bring them unto Thy Father, as the beloved and Only-begotten Son!

As a Lamb wast Thou lifted up upon the Cross, O Word, seeking Thy lost sheep; and having found it, Thou didst unite it with the unslain flock, O Jesus: glory to Thy dominion!

Martyrs:

Desiring the life on high, the glorious Passion-bearers and Martyrs put themselves to death on earth, having undergone many torments and manifold tribulations, O praiseworthy ones [f. 183rA] standing at the tribunals of the unrighteous for Christ, Who is righteous over all, ye sufferers endured all unrighteous judgment, O good ones, justified by God!

O Master Who didst procure impassibility for all who are from Adam: Thou didst endure suffering upon the Cross; and beholding Thee, the earth shook, while the Sovereign Lady wept with maternal lamentation, crying aloud!

Another Canon to the Most Holy Theotokos.

Tone 6. Same Heirmos.

Unto Thee, O holy Virgin: the Lord Who stretched out the heavens and founded the earth, having passed through Thee in the flesh, hath shown Thee forth as an earthly heaven unto us!

Entreat Him Who was buffeted by fire and became man for our sake, O pure one, to have compassion upon us on the day of judgment, who have sinned much against Him!

The Sun that shone forth from Thy pure womb with radiant rays illumines the whole earth, O Sovereign Lady; therefore enlightened, we honor Thee as the Mother of God!

Dispel the gloom of my soul and the darkness brought on by improper thoughts, O Theotokos and Sovereign Lady, by the light of the commandments of Him Who was incarnate of Thee!

Ode 3. Heirmos: There is none holy as Thou, O Lord:

The Cross was planted on earth, and delusion fell down; and creation was shaken, and hearts tossed about by the assaults of the enemy received steadfastness through faith!

Having been blinded by deceit, the unrighteous people condemned Thee, the only Righteous One, unto death, Who justifiest [f. 183rB] the earthly, and deliverest them from the unrighteous hands of the deceiver!

Martyrs:

The deceitful one stirred up all his malice, warring against the Saints; but he was conquered, beholding their invincible endurance and the luminaries of divine splendor!

Martyrs:

Bodily beauty was changed by severe wounds, but the beauty of soul of Christ's Passion-bearers shone forth yet more brightly by the operation of the Holy Spirit!

Theotokion:

"I knew Thee to be fair in beauty, O my Son, beyond all men, when I gave birth to Thee; and how is it that being crucified, Thou hast neither form nor beauty, O Christ?" the Virgin said weeping.

Another [Canon]. Same Heirmos.

Holding in Thy hand Christ Who upholds all things: deliver us from the hand of the wicked devil, O pure Birth-giver of God, and from great harm, who honor Thee!

Deliver us from demonic confusion, O Virgin, and from unrighteous men, and from great temptations, and corruptive diseases, by Thy prayers, O all-undefiled Sovereign Lady!

Behold, all generations call Thee blessed, O Maiden, who didst bear the timeless Word in the flesh in time beyond nature, and didst remain ever Virgin!

As having borne God the Lover of mankind, O Virgin: deliver me, Thy unprofitable servant, from great condemnation in the hour of His dread coming!

*Ode 4. Heirmos: Christ is my power, God and Lord!" the...*

Beholding Thee stretched upon the Tree, the sun was darkened with fear, and the darkness of delusion was dispersed, and all the earth[^261] [f. 183vA] and the enemy was made a laughingstock, and delusion was destroyed!

Thy cross-bearers, the transgressors of the law, and the prisoners who could not be loosed, O Savior: all their bonds were unbound! O unwaning Sun, Christ, all creation hymns Thee!

Martyrs:

By the streams of your blood, ye choked him who boasts immeasurably in hurting minds; and dragging him to the earth, ye passed over rejoicing!

Martyrs:

Having flown over the snares of the enemy on spiritual wings, O sufferers, ye flew up rejoicing to where the first grace is, and life, and unwaning light!

Theotokion:

The gracious Lady was wounded in heart by a sword, when she beheld Him Who was incarnate of her being crucified, and His all-pure side pierced for our sake with a spear!

Another [Canon]. Same Heirmos.

As the temple of God, let all the faithful hymn the holy Virgin brightly, having been deified for her sake and delivered from evils!

As the gate leading unto divine entrance, as divine Paradise, as the spiritual place of sanctification, as the beauty of Jacob, we bless the Virgin!

Christ hath shown Thee forth as the most undefiled and full of grace, O all-undefiled and gracious Lady, unto those who with faith and love call upon Thee from a pure mind as the true Mother of God!

O pure Mary, who didst become the cleansing vessel and spacious dwelling of the Divine indwelling: consume the defilement and filth of my soul!

Ode 5. Heirmos:

[f. 183vB] With Thy divine light, O Good One:

O Christ Who clothest the heaven with clouds: being willingly nailed to the Cross for our sake, Thou didst strip off from me the nakedness of malice, and didst clothe me with the robe of incorruption, O Christ, Who art truly the sweetness of our souls!

Having wisely uprooted all the drunkenness of delusion, the Passion-bearers and Martyrs consumed the bitterness of the tormentor!

Martyrs:

Adorned with sacred wounds, Christ's sufferers, adorned with crowns, stand before God Who suffered in the flesh, asking remission for our transgressions!

Martyrs:

Looking unto the glory there, and unto life and true rejoicing, O Passion-bearers, ye endured a great overturning of cruel torments, being strengthened by the Passion of the Blessed One!

Theotokion:

"Having contained Thee within my womb, O Christ, Who alone art uncontainable by all, I bare Thee without pain; but now I suffer pain seeing Thee crucified!" the pure Virgin said weeping.

Another [Canon]. Same Heirmos.

O Thou Who by the Word didst create all things and dost govern them by wise providence, the only Lord as Thou willest: by the tender compassion of the Creator, Thou didst become flesh ineffably of the all-pure one!

Behold, the Virgin prophetically conceived in her womb God Who is over all, the Master and Lord, and ineffably bare Him, O pure one, remaining incorruptly Virgin after birth-giving!

O Mary, Sovereign Lady of all, deliver me, as [f. 184rA] thou art merciful, from the dreadful flame, I pray; and tear up the handwriting of my sin, by the spear of Him Who was incarnate of thee!

By thy intercession and protection, O Virgin, burst the bonds of my sin; for unto the purified art thou the hope, and unto those who flee with faith unto thy divine shelter!

*Ode 6. Heirmos: Being swallowed up by the abyss of sins...*

Having cut down the thorns of passions by Thine enduring longsuffering, Thou wast pierced in the side with a spear: and Thou didst slay the deceitful serpent that had made us dead!

Lifted up upon the Cross, Thou didst overthrow the enemy's power, O Master; and destroying him who held me in bitter bondage, Thou didst endure slaughter: I bow down before all Thy longsuffering, O compassionate One!

Sheltered by the Cross, the sufferers broke down the wicked walls of delusion, and were translated unto the city on high, adorned with crowns of victory; therefore they are called blessed!

Martyrs:

Having raised yourselves up unto the height of glorious martyrdom, O glorious ones, ye cast down the wicked machinations of the enemy to the earth, and receiving crowns, ye came forward!

Theotokion:

"O Brightness of the Father: how art Thou lifted up upon the Cross, enlightening all creation and casting down the prince of darkness?" the all-pure and gracious Lady said, weeping with maternal lamentation!

Another [Canon]. Same Heirmos.

Leaving Thine inmost womb unconsumed, Jesus Who is fire came forth from Thee [f. 184rB] entreat Him, O pure one, that those who hymn Thee in faith may be delivered from fire and from every torment!

I hymn Thee, the splendor of the Holy Angels, O all-undefiled one; and I pray: consume away from me the unfitting demonic fantasies, preserving my heart in peace!

He Who is united, the Only-begotten of the Father, passed without seed through Thy virgin womb, and preserved Thine honorable virginity uninjured, O all-undefiled one!

Cleanse the multitude of my sins by the multitude of Thy mercy, and save Thy servant, O gracious Lady, who flees unto Thee and faithfully prays unto Thy mercy!

*Ode 7. Heirmos: The Angel made the furnace sprinkle dew for...*

Having been suffocated and suspended upon the Tree, O Only-begotten One, Thou didst choke the venomous malice of the serpent, and didst enlighten all to cry aloud: "Blessed art Thou, O God of our Fathers!"

Having tasted of the tree, Adam the first-formed man found death; but Christ, dying upon the Tree of the Cross, grants immortal life, having slain the multifaceted enemy!

Martyrs:

Enduring suffering, O Martyrs, ye rejoiced in the torments of the Lord; and ye stood upon the firm rock of faith, casting down every wicked malice of the enemy by divine assent!

Martyrs:

Enlightened by sufferings, ye outshone the sun with brightness, and all the dark dominions, O sufferers[^262] [f. 184vA] ye destroyed, O sufferers, singing unto Christ: "Blessed art Thou, O God of our Fathers!"

Theotokion:

"Being unchanging in nature, Thou didst change all creation when suspended upon the Tree, O my Son!" said the Virgin, beholding Thee with lamentation, marveling at Thy great longsuffering!

Another [Canon]. Same Heirmos.

He Who sits uncircumscribed in the bosom of the Father, now sits circumscribed in Thy bosom, O all-pure one, clothed in Thy form, that He might save Adam from the filth of sin!

Pray unceasingly unto God the Lover of mankind, O all-undefiled one, that we may receive eternal forgiveness of our evils, and obtain the good things prepared in the heavens for those who love Him!

We bless Thee, O all-undefiled one, who didst bear the blessed Lord Who crowns human nature with divine blessings, making it new that was waxed old of old!

Having been enriched with Thee as a haven of salvation, O pure one, we are saved from tempest; and possessing the hope that is in Thee as a firm anchor of the soul, we cry: "Blessed art thou who barest God in the flesh!"

*Ode 8. Heirmos: From the flame Thou didst pour forth dew...*

By humility of heart, O transcendent God, Thou didst humble the proud serpent when lifted up upon the Tree; and Adam who was humbled by passions, Thou didst exalt, O compassionate One!

Transforming the bitterness of the tree, Thou wast lifted up upon the Tree, tasting gall [f. 184vB] O Master Who art Thyself sweetness, composite life, light, and salvation unto those who exist!

Martyrs:

Ye bowed not your knees unto carved idols, O all-praiseworthy ones; but ye were sacrificed as unblemished lambs, and ye destroyed the power of the wicked one, hymning Christ unto all ages!

Martyrs:

Ye were shown forth as living temples of the Spirit, O Martyrs, and ye cast down the temples of idols, and were taken up unto the heavenly temple, hymning Christ unto all ages!

Theotokion:

Foreseeing Thee as such a Ladder, O Virgin, leading us up unto the heavenly height who had fallen into the abyss of evils, we bless Thee, O pure one, unto all ages!

Another [Canon]. Same Heirmos.

Truly we confess Thee as the Theotokos, crying faithfully unto Thee the Angel's "Rejoice!"; for Thou alone, O joyful and blessed pure Lady, didst give birth to joy for those on earth!

Thy pure palace capable of holding God, the most holy Ark, prefigured Thee who bearest God in the flesh, O all-undefiled one: supremely exalt the Lord unto all ages!

O unwedded Maiden, joyful in God, haven and hope of Christians in faith: deliver Thy servants from perils, passions, afflictions, and eternal fire!

When Thou comest in the clouds to judge all things, O Master, number me, a sinner, among the sheep on Thy right hand, by the entreaties of Thy Mother, that I may glorify Thee unto ages of ages!

[f. 185rA] *Ode 9. Heirmos: It is impossible for men to see God...*

The Lord of times and seasons was lifted up upon the Tree in the midst of the earth at midday, being crucified, O Thou Who alone art longsuffering, setting right the slip of the forefather who tasted the corrupting fruit!

The Cross was planted, and the tormentor received deadly anguish in his soul; and those who were corrupted were released from destruction; and at once men were caught up, the enemy was brought to naught, and all things were filled with joy!

Martyrs:

The earth was sanctified by the Martyrs of the Lord, with whom Christ, having been sacrificed and crucified, drew your multitude, who endured a multitude of severe torments and became partakers of divine glory!

Martyrs:

Shining with immaterial light, ye became gods by adoption, O Martyrs of the Lord, taking up your abode with the firstborn of the universe, and filled with eternal glory; therefore the faithful duly honor you!

Theotokion:

"A terrible birth-giving did I endure, O Master, when I strangely bare Thee, O longsuffering One; and beholding Thee nailed upon the Tree of the Cross, I was filled with dread!" the undefiled Mother wept, crying aloud as a mother, whom we magnify!

Another [Canon]. Same Heirmos.

The Word and Son of God without beginning, having become incarnate, became the Son of the Virgin by the good pleasure of the Father and the operation of the Holy Spirit, renewing all my corrupted form, as He is almighty!

[f. 185rB] Arise, O my soul, and watch unto prayer and unto all good deeds, casting off the slumber of sloth through diligence; for thou hast the pure Mother of God as an ever-watchful protectress, whom we magnify!

Thou art the hope, shelter, and rejoicing of the faithful, O all-undefiled Theotokos! Therefore, according to Thy tender mercies, enlighten my soul, which the darkness of many sins and evil thoughts hath darkened!

O holy Virgin joyful in God: open unto me the gates of light, lest the night of sin cover me; and direct my life unto the calm haven of the divine commandments of Him Who was made man from Thee!

At the Aposticha, Stichera

Of the Cross. Tone 6.

In the Cross do I have hope, O Christ, and in it do I boast, crying aloud: "O Lord, Lover of mankind, cast down the pride of those who confess Thee not as God and man!"

Sheltered by the Cross, we set ourselves against the enemy, fearing neither his craft nor his barking; for the proud one hath been abolished and trampled down by the power of Christ Who was crucified upon the Tree!

Martyrs:

The memory of the Martyrs works joy, O Lord; for having suffered for Christ, they received crowns from Him, and now with boldness they pray for our souls!

Glory: Now and ever: Cross-Theotokion:

*Podoben: "Having laid aside all earthly hope" (Всю̀ ѿложи́вше):*

When the spotless Ewe-lamb beheld Her Lamb upon the Tree of the Cross, with maternal[^263] [f. 185vA] lamentation she cried aloud, and marveling said: "O sweetest Child, what is this new and glorious sight? How hath the ungrateful assembly delivered Thee unto the tribunal of Pilate, and condemned Thee unto death, Who art the Life of all? Yet I hymn Thy ineffable condescension, O Word!"

ON WEDNESDAY, The Beatitudes.

Tone 6.

Remember me, O God my Savior, when Thou comest into Thy Kingdom, and save me, as Thou alone art the Lover of mankind!

Having willingly been lifted up upon the Tree, Thou didst show forth those who had fallen into the abyss of evil to be once again citizens of Paradise!

[f. 185vB] The earth was shaken, and the sun was extinguished, beholding Thee, the Sun of righteousness, willingly suffering upon the Tree!

Having shared in the sufferings of the Savior, O Passion-bearers, ye share in divine splendor, being deified by participation!

Glory: Triadicon:

Raise me up from the depth of sins, O my Christ, Who art One of the Trinity, having willingly endured crucifixion!

Now and ever: Theotokion:

Standing by the Cross, the Virgin Mother, beholding Her Son willingly suffering, magnified Him!

## WEDNESDAY EVENING VESPERS (FOR THURSDAY) (TONE 6)

ON WEDNESDAY EVENING, AT "LORD, I HAVE CRIED":

*Stichera to the Holy Apostles. Tone 6.*

*Podoben: "Having risen on the third day" (Тридне́вно воскре́слъ е҆сѝ):*

Ye became servants of the great divine mysteries, O Theologians and eye-witness Disciples; and ye received the grace of healings, and heal the diseases of all men!

Ye are the great refuge and shelter of our souls, and the expulsion of evil spirits, O eyewitnesses of God, Apostles of the Lord: therefore we ever honor you!

From great tribulation, and demonic harm, and transgressions, and evil captivity: deliver those who praise you in faith, O blessed divine Apostles!

[f. 186rA] Other Stichera to Saint Nicholas.

*Podoben: "The same Tone and Podoben" (Гла́съ и҆ подо́бенъ то́йже):*

O blessed Nicholas, have compassion on me who fall down before thee, I pray thee; and enlighten the eyes of my soul, that I may purely behold the bountiful Giver of light!
