Deliver me from the enemies that seek to harm me, O father, having boldness before God, O blessed hierarch Nicholas, and save me from bloody torments!

Having acquired thee as a stormless harbor and an unassailable wall, O hierarch, the faithful have a tower of strength, a door of repentance, and a guide [f. 186rB] of our souls, and a bulwark!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

Envying Thy flock, O all-pure one, the malicious adversary ever reproachfully schemes to make a mockery for himself; but do Thou, O Theotokos, deliver us from his harm!

At the Aposticha, Stichera

To the Holy Apostles. Tone 6.

Lord, the Apostles attained: once indeed, with nets, the depth of the sea; and at another time, the height of the Kingdom through their teachings! Once by art they searched out the incomprehensible depth; and at another time, through faith they reached Thine uncircumscribed bosom, and preached Thy timeless Son unto the world: by their prayers have mercy on us!

When of old Thy Disciples were tossed about in the ship, O Christ, they cried aloud: "Teacher, save us, we perish!" And now we also cry: "O Savior, Lover of mankind, deliver us from our perils, we pray Thee!"

Martyrs:

Thy Cross, O Lord, became an invincible weapon unto the Martyrs; for they beheld death lying before them, and foresaw the future life: and they were strengthened by their hope in Thee: by their prayers have mercy on us!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

Sighing from my heart unto Thee, O gracious Lady: despise not my small sighing in the hour when Thy Son judges the world; be Thou my shelter and helper!

ON THURSDAY, AT MATINS.

After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymns

Of the Apostles. Tone 6.

As Thou didst come into the midst of Thy Disciples, O Savior, giving them peace: come Thou unto us and save us! The choir of Thy Disciples enlightened the universe; for they who were once catchers of fish became fishers of men: for their sake, O God, have mercy on us!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

The multitude of my transgressions is very great, O Theotokos! Unto Thee have I fled, O most pure one, needing salvation: visit my suffering soul, and pray unto Thy Son and our God to grant me forgiveness of the evil things I have done, O only blessed one!

After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns

Of the Apostles. Tone 6.

Thy Disciples, O Savior, being sent forth unto the ends of the earth, piously caught the nations like fish, and brought them graciously unto God; therefore we cry unto Thee, O Christ: Grant Thy people great mercy!

O Lord, the memory of Thy Saints hath appeared today like the Paradise of Eden, for in it all creation rejoices: and by their prayers grant us peace and great mercy!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

O all-holy Theotokos, forsake me not in the time of my life, and entrust me not unto human protection; but do Thou Thyself protect me and save me!

After the 3rd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns

*Of the Apostles. Tone 6.*

*Podoben: "Having laid aside all earthly hope" (Все оу҆пова́нїе на нб҃сѣхъ):*

Into all the earth, like lightning from Thy most wise Disciples, O Master Christ, their saving sound went forth, and enlightened[^264] [f. 186vA] those who were in darkness and distress, making us sons of the day and of light: therefore all creation piously glorifies Thee!

With the net of divine faith, the fishermen turned their boats and drew all men from the depth of heresy, and delivered them unto God, acting piously and ever magnifying Him!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

O holy Sovereign Lady, Mother of Christ our God, who didst incomprehensibly bear the Creator of all: pray ever with the sacred Apostles unto His goodness, to deliver us from passions and grant us forgiveness of sins!

CANON TO THE HOLY APOSTLES.

Composition of Theophanes.

Ode 1. Tone 6. Heirmos: When Israel walked on dry land:

Having become light unto the world, O divine speakers, enlighten us with radiant flashings, and deliver us from the night of passions and the darkness of temptations, O divinely-blessed ones!

The Spirit appointed you as princes over all the earth, O honorable Disciples of the Lord; therefore having conquered the prince of the air, ye deliver the faithful!

As radiant coals kindled from the immaterial Fire, O most wise ones, burn up the material passions that trouble me, guiding me unto the light of impassibility and life!

Theotokion:

By the prayers of Thine Apostles, Prophets, and Martyrs, and of the pure Maiden who bare Thee, O Lord Jesus, Lover of all mankind: have compassion upon the people who have sinned against Thee!

Another Canon to Saint Nicholas.

Composition of Joseph.

[f. 186vB] Ode 1. Tone 6. Heirmos: Pharaoh who was cut off:

O most wise father who dwellest joyfully in the heavens: by thy great intercession save those who sing unto thee on earth in concord through faith!

Against harmful passions, against corruptive enemies, and against every deceit and evil malice, strengthen us, O father Nicholas, who flee with faith unto thy holy shelter!

Unto us who are wounded by invisible archers, apply the medicine of thy prayers, O Nicholas, that in health we may walk in the ways of the Lord!

Theotokion:

He Who is co-eternal with the Father, having in these latter days taken flesh as the Son, dwelt within Thy womb for our renewal, O Theotokos of the faithful: therefore we hymn Thee!

Ode 3. Heirmos: There is none holy as Thou, O Lord:

The Divine Spirit, by His dreadful coming like cloven tongues, renewed through you, O glorious Apostles, mankind that had been crushed unto death!

I have sinned in judgment, O Word: what forgiveness shall I receive on the day of judgment? Therefore I cry unto Thee: for the sake of Thy Disciples, have compassion on me who am self-condemned!

Having imitated the saving passions of Christ, O glorious Apostles: heal the passions of my soul that have held me fast for a long time and are grievous, as ye are physicians!

Theotokion:

Turn me back, O Christ, who have sinned, for the sake of the Theotokos and Thine Apostles, O God, and have mercy on me, and free me from eternal fire, O Savior!

[f. 187rA] Another [Canon]. Heirmos:

Upon the firm rock of Thy faith, having strengthened the thoughts of my soul, establish me, O Lord: for Thee do I have, O Good One, as refuge and confirmation!

Having victory over soul-destroying passions, thou didst receive it, O all-blessed Nicholas: from these passions, by which we are ever evilly conquered, deliver us by thy prayers!

Thou didst put bodily members to death through abstinence, and wast translated unto life that waxes not old, which grant also unto us to obtain, O most wise one, who joyfully praise thee!

Cease not, O hierarch, to visit us from the heavenly shelters, driving away all worldly distress by thy prayers unto God!

Theotokion:

Entreat the Redeemer to grant us forgiveness of offenses, O pure one, ever driving away darkness from our souls by thy prayers!

*Ode 4. Heirmos: Christ is my power, God and Lord!" the...*

O stormless havens: lead me unto the calm haven, who am tossed about by the tempest of grievous transgressions!

Sigh, O my soul, and shed tears; unite thy humble heart unto the good Father, that He may deliver thee from the coming flame and torment!

As saviors of men, entreat the Teacher and Lord, O all-blessed Apostles, that He may save us from evil temptations, as He is the Lover of mankind!

Theotokion:

O most pure Virgin, undefiled Maiden [f. 187rB] with the Apostles make supplication for us, that we may be delivered from grievous temptations and perils!

Another [Canon]. Heirmos: I heard, O Lord, Thy report:

Heal my heart, O Savior, that was wounded by the deceiver and is uncorrected: entreat the Giver of grace, O Nicholas!

Thou didst crush the shrines of destruction, O servant of Christ; therefore with faith I pray thee: consume the evil idols of my mind!

Thou wast filled with the breath of fire by righteous deeds, O divinely-wise one, and in Myra thou didst adorn the holy throne, O holy hierarch Nicholas!

Theotokion:

O unwedded Sovereign Lady, blessed Birth-giver of God: save those who hymn Thee from great harm, O only helper of men!

*Ode 5. Heirmos: With Thy Divine light, O Good One, illumine...*

Walking in the path leading unto life through the narrow journey of perils and afflictions, O Disciples of the Word, smooth the paths of my life!

O luminaries of the divine East: deliver me from the darkness of passions and the gloom of pleasures, and from perils and troubles, and the storm of temptations, O Apostles of Christ!

O God-beholding scrolls of the Word: pray, O Apostles, that I may be written in the Book of Life, tearing up the cruel record of my sins by your prayers!

Theotokion:

O my salvation and hope: save me who hope in Thee, the unashamed hope of all toward God[^265] [f. 187vA] by whose prayers and those of the divine Disciples, save me, O all-undefiled Maiden!

Another [Canon]. Heirmos: O Thou Who didst make light shine forth on all the world:

Make me diligent who am held fast by the slumber of sloth, by thy sacred intercessions, O Nicholas!

Entreat Jesus the Savior, O holy hierarch Nicholas, to deliver me from eternal torment; preserve me from worldly scandals and demonic malice, by thy prayers, O holy hierarch Nicholas!

Theotokion:

He Who grants existence unto us dwelt within Thy womb, O Theotokos: entreat Him to save us!

*Ode 6. Heirmos: Being swallowed up by the abyss of sins...*

As tables written by God, ye truly have the honorable ordinances of the Spirit in your souls, O glorious ones, through which ye abolished the law in writings, having saved the world!

O my soul, that sinnest and servest evil custom unto the hurt of the mind: turn back in repentance, and cry unto the compassionate Lord: "For the sake of the Apostles, O Word, save me!"

Number me among the sheep on Thy right hand at Thy dread and terrible coming, and deliver me from the fire, by the prayers of Thy divine preachers, O gentle Lamb Who wast slain!

Theotokion:

The choir of Bodiless ministers entreats Thee, O Son of God without beginning, and the assembly of the Apostles with her who bare Thee offers supplication unto Thee: Grant Thy people [f. 187vB] Thy mercies!

Another [Canon]. Heirmos: Swallowed up by the whale of sins, I cry unto Thee, O Christ: As the Prophet, free me from corruption!

The whole universe is enlightened by the rays of thine unnumbered wonders, O Nicholas, who art an intellectual luminary and a mighty defender!

O watchful intercessor for those who flee unto thee, Nicholas: deliver me from the cruel slumber of sloth!

Thou didst deliver of old, O most wise one, those who were about to die unjustly: likewise deliver me from perils and transgressions, O Nicholas!

Theotokion:

As the only pure and joyful Lady: help me who am ever tossed about by worldly tribulations!

*Ode 7. Heirmos: The Angel made the furnace sprinkle dew for...*

Having drawn all men from the depth of delusion by the rod of the word, the Apostles brought them unto the Word Who was slain for our sake, singing unto Him: "Blessed art Thou, O God of our Fathers!"

Partaking of bodily substance, O Apostles, being united without mediation, ye were enlightened with His primal splendors: therefore enlighten me who cry: "Blessed art Thou, O God of our Fathers!"

Entreat the Good Shepherd, O divine Disciples, to seek out me who am lost upon the mountains of transgression, and to save him who fervently cries: "Blessed art Thou, O God of our Fathers!"

Theotokion:

With the Prophets, Apostles, and Martyrs, O Virgin, entreat Him Whom thou didst bear, to deliver me from earthly [f. 188rA] evils, and vouchsafe me to become a partaker of heavenly blessings, O gracious Lady!

Another [Canon]. Heirmos: Unto Thy holy Fathers:

By the power of God, O all-blessed one, thou didst trample down the assembly of heretics, and didst preserve thy flock from their delusion, O Nicholas!

Appearing unto those who wept, thou didst nourish thy city that was in distress: deliver my soul from deep famine, by thy prayers, O father Nicholas!

Strengthen by thy prayers, O father Nicholas, those who call upon thee for help, calming the evil demonic storm!

Theotokion:

O Sovereign Lady, saving Theotokos of all men: completely free me from the bondage of passions by Thy prayers!

*Ode 8. Heirmos: From the flame Thou didst pour forth dew...*

With the sickle of prayers, destroy all the tares of my mind, O divine laborers of the Word, Apostles, that I may bring forth an ear of saving fruit!

Renew hearts that have grown old with the plow of words, and having brought about honorable tranquility, ye reaped an ear yielding a hundredfold, O eyewitnesses of God!

Having put the malice of the enemy to sleep, ye fell asleep in the righteous sleep that was meet, having become watchful intercessors for us, O Disciples of the Word, unto all ages!

Theotokion:

Deliver me from unquenchable fire, O Lord, by the prayers of Thy Prophets, Martyrs, and Apostles, and of the unwedded Maiden who ineffably contained Thee [f. 188rB] in her womb, O compassionate One!

Another [Canon]. Heirmos: Thy children in the furnace became like the Cherubim, sending up the thrice-holy hymn: Bless, hymn, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

Having ascended unto the height of radiant life, thou wast shown forth known to the whole universe, O Nicholas, bearing manifold wonders, enlightening those in darkness!

O thou who intercedest with God concerning grace for those who honor thee, Nicholas: calm the malice of hostile men who come upon us, O blessed one!

Having crushed all the snares of the enemy by the power of the Spirit: deliver me from them by thy prayers, directing my life, O divinely-wise hierarch Nicholas!

Theotokion:

We hymn Thee, O Virgin Birth-giver of God, through whom the curse became barren, and blessing came upon all who know Thee as the only unwedded Mother of our God!

*Ode 9. Heirmos: It is impossible for men to see God...*

Having preached throughout all the world God Who came unto men and deified mortality by the union of nature, ye freed all from the delusion of godlessness: therefore we ever call you blessed, O most wise Apostles!

Having chosen the passions of Christ through manifold bodily sufferings, O Apostles: put to death the passions of my flesh, and enliven my soul that is fainting, distressed, and slain!

The ranks of Angels and Archangels, Dominions, Powers, Authorities, Principalities, Cherubim, Seraphim, and Thrones, O Christ, and the assembly of the Apostles with her who bare Thee, offer prayer unto Thee, O only King: Save Thy world!

## THURSDAY EVENING VESPERS (FOR FRIDAY) (TONE 6)

[f. 189rA] ON THURSDAY EVENING, AT "LORD, I HAVE CRIED":

*Stichera of the Cross. Tone 6.*

*Podoben: "The Angelic Powers" (А҆́ггл҃скїѧ пред̾и́дꙋтъ си́лы):*

[f. 189rA] The forefather falls, being deceived on account of the tree, and receives a cruel condemnation; but Christ, being nailed upon the Tree, loosed it, and renewing him who was crushed, He raised him up and made him sit with Himself and the Father with the Honorable Spirit!

Grant me thoughts of compunction, O my Christ, that in mind and heart I may ever bear Thine honorable sufferings which Thou didst endure in the flesh for our sake, receiving the Cross and wounds; and weeping, let me ever think upon Thee standing by Thy Cross, and see Thee lifted up upon it like a Lamb!

The earth was terrified and the air was darkened, beholding God insulted by a servant: He Who scatters the mountains with His rebuke and dries up the deeps with a glance, closing His eyes upon the Tree, lifeless and dead in the flesh, He Who holds the great breath of life in His palm!

Other Stichera to the Most Holy Theotokos.

*Podoben: "The same Tone and Podoben" (Гла́съ и҆ подо́бенъ то́йже):*

Enliven my soul that is slain by many passions, O gracious Lady, who didst bear impassibly God the Word Who endured passions while remaining impassible, and Who put death to death, and slaying hades, put to death the sin that dwells in the world [f. 189rB] and direct my mortal thoughts unto divine things!

When Thou wast about to be lifted up upon the Cross, O Christ, then seeing the Disciple whom Thou lovedst and Thy Mother standing by, Thou didst say unto her: "Behold, the Virgin is Thy Mother, and this youth is thy son, O pure Virgin Mother, whom I have loved: the virgin and My Disciple!"

From that time forth, the virgin Disciple took the Virgin into his home; for being called a son by the most bountiful Son on high, he showed filial duty toward the Mother, a fitting sonship and warm kinship ever: by their prayers, O Christ, save our souls!

Glory: Now and ever: Cross-Theotokion:

When the Ewe-lamb beheld Her Lamb born of her being nailed upon the Cross, she cried aloud, tearing her hair: "Woe is me, my sweetest Child! Formerly I bare Thee without pain; but now my heart is pierced, and I cannot endure seeing Thee crucified, O Christ, my most merciful Son!"

ON FRIDAY, AT MATINS.

After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymns

Of the Cross. Tone 6.

Thy Cross, O Lord, is sanctified, for by it healings are granted unto those suffering in sins; therefore we fall down before Thee: Have mercy on us!

As soon as the Tree of Thy Cross was set up, O Christ, the foundations of death were shaken, O Lord; for the mortal whom hades had swallowed up with greed, it released with trembling! Thou hast shown forth unto us Thy salvation, O Holy One: we glorify Thee, O Son of God, have mercy on us!

Glory: Now and ever: Cross-Theotokion:

Standing by the Cross with the virgin Disciple, the Virgin Mother, beholding Him Who came forth from her, unable to endure seeing Him lifted up upon the Cross, cried aloud, overwhelmed with weeping: "How sufferest Thou, Who art impassible in nature? I glorify Thy ineffable goodness, O my Son [f. 189vB] surpassing all understanding!"

After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns

Of the Cross. Tone 6.

Today the word of the Prophet is fulfilled! For behold, we worship at the place where Thy feet stood, O Lord; and having tasted of the Tree of salvation, we have obtained freedom from sinful passions, by the intercessions of the Theotokos, O Thou Who alone art the Lover of mankind!

O Lord, the Judeans condemned Thee unto death, Who art the Life of all! They who passed through the Red Sea with a rod nailed Thee to the Cross; and they who sucked honey from the rock brought Thee gall! Martyrs:

Glory: Now and ever: Cross-Theotokion:

O holy Virgin all-pure, glory of the Angels: when thou didst stand by the Cross of thy Son and God, unable to endure beholding the reproach of enemies, thou didst cry aloud, lamenting as a mother: "How endurest Thou the threats of all, O Lover of mankind? I glorify Thy longsuffering!"

After the 3rd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns

Of the Cross. Tone 6.

Lifted up upon the Tree of the Cross for the sake of mercy and compassion, and pierced in the side with a spear, Thou didst tear up the cruel handwriting of sin, as almighty God [f. 190rA] Therefore we piously hymn Thine ineffable dispensation, O Word!

O Cross, expulsion of demons, physician of the sick, strength and guardian of the faithful, victory of kings, true boast of the Orthodox, confirmation of the Church of Christ: be Thou our confirmation, wall, and guardian, O blessed Tree!

Glory: Now and ever: Cross-Theotokion:

Beholding Thee, her pure Offspring, incarnate, hanging willingly upon the Cross, the spotless Ewe-lamb, the Virgin Mother of God, cried aloud with bitter tears: "O my gentle Son, I hymn Thy most dread dispensation!"

CANON TO THE HONORABLE AND LIFE-CREATING CROSS OF THE LORD.

Composition of Joseph.

Ode 1. Tone 6. Heirmos: He Who hid of old beneath the wave of the sea the pursuing tyrant, and buried beneath the earth the children of those who were saved: let us also, as the maiden, sing unto the Lord, for He hath been gloriously glorified!

By Thy precious Passion, Thou didst honor the nature of mankind that had been dishonored: therefore, honoring Thee with fear, we magnify Thy dominion and faithfully glorify Thee: for Thou hast been gloriously glorified!

By Thy Blood, O Word, Thou didst stop the shedding of unrighteous blood, and didst cleanse the evil defilements of human nature, O Almighty One: therefore, saved by Thy Passion, we glorify Thee!

Martyrs:

By the sparks of your blood, O truly praiseworthy Martyrs, ye overcame [f. 190rB] the assault of the adversary, and subdued the nature of fire through the dew of divine goodness, and stilled the evil storm of polytheism!

Martyrs:

Having dried up the rain of delusion with showers of blood, ye pour forth healings unto the world, and take away the inflammation of passions, O true Martyrs: therefore ye are called blessed!

Theotokion:

Having neither form nor beauty in Thy suffering, O Thou Who art fair in beauty: beholding Thee, the unwedded Maiden, the adornment of the faithful, cried aloud as a mother, and praised Thee with love!

Another Canon to the Most Holy Theotokos.

Tone 6. Same Heirmos.

Thou hast power to do whatsoever Thou willest, and Thou hast a Son Who inclines unto Thy supplications; Thou hast strength, dominion, and an invincible protection, O Theotokos and Sovereign Lady: therefore save Thy servant!

O gracious Lady, helper of all the world, deliverance and salvation of the earthly: deliver Thy servants who praise Thee in faith from manifold perils, passions, and tribulations!

Thou art the protectress of the world, O Virgin; Thou art the boast and hope of Christians: be Thou the protectress, confirmation, joy, and deliverance of my wretched soul, O divinely-blessed one!

Theotokion:

O hope and protectress of the hopeless, unashamed helper of all: having opened the heavenly gates[^268] [f. 190vA] lead me unto Thy Son, O Sovereign Lady, and save me who am lost!

Ode 3. Heirmos: Beholding Thee Who didst suspend the whole earth upon the waters without restraint, hanging upon Golgotha, creation was seized with great dread, crying: "There is none holy save Thee, O Lord, Lover of mankind!"

Beholding Thee Who didst suspend the whole earth upon the waters without restraint, lifted up upon the Tree and pierced in the side, the sun was darkened, O Lord, Who art the enlightenment of all!

The evil enemy who wounded Adam of old is wounded by the sharp nails, O longsuffering One; and having been wounded, he remains incurable unto ages; but we, the faithful, have found healing for all our wounds!

Martyrs:

When the angelic choir beheld the assembly of Martyrs being severed for the Lamb Who was slain, they marveled how material men overcame immaterial enemies, receiving crowns of victory!

Martyrs:

Clothed with strength, the Saints wrestled with the enemy by the strength of the One Who strengthens all things, and trampled down his frail power, receiving crowns of victory!

Theotokion:

When she who bare Thee ineffably beheld Thee wounded by the spear, the all-pure and undefiled Lady was wounded in heart, and weeping, cried aloud: "What hath the lawless assembly rendered unto Thee, O my Child?"

Another [Canon]. Same Heirmos.

[f. 190vB] Water Thy suppliants with saving streams, O Virgin Mother and Maiden, delivering them from the darkness of temptation and from the flame of unquenchable fire, O all-pure one, who honor Thee as the Theotokos and glorify Thee with faith!

Encompassed by the storm of wounds and transgressions, I flee unto Thee, O Birth-giver of God, and pray: Consume these my wounds, and save me, granting me divine health!

O pure Birth-giver of God who rulest over all creation: show me free from grievous sins and improper deeds by which I have been enslaved, through Thy divine power!

I know and understand Thy tender compassion, O all-pure Birth-giver of God: therefore I flee unto Thee and pray to obtain Thy help, O Bride of God, that I may find cleansing of evils!

Ode 4. Heirmos: Foreseeing Thy divine condescension upon the Cross, Habakkuk cried out with dread: "Thou didst cut down the power of the mighty, O Good One, entering into communion with those in hades, as Thou art almighty!"

The stretching forth of Thy hands upon the Tree washed away the intemperance of the hands stretched out unto the tree, O Lord: Thou didst will to stretch forth Thy hands upon the Tree, O Master, and by Thy fall Thou didst loose the bonds of sinners, renewing them!

Thou didst choose to suffer, O most good Lord, that Thou mightest loose us from the passions of dishonor: Thou didst taste gall, granting me the divine sweetness of incorruption, O Slain One, bestowing life upon me, O Master [f. 191rA] divinely-wise, bringing the fire of divine love into their souls, extinguished the fire of the lawless, and Christ's Passion-bearers and Martyrs became radiant lamps!

The divine friends of the King of all, having detached themselves from fleshly love, ran steadfastly unto every torment, and having conquered, were crowned with glory!

Theotokion:

"Without passions I bare Thee; and how do I now behold Thee partaking of passions? How endurest Thou this?" the Virgin cried aloud: "O Son without beginning, I glorify Thy longsuffering!"

Another [Canon]. Same Heirmos.

Hearing the voice of my salvation, I cry unto Thee with hands outstretched: Have mercy on me, O gracious Mother of God; be Thou my helper and protection!

Held fast by storms of immeasurable passions and transgressions, with tears I cry unto Thee: O gracious and pure one, preserve me by Thy divine governance!

Make the dreadful dispute easy for me, O Virgin Sovereign Lady, at the departure of my soul from the body, and show me to be a partaker of the divine rest there, O gracious one!

Behold my affliction, O all-pure Lady; attend unto my sighing and receive my sorrow; and show Thy great grace upon me, filling my humble soul with joy!

Ode 5. Heirmos: Rising early unto Thee, for the sake of Thy tender mercy, He Who is unchanging changed Himself for the sake of the fallen one, and condescended [f. 191rB] impassibly even unto suffering for the Word of God: Grant me peace, O Lover of mankind!

Thou wast seen dead upon Golgotha, Who by the passion of Thy flesh didst put hades to death: Thou hadst neither form nor beauty in it, O Christ, desiring to adorn me, as Thou art the Lover of mankind!

Desiring to deliver the first-formed Adam from grievous sufferings by nails, Thou wast nailed with nails and pierced with a spear, O Christ, forbidding the fiery sword to forbid the entrance of Thy servants!

Martyrs:

Following the footsteps of the Master's Passion, the ranks of Martyrs were nailed upon the tree, their hands and feet together being severed, divinely directed unto the paths of honorable martyrdom!

Martyrs:

With perfect minds, having humbled yourselves in imitation of Him Who exalted all, Christ's Martyrs by humility of heart utterly cast down the proud mind that was lifted up in arrogance!

Theotokion:

Thou didst blossom from the root of Jesse, O Virgin, and as a flower didst bring forth the Planter of the world, drying up the swamp of godlessness with the divine garden of the Cross, which He received in the flesh!

Another [Canon]. Same Heirmos.

Those who piously glorify Thee as truly the Mother of God, O pure one, and who kiss Thine icon, being delighted with enlightenment through Thy supplications unto Thy Son, and with unceasing joy, with all the Saints, are delivered from fire and torment...[^269]

[f. 191vA] According to the multitude of Thy tender mercies and compassion, O good one: grant cleansing of sins and forgiveness of transgressions unto him that flees unto Thee in faith and asks Thy prayers, O Birth-giver of God, Ever-Virgin!

Being grievously wounded by the frequent afflictions of life, and by passions, sorrows, and demonic assaults: deliver me, O good and all-pure Virgin, and grant me the consolation and illumination of salvation!

In slothfulness have I spent my life; I have provoked Thee to anger, O Virgin, and ever do I, the wretched one, lament, and have not found Thy mercy. But by Thy prayers, O good one, look not upon me that I be condemned utterly unto hellish condemnation!

Ode 6. Heirmos:

Cast forth from the whale, yet not held fast in the belly of the sea monster was Jonah, bearing the type of Thee Who didst suffer and wast delivered unto burial; for he came forth from the beast as from a bridal chamber, and he cried aloud unto the guard: "Ye who keep vain and false things have forsaken your own mercy!"

Crossing his hands of old, Jacob prefigured the Cross when blessing the children; therefore, O Thou Most High, ascending thereon, Thou didst loose mankind from the ancient curse, and now dost show forth a blessing unto those who bless Thee, O only blessed One and most glorious Creator!

Prefiguring Thy Passion of old, O Word, the great Moses raised up the bronze serpent, delivering those who looked upon it from the venomous bite of the poisonous serpent; for [f. 191vB] having been crucified, all we faithful were delivered from the harm of the God-hating serpent!

Martyrs:

When others were suffering of old, the divine and steadfast sufferers underwent suffering, despising the eternal rewards and joys; by their prayers, O Savior of the world, deliver from temptations, sins, and perils those who hymn Thee!

Martyrs:

By the outpouring of their precious blood, the divine Passion-bearers truly appeared unto the faithful as streams purifying delusion, and as fountains pouring forth the waters of the knowledge of God; by their prayers, O Savior of the world, rain down forgiveness unto all, cleansing of sins, and great mercy!

Theotokion:

Beholding the Good Shepherd, the Master of all, lifted up upon the Tree, the Ewe-lamb wept with maternal lamentation, crying aloud: "What is this new mystery, O Child? How is it that the immortal Son undergoes death, desiring to deliver mankind from corruption?"

Another [Canon]. Same Heirmos.

I fall down before Thee and pray, O all-pure Sovereign Lady of the world: bury the passions of my soul, the grievous desires of the flesh, and the inclinations of my thoughts; and by Thy power utterly cast down the demonic malice and affliction, O all-pure one, and save me!

My mind, darkened by the gloom of wicked thoughts, the mist of pleasures, and the darkness of transgressions: do Thou enlighten by Thy prayers, O Virgin Mother who didst bear the Divine Light; and direct my unstable path unto the illumination of repentance and goodness [f. 192rA] Direct me unto the divine paths, O Mother of the King of all, delivering me from the unruly paths of passions and sin, and guiding me unto incorruptible life; for Thou art the cause of all good things and salvation unto men, saving from corruption and leading up unto salvation!

Theotokion:

Having carried as a Child Him Who is before all ages, O pure one: unceasingly pray unto Him for peace, O all-blessed Virgin Mother; and as His all-pure Mother, entreat forgiveness of my transgressions, having ever great boldness before Thy Son, O pure one!

Ode 7. Heirmos:

An ineffable wonder! He Who delivered the holy Children from the flame in the furnace is laid in the tomb as a lifeless corpse in the flesh, unto the salvation of us who chant: "O God our Redeemer, blessed art Thou!"

When the Jewish council condemned Thee to death upon the Cross, the earth was shaken and the sun hid its light; and those sitting in darkness beheld the light, chanting: "O God our Redeemer, blessed art Thou!"

Thou didst submit to condemnation, O Savior, granting pardon unto all, and wast crowned with thorns as King by Thine own will, O Christ God, unto the salvation of us who chant: "O God our Redeemer, blessed art Thou!"

Martyrs:

Ye encompassed all the malice of the devil, O all-praised Martyrs, plainly destroying it; and having chosen honor, ye endured unjust torments and death, desiring the life that is to come, and crying aloud: "O God our Redeemer, blessed art Thou!"

Martyrs:

Ye stood in the midst of the flame, O all-praised [f. 192rB] Martyrs, visibly consuming the delusion; and remaining unconsumed by the bedewing of divine goodness, ye cried out, chanting: "O God our Redeemer, blessed art Thou!"

Cross-Theotokion:

Beholding Thee willingly crucified, O unoriginate One, the Birth-giver of God cried aloud: "My soul is encompassed with sorrow, yet Thou diest, bestowing life upon those who chant: O God our Redeemer, blessed art Thou!"

Another [Canon]. Same Heirmos.

Establish my spirit upon the rock of the desires of my Creator, O pure Sovereign Lady, having stilled the tempest of pleasures and the tumult of passions by Thy prayers, and granting me divine tranquility and peace!

Grant me a shower of tears, O all-pure Sovereign Lady, washing away all the defilement and filth of the pleasures of the soul, and presenting me pure unto the Creator, delivering me from all torments!

Having acquired Thee as our protectress and our unashamed support, O blameless and pure one, may we be delivered from the enemy's assault, and may the great snares be made manifest, as well as the dreadful and eternal condemnation!

The night of my grievous transgressions holds me fast, and the mist of lawlessness and the abyss of evil, lo, covers me; lead me forth from the pit of sin, O Mother of God and protectress of the faithful!

Ode 8. Heirmos:

Be astonished and fear, O heaven, and let the foundations of the earth be shaken; for lo, He Who dwells in the highest is numbered among the dead[^270] [f. 192vA] He Who dwells in the highest and abides in a small tomb! Him do ye children bless, ye priests praise, and supremely exalt unto the ages!

Thou didst drink the cup, O Christ, which Thou didst desire through Thy Passion upon the Cross, pouring forth for me streams of remission from Thy life-creating side; for the sake of the rib of him who died, I hymn Thee with songs: Him do ye children bless, ye priests praise, and supremely exalt unto the ages!

When the lawless people condemned Thee, the Giver of life and the Lord, to be crucified in the midst of evildoers, O Jesus, the earth was afraid, and all sang with fear: Ye children bless, ye priests praise, and supremely exalt Him unto the ages!

Martyrs:

Precious before God was your death shown to be, O Martyrs of Christ; for having partaken of many sufferings, ye appeared as partakers of the honorable Passion of Christ; therefore crying out unceasingly: Ye children bless, ye priests praise, and supremely exalt Him unto the ages!

Martyrs:

Truly incorporeal were your weapons, O Martyrs, against the battle-array of the enemies: even hope, faith, and truth, through which ye obtained God and were joined unto the ranks of the elect, crying aloud unto the Master: Ye children bless, ye priests praise, and supremely exalt Him unto the ages!

Cross-Theotokion:

"O Most High and unoriginate Son, Thou endurest spitting, reproaches, and the Cross, stretching out Thy hands unto the adversaries!" the Birth-giver of God cried aloud: "I glorify Thy longsuffering, Whom ye children bless, ye priests praise..." [f. 192vB] praise, and supremely exalt unto the ages!

Another [Canon]. Same Heirmos.

O Thou Who didst bear Christ the Light: by Thy bright supplications and prayers, O Virgin, fill Thy servants with the unsetting Light, who piously hymn Thee in faith; for by Thine intercession Thou art powerful to save whomsoever Thou wilt!

Grievous perils, most bitter evils, and afflictions encompass me, and dire necessities and cruel diseases hold me fast and destroy me; straightway do I invoke Thy help, O Virgin: deliver me from them and from dangers, guiding me unto true tranquility!

Cast down the enemy's battle-arrays by Thy power, O good Birth-giver of God; take away those who war against me and pursue me vehemently, and who rejoice at my destruction; guard, preserve, and deliver me from their wicked craftiness and cruel deceit!

Tame the storm of my sorrows, O pure one, which the multitude of my sins hath brought upon me, and quench the furnace of my burning passions with the dew of Thy divine prayer, that I may hymn Thy fervent protection, O Maiden, and supremely exalt Thee unto all the ages!

Ode 9. Heirmos:

Weep not for Me, O Mother, beholding in the tomb the Son Whom Thou didst conceive in Thy womb without seed in the flesh; for I shall arise and be glorified, and as God I shall exalt with unceasing glory those who magnify Thee in faith and love! [f. 193rA] That Thou mightest deliver from corruption him who was thoroughly corrupted through the sweetness of the tree, O only Savior, as Thou art good, Thou didst deign to be crucified in the flesh and to die; we unceasingly hymn, O Jesus, Thy great compassion and Thy power!

How didst Thou endure sufferings, lying outstretched upon the Cross, delivering me from cruel pains, O good Christ? How wast Thou crowned with thorns, bearing all the painful suffering? How wast Thou given vinegar and gall to drink, drawing for us the cup of joy?

Martyrs:

Being tried by fire and cast into prisons, and cruelly severed upon sharp edges, O sufferers, and violently stretched upon the wheel, and given as food unto wild beasts: being the servants of Christ the Master, ye did not deny Him!

Martyrs:

Far surpassing the rays of the sun, the most radiant and celebrated memory of the sufferers ever enlightens the souls of the pious, driving away the darkness of passions and perils, and burying the deep gloom of demons!

Theotokion:

Thou bearest Him Who bears all things, and holdest Him as an Infant in Thine arms, Who delivers us from the hand of the warring enemy, O most pure Sovereign Lady; and Thou seest Him suspended upon the Tree of the Cross, Who raised up mankind from hidden evils!

Another [Canon]. Same Heirmos.

Grown cold in heart, I bring myself unto Thee in corruption, and cast all my care upon Thee; for Thy sake may I find deliverance from transgressions, that through the stream of Thy prayers I may become a partaker of future adoption and glory! [f. 193rB] Unto the Mother of God, O pure one, have I found Thee as a protectress, a shelter, a hope, a wall, a refuge, a cleansing, and a deliverance from cruel things, O all-pure one; save me from perils and dangers, diseases and passions, and unceasingly do I purely glorify Thee!

O firm salvation and certain hope, Who hast exalted the human race unto heaven, pouring forth upon us the divine rain: O Virgin Birth-giver of God, save us from passions and perils, and from eternal fire!

Having ineffably given birth unto the Word Who is above all beginning, the only-begotten Son and God from the Father: unceasingly entreat Him, O pure Maiden, that they may be delivered from perils and all wrath, who magnify Thee with faith and love!

At the Aposticha, Stichera

Of the Cross. Tone 6.

In the Cross do I have hope, O Christ, and therein do I boast, crying aloud: O Lord, Lover of mankind, cast down the pride of those who confess Thee not as God and man!

Being protected by the Cross, we oppose the enemy, fearing neither his wiles nor his assaults; for the proud one hath indeed been brought to naught and trampled down by the power of Christ Who was crucified upon the Tree!

Martyrs:

O Lord, at the memory of Thy Saints, all creation keeps feast; the heavens rejoice with the Angels, and the earth rejoices with men: by their prayers have mercy on us!

Glory: Now and ever: Cross-Theotokion:

When the all-pure one beheld Thee suspended upon the Cross, she wept and cried aloud with maternal[^271] [f. 193vA] lamentation: "O my Son and my God, my sweetest Child: how endurest Thou this shameful passion?"

ON FRIDAY. The Beatitudes,

Tone 6.

Remember me, O God my Savior, when Thou comest into Thy Kingdom, and save me, as Thou alone art the Lover of mankind!

Stretching out Thy hands upon the Tree, Thou didst embrace the nations who hymn Thy tender compassion, O Christ our God!

Thou wast nailed upon the Cross of Thine own will, and by Thy power, O Christ, Thou didst crush the sting of torment unto the end!

Being fed with manna, O Passion-bearers, ye were accounted worthy of paradise food, praying unceasingly for the world!

Glory: Triadicon:

With every wound unto torments, Thou Who art co-eternal with Thine own Father and the Holy Spirit didst endure the sacred Passion, O Christ!

Now and ever: Theotokion:

Beholding Thee stretched upon the Cross, the Virgin sighed with tears; by her prayers save those who hymn Thee!

## FRIDAY EVENING VESPERS (FOR SATURDAY) (TONE 6)

ON FRIDAY EVENING. AT "LORD, I HAVE CRIED":

Stichera to the Holy Martyrs, Hierarchs, and Venerable Monastics:

*Tone 6.*

*Podoben: "Having laid aside all earthly hope" (Всѐ ѿло́жше):*

Walking in the footsteps of Christ's Passions, the whole assembly of the Martyrs entered steadfastly into many struggles; and before lawless kings they proclaimed God, and endured many torments, expecting to receive heavenly honors. Beholding these things now, they rejoice and stand before God with all the choirs of the bodiless Powers!

O flock chosen of God, ye became imitators of Christ the strong Shepherd, O all-sacred shepherds; ye preserved undamaged unto the end the divine treasures of piety, having driven away the wild wolves, which ye led well into the heavenly fold. Therefore, now dwelling [f. 193vB] therein, remember with love those who praise you well and maintain the piety of Christ, that great mercy may be granted unto our souls!

Having lived venerably, O all ye venerable Fathers, ye conquered all things; and ye endured your own torments, quenching the burnings of the passions; valiantly did ye endure, O blessed ones, and now ye rejoice with the heavenly Powers, having lived as imitators of the life in the flesh. With those all-fruitful ones, pray unto the most good God that they who honor you with good works may find deliverance from falls!

Other Stichera to the Martyrs:

*Podoben: "The same Tone and Podoben" (Гла́съ и҆ подо́бенъ то́йже):*

Thy Martyrs, O Lord, did not deny Thee, nor did they depart from Thy commandments: by their prayers have mercy on us!

O Passion-bearing Martyrs, heavenly citizens: having suffered upon earth, ye endured many torments; by their prayers and supplication, O Lord, preserve us all!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

Who doth not call Thee blessed?

At the Aposticha, Stichera

Of the Martyrs. Tone 6.

Those who suffered for Thy sake, O Christ, endured many torments, and received perfect crowns in the heavens, that they may pray for our souls!

Thy Cross, O Lord, became an unconquerable weapon unto the Martyrs; for beholding the death set before them, and despising the future life, they were strengthened by their hope in Thee: by their prayers have mercy on us!

*Hymn for the Departed (Поко́инъ):*

My beginning and substance was Thy creative command; for desiring to fashion me as a living creature from the invisible and visible nature, Thou didst fashion my body from the earth, and gavest me a soul by Thy divine and life-creating breath. Therefore, O Savior, give rest unto Thy servants in the land of the living, and in the tents of the righteous!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

By the prayers of Her that bare Thee, O Christ, and of Thy Martyrs, Apostles, Prophets, Hierarchs, Venerable, and Righteous ones, and of all the Saints: give rest unto Thy departed servants!

## SATURDAY MATINS: ALL SAINTS, MARTYRS, AND THE DEPARTED (TONE 6)

[f. 194rA] ON SATURDAY AT MATINS

After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymns

Of the Martyrs. Tone 6.

The light of the righteous is everlasting; for the Saints, being enlightened in Thee, shine ever as luminaries, having extinguished the lamp of the impious. By their prayers, O our Savior, do Thou enlighten my lamp, O Lord, and save me!

Having endured the struggle of suffering, the Saints received victory honors from Thee; they brought to naught the devices of the lawless, and received incorruptible crowns. Being entreated by them, O God, grant us great mercy!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

O Thou Who didst call Thy Mother blessed: Thou didst come unto the Passion by voluntary counsel, shining forth upon the Cross, desiring to seek out Adam, saying unto the Angels: "Rejoice with Me, for the lost drachma is found!" O God Who hast wisely ordered all things, glory to Thee!

After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns

Of the Martyrs. Tone 6.

The suffering resistances in the judgment hall were engaged in struggle; and the tormenting wounds were upon the Martyrs, while the choirs of the bodiless stood by, holding victory honors. They astonished the wise tormentors and kings, and cast down Belial by the confession of Christ: O Lord Who didst strengthen them, glory to Thee!

O Lord, in the memory of Thy Saints, today was shown forth as the Paradise that was [f. 194rB] in Eden; for therein all creation rejoices, and by their supplications grant us peace and great mercy!

Truly all things are vanity, and life is but a shadow and a dream; for in vain doth every earthborn man disquiet himself, as the Scripture saith: when we have acquired the world, then do we take up our dwelling in the grave, where kings and beggars are together. Therefore, O Christ God, give rest unto the departed, as Thou art the Lover of mankind!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

The sighings of my heart and from my womb do I offer unto Thee: I pray for Thy timely protection, O all-undefiled one; have mercy on my all-passionate soul, entreat the merciful God to deliver me from judgment and the lake of fire, O only blessed one!

Canon to the Holy Martyrs, Hierarchs, Venerable Monastics, and the Departed.

Composition of Joseph.

Tone 6. Ode 1. Heirmos:

Traversing the deep on foot as on dry land, Israel beheld Pharaoh the pursuer overwhelmed in the waters, and cried aloud: "Let us sing a song of victory unto God, for He is glorified!"

Enlightened in mind amidst the dark surroundings, the Martyrs put to shame the wicked persecutor, becoming victorious in Christ, and they passed over unto the unsetting light!

The sole solemnity of Christ's Hierarchs, the choir of the Venerable, the Prophets, and all the Righteous, shining with the beauties of virtues, ascended unto the heavenly habitations!

The present multitude, having united[^272] [f. 194vA] themselves unto Christ, and having trampled down by manly labors him that had slain mankind by cruel delusion, are called blessed with divine songs!

*Hymn for the Departed (Поко́инъ):*

O Christ Who in the beginning didst fashion man from the earth: give rest unto the souls of Thy servants, we pray Thee, in the place of refreshment, as Thou art good, in the habitations of the righteous!

Theotokion:

More holy than the Cherubim and Seraphim wast Thou shown to be, O pure one, having given birth unto the Creator of creation; Him unceasingly entreat to have compassion upon Thy servants who glorify Thee!

Another Canon for the Departed.

Composition of Theophanes.

Tone 6. Heirmos:

Traversing the deep on foot as on dry land:

In the highest bridal chambers, O valiant Martyrs, ye ever pray unto Christ: account those faithful whom He hath translated from the earth worthy to obtain eternal good things!

Thou didst adorn the magnitude of the mixed living creature within me, O man, creating me both of humility and magnitude; therefore, O Savior, give rest unto the souls of Thy servants!

In the beginning Thou didst establish me as an inhabitant of Paradise and a tiller of the earth; but when I transgressed Thy commandment, Thou didst cast me out; therefore, O Savior, give rest unto the souls of Thy servants!

Theotokion:

O Thou Who in the beginning didst fashion Eve from the rib as our foremother: being incarnate from Thy most pure womb, O Lover of mankind, Thou, O pure one, didst destroy the power of God's death!

Ode 3. Heirmos:

There is none holy as Thou, O Lord my God, Who hast exalted the horn of Thy faithful, O Good One, and hast established us upon the rock of Thy confession! [f. 194vB] having strengthened the thoughts of my soul, establish me, O Lord; for I have Thee, O Good One, as my refuge and support!

Exchanging sufferings for tears, the sufferers looked with joy unto the painless recompense; and now by their goodness they transform our endless sufferings!

Driving away the wicked beasts with a dense darkness, the divine Passion-bearers, the divine sheep of Christ, were preserved unharmed from their afflictions!

The choir of the Venerable today willingly submitted unto heaven, putting to death the fleshly mind, and received eternal life!

*Hymn for the Departed (Поко́инъ):*

Deliver from eternal fire, O Christ, those who have piously departed this life, and grant them remission of their debts, O glorious One, and the enjoyment of the Kingdom!

Theotokion:

The women who loved Christ stand before Thee with joyful mind, O pure Sovereign Lady, who didst ineffably give birth unto Him, and they celebrate!

Another [Canon]. Heirmos:

There is none holy as Thou, O Lord:

Having suffered lawfully, O Giver of life, Thy Martyrs, adorned with crowns of victory, fervently intercede for eternal deliverance for those who have departed in faith!

Having instructed me of old through many wonders and signs, me that had gone astray, at the last Thou didst empty Thyself in the womb, and having sought and found me, Thou didst save me!

Having crossed over from fleeting and unstable corruption unto Thee, O Good One: account them worthy to dwell joyfully in the eternal habitations, having justified them [f. 195rA] through faith and grace!

Theotokion:

There is none spotless as Thou, O all-pure Mother of God; for alone unto the ages didst Thou conceive in Thy womb the true God Who destroyed the power of death!

Ode 4. Heirmos:

I heard Thy report, O Lord, and was afraid; I understood Thy works, and was astonished: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

Standing firm, the Passion-bearers beheld the proud one laid low before their feet, and they thankfully glorified the Creator of all!

Armed with the brightness of virtues, the Hierarchs saved men from the darkness of heresies unto the light of knowledge, like burning coals, having consumed material passions by their fervent union with God; O Venerable ones, ye are glorified in all the world!

*Hymn for the Departed (Поко́инъ):*

O Lord Who rulest over the living and the dead: give rest unto those whom Thou hast translated, with all who have been well-pleasing unto Thee, as Thou art the Lord! The all-pure one ineffably bare the garment of the Incarnation; the assembly of women who valiantly struggled was received!

Another Heirmos: Same.

Thou didst show forth a greater knowledge of wisdom, and that wherewith I was endowed by Thy all-perfect grace, O Master, joining the choirs of Martyrs unto the Angels [f. 195rB] joining them unto the Angels!

Account her that hath departed unto Thee worthy to obtain Thine ineffable glory, O Christ, where the habitation of those who rejoice is tranquility and the voice...

Receive those who hymn Thy divine dominion, whom Thou hast taken from the earth, making them children of light, cleansing away the mist of sin, O most merciful One!

Theotokion:

An all-pure receptacle, an all-blameless temple, an all-holy Ark, a virginal place of sanctification, the beauty of Jacob: the Master hath chosen Thee!

Ode 5. Heirmos:

O Thou Who didst make light to shine forth upon all the world, enlighten my heart, and save me who cry aloud in the night!

Woven from above with grace and clad in a robe, O sufferers, ye stripped the enemy bare!

With the Holy Prophets, honor the divinely-wise Hierarchs and the Venerable ones who were well-pleasing unto God!

In psalms and hymns let the assembly of women be praised, as having been well-pleasing unto the Lord!

*Hymn for the Departed (Поко́инъ):*

In the habitations of Thy righteous ones, O Lord, establish Thy servants, overlooking the transgressions committed in this life!

Theotokion:

Delivering us from great harm and warfare, appear, O Sovereign Lady, praying unto Christ the only compassionate One!

Another [Canon]. Heirmos: Rising early unto Thee:

As a sacred whole-burnt offering and as the first-fruits of human nature, O Martyrs, ye were offered unto the glorified God, ever interceding for our salvation!

Account Thy servants who have fallen asleep before us in the faith worthy of heavenly dwelling and the distribution of gifts, O Lord, granting remission of offenses!

O Thou Who alone art in nature life-creating[^273] [f. 195vA] and Who art truly an unsearchable abyss of goodness: account those who have ended their lives worthy of Thy Kingdom, O compassionate One, Who alone art immortal!

Theotokion:

Strength and song didst Thou become, O Sovereign Lady, having borne the incorruptible One for the world; and salvation came unto the lost, when the enemy was cast out from Adam, for those who bless Thee in faith!

Ode 6. Heirmos:

Beholding the sea of life surging with the tempest of temptations, and fleeing unto Thy calm haven, I cry aloud unto Thee: Lead up my life from corruption, O Most Merciful One!

By the streams of divine blood ye drowned the spiritual enemy, and ye watered the hearts of the faithful, O Passion-bearers!

Having crucified yourselves unto the world and passions, O Venerable and all-wise Hierarchs, ye were accounted worthy of divine glory!

The choir of Prophets and the assembly of honorable women who struggled well, we worthily call blessed!

*Hymn for the Departed (Поко́инъ):*

Give rest, O God, unto the spirits of those who have fallen asleep before us, among Thine elect, overlooking their transgressions!

Theotokion:

O Thou Who didst bear Christ in the flesh: put to death the passions of my flesh, and quicken my soul, O Virgin, by Thine intercessions!

Another [Canon]. Heirmos: The sea of life:

Being nailed upon the Cross, Thou didst gather unto Thyself the choirs of Martyrs who imitated Thy Passion, O Good One; therefore we pray Thee: give rest unto those who have departed unto Thee!

In Thine ineffable glory, when Thou comest fearfully to judge all the world, grant, O Jesus, that Thy faithful servants whom Thou hast taken from the earth may meet Thee brightly upon the clouds [f. 195vB] O Redeemer!

Being the Fountain of life, delivering by divine power Thy servants who were bound, O Master: settle in the food of Paradise those who have departed unto Thee in faith!

Theotokion:

We returned unto the earth, having transgressed the commandment of God, O forebears; but through Thee, O Virgin, we are raised up again from the earth, having shaken off mortal corruption!

Ode 7. Heirmos:

I heard the praises of Thy holy Children, and Thou didst cool the burning furnace: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers!

With hymns let us honor the Passion-bearers of Christ, who quenched the flame of cruel godlessness with rivers of blood!

The glorious Hierarchs destroyed the winter of heresies, and rejoicing in the divine crown, they passed over, having inherited through endurance the abundant grace of the Spirit; chanting, ye destroyed the multitudes of adversaries!

*Hymn for the Departed (Поко́инъ):*

Account them worthy to attain rest, O compassionate One, who have departed from this life in faith, O Most Merciful One!

Theotokion:

He Who showed Thee to be a Virgin even after birth-giving, O pure one, hath saved the choir of holy women who followed after Thee!

Another [Canon]. Heirmos:

The furnace that brought dew:

Being delivered by Thy blood from the first transgression, the Martyrs, sprinkled with their own blood, visibly prefigured Thy slaughter: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

By Thy death Thou didst put death to death, O most life-originating Word; receive those who have fallen asleep in Thy faith, who sing and say: O Christ, blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

Having given a soul unto man by divine inbreathing, O Master, Author of blood: account the departed worthy of Thy Kingdom, that they may chant unto Thee, O Savior: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

Theotokion:

Exalted above all creatures wast Thou, O all-undefiled one, having conceived God Who shattered the gates of death and tore asunder the bonds; therefore we faithful hymn Thee with songs as the Mother of God!

Ode 8. Heirmos:

Thy holy Children in Babylon, being likened unto the Cherubim, sent up the thrice-holy hymn: Bless, chant, and supremely exalt Him unto the ages!

Protected by the endurance of torments, the valiant divine Martyrs passed through by grace, and attained unto the deep tranquility of the Kingdom on high!

The Venerable and all-wise Hierarchs shone forth as the sun, enlightening the universe with the rays of their teachings and the brightness of healings!

O glorious Prophets and first martyrs, all ye Venerable and Righteous ones, multitude of men and women: preserve your flock unshaken from all perils!

*Hymn for the Departed (Поко́инъ):*

Let us hymn Him Who deceitfully fashioned man, and the God-proclaiming faithful, and let us cry aloud [f. 196rA] with compunction: by their prayers, O Word, give rest unto those who have fallen asleep in faith!

Theotokion:

Near unto Thee, who art near unto God, O Virgin, the beloved choir of women was brought in Thy train unto the Master of all, praising Thee with one accord, O all-pure one!

Another [Canon]. Heirmos:

From the flame Thou didst pour forth dew for the holy ones:

Steadfastly showing forth their struggles, and being strengthened with victory-bearing crowns, the choir of Passion-bearing Martyrs cry aloud: We supremely exalt Thee, O Christ, unto the ages!

The faithful who have sacredly left this life and crossed over unto Thee, O Master: receive meekly, giving them rest as Thou art compassionate, who supremely exalt Thee, O Christ, unto the ages!

Now grant, O Savior, that all those who have fallen asleep before us may dwell in the land of the meek, having justified them through faith in Thee and through grace, who supremely exalt Thee, the Lord, unto the ages!

Theotokion:

We all call Thee blessed, O all-blessed one, for Thou didst give birth unto the Word Who is truly blessed, Who became flesh for our sake; Whom we supremely exalt, the Lord, unto the ages!

Ode 9. Heirmos:

Having received the "Rejoice" from the Angel, and having given birth unto Thine own Creator, O Virgin, save those who magnify Thee!

As pure sacrifices were the Passion-bearing Martyrs offered unto God; entreat Him to save our souls!

As shepherds, O Hierarchs, ye tended the faithful in the pastures of piety; and now ye have been led into the divine sheepfold!

With the holy Hierarchs and Prophets, and the choir of women who valiantly suffered, and the choirs of the Venerable, let us call them blessed!

[f. 196rB] *Hymn for the Departed (Поко́инъ):*

Account the departed worthy to obtain that everlasting joy wherein the assemblies of the Saints partake, O Most Merciful One!

Theotokion:

O Thou Who didst give birth unto the Light: enlighten my soul, O Virgin, driving away the darkness of my sin and slothfulness!

Another [Canon]. Heirmos: It is impossible for men to see God:

Hope strengthened the choirs of Martyrs, and winged them with burning desire for Thy love, prefiguring for them that truly unshakable rest which is to come; of which account the faithful departed worthy, O Good One!

Grant, O Christ, that those who have departed in faith may attain unto the radiant and divine brightness of Thy presence; and give them rest in the bosom of Abraham, as Thou alone bestowest mercy upon them and accountest them worthy of eternal blessedness!

O Thou Who art good and merciful in nature, the Lover of mercy and the abyss of tender compassion: where Thy light shines, there establish those whom Thou hast translated, O Savior, from this place of affliction and the shadow of death!

Theotokion:

We understand Thee, O pure one, to be the holy Tabernacle, the Ark, and the Tablet of the Law and of grace; through Thee was forgiveness granted unto those justified by the blood of Him Who was incarnate from Thy womb, O all-undefiled one!

At the Praises, Stichera

Of the Martyrs. Tone 6.

O Lord, in the memory of Thy Saints, all creation keeps feast; the heavens rejoice with the Angels, and the earth rejoices with men: by their prayers have mercy on us!...[^274]

[f. 196vA] O Lord, if we had not Thy Saints as intercessors and Thy goodness showing mercy upon us, how should we dare, O Savior, to hymn Thee, Whom the Angels glorify unceasingly? O Knower of hearts, spare our souls!

The memory of the Martyrs is a coming joy, O Lord; for having suffered for the sake of Christ, they received crowns from Him, and now with boldness they pray for our souls!

O chosen members of our holy God: Rejoice and make merry, all ye His servants, for He hath prepared crowns and His Kingdom for you; but we pray you, forget not us also!

*Hymn for the Departed (Поко́инъ):*

The tasting of the tree of old in Eden became sickness unto Adam, when the serpent spewed forth his venom; for on this account all-destroying death entered in, devouring man. But the Master came and cast down the serpent, and granted us the Resurrection. Therefore let us cry aloud unto Him: Spare those whom Thou hast received, O Savior, and give them rest with the Saints, as Thou art the Lover of mankind!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

Thou art our God, Who in wisdom didst make and finish all things; Thou didst send Prophets, O Christ, to foretell Thy coming, and Apostles to preach Thy mighty works. And some indeed prophesied Thy coming, while others enlightened the nations through Baptism; and the Martyrs obtained what they desired, and the choir of both entreats Thee [f. 196vB] with Her that bare Thee, O Christ: Give rest, O God, unto the souls whom Thou hast received, and account us worthy of Thy Kingdom, O my Redeemer God Who didst endure crucifixion for my sake, the condemned one!

At the Aposticha, Stichera

For the Departed. Tone 6.

*Podoben: "Having laid aside all earthly hope" (Всѐ ѿло́жше):*

Possessing incomprehensible compassion toward us, and unfailing fountains of divine goodness, O Most Merciful One: settle in the land of the living those who have crossed over unto Thee, O Master, in the beloved and desired habitations, the possession that ever abides; for Thou didst shed Thy blood for all, O Savior, and by the life-bearing price didst ransom the world!

*Verse: Their souls shall dwell among good things.*

Thou didst submit to death by Thy life-creating will, and didst pour forth life and give ever-existing food unto the faithful; which grant now also unto the departed in the hope of the Resurrection, forgiving all their transgressions through Thy goodness, as Thou alone art sinless, the only God and Lover of mankind, that Thy name, O Christ, may be praised by all, and being saved, we may glorify Thy love for mankind!

*Verse: Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen and taken to Thyself, O Lord.*

Ruling over the living by Thy God-originating power, and governing the dead, knowing Thee, O Christ, we pray: Give rest in that place unto Thy faithful servants who have departed [f. 197rA] unto Thy faithful servants, with Thine elect, O Lover of mankind, in a place of refreshment, in the splendors of the Saints; for Thou art the Lover of mercy, and savest as God those whom Thou didst create according to Thine own image, O only Most Merciful One!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

Thou wast shown forth as a divinely-fitting habitation, O all-pure one; for Thou didst contain God and didst bear Christ, O Virgin Mother, in two essences, yet in one hypostasis. Entreat Him, O pure one, the only-begotten Firstborn, Who preserved Thee a blameless Virgin even after birth-giving, to give rest unto the souls of those who have fallen asleep in faith, in light and in incorruptible blessedness!

ON SATURDAY

[f. 197rB] Fearing neither fire, nor swords, nor the assaults of wild beasts, O glorious Passion-bearers, ye were accounted worthy of everlasting life!

O Lover of mankind Who hast glorified the Prophets, Teachers, Venerable ones, Hierarchs, and Righteous ones: by their prayers save our souls!

Settle with all the Saints and Righteous, O Word, those whom Thou hast translated from temporary things in faith, that we may glorify Thee!

# TONE 7: SATURDAY VESPERS, SUNDAY MATINS, AND WEEKDAY OFFICES

## SATURDAY EVENING: VESPERS (TONE 7)

[f. 198rA] ON SATURDAY EVENING AT LITTLE VESPERS.

Resurrection Stichera. Tone 7.

[f. 198rA] Come, let us rejoice in the Lord, Who shattered the dominion of death and enlightened the human race, crying aloud with the bodiless: O our Creator and Savior, glory to Thee!

Thou didst endure crucifixion and burial for our sake, O Savior, and by death, as God, Thou didst put death to death; therefore we worship Thy third-day Resurrection: O Lord, glory to Thee!

Beholding the Resurrection of the Creator, the Apostles were astonished, singing the angelic praise: this is the glory of the Church, this is the richness of the Kingdom! O Thou Who didst suffer for our sake: O Lord, glory to Thee!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

Having ineffably been born of Thee, O all-pure Virgin Birth-giver of God, Christ our God is truly the pre-eternal Son of God, and having become man, as the Son He is consubstantial; and on the one hand, having become man for our sake that He might save each nature by Himself: on the one hand shining forth with miracles, and on the other enduring passions; therefore being one [f. 198rB] and the same, He dies as man and rises again as God; Him do Thou entreat, O pure one who knewest not wedlock, that our souls may be saved!

At the Aposticha, Sticheron

Resurrection. Tone 7.

Having risen from the tomb, O Savior of the world, Thou didst raise up man with Thy flesh: O Lord, glory to Thee!

Other Stichera of the Forefathers and Theotokia. Tone 7. Verse:

Virgins shall be brought after her unto the King, her companions shall be brought unto Thee.

With all hymns let us cry aloud with the Angels unto the Birth-giver of God, for Thou didst bear the Savior of the world; and after birth-giving Thou didst remain a Virgin again, and didst deliver the world from delusion by Thy birth-giving, and gavest unto us unfailing food, nourishing with milk the Liberator of our souls!

*Verse: Hear, O daughter, and see, and incline thine ear.*

O spiritual Bride of God, heal the passions of my soul and calm them, that I may glorify[^276] [f. 198vA] Thee, O Birth-giver of God; and bury the multitude of my transgressions in great measure, and drive away the darkness of my passions!

*Verse: I will remember thy name in every generation and generation.*

Traversing the abyss of voluptuousness, I am drowned, O Maiden, and naked do I flee unto Thy protection!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

Grant me time for repentance, O pure one, and deliverance from transgressions, and rescue me from future torments!

[Woodcut engraving of the Golgotha Crucifixion: King of Glory, INRI, IC XC, NIKA, MLRB (The Place of the Skull hath become Paradise)]

[f. 199rA] ON SATURDAY EVENING AT GREAT VESPERS.

Resurrection Stichera. Tone 7.

Composition of John of Damascus.

[f. 199rA] Come, let us rejoice in the Lord, Who shattered the dominion of death and enlightened the human race, crying aloud with the bodiless: O our Creator and Savior, glory to Thee!

Thou didst endure crucifixion and burial for our sake, O Savior, and by death, as God, Thou didst put death to death; therefore we worship Thy third-day Resurrection: O Lord, glory to Thee!

Beholding the Resurrection of the Creator, the Apostles were astonished, singing the angelic praise: this is the glory of the Church, this is the richness of the Kingdom! O Thou Who didst suffer for our sake: O Lord, glory to Thee!

Other Stichera, Anatolian.

Same Tone.

Though Thou wast seized by lawless men, O Christ, yet Thou art my God, and I am not ashamed; Thou wast struck upon the shoulders, and I deny Thee not; Thou wast nailed upon the Cross, and [f. 199rB] I conceal it not: I boast in Thy Resurrection! For Thy death is my life, O almighty Lover of mankind: O Lord, glory to Thee!

Fulfilling the prophecy of David, O Christ, Thou didst reveal Thy majesty in Sion unto Thy Disciples, showing Thyself praised and ever glorified with the Father and the Holy Spirit: first indeed incorporeally as the Word, and afterward incarnate for our sake, put to death as man, and risen with power, as the Lover of mankind!

Thou didst descend into hades, O Christ, as Thou didst will; having despoiled death as God and Master, Thou didst rise again on the third day, raising up Adam with Thyself from the bonds of hades and corruption, who cries aloud and saith: Glory to Thy Resurrection, O only Lover of mankind!

Thou wast laid in the tomb as one sleeping, O Lord, and didst rise again on the third day, mighty in strength, raising up Adam with Thyself from mortal corruption, as the almighty God!...[^277]

[f. 199vA] Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

In truth Thou wast known as Mother above nature, O Birth-giver of God, yet didst remain a Virgin above word and understanding, and the tongue cannot recount the wonder of Thy birth-giving; for Thy conception being most glorious, O pure one, the manner of Thy birth-giving is incomprehensible: for where God wills, the order of nature is overcome! Therefore, knowing Thee all as the Mother of God, we fervently pray Thee to entreat that our souls may be saved!

At the Aposticha, Stichera

Resurrection. Tone 7.

Having risen from the tomb, O Savior of the world, Thou didst raise up man with Thy flesh: O Lord, glory to Thee!

Other Stichera in Alphabetical Order.

*Verse: The Lord is King, He is robed in majesty.*

Come, let us worship Him Who rose from the dead and enlightened all things; for by His third-day Resurrection He hath delivered us from the tyranny of hades, and granted us life and great mercy!

*Verse: For He hath established the world, so that it cannot be moved.*

Having descended into hades, O Christ, Thou didst despoil death, and having risen on the third day, Thou didst raise us up with Thyself, who cry aloud: Glory to Thy Resurrection, O only Lover of mankind!

*Verse: Holiness becomes Thine house, O Lord, unto length of days.*

Terrible wast Thou shown forth, O Lord, lying in the tomb as one sleeping; and having risen on the third day as mighty, Thou didst raise up Adam with Thyself, who glorifies [f. 199vB] Thy versatile resurrection, O Lord, Lover of mankind!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

Fleeing unto Thy protection, O Birth-giver of God, all we earthborn cry aloud unto Thee: O Birth-giver of God, our hope, deliver us from immeasurable transgressions, and save our souls!

Troparion. Tone 7.

Thou didst shatter death by Thy Cross, Thou didst open Paradise to the Thief; Thou didst transform the lamentation of the Myrrh-bearers, and commandedst Thine Apostles to proclaim that Thou hast risen, O Christ God, granting great mercy unto the world!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

As the treasury of our Resurrection, lead up from the pit and depth of transgressions those who hope in Thee, O all-hymned one; for Thou hast saved those guilty of sin, having given birth unto our Salvation: Who before birth-giving wast a Virgin, and in birth-giving a Virgin, and after birth-giving still a Virgin!

## SUNDAY MIDNIGHT OFFICE (TONE 7)

ON SUNDAY AT THE MIDNIGHT OFFICE

Canon to the Holy and Life-Originating

TRINITY.

Composition of Metrophanes.

Ode 1. Tone 7. Heirmos:

By Thy nod upon earth is fashioned the multitude of intellectual beings, and by material order a choir unto the praise of the thrice-radiant one Godhead of all, to chant a song of victory unto Thee!

Bestowing thanksgiving, that Thou mightest show forth the exceeding abundance of Thy goodness, Thou didst fashion man, O unsearchable Trinity, solely as the distinct image of Thine originate, sovereign Lordship of [f. 200rA] the unoriginate Mind, having begotten the co-eternal Word, and glorifying the Spirit with the unoriginate Persons! Account us worthy to worship the one God, united in essence and co-subsistent!

Theotokion:

Thou didst appear unto Moses at the bush, O Word of God, as a flame of fire, yet not burning it, prefiguring Thine Incarnation from the Virgin, whereby Thou didst refashion mankind!

Ode 3. Heirmos:

In the beginning by Thine almighty nod:

Hymning Thee, O Master, as singly-woven, tri-hypostatic, and ageless: we ask deliverance from sins and temptations, O undefiled God, that Thou mayest not overlook those who glorify Thy goodness with faith!

A Branch budded forth from the Father as from an unoriginate root, God the Word, and a Kingdom equal in majesty with the co-equal and divine Spirit; and therefore we faithful, in Trinity of Persons, glorify the one Dominion!

Equally glorious, co-enthroned, and tri-subsistent nature, indivisibly divided: we all, the faithful, praise the one Principle, the Trinity; worshipping, we ask forgiveness of transgressions!

Unchangeably wast Thou likened unto men, O pre-eternal Word of God; and the pure Maiden passed through as Thou didst will; and unto all hast Thou shown forth the tri-hypostatic Godhead, single in essence, in unchangeable Hypostases!

[f. 200rB] After Ode 3, Sessional Hymn:

Have mercy, O Holy Trinity, upon Thy servants who have sinned, and receive those who repent before Thee, O compassionate One, and account them worthy of forgiveness!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

Comfort our souls that are afflicted by sin, O all-holy Birth-giver of God, and deliver from transgressions those who hymn Thee, O Bride of God!

Ode 4. Heirmos:

Not leaving the Father's bosom:

O all-sustaining, thrice-radiant Unity, God-originating and saving unto all: preserve Thy chanters now, and save them from sorrow, passions, and great affliction!

With unutterable sayings of all the incomprehensible, tri-hypostatic Godhead, we hymn Thine unsearchable power, O Lord, Lover of mankind, and supremely glorify Thy might!

On earth as in heaven with the bodiless choirs, O Unity in Trinity, we divide Thee indivisibly, and faithfully glorify Thee as the Cause that brings forth all qualities!

Not departing from the honor of glory, Thou didst willingly descend unto our lowliness; the transcendent One became incarnate, and raised us up unto divine glory, as Thou art merciful!

Ode 5. Heirmos:

A night unillumined unto the unbelieving:

O God-originating Nature, Trinity in qualities and Unity in essence: establish us insatiably in Thy love unto Thy glory!

Mind, Word, and Spirit: one God-originating Nature[^278] [f. 200vA] the deliverer from temptations and all sorrows!

Theotokion:

Being formed into human nature from the Holy Virgin, O Word of God, Thou didst teach us to hymn the Trinity in Unity, co-fashioned and co-enthroned!

Ode 6. Heirmos:

Sailing in the surge:

The equally-glorious dominion and single-originating Godhead, existing in three Persons, do we unchangeably glorify one with another, having distinction only in the hypostatic property of each!

The intellectual ranks of angelic beauties praise the three-personed Godhead, and we also with clay lips, as the Creator of all, chant unto the One and faithfully glorify Him!

In an incomprehensible manner, the Word begotten of the Sun, the Father, another Sun before the ages, shone forth at the last from the Virgin; and being One co-enthroned in three Persons, He proclaimed the unsearchable God!

Sessional Hymn. Tone 7.

*Podoben: "The island of fire" (О҆гня̀ ѡ҆стро́въ):*

Consubstantial Trinity, tri-subsistent Unity: have mercy upon those whom Thou didst create, O immortal One, consuming the wickedness of our souls and enlightening the hearts of those who hymn Thy compassion: O Christ, glory to Thee!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

More holy and more fiery than the flame is the grace of Thy mercy, O Sovereign Lady, rescuing perishing men and enlightening the pious...

[f. 200vB] Ode 7. Heirmos:

He Who cast into the fiery furnace:

Ever shining with radiant splendors, O tri-hypostatic Unity, inaccessible and transcendent: save those who piously believe in Thee, O Master, and who worship Thee; who, serving God, submit to Thy majestic glory: Thee, the One in three Persons, the only God of our fathers, with clay lips and with the songs of immaterial ranks, O Holy Trinity, do we hymn who are united in the One, crying aloud: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers!

Having created Adam from the dust, do Thou renew him again, and deify his corruption unto Thy love for mankind, as he cries aloud unto Thee: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers!

Ode 8. Heirmos:

Unburned by fire in Sinai:

Account the hearts of Thy chanters worthy to be illumined with the light-bearing rays of the thrice-radiant Sun, and now to behold Thy beauty, O Unity in Trinity, as it is ever possible for man, unto all who piously hymn Thy majesty with warmth and glorious praise!

Thou hast a mighty dominion, O Trinity, a single Lordship without beginning, and Thou rulest over heaven and earth; therefore, having ever inclined in love of mercy unto all, preserve him that chants: All ye works of the Lord, bless ye the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto the ages!

Make me a partaker of Thy thrice-radiant brightness, O Lover of mankind, and join me unto the common hosts, and show forth invisible beauties [f. 201rA] and manifest a spiritual understanding in the flesh, O Master, my single-originating God and Lord of glory, that I may warmly hymn Thee unto the ages!

Theotokion:

The God-originating Light that shone forth from Thy womb, O all-pure Mother of God, illumined all the world with light surpassing the sun, and showed forth the earth as another heaven, singing: All ye works of the Lord, bless ye the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto the ages!

Ode 9. Heirmos:

Thee, the Mother of God above mind and nature:

Angels and children praise Thee worthily, Whom the Seraphim unceasingly hymn; unable in our clay garment to praise Thee as man, yet united in dominion, we chant: and we magnify God Who loves mankind!

Deliver from bodily diseases and the darkening of the soul Thy faithful singers, O single and indivisible Trinity; and by Thine uninjured protection account them worthy to escape the affliction of worldly temptations, O equally-honored, God-originating, thrice-radiant One, almighty dominion, ineffable beauty, by the endowment of divine goodness, granting unto Thy servants remission of transgressions and deliverance from temptations and evils!

Theotokion:

[Having assumed mind, spirit, and flesh, Thy pre-eternal Son became man; therefore, Thee who didst give birth unto God the Word do we unceasingly magnify!]

## SUNDAY MATINS (TONE 7)

[f. 201rB] AT MATINS, AFTER "GOD IS THE LORD":

God is the Lord and hath appeared unto us: In Tone 7. And we say the Resurrection Troparion: Thou didst shatter death by Thy Cross: twice. Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion: As the treasury of our Resurrection: the same. The customary stichology of the Psalter.

After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymns

Resurrection. Tone 7.

While the tomb was sealed, O Christ God, Thou Life didst shine forth from the grave; and while the doors were shut, Thou didst come unto the Disciples, O Resurrection of all, renewing an upright Spirit in us through them, according to Thy great mercy!

By Thy foretold burial having despoiled death, and by Thy life-bearing Resurrection [having raised up incorrupt man, O Christ God, as Thou art the Lover of mankind: Glory to Thee!]

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:
