[As] Thou hast tender mercy to help us, and beholdest the destitute on earth, [have mercy upon] us the helpless people, [O blessed] Birth-giver of God: [look upon fallen man, make Thy grace to be upon us for heavenly salvation,] that our souls may be saved!

[After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns]

[Resurrection. Tone 7.]

[...reclining...]

[...lying in the tomb...]

[...]...[^279]

[f. 201vA] When the women came unto the tomb, bearing myrrh with tears, while the soldiers were guarding the King of all, they said among themselves: "Who shall roll away the stone for us?" The Angel of the Great Council is risen, having trampled down death! O almighty Lord: Glory to Thee!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

Unceasingly pray unto Christ God, Who was crucified for us and is risen, and Who hath cast down the dominion of death, O Virgin Birth-giver of God, that He may save our souls!

Hypakoe, Tone 7:

Thou Who didst take upon Thyself our likeness and endure crucifixion in the flesh: save me by Thy Resurrection, O Christ God, for Thou art the Lover of mankind!

Degrees, Tone 7.

Antiphon 1:

Having turned back the captivity of Sion from delusion: do Thou also make me alive, O Savior, delivering me from slavish passions!

They that sow in the south with tears of fasting sorrows: shall reap joyous sheaves that ever nourish life!

Glory: Now and ever:

Unto the Holy Spirit belongs the fountain of divine treasures; from Him proceed wisdom, understanding, and fear: unto Him be praise, glory, honor, and dominion!

Antiphon 2:

Except the Lord build the house of the soul, in vain do we labor; for from Him alone do well-pleasing works [f. 201vB] proceed; for before all things is the dominion of God over all, without Whom nothing is reconciled or given life unto all.

Unto the Holy Spirit, the fruit of the womb is spiritually given as an inheritance, being fatherly adopted unto God.

Antiphon 3:

They that fear the Lord, having found the path of life, are now and ever blessed with incorruptible glory!

Round about thy table, beholding thy children like shoots, rejoice and be glad, bringing them unto Christ, the Chief of pastors!

Glory: Now and ever:

By the Holy Spirit is the depth of gifts, the richness of glory, and great profundity; for He is equally glorified with the Father and the Son, and equally worshipped!

Prokeimenon, Tone 7 (Psalm 9:33):

Arise, O Lord my God, let Thy hand be lifted up; forget not Thy poor unto the end!

Verse (Psalm 9:2): I will give praise unto Thee, O Lord, with my whole heart; I will tell of all Thy wonders!

Let every breath praise the Lord: The Resurrection Gospel. And the rest in order.

Resurrection Canon.

Ode 1. Tone 7. Heirmos:

By Thy nod upon the earth, the image of the watery nature, which formerly flowed easily, was transformed, O Lord; therefore Israel, passing through dry-shod, chants unto Thee a song of victory!

Troparia:

That which was condemned of old by Thy nod, having fallen into slavery among the daughters of Adam through righteous death: Thou didst loose, O Lord and Lover of mankind, by Thy Resurrection, having raised up human nature without condemnation, chanting unto Thee a song of victory!

[Having slain the adversary beast, O Savior, Thou didst tear asunder the waves of death...]

[f. 202rA] ...Thou didst tear asunder the billows of death, O Savior, rising on the third day!

Theotokion:

The pangs of our Fore-mother Eve were loosed, for having escaped travail, Thou didst give birth without knowing man; therefore, knowing Thee as the Birth-giver of God, O all-pure one, all we glorify Thee!

Another Canon of the Cross and Resurrection.

Ode 1. Tone 7. Heirmos:

He covered Pharaoh in the deep:

On the Cross, the Savior poured forth life-bearing streams unto us from a fountain, even from His pierced side; therefore we cry aloud unto Him, for He is glorified!

Having dwelt in the tomb and risen on the third day, O Christ, Thou didst bestow incorruptible praise upon mortals; therefore we chant unto Him, for He is glorified!

Theotokion:

The order of nature was renewed in Thy childbearing, for Thou didst purely bring forth the Creator of the world; therefore we all cry unto Thee: Rejoice!

Another Canon to the Most Holy Theotokos.

*Tone 7. Heirmos: By Thy nod upon earth is fashioned the...*

O Virgin who didst bear the abyss of compassions: illumine my soul with light-bearing rays, that I may worthily hymn the abyss of Thy wonders, O all-pure one!

Wounded by the arrow of sin, the Word, beholding us, had compassion as Benefactor; therefore He ineffably united Himself unto us, taking flesh upon Himself.

The company of mortals was taken captive and made dead by death, O Master of all; therefore, O Savior, Thou didst strike down the curse by Thy death when Thou didst arise!

Resurrection Canon.

Ode 3. Heirmos:

In the beginning, by Thy Word [f. 202rB] established by Thy Word, O Lord and Savior, and by the all-effective and Divine Spirit all their power was made firm: establish me upon the immovable rock of Thy confession!

Ascending upon the Tree, Thou didst heal the suffering race, O compassionate Savior, and enduring wounds, Thou didst become the Mediator of reconciliation and salvation unto the faithful, whereby through Thy mercy we all were reconciled unto Thy Father!

Thou didst rescue me from the wound, O Christ, who was slain by the venomous bites of the serpent, and Thou didst show forth light unto me who lay in darkness and corruption of old; for descending into hades through the Cross, Thou didst raise me up with Thyself!

Theotokion:

By the prayers of Thine all-pure Mother, grant peace unto the world, O Savior, and grant unto our rulers victory over opposing enemies, and account worthy of Thine ineffable glory those who glorify Thee!

Another [Canon]. Heirmos:

The power of the Disciples was struck with awe, O Christ:

The captive weapon was dyed red with blood, and the spear that pierced Thy side was held fast lawfully when blood and water were poured forth upon the Tree at Thy Crucifixion!

O Savior, Thou didst lead the Thief into Paradise, and breaking down the gates of hades, he rejoices, having received remission of sins through Thee!

Theotokion:

[O all-pure Virgin, who remained unconsumed by the divine flame: pray that our souls may be saved!]

Another [Canon to the Theotokos]. Heirmos: He hath helped His servant:

[^280] [f. 202vA] Whom Thou didst bear as Lord! Having in the flesh given birth unto Him from a virginal womb, O pure one: through Thy maternal intercessions grant unto Thy servants that which is well-pleasing, for Thee alone do we know as a compassionate refuge unto God!

Resurrection Canon.

Ode 4. Heirmos:

[The Prophet Habakkuk, having perceived the divine and unsearchable counsel of Thine incarnation, O Christ, cried aloud: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!]

Troparia:

The serpent creeping forth from Eden, deceiving me with the desire for deification, cast me down unto the earth; but He Who is by nature merciful and compassionate, having pity on our noble dignity, ascended upon Thy Tree and became like unto me!

Theotokion:

O Virgin Mother, blessed is the fruit of Thy womb, for as Birth-giver of God Thou art the joy of all; for Thou didst give birth unto Joy for the whole world and vision unto those at the ends of the earth, dispelling the sorrow of sin, O Bride of God!

Eternal life, the light of the knowledge of God, angelic joy and peace didst Thou bear unto us, O Virgin, destroying the ancient warfare against the Father and God, stilling the enmity of all through the confession of grace!

Canon of the Cross and Resurrection.

Ode 4. Heirmos:

Without leaving the Father's bosom and having descended unto earth, O Christ God: I heard the mystery of Thy dispensation, and I glorified Thee, the only Lover of mankind!

Troparia:

Before the tribunal of the unjust judges, Thou, the Judge of all, didst stand as one condemned and guilty, and the Cross was prepared for Thee Who didst fashion man, O God, and Who judgest the whole earth in righteousness

Theotokion:

As truly the Mother of God, pray Thou unto Thy Creator and Son to guide me unto the harbor of salvation, O all-immaculate one, according to His glorious will!

Another Canon to the Theotokos.

Ode 4. Heirmos: Beholding the Prophet:

Knowing no sin, Thou didst become for its sake that which Thou wast not, O Lord, receiving that which was alien, that Thou mightest save the world and extinguish the deceitful tyrant!

Thou wast lifted up upon the Cross, and didst loose the sin of fallen Adam; therefore have I heard of Thy power, that Thou didst come in Thy goodness to save all!

From the all-pure mountain, the Virgin, having come forth, Thou wast enrolled with servants, delivering all from tyranny, ruling unto ages; therefore we glorify Her who gave Thee birth!

Another Canon. Same Heirmos: Without leaving the Father's bosom:

Held fast by corruption, human nature was rescued by God Who existed before the creation of all; in the flesh, O all-pure one, He hastened to save and enlighten the people!

Thou didst bear God unto men, O pure one, incarnate of Thy pure blood, delivering from grievous transgressions those who praise and honor Thee with love, O Virgin Mother!

In an undivided manner the divine Nature was truly united in Thy flesh, in the ineffable mystery of Thy childbearing, O most blessed one!

Resurrection Canon.

Ode 5. Heirmos:

Night is without light unto the unbelieving, O Christ, but unto the faithful it is illumination in the sweetness [f. 203rA] of Thy words; therefore I rise early unto Thee, and hymn Thy Divinity!

Troparia:

For the price of a servant wast Thou sold, O Christ, and enduring a blow upon the cheek, Thou didst procure freedom for those who chant: I rise early unto Thee, and hymn Thy Divinity!

By Thy divine power, O Christ, through the weakness of the flesh Thou didst cast down the strong one, and by Thy Resurrection, O Savior, Thou didst show me forth as conqueror of death!

Theotokion:

Thou didst bear God incarnate, O pure Mother, being truly hymned in a manner befitting God, since Thou knewest not man, but didst bring forth from the Holy Spirit!

Canon of the Cross and Resurrection.

Ode 5. Heirmos: Entreat Him today:

When Thou wast numbered with the lawless, being lifted up upon Golgotha, the luminaries were darkened, the earth was shaken, and the veil of the temple was rent in twain, foreshadowing the downfall of the Jews!

Thee Who didst shatter the power of the tyrant by the might of Thine unsearchable Godhead, and didst raise up the dead by Thy Resurrection, do we glorify with hymns!

Theotokion:

O all-hymned Birth-giver of God, Mother of the King and God: unto those who ever praise Thee with faith and love, send down through Thine intercessions estrangement from transgressions!

Another Canon to the Theotokos.

*Ode 5. Heirmos: Night is without light unto the unbelieving, O...*

Jacob beheld splendors confirmed by the oath, prefiguring Thee who art unceasingly glorious; for through Thee, O all-pure Sovereign Lady, God united Himself unto men!

[f. 203rB] Having found eternal redemption through Thee, O Virgin, we earnestly cry aloud: Rejoice, O Bride of God! And rejoicing in Thy Son, O all-pure one, we magnify Thee with hymns!

Finding Thee alone as a lily in the midst of thorns, O Virgin, shining with the brightness of purity and with the light of virginity, the all-hymned Bridegroom brought Thee forth!

Resurrection Canon.

Ode 6. Heirmos:

Sailing in the surge of the billows of life, and overwhelmed with the ship by sins, and cast before the soul-destroying beast, as Jonah, O Christ, I cry aloud unto Thee: Lead me up from the death-bearing depths!

Troparia:

The souls of the righteous imprisoned in hades remembered Thee, and prayed for salvation from Thee, which Thou, O Christ, didst bestow through the Cross upon those in the underworld, having come as the compassionate One!

When Thine animate and unbuilt temple was destroyed by sufferings, the Apostolic choir of old looked thereon, but worshipping beyond all hope, they proclaimed Thy power!

First receiving the joy of the glad tidings at Thy rising, O Giver of life, the Myrrh-bearing women rejoiced, proclaiming unto the Apostles: The decree of the curse is loosed, for Christ is risen from the dead!

Theotokion:

Who among men can declare the likeness of Thine ineffable childbearing, O all-immaculate Virgin Bride of God? For God the pre-eternal Word united Himself unto me, having become flesh from Thee![^281] [f. 203vA] Canon of the Cross and Resurrection.

Ode 6. Heirmos:

I cried aloud unto the Lord in my affliction:

Being crucified, O Master, Thou didst shake the whole earth, and as the good One didst heal its grievous contortions!

Death was destroyed and hades was despoiled, O Christ, when Thou didst arise, preparing a way for man through Thy Resurrection!

Theotokion:

O all-pure Sovereign Lady, sure hope of those who hymn Thee with love: preserve us as truly the Birth-giver of God!

Another Canon to the Theotokos.

*Ode 6. Heirmos: Sailing in the surge of the billows of...*

The types of the Law and the prophetic utterances clearly foretold Thee who wast to give birth unto the Benefactor of all creation, O pure one, Who in manifold portions and in diverse manners showed goodness unto those who faithfully magnify Thee!

Adam the first-fashioned, estranged of old by the counsel of the manslayer from the enjoyment of divine food, hast Thou, O Bride of God, led up again, having given birth unto Him Who delivered us from transgression!

He Who by divine counsel and creative power brought all things into being out of nothingness came forth from Thy womb, O pure one, and appeared unto those in the darkness of death, illuminating them with God-originating rays!

Kontakion, Tone 7:

No longer can the dominion of death hold mortals fast, for Christ descended, shattering and destroying its powers! Hades is bound, and the Prophets rejoice with one accord, saying: The Savior hath appeared unto those in faith; come forth, ye faithful, unto the Resurrection!

Ikos:

The underworld below trembled [f. 203vB] today, hades and death were afraid of the One of the Trinity; the earth was shaken, and the gatekeepers of hades, beholding Thee, were terrified! And all creation, rejoicing with the Prophets, chants unto Thee a song of victory, unto our Redeemer and God, Who hath now destroyed the power of death: let us shout aloud and cry unto Adam and unto those born of Adam: The Tree hath brought him back again; come forth, ye faithful, unto the Resurrection!

Resurrection Canon.

Ode 7. Heirmos:

The Children of old showed the fiery furnace to be dew-bearing, praising the one God and saying: O God of our fathers, supremely exalted and supremely glorified!

Troparia:

By a tree was Adam put to death, having willingly committed disobedience; but by the obedience of Christ is he made alive again, for for my sake the Son of God, the supremely glorified, is crucified!

All creation hymns Thee Who didst arise from the tomb, O Christ; for Thou didst blossom forth as life unto those in hades, resurrection unto the dead, and the supremely glorified Light unto those in darkness!

Theotokion:

Rejoice, O daughter of corrupt Adam! Rejoice, O only Bride of God! Rejoice, through whom corruption was driven away, for Thou didst give birth unto God: pray unto Him, O pure one, that we all may be saved!

Canon of the Cross and Resurrection.

Ode 7. Heirmos: He Who in the beginning:

Having blunted the sting of sin upon the Tree of the Cross, and torn asunder the handwriting of Adam's transgression by the spear in Thy side: [f. 204rA] Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers!

Being pierced in Thy side, Thou didst cleanse the earth, which was defiled with the blood of idols, by the sprinkling of Thy divine blood: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers!

Triadicon:

In an orthodox manner we theologically praise the indivisible Nature: God the Father without beginning, and the equally good Word and Spirit, crying: Blessed art Thou, O consubstantial Trinity!

Another Canon to the Theotokos.

*Ode 7. Heirmos: The Children of old showed the fiery furnace...*

Comforted by the proclamation, Thine unapproachable Creator and Lord magnified Thee, O Virgin: O God of our fathers, supremely exalted and supremely glorified!

Being purified of old, O Maiden, Isaiah received the coal, beholding in a figure and symbolic sign Thy childbearing: O God of our fathers, supremely exalted and supremely glorified!

Beholding all the symbolic figures of Thy divine childbearing, the divine Prophets joyfully cried aloud, chanting: O God of our fathers, supremely exalted and blessed art Thou!

Resurrection Canon.

Ode 8. Heirmos:

The Bush on Sinai that held communion with the fire without being burned revealed God unto Moses, who was slow of speech and stammering; and the zeal of God showed forth the three Children unburned in the fire, as chanters singing: All ye works of the Lord, bless ye the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto the ages!

Troparia:

The all-pure spiritual Lamb, slain for the world, caused the sacrifices offered according to the Law to cease, purifying these without transgressions as God, unto those who [f. 204rB] ever cry aloud: All ye works of the Lord, bless ye the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto the ages!

Our flesh, which before the Passion was not incorruptible, being assumed by the Creator, was made untouchable by corruption after the Passion and Resurrection, renewing those who were mortal: All ye works of the Lord, bless ye the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto the ages!

Theotokion:

Thy purity and all-immaculate state, O Virgin, cleansed that which was defiled and abominable in the world, and became the cause of our reconciliation unto God, O all-pure one; therefore all the works of the Lord hymn Thee, O Birth-giver of God, unto the ages!

Canon of the Cross and Resurrection.

Ode 8. Heirmos: The only unoriginate King:

Him Who willingly endured passions and was nailed unto the Cross by His own desire, and destroyed the power of hades: Praise Him, ye priests, and supremely exalt Him, ye people, unto the ages!

Him Who abolished the dominion of death and arose in harmony from the tomb, and saved the human race: Praise Him, ye priests, and supremely exalt Him, ye people, unto the ages!

Triadicon:

The only compassionate, pre-eternal Word, Who at the last was born of the Virgin and saved the human race: Praise Him, ye priests, and supremely exalt Him, ye people, unto the ages!

Another Canon to the Theotokos.

Ode 8. Heirmos: Unburned by fire:

By the brightness of Thy childbearing, O Birth-giver of God, Thou didst wondrously enlighten the universe, carrying in Thine arms the existing God, Who illuminates those who faithfully cry: All ye works of the Lord, bless ye the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto the ages!

Piously do we hymn [^282] [f. 204vA] Thy womb: which ineffably contained God Who was incarnate, Who granted unto all the faithful the illumination of the knowledge of God, who unceasingly cry aloud: All ye works of the Lord, bless ye the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto the ages!

With the rays of Thy light, make bright those who hymn Thee, O Virgin Mother who didst bear the Light; for as the dwelling of the Word of Light, Thou dost enlighten the luminary for those who ever cry aloud: All ye works of the Lord, bless ye the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto the ages!

Resurrection Canon.

Ode 9. Heirmos:

Without knowing corruption Thou didst bring forth, lending flesh unto the all-wise Word, O Mother unwedded, Virgin Birth-giver of God, receptacle of the Uncontainable, dwelling-place of Thine uncircumscribed Creator: Thee do we magnify!

Troparia:

Let all who ascribe suffering unto the Godhead be put to shame, holding the same error; for the Lord of glory was crucified in the flesh, but according to His divine Nature He was not crucified, as we magnify the One in two natures!

Ye who disbelieve the resurrection of bodies, go unto the tomb of Christ and learn: that the flesh of the Giver of life was put to death and rose again, as a pledge of the victorious resurrection, which hope we possess!

Triadicon:

We divide not the Trinity into three essences, nor do we reduce the Persons unto a single unit, but honoring the Godhead, we unite Them without confusion: rejecting those who dare to blend Them, Whom we magnify!

[f. 204vB] Canon of the Cross and Resurrection.

Ode 9. Heirmos: Mother of God and Virgin in childbearing:

Beholding in Christ the passions of the flesh and the might of the Godhead, let those who think of a single composite nature be put to shame; for as man He died, but as Creator of all He is risen!

Myrrh unto the dead, but hymns unto the Living; tears unto the dying, but faith unto Life: such was the song the women brought, who cried aloud as heralds of the Resurrection, blessing His rising!

Light of Light, shining forth from the Father, the splendor of His glory shone timelessly; and crying aloud unto Christ that He should dwell among mortals in darkness, He drove away the darkness: Whom we faithful unceasingly magnify!

Another Canon to the Theotokos.

Same Heirmos:

Truly hast Thou appeared unto us as the mediatress of eternal joy and gladness, O Virgin Maiden, having given birth unto the Redeemer, Whom those who honor Him in truth and by the Divine Spirit confess as God the Deliverer!

David Thy forefather, O all-pure one, calls Thee the Ark of divine holiness, who contained beyond nature God Who sits in the bosom of the Father, Whom we faithful unceasingly magnify!

Truly art Thou higher than all creation, O pure one, for Thou didst bear bodily unto us the Designer of all; therefore as Mother of the only Master, Thou dost heal the damage that befell all...

[f. 205rA] AT THE PRAISES: STICHERA OF THE RESURRECTION. TONE 7.

Christ is risen from the dead: He hath broken the bonds of death; proclaim the glad tidings of great joy, O earth: hymn the glory of God, O ye heavens!

Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ, let us worship the Holy Lord Jesus, the only sinless One!

Ceasing not to worship the Resurrection of Christ, for He hath saved us from our iniquities: Holy is the Lord Jesus, Who revealed His Resurrection in the world!

What shall we render unto the Lord for all that He hath accomplished for us? For our sake God appeared among men; for corrupt nature the Word became flesh and dwelt among us! Unto the ungrateful a Benefactor; unto captives a Liberator; unto those sitting in darkness the Sun of righteousness; upon the Cross the impassible One; in hades Light; in death Life; the Resurrection for the sake of the fallen: unto Whom let us cry aloud: O our God, glory to Thee!

Other Stichera (Anatolian). Same Tone:

The gates of hades hast Thou shattered, O Lord, and abolished the dominion of death by Thy mighty power, and didst raise up with Thyself the dead that had slept from the ages in darkness, by Thy divine and glorious Resurrection, as King of all and almighty God!

Come, let us rejoice in the Lord, and let us be glad in His Resurrection, for He hath delivered the dead from the indissoluble bonds of hades [f. 205rB] and as God He granted eternal life and great mercy unto the world!

Verse (Psalm 9:33): Arise, O Lord my God, let Thy hand be lifted up; forget not Thy poor unto the end!

Shining with brightness, the Angel sat upon the stone of Thy life-receiving tomb, and proclaimed glad tidings unto the Myrrh-bearing women, saying: The Lord is risen, as He said unto you before; proclaim unto His Disciples that He goes before you into Galilee, and bestows eternal life and great mercy upon the world!

Verse (Psalm 9:2): I will give praise unto Thee, O Lord, with my whole heart; I will tell of all Thy wonders!

Why have ye set at naught the cornerstone, O lawless Jews? Lo, He is the One Whom God placed in Sion, Who brought forth water from the rock in the wilderness, and poured forth immortality for us from His side! He is the stone cut out without human hands from the mountain of Daniel: the Son of man coming upon the clouds of heaven unto the Ancient of Days, as Daniel said, and His Kingdom is everlasting!

The Matins Gospel. And thereafter spiritually, the Great Doxology, and the Dismissal.

AT THE LITURGY:

Beatitudes. Tone 7.

Fair and good for food was the fruit that brought death upon me; but Christ is the Tree of life, of which eating I die not, but cry aloud with the Thief: Remember me, O Lord, when Thou comest into Thy Kingdom!

Being lifted up upon the Cross, O compassionate One, Thou didst wipe away the handwriting of Adam's[^283] [f. 205vA] ancient sin, and didst save the whole human race from delusion; therefore we cry aloud unto Thee, O Benefactor and Lord: Remember us, O Lord, when Thou comest into Thy Kingdom!

Being laid as dead in the tomb, O Christ, the Life of all, Thou didst shatter the gates of death; and Thou didst arise in glory on the third day as the mighty One, and didst enlighten all who hymn Thee and worship Thy rising!

By Thy rising Thou art the Liberator of Adam, O Christ, the Giver of life, bestowing the ancient incorruption that was in Paradise; therefore I cry aloud with the Thief: Remember me, O Lord, when Thou comest into Thy Kingdom!

The Savior, having risen from the tomb on the third day, granted peace unto the Disciples, as He had said, and sent them forth with glad tidings, saying: Bring all men into My Kingdom!

The serpent poured forth venom into the ear of Eve of old [f. 205vB] but Christ upon the Tree of the Cross poured forth delight unto the world; therefore we cry aloud: Remember us, O Lord, in Thy Kingdom!

Glory: Triadicon:

Light is the Father, Light is the Son and Word, Light is the Holy Spirit, but one Light are the Three; for God is One in three Persons, one simple Nature, indivisible and unconfused, abiding eternally!

Now and ever: Theotokion:

Thou didst give birth bodily for our sake unto the Son and Word of God, as He alone knows, O Birth-giver of God; therefore, O Virgin Mother, being deified through Thee, we cry aloud unto Thee: Rejoice, O Hope of Christians!

## SUNDAY EVENING VESPERS (TONE 7)

ON SUNDAY EVENING, AT "LORD, I HAVE CRIED":

*Penitential Stichera. Tone 7.*

*Podoben: "Today Judas watches" (Дне́сь бди́тъ Ію́да):*

Lift up thine eye, O my soul, and look upon the dispensation and divine ordering of God! How He inclined the heavens and descended unto earth, that He might raise thee up from all the misery of passions, and set thee upon the rock of faith! O fearful wonder! Glory to Thy condescension, O Lover of mankind!

Look upon thine iniquitous deeds, O my soul, and consider how the earth bears thee! How the lightning bolt doth not consume thee! How wild beasts devour thee not! And how the unwaning Sun ever shines upon thee! Arise, repent, and cry aloud unto the Lord: I have sinned against Thee, I have sinned, have mercy upon me!

Having Thee as our hope, O almighty Lord, we pray Thee: deliver us from all perils and from the tempest of passions, that we may peacefully [f. 206rA] spend our life in peace, and reap eternity, finding Thee, O Master, well-pleased and merciful on the day of judgment!

*Other Stichera to the Bodiless Powers. Tone 7.*

*Podoben: "No longer are we forbidden" (Не ктомꙋ̀ возбране́ни есмы̀):*

By the vision of the illumination of the Trinity, do ye, O Archangels, enlighten those who hymn you in faith!

Shown forth as secondary lights by participation, do ye stand before the Primal Light, praying for the perfect!

With the shelter of your wings, preserve all the faithful from evil spirits, destroying their darkness!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

All we with the Angels cry aloud unto the Birth-giver of God in hymns: for Thou didst bear the Savior of the world, and after childbearing didst remain a Virgin again; and by Thy childbearing Thou didst deliver the world from delusion, and didst bestow ineffable food upon us, nourishing with milk the Liberator of our souls!

At the Aposticha, Penitential Stichera. Tone 7:

As the Prodigal Son I have come, O compassionate One; receive me falling down before Thee, as one of Thy hired servants, O God, and have mercy upon me!

As one falling among thieves and wounded, so have I fallen through many sins, and my soul is wounded: unto whom shall I, the guilty one, flee, save unto Thee, the compassionate Physician of souls? Pour out upon us, O God, Thy great mercy!

Glory to Thee, O Christ God, the boast of Apostles [f. 206rB] and the rejoicing of Martyrs, whose preaching was the Consubstantial Trinity!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

Crying unto Thee the "Rejoice" with the Angel, O Bride of God, we name Thee Bridal Chamber, Door, and Fiery Throne, the unhewn Mountain, and the Bush unburned!

ON MONDAY, AT MATINS:

After the 1st Kathisma, Penitential Sessional Hymns. Tone 7:

Possessing the medicine of repentance, O my soul, draw near weeping and crying with sighing: O Physician of souls and bodies, Lover of mankind, loose me from my many transgressions, number me with the Harlot, the Thief, and the Publican, and grant me, O God, forgiveness of mine iniquities, and save me!

O Lord and Lover of mankind, Who didst cleanse Peter's denial with tears and didst forgive the sins of the Publican through sighing: have mercy upon me!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

Higher art Thou than the heavenly hosts, for Thou wast shown to be the Divine Temple, O blessed Birth-giver of God, having given birth unto Christ, the Savior of our souls!

After the 2nd Kathisma, Penitential Sessional Hymns. Tone 7:

I have not emulated the repentance of the Publican, nor have I acquired the tears of the Harlot; for I am bewildered by blindness regarding such amendment: but by Thy compassions, O good One, save me, for Thou art the Lover of mankind!

The abyss of life overwhelms me[^284] [f. 206vA] O Lord, and the billows of mine iniquities submerge me: but stretch forth Thy hand unto me, as unto Peter, and save me!

Martyrs:

O Holy Martyrs, pray that forgiveness of our sins be granted unto us, and that we be delivered from expected perils and bitter death, we pray you!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

More honorable than the glorious Cherubim art Thou, O Most Holy Virgin; for they, unable to bear the Divine Power, cover their faces with wings as they perform their ministry; but Thou, visibly beholding the Incarnate Word, didst bear Him in Thine arms: Him do Thou unceasingly entreat for our souls!

*After the 3rd Kathisma, Penitential Sessional Hymns. Tone 7.*

*Podoben: "Fruit of thy womb" (Пло́дъ чре́ва):*

The tempest of diverse passions and of my sins drowns me in the depth of despair; but by the prayers of Thine Angels, O most merciful Jesus, save me as the Prodigal!

Prepare thyself, O my soul, for thy departure, facing the life to come without wavering! For neither wealth, nor strength, nor friends, nor princes shall avail there: but only the display of deeds and the love of God toward mankind!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

O immaculate Virgin Birth-giver of God: pray unto Thy Son together with the hosts on high, to grant us forgiveness of sins before our end, who faithfully glorify Thee!

PENITENTIAL CANON.

Composition of Joseph.

[f. 206vB] Ode 1. Tone 7. Heirmos:

Unto God Who aided Moses in Egypt to deliver Israel: unto Him alone let us chant, for He is glorified!

Troparia:

Having fallen into the deep of perils, I cry aloud unto Thee: stretch forth Thy hand unto me, O compassionate One, and save me as Thou didst Peter, O Lover of mankind!

Wash me who repent, O Christ, as Thou didst the Harlot, from my many transgressions, by the maternal mercy of Thy compassion, that in faith I may glorify Thee!

Martyrs:

O Christ, Who didst enlighten Thy Holy Martyrs to endure manifold torments: by their prayers deliver me from the darkening of passions!

Martyrs:

Being purified by the endurance of torments, the Holy Martyrs shone forth more brightly than the sun, putting the demonic band to shame!

Theotokion:

O all-hymned Virgin, protectress of the faithful and return unto God for those who sin: by Thine intercessions save me!

Another Canon to the Bodiless Powers.

Composition of Theophanes.

Ode 1. Tone 7. Heirmos: Unto Him Who shook Pharaoh:

Ineffable Christ, with Thy light illumine my mind, that I may be inspired to hymn Thine Angels, for Thou art almighty!

Possessing steadfast radiance proceeding from the God-originating Fountain, ye heavenly ranks honor Christ with hymns!

Theotokion:

Adorned with divine splendors, O pure one, the faithful, knowing Thee to be Mary, cry aloud unto Thee: Rejoice!

[f. 207rA] Ode 3. Heirmos:

My heart is established in the Lord, my horn is exalted in my God, my mouth is enlarged over mine enemies: I have rejoiced in Thy salvation!

Troparia:

Held fast by the night of unmeasured transgressions, illumine me with the light of repentance, O Giver of light and Lover of mankind, that I may glorify Thee, the Good One!

Shaking off all the difficult paths of life that cast me down into the abyss of pleasures, O Jesus, show unto me the divine paths of repentance!

Martyrs:

Having traversed their struggles with an unburdened spirit, the all-glorious Martyrs were accounted worthy of heavenly rewards, suffering for the ages!

Martyrs:

Having endured a multitude of afflictions, O victorious Passion-bearers, ye were accounted worthy of myriads of good things, being joined unto the myriads of bodiless powers!

Theotokion:

Having alone given birth unto the transcendent King, O Virgin: cast down the sin that dwells within me, and having compassion, save me!

Another Canon [to the Bodiless Powers].

Ode 3. Heirmos: Be established, O Church of Christ:

Being intercessors of divine boldness, ye angelic ranks cry aloud immaterially: Holy art Thou, O Lord, Who hast saved our souls!

By the law of love dispensing divine illuminations one to another, ye chant harmoniously unto Christ: Holy art Thou, O Lord, Who hast saved our souls!

Emulating the first splendors and secondary lights in godly living, the faithful chant with one accord unto Christ: Holy art Thou, O Lord, Who hast saved our souls!

[f. 207rB] Theotokion:

God, Who brought all things out of nothingness by His will, borrowed flesh from Thee, O Virgin: the Word becoming man in His compassion, as Lover of mankind!

Penitential Canon.

Ode 4. Heirmos:

Thy virtue, O Christ God, hath covered the heavens through the dispensation of Thine ineffable wisdom, O Lover of mankind!

Troparia:

O Thou Who desirest all men to be saved, O compassionate One: save me who have transgressed Thy commandments, O Word, and despise me not!

I have subjected myself unto irrational passions and become like the beasts, wretched that I am: O compassionate Son of God, have pity and save me!

Martyrs:

Burning with divine fire, ye consumed delusion, inflamed with the zeal of piety, O Martyrs!

Martyrs:

Ye appeared as a spiritual paradise, having in your midst the Tree of life, O blessed ones: Christ the Planter of all!

Theotokion:

As pure and full of divine grace, having bestowed grace upon my mind, completely free me from the darkness of ignorance!

Another Canon [to the Bodiless Powers].

Ode 4. Heirmos: I heard Thy report:

O angelic hosts standing before Christ as chosen ministers, entreat Him for the unyielding wounds of my soul!

The armies of the Bodiless Powers reverently surround Thy throne, O Master, clearly crying aloud: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

The angelic ranks were astonished, beholding Thee, O Christ, in the flesh upon earth, dwelling among mortal men!

Theotokion:

[^285] [f. 207vA] having ineffably given birth unto God in the flesh: pray Thou unto Him that we may be saved!

Penitential Canon.

Ode 5. Heirmos:

Rising early unto Thy glory and praise, O Christ, we unceasingly hymn the image of Thy Cross, which Thou hast given us as a weapon unto our aid!

Troparia:

In slothfulness have I spent my life, and I tremble before the unavoidable judgment seat whereon I, the wretched one, must be judged: have pity upon me, O Lord!

O Thou Who didst enlighten the blindness of the blind: open the eyes of my soul that are grievously darkened, to behold the light of Thy commandments!

Martyrs:

Confessing Christ with a steadfast mind, ye endured the torment of every affliction, O valiant sufferers: therefore ye are blessed!

Martyrs:

Having sailed across the sea of every contradiction of torments, ye reached the harbor of the Kingdom on high, filled with incorruptible peace, O Martyrs!

Theotokion:

God the Word, Who created all things by His will, ineffably took flesh beyond word: earnestly pray unto Him for all!

Another Canon [to the Bodiless Powers].

Ode 5. Heirmos: Rising early unto Thee:

With most holy and many-eyed mouths the Seraphim chant unto the supreme, unoriginate, and divine Principle, inflamed with immaterial splendors!

Covering themselves with most holy and all-radiant wings, not daring to gaze upon the Divine Splendor, the Cherubim spread forth the dwellings of the transcendent Godhead!

[f. 207vB] With divine understanding, the glorious Thrones, enjoying the fairest radiances, are shown forth exceedingly as beholders of ineffable things!

Theotokion:

The transcendent Mind was united unto human nature, O all-pure one, in Thine immaculate and all-pure womb, united unconfusedly and indivisibly according to hypostasis!

Penitential Canon.

Ode 6. Heirmos:

Jonah cried aloud from the belly of hades: Lead up my life from corruption! And we cry aloud unto Thee: O almighty Savior, have mercy upon us!

Troparia:

The abyss of transgressions hath encompassed me, and I have sunk into the depth of destruction: lead me up from corruption unto life, O Word, as of old Thou didst Jonah!

The storm of evil thoughts casts me down; guide me, O compassionate One, unto the harbor of true repentance, preserving my heart in peace!

Martyrs:

Protected by the shield of truth, the Holy Martyrs turned away the deceitful flatteries of tyrants, and were unwounded by the barbs of the enemy!

Martyrs:

Exalted by love toward God, hating the love of the world, the Martyrs appeared as friends unto the Creator of all!

Theotokion:

We hymn Thee, O all-pure Maiden, who didst bear the all-hymned Word, Whom all the heavenly hosts praise with unceasing voices!

Another Canon [to the Bodiless Powers].

Same Heirmos:

Youthfully shining with splendors in the palace of the Lord, and chanting His ineffable glory, the Dominions ever appear!

Longingly gazing upon the might of the supreme Power, the Divine Powers abide in strength, visibly prevailing!

[f. 208rA] Theotokion:

Having sprung from a royal tribe, O Virgin, Thou didst bear beyond nature and word the King of all, and didst truly remain a Virgin!

Penitential Canon.

Ode 7. Heirmos:

Thou didst bedew the burning furnace, O Savior, and didst save the Children who sang and said: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

Troparia:

Offer unto God the sacrifice of praise, O my soul! Hasten and repent while the festival of life endures, and the market of good works is open!

The mortal cutting-down draws near, O my soul: bring forth worthy fruits, lest like an unfruitful tree thou be cast into the fire of Gehenna, and weep without avail!

Martyrs:

Having extinguished the furnace of delusion with streams of blood, the Holy Martyrs cried aloud as the Children: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers!

Martyrs:

Ye were shown to be sons of light, O Martyrs, shining with fair light, and ye enlightened all that were in darkness, driving away the mist of delusion!

Theotokion:

The unburned Bush prefigured Thee, O pure one, for Thou didst bear uncontainable Fire, O Virgin: therefore I cry unto Thee: consume my material passions!

Another Canon [to the Bodiless Powers].

*Ode 7. Heirmos: The Children of old showed the fiery furnace...*

Unswervingly blessing, surrounding Thy throne in spiritual choirs, the angelic ranks cry aloud: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

The Princely Principalities earnestly encompass the one Principle immaterially [f. 208rB] encompassing Him with unceasing hymns, crying: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers!

Theotokion:

One Person in two natures, O Birth-giver of God, didst Thou seedlessly bear: Christ, the only Lover of mankind, Who accomplishes a fearful dispensation: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

Penitential Canon.

Ode 8. Heirmos:

Being made like unto the Children in the furnace, having received the dew of the Spirit, let us cry aloud in faith: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; hymn and supremely exalt Him unto the ages!

Troparia:

I received the Word as a shining lamp, but I, the wretched one, inclined unto irrational passions, and ever walked in evil darkness!

The judgment is near, as we know: make haste, O my soul, and despond not! Watch and cry aloud with vigilance: O compassionate Lover of mankind, save me!

Martyrs:

Inflamed with the divine flame, ye endured bitter suffering, and now ye enjoy the divine rewards of the Word, O Martyrs!

Martyrs:

Ye ascended unto the divine rest, having obtained the good things of piety, O all-praised Martyrs: therefore we worthily call you blessed!

Theotokion:

Human nature was loosed from the curse by Thy childbearing, O Virgin, for Thou didst give birth unto the All-blessed One Who blessedly adorns all unto the ages!

Another Canon [to the Bodiless Powers].

Ode 8. Heirmos: The only unoriginate King of glory:

Him Whom the heavenly hosts praise, and before Whom the ranks of Angels tremble: Praise Him[^286] [f. 208vA] ye priests, and supremely exalt Him, ye people, unto the ages!

Possessing all desire toward God and enjoying His radiances from on high, O Archangels: earnestly pray that forgiveness of sins may be granted unto us unto the ages!

O purest Minds, free from every alteration of material passion, O Angels: save all who praise Christ with love, blessing Him unto ages of ages!

Theotokion:

Receiving the unapproachable Light ineffably into Thy womb, O Virgin Birth-giver of God, Thou didst enlighten those held fast in the darkness of life, that they may piously glorify Christ Who ineffably came forth from Thee!

Penitential Canon.

Ode 9. Heirmos:

Thee Who art Mother beyond nature and Virgin according to nature, the only blessed one among women: in hymns, we the faithful magnify Thee as the Birth-giver of God!

Troparia:

Lo, the judgment draws near, and the deeds of condemnation terrify me: I tremble at all things; O righteous Judge, Christ God, condemn me not!

As the faithful Canaanite woman, I cry unto Thee: Have mercy upon me! And as Thou didst the bowed-down woman of old, make me upright, that I may walk straight in Thy paths, O Lover of mankind!

Martyrs:

Having stripped yourselves of the garments of malice, ye adorned yourselves with the clothing of martyrdom, O Passion-bearers, obtaining the garments of all glory!

Martyrs:

The divine land of the living, Sion the heavenly city, received the holy sufferers as the first-fruits of good things, adorned with the beauty of their struggles!

Theotokion:

With the light-giving rays of the Word Who shone forth from Thee [f. 208vB] O all-pure Virgin, illumine me who walk in the darkness of sins and passions!

Another Canon [to the Bodiless Powers].

Ode 9. Heirmos: O all-pure one, higher than the heavens:

Enjoying the splendors of the divine outpouring of light, all the angelic choirs unceasingly praise the supremely glorified God, and ever glorify and magnify Him!

Unceasingly entreating the Redeemer: O Cherubim and Seraphim, Powers, Authorities, Angels, Archangels, Principalities, Thrones, and Dominions: earnestly pray unto Christ!

Theotokion:

As the Mother having boldness now before Thy Son, O Birth-giver of God: deliver those who hymn Thee with love from grievous transgressions, diseases, and perils, that all we may ever magnify Thee!

At the Aposticha, Penitential Stichera. Tone 7:

As the barren fig tree, cut me not down, O Savior, sinner that I am; but grant me forgiveness for many years, watering my soul with tears of repentance, that I may bring forth the fruit of prayer unto Thee!

Being the Sun of righteousness, illumine the hearts of those who hymn Thee: O Lord, glory to Thee!

Martyrs:

Celebrating the memory of Thy Holy Passion-bearers, we chant unto Thee, crying aloud: O Lord, glory to Thee!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

Stills the tumult of our life by the prayers of the Birth-giver of God, unto us who cry unto Thee: O Merciful One, Lord, glory to Thee!

ON MONDAY:

Beatitudes. Tone 7:

Fair and good...

[f. 209rA] Fair and good for food was the fruit that brought death upon me; but Christ is the Tree of life, of which eating I die not, but cry aloud with the Thief: Remember me, O Lord, when Thou comest into Thy Kingdom!

As the faithful Canaanite woman, I cry unto Thee from my heart: grant me relief from the sorrows of my heart; have mercy upon me, O Savior, for Thou art good: for my soul is in peril through the great wiles of the enemy, and is ever tempest-tossed!

Cherubim and Seraphim and Thrones, Principalities and Powers together, Archangels and the Angelic hosts, Dominions and the councils of all-wise Authorities: all glorify Thee, O Benefactor and Lord!

Martyrs:

Raised up toward God, the holy sufferers utterly cast down the wicked arrogances of the enemy [f. 209rB] and appearing as conquerors, they dwell now in joy in the heavens, shining with incorruptible glory!

Glory: Triadicon:

Indivisible Trinity in Unity, one natural essence in three Persons: we worship Thee together with the hosts on high: O Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, one Godhead and one Power, one God, consubstantial Trinity!

Now and ever: Theotokion:

Defiled by worldly pleasures, I have fled unto Thee, the immaculate Virgin: deliver my all-immaculate soul from every blemish and transgression, that I may ever call Thee blessed!

## MONDAY EVENING VESPERS (FOR TUESDAY) (TONE 7)

ON MONDAY EVENING, AT "LORD, I HAVE CRIED":

*Penitential Stichera. Tone 7.*

*Podoben: "Today Judas watches" (Дне́сь бди́тъ Ію́да):*

O all-compassionate Master and God: by whatever judgments Thou knowest, grant me to come unto contrite feeling! Grant me to love Thee with all my soul! Grant me to be angry against the deeds of the enemy, and to do Thy will unto salvation! For Thou art our God, Who didst say: Ask, and ye shall receive!

Satan hath made me his mockery, an object of contempt unto men, a cause of weeping unto the righteous, of lamentation unto the Angels, a defilement unto the air, the earth, and the water: for I have defiled my body, and stained my soul and mind with irrational deeds, and have become an enemy of God! Woe is me, woe is me! O Lord, I have sinned against Thee, I have sinned: forgive me!

Accept the prayer offered for me, the unfruitful one, O long-suffering Master, and cut me not down as an unfruitful tree by the mortal cutting that casts into the fire; but be Thou entreated to make me fruitful, granting me time for repentance, as Thou art the Lover of mankind, that I may wash away[^287] [f. 209vA] O Savior, my many sins!

Other Stichera to the Holy Forerunner John. Tone 7:

Living blamelessly in the wilderness: my mind that hath fallen through sins, do Thou renew, O Forerunner!

Knowing Thee as the fairest turtledove, O Forerunner, we glorify Thee: who didst proclaim unto those in the world the divine springtime!

O divine Forerunner, protector of my life and guardian of my soul: deliver me, Thy servant, from the deceitful tongue of man!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

Tempest-tossed by the tumult of slothfulness: guide me unto the tranquil harbor of salvation, O Sovereign Lady!

At the Aposticha, Penitential Stichera. Tone 7:

As the Prodigal Son I have come, O compassionate One; receive me falling down before Thee, as one of Thy hired servants, O God, and have mercy upon me!

As one falling among thieves and wounded, so have I fallen through many sins, and my soul is wounded: unto whom shall I, the guilty one, flee, save unto Thee, the compassionate Physician of souls? Pour out upon us, O God, Thy great mercy!

Martyrs:

O Holy Martyrs, who strove well and received crowns: pray unto the Lord that our souls may be saved!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

Rejoice, O Cloud of the spiritual Sun and Sovereign Lady of the earth! Rejoice, O radiant Candlestick! Rejoice [f. 209vB] all-golden crown of all! Through Thee, O all-pure one, mankind was delivered from the curse: but having boldness before Thy Son and Lord, through Thy maternal prayer preserve us unceasingly, O all-pure one!

ON TUESDAY, AT MATINS:

After the 1st Kathisma, Penitential Sessional Hymns. Tone 7:

Possessing the medicine of repentance, O my soul, draw near weeping and crying with sighing: O Physician of souls and bodies, Lover of mankind, loose me from my many transgressions, number me with the Harlot, the Thief, and the Publican, and grant me, O God, forgiveness of mine iniquities, and save me!

O Lord and Lover of mankind, Who didst cleanse Peter's denial with tears and didst forgive the sins of the Publican through sighing: have mercy upon me!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

Rejoice, O Birth-giver of God, who didst contain in Thy womb Him Whom the heavens cannot contain! Rejoice, O Virgin, the proclamation of the Prophets, through whom Emmanuel shone forth unto us! Rejoice, O Mother of Christ God!

After the 2nd Kathisma, Penitential Sessional Hymns. Tone 7:

I have not emulated the repentance of the Publican, nor have I acquired the tears of the Harlot; for I am bewildered by blindness regarding such amendment: but by Thy compassions, O good One, save me, for Thou art the Lover of mankind!

O Savior, Who didst receive the tears of the Harlot and of Peter, and didst justify the Publican [f. 210rA] who sighed from the depths: have compassion on me who despond because of my deeds, and save me!

Martyrs:

Thy Saints, O Lord, having struggled upon earth, trampled down the enemy and abolished the delusion of idols: therefore, having received crowns from Thee, O good Lover of mankind, grant great mercy unto the world!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

Rejoice, O Birth-giver of God, who didst contain in Thy womb Him Whom the heavens cannot contain! Rejoice, O Virgin, the proclamation of the Prophets, through whom Emmanuel shone forth unto us! Rejoice, O Mother of Christ God!

*After the 3rd Kathisma, Penitential Sessional Hymns. Tone 7.*

*Podoben: "Fruit of thy womb" (Пло́дъ чре́ва твоегѡ́):*

As the Harlot I fall down before Thee, O Lover of mankind, though I lack tears of compunction: by the intercessions of Thine all-pure Mother, have mercy through prayer, and save me!

My soul being defiled, O Savior, through the intercession of Thy Mother wash me clean as the Good One: and purifying me from the filth of passions, have mercy upon me, O Master: save Thine own creation through the intercessions of Thine immaculate Mother, O only most merciful One!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

A fervent protectress and helper art Thou unto Christians, O all-hymned Birth-giver of God: therefore, together with the Forerunner, pray Thou unto Thy Son that we may find mercy!

PENITENTIAL CANON.

Composition of Joseph.

[f. 210rB] Ode 1. Tone 7. Heirmos:

Unto Him Who shattered wars with a high arm, and drowned the captains and chariot-riders: let us chant unto Him, as our Deliverer and God, for He is glorified!

Troparia:

All the day have I sinned, and I feared Thee not, O Christ, Who hast long-suffering toward my repentance: grant me the thought of turning back, as Thou art good, and despise me not!

Adding sin unto sins, O Christ, I, the wretched one, can in no wise cease: O only Good and Sinless One, have pity and save me!

Martyrs:

The valiant sufferers boldly cried aloud: Lo, the stadium is full of struggles; let us run, that Christ the Judge of contests may crown us with the wreath of conquerors over the enemy!

Martyrs:

Having adorned the brightness of your bodies with manifold wounds, ye clothed yourselves with the robe of incorruption, O Martyrs of Christ, becoming sons of compassion!

Theotokion:

Heal my soul that is afflicted with many sins, O Virgin Birth-giver of God, that with voices of thanksgiving I may earnestly and ever glorify Thee!

Another Canon to the Forerunner John.

Composition of Joseph.

Ode 1. Tone 7. Heirmos: By Thy nod upon the earth:

Adorned as the beauty of the Church, Thou didst appear, O blessed Forerunner: by Thy prayers ever save from all peril of heresies, O steadfast and unshakable one!

As an immaculate, holy sacrifice didst Thou offer Thyself unto the Creator, being slain, O divine Forerunner, as a gentle lamb[^288] [f. 210vA] therefore in faith I cry unto Thee: deliver me from all malice of the enemy!

Heal our bodily and spiritual diseases, O all-blessed Forerunner, ever praying unto the Word, Who compassionately took upon Himself the infirmities and diseases of all!

Theotokion:

O Most Holy one, who didst bear the Incomprehensible Word: entreat Him in the flesh, as Lord, to save those who ever faithfully bless Thee!

Penitential Canon.

Ode 3. Heirmos:

O Thou Who didst establish the heavens by Thy Word, and strengthen the foundations of the earth upon many waters: establish my mind in Thy will, O only Lover of mankind!

Troparia:

O Thou Who overlookest the sins of men according to Thine abundant love for mankind, O Christ: do Thou alone, O Savior, overlook the multitude of mine evils, that I may glorify Thee, the supremely Good One!

That I might fulfill the desires of the flesh, I, possessing an insensible conscience, neglected Thy will, O Christ: deliver me, O Word, from the flaming torment thereof!

Martyrs:

Partaking of bodily sufferings, the holy sufferers never looked down upon this sorrowful life: which they turned into joy, ever lightening the afflictions of the faithful!

Martyrs:

With the rays of your sufferings, O God-bearing ones, ye dissolved the grievous night of delusion, and passed over unto the unwaning light, ever taking away the darkness of our diseases!

Theotokion:

The Prophet foresaw Thee as the Gate of God, through which He alone passed as He knew, O all-pure Virgin: therefore open Thou unto me [f. 210vB] the gates of repentance through prayer!

Another Canon to the Forerunner.

Ode 3. Heirmos: Those who assault us:

With sun-like splendors Thou dost enlighten all creation, for Thou wast shown forth as the star of the spiritual Luminary, O Forerunner: earnestly pray unto Him to drive away the darkness of passions from our sorrowful hearts!

Standing between the Law and Grace, O divine Forerunner, Thou didst clearly show forth unto all: that the one should cease, and the other blossom forth, granting complete renewal of transgressions unto those who find it!

Deliver us, we cry aloud, O Baptist of Christ, from the wrathful assault of worldly temptations and from every sorrow: pray unto the Supremely Good One, and free us from future torment!

Theotokion:

O God-like one, who ineffably didst bear God: together with His divine Baptist, unceasingly pray, O Sovereign Lady, for us who fall into the temptations of life and are held fast by sins!

Penitential Canon.

Ode 4. Heirmos:

Perceiving Thy bodily coming, O Christ, the Prophet Habakkuk cried aloud: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

Troparia:

I have strayed from the path that leads unto life, and have fallen into the evil pit: O Savior, despise me not!

Send down streams of tears unto me, O Word of God, that I may wash away the filth of my many transgressions!

Martyrs:

Led as lambs unto the slaughter, the Martyrs slew the tyrant enemy, being accounted worthy of glory!

[f. 211rA] The streams of blood poured forth, O all-praised and divine Martyrs, prepared for you streams of delight!

Theotokion:

The Lord became incarnate of Thy pure blood, granting repentance unto mortals through Thine intercession, O Maiden!

Another Canon to the Forerunner.

*Ode 4. Heirmos: Without leaving the Father's bosom and having descended...*

Having cast down the hosts of the enemy and valiantly shone forth, pray, O Baptist, that by Thy prayers the sin reigning within me may be cast down!

Thou didst appear as a spiritual lamp, O blessed one, showing forth upon earth Jesus, the great Sun of righteousness, by Whom the hearts of all are illumined!

In iniquities was I conceived and born, awaiting the outer darkness and the end of torments there: have mercy upon me and rescue me, O Baptist, having entreated God!

Having washed my prayers clean, present them now unto God, O Baptist, for me who honor Thee, that He may deliver all of us from every grievous circumstance and demonic harm!

Theotokion:

The shadows of the Law in manifold ways showed Thee forth as the one who was to bear God: Whom do Thou entreat, O all-immaculate one, to deliver me from every lawlessness and bodily passions!

Penitential Canon.

Ode 5. Heirmos:

Having driven away the dark night of passions, O Spiritual Light Who didst drive away the primal darkness from the abyss, and didst establish the first-created light for the world: O Creator of all!

Troparia:

Spare me, O Word, from Thy righteous wrath when Thou judgest the earth [f. 211rB] and having cleansed me through repentance from my many sins, show me forth as a temple of Thy goodness, O only Creator of all!

With the grievous mist of passions have I blinded my mind, and with a troubled heart I know not what I do: turn me back, O Christ, and grant me repentance that cleanses all defilement!

Martyrs:

Having youthfully run the course that was full of sweat, O holy sufferers, ye reached the unwaning splendor, having received the prize of victory from the life-originating Hand: therefore ye now rejoice!

Martyrs:

By the strong sinews of your sacred sufferings, O holy sufferers, ye truly strangled the prince of the malicious serpent, and were accounted worthy of heavenly food: therefore we praise you!

Theotokion:

O radiant Cloud of the Sun, kindle within me the spiritual light of true repentance, and drive away the darkness of wicked thoughts, that in faith I may hymn Thee as the salvation of the faithful!

Another Canon to the Forerunner.

Ode 5. Heirmos: The Lord our God:

Thou didst foresee the voice of him that cries in the wilderness, O all-wise one, preaching the knowledge of God: therefore I pray Thee, renew my soul that is made desolate by all manner of transgressions!

Having been shown forth as a radiant vessel, O divine Forerunner: by Thy prayers deliver me from dishonorable deeds, and entreat the Benefactor that I may obtain eternal honor!

Iniquities have drawn near unto us in the departure of slothfulness: establish me in the ways of repentance, O blessed Forerunner, that I may earnestly walk in the ways of the Lord, chanting unto Thee!

Theotokion:

Put to death the earthly mind of my flesh...[^289]

[f. 211vA] ...mind of the flesh, O Birth-giver of God, who didst bear the Life: by death having washed away death by divine power, O all-immaculate and pure one, destroying it!

Penitential Canon.

Ode 6. Heirmos:

Into the deep of transgressions have I fallen, O Master; as Jonah from the whale, I cry unto Thee: Lead my life up from corruption, and save me, O Lover of mankind!

Troparia:

A new prodigal have I appeared, having lived defiledly upon earth, and I have bowed down unto gluttonous passions: turn me back, O Christ my God, and save me, as Thou art the Lover of mankind!

Cry aloud, O my soul, that thou mayest be delivered from weeping and groaning: so that thou receivest not there unceasing tears in vain, in pain and torment having no profit!

Martyrs:

Fixed like precious stones set in the crowns of Christ's Church, ye were a beauteous adornment unto her, O venerable Great Martyrs!

Accounted worthy of an end worthy of God, O most wise ones, ye inherit boundless rewards of honey: therefore pray, O Martyrs, that our ends also may be in repentance!

Theotokion:

From the deep of slothfulness and immeasurable evils lead me up, O good one, who didst bear the abyss of compassions; and grant unto me a fountain of tears continually, O Virgin!

Another Canon [to the Forerunner].

Ode 6. Heirmos: Jonah cried from the belly of hades:

Having shone forth like the beams of virtues and through radiant martyrdom, O holy one, thou dost enlighten all creation with the spiritual Orient, blessed and noble one!

Thou didst blossom forth from a barren mother, O blessed one [f. 211vB] therefore I cry unto thee: me who am grown old through many sins, renew by the beauties of repentance through thy prayers!

O lamp of the unwaning Light, divine Forerunner: kindle the extinguished lamp of my soul by thy prayers, and make me a partaker of the divine Light!

Theotokion:

As rain upon the fleece the Word came down into thy womb, Whom do thou entreat, O all-pure Virgin, by thy prayers to dry up the streams of my boundless evils!

Penitential Canon.

Ode 7. Heirmos:

The Young Men in the furnace were untouched and unharmed by the fire; then the three, as with one mouth, sang and blessed, saying: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

Troparia:

Into shameful dishonor have I fallen, O Savior, likened unto brute beasts; and being darkened, I see not: O Word, Who art long-suffering in waiting for me, grant me time for conversion, and save me!

In slothfulness have I finished my life, doing deeds that are unlawful to do; and lo, now I have drawn near unto the gates of hades, having no sense of feeling: despise me not, O Christ, Who alone art good!

Martyrs:

Desiring eternal life, O Martyrs, ye put to death worldly deceit; and having utterly slain the enemy, ye took flight unto the heavens, ever praying for us, O sufferers!

By the tearing of your flesh ye loosed that bodily constraint of deceptive bonds; and bound in soul by the strong love of Christ, O Martyrs, ye proclaimed Him Who appeared in the flesh and destroyed corruption!

[f. 212rA] The Prophet foresaw Thee as a new scroll, wherein the Father's Word was written; therefore, O pure one, I pray Thee: account me worthy to be written in the Book of the Living, tearing up the handwriting of my many evils!

Another Canon [to the Forerunner].

*Ode 7. Heirmos: The Children of old showed the fiery furnace...*

Grant me showers of tears, I pray thee, O blessed one, having sharpened my sorrow; thou who didst wash away the mud of the abyss with river streams, O Forerunner: cleanse me entirely from the defilement of flesh and spirit!

Offer supplication, O blessed one, unto our God Who is over all: that He may have mercy also upon me, as He is compassionate, who have sinned much, and have no means of rising up!

O barren soul, make haste to repent: lest the divine judgment suddenly cut thee down like a barren fig tree! Cry aloud unto God: O God, have compassion upon me, and save me!

Theotokion:

Having acquired a deadened soul through grievous, wicked transgressions: unto Thee, who by thy childbearing didst put hades to death, I pray, O Good One: make me alive by the ways of repentance!

Penitential Canon.

Ode 8. Heirmos:

Him Who is unceasingly praised by the Angels and glorified as God: let the heavens of heavens, the earth, the mountains, the hills, and the abyss, and all the human race: bless and praise Him continually in hymns as Creator and Redeemer, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

Troparia:

Having excessively and mindlessly delighted in harmful pleasures, senseless as I am, I have surpassed every sinner: O Thou Who hast an abundance of loving-kindness, grant me cleansing of my transgressions!

[f. 212rB] Now the Bridegroom is at the doors: adorn thy lamps, O soul, fueling them with the oil of mercy and with all good works, before the doors are shut: make haste to enter with Christ into ineffable joy!

Martyrs:

When the valiant sufferers endured the pain of torments, they cried: "Lo, the acceptable time! Let us all stand with a steadfast mind; by small pains let us acquire a life free from sickness and food that never grows old!"

Watered abundantly with divine waters, O passion-bearers of the Savior, ye water the earth with the imitation of your struggles, and make it fruitful in virtues unto the ages in Christ!

Theotokion:

O Birth-giver of God, sure protectress and hope of Christians: in the dreadful day stand by me who have sinned greatly, and deliver me from the dreadful Gehenna, numbering me with the sheep on the right hand!

Another Canon [to the Forerunner].

Ode 8. Heirmos: Unto the only Beginningless King of glory:

To be loosed from the bonds of many sins, pray, O Forerunner, unto the only Redeemer, Who was bound and granted release unto the bound, that I may unceasingly glorify thee unto the ages!

I have drawn near, O Forerunner, unto the weapon of pleasures, and in pain of heart I cry aloud: heal the sickness of my soul, having entreated Christ, the only Physician of souls and bodies!

As thou art the Forerunner of the Word Whom thou didst baptize, unceasingly pray without ceasing, to deliver me from the river of sin, who have sinned much...[^290]

[f. 212vA] ...greatly, and am humble and condemned.

As I have excessively buried in the earth the talent entrusted unto me by God, I await bitter torment: from which snatch me away, O Baptist, by thy prayers, as I faithfully beseech thee!

Theotokion:

Thou didst remain unburnt, O Virgin, having received the incomprehensible Fire in thy womb: therefore snatch me away from the unquenchable fire, dewing me now with beauteous forms of genuine repentance!

Penitential Canon.

Ode 9. Heirmos:

Who among the earthborn can declare the conception of the seedless birth? Who among men marvels not at the birthgiving of the incorruptible birth? Therefore all we, the earthly generations, magnify thee, O Birth-giver of God!

Troparia:

Let us weep, let us groan, let us entreat Christ while we, the faithful, yet have time for repentance and supplication, that the enduring good things may overtake us!

Like the Canaanite woman I cry unto Thee: Have mercy upon me, O Christ! As of old Thou didst heal the bowed-down woman, make me upright, O Lord; and save me, O Savior, who am submerged in sins!

Martyrs:

Constrained by afflictions, prisons, and torments, the passion-bearing Martyrs passed into the broad expanse of rest, delivering us from transgressions!

The earth indeed hath now covered your bodies, but heaven holds your holy spirits, acceptably standing before the throne of glory and rejoicing with the Angels!

Theotokion:

The Lord clothed Himself with me, having passed through Thee, O all-pure one; do Thou therefore entreat Him, O Virgin, to enlighten me with a radiant garment, having stripped me of the grievous sackcloth of passions [f. 212vB] the most burdensome.

Another Canon [to the Forerunner].

Ode 9. Heirmos: O Master and Lover of mankind:

Thou didst bud forth from a holy root, having been born through the necessity of barrenness, O holy Forerunner; and thou didst uproot all evil roots, thereby enabling me to bring forth fruits of divine repentance, delivering me from the snares of vanity!

The Church knows thee, O great Forerunner, as the fairest and sweet turtledove; for thou didst proclaim the hymn of repentance unto souls that were desolate and frozen in evils: therefore in faith we ever call thee blessed!

Thou didst show forth unto all the divine paths that lead unto salvation, O glorious Forerunner: strengthen me to walk therein, who am wandering in all the pathless ways of life, and through delusion have committed deceit!

The dreadful day at the doors hath drawn near, and having deeds worthy of condemnation, I weep aloud: O Lord, O Lord, Who alone art merciful, by the prayers of Thy Forerunner and of all the Saints, show me then uncondemned!

Theotokion:

O Maiden full of God's grace, who didst bear the Divine Light: enlighten my soul, I pray, which is darkened by transgressions, and show me free from eternal darkness, that I may ever magnify and glorify thee, the blessed one!

Aposticha Stichera,

Penitential. Tone 7:

Like the barren fig tree, cut me not down, O Savior, sinful as I am; but grant me patience for many years, watering my soul [f. 213rA] with the tears of repentance, that I may bring forth unto Thee the fruit of almsgiving!

As Thou art the righteous Sun: enlighten the hearts of them that praise Thee; O Lord, glory to Thee!

Martyrs:

In the midst of the tribunal of the lawless, Thy passion-bearers rejoiced, crying: O Lord, glory to Thee!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

O Christ, Thou Light that didst sprout from the Virgin and hast enlightened the human race: O Lord, glory to Thee!

On Tuesday,

Beatitudes. Tone 7:

Beautiful was that fruit and good for food which put me to death; but Christ is the Tree of Life, whereof eating I die not, but cry aloud with the Thief: Remember me, O Lord, when Thou comest into Thy Kingdom!

Heal the incurable wounds of my heart, O compassionate Lord, as Thou art the Physician of souls and bodies; and always prosper my walking uprightly in the paths of salvation!

O Baptist of Christ, forerunner unto the righteous Sun: kindle the lamp of my soul that is extinguished by many evils, through thy divine prayers, that being saved, I may ever call thee blessed!

[f. 213rB] Martyrs:

Having suffered and been crowned, ye put the enemy to shame, O most wise Martyrs; and now ye dwell in the heavens, filled with unceasing light, praying for our souls!

Glory: Triadikon:

Turn back my soul from long-standing passions, O Divine Trinity, granting me good confession and eternal life for the sake of Thy Forerunner, that I may magnify Thine immeasurable mercy!

Now and ever: Theotokion:

In thy corruptible womb thou didst contain Him Whom nothing can contain; Him do thou ever entreat, O pure Mother, to deliver thy servants, who in love glorify thee, from every distress and assault of passions!

## TUESDAY EVENING VESPERS (FOR WEDNESDAY) (TONE 7)

ON TUESDAY EVENING, AT "LORD, I HAVE CRIED":

*Stichera of the Cross, Tone 7.*

*Podoben: "No longer are we forbidden" (Не ктомꙋ̀ возбране́ни е҆смы̀):*

Of old the tree cast me out of Paradise; but now the Tree of the Cross hath led me back, when Thou wast crucified, O Christ!

A fearful wonder! How the Creator of creation, the throne of the Creator, is condemned and crucified for the salvation of mankind!

The Cross of Christ is a wonder unto holy Angels, but unto the devil and demons a great plague: save Thy servants!

Other Stichera to the Most Holy Theotokos,

*Tone 7.*

*Podoben: "Today Judas watches" (Дне́сь І҆ꙋ́да):*

Beholding the Lamb stretched upon the Tree...[^291]

[f. 213vA] ...the spotless Ewe-lamb and Virgin, between two thieves, cried aloud: "Woe is me, my sweetest Child! What is this strange and most glorious mystery? How hath the lawless council lifted Thee up upon the Cross, and given gall to drink unto Him Who satisfied men with manna?"

When the Virgin and Thy Mother beheld Thee nailed upon the Cross, O my Christ, by the judgment of the lawless, by the Jews in the Place of the Skull, she cried aloud: "Woe is me, my most beloved Son! What is this strange sight? How do the senseless children of the Hebrews nail Thee upon the Cross, Who art the Lord of all?"

Thee alone, O all-hymned Sovereign Lady, did we know as Virgin after childbearing, and seeing Him Whom thou didst bear without seed willingly nailing His hands upon the Tree, the all-pure one weeping cried aloud: "Willingly, O Long-suffering One, Thou diest, delivering from death all them that praise Thee!"

Glory: Now and ever: Stavrotheotokion:

O all-hymned Sovereign Lady, Virgin who didst bear the Lord, Who for compassion's sake was nailed upon the Cross and poured forth streams of life unto the world: do thou entreat Him that our souls may be saved; for thee alone have we, the faithful, as refuge, rampart, and protection: therefore do we flee unto thy protection!

Aposticha Stichera

to the Cross. Tone 7:

No longer are we forbidden from the Tree of Life, having the hope of Thy Cross: O Lord, glory to Thee!

[f. 213vB] Having been hanged upon the Tree, O Immortal One, Thou didst break the snares of the devil: O Lord, glory to Thee!

Martyrs:

O holy Martyrs, who also courageously preached Christ at the tribunal: ye received from Him the reward for your torments; but as ye have boldness, entreat Him as Almighty God to save our souls, who flee unto you, we pray you, O glorious ones!

Glory: Now and ever: Stavrotheotokion:

Beholding of old thine own Son upon the Tree, O all-pure one, a sword of sorrow pierced thy heart!

ON WEDNESDAY, AT MATINS.

After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymns

of the Cross. Tone 7:

Jacob cries aloud unto Thee, O Christ God, worshipping Thee through the pine, the cedar, and the cypress: grant victories unto our hierarchs, O Compassionate One, and have mercy upon us!

Thou Who for my sake didst endure being nailed upon the Cross: accept also my vigilant praise, O Christ God, and save me!

Glory: Now and ever: Stavrotheotokion:

Unceasingly pray, O Virgin Birth-giver of God, unto Christ our King Who was crucified for our sake and hath cast down the dominion of death, that He may save our souls!

After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns

of the Cross. Tone 7:

A fire brighter and more efficacious than flame hast Thou shown forth the Tree of Thy Cross to be, consuming the sins of men and enlightening [f. 214rA] the hearts of them that praise Thy voluntary crucifixion: O Christ God, glory to Thee!

O Thou Who rulest over the bodiless hosts: heal the blindness of my soul, and by Thy Cross save me, O Christ, as Thou art the Lover of mankind!

Martyrs:

Rejoice, ye righteous! Let the heavens be glad! For the Martyrs, having contended upon earth, trampled down the enemies; let the joyful company of men celebrate, unto the only Umpire of the contest and Wonder-working God, Who grants great mercy unto the world!

Glory: Now and ever: Stavrotheotokion:

When the Virgin beheld Thee crucified, O Lord, weeping she cried aloud unto Thee: "I hymn Thine ineffable long-suffering, O my Son, and Thy supreme and divine descent unto mankind!"

After the 3rd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns

of the Cross. Tone 7:

When Thou wast crucified, O good Christ, the enemy was bound, and from the dead the souls that were held fast in hades beneath were loosed from their bonds!

Thou Who for our sake didst accept reproachful crucifixion: accept them that praise Thy passions, O Christ God, and save us!

Glory: Now and ever: Stavrotheotokion:

Being ever preserved by the Cross of thy Son, O Virgin, we escape the assault of heretical errors; therefore, as is meet, praising thee we glorify thee, O all-hymned Birth-giver of God!

CANON to the Precious and

Life-Creating Cross of the Lord.

Work of Joseph.

Ode 1. Tone 7. Heirmos:

By Thy nod upon the earth:

[f. 214rB] Troparia:

The Master, enduring crucifixion and reproach, bears the reproaches of men, as He is the Lover of mankind!

Pierced in the side with a spear, He slaughters the warring enemy!

Bending Thy Cross like a bow, O Merciful One, Thou didst wound the adversary with the arrows of nails, O Savior, and didst heal mortals who of old were wounded by him!

Martyrs:

By the blood of the saints, the abominable pollutions of blood offered unto idols ceased, and all the earth was cleansed, delighting them with praises!

Martyrs:

The heavenly powers sang praise, beholding the earthly martyrs lifted up and holding hands with the bodiless; therefore the Umpire of the contest crowned the victors!

Theotokion:

The handwriting of Adam was torn asunder, cried the all-pure Ewe-lamb, when Thy side was pierced with a spear, O Son; therefore I praise Thy suffering which hath poured forth dispassion unto all!

Another Canon to the Most Holy Theotokos.

Ode 1. Same Heirmos.

Loving to praise thy greatness, O Birth-giver of God, save thy people and deliver them from harm; for thou art our protectress, pure guide, and confirmation!

Having brought forth the Water of Immortality, O Virgin, grant us waters of healing, washing away all death-bearing passions from our souls and bodies!

Thou wast shown forth as the joyful dwelling-place, O Birth-giver of God full of God's grace, of Him Who honored the nature of our forefather: therefore, O pure one, we pray thee: deliver us from every dishonor of passions...[^292]

[f. 214vA] ...passions which assail us!

Having given birth unto the Sun of Righteousness for the world, O Maiden, Who hast enlightened all that are in darkness: in thy light-bearing and holy temple, O all-immaculate one!

Canon of the Cross.

Ode 3. Heirmos:

Thou Who in the beginning established the heavens by Thy Word, O Lord and Savior, and by the all-effective and Divine Spirit all their power was made firm: establish me upon the immovable rock of Thy confession!

Troparia:

When Thou wast stretched upon the Tree, O Jesus, Thou didst heal the incontinence of Adam's hands, as Thou art merciful; and from the hand of the deceiver Thou didst snatch away all that were in delusion!

The lawless people crowned Thee with thorns, O Christ, Who hast crowned the earth with flowers; taking away the thorn of Adam's ancient disobedience, and granting us the knowledge of God!

Martyrs:

Through the nature of mortal men, ye put death to death, O most wise Martyrs: therefore having died unto bodily wounds and torments, ye rejoice, enduring all things!

With a steadfast mind, having overcome the hostile prince of evil, O valiant sufferers, ye were magnified in Christ, and were exalted by the divine right hand to live with Him forever!

Theotokion:

When the Ewe-lamb and Mother beheld the Lamb Who came willingly unto the slaughter, weeping she cried aloud: "What is this strange wonder? How diest Thou, O Blessed One, Who hast willed to make alive all them that are dead?"

Another Canon [to the Theotokos].

Ode 3. Same Heirmos:

Grant forgiveness unto Thy servants, O pure one [f. 214vB] in this holy temple, wherein thou hast shown a fountain of wonders to flow continually: delivering us from eternal torment by thy divine mediation!

Having given birth, O pure one, unto Christ the abyss of grace, Who is beyond cause and word, the Giver of all good things: by thy divine visitation heal the wounds of my soul from great passions!

Blessed is the fruit of thy womb, O Virgin, who didst bear joy unto all the world, and didst in truth contain the Lover of mankind: destroy the sorrow of my sins, O Virgin!

Stavrotheotokion:

O spiritual Ark, who didst truly bear the Manna that cannot be consumed: come into our midst, and from every defilement deliver them that honor thee, magnifying thee, O all-pure one!

Canon of the Cross.

Ode 4. Heirmos:

Without leaving the Father's bosom, Thou didst come down to earth, O Christ God; I have heard the mystery of Thy dispensation, and I have glorified Thee, Who alone art the Lover of mankind!

Troparia:

By the shedding of Thy blood, O Jesus, Thou didst redeem mankind, suffering for the unjust, O Long-suffering One: we chant unto Thy supreme loving-kindness!

Martyrs:

By the fierce burning of fire, and by the cutting-off of hands and feet, and by many torments, the Martyrs endured, interceding for us [f. 215rA] unto the divine enjoyment of the end of bodily struggles, crying aloud unto the God of all: their voices were heard, and they were accounted worthy of divine perfection!

Theotokion:
