I pray thee, who didst bear the Incarnate One: make me, who am poor and in need of help, a temple of the Holy Spirit, O Birth-giver of God; that I may find help in the time of judgment, through the mediation of Him Who was born of thee, glorifying thee!

Another Canon [to the Theotokos].

Ode 4. Heirmos: Habakkuk foresaw the mountain:

O pure Birth-giver of God, adorned with the beauty of virtues, O Sovereign Lady, put out the fire of primal evil, which hath kindled within me!

Accept the supplication of Thy servants, O pure one, who didst bring forth Christ: save from every harm them that are redeemed by His blood, as we praise thee as is meet!

Thy grace is exceedingly praised, O Maiden full of God's grace; for it heals the sickness of souls and bodies, and cleanses defilement, as we faithfully glorify thee!

By thy visitation, O Virgin, save us from temptations and afflictions, and by thy holy prayers, deliver us who love thee from all evil, granting us life and forgiveness!

Canon of the Cross.

Ode 5. Heirmos:

O Lord my God, from the night I awake early unto Thee, I pray Thee: grant me remission of my transgressions, and direct my path unto the commandments of Thy precepts!

Troparia:

When Thou wast lifted up upon the Cross, O Word of God, Thou didst receive gall [f. 215rB] tasting it, Thou didst destroy the bitterness of the ancient food: Glory to Thy great mercy, O Savior!

When Thou wast lifted up upon the Tree, the whole earth was shaken, O Christ, by Thy divine power; and the shaken souls of men Thou didst establish in the knowledge of Thee!

Martyrs:

The valiant Martyrs spread their limbs upon wheels: but they were not broken from Christ; for through fire and water they attained unto the heavenly mansions!

Martyrs:

Tormented with unsparing tortures, the passion-bearers endured: as if others were suffering, they sang: "Unto Thee, O Savior, we offer our struggles!"

Theotokion:

With what eyes shall I look upon Thee, O Eye that seest all, when Thou art lifted up upon the Cross, cried the Virgin, weeping and lamenting within herself!

Another Canon [to the Theotokos].

Ode 5. Heirmos: Having driven away the dark night:

Deliver me, O pure one, from the heavy slumber of sin, who wake early in thy holy temple, praising thee, O all-immaculate one!

Theotokion:

Extend thy hand unto all of us, O pure one, who flee unto thee: deliver us from the darkness of all evil defilement, and heal our diseases by thy prayers!

Having conceived God in thy virgin womb, O Birth-giver of God, and given birth unto Him, O pure one: deliver from eternal condemnation them that praise thee, who with faith enter into thy temple...[^293]

[f. 215vA] ...who walk therein: renewing our soul that is grown old through sin: and as is meet we praise thee, O all-immaculate one!

Canon of the Cross.

Ode 6. Heirmos:

Floating on the sea of life, and tossed by the tempest of passions, I run to Thy calm haven, O Christ: lead my life up from corruption, O most merciful One!

Troparia:

Through ancient lack of restraint, I fell into bitter falling, O Christ; but when Thou wast lifted up upon the Tree, Thou didst stretch out Thy hands, O Savior, and didst heal my wounds: glory to Thy power, O Lord!

By the sleep of delusion the enemy put the first-created to sleep; but when Thou wast put to sleep upon the Cross, O Word of God, Thou didst awaken all from the sleep of death!

Martyrs:

Established upon the rock of Christ's commandments, the venerable Martyrs were unshaken by the assaults of torment: therefore having run the course, they were crowned by the divine hand!

Theotokion:

Thou didst bear the Child, Who before was bodiless, O Maiden; Who by the Cross renewed the nature of mortals that was grown old through sin: therefore we praise thee, O all-immaculate one!

Another Canon [to the Theotokos].

Ode 6. Heirmos: Jonah cried from the belly of hades:

Remember us, O Savior, who call upon Thee [f. 215vB] Thou Who alone art the Lover of mankind, who didst deliver our race from delusion; by the prayers of the all-pure one, and through Thy Cross, grant us freedom from passions!

Cleanse the sores of our souls, O Birth-giver of God, by the sprinkling of thy compassion, and heal bodily illnesses, that we may glorify thee, the good protectress!

Having broken the bond of ancient Eve, O Maiden, by thy divine childbearing: loose the bonds of our transgressions, who faithfully run unto thy shelter!

Canon of the Cross.

Ode 7. Heirmos:

The Children in the furnace were untouched and unharmed by the fire; then the three, as with one mouth, sang and blessed, saying: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

Troparia:

Delivered from the curse of the Law, the Lawgiver was lifted up upon the Cross, bringing forth blessing and mercy, and the fountain of incorruption unto them that praise Him!

Martyrs:

Cast into the burning fire by the decree of the lawless, the holy Martyrs extinguished the flame by the dew of the Spirit, and sang: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

Having offered their bodies unto various torments, the Martyrs poured forth streams of blood, and through their struggles put down the arrogance of the adversary!

Theotokion:

How dost Thou endure crucifixion, O Child, cried the all-pure Virgin; I behold Thee hanging upon the Tree, Who didst establish the earth upon the waters [f. 216rA] O Child, beholding Thee, how can I not weep, seeing Thee suffer unjustly, Who hast crowned creation with beauty!

Another Canon [to the Theotokos].

Ode 7. Same Heirmos:

O Fire Who didst bear the Divine Fire, consume the thorns of my passions, and by the light of repentance illumine my soul, as I faithfully call thee blessed!

Having delivered the three Children from the furnace, O pure one, show me to be a temple of the Divine Spirit, who am consumed by the fire of sins, as I faithfully hymn thee!

Having brought forth the Wellspring of healing unto the world, heal the incurable wounds of my soul, O Virgin, and quench the burning furnace of passions by thy prayers!

Canon of the Cross.

Ode 8. Heirmos:

The unconsumed fire on Sinai showed forth the virginity of the Mother of God; and now the Cross of the Savior hath renewed the world: let all works praise the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

Troparia:

Crowned with thorns, O Savior, Thou didst pull up the thorns of the ancient curse; and tasting vinegar and gall, Thou didst sweeten our bitterness: let all works praise the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

[f. 216rB] Martyrs:

The Martyrs, rich in the treasures of truth, accounted worldly poverty as nothing, and through their blood enriched the Church, crying: Let all works praise the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

Martyrs:

Thrown into the fiery furnace by the lawless decree, the holy Martyrs were preserved by the dew of God, and sang: Let all works praise the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

Theotokion:

The rod of Aaron prefigured Thee, O pure Virgin, who without seed didst bud forth Christ the Lawgiver: Whom the lawless people nailed upon the Cross: let all works praise the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

Another Canon [to the Theotokos].

Ode 8. Same Heirmos:

Unto the only beginningless King of glory, Whom the heavenly hosts praise and before Whom the ranks of Angels tremble: praise Him, ye priests, and supremely exalt Him, ye people, unto all ages!

Having brought forth the rich Fountain of dispassion, O Virgin, dry up the torrent of our passions, and grant streams of tears unto us who faithfully honor thee as the Mother of God!

O radiant Sun of Righteousness, Who didst shine forth from the Virgin: illumine them that are in darkness, and make them sons of light, who faithfully praise Thee, O Christ, unto the ages!

We who are assembled in thy holy temple, O Virgin, praise thee as the Mother of God...[^294]

[f. 216vA] ...and bless Him Who was born of thee unto all ages!

In the light of thy childbearing, O Birth-giver of God, the world was enlightened; for thou didst bear the true God, Who enlightened all by His Cross: let all works praise the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

Canon of the Cross.

Ode 9. Heirmos:

A Mother of God and Virgin, giving birth and remaining a virgin, is not a work of nature, but the condescension of God: therefore as the only Mother of divine gifts, we magnify thee, O pure one!

Troparia:

The enemy's power was broken, O Savior, when Thou wast lifted up upon the Cross; and through Thy death Thou didst slay the deceiver, raising up Adam who was fallen: glory to Thy power, O Lord!

Like a lamb, Thou wast led willingly unto the slaughter, O Savior, and didst stretch out Thy hands upon the Cross: gathering the scattered sheep into the fold of Thy commandments!

Martyrs:

Imitating the passions of Christ, the glorious Martyrs endured diverse torments: therefore having received crowns of glory, they were accounted worthy of Thy Kingdom, O Christ!

The assemblies of the faithful praise the memories of the Martyrs; who by their blood adorned the Church of Christ: therefore we celebrate their venerable memory!

[f. 216vB] Theotokion:

Beholding Thee hanging upon the Tree, O my Son, cried the Virgin, my heart is wounded with sorrow: but rising on the third day, as God, raise up Adam who was fallen!

Another Canon [to the Theotokos].

Ode 9. Same Heirmos:

Higher than the heavens art thou shown forth, O pure Virgin, having brought forth the Creator of all: therefore with the Angels we unceasingly magnify thee!

As the radiant mountain of God, the Prophet foresaw thee of old, O Virgin; from whence Christ came forth, enlightening the ends of the earth: therefore we call thee blessed!

Thou didst appear as the golden jar, containing the heavenly Manna, Christ the Giver of Life: therefore we faithfully praise thee, O Birth-giver of God!

A glorious tabernacle and holy dwelling-place of God didst thou appear, O Maiden; therefore deliver me from the defilement of sins, that I may magnify thee with pure lips!

O Virgin who didst bear the unwaning Light: deliver me from eternal darkness, and enlighten my darkened soul, that in love I may hymn thee!

Aposticha Stichera

to the Cross. Tone 7:

Having redeemed the world by Thy Cross, O Lover of mankind: O Lord, glory to Thee!

When Thou wast nailed upon the Cross, the sun was darkened, and the earth was shaken: O Lord, glory to Thee!

[f. 217rA] Thou didst grant Thy Cross as an invincible weapon unto Thy people: O Lord, glory to Thee!

Martyrs:

The passion-bearing Martyrs of Christ endured torments, and received the reward of victory: therefore they pray for our souls!

Glory: Now and ever: Stavrotheotokion:

Beholding Thee nailed upon the Cross, O Word of God, the all-pure one wept, saying: "Woe is me, my sweetest Child! How diest Thou willingly, wishing to deliver mankind from corruption?"

## WEDNESDAY EVENING VESPERS (FOR THURSDAY) (TONE 7)

ON WEDNESDAY EVENING, AT "LORD, I HAVE CRIED":

*Stichera of the Holy Apostles, Tone 7.*

*Podoben: "No longer are we forbidden" (Не ктомꙋ̀ возбране́ни е҆смы̀):*

Ye spiritual luminaries of the Church, glorious Apostles: who by your preaching enlightened the whole earth, and dispelled the mist of idolatry: pray unto Christ our God that our souls may be saved!

Having cast the net of the Gospel into the deep of the world, ye drew the nations unto the knowledge of Christ: O blessed Apostles, pray for us!

Having plowed the human heart with the plow of faith, ye sowed the divine seed, bringing forth fruit unto God: O glorious disciples of the Savior...[^295]

[f. 217vA] ...of God, the assemblies of the nations.

Other Stichera to Saint Nicholas,

*Tone 7.*

*Podoben: "The same" (то́йже):*

As of old thou didst deliver the three commanders who were about to die, O Nicholas, by thy prayers: so now also save us!

All who in faith and love call upon thee and praise thee, O all-blessed hierarch Nicholas: deliver from famine, earthquake, and destruction, and from every sorrow and need free thy servants, O wise hierarch Nicholas!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

Offer supplication for thy servants, O all-hymned one, unto thine own Son, that He may save all whom He hath created!

Aposticha Stichera

to the Holy Apostles, Tone 7:

Glorious Apostles, pillars of the Church, true preachers, being radiant luminaries: in the spiritual fire ye burned up the great deceit, and enlightened the human race through faith: therefore we pray you: entreat our Savior and God, to give peace unto the world and save our souls!

Apostles of Christ, laborers of the Word, who bore the Cross upon your shoulders like a plow, plowing the earth that was barren through idolatrous deceit: ye sowed the word of faith, and are worthily praised, O holy Apostles of Christ!

Martyrs:

Praised Martyrs, spiritual sacrifices, acceptable whole burnt offerings well-pleasing unto Christ: the earth hath hidden you now, but [f. 217vB] heaven hath received you; ye were made partakers with the Angels: with them pray, we beseech you, unto our Savior and God, to grant peace unto the world and save our souls!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

Thee alone as pure Virgin after childbearing do we hymn, saying: As the Mother of God the Word: Glory to Thee!

ON THURSDAY, AT MATINS.

After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymns

of the Apostles. Tone 7:

Thou didst show forth Thine Apostles as laborers of the world, O Word, cutting down idols: therefore having preached Thee among the nations, they piously magnified Thee!

Earthly things upon earth did the blessed ones not value: having preached the heavenly God unto men, they brought all unto Him!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

Though creation knew thee as a Mother, yet the Creator showed thee to be a Virgin; for in the flesh thou didst bear Christ God, Who saves our souls!

After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns

of the Apostles. Tone 7:

As the helmsmen of our salvation, the most wise Apostles of Christ: let us honor with songs and hymns as is meet; for they drove away the impiety of delusion and saved the world, as eyewitnesses and ministers of the Word, and His friends and brethren!

Martyrs:

Thy Martyrs, O Lord, overcame the enemy and put idolatrous deceit to shame, being armed with the power of Thy Cross: therefore singing with the Angels, they cry aloud the victory hymn, glorifying Thee, O Christ: by their prayers grant cleansing and great mercy unto our souls!

[f. 218rA] ...grant cleansing and great mercy unto our souls!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

Rejoice, for the unavoidable and unchangeable Word became flesh and dwelt among us! Rejoice, pure one, rejoicing of the Apostles and Martyrs, and salvation unto us the faithful! Rejoice, Mother of Christ God!

After the 3rd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns

*of the Apostles. Tone 7.*

*Podoben: "Fruit of thy womb" (Пло́дъ чре́ва твое́го):*

All-praised disciples of the Lord, who like luminaries illuminated the whole inhabited earth: pray that I may be enlightened, who am in the darkness of passions and transgressions!

Being luminaries unto the world, O Apostles of the Lord: ye ever cause the word to shine forth unto the faithful, driving away the mist of wicked delusion: therefore by baptism ye also enlighten the nations, being ever-honored preachers of the Trinity!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

O thou who didst bring forth Joy unto the world, O Virgin: unceasingly pray with the Apostles unto thy Son, that He may grant us forgiveness of transgressions and reformation of life!

CANON to the Holy Apostles.

Work of Theophanes.

Ode 1. Tone 7. Heirmos:

By Thy nod upon the earth:

Troparia:

Having become God-beholders through divine assent, when ye brought the ungodly to completion, ye lifted them up unto divine love, O all-honorable Apostles of Christ!

Called as the salt of all the earth, O loud-voiced Apostles of the Lord: stop all the rotting [f. 218rB] of my heart, and heal that which is grievously corrupted!

When the most righteous Judge of all is about to sit with you in His second coming, O divine Apostles: then deliver us from all condemnation!

Theotokion:

O all-pure Birth-giver of God, with the Bodiless Angels, the Prophets, the Martyrs, and the Apostles: pray that we may receive remission of transgressions and rich mercy!

Another Canon to Saint Nicholas.

Work of Joseph.

Ode 1. Tone 7. Heirmos:

Unto God Who worked salvation:

Having gloriously passed through life upon earth, O Nicholas: make them that glorify thee partakers of the glory that is there!

Sailing across the deep of corruptible life, tossed by the billows of temptations, O all-blessed one, we are surrounded: preserve us therefrom!

Extend unto me now a helpful hand, O father Nicholas: and deliver me from enemies visible and invisible!

Theotokion:

He Who created the bodiless ministers, O Birth-giver of God, was born of thee through ineffable mercy, and was seen as man!

Canon of the Apostles.

Ode 3. Heirmos:

In the beginning the heavens, O Almighty:

As the heavens declare the glory of God, as the Prophet said, so do ye proclaim it, O divine disciples, explaining His divine incarnation, O most wise ones, and His passions, whereby ye delivered all from passions, death, and corruption!

Sharpened arrows of Christ the Mighty One...[^296]

[f. 218vA] ...having been shown forth: from the arrows of the evil one deliver me, O most wise disciples of the Lord, and heal my heart that is grievously wounded by the weapon of sin!

Me who am grievously deceived and stripped naked of divine garments: make haste to enlighten with divine garments, O disciples of Christ, who through faith laid bare all the wiles of the enemy, and clothed him with shame!

Theotokion:

O God, Who by Thy Word didst fashion the heavenly hosts, and didst grant grace unto the Prophets, disciples, and all the Martyrs: by their supplications and of Thine all-pure Mother, O Savior of all, have compassion, as Thou art merciful!

Another Canon [to St. Nicholas].

Ode 3. Heirmos:

Thou Who didst establish the heavens by Thy Word, and didst make firm the earthly foundation upon many waters: establish my mind in Thy will, O only Lover of mankind!

Offering supplications for the inhabited earth, in great necessity and unnumbered sorrows, save us, O hierarch Nicholas!

As thou didst deliver them that were bound in the inescapable prison, breaking the bonds of my evils by thy prayers: reconcile me unto God, O hierarch Nicholas!

Night and day we call upon thee as our protector: offer our supplications unto the Lord, ever preserving us, O hierarch Nicholas!

Theotokion:

As the bush that received the Divine Fire within thy divine womb and was not consumed: burn up our transgressions, O all-pure one!

[f. 218vB] Canon of the Apostles.

Ode 4. Heirmos:

Without leaving the Father's bosom:

The Son Who shares the throne with the Father, having become incarnate upon earth as man: chose you as disciples, to proclaim His divinity unto all the nations!

In the Creator of all, fallen into passions and wounded in mind, wounded in heart by the robbers of passions: heal me with mercy, O Apostles, physicians of the sick!

Deliver us from passions and grievous dangers, and sorrows, O glorious Apostles, and from every assault and endless torment!

Chosen Mother of God, with the holy Apostles, Martyrs, and Prophets, pray: that He may deliver us from dangers, sorrows, and transgressions!

Another Canon [to St. Nicholas].

Ode 4. Heirmos: Thy virtue covered the heavens:

By thy wisdom obscuring the mind that of old was darkened by heresy: thou hast now enlightened them that were deceived, O Nicholas!

Heal my many wounds by thy God-acceptable prayers, O God-blessed father Nicholas, and enlighten my heart!

Having put to death passionate stirrings: by thy prayers make me alive and renew me, all-blessed one, who am put to death by them!

Theotokion:

In the flesh thou didst bear the Beneficent One, Whom do thou entreat to deliver us from long-standing evils, O all-immaculate helper!

Canon of the Apostles.

Ode 5. Heirmos:

O Lord my God, from the night I awake early unto Thee, I pray Thee: grant me remission [f. 219rA] of my transgressions, and direct my path unto the light of Thy commandments, I pray Thee!

O Lord my God, Who of old didst grant Thy peace unto Thine Apostles: by their prayers grant peace and remission of transgressions unto all!

O Lord my God, Who knowest the transgressions of my soul, and the uncorrected disposition of my heart: freely have compassion upon me and save me, through the prayers of the Apostles!

O Lord my God, Who for Thy supreme goodness didst save the thief and the harlot when they sinned: through the prayers of Thine Apostles, have compassion also upon me, the prodigal!

O Lord my God, born of the Virgin that knew not wedlock: through her prayers and of Thine Apostles, grant me cleansing of transgressions, and deliver me from future torment!

Another Canon [to St. Nicholas].

Ode 5. Heirmos: In the morning my spirit:

The counsels of undisciplined men that are continually stirred up against us, make of no effect by thy prayers, O Nicholas!

Break the bonds of our evils by thy prayers, thou who didst bind the malice of the soul-destroying serpent, all-holy Nicholas!

Slipping continually in our disposition and held fast by a multitude of grievous things, O father Nicholas, we call upon thee as our fervent protector!

O Sovereign Lady of all creation, who hast power to reign without passion: completely free my humble heart!

Canon of the Apostles.

Ode 6. Heirmos:

Floating on the sea:

Having become divine disciples by His wisdom, they made foolish the wisdom of the Greeks, and destroyed the malice of the wise, and being most wise they enlightened them that wandered in ignorance unto piety!

[f. 219rB] Thou Who of old didst cleanse Peter's denial through tears: by his prayers cleanse the unnumbered transgressions of my soul, according to Thy great loving-kindness and surpassing grace, O Christ!

Thou Who of old didst have compassion upon the Ninevites who repented: by Thine own loving-kindness have mercy upon me for the sake of Thine Apostles, and deliver me from being surrendered to many torments for the multitude of my transgressions, O Redeemer!

Theotokion:

O thou who didst bear the Light: enlighten my soul that is darkened by passions; and pray, with the Apostles, Prophets, and Martyrs, to deliver me from great sin, from every harm, and from all the malice of the enemy!

Another Canon [to St. Nicholas].

Ode 6. Heirmos: Jonah cried from the belly of hades:

Thou didst annul the unjust condemnation of death, and by thy mercy didst save them that were about to die, O father Nicholas, as a fervent protector of them that call upon thee!

Stop the diseases of our souls, and ward off the impending dangers from them that love thee, O most holy shepherd!

Thou didst consume the bitter pasture of Arius's impiety, O Nicholas, by the mingling of thy words, O sacred initiate: thou art the confirmation of the Orthodox!

Heal the wounds...[^297]

[f. 219vA] Heal, O all-immaculate one, my wretched soul that is incurably sick with worldly delusions and grown old through many sins!

Canon of the Apostles.

Ode 7. Heirmos:

The Children in the fiery furnace:

The furnace of bitter godlessness of old did ye extinguish, O glorious Apostles, with the dew of divine preaching, crying aloud: Blessed and supremely praised is the God of our fathers!

From grievous sin, O Christ, from torment in hades, and from sickness in Gehenna, snatch me away and save me, O Word, through the supplications and prayers of Thine Apostles!

Having caught men with the net of the Word out of the deep of ignorance: save me, O disciples of Christ, who am submerged in boundless transgressions and defiled!

Theotokion:

With the Angels, the Martyrs, and the Apostles, O all-immaculate one, pray unto thine own Son and Lord: that He may save thy servants from all temptations and sorrows!

Another Canon [to St. Nicholas].

*Ode 7. Heirmos: The Children of old showed the fiery furnace...*

Having become a spiritual vessel of the Church, O most wise one, deliver me from every ugliness of dishonorable passions, entreating the Benefactor of the whole world, O hierarch Nicholas!

With the showers of thy prayers, O wise Nicholas, water the hearts of all of us: that we may bring forth unto thee fruits of divine virtues, mediating an unending life!

Enlighten our thoughts through prayers, who awake early in faith and pray unto God, O holy Nicholas, who by thy prayers didst destroy the temple of Artemis!

[f. 219vB] Theotokion:

Every nation glorifies thee in faith, O pure one: as the only glory and praise of our race, and the guide of the wandering, O all-blessed Birth-giver of God!

Canon of the Apostles.

Ode 8. Heirmos:

Unconsumed by fire on Sinai:

Kindled with the spiritual Fire as coals: like reeds the disciples of Christ burned up all idolatrous deceit, and enlightened the souls of the faithful, crying: Let all works of the Lord praise the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

Enlighten my soul that is darkened by sin, and my heart that is now grown rough with dishonorable passions, O partakers of the everlasting Light, Apostles of Christ: that I may unceasingly cry: Let all works of the Lord praise the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

Heal my wounded soul that is bitten by venomous bites of pride, O Thou Who didst receive wounds in the flesh: through the prayers of Thy sacred disciples: and save me who praise Thee: Let all works of the Lord praise the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

Theotokion:

Having brought forth the Fire, thou wast preserved unburnt, O all-pure Virgin Mother: therefore pray unto Him Whom thou didst bear, with the bodiless choirs and with the Apostles: to save them that praise in faith: Let all works of the Lord praise the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

Another Canon [to St. Nicholas].

Ode 8. Heirmos: Likened unto the Children in the furnace:

Having received the grace of the Spirit, likened unto the Children in the furnace, in faith we cry aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; praise the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

Thy body lying in Myra, all-holy Nicholas, and smelling of fragrant myrrh, pours forth streams of myrrh unto them that run thither, and assuages diseases!

He Who is the Creator and Lord of the world showed thee forth as a protector unto the world; therefore, O Nicholas, unto them that now call upon thee thou art found a ready deliverer!

There is none that calls upon thee in sorrows and doth not quickly find comfort; therefore we pray thee, Nicholas: lighten all our sicknesses!

Theotokion:

Every tongue praises and glorifies thee: for thou didst bear the all-hymned God, O Bride of God: unceasingly pray unto Him for our souls!

Canon of the Apostles.

Ode 9. Heirmos:

She who brought forth the fountain of incorruption:

As sons of the light and the day did the Word of God the Father show you forth, O divine Apostles who loved Him: luminaries unto the inhabited earth, destroyers of the Greeks, guides of the wandering, firm foundations of the Church!

Bearing the light yoke of the plow of the Word upon your necks, renew now my soul that is frozen with passions, and make it fruitful with the seed of repentance!

Me who have despised Thy divine laws, and have become a dwelling of demons and a workshop of every sin: have compassion upon me, O Word, through the prayers of Thy glorious Apostles, as Thou art the Lover of mankind!

Send me not into the fire prepared for me: the Virgin who bore Thee entreats Thee, and the divine bodiless choirs [f. 220rB] Apostles, Prophets, Martyrs, Hierarchs, and all the righteous: O all-compassionate and most merciful One!

Another Canon [to St. Nicholas].

Ode 9. Heirmos: Her that is Mother above nature and Virgin:

Thou didst follow the customs of the sacred Apostles, and didst inherit their throne, O venerable hierarch, worthy of all blessing, Nicholas!

As a divine zealot and a helper everywhere, the Creator showed thee forth greatly unto the whole world, O blessed one, unto them that fervently call upon thee!

With a contrite heart we cry aloud unto thee, O father: be comfort unto us in sorrows, ever dispelling grief from our souls, O Nicholas!

The cutting down of death lies like an axe upon the tree for thee, O soul: be not slothful therefore, but make haste to show forth the fruits of repentance!

Theotokion:

Bearing Him Who bears all things in thine arms, O pure one: entreat Him that we may be saved unharmed from alien evildoing!

Aposticha Stichera

to the Holy Apostles, Tone 7:

Glorious Apostles, pillars of the Church, true preachers, being radiant luminaries: in the spiritual fire ye burned up the great deceit, and enlightened the human race through faith: therefore we pray you: entreat our Savior and God, to give peace unto the world and save our souls!

Apostles of Christ, laborers of the Savior...[^298]

[f. 220vA] ...bearing the Cross upon your shoulders like a plow, plowing the earth that was barren through idolatrous deceit: ye sowed the word of faith, and are worthily praised, O holy Apostles of Christ!

Martyrs:

United in mind, and looking unto the One, the passion-bearing Martyrs found the one path of life, even death for Christ: equally emulating one another in their end!

O wonder! Like treasuries of torments snatching away the contest, one said unto another: "If we die not now, we shall die in any case; let us render what is due unto our nature! Let us make a necessity into an honor, and buy what is common by giving our own: by death let us purchase life!" By their prayers, O God, have mercy upon us!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

Ineffably born of the Virgin, Thou didst enlighten the nations, all crying: O Lord, glory to Thee!

ON THURSDAY,

Beatitudes. Tone 7:

Beautiful was that fruit and good for food which put me to death; but Christ is the Tree of Life, whereof eating I die not, but cry aloud with the Thief: Remember me, O Lord, when Thou comest into Thy Kingdom!

[f. 220vB] From the deep edge of evils, O most wise Apostles, ye caught the flocks of the nations unto the God-comely faith, and faithfully brought all as well-instructed disciples unto the spiritual table, O glorious Apostles!

Martyrs:

Having driven away the darkness of grievous deceit by the light of preaching, O Apostles of the Lord: ye enlightened the hearts of us, the pious: therefore in divine songs we call you blessed!

Severed limb from limb by the sword, O divine sufferers: ye remained unsevered from the love of the Redeemer; unto Whom having ascended, ye now live in joy, all irradiated with eternal glory!

Glory: Triadikon:

Evil-ending, the corrupter of the human race holds me fast: by the prayers of Thy preachers, O almighty Trinity, snatch me away from this burning, that I may magnify Thine immeasurable mercy!

Now and ever: Stavrotheotokion:

O Virgin, from thy pure blood, O all-pure one, thou didst bring forth the Son Who shares the throne with the Father, bearing mortal flesh, that He might renew the nature of earthly beings: therefore as is meet all we call thee blessed!

## THURSDAY EVENING VESPERS (FOR FRIDAY) (TONE 7)

ON THURSDAY EVENING, AT "LORD, I HAVE CRIED":

*Stichera of the Cross, Tone 7.*

*Podoben: "No longer are we forbidden" (Не ктомꙋ̀ возбране́ни е҆смы̀):*

That Thou mightest make man a god, Thou becamest man, O all-good Christ, and wast crucified: glory to Thy power!

When the Jewish council desired to crucify Thee, O Jesus: the earth was shaken, and the light of the sun was hidden!

The crown of thorns [f. 221rA] wherewith the lawless crowned Thee, O Immortal One: uprooted the thorns of deceit, renewing mankind!

Other Stichera to the Most Holy Theotokos,

*Tone 7.*

*Podoben: "Today Judas watches" (Дне́сь І҆ꙋ́да):*

Beholding the Lamb stretched upon the Tree, the spotless Ewe-lamb and Virgin, between two thieves, cried aloud: "Woe is me, my sweetest Child! What is this strange and most glorious mystery? How hath the lawless council lifted Thee up upon the Cross, and given gall to drink unto Him Who satisfied men with manna?"

When the Virgin and Thy Mother beheld Thee nailed upon the Cross, O my Christ, by the judgment of the lawless, by the Jews in the Place of the Skull, she cried aloud: "Woe is me, my most beloved Son! What is this strange sight? How do the senseless children of the Hebrews nail Thee upon the Cross, Who art the Lord of all?"

Thee alone, O all-hymned Sovereign Lady, did we know as Virgin after childbearing, and seeing Him Whom thou didst bear without seed willingly nailing His hands upon the Tree, the all-pure one weeping cried aloud: "Willingly, O Long-suffering One, Thou diest, delivering from death all them that praise Thee!"

Glory: Now and ever: Stavrotheotokion:

O all-hymned Sovereign Lady, Virgin who didst bear the Lord, Who for compassion's sake was nailed upon the Cross and poured forth streams of life unto the world: do thou entreat Him that our souls may be saved; for thee alone have we, the faithful, as refuge, rampart, and protection: therefore do we flee [f. 221rB] unto thy protection!

Aposticha Stichera

to the Cross. Tone 7:

No longer are we forbidden from the Tree of Life, having the hope of Thy Cross: O Lord, glory to Thee!

Having been hanged upon the Tree, O Immortal One, Thou didst break the snares of the devil: O Lord, glory to Thee!

Glory to Thee, O Christ God, praise of the Apostles and rejoicing of the Martyrs, whose preaching was the Consubstantial Trinity!

Glory: Now and ever: Stavrotheotokion:

Beholding Thee willingly nailed upon the Tree, O all-immaculate one, weeping she sang praise unto Thy dominion, O Master!

After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymns

of the Cross. Tone 7:

Jacob cries aloud unto Thee, O Christ God, worshipping Thee through the pine, the cedar, and the cypress: grant victories unto our hierarchs, O Compassionate One, and have mercy upon us!

Thou Who for my sake didst endure being nailed upon the Cross: accept also my unslumbering supplication, O Christ God, as Thou art the Lover of mankind!

Glory: Now and ever: Stavrotheotokion:

Being ever preserved by the Cross of thy Son, O Virgin, we escape the assault of heretical errors; therefore, as is meet, praising thee we glorify thee, O all-hymned Birth-giver of God!

After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns

of the Cross. Tone 7:

A fire brighter and more efficacious than flame hast Thou shown forth the Tree...[^299]

[f. 221vA] ...of Thy Cross, which burns up the sins of men and enlightens the hearts of them that sing: O Christ God, glory to Thee for Thy voluntary Crucifixion!

Today beholding the elevation of Thy Cross, ever falling down in faith and kissing it with songs and singing, in fear and joy: cleanse Thy servants, and give peace unto Thy world by its manifestation, O Thou Who alone art most merciful!

Martyrs:

Pray ye, O holy ones, that forgiveness of our transgressions may be granted unto us, and that we may be delivered from grievous secret sins and bitter death, we pray you!

Glory: Now and ever: Stavrotheotokion:

Beholding her Son hanging upon the Cross, O pure Birth-giver of God, ever Virgin, weeping like a Mother, the unwedded Sovereign Lady magnified His dreadful condescension!

After the 3rd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns

of the Cross. Tone 7:

Thy precious Cross, O Christ, hath become a weapon and an invincible victory unto the world; wherewith casting down the invisible enemies, we thankfully sing praise unto Thee!

O Thou Who by the Tree of the Cross didst heal the condemnation of Adam: heal our incurable contusions, and save us!

Glory: Now and ever: Stavrotheotokion:

The Fruit of thy womb, O all-pure one, hath planted the Cross in the ends of the earth and delivered the world from corruption: therefore, O most glorious one, we magnify thee!

CANON

to the Precious and Life-giving Cross of the Lord.

Creation of Joseph.

Ode 1. Tone 7. Heirmos:

Let us shake Pharaoh in the Red Sea before God: let us sing a song of victory, for He hath been glorified!

Troparia:

Lifted up upon the Cross, O Christ, Thou didst draw all men unto Thyself, and didst cast down the enemy who had cast down all!

[f. 221vB] From Thy life-bearing side, O Jesus, Thou didst pour forth the stream of my life, and didst slay the enemy, having become as one dead!

Martyrs:

Offer supplication diligently unto Christ for us, O passion-bearers: that all may be delivered from the dreadful judgment!

Having humbled yourselves for the sake of Christ, O most wise Martyrs: by divine grace ye cast down the proud enemy!

Theotokion:

Beholding Him Who shone forth from thee in exceedingly great compassion upon the Cross, O Sovereign Lady, thou didst weep, glorifying Him!

Another Canon to the Most Holy Theotokos.

Ode 1. Tone 7. Heirmos: The same.

When our forefather Adam fell under corruption, having been deceived: thou didst renew him, O all-pure one, having borne God in the flesh!

With joy I cry aloud unto thee the voice of Gabriel, O pure one: Rejoice, expectation of all, O all-pure Bride of God!

My deadened mind, by the action of the Life Who was truly born of thee, O all-pure Virgin, do thou make alive!

They that bless thee in faith are manifestly blessed of God; for thou didst bear the Fountain of blessing, O only all-immaculate, all-lauded one!

Ode 3. Heirmos:

The Church of Christ hath been established by faith: the heaven unceasingly cries aloud with hymns, praising:

[f. 222rA] praising: Holy art Thou, O Lord, and my spirit sings praise unto Thee!

Troparia:

"The Sinless One is moved: how did He endure suffering, Who is breathing life unto me? How was He put to death upon the Tree?" Thy Mother beat her breast, crying aloud at Thy long-suffering, O Savior!

Lifted up unjustly upon the Cross between thieves, O Word: by faith Thou didst justify him that acknowledged Thee as Creator of all creation, willingly suffering!

Martyrs:

Enduring the tearing of your flesh, the severance of hands and feet, and every torment of limbs, O passion-bearers: ye were accounted worthy of glory, O youths!

Having been divinely enlightened by the multitude of torments, surpassing glory, O most wise ones, ye now inherit: ever praying for our souls!

Theotokion:

Entreat for us remission of debts, O Virgin Mother, and grant it through thy prayers, having borne God the Word made man, Who was nailed upon the Cross!

Another Canon [to the Theotokos].

Ode 3. Heirmos: The same.

God showed thee forth on the mountain unto Moses the Lawgiver as a living, all-holy tabernacle; for thou becamest the dwelling-place of Him Who sanctifies all!

We all know thee, O Virgin, as holy earth, who hast sprouted forth for us without seed the beauteous Ear of Wheat, Jesus Christ, Who nourishes them that call thee blessed, O Virgin, in faith and love!

The goings of the most high God from thee, O Virgin, were seen, when He was ineffably incarnate; for thou becamest the Mother of Him Who reigns over all!

Ever guided, the Church of Christ glorifies thee before God: O Virgin Mother of God [f. 222rB] thou didst bear the incarnate Savior unto them that sing praise unto thee, O Virgin!

Ode 4. Heirmos:

I heard Thy report, and was afraid; I understood Thy works, and glorified Thee, O Lord, Lover of mankind!

Troparia:

Lifted up upon the Cross like the fairest cluster of grapes: Thou dost pour forth the new wine of gladness unto all, O Lover of mankind!

As Thou didst receive voluntary suffering in Thy flesh, O Master: Thou didst put an end to the painful sufferings of men!

Martyrs:

Being wounded with wounds, O passion-bearers: ye became the wounders of the adversary, and appeared as physicians unto our souls!

The passion-bearers set themselves in array against the tormentors; and having conquered, they were crowned with the triumphant wreath!

Theotokion:

Without seed thou didst bring forth the Word, O Virgin: Who by the Cross destroyed corruption through His goodness!

Another Canon [to the Theotokos].

Ode 4. Heirmos: The same.

Habakkuk heard of thee, O all-pure mountain, being enlightened by spiritual shadows, that God was manifest incarnate from thee!

The Orthodox assembly is made upright, singing praise unto thee, the all-holy Mother of God, and crying with the Archangel: "Rejoice!"

The face of Nestorius is confounded, who was unwilling to confess thee as pure Birth-giver of God; for thou didst truly bear God, O all-pure one!

Having found thee beauteous and radiant in virtues, the Bridegroom took up His abode in thee, and made thee the all-holy Birth-giver of God!

Ode 5. Heirmos: My spirit seeks Thee early in the morning, O Christ...[^300]

[f. 222vA] Lifted up upon the Tree in the flesh, O Master: Thou didst deliver all creation from the cruel slavery of folly unto Thy knowledge, O Lover of mankind!

Upon the Place of the Skull, the lawless and unjust people crucified Thee, O Jesus, Who crushest the venomous head of the serpent!

Martyrs:

Ye extinguished the torrents of impiety, O Martyrs of Christ, by your divine blood, and therein drowned Pharaoh the tormentor!

Being mercilessly scraped with claws, O passion-bearers, ye tore in pieces the hearts of the wise tormentors by your reproof, and became victors!

Theotokion:

God entered thy womb, O holy and pure one, and was seen as Emmanuel lifted up upon the Cross, raising up creation with Himself!

Another Canon [to the Theotokos].

Ode 5. Heirmos: The same.

The all-holy turtledove, beauty of God, most sweet and purifying: having desired thy beauty, the Master God took up His abode in the Virgin!

O all-holy and light-bearing gate of grace, who shinest upon the universe with the light of the Sun: having illumined us, O Maiden, enlighten them that sing praise unto thee!

Accounting thee as the bush, O Virgin Mother: may we be accounted worthy through thee, O Mother of God, to obtain the passing kingdom and food!

Thou wast shown forth as the temple of the all-seeing Almighty, Who found thy womb more honorable than the heavens and took up His abode therein, O all-venerable Birth-giver of God!

Ode 6. Heirmos:

Jonah cried aloud from the belly of hades: Lead my life up from corruption! And we cry aloud unto Thee, O almighty Savior: Have mercy upon us!

[f. 222vB] Troparia:

When human nature fell sick, Thou didst appear in compassion, O Savior, as a Physician unto the suffering; and by Thy Cross and Passion Thou didst heal it!

By the tree Adam was first condemned; but by the Tree of the Cross he hath now been justified, receiving entrance into Paradise and the enjoyment thereof once again!

We sing praise unto Thee Who wast lifted up upon the Cross; we glorify Thee, the most good King, Who wast crowned with endurance and dost crown men with glory!

Martyrs:

Having now passed through the threefold waves of torments, the passion-bearers, clad in suffering, died with Christ: neither persecution, nor famine, nor nakedness, nor peril, nor death could by any means separate the divine sufferers from the love of Christ!

Theotokion:

In sorrow of heart thou didst behold Him Who was incarnate of thee, O pure and all-immaculate Virgin Mother, weeping as thou didst look upon Him lifted up upon the Cross!

Another Canon [to the Theotokos].

Ode 6. Heirmos: The same.

Thou didst bear the One Who lived among men, O Virgin Birth-giver of God, the only Savior Who grants life unto mankind!

Emmanuel, O Birth-giver of God, Whom thou didst bear according to essence, the perfect Word before all ages, incarnate God Who grants redemption unto us!

The Ark that contained the tables of the law prefigured thee, O Birth-giver of God, as having received the Word of God in thy womb, incarnate for our sake!

Ode 7. Heirmos:

[f. 223rA] The Children in the furnace of burning fire of old showed it forth dewy, singing of the one God and saying: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

Troparia:

Thou didst lighten the weight of my transgressions, lifted up upon the Cross between the lawless, O most good Lord, God of our fathers, Who art supremely exalted: Blessed art Thou!

Pierced with a spear in Thy divine side, O God, Thou didst make upright the slip of the rib, ever commanding the flaming sword to grant me entrance into Paradise, O Savior!

Martyrs:

Having become stars set upon the heights of the Church, the Martyrs enlighten creation by the manifestations of their sufferings and by the radiance of healings!

The Book of the living ever brings the names of the Lord's Martyrs written therein, who fervently preserved the divine commandments and valiantly suffered!

Theotokion:

The all-holy Mother, beholding the all-holy Word Who came forth from her lifted up upon the holy Cross and cleansing mankind, wept aloud!

Another Canon [to the Theotokos].

Ode 7. Heirmos: The same.

We thankfully offer unto thee the "Rejoice," O Mother of God, having truly been delivered through thee from every difficulty, and harmoniously crying aloud: In majesty and joy we magnify thee!

David the forefather of God describes thy glory, O Virgin, and divinely proclaims thee as Queen of creation standing at the right hand of God the Father, O all-immaculate one!

[f. 223rB] Thou hast renewed the nature of earthborn beings, O pure one, by the renewal of thy childbearing; therefore we cry aloud unto thee, O Virgin: Blessed unto all ages is God, the Fruit of thy womb!

Condemned Adam, held fast by death, is led up by the second Adam through thee, O all-pure one, crying: Blessed art Thou, Who hast renewed him by Thy birthgiving!

Ode 8. Heirmos:

The only beginningless King of glory, Whom the heavenly hosts praise and the angelic ranks tremble before: Praise Him, ye priests, and supremely exalt Him, ye people, unto all ages!

Troparia:

The tree of knowledge showed me dead; but Thou, O my Christ, having been put to death upon the Tree, didst make me alive and enlighten me to sing: Praise Him, ye priests, and supremely exalt Him, ye people, unto all ages!

The lawless assembly crowned Thee with patience, O King, disobeying the long-suffering of Adam the first-formed; and they lifted Thee upon the Cross, Who didst deliver all from headlong fall!

Martyrs:

O Word Who didst stretch out the heavens by Thy wisdom: the senseless people stretched Thee upon the Tree, Who by Thy Passion dost heal our passions, O Savior, and forgivest sicknesses by the pain of the nails!

The relics of the Martyrs pour forth sweet-smelling fragrances of miracles unto them that approach with undoubting heart, ever driving away the stench of passions and granting health from God unto all!

Theotokion:

The ranks of the angels beseech the Maiden, for He Who came forth from thy womb...[^301]

[f. 223vA] God Who came forth from thee, O pure Virgin, showed forth unto these holy ones the sufferings upon the Cross; and they bless thee as more honorable than all!

Another Canon [to the Theotokos].

Ode 8. Heirmos: The same.

The incomprehensible Master of all, Whom the heavens cannot contain, O Mother of God: is contained in thy womb, O Virgin; therefore we, the faithful, supremely exalt thee in love unto all ages!

Him Who is beyond the mind of all creation, O Maiden, Whose birth human nature cannot behold: thou didst carry in thine all-pure arms; therefore we, the faithful, supremely exalt thee in love unto all ages!

Having borne the Word, entreat Him, O Virgin: to send down salvation unto them that faithfully honor thee, deliverance from perils, speedy changing of grievous sicknesses, and eternal grace!

Seeing thee adorned with diverse virtues and enlightened, O all-holy Virgin, as the Church of the Most High: we piously sing praise unto thee and glorify thee unto all ages!

Ode 9. Heirmos:

O all-pure one, higher than the heavens, who didst conceive the beginningless Word in thy womb and bear God incarnate unto men: therefore all we ever magnify thee!

Troparia:

When the sun beheld Thee lifted up upon the Cross, O King of all, it was extinguished, and the earth was shaken, and the veil of the temple was rent in twain, unable to endure Thy radiance, O almighty Jesus!

The lawless dug through Thy hands and feet, and pierced Thy life-bearing side with a spear, and gave Thee gall and vinegar to drink, O my Christ, Who art the Sweetness of all and true God!

[f. 223vB] Martyrs:

The valiant passion-bearers crushed the evil-originating demons by manifold forms of torments; and having become crown-bearers in victory, they are called blessed!

By the laying down of their relics the passion-bearers cleansed all the earth, and put an end to the filth of idol sacrifices, having offered themselves unto the fire and therein mystically been ignited!

Theotokion:

O comely one, holier than the Cherubim, who didst bear God the Word incarnate in the flesh: pray diligently unto Him for all, Who was willingly lifted up upon the Cross!

Another Canon [to the Theotokos].

Ode 9. Heirmos: The same.

Divinely perfected humanity was assumed from thee, O all-pure Maiden, united unto the Word, flesh animate, adorned with the Word: therefore all we, the faithful, magnify thee!

Let Egyptian praise now be silent; but let the trumpet of David divinely sound, praising thee, O Virgin, with radiant voices, and confessing thee as the true Birth-giver of God!

Humanity was now pitied through thee, being truly united in person unto the Word: and God, having become man, was lifted up, O Virgin: therefore all we ever magnify thee!

Foreknowing by prophetic sharp vision the mystery of thy childbearing, O Maiden, that thou didst bear God incarnate unto men, Who delivers us from temptations: by thy prayers save us!

[f. 224rA] Aposticha Stichera

of the Cross. Tone 7:

Being the Master, Lover of mankind, and Giver of life, Thou didst redeem the universe by Thy Cross: O Lord, glory to Thee!

The true Vine was nailed upon the Cross, embracing the nations: the Paradise of the Church with the Thief! Lo, this is the glory of the Church; lo, this is the richness of the Kingdom: O Thou Who didst suffer for our sake, Lord, glory to Thee!

Martyrs:

Celebrating the memory of Thy holy passion-bearers, we sing praise unto Thee, O Christ, crying aloud: O Lord, glory to Thee!

Glory: Now and ever: Stavrotheotokion:

Beholding her Son upon the Tree of old, the grief of a sword wounded the heart of the all-pure one!

ON FRIDAY AT THE DIVINE LITURGY:

Beatitudes. Tone 7:

Beautiful was that fruit and good for food which put me to death; but Christ is the Tree of Life, whereof eating I die not, but cry aloud with the Thief: Remember me, O Lord, when Thou comest into Thy Kingdom!

Healing the disease of Adam, which he received through the counsel of the enemy, Thou wast lifted up upon the Tree of the Cross, O Christ King, and didst endure suffering, having Thy hands and feet nailed: therefore we glorify Thy long-suffering, O Word!

[f. 224rB] In the midst of the lawless the Jewish assembly crucified Thee, the only Lawgiver and Deliverer, Who deliverest the human race from every transgression, O Christ: therefore we sing praise unto Thee!

Martyrs:

Bearing the wounds of many torments like beauteous ornaments, the valiant sufferers were manifestly recognized as the adornment of the Church: ever praying for our souls!

Glory: Triadikon:

O Holy Trinity, deliver Thy faithful servants from torments, who have believed in Thee as God, piously glorifying the one Godhead unceasingly; and grant Thy eternal Kingdom!

Now and ever: Stavrotheotokion:

Having neither form nor beauty, O Christ, when the all-immaculate Virgin beheld Thee lifted up in the flesh upon the Tree of the Cross, she sighed in pain: "Woe is me, my Child! How have the dark, lawless ones wounded Thee?"

## FRIDAY EVENING VESPERS (FOR SATURDAY) (TONE 7)

ON FRIDAY EVENING, AT "LORD, I HAVE CRIED":

Stichera to the Holy Martyrs, Hierarchs, and Venerable Monastics.

*Tone 7.*

*Podoben: "No longer are we forbidden" (Нїкто́мꙋ возбра́няеми):*

The Martyrs quenched the fire, and drove away idol deceit, showing forth in their time the light of the knowledge of God unto men!

By Orthodox teachings, with divine beams, ye illumined the Church of the Lord, O all-lauded pastors, in every...[^302]

[f. 224vA] ...way ye broke the snares, dwelling continually in the trackless wilderness, O venerable fathers!

Other Stichera to the Holy Martyrs.

Glory to Thee, O Christ God: the praise of the Apostles and the joy of the Martyrs, whose preaching was the Consubstantial Trinity! (Twice)

Holy Martyrs, who valiantly suffered and were crowned: pray unto the Lord, that our souls may have mercy!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

Thou wast known as a Mother beyond nature...

Aposticha Stichera

to the Martyrs. Tone 7:

Disregarding all earthly things, O holy Martyrs, and valiantly confessing Christ in the judgment hall: ye received from Him the reward of your sufferings; but as ye have boldness: pray unto Him as almighty God to save our souls, who flee unto you, we pray!

All-lauded Martyrs, spiritual armor, rational whole-burnt offerings, acceptable sacrifices well-pleasing unto God: the earth hid you not, but heaven received you! Ye were made partakers with the Angels; with them pray, we beseech you, unto our Savior and God, to give peace unto the world and save our souls!

*Hymn for the Departed (Поко́инъ):*

O Thou Who in the beginning didst create man according to Thine own image and likeness, and didst set him in Paradise to rule over Thy creatures; but being deceived through the envy of the devil, he partook of the food, becoming a transgressor of Thy commandments: therefore Thou didst condemn him, O Lord, to return again unto the earth whence he was taken, and to ask for rest!

[f. 224vB] *Hymn for the Departed (Поко́инъ):*

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

O thou who alone didst contain the Uncontainable and didst bear God the Word incarnate: pray that our souls may be saved!

## SATURDAY MATINS: ALL SAINTS, MARTYRS, AND THE DEPARTED (TONE 7)

ON SATURDAY AT MATINS.

After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymns

to the Martyrs. Tone 7:

Pray ye, O holy ones, that forgiveness of our transgressions may be granted unto us, and that we may be delivered from grievous secret sins and bitter death, we pray you!

Thy holy ones, O Lord, having struggled upon the earth, trod down the enemy and abolished idol deceit: therefore they also received crowns from Thee, the Master Who lovest mankind and merciful God, Who grantest great mercy unto the world!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

As the treasury of our resurrection, O all-hymned one, lead us up from the pit and depth of transgressions, who hope in thee; for thou hast saved them that were guilty of sin, having borne our Salvation: who wast a Virgin before childbearing, a Virgin in childbearing, and after childbearing art still a Virgin!

After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns

to the Martyrs. Tone 7:

Rejoice, ye righteous, and let the heavens be glad! For the Martyrs having struggled upon earth, abolished deceit!

[f. 225rA] Let the Church dance, triumphantly celebrating the contest of the athletes, and sending up honor unto Christ God, the only Triumphant One, Who grantest great mercy unto the world!

Thy Martyrs, O Lord, conquered the enemy and put to shame idol deceit, being armed with the power of Thy Cross: therefore, singing with the Angels, they send up a hymn of victory, glorifying Thee, O Christ! By their supplications grant unto our souls cleansing and great mercy!

In the land of the living, O Lord, and in the tabernacles of Thy righteous ones, do Thou place those whose memory we celebrate, O Lover of mankind! And whatsoever they have sinned in this common life, as Thou art merciful and easily reconciled God, forgive, granting great mercy unto the world!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

O unwedded Maiden, all-immaculate, who from thy blood didst bear our incarnate God: ever pray with the Prophets and the holy Martyrs, that our souls may be saved!

to the Holy Martyrs, Hierarchs, Venerable Monastics, and the Departed.

Creation of Joseph.

Ode 1. Tone 7. Heirmos:

Troparia:

The choir of Martyrs, having conquered every deceit of the adversary, rejoice together before the face of Him Who created them!

Hierarchs of Christ and all venerable ones who have struggled: ye were accounted worthy of eternal sustenance by grace!

[f. 225rB] Deliver us from all wrath by the prayers of Prophets, Venerable ones, and Holy Women, O Christ, and save our souls!

Theotokion:

Another Canon for the Departed.

Creation of Theophanes.

Ode 1. Tone 7. Heirmos: By Thy nod upon the earth:

Creation adorned with virtuous forms and a divine offering radiant with diverse beauties, divinely marked, O Martyrs: ye were offered unto Christ God!

Account Thy translated servants worthy to receive the beam of the inaccessible, super-solar radiance, O most merciful Lord: whence all sickness, sorrow, and sighing have fled away!

Nature having been condemned unto death, O Giver of life, having established life, Thou Thyself, O Christ, didst raise it up; therefore, as the only King, give rest unto them that were translated unto Thee in faith!

Theotokion:

Thou didst make upright the ancestral fall, O all-pure one, having borne the Lord Word Who raised her up, and breathed life into them that are in the graves by the authority of the Godhead!

Ode 3. Heirmos: Established...[^303]

[f. 225vA] Be Thou my establishment, O Word Who established the heavens, and founded the earth upon the waters, O Savior: as Thou art mighty, save our souls!

Troparia:

Being crushed with stones and cast into pits: ye crushed all the power of the evil one, and remained unbroken in mind, O Martyrs!

By the beam of divine traditions and the rays of virtues, O venerable hierarchs, ye enlighten the faithful, driving away all the mist of heresies!

Having died unto the world, Thy venerable ones, O Word, truly inherited the supermundane life: for whose sake, O Christ, have compassion upon us all!

Them that were translated in faith and hope, we all beseech Thee, O good Master, that Thou mayest spare them in the hour of judgment!

Theotokion:

O Word from the unwaning Father's bosom: held in thy bosom as an infant, O all-pure one, the beginningless was seen, taking a beginning from thee!

Another Canon [for the Departed].

Ode 3. Heirmos: In the beginning the heavens:

The company of the Martyrs showed forth youthful and steadfast endurance valiantly unto the tormentors: alone they endured onslaughts and the wounds of torments, desiring the incorruptible glory and beauty of God, O Savior!

Receive, O merciful One, the souls of them that died in the hope of Thy eternal life; and settling them in the desired, divine bosom of holy Abraham, number them with Lazarus and Thine elect!

O compassionate Savior Who camest down from heaven to save the human race: account them that were piously translated worthy through Thy tender-heartedness to enjoy Thine immaterial Light and divine glory and joy!

[f. 225vB] When thou didst conceive the incomprehensible Word in thee, O pure one, the laws of nature were broken; and the divine law was given unto us, granting forgiveness of transgressions unto all through the grace of divine goodness!

Ode 4. Heirmos:

The Prophet Habakkuk, being assured of Thy coming in the flesh, O Christ, cried aloud: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

Troparia:

Bound with the bonds of love toward the Lord, the Martyrs withered the power of the enemy: therefore they are called blessed!

As shepherds of the flock and of the lambs, O blessed hierarchs: ye became protectors of the rational flock by divine grace!

Radiant like stars with the brightness of virtues: ye illumined the fulness of the faithful, O our venerable fathers!

The single company of valiant women and the assembly of holy Prophets have obtained heavenly good things!

Theotokion:

Pray, O all-hymned one, unto Him Whom thou didst bear, that thy flock may be delivered from great tribulations and sorrows!

Another Canon [for the Departed].

Ode 4. Heirmos: The heavens heard:

Having patiently shown forth the sufferings of athletes, O Christ, the Martyrs were crowned with the crowns of Thy righteousness and glorified Thy glory!

Account them that were piously translated worthy of the supernatural beauty of Thy glory, O Christ, when Thou comest in Thy glory with Thine Angels, O all-compassionate and most merciful One!

[f. 226rA] Account them that have departed before us and glorify Thee, O Lover of mankind, worthy to enjoy the beam of the Triple-radiance and the lightning of the one Godhead!

Theotokion:

Without leaving the Father, Christ took up His abode in the virginal womb, and delivered them that bless thee from death, O Mother of good, only all-pure one!

Ode 5. Heirmos:

My spirit seeks Thee early in the morning, O Christ God; for Thy commandments are light, and have become healings unto Thy servants, O Lover of mankind!

Troparia:

The valiant passion-bearers cared not for bodily bonds, and by your divine wounds ye heal the wounds and passions of all!

Ye received authority to loose and to bind upon earth, O hierarchs of Christ: therefore ever loose the burdens of our evils!

With one mind we honor the godly company of the race, the honored ranks of Prophets and Righteous, and the choirs of venerable women, rejoicing together!

*Hymn for the Departed (Поко́инъ):*

Theotokion:

Theotokion:

Another Canon [for the Departed].

Ode 9. Heirmos: The same.

Manifestly the valiant Martyrs enlighten the world, being pillars of the faith, unshakable foundation and bulwarks of piety unto the Churches: them, as is meet, we, the faithful, call blessed!

Deliver from the fire of Gehenna them that have been translated from us, O Master; for with the spear of Thy side Thou didst tear up the handwriting of sins, as Thou alone art the Lover of mankind: and account them worthy of the brightness of the Saints!

As Thou art good and the Lover of mankind, merciful and compassionate, as Thou art the inexhaustible treasury of immortal life, O Savior: account them that have fallen asleep before in faith worthy of Thine incorruptible sustenance!

The shadows of the law and former dark riddles have passed away by thy childbearing; for Christ became the fulfillment of the Law and the Prophets, Whom...[^305]

[f. 227vA] ...Whom singing as essentially God, we ever call thee, the pure Virgin, blessed!

At the Praises, Stichera

to the Martyrs. Tone 7:

Celebrating the memory of Thy holy passion-bearers, we sing praise unto Thee, O Christ, crying aloud: O Lord, glory to Thee!

In the midst of the lawless judgment hall, the passion-bearers rejoiced, crying out unto Thee, O Christ: O Lord, glory to Thee!

The all-lauded passion-bearers appeared as luminaries unto the universe, crying aloud unto Christ: O Lord, glory to Thee!

United in mind, and looking unto the One, the passion-bearing Martyrs found the one path of life, even death for Christ: equally emulating one another in their end! O wonder! Like treasuries of torments snatching away the contest, one said unto another: "If we die not now, we shall die in any case; let us render what is due unto our nature! Let us make a necessity into an honor, and buy what is common by giving our own: by death let us purchase life!" By their prayers, O God, have mercy upon us!

O Thou Who in the beginning didst create man according to Thine own image and likeness, and didst set him in Paradise to rule over Thy creatures; but being deceived through the envy of the devil, he partook of the food, becoming a transgressor of Thy commandments: therefore Thou didst condemn him, O Lord, to return again unto the earth whence he was taken, and to ask for rest!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

We sing praise unto thee, O all-holy Birth-giver of God, and we glorify [f. 227vB] Him Whom thou didst bear, God the Word, crying: Glory to Thee!

Aposticha Stichera.

*Podoben: "Rejoice, O container of ascetics" (Ра́дꙋйся по́стникѡвъ):*

*Hymn for the Departed (Поко́инъ):*

Seen dead upon the Cross, O Thou Who alone art immortal, and laid in the grave as one dead: delivering men from deadness and mortal corruption; but as Thou art an inexhaustible abyss of compassion and a fountain of grace: give rest unto the souls of Thy servants who have departed from us!

*Verse: Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen and taken to Thyself, O Lord.*

By Thine ineffable goodness, the sweetness of Thy beauty, and the beams of Thy divine Light, account them that were translated worthy to be brightly illuminated, O Good One: rejoicing before Thee, the Master, King of glory, and Lord, with the Angels at the immaterial out-pouring of Thy Light!

*Verse: Their souls shall dwell among good things.*

As Thou hast an unfailing greatness of gifts, as an unfailing treasury of the wealth of grace: settle them that have been translated unto Thee, as God, in the lands of Thine elect: in a place of refreshment, in the house of Thy glory, in the delight of Paradise, in the spiritual chamber, as Thou art merciful!

Glory: Now and ever: Stavrotheotokion:

Thou didst bear the Deliverer Who came in the flesh as the fulfillment of the Law, Who became justification unto them that were formerly under the Law; and for our sake Christ was crucified and justified [us]...
