# TONE 8: SATURDAY VESPERS, SUNDAY MATINS, AND WEEKDAY OFFICES

## SATURDAY EVENING: VESPERS (TONE 8)

[f. 228rA] SATURDAY EVENING, AT LITTLE VESPERS

Resurrectional Stichera, Tone 8.

Creation of John of Damascus.

[f. 228rA] An evening song and rational service we offer unto Thee, O Christ: for Thou wast well pleased to have mercy upon us for the sake of Thy Resurrection!

O Lord, Lord, cast us not away from Thy face; but be well pleased to have mercy upon us for the sake of Thy Resurrection!

Rejoice, O holy Sion, mother of the Churches, dwelling-place of God: for thou didst first receive forgiveness of sins for the sake of the Resurrection!

Other Eastern Stichera.

Tone 8:

The Word born of God the Father before all ages: in the last times, incarnate of the unwedded Virgin by His own will, endured death upon the Cross: and saved man, deadened of old, by His Resurrection!

Thy Resurrection from the dead we glorify, O Christ: wherewith Thou didst set free the race of Adam from the tyranny of hades, and as God didst bestow upon the world eternal life and great mercy!

[f. 228rB] Glory to Thee, O Christ Savior, only-begotten Son of God, Who wast nailed upon the Cross, and didst rise from the tomb on the third day!

Thee do we glorify, O Lord, Who willingly didst endure crucifixion for our sake: and unto Thee we bow down, O almighty Savior, cast us not away from Thy face; but hear and save us for the sake of Thy Resurrection, O Lover of mankind!

Glory: Now and ever: Dogmatic Theotokion:

The King of heaven for His love of mankind appeared upon earth and lived among men: for taking flesh from the pure Virgin and coming forth from her with the assumption thereof, He is one Son, twofold in nature, but not in hypostasis: therefore, truly proclaiming Him as perfect God and perfect man, we confess Christ our God! Entreat Him, O unwedded Mother, that our souls may be saved![^306]

[f. 228vA] At the Aposticha, Stichera

Resurrectional. Tone 8:

Thou didst ascend the Cross, O Jesus, Who camest down from heaven; Thou camest unto death, O immortal Life, the true Light unto them that were in darkness; the Resurrection and illumination of all them that had fallen: O our Savior, glory to Thee!

Other Stichera according to Alphabet:

*Verse: The Lord is King, He is robed in majesty.*

We glorify Christ Who rose from the dead: for He assumed soul and body, and by His Passion separated them one from the other: His soul indeed descended into hades, which also He despoiled; but in the tomb His holy body saw no corruption, the Redeemer of our souls!

*Verse: For He hath established the world, so that it cannot be moved.*

With psalms and songs we glorify Thy Resurrection from the dead, O Christ, wherewith Thou didst free us from the tyranny of hades; and as God Thou didst bestow upon us eternal life and great mercy!

*Verse: Holiness becomes Thine house, O Lord, unto length of days.*

O incomprehensible Master of all, Creator of heaven and earth: by the sufferings of the Cross Thou didst pour forth dispassion unto me; and having received burial and risen in glory, Thou didst raise up Adam with Thyself by Thine almighty hand! Glory to Thy third-day rising, wherewith Thou hast granted us eternal life and cleansing of sins, as Thou alone art compassionate!

[f. 228vB] Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

O unwedded Virgin, who ineffably didst conceive God in the flesh, Mother of God the Most High: receive the supplications of thy servants, O all-immaculate one, who grantest unto all cleansing of transgressions: now receiving our entreaties, pray that we all may be saved!

Troparion, Tone 8:

From on high didst Thou descend, O Compassionate One, and didst submit to three-day burial, that Thou mightest free us from our passions: O our Life and Resurrection, Lord, glory to Thee!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

O Thou Who for our sake wast born of the Virgin and didst endure crucifixion, O Good One: Who by death didst despoil death and show forth the Resurrection as God: despise not them whom Thou didst create with Thine own hand; show forth Thy love for mankind, O Merciful One; accept the Birth-giver of God who bore Thee, who prays for us: and save a despairing people, O our Savior!

SUNDAY AT THE MIDNIGHT OFFICE

Canon to the Holy and Life-Originating

T R I N I T Y.

Creation of Metrophanes.

Ode 1. Tone 8. Heirmos:

He plunged the armed Pharaoh into the deep:

Troparia:

Unto the Triple-radiant dominion, the Creator and Provider of all things, God Who alone is good by nature, and possesses the single glory of Godhead: we fall down before the single Beginning, singing the Thrice-holy hymn!

Remembering the divine utterances and the all-pure sayings that declared it: we glorify the single divine Nature, ever-existing, co-beginningless, in three Persons: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, creative and almighty!

[f. 229rA] Abraham having become a sacred mystagogue, saw the Trinity of old in sacred manner, and receiving it as unto the Lord in three Persons, he rejoiced; and in three Hypostases he recognized the single dominion!

Theotokion:

Without experience of wedlock thou didst bear Christ, Who assumed our nature for our sake, O all-pure one, and remained unchanged in both: Whom do thou entreat without ceasing, to grant me forgiveness of sins and deliverance from temptations!

Ode 3. Heirmos:

Thou Who in the beginning established the heavens:

Troparia:

Isaiah, seeing Thee on high upon the throne, O inaccessible God and King of glory, and the Cherubim and Seraphim crying aloud with unceasing hymns, praised the single three-hypostatic God!

The marvelous Word, begotten of the Father as from Mind, and the Holy Spirit ineffably proceeding: comprehended by each thought and by scriptural teachings, we honor the one Triple-radiant God!

The unbegotten Father, having incorruptibly begotten the Son as the radiance of His own essence, Light from Light, sets forth by procession the co-enthroned Light of the Spirit, all-creative and of equal honor!

Theotokion:

Thou wast shown forth as a pure temple, O Virgin Mother Mary: unto Him Who divinely, all-powerfully, and most wisely established the other creation, ordering and upholding it: make Him merciful through thy maternal prayers!

[f. 229rB] Sessional Hymn, Tone 8.

*Podoben: "That which was commanded mystically" (Пове́лѣнное та́инственно):*

The power of the Triple-radiant and honorable Godhead let us, the faithful, praise in hymns: for by a nod alone He established all things: the higher angelic ranks and the lower sacred orders of the Church, that they may cry: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, O most good God! Glory and song be unto Thy dominion!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

O thou who didst bear the Unchangeable God: my heart, ever changing through sin and slothfulness by the assaults of the deceitful one, do thou, as good, establish by thy maternal prayers, that I also may thankfully glorify thee: O Birth-giver of God Mary, have mercy upon thy flock which thou hast acquired, O all-immaculate one!

Ode 4. Heirmos:

The mysteries, O Christ Lord...

Troparia:

The Orient of the Godhead having appeared: it dispersed all the dark night of passions from them that were in darkness, and the Sun of Righteousness shone forth: simple indeed according to essence, but three-hypostatic in Persons: Whom we ever praise and glorify!

Praised by Seraphic mouths, with one mouth we glorify Thee, the single and Triune in glory, in essence and in hypostases: crying aloud unto Thee for all: grant diverse forgiveness of sins unto Thy servants, O Upholder of all existing things![^307]

[f. 229vA] Indivisible, all-compassionate, tender-hearted, loving mankind, honorable and divine Trinity: forget not me Thy servant unto the end, nor annul the covenant which Thou hast made with Thy servants, for Thine ineffable mercy's sake!

Theotokion:

He Who was born of thee, O all-pure one, One of the Trinity, the all-creative and divine Word, almighty God, renewed human nature: Whom do thou entreat without ceasing, to deliver me from all sorrow!

Ode 5. Heirmos:

My spirit seeks Thee early in the morning:

Troparia:

I understand Thee, O three-hypostatic, co-ever-existing Three Persons glorified: yet one Lord, the divine Nature, simply dividing and uniting; and faithfully we cry aloud: O single Beginning, Holy Trinity, deliver Thy servants from sorrow!

I weep bitterly for the weakness of my mind: how do I suffer against my will? An unstable alteration in truth: therefore I cry unto the Life-originating Trinity: O Holy Trinity, establish me in the good station!

Weighed down by the slumber of my sin, and cast into the sleep of death: as Thou art loving mankind, most good, and all-merciful, O divine Holy Trinity, have compassion and raise me up!

Theotokion:

O Virgin Mother, Maiden, all-pure, all-immaculate, full of God's grace: by thy prayers make Thy Son and God, the Lord Who loves mankind, merciful unto me; and speedily deliver Thy servant from the passions of sin!

[f. 229vB] *Ode 6. Heirmos: Cleanse me, O Savior, for many are mine...*

Troparia:

Emulating the ranks of heavenly minds, O single Beginning of all, supersubstantial Trinity: with Thrice-holy hymns we glorify Thee!

With our earthen lips, unto Thee Who didst create man according to Thine image, and didst most wisely bring all things from non-being, God in three Persons, I bow down and honor, sing and magnify Thee!

O God the Ruler of all, and only Indivisible One: beholding me in Thine ineffable mercy, O three-hypostatic Master: enlighten me and give me understanding, as Thou art merciful!

Theotokion:

Thou wast shown forth as a temple unto the Uncontainable God, O all-pure one: show me also forth as a temple of divine grace, O all-holy Sovereign Lady, by thy supplications, and preserve me unharmed!

Sessional Hymn, Tone 8.

*Podoben: "That which was commanded mystically" (Повелѣ́нное та́инственно):*

As beginningless Root, and co-beginningless Son, and Divine Spirit, truly we confess: unconfusedly, unchangeably, and indivisibly: a simple Trinity in essence and equal in dignity, singing with the Angels: Holy art Thou, O Father, and Son, with the most holy and honorable Spirit: remember them whom Thou hast created according to Thine image, O Word!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

We ever thank thee, O Birth-giver of God, and we magnify thee, O pure one, and bow down before thee: singing of thy birthgiving, O full of grace, crying unceasingly: Save us, O most merciful Virgin, as thou art good [f. 230rA] before the trial, that we thy servants may not be put to shame!

Ode 7. Heirmos:

The descending of the Father, the fire:

Troparia:

By Thine ineffable wisdom and the abyss of Thy goodness, show me Thy servant pitied now as of old; and deliver me from affliction, O Trinity, single God, and from sins and passions!

The Father unbegotten Father, and the Word begotten of Him, and the Divine Spirit, proceeding incomprehensibly: O single Beginning and Triple-radiant: unto Thee I sing: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

Theotokion:

Slaying all by giving them to drink of the venom of sin, the enemy came upon me; but fleeing unto thee in faith, who didst bear the Prince of life: by thy prayers make Thy servant alive, and deliver me from assaults and passions, O only pure one!

Ode 8. Heirmos:

Sevenfold the furnace was heated:

Troparia:

Light unwaning, triple-radiant and supremely brilliant, single Beginning, sovereign, most simple, incomprehensible God, and sovereign Lord: now illumine my dark and darkened heart, and show it forth radiant and light-bearing, faithfully to praise and glorify Thee unto all ages!

With most sacred wings the divine Seraphim reverently cover their faces and feet, unable to endure the incomprehensible glory of Thy divine, [f. 230rB] self-beginning, supremely radiant Trinity: yet we also dare to sing of Thee and glorify Thee unto all ages!

Beginningless Lordship, all-powerful, most good, perfect in origin, beneficent, creative, ever-existing, providing for and saving all, single in essence and in three Persons: I glorify Thee, O my God, in faith unto all ages!

Theotokion:

The unwaning Sun shone forth upon earth by thy virginal birthgiving, O all-pure Sovereign Lady, and delivered earthly beings from the dark gloom of idolatry and evil: therefore now illumine me even more with the rays of the Godhead, and preserve thy servant!

Ode 9. Heirmos:

The heaven was amazed at this:

Troparia:

O Nature ruling over all, all-creative, primordial, higher nature, life-originating, tender-heartedly loving mankind: O single Beginning, Trinity, we sinners now glorify Thee, asking forgiveness of sins, peace unto the world, and unity of mind unto the Churches!

O single Dominion and Triple-radiant, single Beginning and Triple-sun: accept Thine own singers in beauteous manner, and deliver from transgressions, temptations, and difficulties; and speedily grant peace, O Lover of mankind, and union unto the Churches!

Theotokion:

Taking up Thine abode in the virginal womb, O Christ my Savior...[^308]

[f. 230vA] ...wisely, in a God-man manner, unchangeably, unconfusedly in truth: and sanctifying forever, Thy mercy abides with Thy servants; therefore by the prayers of her that bore Thee, grant peace unto Thy Church!

## SUNDAY MATINS (TONE 8)

AT MATINS, AFTER THE PSALMS:

"God is the Lord": and the Resurrectional Troparion. Glory: Now and ever: "O Thou Who for our sake wast born of the Virgin": Then the customary chanting of the Psalter.

After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymns

Resurrectional. Tone 8:

Thou didst rise from the dead, O Life of all; and a radiant Angel cried unto the women: "Cease from tears, proclaim the good tidings unto the Apostles, crying aloud and singing: Christ the Lord hath risen, Who was well pleased as God to save the human race!"

Having truly risen from the tomb, Thou didst command the holy women to preach the Resurrection unto the Apostles, as it is written: and Peter, running swiftly, came unto the tomb, and seeing the light in the tomb, he was amazed; and he saw the winding-sheets lying alone, which no one could see in the night: and believing, he cried aloud: Glory to Thee, O Christ God, for Thou savest all, O our Savior, for Thou art the Radiance of the Father!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

Rejoice, thou who from the Angel didst receive the joy of the world! Rejoice, thou who didst bear the Creator of creation! Rejoice, thou who wast accounted worthy to be the Mother of God!

[f. 230vB] After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns

Resurrectional. Tone 8:

Men sealed Thy tomb, O Savior, and an Angel rolled away the stone from the doors: and the women, seeing Thee risen from the dead, proclaimed the good tidings unto Thy disciples in Sion: that the Life of all hath risen, and the bonds of death have been loosed! O Lord, glory to Thee!

The women, bringing burial myrrh, heard an angelic voice from the tomb: "Cease from tears, and bring joy instead of grief; shout aloud, singing: Christ the Lord hath risen, Who was well pleased as God to save the human race!"

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

In thee, O full of grace, all creation rejoices: the angelic assembly and the human race: hallowed temple and rational paradise, virginal boast: whereof God was incarnate and became a child, Who is our God before all ages! For He made thy womb a throne, and made thy belly more spacious than the heavens! In thee, O full of grace, all creation rejoices: glory to thee!

Ypakoë. Tone 8:

The Myrrh-bearers, standing before the life-giving tomb, sought the Master, the Immortal One among the dead: and receiving the joyful tidings from the Angel, they announced unto the Apostles that Christ God hath risen, granting great mercy unto the world!

Hymns of Ascent (Anavathmoi). Tone 8.

Antiphon 1:

[f. 231rA] From my youth the enemy tempts me and burns me with pleasures; but hoping in Thee, O Lord, I conquer him!

They that hate Sion shall become as grass before it is plucked up; for Christ shall cut off their necks with the cutting of torments!

Glory: Now and ever:

By the Holy Spirit all things have life: Light from Light, great God, we sing praise unto Him with the Father and with the Word!

Antiphon 2:

I cried unto Thee, O Lord, attend, incline Thine ear unto me as I cry; and cleanse me before Thou takest me hence!

He that hath hope in the Lord shall not be afraid then, when He shall judge all things with fire and torment!

Glory: Now and ever:

By the Holy Spirit is the God-spoken unity, the Thrice-holy: for the Father is beginningless, from Whom the Son was timelessly begotten; and the Spirit, co-enthroned and conformed, proceeds from the Father!

Antiphon 3:

Let my heart be covered with Thy fear, being humble-minded: lest being lifted up, it fall away from Thee, O all-compassionate One!

Everyone that departs unto his mother, the earth, shall come again to receive torments or rewards according to what he hath lived!

Glory: Now and ever:

By the Holy Spirit everyone divinely sees and foretells: he works wonders on high, singing of one God in three Persons: for though it shines triply, the Godhead reigns as one!

Antiphon 4:

[f. 231rB] Behold now, what is so good, or what is so pleasant, as for brethren to dwell together in unity? For herein the Lord promised eternal life [Ps. 132:1]!

Concerning His garment, He Who adorns the lilies of the field commands that it is not meet to be anxious [Matt. 6:28]!

Glory: Now and ever:

By the Holy Spirit, as by a single cause, all things are upheld, giving peace: for He is God, consubstantial with the Father and the Son, in Lordship!

Prokeimenon, Tone 8:

The Lord shall reign forever: thy God, O Sion, from generation to generation [Ps. 145:10].

*Verse: Praise the Lord, O my soul [Ps. 145:1].*

Then: "Let every breath praise the Lord" [Ps. 150:6].

*Verse: Praise God in His saints; praise Him in the firmament of His power.*

The Resurrectional Gospel. Then: "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ": Psalm 50: And the rest in order.

RESURRECTIONAL CANON.

Ode 1. Tone 8. Heirmos:

He plunged the armed Pharaoh into the deep: of old the wonder-working rod of Moses, striking the sea crosswise, divided it; and it saved Israel, the fugitive traveling on foot, as he sang a song unto God!

Troparia:

How can we not marvel at the almighty Godhead of Christ? Which gushes forth dispassion unto all the faithful from His sufferings, an ever-flowing fountain from the Holy One, and [everlasting life]!

As Thou wast well [pleased to take flesh, O Christ], now having [sanctified] our nature [by Thy divine Passion]...[^309]

[f. 231vA] ...by the spear: The Lord hath risen!

Theotokion:

Most glorious things have been spoken of thee in generation and generation: who didst contain God the Word in thy womb, yet remainedst pure, O Virgin Mother of God: therefore we all revere thee, our mediatress before God!

Another Canon, Cross-Resurrectional.

Ode 1. Heirmos: Passing through water:

The gates of anguish were broken open, and the gatekeepers of hades were terrified, beholding the Most High in the nether regions, Who is transcendent above all nature!

The angelic ranks were amazed, beholding fallen human nature, which had been shut up in the nethermost parts of the earth, seated upon the divine Throne!

Theotokion:

The angelic and human ranks unceasingly praise thee, unwedded Mother; for thou didst bear in thine arms, as an Infant, the Creator of all!

Another Canon to the Most Holy Theotokos.

Tone 8. Ode 1. Heirmos: Let us sing unto the Lord:

[O Most Holy] Theotokos... who didst bear beyond nature the divine Word, [Who came in the flesh]: we sing praise unto thee!

[O Most Holy Theotokos... as a] life-bearing [paradise] and all-pure Virgin, thou didst bear Christ, [Who] sprinkles... of salvation unto all the world!

[O Most Holy Theotokos... thou who art] elevated beyond understanding... [save] thee!

[f. 231vB] Ode 3. Resurrectional Canon. Heirmos:

Thou Who didst establish me upon the rock, O Christ, establish the Church: for none is holy save Thee, O Lover of mankind!

Troparia:

Having been condemned by the tasting of sin, O Adam: by the saving Passion of Thy flesh Thou didst justify him, O Christ: for Thou Thyself, sinless One, wast not subject unto the test of death!

The light of the Resurrection hath shone forth unto them that sit in the darkness and shadow of death, my God Jesus: and having bound the strong one by His Godhead, He plundered their vessels!

Theotokion:

Higher than the Cherubim and Seraphim wast thou revealed, O Theotokos; for thou alone, immaculate one, didst receive the uncontainable God in thy womb: therefore, all we faithful bless thee with hymns, honoring thee!

Another Heirmos: The vault of heaven:

(Cross-Resurrectional)

Having first disobeyed the commandment of the Lord Who made me, from Whom I was estranged: into which I was plunged, and having been punished for transgression by death, Thou didst establish me by Thy Crucifixion!

O Thou Who by wisdom orderest all things [by the hand of the Lord, and by Thy] understanding didst establish the nether parts: by Thine [ineffable] descent, O Word of God, and by Thy Resurrection, [restore] that which is according to Thine image!

Theotokion:

Thou didst dwell bodily in the Virgin, O Lord, and appearedst unto men as it was meet to behold Thee: and Thou didst show her forth as an incorrupt Theotokos and help unto the faithful, O Thou Who alone art the Lover of mankind!

Another Heirmos: Thou art the establishment:

(Canon to Theotokos)

Grant unto us help by thy prayers, O all-pure one, [repelling the cruel assaults of tribulations]!

[f. 232rA] [repelling the cruel assaults of tribulations]. Of Eve our foremother thou wast the restoration, having borne the Prince of life unto the world, O Theotokos!

Fill me with power, O all-pure one: who didst truly bear God in the flesh, whence broken power is restored!

Ode 4. Heirmos:

Thou art my Lord, O Christ, Thou art my power, Thou art my God, Thou art my rejoicing: Who without leaving the bosom of the Father didst visit our poverty: therefore with the Prophet Habakkuk I cry aloud unto Thee: Glory to Thy power, O Lover of mankind!

Troparia:

When I was an enemy, Thou didst exceedingly love me: by a strange self-emptying Thou didst descend upon the earth, O Savior of the world, not refusing the reproach of my dishonor: and remaining in the height of Thine all-pure glory, Thou didst glorify him who had formerly been dishonored!

Who that beholds, O Master, is not amazed now? By Thy Passion death is destroyed; by the Cross corruption is banished; and by death the riches of hades are despoiled: an awesome work wrought by the power of the Cross of Thee Who wast crucified, O Lover of mankind!

Theotokion:

Thou art the boast of the faithful, O unwedded one; thou art the mediatress; thou art the refuge of Christians, a rampart and a harbor: for unto thy Son thou bearest supplications, O all-blameless one, and dost save from ignorance them that know thee in faith and love as the honored Theotokos!

Another Heirmos: I heard Thy report, O Lord:

(Cross-Resurrectional)

Upon the Cross the children of the transgressors nailed Thee...

[f. 232rB] ...the children of the transgressors nailed Thee, O Christ God: whereby Thou didst save them that praise Thy sufferings, as Thou art compassionate!

Having risen from the tomb, Thou didst raise together with Thyself all the dead that were in hades: and as Thou art tender-hearted, Thou didst enlighten them that praise Thy Resurrection!

Theotokion:

Pray thou unto God Whom thou didst bear, O all-pure Mother, that forgiveness of transgressions may be granted unto thy servants!

Another Heirmos: The same.

(Canon to Theotokos)

O unplowed field that budded forth the curse unto life, bearing Him Who gives life unto the world: O Theotokos, save them that sing praise unto thee!

All-venerable font that enlightens all, as we know: for thou didst bear the Sun of righteousness, O ever-Virgin!

Grant cleansing unto our ignorances, as Thou art sinless, and give peace unto Thy world, O God, through the prayers of the Angels and of her that bare Thee!

Ode 5. Heirmos:

Why hast Thou cast me off from Thy face, O Light never-setting? And strange darkness hath covered me, the wretched one: but convert me, and unto the light of Thy commandments direct my ways, I pray Thee!

Troparia:

Thou didst deign to be clothed in the purple robe of mockery before Thy Passion, O Savior, healing the ugly nakedness of the First-formed: and naked Thou wast nailed upon the Cross in the flesh, stripping away the deadening, O Christ, of mortality from the dust of mortals, and Thine ineffable [re-creation]...[^310]

[f. 232vA] ...Thou didst fashion, showing it forth as the royal image, shining with the light of incorruption.

Theotokion:

Having maternal boldness toward thy Son, O all-pure one: despise not the kinship of Thy providence toward us, we pray thee; for thee alone, the Christians' merciful cleansing, do we present before the Master!

Another Heirmos: Enlighten us:

(Cross-Resurrectional)

Guide us unto the light by the power of Thy Cross, O Christ; for thereby we fall down before Thee: grant Thy peace unto us, O Lover of mankind!

Direct our life now, O most good Christ our God, as we sing of Thy rising, and grant peace unto us, O Lover of mankind!

Theotokion:

Pray thou, O pure one, unto thy Son and our God, unwedded Mary all-pure, to send down upon us, the faithful, great mercy!

Another Heirmos: Rising early in the morning we cry:

(Canon to Theotokos)

The angelic ranks and human assemblies uphold thy praise, O all-pure Theotokos!

Calm the unsteady tempest of my passions, O Virgin, who didst bear God the Helmsman and Lord!

Thee, unwedded Theotokos, the hope of the faithful: keep safe from the grasp of the enemies them that sing praise unto thee!

Ode 6. Heirmos:

Cleanse me, O Savior, for many are mine iniquities, and lead me up from the depths of evils, I pray Thee: for unto Thee have I cried, and the God of my salvation hath heard me!

Troparia:

By the Tree the author of malice mightily cast me down; but Thou, [having risen, O Christ, didst raise me up again]...

[f. 232vB] ...by Thine apparel: and Thou didst resurrect him that was fallen!

Thou didst show mercy unto Sion, shining forth from the tomb: making new instead of old, as Thou art tender-hearted, by Thy divine Blood; and now Thou reignest therein unto ages of ages, O Christ!

Theotokion:

That we may be delivered from grievous sins by thy prayers, O pure Birth-giver of God, and that we may obtain, O all-pure one, the divine radiance of the Son of God Who was ineffably incarnate!

Another Heirmos: I pour out my prayer:

(Cross-Resurrectional)

Thou didst stretch out Thy hands upon the Cross, healing the condemned outstretched hand of the first-formed man in Eden; and for the sake of sweetness having tasted gall, O Christ, Thou didst save him as Thou art mighty, who glorifies Thy sufferings, O Savior!

In truth the Deliverer of all from death, having descended into the filth of hades as the Mighty One, in order to destroy the kingdom of the first condemnation and corruption: and He saved, as He is mighty, them that praise His Resurrection!

Theotokion:

Cease not to pray for us, O Most Holy Virgin Theotokos; for thou art the establishment of the faithful, and in thy hope we are strengthened: therefore in love we unceasingly glorify thee and God Who was incorruptibly incarnate of thee!

Another Heirmos: Give me a robe:

(Canon to Theotokos)

A temple of God, the Ark, a living bridal chamber, and the gate of heaven, O Theotokos, do we the faithful proclaim thee: worshipping Him Who destroyed corruption as God, even thy Childbearing, O Mary Bride: we bow down before thee!

[f. 233rA] As God with the Father and the Spirit, God the Word showed thee forth unto earthborn men, O Theotokos, as a heavenly ladder: for through thee He descended unto us!

KONTAKION, Tone 8.

*Podoben: "As first-fruits of nature" (Я҆́кѡ нача́тки е҆стества̀):*

Having risen from the tomb, Thou didst raise the dead, and didst resurrect Adam, and Eve dances in Thy Resurrection: the ends of the world hold festival at Thy rising from the dead, O most merciful One!

IKOS

Having plundered the realms of hades, and having resurrected the dead, O long-suffering One: Thou didst meet the Myrrh-bearing women, bringing joy instead of sorrow: and Thou didst proclaim unto Thine Apostles the tokens of victory, O my Savior, Giver of life: and Thou dost enlighten creation, O Lover of mankind! Therefore also the world rejoices together at Thy rising from the dead, O most merciful One!

Ode 7. Heirmos:

The fire was ashamed before the condescension of God in Babylon of old: therefore the Children in the furnace with joyful step, as in a radiant meadow, danced, singing: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

Troparia:

The glorious self-emptying, the divine wealth of Thy poverty, O Christ, amazes the Angels, who behold Thee nailed in the flesh upon the Cross, in order to save them that cry aloud in faith: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

By Thy divine descent the nether regions were filled with light, and the darkness which formerly drove them was banished...

[f. 233rB] ...banished: therefore the prisoners from the ages arose, crying aloud: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

Triadicon:

As Lord of all, yet to the only-begotten Son alone, we orthodoxly proclaim Thee, glorifying His Father: one upright, co-essential, and co-eternal God!

Another Heirmos: The Children from Judea:

(Cross-Resurrectional)

He wrought salvation in the midst of the earth, the all-pure One pierced with a spear: for having been lifted up upon the Tree, Thou didst call all that cry aloud in faith: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

Having risen from the tomb as from sleep, O compassionate One: Thou didst deliver all from corruption, and creation was established by the Apostles who preached the Resurrection: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

Triadicon:

We worship the Father, and the pure Son, and the Holy Spirit, confessing three consubstantial Persons, and one God and Lord, crying aloud: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

Another Heirmos: The same.

(Canon to Theotokos)

Having become incarnate from the virginal womb, Thou didst appear for our salvation: therefore knowing Thy Mother as the Theotokos, we orthodoxly cry: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

A Rod from the root of Jesse didst thou bud forth, O Virgin, an all-blessed Fruit, bearing the saving Flower unto them that cry aloud in faith unto thy Son: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

Fill all with wisdom and divine strength...[^311]

[f. 233vA] ...divine strength: ordering the wisdom of the Most High for the sake of the Theotokos, unto them that cry aloud in faith unto Thee: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

Ode 8. Heirmos:

Sevenfold the furnace the Chaldean tyrant fiercely kindled for the godly: but seeing them saved by a higher power, he cried aloud unto the Creator and Deliverer: Ye children, bless; ye priests, sing praise; ye people, supreme Him unto all ages!

Troparia:

The divine power of the Word of God hath divinely shone forth in us; for having taken upon Him the testament of death upon the Cross, He shattered the power of hades: Him unceasingly bless, ye children; praise, ye priests; supreme Him, ye people, unto all ages!

The Crucified hath risen! The haughty one is fallen! And fallen, crushed man is restored: corruption is overthrown, and incorruption hath blossomed; for that which was mortal hath been swallowed up by life! Ye children, bless; ye priests, praise; ye people, supreme Him unto all ages!

Triadicon:

The Triune Godhead, shining forth with single flash from one three-hypostatic Nature: the unoriginate Begetter, and the Son consubstantial with the Father, and the co-hallowed Spirit reigning on high: Ye children, bless; ye priests, praise; ye people, supreme Him unto all ages!

Another Heirmos: The victors in the furnace:

(Cross-Resurrectional)

Unto Him Who stretched out His hands upon the Tree for me...

[f. 233vB] ...for me who was naked, calling me to be buried with His honorable nakedness, and to say: Bless all ye works of the Lord, sing praise unto the Lord, and supreme Him unto all ages!

Unto Him Who raised me that was fallen from nethermost hades, and honored me with high-enthroned paternal glory, as I cry: Bless all ye works of the Lord, sing praise unto the Lord, and supreme Him unto all ages!

Triadicon:

The indivisible Godhead manifest in three Persons, three Hypostases in one holiness and glory, singing: Bless all ye works of the Lord, sing praise unto the Lord, and supreme Him unto all ages!

Another Heirmos: The King of heaven:

(Canon to Theotokos)

Extinguish the burning and flaming arrows of adversities, O pure one: that we may sing praise unto thee unto all ages!

Beyond nature didst thou bear God the Word, the Creator and Savior, O Virgin: therefore we sing praise unto thee, O pure one, unto all ages!

Enlightening and gold-gleaming, an inaccessible lampstand in the dark, O pure Virgin, didst thou appear as a torch unto the world: therefore we sing praise unto thee unto all ages!

Ode 9. Heirmos:

The heaven was amazed at this, and the ends of the earth were struck with wonder: that God appeared unto men in the flesh, and thy womb became more spacious than the heavens: therefore the ranks of Angels and of men magnify thee, O Theotokos!

Troparia:

Being simple in Thy divine and beginningless Nature: Thou becamest composite...

[f. 234rA] ...Thou becamest composite by the assumption of the flesh, subsisting in Thyself, O Word of God; and having suffered as man, Thou remainedst beyond passion as God: therefore we magnify Thee in two natures, undivided and unconfused!

Being Father according to divine essence, yet becoming man according to nature: the Son of God Most High descended unto His servants: and having risen from the tomb by the grace of the Father, He set forth for earthborn men God and Master according to nature: with Whom we all magnify Thee!

Theotokion:

O Virgin, Mother of God, thou wast seen to have borne beyond nature in the flesh the good Word: Whom the Father brought forth from His heart before all ages as good: Whom now we understand to be above bodies, even though He was clothed in a body!

Another Heirmos: Beginningless Nature:

(Cross-Resurrectional)

We all know Thee as Son by nature, conceived in the womb of the Mother of God, and become man for our sake, and nailed upon the Cross: suffering indeed by Thy fleshly nature, yet remaining impassible as God!

Gloomy darkness hath been dispersed; for from hades the Sun of righteousness hath shone forth, O Christ, enlightening all the ends of the earth, the power of the Godhead shining upon frail man: Whom in two natures we magnify!

Theotokion:

O Son of the Mother of God, subduing the Ishmaelite people that boast against us, grant victory unto the Christ-bearing king, as Thine invincible weapon: wherewith He hath endowed us...

[f. 234rB] ...hath endowed them that are pierced with the spear of Thy Cross!

Another Heirmos: Truly the Birth-giver of God:

(Canon to Theotokos)

Full of joy and gladness is thy memory, flowing with healings unto them that approach: and piously proclaiming thee as the Theotokos!

With psalms we sing praise unto thee, O full of grace, and unceasingly cry unto thee: Rejoice! For thou didst pour forth gladness unto all!

Fair blossomed thy fruit, O Theotokos: bringing life unto them that partake of incorruption, and interceding for them that magnify thee in faith!

AT THE PRAISES: Resurrectional Stichera. Tone 8:

O Lord, though Thou didst stand before the judgment seat, judged by Pilate, yet Thou didst not depart from the Throne, sitting together with the Father: and having risen from the dead, Thou didst deliver the world from the bondage of the stranger, as Thou art compassionate and the Lover of mankind!

O Lord, Thou didst give us Thy Cross as a weapon against the devil: for he trembles and shakes, not enduring to look upon its power; for it raises the dead, and hath abolished death: therefore we worship Thy Burial and Thy Resurrection!

Though the Jews laid Thee as dead in the tomb, yet the soldiers guarded Thee as a sleeping King, and sealed Thee with a seal as a treasury of life: but Thou didst rise and grant incorruption unto our souls!

Thine Angel, O Lord, who proclaimed the Resurrection, struck terror into the guards, and cried unto the women...[^312]

[f. 234vA] ...saying: "Why seek ye the Living among the dead? He hath risen, being God, and hath granted life unto the world!"

Other Stichera, Eastern. Tone 8:

Thou didst suffer upon the Cross, being impassible in Thy Godhead; Thou didst accept three-day Burial, that Thou mightest deliver us from the bondage of the enemy, and make us immortal and quicken us, O Christ God, by Thy Resurrection, O Lover of mankind!

We worship, and glorify, and sing praise unto Thy Resurrection from the tomb, O Christ, whereby Thou didst deliver us from the insoluble bonds of hades, and didst grant unto the world, as God, incorruption and eternal life: for Thou alone art good and the Lover of mankind!

*Verse: Arise, O Lord my God, let Thy hand be lifted up; forget not Thy poor unto the end.*

The transgressors kept watch over Thy life-receiving tomb, and sealed it with a guard: yet Thou, as immortal God and almighty, didst rise on the third day!

*Verse: I will give thanks unto Thee, O Lord, with my whole heart; I will speak of all Thy marvelous works.*

When Thou didst descend unto the gates of hades, O Master Christ, and didst shatter them, the captives cried aloud thus: "Who is this, that He is not condemned in the nether parts of the earth, but hath destroyed the bonds of death like a shadow? I received Him as one dead, and I tremble at Him as God!" [O Lord, glory to Thee!]

Glory: Evangelical Sticheron. Now and ever: Thou art most blessed, O Virgin Theotokos: The Great Doxology: And the Dismissal.

[f. 234vB] AT THE LITURGY:

Beatitudes. Tone 8:

Remember us, O Christ, Savior of the world, as Thou didst remember the Thief upon the Tree: and account us all worthy of Thy heavenly Kingdom, O Thou Who alone art compassionate!

Today Christ hath risen from the tomb, granting incorruption unto all the faithful: and He renews joy unto the Myrrh-bearing women, after Thy Passion and Resurrection, O Lord!

Having been nailed upon the Tree, O Savior, upon the wood: Thou didst deliver Adam from the curse of the tree, and didst restore, as Thou art compassionate, that which is according to Thine image, and the habitation of Paradise!

As in heaven the multitude of Angels, so on earth the human race celebrates the most holy Resurrection of Thy goodness, O Lord!

Raise us up from the tomb of sin, O Savior, who are deadened by many passions: and by Thy rising destroy the tyranny of death, as Thou art the Lover of mankind!

Hear, O Adam, and rejoice with Eve; for he that formerly stripped you both, and took you captive through deceit, is abolished by the Cross of Christ!

Glory:

Beginningless Trinity, undivided Unity, co-enthroned Monad, equal in honor of glory, supreme Nature and Kingdom: save them that sing praise unto Thee in faith!

Now and ever: Theotokion:

Rejoice in our behalf, O Holy Theotokos, palace that didst bear joy unto the world! Rejoice, only mediatress of men, and salvation of our souls!

## SUNDAY EVENING VESPERS (TONE 8)

[f. 235rA] ON SUNDAY EVENING, AT "LORD, I HAVE CRIED":

Penitential Stichera, Tone 8.

*Podoben: "O Lord, though Thou didst stand before the tribunal" (Гдⷭи, а҆́ще и҆ на сꙋди́щи):*

O Lord, Who camest into the world to call sinners, and didst receive the Thief, the Publican, the Harlot, and the Prodigal: call me also, who have sinned against Thee more than all men, O my Christ, though I repent not, as Thou art the Lover of mankind!

O Lord, Who from publicans didst appoint a Pastor of Thy Church, and didst make him who was formerly a persecutor to be now a defender: by their supplications show me forth as Thine own sheep, O Savior, lest I follow after the stranger and become unprofitable, O Savior!

Weep, O wretched soul, before the end, and cleave unto God, crying aloud unto Him for betrothal; and groaning for all wherewith thou hast defiled thyself: "I have sinned against Thee, O Christ, despise me not, I pray Thee: but having compassion upon me, as Thou art merciful, account me worthy of forgiveness!"

Other Stichera to the Bodiless Hosts. Same Tone:

O Lord, the assemblies of the Bodiless unceasingly glorify Thee, enjoying Thy beauty and Thine ineffable goodness, and being richly illuminated with three-sunned rays: by their supplications and intercession, O Savior, save our souls!

O Lord, the sleepless choirs of the Angels Thou didst establish by Thy sublime Word...

[f. 235rB] ...Word, and by Thy Holy Spirit, granting them a radiance that falls not away: by their supplications and intercessions, O Christ Savior, save all us that sing praise unto Thee!

O Lord, the Seraphim sing praise unto Thee: the Principalities, the Angels, the Authorities, the Dominions, the Thrones, the Powers, the Archangels, and the dread Cherubim sing hymns unto Thee: by the protection of them all, save all that sing praise unto Thee in faith!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

Continually do I anger and grieve the Creator; grant me amendment, O Maiden, having first made Him well-pleased; and by thine aid rise up unto works well-pleasing, that I may obtain salvation and forgiveness!

At the Aposticha, Penitential Stichera. Tone 8:

Unto Thee, the King and God, the Angels unceasingly sing praise; and I fall down before Thee, crying like the Publican: O God, cleanse me and have mercy on me!

Immortal art thou, O my soul; be not overwhelmed by the waves of this life: but crying with sober mind unto thy Benefactor: O God, [cleanse me and save me]!...[^313]

[f. 235vA] ...cleanse me and have mercy on me!

Martyrs:

Ye Martyrs of the Lord hallow every place and heal every sickness: and now pray ye that our souls may be delivered from the snares of the enemy, we pray you!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

Receiving the voice of the Archangel Gabriel, let us say: Rejoice, Mother of God, who didst bear the Giver of life unto the world!

## MONDAY MATINS: REPENTANCE AND THE BODILESS POWERS (TONE 8)

ON MONDAY AT MATINS:

After the 1st Kathisma, Penitential Sessional Hymns. Tone 8:

O most tender-hearted Lord, behold my lowliness, for little by little my life is consumed, and from my works there is no salvation for me: therefore I pray: O most tender-hearted Lord, behold my lowliness and save me!

When the Day of the Judge is come, take heed, O my soul, and meditate upon the hour of that dread Day; for judgment is without mercy unto them that have shown no mercy: therefore spare me, O Savior, for Thou alone art sinless!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

Conceiving in his mind the commanded mystery, the Bodiless One speedily presented himself in the tent of Joseph, saying unto the unwedded Maiden: He Who bowed the heavens by His descent is contained wholly and unchangeably in thee: and beholding Him in thy womb taking the form of a servant, I am amazed to cry unto thee: Rejoice, unwedded Bride!

After the 2nd Kathisma, Penitential Sessional Hymns. Tone 8:

Meditating upon that dread Day, O my soul, watch: lighting...

[f. 235vB] ...lighting thy lamp and brightening it with oil; for thou knowest not when the voice shall come unto thee, saying: "Behold, the Bridegroom comes!" Take heed therefore, O my soul, lest thou slumber and remain outside knocking, like the five foolish Virgins: but wait vigilantly, that thou mayest meet Christ God with fatness of oil, and He may give thee the chamber of His divine glory!

Like the Harlot I fall down before Thee, that I may receive forgiveness; instead of myrrh I offer Thee tears from my heart: that as Thou didst have compassion on her, O Savior, so Thou mayest grant me cleansing of sins: for like her I cry aloud unto Thee: Deliver me from the mire of my deeds!

Martyrs:

With heavenly light this temple is enlightened today; for the angelic hosts rejoice therein, and with them the choirs of the Martyrs make merry in memory of the Passion-bearers: by their prayers send down peace and great mercy upon Thy world, O Christ!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

Rejoice, gate of the King of glory, through which the Most High alone passed, and which remained sealed according to His good pleasure, for the salvation of our souls!

After the 3rd Kathisma, Penitential Sessional Hymns. Tone 8.

*Podoben: "That which was commanded mystically" (Повеле́нное таинство):*

Receive before the end, O my soul, the groaning of the Publican and the weeping of the Harlot, confessing unceasingly with weeping and mourning, with fasting, vigilance, and sorrow of heart unto Him Who knows thy secret deeds, crying aloud: "I have sinned; cleanse me, O Savior, by the prayers...

[f. 236rA] ...of Thine Angels, as Thou art compassionate, and save me!"

How long, O my soul, dost thou live in negligence? How long dost thou abide in despondency? Arise from the sleep of despondency, O wretched one, taking knowledge of thy deeds! Tremble at the answer: what shalt thou answer in that hour? Or how, remaining unamended, shalt thou escape the burning that awaits thee? Cry aloud before the end unto the Judge: "Grant me forgiveness of transgressions, O Savior, for Thou alone art long-suffering!"

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

O full of grace, pure and blessed one, who didst bear Him Who was born of heaven through the compassion of His mercies: with the Hosts on high, with the Archangels, and with all the Bodiless Powers, unceasingly pray for us: that forgiveness and cleansing of sins, and amendment of life may be granted unto us before the end, that we may find mercy!

PENITENTIAL CANON.

Creation of Joseph.

Ode 1. Tone 8. Heirmos:

Passing through water as on dry land, and fleeing from Egyptian evil, the Israelite cried aloud: Let us sing unto our Deliverer and God!

Troparia:

Deliver me from gehenna, which I have prepared for myself by unbecoming deeds, O Deliverer: and kindle in my mind the blessed fire of Thy love!

I have bowed down unto the passions, and have been darkened, and have become irrational...

[f. 236rB] ...irrational: having been honored by the Word, O Lord, grant recovery unto my soul: and by whatever judgments Thou knowest, save me!

Martyrs:

Having their bodies tormented with wounds, they possessed an upright and inflexible character: even their love toward the Creator, O all-lauded crown-bearers!

The rivers of blood that flowed from the bodies of Thy holy, glorious sufferers, by Thy power, O compassionate One, quenched the thorns of idol-madness!

Theotokion:

Heal me, O pure one, who am grievously afflicted with deadly sin, from fleshly and spiritual defilements: that in faith I may ever bless thee!

Another Canon to the Bodiless Hosts.

Creation of Theophanes. Heirmos: The same.

As leaders of the holy Angels, enjoying the splendor of the vision of God: pray ye unto the Giver of grace and the Savior for us, O Archangels!

Held fast by distressing temptations, unto you as intercessors do we the faithful now flee, O divine Archangels: entreat the Good One in our behalf!

Theotokion:

Be thou unto me a refuge, O Virgin: a harbor, a rampart, and an intercessor, who in the flesh didst bear God, the Mother of God: the Deliverer and all-compassionate One!

Ode 3. Heirmos:

O Lord, Builder of the vault of heaven and Founder of the Church: do Thou establish me in Thy love, O summit of desires, confirmation of the faithful, O Thou Who alone art the Lover of mankind!

Troparia:

With what eyes shall I look upon Thee, O Christ...[^314]

[f. 236vA] ...with what eyes shall I look upon Thee, O Savior, having not kept even one of Thy commandments upon the earth? How shall I stand before Thine unbearable Throne, to render an account of mine immeasurable evils?

Stretching out the hands of Thy compassions, receive me as formerly the Prodigal, who in like manner was enslaved to dishonorable passions, and departed far from Thee, O most good Jesus, Lover of mankind!

Martyrs:

Rooted upon the rock of the knowledge of God, O Martyrs of Christ, passion-bearers: with the sword of faith ye uprooted the thorns of ignorance, and yielded the fruits of suffering!

Unshakable pillars of true understanding, all-radiant adornments of the Church, most sacred sheep of Christ willingly slain: let the Martyrs be praised!

Theotokion:

Thee have I gained as a guardian in temptations, O most holy one; thee next to God have I as a vigilant intercessor: may I find thee, O Sovereign Lady, delivering me from all condemnation in the Day of judgment!

Another Heirmos: The same.

(Canon to Bodiless Hosts)

O light-radiant pair of the angelic rank, as chief commanders and masters, Archistrategoi: adorning the Church of Christ, ye firmly preserve her by your intercession!

With the weapon of good will, the fulfillment of the faithful, being crowned today with the beauties of Orthodoxy: from tribulations deliver us, O benign intercessors of God, divine Archangels!

Theotokion:

Thou becamest the divine Tabernacle of incorruptible life, higher than all, O pure Virgin Mother: therefore, all-holy one, direct me who am asleep in the shadow of death unto life by thy prayers!

[f. 236vB] Ode 4. Heirmos:

From the overshadowing mountain, O Word, the Prophet divinely perceiving Thee about to become incarnate of the only Theotokos, with trembling glorified Thy power!

Troparia:

Great is the contest of the soul, perceiving the dread trembling: when the Judge sits, and each man's sins are made manifest! Woe is me, what shall I do, the condemned one?

Having a heart full of defilements, and the heavy burdens of sins, I flee unto Thy compassions: despise me not, but have mercy upon me, O Good One!

Martyrs:

Precious was your death found before God, O noble passion-bearers; for ye denied Him not when surrounded by myriads of sorrows and wounds!

The enemy was wounded by the wound of the Martyrs; his haughty heresy is fallen: and the sacred Crown-giver is magnified, being glorified with divine songs!

Theotokion:

Thee, pure receptacle of God, in faith I entreat: cleanse me, O Birth-giver of God, from every defilement, and show me forth as a temple unto the pure and divine Spirit!

Another Heirmos: I heard Thy report, O Lord:

(Canon to Bodiless Hosts)

O pair holding chief rule over the angelic choir: save from every adversity them that flee beneath your protection!

Beholders of the primal brightness and grace-givers, all-glorious Archistrategoi: enlighten now your flock!

Theotokion:

Sacredly do the divine hosts of the Bodiless glorify thee, all-immaculate Mother of God; for thou didst bear their Creator!

Ode 5. Heirmos:

Enlightening us by Thy commandment, O Lord, and by Thy high arm grant Thy peace unto us, O Thou Who alone art the Lover of mankind!

Troparia:

By evil darkness have I embittered Thee, O Lord, committing unbecoming deeds: but have compassion upon me as I turn back, and save me!

Having a mind that rises not from evil, and through senseless insensibility: dispel my darkness, O Jesus, and save me!

Martyrs:

Thou didst set Thy divine Martyrs in this age, O Giver of light, as precious stones shining with the knowledge of God, and dispersing the darkness of deceit!

Against wicked laws ye set the divine laws: and preaching God, ye were slain for His sake, willingly enduring!

Theotokion:

Slay, O pure one, the motions of my flesh: who by thy childbearing didst slay the living sin of our forefather, O Maiden!

Another Heirmos: The same.

(Canon to Bodiless Hosts)

Standing around the Cross, O Archistrategoi, and enlightened thence by incorruptible rays: preserve your flock!

That healing may be granted unto us, entreat the Master and our God, as intercessors of the deliverance of all!

Theotokion:

Mystical myrrh do we name thee, all-pure one: as having borne God in the flesh, Who bestows gifts of sweet fragrance!

Ode 6. Heirmos:

Jonah in the whale, O Lord, Thou alone didst cause to dwell: and me that am bound in the nets of the enemy save, as Thou didst save him from corruption!

Troparia:

Cause the sunlit light of repentance to shine upon me who sit in the darkness of transgressions, O Christ, Giver of light: that I may sing of Thy grace!

I tremble ever at Thy dread tribunal, yet I depart not from evils, being enslaved to evil custom: amend me, O Christ, that I may sing of Thy grace!

Martyrs:

The choirs of the honorable Martyrs suffered, and vanquished the demon ranks: and were united in joy with the angelic choirs: by their prayers, O Lord, save our souls!

By Thy strength Thou didst show forth Thy Martyrs as mighty, O Lord, and they cast down the whole power of the ancient deceiver: by their prayers, O Lord, save our souls!

Theotokion:

That with compassionate voices I may ever glorify thee, all-blameless one, chase away the darkness of my soul: and by the light of repentance loose my gloomy transgressions!

Another Heirmos: I pour out my prayer:

(Canon to Bodiless Hosts)

Now standing before the dread throne, having become like God-seers without wavering: and filled with the splendor of the Holy Trinity: pray ye for them that flee unto you, that they may be delivered from temptations and passions, O Archangels!

Theotokion:

Entreat ye that we may obtain blessed citizenship...

[f. 237rA] ...blessed citizenship, who in faith praise you with hymns, and that we may be accounted worthy of everlasting joy and divine splendor, O God-beholding Archangels Gabriel and Michael all-glorious!

Living bridal chamber of the Master, who with radiant rays of virginity didst blossom forth brightly as a lily in the midst of thorns: all-pure Virgin Theotokos, receptacle of God, thou art glorified!

Ode 7. Heirmos:

The Children from Judea that arrived in Babylon of old: established by faith, trampled the flame of the furnace, singing: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

Troparia:

Grant me groaning, O Christ, as once unto the Publican and the Harlot, washing away the foulness of mine evils with tears: and have compassion upon me as I cry: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

Having fallen among soul-destroying thieves, O Savior, and being sorely wounded: heal me with the oil of primal repentance, and make me complete to sing unto Thee: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

Martyrs:

Ye were deadened unto the world, and denying not Christ Who was dead and life-bearing, O noble passion-bearers, ye cried aloud, singing: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

Triadicon:

Cutting not asunder the one nature of the Trinity in three Characters, O wise passion-bearers of the Lord: ye destroyed manifold deceit, singing: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

Theotokion:

God the Word of God dwelt in thy womb, O Virgin pure Mother, and showed thee forth as our intercessor and hope as we cry: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

[f. 237rB] Another Heirmos: The same.

(Canon to Bodiless Hosts)

Manifold grace, O divine Archistrategoi, hath the Benefactor of all granted unto you: Whom now the Church sings praise unto as ye protect her: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

Strengthened by the power of the All-seeing One, ye traverse now all the ends of the earth, and save all that sing praise in faith: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

Theotokion:

Having thee now as a saving harbor, O Virgin Theotokos: we flee from worldly perils and turmoils, crying aloud unto thy Son: O God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

Ode 8. Heirmos:

Him Who was manifested on the holy mountain, and in the fiery bush revealed the mystery of the Virgin unto Moses: sing praise unto the Lord, and supreme Him unto all ages!

Troparia:

Enticed by fleshly pleasures, and foolishly departed far from Thee, O Word, and become like unto all the beasts: despise me not, O Savior, but turning me back before the end, save me!

Having no forgiveness of sins, never working conversion, I cry, the wretched one: I have sinned against Thee, O Lord, and the deceiver hath impoverished my soul, O compassionate One...

Martyrs:

The noble passion-bearers of the Lord, made all-radiant by streams of blood, were not defiled by second stains...[^315]

[f. 237vA] ...were not defiled by second stains: and crowned, they keep festival with the Angels unceasingly!

Strengthened by the hope of future blessings, having nobly endured a multitude of torments for piety, and finished their course: they stand unceasingly before the throne of the Master!

Theotokion:

Thou art the confirmation of them that stand, and the restoration of them that are fallen, O Maiden: therefore raise me up that am fallen, that I may glorify thee, the blessed and full of grace!

Another Heirmos: The King of heaven:

(Canon to Bodiless Hosts)

Receive the ministers and singers of Thine ineffable and unutterable glory, who now entreat Thee, O Christ, for the world!

O Thou Who alone art good, O Christ: receive the angelic hosts now entreating Thee in our behalf, who sing praise unto Thee unto the ages!

Theotokion:

With radiant flashings, O Mother of God, thou enlightenest them that sing praise unto thee in faith and supreme Christ unto all ages!

Ode 9. Heirmos:

Every hearing was amazed at the ineffable condescension of God, how the Most High willingly descended even unto the flesh, having become man from the virginal womb: therefore the faithful magnify the all-pure Theotokos!

Troparia:

As of old Thou didst cleanse the Harlot who fell down with weeping, O Christ Savior; and as Thou didst justify the Publican, speed forth, O God-inspired Word; as Thou didst receive Manasseh, and as Thou didst have mercy on David when he repented: so also receive me and save me, O Lover of mankind!

Sigh and weep, O my soul, and depart from thy former sins...

[f. 237vB] ...depart from thy former sins, and openly fall down before Him Who knows thy secrets, and warmly cry aloud: "I have sinned against Thee, O Lord, have compassion upon me, as Thou hast bowels of compassions, O most merciful One!"

Martyrs:

Having suffered most patiently upon the earth, the God-wise passion-bearers obtained an unshakable kingdom: and rejoicing, they partake of the delight of Paradise: by their prayers, O Christ God, make us partakers of all Thy glory!

Truly ye appeared as unwaning stars of the East, and destroyed the night of godlessness, O most wise ones; and with sacred rays ye illuminate all that magnify your light-bearing feast, O passion-bearers!

Theotokion:

Enlighten, O Sovereign Lady, the radiant doors of mine eyes of heart, I pray thee, which deep sinful darkness hath darkened: and send down upon me the dawn of repentance, and from eternal fire deliver me by thine intercession, O pure one!

Another Heirmos: Truly the Birth-giver of God:

(Canon to Bodiless Hosts)

Confessing thee as truly the Theotokos, saved by thee, O pure Virgin, with the bodiless hosts we magnify thee!

Show forth Thy Church imitating the choirs of the Bodiless by virtue, shielding Thy flock with Angels, O Christ!

Pray ye that salvation may be granted by God, O angelic defenders, unto them that flee beneath your protection, O all-glorious ones!

Theotokion:

As a morning dawn unto them that sit in darkness and error, O Virgin: holding the righteous Sun, Christ, upon thine arms, thou didst shine forth!...[^316]

[f. 238vA] At the Aposticha, Penitential Stichera. Tone 8:

When I take to mind the multitude of mine evil deeds, and come to the thought of that dread reckoning, held fast by trembling, I flee unto Thee, the Lover of mankind and God: therefore despise me not, I pray Thee, O Thou Who alone art sinless: grant compunction unto my humble soul before the end, and save me!

Grant me tears, O God, as formerly unto the sinful woman: and account me worthy to wet Thy feet, which delivered me from the path of error, and to offer Thee sweet-smelling myrrh: a pure life acquired by repentance: that I also may hear Thy good voice: "Thy faith hath saved thee, go in peace!" [Luke 7:50]

Martyrs:

What shall we call you, O holy ones? Cherubim? For upon you Christ rested. Seraphim? For unceasingly ye glorify Him. Angels? For ye turned away from the body. Powers? Ye work in miracles: many are your names and greater your gifts: pray ye that our souls may be saved!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

Heavenly beings sing praise unto thee, O full of grace, unwedded Mother: and we glorify thine unsearchable Childbearing: O Theotokos, pray that our souls may be saved!

[f. 238vB] ON MONDAY:

Beatitudes. Tone 8:

Remember us, O Christ, Savior of the world, as Thou didst remember the Thief upon the Tree: and account us all worthy of Thy heavenly Kingdom, O Thou Who alone art compassionate!

Heal, O Christ, the passions of my soul, O Thou Who alone art the Physician of souls and bodies: and washing me with streams of compunction, cleanse me wholly, as Thou art merciful!

Standing around the throne of the honored Godhead, the Thrones, Cherubim, Principalities, and Authorities, and the other ranks of the Bodiless sacredly sing praise!

Martyrs:

Kindled with the warmth of the love of Christ: unconsumed in the midst of fire the sufferers remained, burning up the thorns of impiety by divine grace!

Glory: Triadicon:

Simple Trinity, most primal Unity: deliver Thy servants from unquenchable fire, by the supplications of the divine Bodiless Powers, and account them worthy of Thy Kingdom!

Now and ever: Theotokion:

A scroll Isaiah of old foresaw thee, O full of divine grace, wherein by the Father's finger the Word was ineffably written, inscribing us in the book of the living!

## MONDAY EVENING VESPERS (FOR TUESDAY) (TONE 8)

[f. 239rA] ON MONDAY EVENING, AT "LORD, I HAVE CRIED":

Penitential Stichera, Tone 8.

*Podoben: "O most marvelous wonder" (Ѡ пресла́внагѡ чꙋдесѐ):*

No compunction have I gained, nor fountain of tears, nor warm confession, nor tears that bring tenderness, nor intellectual humility; neither have I become an emulator of the Publican, nor of the Harlot: how then shall I find deliverance from the torments of many sins? But by whatever judgments Thou knowest, O Christ, save me!

Estranged from every divine commandment have I made myself; of the virtue of the soul I took no care at all, and foolishly I lived in prodigality through all my life: and unto myself I did all deeds unbecoming and lawless: therefore, O Christ, have compassion as Thou art tender-hearted, and save me from the abyss!

Clothe me sacredly, the work of the hands of Thy goodness, who was torn away by senseless mind: O Lover of mankind, Who for my sake was well pleased to be born after me, for the sake of the abyss of Thine ineffable compassions: by the prayers of Thine ever-Virgin Mother, O Word, account me worthy of divine conversion, as God!

*Other Stichera to the Forerunner John.*

*Podoben: "The same Tone and Podoben" (Гла́съ и҆ подо́бенъ то́йже):*

Blessed John Forerunner: ever increasing my humble soul in love toward the Lord by thy sacred intercessions...

[f. 239rB] ...quench the fire of my pleasures, stir me up to the fulfillment of the divine commandments, and cleanse the feelings of my heart in truth, that I may glorify thee!

Offspring of the barren woman, and garden of pious purity, adornment of men, all-lauded Forerunner John: divine guardian of my humble soul, grant beneficence by thy prayers, delivering me from the serpent's deceit, and from his wicked assaults and snares!

All sweetness art thou and delight, filled with divine grace, O ever-glorious one, gladdening all that in faith come unto thee: sweetening human infirmities of soul and body, sorrows and assaults of evil, and destroying for us the bitterness of all soul-corrupting pleasures!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

All my hope I place in thy protection, O pure Birth-giver of God: from temptations, perils, dread outpouring of wrath, and demonic oppression save me, as thou hast an abyss of mercy, and wast revealed as the mediatress of salvation, O Sovereign Lady: who didst bear the merciful God, Who alone is all-compassionate and abundant in tender mercies!...[^317]

[f. 239vA] At the Aposticha, Penitential Stichera. Tone 8:

Unto Thee, the King and God, the Angels unceasingly sing praise: and I fall down before Thee, crying like the Publican: O God, cleanse me and have mercy on me!

Immortal art thou, O my soul; be not submerged by the waves of this life: but arise, crying aloud unto thy Benefactor: O God, cleanse me and have mercy on me!

Martyrs:

Ye Martyrs of the Lord, pray unto our God, and entreat for our souls a multitude of compassions, and cleansing of our many transgressions, we pray you!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

Rejoice, boast of the universe! Rejoice, temple of the Lord! Rejoice, overshadowing mountain! Rejoice, refuge of all! Rejoice, golden lampstand! Rejoice, pure glory of the Orthodox! Rejoice, Mary Mother of Christ God! Rejoice, Paradise! Rejoice, divine table! Rejoice, temple! Rejoice, all-golden jar! Rejoice, hope of all!

## TUESDAY MATINS: REPENTANCE AND ST. JOHN THE FORERUNNER (TONE 8)

ON TUESDAY AT MATINS:

After the 1st Kathisma, Penitential Sessional Hymns. Tone 8:

O most tender-hearted Lord, behold my lowliness, for little by little my life is consumed, and from my works there is no salvation for me: therefore I pray: O most tender-hearted Lord, behold my lowliness and save me!

When the Day of the Judge is come, take heed, O my soul, and meditate upon the hour of that dread Day; for judgment is without...

[f. 239vB] ...without mercy unto them that have shown no mercy: therefore spare me, O Savior, for Thou alone art sinless!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

As the unshakable establishment of the faith and the honorable gift unto our souls, in songs do we the faithful magnify the Theotokos: Rejoice, thou who didst contain the living Stone in thy womb! Rejoice, hope of the ends of the earth, and defender of the sorrowful! Rejoice, unwedded Bride!

After the 2nd Kathisma, Penitential Sessional Hymns. Tone 8:

Like the Harlot I fall down before Thee, that I may receive forgiveness; and instead of myrrh, I offer Thee tears from my heart: that as Thou didst have compassion on her, O Savior, so Thou mayest grant me cleansing of sins: for like her I cry aloud unto Thee: Deliver me from the mire of my deeds!

My life is drawing to a close, and the dread throne is being prepared; life passes by, the judgment awaits me, threatening me with fiery torment and unquenchable flame: grant me a rain of tears and quench its power, O Thou Who desirest all men to be saved!

Martyrs:

As spiritual luminaries were ye revealed, O holy Martyrs: for by faith ye destroyed the mist of deceit, enlightened your spiritual lamps, and entered with glory into the heavenly bridal chamber with the Bridegroom: and now pray ye that our souls may be saved!

Theotokion:

All-pure Virgin, Mother of Christ: healing the cruel passions of my soul, I pray thee: and grant forgiveness unto my transgressions...

[f. 240rA] ...transgressions, which I have foolishly committed, defiling my soul and polluting my body, the wretched one! Woe is me, what shall I do in that hour when the Angels shall separate my soul from my wretched body? Then be thou my helper and intercessor, for in thee thy servant hath placed his hope!

After the 3rd Kathisma, Penitential Sessional Hymns. Tone 8.

*Podoben: "That which was commanded mystically" (Повеле́нное та́инство):*

Taking to mind the day and the hour of Thy dread, awesome, and inexorable tribunal, O Master Christ: I tremble like a malefactor, having shameful works and cruel deeds, which alone I have zealously committed: therefore with fear I fall down before Thee, and painfully cry aloud: By the prayers of Thy Forerunner, O most merciful One, save me!

O my soul, consuming thy life in negligence: arise at last and cry aloud unto repentance! Weep for the ruin of hardened hearts, lest thou wail there without success, shuddering with fear as thou meditatest upon the dread Second Coming; and before the judgment, condemn thyself, and thou shalt escape that righteous tribunal!

Glory: Now and ever: Theotokion:

Entreated by the prayers of Thy Bodiless Hosts, O Christ, and of Thy Forerunner, the Disciples, the Prophets, the Martyrs, and All the Saints, and of Thine unwedded Theotokos and good Mother: grant us to walk in Thy light, and account us worthy to obtain Thy Kingdom, for the tender mercies of Thy grace!

[f. 240rB] PENITENTIAL CANON.

Creation of Joseph.

Ode 1. Tone 8. Heirmos:

Unto Him Who crushed wars with His arm, and led Israel through the Red Sea: let us sing unto Him as our Deliverer, for He hath been glorified!

Troparia:

Fill my heart with compunction, O Christ, that through repentance I may enter into the habitation: and I will bring confession unto Thee, Who hast loosed me from debts!

Loose me, O Word, from the bonds of my countless evils: that I may walk in repentance in Thy righteous paths, which guide unto the divine resting-place of eternal beauty!

Martyrs:

The great majesty of Thy Martyrs was lifted up unto the heights, O Christ, having suffered most excellently: and they were magnified with Thy supreme gifts of grace!

By the sprinkling of the divine blood of the holy sufferers, the blood sacrifice offered by the enemy ceased: and the earth was sanctified by the grace of the Spirit!

Theotokion:

Show me the paths of repentance, O Virgin: and turn my steps that open unto sin, that I may sing praise unto thee, all-hymned Birth-giver of God!

Another Canon to the Forerunner John.

Same Tone and Heirmos:

[Let us shake the tyrant in the sea]... O Forerunner, herald of repentance... my soul being bound by vows, ever pray unto the Savior and Lord, enlightening my mind and heart, who honor thee in love!

As a most fair nurture...[^318]

[f. 240vA] ...most fair nurture, O Forerunner, Martyr of Christ: guide me who am now in the wilderness of the passions unto the life of repentance, by thy divine prayer!

Quickly deliver me by thine intercession from sin which torments me, O wise Forerunner, I pray thee: and destroy the moving darts of demons against us!

Theotokion:

Save me, Mother of the Truth, who am sorely tempest-tossed by passions and often submerged: and direct me, O pure one, unto the calm harbor of salvation!

Ode 3. Heirmos:

My heart hath been established in the Lord: my horn hath been exalted in my God; my mouth hath been enlarged over mine enemies: I have rejoiced in Thy salvation [1 Sam. 2:1]!

Troparia:

Wash my heart clean from malicious defilement, and account me worthy to appear blameless before Thee in the dread Day, O my Christ, as Thou art most good!

Belial was able to deaden me through deceit by the sting of sin, O Word; but do Thou Thyself heal me with the life-bearing remedies of repentance, O Christ!

Martyrs:

Couragiously the passion-bearers cried aloud unto one another in the stadium: "Let no one deny! The Master stands before us as helper, while we suffer with noble mind!"

Precious stones of the Church, divine pillars of piety, overthrowers of deceit: let us all praise, honoring in faith the Martyrs of the Lord!

Theotokion:

Restoration of the fallen, O all-pure one...

[f. 240vB] ...raise me up that am fallen from the pit of mine evils, and establish me, O Sovereign Lady, upon the rock of the commandments of God!

Another Heirmos:

(Canon to the Forerunner)

Establish our mind and hearts: rain down upon me a drop of repentance, O thou who in the river Jordan didst baptize the tender-hearted Lord of all, O Forerunner and Martyr worthy of glory!

My mind is ever tossed about by the entwined waves of life: I flee unto thy protection, O Forerunner of the Savior: speed forth as a helper unto thy servant!

In nightly prayers I call upon thee, the torch of day unto the world, O God-blessed Forerunner: enlighten the feelings of my heart!

Theotokion:

Rejoice in our behalf, O Holy Theotokos! Rejoice, thou who didst bear joy unto the world! Rejoice, jar whence the heavenly Manna was given unto all the faithful!

Ode 4. Heirmos:

Troparia:

The deceiving enemy by the tasting of sinful deceit hath driven me far from Thee, O Good One, and by his custom hath made me his food: speed forth, O Thou Who alone art the Savior, to deliver me!

Unrevealed and secret things of mine Thou Thyself knowest, O Lord, who have sinned much against Thee: have compassion according to the multitude of Thy tender mercies, as Thou art the Word of God abundant in mercy, and grant me a cleansing season of repentance...

[f. 241rA] ...grant me a cleansing season of repentance!

Martyrs:

Being tempest-tossed by torments as by waves, O Martyrs, by the pilotage of Christ ye were guided unto the harbors of the heavenly Kingdom, having severed the enemy: truly adorned with crowns!

Having renewed the earth by piety through sufferings, O Martyrs: ye sowed the seed of confession upon it, and reaped the harvest of eternity from martyrdom, a fair ear of wheat yielding a hundredfold by grace!

Theotokion:

All-pure Sovereign Lady, fill my thought with all joy as I sing aloud unto thee: granting me good weeping, causes of repentance, and understanding of salvation!

Another Heirmos: I heard Thy report, O Lord:

(Canon to the Forerunner)

I weep for myself, having an uncorrected life ever: save me and have compassion upon me, O Forerunner, who have sunk in sins!

In prayers and supplications may I find thee as a helper, O blessed one, strengthening my soul and illuminating my thought!

Submerged by the tempest of transgressions and in peril, O Baptist of Christ: guide me unto the harbor of divine knowledge!

Theotokion:

Having humbled me who live in high-mindedness, save me, O all-pure one: who didst bear Him Who exalted our humbled nature, O all-pure one!

Ode 5. Heirmos:

Drive away the darkness of my soul, O Giver of light, Christ God, Who didst banish the primordial darkness from the abyss: and grant me the light of Thy commandments, O Word, that rising early in the morning, I may glorify Thee!

[f. 241rB] Troparia:

O Thou Who didst cleanse the Harlot and the lepers by Thy command, Creator of all things: cleanse my humble soul from the defilement of sin, and make it beautiful with shining garments, O Master!

Loosing me from the bonds of my many transgressions, O Christ God: direct me to walk without stumbling in Thy paths, that being delivered from the flesh and having dwelt in the resting-place of the Saints, I may glorify Thee!

Martyrs:

Having decayed the garment of their bodies in afflictions, the glorious Martyrs, being clothed, were adorned: they dwell in the Kingdom on high in joy, adorned with radiant severed crowns!

The fury of the persecutors the Martyrs wisely exchanged: being weighed down and surrounded by diverse torments, they hastened rejoicing unto the true expanse of the heavenly Kingdom!

Theotokion:

Holy Theotokos, who didst bear in the flesh the Holy Word, Who alone rests upon all the Saints: hallow my mind, that it may ever cleave unto good works!

Another Heirmos: From the night of ignorance:

(Canon to the Forerunner)

In the night of life, enlighten me who have gone astray, O glorious Forerunner: who art the lamp of the Sun of righteousness!

In the coming judgment, when I am to stand before the Tribunal: may I find thee as an intercessor, O Forerunner, delivering me from dread condemnation!

In assault, and shaken by the attacks of demons: establish me...[^319]

[f. 241vA] ...established upon the rock of divine desires imparted unto me!

Theotokion:

Ode 6. Heirmos:

Even as Thou didst deliver the Prophet from the nethermost deep, O Christ God: so also deliver me from my sins, as Thou art the Lover of mankind, and direct my life, I pray Thee!

Troparia:

Like the Publican I groan; like the Harlot I shed tears; like Peter I cry aloud: being submerged by many transgressions, O Christ: stretch forth Thy hand of help unto me, and save me!

Martyrs:

As divinely radiant beacons, ye illumine all the surrounding world with the rays of your sufferings: and disperse the darkness of deceit, O Martyrs of Christ, by your confession!

Having found a most blessed end, O all-holy Martyrs, ye ever honor the blessed God: taking delight in His splendors!

Theotokion:

The jar that received the Manna formerly prefigured thee, O Theotokos: for thou didst bear Christ, Who gave the spiritual Manna unto all that honor thee!

Another Heirmos: Grant me a voice:

(Canon to the Forerunner)

By the tears of true repentance cleanse the substance of my heart, O all-wise John: making it fruitful in virtues!

[f. 241vB] ...deliver me from cruel afflictions!

Theotokion:

O pure one who alone in the flesh didst bear the Word: deliver our souls, I pray thee, from the snares of the enemy!

Ode 7. Heirmos:

Troparia:

Martyrs:

Having endured suffering with fortitude, the Martyrs, mediating immortality: pour forth a stream of healings, putting human passions to shame!

Theotokion:

Another Heirmos:

(Canon to the Forerunner)

[f. 242rA] O Forerunner who didst prepare the ways of the Lord: direct my paths unto Him, that I may cry aloud: Blessed art Thou unto ages, O God of our fathers!

Martyrs:

Ye quenched the burning furnace of polytheism, O wise sufferers...

[f. 242rB] ...shedding your many streams of blood unjustly poured out for the sake of the love of the Creator: therefore take delight in the torrent of pleasure!

Theotokion:

Tossed about by the storm of sin, I cry aloud unto thee, O good and pure one: by thy mediation direct me unto saving repentance and unto the eternal haven: that I, who am continually darkened by slothfulness, may know the light of salvation!

(Canon to the Forerunner)

Theotokion:

[f. 242vA] ...in the house of David His servant; wherein the Dayspring from on high hath visited us, and hath directed us into the way of peace [Lk. 1:68-69, 78-79]!

Troparia:

That I also may be saved, I give thanks unto Thee, O Christ, and magnify Thee; look down upon me who have received many wounds upon my back: and heal me, pouring in the wine and oil of the knowledge of Thy compassion, O Savior!

Even as Thou didst deliver the good-natured thief from murder and cruel ruin at his innocent cry: even as Thou didst show mercy unto the weeping harlot, and unto Peter the great disciple, and David the Prophet: so also have mercy upon me, O Savior!

Martyrs:

Having become conformed unto the Passions of Him Who suffered for our sake, the passion-bearers are glorified together with Him: being deified by divine communion, and shining brighter than the rays of the visible sun: ye enlighten the hearts of the faithful!

The virtue of the holy sufferers shone forth, enriching every city with these imperishable treasures of faith: shining with the consecrated grace of most glorious miracles: we hymn them as fervent protectors!

Theotokion:

With the illuminating splendors of the Son of God Who came forth from thy womb, O all-immaculate one: enlighten them that sing praise unto thee in faith: and deliver from ignorant darkness and future torment us that have thee as mediatress of all!

Another Heirmos:

(Canon to the Forerunner)

Him Who was manifested on the mountain:

[f. 242vB] Troparia:

As the voice of the Word: direct my paths unto God, O all-wise Baptist: and deliver me from the malice of demons and from the assault of men: that I may worthily bless thee!
