Theotokion:

O pure and most glorified Virgin Theotokos: with the Forerunner pray thou unto thy Son and God, to save from every distress them that bless thee in faith!

Penitential. Tone 8.

When I consider in my mind the multitude of evils committed by me, and come to the thought of that dread examination: seized with trembling, I flee unto Thee, the Lover of mankind and God. Therefore, despise me not, I pray Thee, Who alone art without sin: grant compunction unto my humble soul before the end, and save me!

Grant me tears, O God, as once unto the sinful woman: and account me worthy to wet Thy feet that have delivered me from the path of error; and to offer unto Thee the myrrh of sweet fragrance: a pure life acquired by me through repentance, that I also may hear Thy gracious voice: Thy faith hath saved thee, go in peace [Lk. 7:50]!

[f. 243rA] Martyrs:

Greatly did ye contend, O holy ones, enduring torments from the lawless with valor: confessing Christ before kings, and having departed from life, ye work wonders in the world: and heal the sick by your sufferings, O holy ones. Intercede that our souls may be saved!

Glory... Both now... Theotokion:

Thy protection, O Virgin Theotokos, is a spiritual infirmary: for fleeing thereto, we are delivered from spiritual illnesses!

Deliver me from passions, and sins, and cruel future torment, by thy prayers, O most pure Theotokos: who blessest them that piously magnify thee!

## TUESDAY EVENING VESPERS (FOR WEDNESDAY) (TONE 8)

ON TUESDAY EVENING, AT "LORD, I HAVE CRIED":

*Stichera of the Precious Cross, Tone 8.*

*Podoben: "Martyrs of the Lord" (Мч҃нци Гдⷭ҇ни):*

Nailed upon the Cross, O Christ, Thou wast pierced in the ribs, and in Thy side Thou wast wounded: pouring forth drops of divine salvation unto me, O most good One, both blood and water, that Thou mightest wash away my festering filth and defilement. Glory to Thy goodness, O all-compassionate One!

Having endured suffering, O Master, that Thou mightest grant passionlessness unto all them...

[f. 243rB] ...that venerate Thy Sufferings, and voluntary Slaughter, and Spear, and Nails, and Reed: which Thou didst endure willingly in long-suffering, that Thou mightest procure passionlessness for me, O Lord, by Thy Sufferings!

Stavrotheotokion:

The unblemished Heifer, beholding the Bullock voluntarily suspended upon the Tree, lamented and cried aloud with compunction...[^321]

[f. 243vA] ...Woe is me, most beloved Child! What hath the ungrateful Jewish assembly rendered unto Thee, seeking to bereave me of Thee, O all-beloved One?

Other Stichera to the Most Holy Theotokos:

Tone the same.

I cannot bear, O Child, to see Thee asleep upon the Tree, Who givest vigilance unto all: that Thou mightest grant divine and saving vigilance unto them that of old fell asleep through the slumber of the fruit's transgression, cried the weeping Virgin: whom we magnify!

The unjust assembly lifted Thee up upon the Cross, O Lamb That takest away the sins of the world: and the spear pierced Thy ribs, O Long-suffering One; and they nailed Thy hands and Thy feet: O what wicked boldness! O what impudence! cried the most pure one with compunction, weeping!

What is this sight that I now behold, O Master? Thou Who most marvelously holdest all creation in Thy palm art unjustly slaughtered upon the Tree like a lamb, O Word of God, hanged among the disobedient! O what forbearance! O what goodness of Thine, all-compassionate One! cried the all-immaculate one with tears!

Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion:

When the Ewe-lamb and Virgin beheld Thee, the Lamb, led unto the slaughter: she followed with tears, O Word, and cried aloud: Whither art Thou hastening, my Child? I shall go with Thee, my sweetest One; for I cannot bear not to behold Thee, O my Jesus abundant in mercy!

[f. 243vB] At the Aposticha, Stichera:

Of the Cross, Tone 8.

Having been lifted up upon the Cross, O Christ God: and Thou didst open the gates of Paradise: we glorify Thy Sufferings!

Thou wast nailed upon the Cross, O Christ God: and didst save the human race: we glorify Thee, our Deliverer!

Martyrs:

Thy Martyrs, O Lord, forgot the things of this life and disregarded torments for the sake of the life to come: and were shown forth as heirs thereof: therefore they also rejoice with the Angels. By their prayers, grant great mercy unto Thy people!

*Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion.*

*Podoben: "O Lord, though Thou didst stand before the tribunal" (Гдⷭ҇и, аще и на судїщи):*

O Lord, when the sun beheld Thee, the Sun of righteousness, suspended upon the Tree: it hid its rays, and the moon turned its light into darkness; and Thine all-immaculate Mother was pierced in her maternal heart!

ON WEDNESDAY, AT MATINS,

After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymns:

Of the Cross, Tone 8.

Beholding the Author of life hanging upon the Cross, the thief said: If He that is crucified with us were not God incarnate, the sun would not have hidden its rays, nor would the earth have quaked with trembling. But O Thou Who endurest all things: Remember me, O Lord, when Thou comest into Thy Kingdom!

Between two thieves Thy Cross was found as a righteous balance: for the one, it was dragged down into hades by the weight of blasphemy; but for the other, it was lightened of sins unto the knowledge of theology...

[f. 244rA] ...O Christ God, glory to Thee!

Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion:

Beholding the Lamb, Pastor, and Deliverer unjustly lifted up upon the Cross, the Ewe-lamb wept bitterly and cried aloud: The world indeed rejoices, receiving redemption through Thee; but my maternal heart burns, beholding Thy Crucifixion which Thou endurest for the tender mercy of Thy compassion, O most good, sinless Lord! Therefore with one accord let us cry aloud: O Virgin, have compassion upon us, and deliver thy servants from every distress!

After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns:

Of the Cross, Tone 8.

In the midst of Eden a tree budded forth death; but in the midst of all the earth, the Tree blossomed life. For having tasted of the first fruit, being incorrupt, we became corrupt; but having obtained the second, we have enjoyed incorruption: for by the Cross we have been saved, since God is the Deliverer of the human race!

In Paradise of old the tree stripped man bare, through the tasting of which the enemy brought in deadening; but the Tree of the Cross, bearing for mankind the garment of eternal life, was planted upon the earth, and all the world was filled with all joy. Beholding it lifted up, let us the faithful people cry aloud in faith unto God: Thy house is full of glory!

Martyrs:

Shown forth as ever-shining beacons unto the universe through faith, O Martyrs, ye placed all your hope upon the Lord: and by the spiritual brilliance of the Holy Spirit, ye enlightened the eyes of your souls. Therefore, pouring out your blood like water as a spiritual chalice...

[f. 244rB] ...ye were revealed unto the Church, O all-praised Passion-bearers: pray unto Christ God, to grant forgiveness of transgressions unto us that celebrate your holy memory with love!

Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion:

When thou didst behold Him Who was incarnate without change lifted up upon the Cross between two thieves, having taken up lamentation, thou didst cry aloud: Woe is me, my sweetest Child! How art Thou willingly crucified, Who takest away the sins of the world? For as Thou art compassionate, Thou didst desire, as God, that hymns of praise should be offered unto Thee by mankind!

After the 3rd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns:

*Of the Cross, Tone 8.*

*Podoben: "That which was commanded mystically" (Повеленное таинственно):*

Beholding Thee lifted up upon the Cross, O Christ, the unwaning Sun: through fear the sun was darkened, and all the earth quaked; the stones split apart in trembling, and the veil of the temple was rent in twain; and the dead arose from the tombs, glorifying the dread and divine condescension of our only God!

The tree in Eden formerly brought forth bitterness; but the Tree of the Cross hath blossomed forth sweet life. For Adam by eating slid into corruption; but we, partaking of the flesh of Christ, are quickened and deified mystically, receiving the unshared Kingdom of God. Therefore in faith we cry aloud: Glory to Thy Passion, O Christ![^322]

[f. 244vA] Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion:

Being preserved ever by the Cross of thy Son and God, O Virgin: we overcome demonic assaults and snares: chanting unto thee, the true Theotokos, and loving thee, all generations bless thee, O all-pure one, even as thou didst foretell. Therefore grant forgiveness of our transgressions through thy prayers!

CANON OF THE PRECIOUS AND LIFE-CREATING CROSS OF THE LORD.

Composition of Joseph.

Ode 1. Tone 8. Heirmos:

He submerged the armed Pharaoh:

Troparia:

When I was dead through the pleasurable fall by the tree, O Word: dying upon the Cross Thou didst quicken me, and didst adorn me with glory: I venerate Thy Wood, glorifying Thy Sufferings and boundless mercy!

When the Vine was stretched out upon the Tree: He poured forth the uncultivated wine of grace: gladdening hearts, utterly destroying the drunkenness of deceit, and cleansing sin!

Martyrs:

Adorned with wounds, O great martyrs, and beautified with the sufferings of torments: ye stand with glory before the Master Who made all things beautiful, shining ingloriously yet revealed as godlike!

Plainly strengthened by divine power, O blessed ones: ye manfully cast down all the destructive might of the strong one: and crowned with crowns of victory, ye stand rejoicing before God!

Stavrotheotokion:

Standing by Thy Cross, O Lord, she that knew not wedlock...

[f. 244vB] ...and beholding Thy wounding, O Master, lamented and cried aloud: Woe is me, my Child! Having escaped pains in Thy birthgiving, now I am pained and torn with grief!

Another Canon to the Most Holy Theotokos.

Heirmos the same.

Upon thee, O Virgin, have I placed the hope of my salvation: wash me clean from all defilement of sin, and make me pure before God and thy Son, to do that which is well-pleasing unto His all-holy name!

O Gate of Light, enlighten mine eyes which the gloomy serpent hath darkened with the darkness of transgressions; and open unto me the gates of repentance, O Virgin: and guide me unto life, snatching me from flame and darkness!

O Mother of God, as thou hast boldness toward the only-begotten Word Who was incorruptibly born of thee, and Who is co-beginningless with the Father: pray, O all-immaculate one, to deliver my soul from demonic malice, and from fire, and from every torment!

Blessed is the Fruit of thy womb, O Bride of God: whereby all we earthborn were delivered from the curse: O blessed, all-pure one, ineffable wonder, incomprehensible vision, salvation of all the faithful!

Ode 3. Heirmos:

O Thou Who in the beginning didst establish the heavens:

Troparia:

Thou Who didst establish the heavens, and didst lay the foundation of the earth, and didst bind the sea by Thy word: Thou wast proclaimed for my sake and nailed unto the Cross, that Thou mightest loose me from the bonds of sin, O Lover of mankind!

[f. 245rA] Rushing against the Tree of the Cross, the enemy was slain together with all his evil deeds; and he that was condemned by deceitful arrogance was shown mercy: and the establishment of piety was established in Thee!

Martyrs:

Delivered over by the wicked persecutor unto diverse woundings, and to the sword, and to beasts, with stripped flesh, O divine and noble sufferers: ye remained unshaken by the divine nod!

Lifting up their contemplation and elevating their minds unto eternal things, the glorious Martyrs of Christ completely disregarded passing things: therefore rejoicing they endured unbearable pains!

Stavrotheotokion:

The all-hymned Ewe-lamb, beholding the Lamb unjustly lifted up upon the Tree: lamented and cried aloud, weeping with maternal tears, singing and glorifying His long-suffering!

Another Heirmos: Thou art the establishment:

(Canon to Theotokos)

Directing all my desire unto thee, O good and pure one: quickly deliver me from carnal desires!

Shining upon me with the pure dawn of repentance, O good one, Gate of Light: disperse the mist of my sins!

O thou who alone art all-immaculate: deliver us from great reproach, and from coming temptations, and from eternal fire!

Hasten to visit him that is sick, O honored one: and deliver me from cruel wounds and from great sorrow!

Ode 4. Heirmos:

Thou art my Christ, O Lord, Thou art my power [f. 245rB] Troparia:

The human race was raised up from the fall which the First-formed suffered of old: for the Creator of all was lifted up upon the Tree, His fingers stained with blood, willingly nailed by nails in His hands, and pierced with a spear in His side!

The Cross was set up, and all hades fell down: when Thou wast stripped naked, O Savior, the stranger was stripped bare; and Adam was clothed in the garment of divine incorruption: creation was enlightened when the sun was darkened, while Thou wast crucified upon the Tree, O Christ!

Martyrs:

As lambs of the new slaughter, O Martyrs, ye were offered unto the slaughtered Word: by streams of blood having dried up the sea of deceit through divine grace, and having quenched the burning of passionate diseases by the shower of miracles, O glorious ones, ye are ever praised!

The severance of all limbs ye endured, O Martyrs: the tearing of skin and nails, the pitiless cutting off of hands and feet, of tongue, and the dismemberment of the joints of the body: therefore ye were accounted worthy of exceeding great glory, standing before the God of all!

Stavrotheotokion:

Beholding her Lamb lifted up upon the Tree, the immaculate Heifer cried aloud with lamentation: My Child! How hath the lawless assembly shown no compassion at all unto Thee Who didst show them mercy, but through deceitful counsel unjustly resolved to deliver Thee unto death?

Another Heirmos: I heard Thy report, O Lord:

(Canon to Theotokos)

Mine obscure soul, darkened by transgressions, do thou illuminate with light, O ever-Virgin: who didst bear the Sun of righteousness![^323]

[f. 245vA] Deliver me from temptations, and from the soul-destroying storm of life, and free me from eternal fire, O Bride of God!

O radiant and sacred vessel, and dwelling of the uncontainable Nature: enlighten my soul which is darkened by many passions!

O most holy Bride of God, Sovereign Lady of the world: save me, delivering me from tribulations and driving away the assault of passions by thy supplication!

Ode 5. Heirmos:

Therefore hast Thou cast me off from Thy face:

Troparia:

That Thou mightest deliver me from pleasurable tasting, O Long-suffering One, Thou didst willingly taste gall; and that Thou mightest strip me of deadness, O Jesus, Thou didst deign to be nailed naked upon the Tree: I sing praise unto Thy compassion!

Making new my soul that had become corrupt through passions, O Word, Thou didst surrender Thy soul unto the Father while hanging upon the Tree: and the soulless earth, unable to endure this, shook with fear, singing praise unto Thee!

Martyrs:

Ye were adorned, O divine Martyrs, being beautified with sufferings, and following in the footsteps of Him Who through His Passions granted passionlessness unto all, the only-begotten Word of the beginningless Father: therefore ye are glorified together with Him!

Having withdrawn from earthly things, ye inherited invisible things, taking up your abode in the heavenly mansions: and being deified immaterially by divine communion, O victorious Martyrs, ye are saved!

Stavrotheotokion:

An awesome vision do I behold! cried the all-praised one, sighing: How hast Thou Who by a nod shakest all the earth...

[f. 245vB] ...fallen asleep, suspended upon the Tree, desiring to awaken sleeping men? I venerate Thy long-suffering, O my Son!

Another Heirmos: Rising early in the morning:

(Canon to Theotokos)

We sing praise unto thee, O all-immaculate Virgin: who didst contain God the Word in thy womb, O all-blameless one!

From unquenchable fire and from the worm deliver me, O Mother of God: as thou hast the power to show mercy with compunction!

A rampart and all-holy strength art thou unto the faithful: save from perils them that sing praise unto thee!

Heal my sick soul, O pure Sovereign Lady: who didst bear the salvation of all and the Bearer of diseases!

Ode 6. Heirmos:

The abyss of sins and the storm of transgressions trouble me, and violently cast me into the deep of despair: but do Thou Thyself stretch forth Thy strong hand unto me, as unto Peter, and lead me up from corruption, O my God!

Troparia:

All the heavenly Powers sang praise and were terrified, beholding Thee, O Word, hanging upon the Cross: and wounded Adam was healed by Thy wound, O Savior, and the curse was banished!

Humanity is loosed from unbreakable bonds, when Thou, O Word, wast bound in the flesh: and the tormentor is exposed like a bird, and mocked in the hands of the faithful: glory to Thy compassion, O Christ!

Martyrs:

The passion-bearers of the Lord were revealed like coals of fire, burning up every substance of impiety by grace...

[f. 246rA] ...and walking upon the coals of fire with pure feet, they received divine refreshment!

Revealed as sheep of the true Shepherd, O passion-bearers: ye remained uninjured in the midst of wild wolves, and having finished well the divine course, ye took up your abode in the heavenly city!

Stavrotheotokion:

When the Virgin beheld Thee, the Life, Who art beautiful in countenance beyond the sons of men, she cried aloud: And how dost Thou die for my sake, O Son, without form upon the Crucifixion, Who didst adorn all things by Thy nod?

Another Heirmos: Cleanse me, O Savior:

(Canon to Theotokos)

O pure Mary and all-honored dwelling of the Creator of all: granting tears that cleanse the soul, deliver me from future judgment and torment!

O Gate of God, show divine entrances unto my humble soul: entering into which with confession, I may receive forgiveness of evils, O Theotokos!

A deep of sins and waves of despair buffet my mind: have compassion, O Sovereign Lady, and stretch forth thy hand unto me and save me, who didst bear the Savior!

All we faithful have thee as mediatress and rampart, who ever find ourselves in the depth of evils, tumult, and afflictions, O Theotokos, sole refuge of the faithful!

Ode 7. Heirmos:

The fire was ashamed before the condescension of God: Thou wast pierced in Thy hands wherewith Thou didst work miracles, O Christ, and didst endure wounds, healing all my wounds: I sing praise unto Thee, crying aloud...

[f. 246rB] ...Blessed is the God of our fathers!

Thou wast nailed in Thy hands and feet with nails, O Savior, when Thou wast crucified, and pierced in the side: pouring forth streams of forgiveness unto all them that unceasingly sing praise, saying: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

Martyrs:

The Martyrs of God formed a choir, singing praise: being numbered with the angelic ranks, and enlightening the earth, and ever chanting: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

The universe, being illumined with the splendors of the Saints, sends up sanctification and deliverance unto all them that praise you, O divine Martyrs, and sing praise unto Christ: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

Stavrotheotokion:

How hath the unwaning Sun set, crucified upon the Tree? cried the Virgin unto Thee, O Word; and seeing it, the sun stayed its course, unable to shine: while Thou sufferest, O Master, I praise Thy guilelessness, O my Son!

Another Heirmos: The Children from Judea:

(Canon to Theotokos)

I pray thee, O all-pure one: put to death the sin that dwells in me, and account me worthy to attain life, O Virgin, and deliver me from the portion of them that are tormented there!

Diverse passions surround me: O pure one who didst bear the Fountain of passionlessness, deliver me from their dominion and from eternal fire, O Theotokos, by thy prayers!

Through willful inclination I have sinned, and I am enslaved to disorderly habits: renew me who now flee unto thy tender mercy, and save me from despair, O all-holy Theotokos: quench...[^324]

[f. 246vA] ...quench the burning coals of the passions of my soul, and calm the storm of my heart, O pure Mother of God; and deliver me, O all-pure one, from demonic torment and from eternal fire!

Ode 8. Heirmos:

Sevenfold the furnace:

Troparia:

Having sprung from the root of Jesse, O Christ, incarnate: Thou dost root out the overgrowing thorn of Adam's transgression, wearing a crown of thorns and nailed upon the Tree, which budded forth healing from the wood for them that sing of Thy salvation: Children, bless; priests, sing praise; people, supremely exalt Him unto ages!

That Thou mightest make man a lover of God, O Christ Lover of mankind, Thou becamest man and partookest of the Cross, pierced in the ribs and given vinegar with gall to drink: therefore, saved by Thy Sufferings, O Word, we cry aloud in thanksgiving: Children, bless; priests, sing praise; people, supremely exalt Christ unto ages!

Martyrs:

Bound as martyrs and slaughtered like lambs, and pitilessly roasted upon the fire, cast unto wild beasts, and beheaded in the head: ye rejoice with ineffable joy, crying aloud: Children, bless; priests, sing praise; people, supremely exalt Christ unto ages!

Crowned Martyrs, companions of the Angels, who trampled underfoot the bodiless enemies: make supplication unto the Lord for us, that we may live in love and great unity of mind, crying aloud: Children, bless; priests, sing praise; people, supremely exalt Christ unto ages!

Stavrotheotokion:

Maternally groaning in pain, lamenting, and unable to bear the agitation of her maternal heart...

[f. 246vB] ...looking upon the Cross unto Him Who was born of her womb, she cried aloud: What is this sight, my Child? How dost Thou suffer, Who art impassible by nature, desiring in every way to free the human race from corruption?

Another Heirmos: The King of heaven:

(Canon to Theotokos)

O Virgin Birth-giver of God: hide my sins, and lighten the burden of my transgressions, that I may magnify thee!

O Virgin who alone didst bear Christ God: by thy fervent and transforming supplications, show His prayer favorable unto me, O pure one, that I may be saved from eternal fire!

My transgressions have multiplied, rising above my head, O Theotokos: give me now a helping hand, and deliver me, an unprofitable servant, from unquenchable flame!

Enlighten the eyes of my heart, I pray thee, O all-pure one, who am blinded by the blackness of sin, and show them receptive of divine radiance: that through thee I may appear pure unto thy Son!

Ode 9. Heirmos:

Every ear was amazed at this:

Troparia:

Thou didst heal my wounds, O my Master, being wounded and staining Thy hands with blood: and to walk in saving paths, as Thou art good, Thou didst direct me, O Lord, having nailed Thy feet upon the Cross: seeing Thee walking of old in Paradise, the forebears hid themselves; but restored upon the Cross, the First-formed who fell in a great fall was righted...

[f. 247rA] ...and all the might of the adversary fell down: and all the earth was sanctified by the blood and water poured forth from Thy ribs: therefore we unceasingly magnify Thee, O all-compassionate One!

Martyrs:

Blessed holy Martyrs: ye loosed the bonds of the wicked one, and by the fetters which ye patiently endured ye bound him, and made him subject beneath your feet, filled with shame and made a laughing-stock unto the beholders by divine grace!

The earth was sanctified by the laying down of the relics of the holy Martyrs; for it pours forth a fountain of great healings: these things divinely establish us, unceasingly curing the passions of body and soul, and banishing the malice of demons by divine grace!

Stavrotheotokion:

Having escaped maternal pains at the time of Thy birthgiving, O Long-suffering One: yet now beholding Thee partaking of the pains of suffering, and having received Thee upon her knees from the Cross, the all-pure one was filled with grief of heart and soul, and cried aloud: whom worthily we magnify!

Another Heirmos: Amazed was every ear:

(Canon to Theotokos)

Have compassion, O all-pure one, upon my wretched soul, and put to death destructive passions: and drive away tormenting perplexity, and grant me streams of holy tears multiplied: whereby I may be delivered from the cruel condemnation awaiting me!

A rampart unto Christians and a firm refuge unto the world, wherein we are saved, art thou, O pure Virgin Bride of God: for God, truly incarnate, gave thee unto all as a saving protection...

[f. 247rB] ...therefore, O pure one, save me, the unworthy one!

O beginningless Word of the Father, my Son, and co-enthroned with the Holy Spirit: how hast Thou stretched out Thy most pure hands upon the Cross? Whither hath Thy great poverty fled? cried the all-immaculate one, standing before Thy Crucifixion!

Distilling divine sweetness, O thou that didst bear the Joy of all: sweeten my soul which hath been embittered by the venom of the serpent, alienating me from bitter sin ever through thine intercession, O unashamed mediatress of the faithful!

At the Aposticha, Stichera:

Of the Cross, Tone 8.

The rod of Moses prefigured Thy precious Cross, O our Savior: for thereby Thou savest Thy people from the depth of the sea, as the Lover of mankind!

In the Paradise of Eden of old, a tree bringing eating blossomed in the midst of the orchard; but the Church, O Christ, blossomed Thy Cross, pouring forth life unto all the world. But that one brought death unto Adam who ate thereof; whereas this one quickened the thief who was saved through faith. Show us also partakers of his salvation, O Christ God, Who by Thy Passion didst destroy the snares of the enemy against us, and account us worthy of Thy Kingdom, O Lord!

Martyrs:

Invincible Martyrs of Christ: having conquered deceit by the power of the Cross, and received the grace of eternal life, ye feared not the threats of the tormentors, and were glad when bruised with tortures...[^325]

[f. 247vA] ...And now your blood hath become healings for our souls: intercede that our souls may be saved!

*Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion.*

*Podoben: "O Lord, though Thou didst stand before the tribunal" (Гдⷭ҇и, аще и на судїщи):*

Beholding Thee nailed unto the Cross, O Lord, she that bare Thee, the pure one, in sorrow and weeping cried aloud: My Child, why dost Thou suffer these things in the flesh? Thou hastest to make me bereft of honor; make haste to be glorified, that I may be magnified by Thy Passion!

ON WEDNESDAY,

The Beatitudes. Tone 8.

Remember us, O Christ, Savior of the world, as Thou didst remember the thief upon the Tree: and account us all worthy of Thy heavenly Kingdom, O Thou Who alone art compassionate!

Prefiguring the Cross with his rod, Moses divided the deep, leading through the people of Israel; but we, picturing this, conquer noetic enemies!

[f. 247vB] Of old Jacob, blessing the children, the sons of his sons: stretching out his hands crosswise, prefigured Thy Cross, O Christ Savior, whereby we all were freed from the curse!

Martyrs:

Emulating the Sufferings of Christ, O passion-bearers, ye manfully bore bitter torments: and crowned with incorruptible crowns, ye dwell in the heavens!

Glory...

O Christ, Who art one in the Trinity: cause me to observe Thy laws, and snatch me from the lawful bondage of the wicked one by the power of the almighty Cross!

Both now... Stavrotheotokion:

From thy virginal womb, O pure one, the Creator of the sun and of day shone forth: beholding Whom suspended upon the Tree, all creation was shaken!

## WEDNESDAY EVENING VESPERS (FOR THURSDAY) (TONE 8)

ON WEDNESDAY EVENING, AT "LORD, I HAVE CRIED":

*Stichera of the Holy Apostles, Tone 8.*

*Podoben: "O Lord, though Thou didst stand before the tribunal" (Гдⷭ҇и, аще и на судїщи):*

O Lord, with the rays of the Comforter Thou didst enlighten Thine Apostles, and set them as luminaries, the establishment of the faith, through the noetic illumination of Thy knowledge, O Master: therefore we venerate Thine ineffable love for mankind!

O Lord, by the prayers of the Apostles protect this Thy flock, preserving it unharmed from the assaults of enemies: since Thou didst redeem it with Thy precious blood from the bondage of the stranger, as Thou art compassionate and the Lover of mankind!

Ye appeared together in the foundation of the Church like precious stones, shining upon the universe with bright radiance, the certain knowledge of God, O divine Apostles: intercessors before the Trinity, and pray-ers for our souls!

[f. 248rA] Other Stichera to Saint Nicholas:

Tone the same.

O Lord, Thou didst glorify Thy holy hierarch Nicholas in the ends of the earth, giving unto him the grace of miracles, and showing him forth as a champion unto them that are in cruel perils, and who fall under the affliction of sorrows, and who ever ask of him protection!

O Lord, through the divine supplications of Thy hierarch, have mercy: and deliver Thy servants from every distress, and from all harm, and from the assault of enemies, who in faith venerate Thine invincible dominion!

Having thee as an advocate and fervent protector before the Sovereign Lady, O Nicholas: we flee unto thee in faith, and cry aloud: Turn us not away, unprofitable ones, from thy protection, but show thy mercy stretched out over thy servants!

Glory... Both now... Theotokion:

Behold the groaning of my contrite heart, O Bride of God; accept, O Virgin Mary, the lifting up of the hands of me, thy servant, as thou art the lover of mankind, and cast me not off, O all-immaculate one: that I may sing praise and magnify thee, who didst magnify our race!

At the Aposticha, Stichera:

Of the Holy Apostles. Tone 8.

O Lord, Thine Apostles, truly loving Thee upon the earth, counted all things as refuse that they might gain Thee alone: and for Thy sake they surrendered their bodies unto wounds: therefore, being glorified, they pray for our souls!

[f. 248rB] O Lord, Thou didst magnify the memory of the Apostles upon the earth: assembled together on this day, we glorify Thee, for through them Thou grantest healings unto us, and peace unto all the world by their prayers, and great mercy!

Martyrs:

If there be any virtue, and if there be any praise, it is meet for the Saints: for having bowed their necks unto the sword for Thy sake Who didst bow down the heavens and descend, they shed their blood for Thy sake Who didst empty Thyself and take the form of a servant; they humbled themselves even unto death, emulating Thy poverty: through the multitude of whose tender mercies, O God, have mercy upon us!

Glory... Both now... Theotokion:

I, O holy Virgin Theotokos, flee under thy protection: I know that through thee I shall find salvation, for thou art able, O pure one, to help me!

ON THURSDAY, AT MATINS,

After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymns:

*Of the Apostles, Tone 8.*

*Podoben: "Guiding unto wisdom" (Премꙋдрости напꙋтл):*

Luminaries unto the world and guides of our salvation: let us sing praise unto the divine Disciples of our God from the beginning; for they shone forth like light unto us that were in darkness, and proclaimed the Sun of glory unto all. Therefore they also cast down idolatrous deceit, having trumpeted forth the proclamation of the one Godhead: therefore we pray unto you, O Apostles: intercede with Christ God to grant forgiveness of transgressions unto us, and great mercy!

Into all the ends of the earth went forth your all-wise utterance: for truly, O all-praised Apostles of the Lord...[^326]

[f. 248vA] ...ye proclaimed the knowledge of God openly unto the world, and converted gentile ignorance into understanding: whence, having driven away idolatrous mist, the light of understanding shone forth unto them that were in darkness: therefore we pray: Intercede with Christ God to grant forgiveness of transgressions unto them that celebrate your holy memory with love!

Glory... Both now... Theotokion:

Having fallen into manifold temptations from enemies visible and invisible, and held fast by the tempest of mine innumerable sins, O all-pure one: I flee unto thy grace as unto fervent protection, and rampart, and my haven. Therefore, O all-pure one, pray thou unto Him Who was incarnate of thee without seed on behalf of all thy servants who unceasingly sing praise unto thee, O immaculate Theotokos: entreating Him earnestly to grant forgiveness of transgressions unto them that venerate thy birthgiving in faith!

After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns:

Of the Apostles, Tone 8.

Into all the earth, as the Prophet said, went forth the utterance of the all-wise Apostles: for having proclaimed the Word, they enlightened all nations. Therefore, worthily praising them, let us honor them with songs, for they ever intercede with Christ that our souls may be saved!

Martyrs:

Having put to death the fiery looks and motions of the passions through abstinence, the Martyrs of Christ received grace to drive away illnesses from the sick...

[f. 248vB] ...and while living in rest to work wonders in truth, a most glorious miracle: that bare bones pour forth healings! Glory to the one all-wise Creator God!

Glory... Both now... Theotokion:

O receptacle of the faithful, Birth-giver of God, joy of the sorrowing, and great consolation of the weeping: pray thou unceasingly together with the holy Apostles unto Him Who was born beyond nature from thy womb, O all-holy Virgin, to deliver us from every testing and cruel condemnation!

After the 3rd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns:

*To the Apostles, Tone 8.*

*Podoben: "That which was commanded mystically" (Повеленное таинственно):*

Ye appeared as radiant luminaries, eyewitnesses of Christ: ever enlightening all the earth, and driving away the darkness of polytheism with the light of the teachings of piety. Therefore, enlighten me who am in the darkness of passions, walking without fear, by your holy prayers, O God-bearing Apostles!

Catching men endowed with reason alive in the net of divine words like fish: ye brought them as firstfruits unto our God; and having loved the wounds of Christ, ye desired them, and were shown forth as imitators of His Sufferings. Therefore, having come together, we worthily honor your celebration today, O glorious Apostles, and with one accord cry aloud: Intercede with Christ God that forgiveness of transgressions may be granted unto them that celebrate your holy memory with love!

Glory... Both now... Theotokion:

O Theotokos, pray thou together with the Apostles...

[f. 249rA] ...unto the incomprehensible Son and Word of God, Who was ineffably born of thee incorruptibly beyond understanding, to grant true peace unto the universe, and to bestow upon us forgiveness of transgressions before the end, and to account thy servants worthy of the heavenly Kingdom for the sake of His extreme goodness!

CANON TO THE HOLY APOSTLES.

Ode 1. Tone 8. Heirmos:

Passing through water as on dry land:

Troparia:

The light-bearing choir of the Apostles, standing before the great Light: illuminate my darkened heart, and direct me unto saving paths!

Close friends of the Deliverer: deliver me from friendship with passions, who am overcome by many deceptions of life, and covered by the night of ignorance!

Heal the weapon-wounded of the wicked one, being the arrows of the Mighty One, O divine Apostles: unto them that flee under your protection in faith!

Theotokion:

He that is full empties Himself in godlike manner, and issues from thy womb bearing flesh, O pure Mother: saving by His compassion them that were deceived by the malice of the serpent!

Another Canon to Saint Nicholas.

Composition of Joseph.

Ode 1. Tone 8. Heirmos:

Unto Him Who cleft the unhewn sea:

O sacred and supreme among saints, standing all-blessed before the throne and God: save us who upon earth continually invoke thee, Nicholas, from every cruel affliction: asking forgiveness of our transgressions!

[f. 249rB] Enriched with thee as an advocate, O Nicholas, in day and night we cry unto thee in faith: now incline unto us who are sorely troubled by demonic evil plots and corrupt men, that having obtained refreshment, we may praise thee!

With the strongest sinews of thy prayers, O Nicholas, having delivered unto utter destruction them that strive to strangle us: deliver us from their cruel plot, who cry aloud in praise: Let us sing unto the Lord, for He is gloriously glorified!

Theotokion:

Beyond the laws of nature thou didst bear God the Lawgiver, Who became man: entreat Him as good, O all-immaculate one, to overlook our iniquities, who ever cry aloud: Let us sing unto the Lord, for He is gloriously glorified!

Ode 3. Heirmos:

Thou art the establishment of them that flee unto Thee, O Lord, Thou art the Light of the darkened: and my spirit chants praise unto Thee!

Troparia:

Gird my fainting heart with power, O Apostles of the Savior, and by your noetic thoughts, O brightest divine radiance: destroy the darkness of polytheism!

Heal the cruelest woundings of my heart, as physicians with divine motion of the hands, O Disciples of our God!

Theotokion:

O pure Sovereign Lady, haven of salvation: who beyond nature didst bear the Creator of all, both Master, and Savior, and Lord!

Another Heirmos the same.[^327]

[f. 249vA] (Canon to Saint Nicholas)

That we may honor thee and sing praise unto thee, O holy one: grant us a hand of help, O hierarch Nicholas!

Put to sleep, O Nicholas, by thine unsleeping prayers, the affliction that rises up against us, we pray thee!

Heal me who am wholly surrounded by passions and by the temptations of wicked men, by thine intercession, O Saint Nicholas!

Theotokion:

Pray thou, O pure one, unto the Deliverer to grant me forgiveness of sins and deliverance from the cruel distresses of life!

Ode 4. Heirmos:

I heard, O Lord, the report of Thy dispensation:

Troparia:

Ye were adorned, O glorious Apostles, being beautified with divine splendors, and enlightened with rays by Him Who showed you forth as luminaries unto the world!

Deliver me from a great storm, O helmsmen of all, divine Apostles: who am in peril in the abyss, and troubled by the temptations of life!

O horses chosen of God, who troubled the sea of polytheism: drown the abyss of my transgressions by your prayers!

Theotokion:

Equally effective with the Father, O Virgin, thou didst embody the Word from thy womb: therefore thou wast revealed as higher than all creatures, O Sovereign Lady!

Another Heirmos the same:

(Canon to Saint Nicholas)

From the multitude of my transgressions I have fallen into a multitude of innumerable sorrows: show thyself, O Saint Nicholas, as helper and benefactor!

I weep for myself who am lost, living in slothfulness...

[f. 249vB] ...by thy prayers, O Nicholas, lead me unto repentance!

O Nicholas who didst deliver the three youths from being surrendered unto death: deliver me from every constriction and from eternal condemnation!

Theotokion:

Strengthen me, O all-pure one, who am devoid of spiritual understanding: directing the movements of my soul unto life-bearing entrances!

Ode 5. Heirmos:

Rising early in the morning we cry unto Thee, O Lord, save us: for Thou art our God, and beside Thee we know no other!

Troparia:

Being straitened by many transgressions: direct us unto saving expanse, as helmsmen, O Apostles!

O eyewitnesses of God in the Spirit: deliver me who am caught in the snare of dishonorable deeds, we pray you!

Having emulated the holy Sufferings of the Savior: drive away all voluptuousness from my soul, O Apostles!

Theotokion:

Heal my sick soul, O all-pure Sovereign Lady: who didst bear Him Who bears away the diseases of all!

Another Heirmos the same:

(Canon to Saint Nicholas)

Strengthen us by thy prayers, O divinely blessed Nicholas, to keep the commandments of Christ, our only God!

Having lived in Myra, O Nicholas: fill us with divine fragrance, who piously sing praise unto thee!

Have compassion upon us through thy prayers, O hierarch: entreat God, the all-compassionate, O Nicholas!

Theotokion:

Being full of life-bearing waters, O Maiden...

[f. 250rA] ...give drink unto all of us that piously and wisely sing praise unto thee!

Ode 6. Heirmos:

I pour out my prayer unto the Lord, and unto Him will I declare my sorrows: for my soul is filled with evils, and my life hath drawn near unto hades; but like Jonah I pray: Lead me up from corruption, O my God!

Troparia:

By the invocation of prayers ye cast down the temples of idols, O Disciples of Christ: but I pray in faith: crush the idols of my mind, and show me forth as a temple of God, who am guilty of many sins!

Built upon the rock of discernment, as chosen stones, O eyewitnesses of God: save my heart built upon the moist sand, for the rivers of temptations rush together and cruelly batter me!

Deliver me from the deceitful friendship of the flesh, O friends of the Word, and bring me who have become hateful through much malice unto the love of the Beloved, through the forgiveness of sins for the sake of His great mercy!

Theotokion:

As a rose, as a chosen lily, as a sweet-smelling fragrance from the damp valleys of the world: the Creator, having chosen thee, O Maiden, dwelt in thy womb, and being born, filled all things with fragrance!

Another Heirmos the same:

(Canon to Saint Nicholas)

Thy heart was revealed as a Paradise, O Nicholas, having the Tree of life in its midst, Christ the Deliverer: Whom entreat unceasingly...

[f. 250rB] ...to make citizens of Paradise all of us that have acquired thee as a fervent protector!

In slothfulness I pass my life, and unceasingly I sin, wretched one: and I behold that ineffable judgment there, and I am seized with fear: have compassion upon me, O God, by the prayers of Nicholas, as Thou art compassionate!

Against the storm of manifold temptations that suddenly comes upon me for the multitude of my sins, I cry: Leave me not, O blessed one, without protection; but stretch forth unto me a hand of merciful help, and save me!

Theotokion:

Palace of the high King, and fiery throne wast thou, O Virgin, higher than the Cherubim and Seraphim beyond understanding: therefore let every breath glorify thee as the Mother of the Creator!

Ode 7. Heirmos:

The Hebrew Children in the furnace boldly trampled upon the flame, and turned the fire into dew, crying aloud: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers!

Troparia:

The night of slothfulness holds me fast, and the darkness of sin covers me: O all-wise Apostles who were revealed as the light of the world, hasten to enlighten my darkened heart!

Revealed as another heaven, declaring the glory of our God: deliver from the misery of passions, O divine heralds, them that flee in faith under your mighty protection!

Revealed as fiery coals, O Apostles: kindled by the fire of the Comforter...[^328]

[f. 250vA] ...burn up every substance of our malice, and deliver us from unquenchable fire unto ages!

Theotokion:

Thou wast revealed as an overshadowing mountain unhewn, from which the Cornerstone was cut: therefore grant compunction, O Sovereign Lady, unto my soul darkened and petrified by bitter pleasures!

Another Heirmos the same:

(Canon to Saint Nicholas)

Thou didst pour forth streams of teachings, and driedst up the torrents of heresy, sweetly watering the souls of the faithful, O sacred minister Nicholas: therefore we honor thee!

Thou wast strengthened by the power of the Trinity, prevailing to destroy the sluggish idols: therefore, by thy faithful prayer, drive away the passionate idols of my mind!

Having become the first-enthroned hierarch of the people of Myra, O venerable one: after death thou pourest forth divine myrrh, driving away our foul-smelling illnesses, O all-blessed Nicholas, from them that approach thee in faith!

Theotokion:

Thou didst stay the mortal assault, having borne the immortal God: Whom pray, O pure one, to put to death the passions of my humble body, and to account me worthy of life!

Ode 8. Heirmos:

Sevenfold the furnace:

Troparia:

Strengthen my soul that is shaken by passions, O ye who are the indestructible foundations of the Church and immovable pillars, the ramparts of the faithful, fishers of them that are in the deep of perdition, pleasant havens unto them that sing in faith...

[f. 250vB] ...Children, bless; priests, sing praise; people, supremely exalt Him unto ages!

Unto me lying in the pit of dark despair, and fallen into the nether pit of passions: raise me up by your prayers, have compassion, O Disciples of the Savior, who were enriched with the Teacher's compassion, as ye were accounted worthy, O God-beholding Apostles, unto ages of ages!

Theotokion:

Bright in the beauties of virtues didst thou appear, O all-pure one: having contained in thy womb the fair-visaged beauty of the Creator of all: Whom earnestly entreat, O pure one, to enlighten my soul, held fast by the growth of sins and estranged from ancient beauty, exceedingly beautiful, unto ages of ages!

Another Heirmos: The God-proclaiming Children:

(Canon to Saint Nicholas)

Being an illuminator, O divinely wise hierarch, with the light-bearing rays of the sunlike Godhead: destroy the darkness of my passions, O Nicholas, by thy prayers!

O sacred initiate Nicholas, who by an awesome appearance didst deliver the generals from death: deliver us from great deadly harm!

Strengthen us by thy prayers, O all-blessed Nicholas, who are shaken by demonic temptations and by abusive men: and keep us unharmed!

Theotokion:

Offer supplication unto the Lord, O most holy Virgin, helper of mankind: to have compassion and to save them that flee unto thee!

[f. 251rA] Ode 9. Heirmos:

Amazed was the heaven at this, and the ends of the earth were struck with awe, that God appeared unto men in the flesh, and thy womb became more spacious than the heavens: therefore the ranks of Angels and men magnify thee, O Theotokos!

Troparia:

Having crushed the jaws of soul-destroying deceit by divine power, O Apostles: ye were set as princes upon the earth by Christ, spiritually correcting with psalms in piety: therefore subdue the disorderly audacities of my heart unto the divine law!

Having proclaimed in the world the Word of God, Who appeared more beautiful than all the sons of men: your feet were adorned, as ye preached the Gospel of peace and life unto all: therefore by your prayers put to death my soul which is languishing with passions!

Having put to death your limbs upon the earth, ye were clothed with great life, having depicted the Passions through passions: therefore quicken me who was slain by the arrow of the malice of the wicked one, through the remedies of true repentance, O divinely blessed Apostles!

Theotokion:

Heal my soul that is sick with cruel passion, O thou who didst bear the most good God, as thou art merciful: and deliver me ever, O all-pure one, from the enemies that destroy me and attack me: that being saved, I may earnestly magnify thee, who didst magnify our race!

Another Heirmos: Truly the Birth-giver of God:

(Canon to Saint Nicholas)

As the deliverer of them that pray unto thee in faith: deliver me from all malice of visible and invisible enemies, O all-blessed Nicholas...

[f. 251rB] ...all-blessed Nicholas!

Dwelling now with the heavenly choirs, O most sacred father Nicholas: by a nod of the Good One, intercede that we may obtain mercy!

The judgment is at the doors, take heed, O my soul! And cry aloud unto the Judge and God: By the prayers of Nicholas, spare me, O Lord!

Theotokion:

O receptacle of the Light: enlighten my soul, O Virgin, which hath been darkened by passions: that in faith and love I may ever glorify thee!

At the Aposticha, Stichera:

Of the Apostles, Tone 8.

O Lord, Thine Apostles, truly loving Thee upon the earth, counted all things as refuse that they might gain Thee alone: and for Thy sake they surrendered their bodies unto wounds: therefore, being glorified, they pray for our souls!

O Lord, Thou didst magnify the memory of the Apostles upon the earth: assembled together on this day, we glorify Thee, for through them Thou grantest healings unto us, and peace unto all the world by their prayers, and great mercy!

Martyrs:

Clothed well in the faith of faith, and armed with the weapon of the Cross: ye appeared as valiant soldiers, manfully opposing the tormentors, and casting down the deceit of the devil; having become victors, ye were accounted worthy of crowns: pray unceasingly on our behalf, that our souls may be saved!

Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion:

Snatch me, O Sovereign Lady, from the hands of the serpent...[^329]

[f. 251vA] ...of the manslayer, who desires craftily to swallow me up utterly: crush his jaws, I pray thee, and destroy his snares: that, delivered from his claws, I may magnify thy protection!

On Thursday, at the Divine Liturgy.

The Beatitudes. Tone 8.

Remember us, O Christ, Savior of the world, even as Thou didst remember the thief upon the Tree: and account all worthy, O Thou Who alone art compassionate, of Thy heavenly Kingdom!

Revealing yourselves as the trumpets of Christ, O Apostles: ye raised up them that were lying in the graves of wicked belief, and made them partakers of divine life!

Sowing the secret seed of the Word of God, O eloquent ones: ye made the barren hearts of all the nations fruitful with divine understanding...

[f. 251vB] ...with divine understanding: therefore ye are worthily blessed!

Martyrs:

Stripping away great malice from themselves, the champions passed manfully through the midst of cruel trials, and were clothed from heaven with a robe of radiance!

Glory... Triadikon:

Put to death the uprising of passions, O honored, all-holy Trinity, by the prayers of Thy divine Apostles: that, being saved, we may glorify Thee!

Both now... Stavrotheotokion:

Rejoice, O all-immaculate Virgin, who didst heal the curse of divine sorrow, and them that proclaimed the curse unto Adam, O all-pure Theotokos: through whom we have been delivered from corruption!

## THURSDAY EVENING VESPERS (FOR FRIDAY) (TONE 8)

On Thursday Evening, at "Lord, I have cried":

*Stichera of the Precious Cross. Tone 8.*

*Podoben: "O most marvelous wonder" (О преславное чудо):*

O most glorious wonder! The life-bearing tree, the all-honored Cross, is shown today lifted up on high! All the ends of the earth glorify it, and all the demons are driven away! O what a divine gift hath been bestowed upon earthly men, through which, O Christ, save our souls, as Thou art alone compassionate!

O most glorious wonder! As a cluster of divine life, borne from on high, taken up from the earth: the Cross is exalted today...

[f. 252rA] ...whereby we have all been drawn unto God, and death hath been swallowed up utterly! O all-honored Tree, whereby we have taken delight in the immortal food in Eden, glorifying Christ!

Many are Thy bounties toward us, O good Jesus! How Thou didst humble Thyself, and became man, and didst will to suffer the Cross and shameful death, held fast for the sake of unprofitable servants! What worthy gift, meet for God, shall we offer unto Thee? Only glorifying Thee, we the faithful give thanks!

Other Stichera to the Most Holy Theotokos. Tone 8.

O the ineffable goodness of Him Who was incarnate of thee, O all-hymned Theotokos! For as the Lover of mankind He endured the Cross and death, that He might save the world which He created. Entreat Him to deliver me, wretched one, from painful torment, and to settle me where the unwaning Light shines!

What is this visible sight which is seen by mine eyes, O Master, Who upholdest all creation? Lifted up upon the Tree, and dying, Thou givest life unto all! The Theotokos, weeping, cried aloud when she beheld the King and God, Who shone forth ineffably from her, lifted up upon the Cross!

Deliver from tribulations, O all-pure one, by thy precious prayers, the flock which Thy Son and God acquired and sprinkled with His Blood: driving away visible and invisible enemies like wild beasts, and fill their faces with dishonor, even as David the singer proclaimed of old, O pure one!

Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion:

Beholding Thee nailed upon the Cross, O Jesus, and willingly accepting sufferings, the Virgin and Thy Mother, weeping, cried aloud: Woe is me, my sweet Child! How dost Thou suffer wounds unjustly, O Physician Who didst heal human infirmity and didst deliver all from corruption by Thy tender mercy?

[f. 252rB] At the Aposticha, Stichera of the Precious Cross. Tone 8.

Lifted up upon the Cross, O Christ God, Thou didst save the human race: we glorify Thy sufferings!

Nailed upon the Cross, O Christ God, Thou didst open the gates of Paradise: we glorify Thee, our Deliverer!

Martyrs:

O Martyrs of the Lord, ye sanctify every place and heal every infirmity: and now pray ye that our souls may be delivered from the snare of the enemy, we pray you!

Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion:

The unblemished Heifer, beholding the Bullock willingly lifted up upon the Tree, weeping bitterly, cried aloud: Woe is me, longed-for Child! What hath the ungrateful Jewish council rendered unto Thee, desiring to make me childless of Thee, O Beloved?

On Friday, at Matins.

After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymns of the Precious Cross. Tone 8.

Beholding the Author of life hanging upon the Cross, the thief said: If He Who is crucified with us were not God incarnate, the sun would not have quenched its rays, nor would the quaking earth have trembled! But Thou Who endurest all things, remember me, O Lord, when Thou comest into Thy Kingdom!

In the midst of two thieves Thy Cross was found as a righteous balance: unto the one, bringing him down into hades by the weight of blasphemy; but unto the other, lightened of sins, unto the knowledge of theology: O Christ God, glory to Thee!

Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion:

Preserved unceasingly by the Cross of Thy Son and God, O Virgin: the demonic snares...[^330]

[f. 252vA] ...and assaults we repel, singing praise unto thee who art truly the Theotokos: and with love all generations bless thee, O all-pure one, even as thou didst foretell. Therefore grant us the forgiveness of transgressions by thy prayers!

After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns of the Precious Cross. Tone 8.

In the midst of Eden, the tree blossomed forth death: but in the midst of all the earth, the Tree grew forth life! For having tasted of the first fruit, being incorruptible, we became corruptible; but having partaken of the second, we have enjoyed incorruption. For by the Cross Thou hast saved the human race, as Thou art God!

The tree in Paradise stripped me bare of old, the enemy bringing in death through tasting: but the Tree of the Cross, bearing the garment of eternal life for men, was planted upon the earth, and all the world was filled with all joy! Beholding it exalted, let us the people cry aloud in faith unto God with one accord: Fill Thy house with glory!

Martyrs:

Today this temple is enlightened with heavenly light: for the angelic hosts rejoice in God, and with them the choirs of Martyrs make merry at the memory of the passion-bearers. At their supplications, send down now, O Christ, peace unto Thy world, and great mercy!

Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion:

Beholding Him Who was incarnate of thy precious blood, and Who beyond understanding was born of thee, O pure one, hanging upon the Tree in the midst of evildoers, suffering in thy womb, and weeping like a mother, thou didst cry aloud...

[f. 252vB] ...Woe is me, my Child! What is this divine and ineffable dispensation of Thine, whereby Thou hast quickened Thine own creation? I hymn Thy tender mercy!

*After the 3rd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns of the Precious Cross. Tone 8.*

*Podoben: "That which was commanded mystically" (Повелѣнное таинственно):*

By Thy Cross, O Christ Savior, and by Thy death, the tyranny of the enemy was cast down, and death was put to death; and the dead whom hades held fast from the ages were suddenly loosed as captives, praising Thy dominion, and Thy dread and divine descent, O Good One, whereby Thou hast saved all!

Hoping for false deification, the forefather became the author of corruption for all: but Thou, by Thy Cross, hast granted unending life as Thou art most good: for Thou wast willingly nailed, that Thou mightest loose us from the first condemnation. Therefore we hymn Thy voluntary Passion, O Christ!

Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion:

The unblemished Ewe-lamb, beholding the Lamb and Shepherd hanging upon the Cross, cried aloud: My Child, what strange and unexpected sight is this? How is Life condemned unto death, like unto earthly men? But rise again on the third day from the dead, as Thou didst say: that rejoicing, I may glorify Thee!

Canon to the Precious and Life-creating Cross of the Lord.

A work of Joseph.

Ode 1. Tone 8. Heirmos:

Moses, having traced the Cross [f. 253rA] cut the Red Sea upright with his rod for Israel that went on foot; and turning it back, he struck and united it over Pharaoh and his chariots, writing crosswise the invincible weapon: therefore let us sing unto Christ our God, for He hath been glorified!

Stretching forth Thy divine palms upon the Cross, O Jesus: Thou didst gather unto Thyself the creation of Thy hands, and didst deliver it forever from the hand of the deceiver, and didst subdue it with Thy mighty hand unto the Church of all: therefore, we the faithful sing praise unto Thy majesty, for Thou hast been glorified!

Slaying in Eden was the bitter tasting of the tree, bringing in death; but Christ, being put to death upon the Tree, poured forth life unto all, and put the serpent to sleep by divine power: therefore let us sing unto Him, our God, for He hath been glorified!

Martyrs:

The multitude of Martyrs stood manfully, O Jesus: and by Thy Cross and Passion they rose up against passions, and confessed Thee as King and good Master before enemies: and they endured boundless torments and tribulations. Therefore they have attained the glory of all, the everlasting life!

Having found deliverance by the sprinkling of Thy precious and life-creating Blood, O Lord: Thy Martyrs poured forth their blood to the end, being unjustly tormented to offer sacrifices unto defiled demons: therefore they were offered unto Thee as precious sacrifices, O King of all!

Theotokion:

When the immaculate one beheld Thee, Who seest all things, nailed upon the Cross, weeping she said: What is this, my Child? What have they rendered unto Thee...

[f. 253rB] ...who enjoyed Thy many gifts? How hast Thou endured pains? Glory to Thy tender mercy and to Thy dread dispensation, O longsuffering One!

Another Canon to the Most Holy Theotokos.

Ode 1. Tone 8. Heirmos: Passing through water as on dry land:

Troparia:

With Thine enlightenment, O Mother of God: enlighten my soul, which is darkened by the pleasures of life and helplessly troubled by worldly sorrows!

The heavenly gates were opened by thy divine Childbearing, O Mother of God: whereinto grant my soul an entrance through prayer, and direct me unto them!

Heal my soul, O Virgin, with thy mercy: which hath been struck by the arrow of the wicked one, and wounded by his wiles and deceits!

O hope of the hopeless, correction of the fallen: who didst bear the divine Light: enlighten my soul which is in darkness!

Ode 3. Heirmos:

O Lord, Supreme Creator of the heavenly circle:

(Canon of the Cross Ode 3 Troparia):

The rod is received as an image of the mystery, for by foretokening it appointed the priest; and for the Church that formerly was barren, the Tree of the Cross hath now blossomed forth into dominion and establishment!

The sun was darkened in its course, beholding Thee unjustly lifted up upon the Tree: and the rocks were split, and all the earth was terrified with fear, O Thou Who alone art the Savior, the deliverance of all!

Moses, stretching forth his hands, prefigured the precious Cross: which we now, God-wisely depicting, overcome all the ranks of aliens...[^331]

[f. 253vA] ...and overcome all demonic workings, remaining unharmed from every hurt of theirs!

Martyrs:

Enduring sufferings, the passion-bearers depicted the Passion, partaking in manifold passions of Him Who willingly suffered and granted life unto the world!

Having trodden the path of martyrdom without turning back, the glorious trophy-bearers cast down the stumbling-blocks of deceit from their hearts, and hastened with rejoicing unto divine rest!

Theotokion:

Beyond the lawful customs of men, I brought Thee forth, my Child; and how have the lawless lifted Thee up upon the Tree in the midst of the lawless, Who alone didst establish the law of life? the Theotokos, weeping, cried aloud!

Another Heirmos:

O Lord, Supreme Creator of the heavenly circle:

(Canon to the Theotokos Ode 3 Troparia):

Grant me unceasing groans, and fervent tears, and a contrite heart, O Virgin: that I may weep for what I have committed, and consume the passions that grow within me, O thou who alone art all-hymned!

Snatch my soul, O good one, which is weighed down by the slumbers of sin and hath slipped down unto the womb of hades: and grant me the thought of true repentance, O divinely blessed one!

Grant unto my soul, which is grievously deficient in understanding and virtues and hath sinned through transgressions, O all-immaculate one: to love silent contemplation and to possess divine desire, O all-immaculate one!

Placing my hope in thee, O Mother of God, may I quickly be delivered from despair: for I know, yea, I know the wealth of thy tender mercy...

[f. 253vB] ...and the saving strength of thy boldness!

Ode 4. Heirmos:

I heard, O Lord, the mystery of Thy dispensation, I understood Thy works, and I glorified Thy Divinity!

(Canon of the Cross Ode 4 Troparia):

Bearing piety like the cedar, faith like the cypress, and love like the pine: let us worship the divine Cross!

By Thy Cross, O Savior, Paradise was opened: and the condemned man entered therein again, magnifying Thy goodness!

Having become dead, O Savior, Thou didst quicken men who were slain, and didst put to death the serpent who brought in sin!

Martyrs:

Having become partakers of Christ's Sufferings, the divine Martyrs were also shown to be partakers of heavenly splendor!

Ye were adorned, O Martyrs, being united unto the fair Word: brightly enlightened, having loved the Sun of righteousness!

Theotokion:

Thou didst bear as a young babe Him Who was perfect before the ages, O all-immaculate Maiden, Who accomplishes marvelous deeds by the Cross and through goodness!

Another Heirmos: Thou art my strength, O Lord:

(Canon to the Theotokos Ode 4 Troparia):

O thou who didst ineffably bear God the Word: assuage the passions of my soul, pouring out the grief of cruel assaults with the precious Blood of thy Son, Who destroyed the soul-devouring womb of hades and poured forth resurrection unto the world!

[f. 254rA] O Bride of God, send down cleansing of transgressions unto my suffering soul, and drive away evil thoughts, and account it worthy to become most pure: for I have fled unto thy mediation and thy help, O Virgin Theotokos!

I flee now unto thy protection, O all-pure one: anticipate and deliver me, O all-honored one, from the cruel storm of the enemy and from the torrents of iniquity that trouble me; and direct me without turning aside unto thy haven and unto thy calm, O Mother of God!

The enemy hath wounded all my soul with the arrows of sin, and defiled my heart with pleasures, and turned me away from the right path: therefore I cry aloud unto thee: Having converted me, heal me and save me!

Ode 5. Heirmos:

O thrice-blessed Tree, whereon Christ the King and Lord was crucified, through which he who deceived by the tree fell, being caught by thee, when God was nailed in the flesh, Who grants peace unto our souls!

(Canon of the Cross Ode 5 Troparia):

Desiring to clothe us who were stripped bare of the garment of incorruption: Thou wast crucified upon the Cross, O Christ, and didst strip bare the wiles of the enemy: therefore we glorify Thy sufferings!

The saving Blood of incorruption from Thy side hath cleansed the world for Thee: the blood of idol-shrines hath ceased, and Thou hast renewed the incorruptible through intelligent fruit, and poured forth incorruption unto our souls!

Martyrs:

Having blossomed with the beauty of manifold wounds, O glorious Martyrs...

[f. 254rB] ...and marked with divine blood, they have passed now through the sword that formerly barred the way, and rejoice making merry in Paradise!

How wondrous art Thou in Thy saints, O Christ, who loved Thee in faith: for enriched by Thee, they pour forth rivers of divine healings unto the world, and dry up the outflow of our passions!

Theotokion:

Thou hast healed us who were sick with sin, O Virgin, having born the Savior and Physician of all: Who was nailed upon the Tree of the Cross, O all-pure one, and poured forth salvation unto our souls!

Another Heirmos: Therefore hast Thou cast me off:

(Canon to the Theotokos Ode 5 Troparia):

With deliberate zeal I hasten unto thy protection, O all-immaculate one, and I lift up the eye of my soul: turn not away from me, but protect me as thou art good, and heal me, and wash away the filth of my transgressions!

The deadly venom of the bites of sin was injected: but destroy it by the divine nails and spear of thy Child, Who suffered in the flesh for our sake through tender mercy, O thou who alone art all-hymned!

Quicken me who was slain in my manner of life and corrupted by transgressions, O thou who didst bear the eternal Life: and by spiritual renewal, transform me unto incorruption, O divinely blessed one!

Deliver me, O good one, from the corrupter of the Jewish nation and from evil expectations: and speedily heal the sickness of my soul and body, O thou who alone didst bear the Physician, Savior, and Lord of our great flesh and sins!

Ode 6...[^332]

[f. 254vA] Ode 6. Heirmos:

Jonah stretched forth his hands crosswise in the belly of the sea monster, clearly prefiguring the saving Passion; therefore also, coming forth on the third day, he depicted the transcendent Resurrection of Christ God, Who was nailed in the flesh and by His three-day Resurrection enlightened the world!

(Canon of the Cross Ode 6 Troparia):

The Cross was planted on the place of a skull, in the midst of the earth: and healed the wound that sprouted from the tree in the midst of Paradise! For Christ, counted as the only righteous One in the midst of lawless thieves, overturned everything, and cast down from the height him that had fallen into the nethermost abyss!

Bending the bow of Thy divine and all-honored Cross, O Christ: Thou didst release arrows against the fighting enemy, even the nails of Thy hands, penetrating into his darkened and sunless heart, O Master: and Thou didst utterly put him to death, and quicken those slain by him, O compassionate One!

Martyrs:

The streams of blood that flowed from the wounds of the bodies of the holy martyrs extinguished the flames of idolatry by the Spirit, and watered the honored furrows of the Church, making ears of grain to blossom forth in saving hope and faith, wherewith every soul is nourished by divine grace!

Kindling the fire of greater divine manifestation, the glorious passion-bearers repelled the judges of utmost deceit: when condemned by lineage to be burned with material fire, they were preserved unharmed by the operation and grace of the Holy Spirit, Who crowned them that suffered lawfully!

Theotokion:

A sword pierced thy heart, O all-pure Maiden, beholding thy Son stretched upon the Cross, enduring suffering, and willingly pierced in His divine side with a spear, slaying the warring serpent: therefore weeping like a mother, thou didst bless and magnify Him!

[f. 254vB] Another Heirmos: Cleanse me, O Savior:

(Canon to the Theotokos Ode 6 Troparia):

In passions and profligacy have I lived, and wretchedly have I been enslaved unto pleasures, and stripped bare of every divine virtue: but show compassion unto me, O all-pure one!

I have become a fugitive from the commandments given unto me, and have departed far from life, drawing near unto death: but guide me unto conversion, O all-pure Mother of God!

My life is profligate and full of negligence: but let thy many and ineffable mercies, O all-pure one, prevail, and let the tender mercy of thy goodness overcome the weakness of my mind!

Having born the Savior, Deliverer, and all-compassionate One: cleanse me, O pure one, and save and deliver me from the evils that have befallen me and unmercifully assault my infirmity!

Ode 7. Heirmos:

The senseless command of the wicked tyrant shook the people, breathing forth threats and blasphemy hateful to God [f. 255rA] yet the bestial fury and the consuming fire frightened not the three Children; but as a cool Spirit breathed against the fire, being in the furnace they sang: O God of our fathers, supremely praised and blessed art Thou!

(Canon of the Cross Ode 7 Troparia):

When Thou wast stretched upon the Tree of the Cross, O Word of the Father, as the Vine: Thou didst drop down mystic sweet wine, taking away the drunkenness of transgressions, and gladdening all that know Thee as God and Creator willingly suffering, and that sing of salvation: O God of our fathers, supremely praised and blessed art Thou!

Thou didst endure the shameful Crucifixion, O my Christ Jesus: taking away reproach and groaning from men! And Thou didst taste gall, destroying every bitter sorrow; Thou didst wound Thine own hands, healing our spiritual wounds, O compassionate One, and commanding us to sing: O God of our fathers, supremely praised and blessed art Thou!

Martyrs:

By painless suffering, the valiant sufferers acquired painless life! Therefore ye lighten our illnesses, having received great grace from on high, O holy ones, to heal passions, to drive away spirits, to protect the faithful, and to save them that sing: O God of our fathers, supremely praised and blessed art Thou!

Standing as pillars before the tribunal, preaching Christ Who took flesh for our sake, the Martyrs appeared as conformable unto His ultimate Passions: ye endured the burning of fire and all other torments, crying aloud in gladness...

[f. 255rB] ...crying aloud: O God of our fathers, supremely praised and blessed art Thou!

Theotokion:

Filled with sorrow, beholding Thee unjustly suffering, O Son, I am wounded in my soul: seeing Thee pierced in Thy side with a spear, the Theotokos cried aloud, weeping and lamenting, she who alone is good: whom we all worthily bless, crying aloud in piety: O God of our fathers, supremely praised and blessed art Thou!

Another Heirmos: The Hebrew Children:

(Canon to the Theotokos Ode 7 Troparia):

Thou art all light-bearing, O Virgin, having received the unwaning Light, and thou dost enlighten, O pure one, them that cry aloud unto thee in faith: Blessed art thou, O all-pure one, and blessed is the Fruit of thy womb!

Show forth thy love for mankind and thy mercy, O Virgin: raise me up, delivered from evils, who cry aloud: Blessed art thou, O all-pure one, and blessed is the Fruit of thy womb!

Unto thee, O Mother and Virgin, do I flee, being wounded by hidden arrows of the soul: protect me with all thy mercy, as I cry aloud: Blessed art thou, O all-pure one, and blessed is the Fruit of thy womb!

Deliver me, O Mother of the Savior, from the cruel captivity of wicked thoughts and sinful causes that holds me fast: that, being ever saved, I may glorify thee as is meet!

Ode 8. Heirmos:

Bless, ye Children, equal in number to the Trinity: sing praise unto God the Father and Creator, and unto the Word Who came down and turned the fire into dew; and supremely exalt unto all ages the all-holy Spirit, Who gives life unto all!

(Canon of the Cross Ode 8 Troparia):

Blessed is the Tree, whereby all the curse was destroyed that sprouted in Eden...[^333]

[f. 255vA] ...the cruel curse that grew from the branch of the evil tree: and Christ, the supremely glorified, is lifted up, Who hath cleansed us, having willed it of His own accord through tender mercy!

Sacredly crossing his hands, the ever-glorious patriarch blessed his grandsons of old, revealing the image of the sacred Tree: whereby blessing was granted unto all who were cursed through the evil eating of the tree and had slipped down into the depth of evils!

All mankind is righted, O Master, when Thou wast stretched upon the Cross; and the host of wicked demons falls, and being scattered, receives destruction; and the dominion of Thy power and Thy strength is exalted unto ages!

Martyrs:

Blessed glory, and incorruptible food, and light-bearing dwellings have ye inherited now, O divine martyrs of the Lord: and ye have been joined with heavenly ranks, and in gladness have received now the fulfillment of your blessed hopes!

With courage surpassing the sun, the light-bearing martyrs of Christ shone forth, and by divine power ground to powder all the deceit of the devil, and God-wisely enlightened the hearts of all in all ends of the earth unto ages!

Theotokion:

Spiritual cloud and sacred shadow, throne of God, and gate of light, candlestick and dawn of the Word, all we the faithful call thee, O all-pure Virgin: being the Mother of Him Who made all things, O blessed one!

Another Heirmos: Sevenfold the furnace:

(Canon to the Theotokos Ode 8 Troparia):

The Almighty Lord, the all-powerful, dwelling in thy womb, O Virgin: showed thee forth as a pillar of establishment unto the faithful: fleeing unto whom, we are delivered from misfortunes and perils...

[f. 255vB] ...and are freed from temptations, singing with one accord: Ye priests, sing praise; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto ages!

Having fallen away from sacred life, O Sovereign Lady, I am dragged without restraint toward sin and enslaved unto it, and I am stripped bare of the freedom that is in Christ and of true righteousness: but despise me not, O treasury of salvation, who flee unto thee naked and afflicted!

Let the petition of my prayer be righted unto the Lord, O Virgin, Who came forth from thy womb: and may He deliver me from the transgression of commandments, and from condemnation and the legal curse; and may He wash away the filth of my grievous sins, as He alone is merciful!

O all-pure Birth-giver of God: cleanse the wounds of my soul and sinful stumbling-blocks, washing them with the fountain that flowed from the side of thy Son, and with the arrows of comfort that come from Him: for unto thee do I call, and unto thee do I flee, and thee do I invoke, O full of divine grace!

Ode 9. Heirmos:

Death, which came upon our race through the eating from the tree, hath been abolished today by the Cross; for the curse of our foremother and of our race hath been loosed by the blossoming of the pure Mother of God, whom all the heavenly Powers magnify!

(Canon of the Cross Ode 9 Troparia):

Exalting Thee most sacredly, O compassionate One, we worship Thy Cross...

[f. 256rA] ...we worship Thy Cross, and the Spear, and the Sponge, and the Reed, and the holy nails driven into Thy hands and feet, O Master: whereby we have found perfect forgiveness and have been accounted worthy of dwelling in Paradise!

O how the most righteous One, the only King of all, was condemned unjustly to be nailed and crucified upon the Tree, to justify all who with faith glorify Thy voluntary sufferings and dispensation, and who faithfully magnify Thee, O my Christ!

Martyrs:

Having surrendered their bodies unto torments with their whole soul, the glorious Martyrs endured wounds and violent death, the severing of limbs, and tearing, and burning with fire, being kindled with love toward God: therefore, crowned with victors' wreaths, they dwell in the heavens!

O sweetness of the Apostles and the Martyrs: by their prayers fill us all with mercy, as Thou art tenderhearted, granting the remission of sins, and deliverance from all evils, and the joy of Thy Kingdom, O Christ God, Who for our sake didst appear as man!

Theotokion:

A light-bearing bridal chamber wast thou shown to be, O Virgin, of Him Who dwelt in thy virginal womb, and willingly endured the divine Passion, and granted dispassion unto all through ineffable mercy: Whom worshipping, with gracious voice we magnify thee!

Another Heirmos: Amazed was the heaven at this:

(Canon to the Theotokos Ode 9 Troparia):

O true Mother of God of the true God: cease not to entreat Him...

[f. 256rB] ...Whom thou didst bear, to grant forgiveness of sins unto thy servants, and complete pardon of the evils committed by me, and to account me worthy in due time of eternal enjoyment!

Gird my humble soul with spiritual strength and power, with weapon and dominion, O most holy Theotokos: and clothe it with the armor of the Cross; and cleanse the wounds of my sin with the dew of thy love for mankind and with thy great mercy!

Be thou a pillar of salvation unto me, O pure one, chasing away the invisible ranks of demons, cutting off the multitude of temptations and tribulations, driving far off the assaults of passions, and granting pure liberation!

O pure and glorified Mother of God: save them that sing praise unto thee in love, and mercifully destroy the tempest of temptations: for having born God, thou canst do whatsoever thou desirest, and dost grant it without hindrance, O Virgin: therefore we all magnify thee!

At the Aposticha, Stichera of the Precious Cross. Tone 8.

The rod of Moses prefigured Thy precious Cross, O our Savior, whereby Thou didst lead Thy people unto salvation, as from the depths of the sea, O Lover of mankind!

The tree that grew in the midst of the garden in Eden of old was for food; but the Church, O Christ, hath blossomed forth Thy Cross, pouring forth life unto all the world: but that one brought death unto Adam who ate of the food, whereas this one quickens through faith...[^334]

[f. 256vA] ...and saved the thief through faith: show us forth as partakers of his salvation, O Christ God, Who by Thy Passion didst loose the snares of the enemy that were set against us: and account us worthy of Thy Kingdom, O Lord!

Martyrs:

What shall we call you, O holy ones? Cherubim? For Christ rests upon you! Seraphim? For unceasingly ye glorify Him! Angels? For ye turned away from the body! Powers? For ye work miracles! Many are your names, and yet greater are your gifts! Pray ye that our souls may be saved!

Glory... Both now... Stavrotheotokion:

I cannot endure, my Child, beholding Thee fallen asleep upon the Tree, Who bestowest wakefulness unto all: that Thou mayest bestow divine and saving wakefulness unto them that of old fell asleep in the fatal sleep through the fruit of transgression! the Virgin said, weeping: whom we magnify!

On Friday, the Beatitudes. Tone 8.

Remember us, O Christ, Savior of the world, even as Thou didst remember the thief upon the Tree: and account all worthy, O Thou Who alone art compassionate [f. 256vB] of Thy heavenly Kingdom!

Stretching forth Thy palms upon the Tree, O Christ, Thou didst strip bare the principalities and powers of the devil, and didst save from their harm them that piously glorify Thee!

Pierced suddenly with a spear upon the Tree, Thou didst pour forth streams of immortality unto us who were put to death through mindless transgression: therefore, with fear we glorify Thee!

Martyrs:

Desiring strange things beyond the earth, the visible masters of earthly things, the sufferers gave themselves unto strange torments, wounding the apostate with their holy wounds!

Glory... Triadikon:
