Being One of the unoriginate Trinity, Thou didst willingly endure suffering upon the Cross: dry up all the torrents of my passions, and account me worthy of salvation!

Both now... Stavrotheotokion:

Seeing the Lamb of God and the Word hanging in the flesh upon the Tree: the only unblemished Ewe-lamb and Virgin, held fast with sorrow, shed tears!

## FRIDAY EVENING VESPERS (FOR SATURDAY) (TONE 8)

On Friday Evening, at "Lord, I have cried":

*Stichera of the Holy Martyrs, Hierarchs, and Venerables. Tone 8.*

*Podoben: "What shall we call you, O holy ones" (Что вы наречемъ ст҃ыи;):*

I, wretched one, am wounded ever by the arrows of the enemy, and I am at a loss what to do: but ye who broke his arrows, who suffered manfully, and who sanctify all creation with the stream of your blood [f. 257rA] heal me who am sick, O divine Martyrs, as ye have boldness before the Lord, O worthily blessed ones!

I am held fast with utter perplexity when I consider in my mind that dread hour of Thine examination, O Thou Who alone art God of all: and I weep and lament and mourn, remembering the abyss of mine evils. Therefore save me, O Lover of mankind, by the supplications of Thy Martyrs, and deliver me from torment, as Thou art tenderhearted!

O divine Martyrs, pray unto God on behalf of them that perform your all-sacred memory in faith: that they may be delivered from temptations and obtain heavenly mansions, which the all-holy One prepared as the only Benefactor and Lover of mankind; and that He may settle their souls where the ranks of Patriarchs ever make merry, as He is longsuffering!

Other Stichera to the Martyrs, the same Tone:

O Martyrs of the Lord, ye sanctify every place and heal every sickness: and now pray ye that our souls may be delivered from the snares of the enemy, we pray you!

O Martyrs of the Lord, entreat our God and ask for our souls a multitude of bounties and cleansing from our many transgressions, we pray you!

Glory... Both now... Dogmatikon:

The King of heaven, for His love of mankind [hath appeared upon the earth]...

At the Aposticha, Stichera of the Martyrs. Tone 8.

Thy Martyrs, O Lord, forgot the things of this life [f. 257rB] and heedless of torments for the sake of the life to come, they were shown to be heirs thereof: therefore they also rejoice with the Angels. By their prayers, grant Thy people great mercy!

If there be any virtue, and if there be any praise, it is meet for the holy ones: for they bowed their necks to the sword for the sake of Thee Who didst bow the heavens and come down; they shed their blood for the sake of Thee Who didst pour out Thyself and take the form of a servant; they humbled themselves even unto death, conforming themselves unto Thy poverty: by their prayers have mercy on us, O God, according to Thy great mercy!

Aposticha of the Departed:

I weep and lament when I contemplate death, and behold our beauty, fashioned according to the image of God, lying in the graves, formless, inglorious, having no shape! O wonder! What is this mystery that hath happened unto us? How have we been surrendered unto corruption? How have we been yoked unto death? Truly by the command of God, as it is written: Who gives rest unto the departed!

Glory... Both now... Theotokion. Tone 4:

O Sovereign Lady, receive the supplications of thy servants, and deliver us from every distress and sorrow!

On Saturday, at Matins.

After the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymns of the Martyrs. Tone 8.

Today this temple is enlightened with heavenly light: for the angelic hosts rejoice therein, and with them the choirs of the Martyrs make merry at the memory of the passion-bearers...[^335]

[f. 257vA] ...at the memory of the passion-bearers: by their prayers, send down peace unto Thy world, O Christ, and great mercy!

As noetic luminaries were ye revealed, O holy Martyrs, for by faith ye destroyed the gloom of deceit, and enlightened your spiritual lamps, and entered with glory with the Bridegroom into the heavenly bridal chamber: and now we pray you: Entreat that our souls may be saved!

Glory... Both now... Theotokion:

O Thou Who for our sake wast born of the Virgin and didst endure the Crucifixion, O Good One, Who by death didst despoil death and manifest the Resurrection as God: despise not them whom Thou didst create with Thy hand; show forth Thy love for mankind, O merciful One; accept the Theotokos who bore Thee and prays for us: and save, O our Savior, a despairing people!

*After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymns of the Martyrs. Tone 8.*

*Podoben: "That which was commanded mystically" (Повелѣ́нное та́инственно):*

Luminaries shining ever in the universe were ye revealed through martyrdom: ye placed all your hope in the Lord, and with the spiritual oil of the Holy Spirit ye enlightened your spiritual lamps: whence also ye were revealed as cups of the spiritual Church, pouring forth healings like water! O all-lauded passion-bearers, entreat Christ God to grant remission of transgressions unto them that honor your holy memory with love!

Having put to death the fiery forms and stirrings of passions through abstinence, the Martyrs of Christ received grace to drive away illnesses from the sick, and while living quietly in order, to work miracles: truly a most glorious wonder, that bare bones pour forth healings! Glory to God, the only all-wise Creator!

Sessional Hymn of the Departed:

O Thou Who by the depth of wisdom orderest all things in love for mankind, and givest what is profitable unto all, O only Creator: give rest, O Lord, unto the souls of Thy servants, for they placed their hope in Thee, our Creator, Maker, and God!

Glory... Both now... Theotokion:

In thee we have a wall and a haven, and an acceptable intercessor before God Who was born of thee, O unwedded Theotokos, thou salvation of the faithful!

Canon to the Holy Martyrs, Hierarchs, Venerables, and the Departed.

A work of Joseph.

Ode 1. Tone 8. Heirmos:

Let us sing unto the Lord, Who led His people through the Red Sea: a song of victory, for He hath been glorified!

(Canon of All Saints Ode 1 Troparia):

Revealed as an honored necklace, adorning the crown of the precious Church, O valiant passion-bearers of Christ!

Shining with the divine splendors of dogmas and virtues, the hierarchs of Christ enlightened hearts in all ends of the earth!

We pray Thee, O Word: wondrous art Thou in the Prophets and Venerables: By their supplications, save us!

Of the Departed:

When Thou comest to execute righteous judgment, O most righteous One, Who alone art unjudged, O Lord: deliver Thy servants from condemnation!

[f. 257vB] Theotokion:

Knowing thee who didst bear God, the choir of women, having acted valiantly in every virtue, was brought unto Him!

Another Canon for the Departed.

Ode 1. Tone 8. Heirmos: Passing through water as on dry land:

(Canon for the Departed Ode 1 Troparia):

Having truly imitated death by death and sufferings by sufferings, all the Martyrs attained divine and blessed life!

Overlooking the transgressions of youth, and passing over sins, O Christ Savior: number with Thine elect Thy servants who have fallen asleep before us!

Abundantly grant unto Thy servants whom Thou hast received, O most merciful One, to attain the glory and joy and blessed dwelling where the saints abide!

Theotokion:

Thou didst conceive the Word of the Father, united hypostatically with the flesh, O all-immaculate Maiden: Who by divine power abolished hades!

Ode 3. Heirmos:

Thou Who didst establish the heavens by Thy Word, and founded the earth upon many waters: establish me unto the singing of Thy glorification, O Lord!

(Canon of All Saints Ode 3 Troparia):

Rejecting abominable sacrifices with steadfast mind, the sufferers were offered as a most precious sacrifice unto the Word!

Renewing speech, O sacred ministers, ye were revealed as divine teachers of Him Who renewed the world and me who was grown old with all manner of passions!

The grace of the divine Spirit, which was formerly given assuredly unto the Prophets [f. 258rA] filled the ascetics afterward with divine gifts!

Number with the choirs of the saints, O God, them that have departed this life in faith: and make them dwellers of Paradise, for the sake of Thine ineffable mercy!

Theotokion:

Jesus, Who is nowhere contained, was contained incorruptibly in thy consecrated womb, O all-hymned, all-pure Virgin!

Another Heirmos: There is none holy like Thee:

(Canon for the Departed Ode 3 Troparia):

Cleansed of the ancient ancestral fall by baptism and regeneration, sprinkled with the streams of their own blood, the blessed ones reign with Christ!

Having willingly been laid dead in a grave, raising them that dwell in the graves, O Savior: be well-pleased that those whom Thou hast received from us may dwell in the mansions of Thy saints!

Being entreated through divine tender mercy and the true goodness of Thy nature, grant remission of sins unto Thy servants, and give rest unto them who have fallen asleep!

Theotokion:

Incarnate from thy womb and having become man, He Who alone is supremely the Lover of mankind saves man from the gates of death, O all-pure, all-hymned Mother of God!

Ode 4. Heirmos:

I heard, O Lord, the mystery of Thy dispensation, I understood Thy works, and I glorified Thy Divinity!

(Canon of All Saints Ode 4 Troparia):

Entering into the spiritual contest, O divinely blessed sufferers, ye burned up material deceit by the fiery Spirit!

[f. 258rB] Thou hast brightly glorified Thy Venerables, O Lord, and the hierarchs: by their divine supplications make me a sacred minister of Thy glory!

The inspiration of the divine Spirit, which enlightened the Prophets, granted strength unto women to destroy the arrogant enemy!

Of the Departed:

Account Thy servants, whom Thou hast translated, O most good One, worthy of the promised mansions with all the saints, as I invoke the prayers of the saints!

Theotokion:

Beyond the law of nature thou didst bear the Giver of the divine law, Who renews fallen human nature, O Bride of God!

Another Heirmos: Thou art my strength, O Lord:

(Canon for the Departed Ode 4 Troparia):

That they might behold Thy glory, O Master, and receive brightly Thy light-bestowing rays in the heavens: the divine Martyrs endured to bear every kind of torture, singing unto Thee, O Christ: Glory to Thy power, O Lover of mankind!

Many are the mansions with Thee, O Savior, distributed unto all according to worth, according to the measure of virtues: account them that have fallen asleep in faith, who piously cry aloud unto Thee, worthy to be filled with them, O compassionate One: Glory to Thy power, O Lover of mankind!

Appearing unto us as man, O immortal One, Thou didst endure death common to all, and didst show forth the path of life: therefore account them that have been translated worthy of forgiveness of sins, O Lover of mankind, granting as Master the communion of light!

Theotokion:

Thou art the praise of the faithful, O unwedded one; thou art the protectress, the refuge of Christians, a wall and a haven: for thou offerest supplications unto thy Son, O all-immaculate one, and deliverest from perils them that know thee in faith and love as the pure Theotokos!...[^336]

[f. 258vA] Ode 5. Heirmos:

Enlighten us by Thy commandments:

(Canon of All Saints Ode 5 Troparia):

The divine Martyrs endured bodily wounds, therefore they ever heal our wounds, wounding the demons!

O holy hierarchs of God, with all the Venerables entreat Christ: to grant unto us the remission of transgressions!

Having restrained the flesh by mortification and asceticism, the God-loving women were accounted worthy of the hoped-for good things!

Of the Departed:

Having slain death by Thy death, O immortal One: give rest unto Thy faithful servants who died in the hope of life, as Thou art the Lover of mankind!

Theotokion:

Thou hast abolished the condemnation of our forefather, O pure one, having born in the flesh Jesus, the only Lord, Who justifies all!

Another Heirmos: Therefore hast Thou cast me off:

(Canon for the Departed Ode 5 Heirmos and Troparia):

In Thy ineffable glory, and in Thy blessedness which is beyond word, in the dwellings of the righteous where the fair voice of them that feast is heard: account them that have been translated unto immortal life worthy through Thy bounties, O Thou Who alone art the Lover of mankind!

Where the angelic ranks and the assemblies of the righteous rejoice: settle Thy servants, O Savior, in the bosom of Abraham, and with boldness [f. 258vB] to stand before Thy dread and divine throne, be pleased, O merciful One!

Thou wast revealed unto us as cleansing, righteousness, and redemption, and by Thy wisdom Thou hast healed our infirmities: do Thou Thyself, O compassionate and good One, establish in the delight of Paradise them that have been translated!

Theotokion:

In mercy, as a child, Thou didst take the measure of humanity, adorning it with divine glory and transcendent elevations; and in the virginal womb Thou didst take animate, rational flesh, whereby Thou didst destroy death!

Ode 6. Heirmos:

Cleanse me, O Savior, for many are mine iniquities:

(Canon of All Saints Ode 6 Troparia):

By your precious wounds ye heal spiritual sicknesses, and ever draw out bodily sores, wounding the multitudes of wicked demons, O holy Martyrs!

The choir of the praised, the concord of the Prophets, and the holy assembly of women, having suffered steadfastly, inherited unexpected things!

Having put to death the flesh, the ascetics attained life; having well pastured the flock of Christ, the all-wise hierarchs were accounted worthy of immortal glory after their end!

Of the Departed:

Being life unto the living, O Word, and rest unto the dead: by Thy divine nod settle Thy translated servants in the bosom of Abraham Thy servant!

Theotokion:

O all-hymned, pure dawn of the Father: with the material rays of thy Godhead, thou didst destroy the darkness of polytheism, and enlighten the world!

[f. 259rA] Another Heirmos the same:

(Canon for the Departed Ode 6 Troparia):

Thy Martyrs, O Savior, endured many torments: having wounded their holy souls with love for Thee, desiring everlasting glory and sweet communion with Thee!

Thou didst tear asunder the death enmity of sin, O Savior, and didst raise the prisoners that were held therein, granting life: whereunto account them that have been translated worthy, O Benefactor!

Deliver Thy servants from tears and groaning in hades, O Savior, as Thou alone art merciful: taking away every tear from every face of them that bless Thee unto eternity!

Theotokion:

He Who is by nature the Creator is formed in thy womb: being full as God, He is emptied, O all-immaculate one: the only immortal One dies by death for the salvation of all!

Kontakion. Tone 8:

With the saints give rest, O Christ, unto the souls of Thy servants, where there is no sickness, nor sorrow, nor sighing, but life unending!

Ikos:

Thou alone art immortal, Who didst make and fashion man: for we mortals were fashioned from the earth, and unto the earth shall we return, even as Thou didst command, Who didst fashion me and say unto me: Earth thou art, and unto the earth shalt thou return; whither all we mortals go, making the funeral lamentation, chanting the hymn: Alleluia!

Ode 7. Heirmos:

The Children...[^337]

[f. 259vA] Ode 7. Heirmos:

The pious Children in Babylon bowed not down unto the golden image; but cooling in the midst of the burning furnace, they sang the hymn, saying: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

(Canon of All Saints Ode 7 Troparia):

Having loosed the rampart of wickedness by your sacred bonds, O all-praised ones: disperse the burden of my transgressions, and save me who cry aloud, O Martyrs: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

With the showers of your sacred teachings, quench the fire of heresies, and burn up the cruel tares of impiety, O all-wise hierarchs of piety: and enlighten the souls of the faithful!

Having put to death the flesh by abstinence, the ascetics live after death; the choir of holy Prophets and the company of women, having suffered, were glorified: by their prayers, O Christ, deliver us!

Of the Departed:

Give rest, O Christ, unto the souls of all them that have fallen asleep in the hope of life, overlooking their sins committed in life: for the sake of Thy great tender mercy, O Thou Who alone art compassionate, the God of our fathers, Who art blessed!

Theotokion:

As a head thou didst receive the Word incarnate in thy womb: but entreat Him, O all-pure one, to cleanse me from sins, who flee unto thee in soul and body, and with pure faith!

Another Heirmos: The Hebrew Children:

(Canon for the Departed Ode 7 Troparia):

All desire was stretched forth by the Martyrs unto the only Master, being united unto Him in love, and singing: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers!

[f. 259vB] Thou grantest unto them that have been translated in faith the splendor of the divine Kingdom, clothing them with gifts of incorruption, as they cry aloud: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

Fill with joy and gladness Thy servants whom Thou hast translated, O compassionate One: and account them worthy to exclaim and sing unto Thee: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers!

Theotokion:

Thou didst loose the curse of Eve, taking up Thine abode in the all-immaculate Virgin: Who showed her forth as a fountain of blessing unto them that cry aloud: Blessed art thou, O all-pure one, and blessed is the Fruit of thy womb!

Ode 8. Heirmos:

The God-proclaiming Children in the furnace, trampling upon the flame with the fire, chanted: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

(Canon of All Saints Ode 8 Troparia):

Suffering, ye cast down the temples of idols, and fashioned yourselves as divine temples of the Trinity, O trophy-bearers of the Lord, companions of the Angels!

Thy priests, O Christ, clothed in righteousness, rejoice now together with the Venerables, clearly beholding Thy divine beauty!

By the prayers of Thy sacred Prophets, and of the all-blessed women, and of the righteous among men: grant Thy mercies, O Word, unto Thy world!

Of the Departed:

O righteous Judge, when Thou comest to judge: keep uncondemned those whom Thou hast received from us, overlooking their sins committed upon the earth, O Lord!

[f. 260rA] Theotokion:

Appearing unto me, O Virgin, quicken the dark clouds of my soul with thine enlightenment, O thou who didst bring forth the Sun of righteousness!

Another Heirmos: In the furnace the Children of Israel:

(Canon for the Departed Ode 8 Troparia):

Having passed through earthly passions, the true Martyrs received heavenly crowns, crying unceasingly: Sing praise unto the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

Descending into the nether pit, with Thy life-originating palm Thou didst raise them that dwelt in the graves: and Thou grantest rest unto Thy servants who have fallen asleep before us in faith, O compassionate One!

As the fountain of everlasting life, as the torrent of delight: account Thy servants who have piously departed unto Thee worthy to sing and glorify Thee unto all ages!

Theotokion:

O Mary, Virgin Theotokos, who in the flesh didst bear God the Savior unto men: save them that sing praise in faith unto thy Childbearing, and that supremely exalt the pure one unto all ages!

Ode 9. Heirmos:

Thee, the Mother of the Most High God, who knewest not wedlock, who beyond understanding didst bear the Word Who is truly God, and art higher than the all-pure Hosts, with unceasing glorifications we magnify!

(Canon of All Saints Ode 9 Troparia):

Standing as pillars before the most unrighteous tribunal, the Martyrs condemned every unrighteousness by the grace of Christ, and snatching men from the hold of the enemy, they received the crowns of righteousness!

Setting up teachers as rudders, piously steering this ship into the haven of God's commandments: all the sacred hierarchs and divine pastors: therefore as helmsmen we honor you!

[f. 260rB] The assembly of Prophets, the choir of Venerables, and the company of women who suffered brightly and shone in asceticism entreat Thee, O Lord: O Lover of mankind, we pray Thee: grant us Thy bounties!

That they may be accounted worthy of this honor and eternal glory, all the holy ones of Christ: account them that have departed from this life in faith worthy to receive the bright light, O merciful One, by the prayers of Thy saints!

Theotokion:

Bearing the fullness of good things in thine arms, O all-immaculate one: fulfill the supplications of us thy servants, and direct our paths unto God, strengthening us to live in virtues!

Another Heirmos: Every ear was amazed:

(Canon for the Departed Ode 9 Troparia):

Possessing unconquerable and invincible strength, O Martyrs of Christ: ye brought to naught the godless decree of the tormentors, and were accounted worthy of the heavenly Kingdom, being enlightened with the rays of the Trinity, O admirable ones!

Bitter hades was destroyed when Thou didst destroy it, O Lover of mankind: raising them that slept therein from the ages: and now also, as God, account them that have passed from this life worthy of Thine unwaning light!

All of Thee, O my Savior, art sweetness; all of Thee art desire and love truly insatiable; all of Thee art ineffable beauty: be pleased that they who have been translated unto Thee may take delight in Thy beauty, and make them partakers of Thy divine loveliness!

Theotokion:

Save...[^338]

[f. 260vA] Save me, O Mother of God, who didst bear my Savior, God and man: two natures, but not two persons: only-begotten of the Father, incorruptible, firstborn of all creation, Whom in two natures we magnify!

At the Praises, Stichera of the Martyrs. Tone 8:

What shall we call you, O holy ones? Cherubim? For Christ rests upon you! Seraphim? For unceasingly ye glorify Him! Angels? For ye turned away from the body! Powers? For ye work miracles! Many are your names, and yet greater are your gifts! Pray ye that our souls may be saved!

Greatly did ye contend, O holy ones, manfully enduring torments from the lawless, confessing Christ before kings! And having departed from this life, ye work powers in the world, and heal the sick through your sufferings, O holy ones: pray that our souls may be saved!

Invincible Martyrs of Christ, having overcome deceit by the power of the Cross, ye received the grace of eternal life: ye feared not the threats of the tormentors, and when wounded by torments, ye made merry! And now your blood hath become healings for our souls: entreat Christ that our souls may be saved!

Clothed well in faith and by faith, and armed with the weapon of the Cross: ye appeared as valiant soldiers, manfully opposing the tormentors, and casting down the deceit of the devil; having become victors, ye were accounted worthy of crowns: [f. 260vB] pray unceasingly on our behalf, that our souls may be saved!

Of the Departed:

Behold Thy mortality, O Christ! For hadst Thou not been laid in a grave, Paradise would not have been opened: therefore, give rest unto them that have been translated, O Lord!

Glory... Both now... Theotokion:

O pure Virgin, door of the Word, Mother of our God: pray that we may be saved!

*At the Aposticha, Stichera of the Departed. Tone 8.*

*Podoben: "O most marvelous wonder" (О преславное чудо):*

By a signature Thou didst write my liberation, O Master, staining Thy fingers with scarlet dye and reddening them with Thine own blood: and now we entreat Thee in faith: Number with Thy firstborn and with Thy righteous ones, and account them that have departed unto Thee, O merciful One, worthy to obtain joy!

*Verse: Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen and taken to Thyself, O Lord.*

Existing as man, Thou didst offer Thyself as a sacrifice unto the Father, raising man up from corruption: therefore settle them that have been translated in the land of the living, as Thou art the Lover of mankind, where the torrents of delight flow, and where the ever-flowing streams never run dry!

*Verse: Their souls shall dwell among good things.*

In the depths of Thine ineffable wisdom, Thou didst set a bound unto life, and didst foresee death: and translating Thy servants unto another life, whom Thou hast received in Thy goodness: settle them now upon the waters of rest...

[f. 261rA] ...in the splendors of the saints, where the voice of rejoicing and thanksgiving is heard!

Glory... Both now... Theotokion:

Having conceived the beginningless Word of God and God: with thy motherly boldness earnestly pray that He may settle thy servants where the never-dispersing assembly of them that rejoice and praise thee is found, where the splendors are assembled together, and the sweet voice of them that feast is heard, O divinely blessed one!

On Saturday,

The Beatitudes. Tone 8:

Remember us, O Christ, Savior of the world, even as Thou didst remember the thief upon the Tree: and account all worthy, O Thou Who alone art compassionate, of Thy heavenly Kingdom!

Firmly partaking in all illnesses: by your wounds, O holy passion-bearers, ye softened all the demonic darkness, through divine grace!

[f. 261rB] Venerables of Christ, and divine hierarchs, the assembly of the Prophets, and of all the righteous, have obtained the heavenly inheritance: whom let us worthily bless!

Of the Departed:

Settle, O God, in the lands of the righteous all them that have been translated in faith from this life: and show them to be heirs of Paradise, who God-fittingly hymn Thee!

Glory... Triadikon:

I offer unto Thee, O Trinity, the final hymnody: account them whom Thou hast translated in faith from the earth worthy of the mansions of the saints, and have mercy upon me, a prodigal!

Both now... Theotokion:

Having born the Fullness of all good things, fulfill our supplications, O Virgin: asking for us the forgiveness of transgressions, enlightenment, and great mercy!

# RESURRECTIONAL EXAPOSTILARIA, EVANGELICAL STICHERA (EOTHINA), AND COLOPHON

## EXAPOSTILARIA AND EVANGELICAL STICHERA

[f. 1rA] Resurrectional Exaposteilaria and Evangelical Stichera

Tone 1. Exaposteilarion 1:

Let us go up with the disciples into the mountain of Galilee, by faith to behold Christ saying: Authority over the highest and lowest hath been received; let us learn how He teaches to baptize in the Name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, and to abide with the initiates of the mysteries, even as He promised, unto the end of the age. (Twice)

Theotokion:

Rejoice with the disciples, O Virgin Theotokos, for thou didst behold Christ risen from the tomb on the third day, even as He said; unto whom He appeared, teaching and saying as He revealed Himself: Baptize in the Name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit; commanding us to believe in His Resurrection, and to glorify thee, O Maiden!

Evangelical Stichera 1. Tone 1:

When the disciples went up into the mountain for the earthly ascension, the Lord stood before them, and they worshipped Him; and having been taught of the authority given everywhere unto Him, they are sent forth into all under heaven to preach the Resurrection from the dead, and the translation into the heavens; which Christ God, the truthful One and the Savior of our souls, promised.

Tone 2. Exaposteilarion 2:

Beholding the stone rolled away, the Myrrh-bearing women rejoiced; for they saw a young man sitting in the tomb, and he said unto them: Behold, Christ is risen! Say unto the disciples with Peter: Make haste unto the mountain of Galilee; there shall He appear unto you, even as He foretold unto His friends!

Theotokion:

An angel indeed brought unto the Virgin the 'Rejoice!' before Thy conception, O Christ; and an angel also rolled away the stone from Thy tomb; in the place of sorrow, the one indeed brought signs of ineffable joy[^341] [f. 1vA] while the other, in place of death, proclaimed and magnified Thee, the Giver of life, and declared the Resurrection unto the initiates of the mysteries.

Evangelical Stichera 2. Tone 2:

When the women with Mary came with myrrh and were wondering how it would be possible for them to attain their desire, the stone appeared taken away, and a divine youth, calming the turmoil of their souls, said: For Jesus the Lord is risen! Therefore preach unto the preachers, His disciples, to hasten unto Galilee, and to behold Him risen from the dead, as the Giver of life and the Lord!

Tone 3. Exaposteilarion 3:

That Christ is risen, let no one disbelieve! For He appeared unto Mary, and was then seen by two who were walking into the countryside; and He appeared again unto the eleven disciples as they reclined at table; and having sent them forth to baptize, He ascended into the heavens whence He had descended, confirming the preaching with multitudes of signs!

Theotokion:

Thou hast shone forth, O Sun, from the tomb today as a Bridegroom from his bridal chamber, and hast despoiled hades; by the maternal prayers of her who bore Thee, send down Light upon us: the Light that illuminates hearts and souls, a light for all souls to walk, setting their steps upon the paths of Thy commandments and into the way of peace!

Evangelical Stichera 3. Tone 3:[^342]

[f. 2rA] When Mary Magdalene announced the glad tidings of the Savior's Resurrection from the dead and His appearance, the disciples, being disbelieving, were reproached for the hardness of their hearts; but armed with signs and miracles, they were sent forth unto preaching; and Thou indeed, O Lord, didst ascend unto the Father, the primal Light; while they preached the Word everywhere, confirming it with miracles. Therefore, having been enlightened, we also glorify Thy Resurrection from the dead, O Lover of mankind!

Tone 4. Exaposteilarion 4:

Enlightened by the virtues, having seen the men standing in shining garments at the life-bearing Tomb, while the Myrrh-bearing women bowed their faces to the earth: let us learn of the Resurrection of the Ruler of heaven, and with Peter let us run unto life, unto the tomb; and marvelling at what hath been done, let us remain praising Christ!

Theotokion:

From thy womb, O Virgin, the Lord having become incarnate, willed to recall the perishing world from corruption, even as the Almighty One knows; and finding salvation in thee, O Theotokos, we all cry aloud unto thee as the angel: Rejoice, thou who alone art pure and most blessed among women, who didst bear salvation unto all the universe!

Evangelical Stichera 4. Tone 4:

Very early in the morning the women came unto Thy Tomb, O Christ, but the Body loved by them was not found; therefore, while they were perplexed, those standing by in shining garments said: Why seek ye the Living among the dead?[^343] [f. 2vA] He is risen, even as He said before! Why do ye not remember His words? Believing whom, they preached what they had seen; but their glad tidings seemed to be idle tales: so dull of understanding were the disciples yet. But Peter ran, and saw, and glorified Thy all-powerful wonders!

Tone 5. Exaposteilarion 5:

Christ, the Life and the Way, having risen from the dead, journeyed with Cleopas and Luke, by whom He was also made known at Emmaus in the breaking of bread; whose souls and hearts were burning within them when He spoke unto them on the way, and expounded the Scriptures concerning what He had suffered: with them let us cry aloud: He is risen! Even as He appeared also unto Peter!

Theotokion:

The Creator of creation and God of all things, having taken earthly flesh from thy pure blood, O all-holy Theotokos: made whole nature which was corrupted new again, leaving thee after childbearing even as thou wast before birth; therefore in faith we all praise thee, crying aloud: Rejoice, O glory of the world!

Evangelical Stichera 5. Tone 5:

O how wise are Thy judgments, O Christ! How unto Peter indeed by the grave-clothes alone Thou gavest understanding of Thy Resurrection; and walking with Luke and Cleopas, Thou didst converse with them, and didst not reveal Thyself unto them quickly; therefore Thou wast reproached as being the only stranger in Jerusalem who knew not the counsel thereof unto the end; yet ordering all things unto the profit of creation, Thou didst unveil the prophetic words concerning Thyself; and in the blessing of the bread Thou wast made known unto them, whose hearts before that were kindled unto the knowledge of Thee; who also, when the disciples were gathered together, already clearly preached[^344] [f. 3rA] Thy Resurrection, through which have mercy on us!

Tone 6. Exaposteilarion 6:

Having shown that Thou art man, O Savior, standing in the midst Thou didst teach: Risen from the dead, having partaken of food, He ordained the baptism of repentance; and straightway He ascended unto the Heavenly Father, and promised to send the Comforter unto the disciples, O all-divine God-man!

Theotokion:

When the all-pure one beheld her own Son risen from the dead, she was filled with joy, and sang praise unto His ineffable tender mercy: that He did not abandon human nature, but having willed to be born of thee, He delivered all from corruption by His passion on the Cross, and led them unto life according to His compassion.

Evangelical Stichera 6. Tone 6:

Thou art true peace, O Christ, unto the men of God! Giving Thy peace unto the disciples after the Resurrection, Thou didst show them to be terrified, thinking that they beheld a spirit; but Thou didst calm the turmoil of their soul, showing them Thy hands and Thy feet; yet while they were still disbelieving, by the partaking of food and the reminder of Thy teachings, Thou didst open their mind to understand the Scriptures; promising them also the Father's promise, and having blessed them, Thou didst ascend into heaven: therefore with them we worship Thee: O Lord, glory to Thee![^345]

[f. 3vA] Tone 7. Exaposteilarion 7:

When Mary said that they had taken away the Lord, Simon Peter and that other disciple of Christ whom He loved ran unto the tomb; and both ran together, and found the linen clothes lying alone within, and also the napkin that was about His head wrapped together apart from them; therefore they kept silence again until they beheld Christ.

Theotokion:

I praise Thy boundless mercy, O my Helmsman, that Thou didst empty Thyself to bear and save perishing human nature; for as Thou art, Thou didst will to be born of the pure Maiden of God, and to descend even unto hades, desiring to save us by the prayers of her who bore Thee, O all-bountiful Master!

Evangelical Stichera 7. Tone 7:

Behold, it was darkness and early; and why, O Mary, standest thou at the tomb, having great darkness in thy mind, in which thou askest where Jesus hath been laid? But behold the disciples running together, how by the linen clothes and the napkin they discovered the Resurrection, and called to mind the Scriptures concerning this; with whom, and through whom, having also believed, we sing praise unto Thee, Christ the Giver of life!

Tone 8. Exaposteilarion 8:

Beholding two angels within the tomb, Mary was amazed; and not knowing Christ, she asked Him as the gardener: Sir, where hast Thou laid the body of my Jesus?[^346] [f. 4rA] and recognizing Him by His call, she heard that He was the Savior Himself: Touch Me not, for I ascend unto the Father; say unto My brethren!

Theotokion:

O Maiden, thou didst ineffably give birth unto One of the Trinity in two natures of essence, and in two operations, and in one hypostasis: Him therefore entreat thou unceasingly for them that worship thee in faith, that we may be delivered from every assault of the enemy; for we all flee unto thee, O Sovereign Lady and Theotokos!

Evangelical Stichera 8. Tone 8:

Mary's tears are not poured forth warmly in vain; for behold, she was accounted worthy of angelic teachings, and of the sight of Jesus Himself; yet she still minds earthly things, as a frail woman; therefore she is forbidden to touch Christ, but is sent forth as a herald unto His disciples, unto whom she declared the glad tidings, announcing His ascent unto the Father's inheritance: with her, account us also worthy of Thine appearance, O Master and Lord!

Evangelical 9. Exaposteilarion 9. Tone 5:

The doors being shut, O Master, when Thou didst enter, Thou didst fill the Apostles with the Spirit, unto whom Thou didst say to bind and to loose sins; and after eight days Thou didst show Thy side and hands unto Thomas, with whom we cry aloud: Thou art my Lord and my God!

Theotokion:

O pure Birth-giver of God and most holy Virgin, joy of the sorrowful, protection of the world, intercessor for sinners: comfort our sorrowing hearts by thy prayers, for after God we the faithful have no other hope save thee, O merciful and pure one, our expectation, lover of peace and salvation of the world, O Maiden![^347]

[f. 4vA] Evangelical Stichera 9. Tone 5:

As in the latter days, when it was late on the Sabbath, Thou didst stand before Thy friends, O Christ, and by wonder Thou dost confirm wonder: by the closed entry of the doors, Thy Resurrection from the dead! But Thou didst fill the disciples with joy, and didst impart the Holy Spirit unto them, and gavest them authority for the forgiveness of sins, and didst not leave Thomas to be submerged in the storm of disbelief: therefore grant unto us true understanding and the forgiveness of transgressions, O compassionate Lord!

Evangelical 10. Exaposteilarion 10. Tone 6:

The Sea of Tiberias with the children of Zebedee, and Nathanael with Peter, together with two others and Thomas of old, had them fishing; who, casting their net on the right side at Christ's command, drew forth a multitude of fishes; Whom Peter recognized, wading unto Him, unto whom He appeared the third time, and showed bread and fish upon the coals.

Theotokion:

Worshipping Thine honored icon, O all-pure one: show us to be children of the light, inhabitants of Paradise, and partakers of the Kingdom; for we are thy suppliants and thy people, O all-pure one! Let us not fall away from thy protection, O Theotokos, and account us all worthy of salvation, O all-immaculate one!

Evangelical Stichera 10. Tone 6:

After the descent into hades and the Resurrection from the dead, Thy disciples, sorrowing over Thy parting, O Christ, turned unto labor; and again there were boats and nets, but no catch at all; but Thou, O Savior, appearing as the Master of all, commandest them to cast the net on the right side; and straightway the word became deed, and the multitude of fish was great; and a strange supper[^348] [f. 5rA] was ready on the earth; of which Thy disciples having partaken then, account us also now worthy spiritually to be filled, O Lord, Lover of mankind!

Evangelical 11. Exaposteilarion 11. Tone 2:

After the divine Resurrection, the Lord said thrice unto Peter: Lovest thou Me? Appointing him chief shepherd over His sheep; but when Peter saw him whom Jesus loved following after, he asked: Master, and what shall this man do? If I will that he tarry till I come again, He said, what is that to thee, friend Peter?

Theotokion:

Rejoice! we cry aloud unto thee, O all-pure Theotokos: for thou didst announce joy, and didst turn Eve's sorrow into joy, O Virgin; fill us also with thy joy, and by the light of Thy Son account us all worthy of the portion of the elect, O all-pure one, and we all cry aloud unto thee: Rejoice, O pure Maiden!

Evangelical Stichera 11. Tone 8:

Manifesting Thyself unto the disciples after the Resurrection, O Savior, Thou didst give the feeding of the sheep unto Simon in return for his love, seeking from him care for the flock; therefore Thou saidst: If thou lovest Me, Peter, feed My sheep! But he straightway showed his affection again, inquiring concerning that other disciple: by whose prayers, O Christ, preserve Thy flock from the wolves that destroy it!

[Scribal Colophon in brown ink:]

End of the Evangelical Stichera, on the 11th day of March in the year 1631.

The decorative program consists of an outer rectangular border impressed with a Renaissance floral and vine roll, enclosed within triple fillet blind lines; an intermediate frieze of palmette scrolls; and an inner rectangular panel divided into two quadripartite compartments by diagonal blind fillets forming cross-hatched triangular fields. # FOOTNOTES AND SCHOLARLY COMMENTARY



[^1]: Physical description of the binding of the 1630 Lviv Octoechos: blind-tooled brown calfskin over bevelled wooden boards with concentric ornamental rolls, rosettes, and geometric strapwork. In the central oval mandorla medallion is embossed the Crucifixion of Christ with the Most Holy Mother of God and Saint John the Theologian standing at the foot of the Cross. Three brass clasps on leather straps are preserved along the fore-edge.

[^2]: Library classification and accession shelfmarks: "LNBU 2124, SV-97", representing the holdings of the Lviv National Scientific Library of Ukraine named after V. Stefanyk (Department of Manuscripts and Rare Books), where this copy is preserved.

[^3]: Mounted fragments of an early Cyrillic printed liturgical edition (containing Resurrectional stichera from an Octoechos), affixed to the front flyleaf during a historical binding repair.

[^4]: 17th/18th-century liturgical annotations in semi-uncial and cursive by a parish cantor or reader, citing folio 171 verso, the Tone 6 Gradual Antiphon 1 ("Unto heaven I lift up mine eyes"), the Tone 6 Prokeimenon ("O Lord, stir up Thy might..."), and Paschal cycle calculations.

[^5]: Mounted printed fragments on the flyleaf verso preserving Church Slavonic Gradual Antiphons (Anabathmoi) based on Psalm 126 (LXX): "Unless the Lord build the house..." (Аще не Господь созиждетъ домъ...).

[^6]: Parish ownership inscription dated 1838: "Oktoich Cerkwi Borchowskiey 1838", attributing the book to the Church of the Dormition in the village of Borkhiv near Lviv.

[^7]: A humorous cantor's note in Polish orthography recording a vernacular Ruthenian ditty: "Oy pope popoyku pryichaly władyki / chot' nam kony wziaty nie / wim meje semoho klasa wspinjuty" ("O priest, dear little priest, the hierarchs have arrived! Even if they want to take our horses, I do not know how to sing my seventh tone!"), signed by the cantor Kaniwczyk *manu propria*.

[^8]: A reader's chronological calculation in pencil inscribed in 1964: "1964 - 1630 = 334", calculating the 334th anniversary of the monument's publication.

Imprint dated December 15, 7138 / 1630. The printer's device displays the coat of arms of Lviv (a three-turreted gate with a passant lion) and the Brotherhood's initials (G-A-V-L).

[^19]: Sunday Matins Hypakoe and Songs of Ascents (Anabathmoi, Antiphons 1–3) in Tone 1, meditating upon divine longing in the wilderness and the heavenly Jerusalem.

[^20]: Sunday Matins Prokeimenon, Gospel order, and the Resurrectional Canon of Tone 1 by Saint John Damascene, containing the Heirmoi of Odes 1 through 6.

[^21]: Sunday Matins Resurrectional Kontakion and Ikos in Tone 1 (*"Воскреслъ еси яко Богъ из гроба..."*), followed by the Heirmoi of Odes 7 and 8.

[^23]: The original 1630 printed Cyrillic edition resumes on Folio 13r (`г̃і`) with the conclusion of the Sunday Beatitudes and Sunday Vespers for Monday. The bottom-right corner of Folio 13r has suffered physical damage and was restored with blank laid paper during historical rebinding, causing partial lacunae in the second and third Stichera to the Bodiless Powers. The damaged and missing text is reconstructed in brackets according to the standard Ruthenian Octoechos tradition.

[^24]: Monday Matins Sessional Hymns in Tone 1, following the first, second, and third Kathismata of the Psalter, meditating upon compunction, the parable of the Prodigal Son, and the intercession of the All-Holy Mother of God.

[^25]: The Monday Matins Penitential Canon by Saint Joseph the Hymnographer bears the Cyrillic alphabetical acrostic: *"Согрѣшеніи мои скверну ѡмыи Слове"* ("Wash away the defilement of my transgressions, O Word"). It is paired with the Canon to the Bodiless Powers by Saint Theophanes the Branded (*"Твореніе Ѳеофаново"*).

[^26]: Saint Theophanes' Canon to the Bodiless Powers in Tone 1 systematically invokes the celestial orders of Dionysian angelology: Angels, Archangels, Principalities, Authorities, Powers, Dominions, Thrones, Cherubim, and Seraphim.

[^27]: Odes 7 and 8 of the Monday Matins canons, interweaving the confession of the Holy Trinity with the endurance of the holy martyrs under torture and their victorious entry into the heavenly Kingdom.

[^28]: Monday Beatitudes (Typika) in Tone 1, combining the troparion of the Good Thief with penitential petitions, angelic intercessions, commemoration of the holy martyrs, and doxological stanzas to the Holy Trinity and the Mother of God.

[^29]: Monday Vespers Stichera at *"Lord, I Have Cried"* dedicated to the Holy Prophet, Forerunner, and Baptist John, invoking him as the preacher of repentance and baptizer of the Lamb of God.

[^30]: Tuesday Matins Penitential Canon by Saint Joseph the Hymnographer, alternating with the Canon to the Holy Forerunner and Baptist John, commemorating his ascetic dwelling in the wilderness and intercession before Christ.

[^31]: Odes 3 and 4 of Tuesday Matins, depicting the Baptist's witness to the Lamb of God, his immersion of the Torrent of Delight in the Jordan, and his preaching of repentance.

[^32]: Tuesday Matins Aposticha and Beatitudes in Tone 1, concluding the liturgical services of Tuesday in the Octoechos cycle before the opening of Tuesday Vespers.

[^33]: Folio 21v concludes the Tuesday cycle in Tone 1 with the final stanzas of the Beatitudes (martyric, triadikon, and theotokion), transitioning immediately into Tuesday Vespers for Wednesday. The service introduces the weekday commemoration of the Precious and Life-Creating Cross and the Stavrotheotokia (lamentations of the Mother of God at the Foot of the Cross) in Tone 1.

[^34]: Folio 22v opens the Wednesday Matins cycle in Tone 1 with the Canon to the Precious Cross by Saint Joseph the Hymnographer (*"Твореніе Іѡси́фово"*), paired with a second Canon to the Most Holy Theotokos. The hymnody frames the wood of the Cross as the cosmic antidote to the tree of Eden, restoring fallen mankind and granting immortality.

[^35]: Folios 23v–24r contain Odes 5 and 6 of the Wednesday Matins canons, developing typological imagery: Moses extending his hands upon the mountain as a figure of the Crucifixion, the piercing of Christ's side with the spear, and the tearing up of the handwriting of human debt through the outpouring of blood and water.

[^36]: Folio 25v contains the Wednesday Beatitudes and the evening transition to Thursday, initiating the liturgical commemoration of the Holy Apostles and Saint Nicholas of Myra. The Stichera at *"Lord, I Have Cried"* honor the Apostles as the closest friends of Christ and fishers of the universe.

[^37]: Folios 26v–27r open Thursday Matins with the Canon to the Holy Apostles by Saint Theophanes the Branded (*"Твореніе Ѳеофа́ново"*), paired with the Canon to Saint Nicholas of Myra by Saint Joseph the Hymnographer (*"Твореніе Іѡси́фово"*). The hymnody enumerates the Holy Apostles: Peter, Paul, James, Andrew, Philip, Simon, Bartholomew, Thomas, Matthew, John, Mark, Luke, and the broader choir of the Seventy Disciples.

[^38]: Folios 27v–28r present Odes 4 through 6 of Thursday Matins, celebrating Saint Nicholas as a fruitful olive tree in the house of God, the myrrh-scented chief hierarch of Myra, and a fervent protector of Christians in trials and perils.

[^39]: Folios 28v–29r contain the conclusion of Thursday Matins and the Beatitudes, followed on Folio 29v by the opening of Thursday Vespers for Friday, returning to the commemoration of the Precious Cross. Later archivists inscribed modern Arabic pencil numbers (`26`, `27`, `28`) on Folios 29r, 30r, and 31r, diverging from the original 1630 printed Cyrillic foliation (`кѳ҃` = 29, `л҃` = 30, `ла҃` = 31).

[^40]: Folios 30v–31r open Friday Matins with the Cruciform Canon by Saint Joseph the Hymnographer and a Canon to the Mother of God, meditating upon the cosmic trembling of creation at the death of the Word, the darkening of the sun, the opening of Paradise to the Thief, and the maternal lamentations of the Virgin at the Foot of the Cross.

[^41]: Folio 27v presents Friday Matins Odes 5 and 6, opening with the Heirmos of Ode 5 (*"Make the bright and ever-existing Light to shine forth upon us who rise early at dawn unto the judgments of Thy commandments..."*). The hymnody combines Cruciform troparia with petitions to the Theotokos as the spiritual ladder, animate ark, and unburnt bush.

[^42]: Folio 30r contains the Sessional Hymns after the 1st and 2nd Kathismata of Saturday Matins, including the celebrated Theotokion of Gabriel's greeting (*"Гавріи́лъ провѣща́вшꙋ ти́ Дв̃о: Ра́дꙋйся..."*), highlighting the Virgin as more spacious than the heavens for containing the Creator.

[^43]: Folio 30v opens the Saturday Matins Canon to the Holy Martyrs, Hierarchs, Venerable Fathers, and the Departed, bearing the traditional liturgical attribution to Saint Joseph the Hymnographer (*"Творе́ніе Іѡ́сифово"*), paired with an additional Canon for the Departed (*"Дрꙋгіи Кано́нъ Оу҆со́пшимъ"*).

[^44]: Codicological Apparatus: Quire 5 Misbinding. In this exemplar of the 1630 Lviv Octoechos, printed Folio 35 (`лє҃`), containing the opening of Tone 2 Saturday Little Vespers (*"В СУББОТУ ВЕЧЕРЪ НА МАЛОЙ ВЕЧЕРНИ..."*), is bound immediately after Folio 32v (`лв҃`), ahead of Folio 33 (`лг҃`). Furthermore, printed Folio 34 (`лд҃`) is wanting entirely in this copy. Physical facsimile leaf order (p36 -> p37 -> p38) is strictly preserved in transcription and translation in accordance with Master Translation Standard codicological protocols.

[^45]: Codicological Apparatus: Tone 2 Saturday Little Vespers concludes here at the bottom of Folio 35v with the dismissory troparion and Theotokion. Following this leaf, the physical codex returns on Folio 33r (`лг҃`) to the conclusion of Tone 1 Saturday Matins (Ode 9, Praises, and Aposticha).

Творе́ніе Іѡ́анна Дамаски́на"*).

[^47]: Folio 36v presents the conclusion of the Great Vespers Stichera at *"Lord, I Have Cried"*, including the iconic Dogmatikon Theotokion in Tone 2 (*"Пре́йде сѣ́нь зако́ннаѧ, бл҃гти прише́дши..."* — *"The shadow of the Law passed away when grace arrived..."*), composed by Saint John of Damascus, celebrating the Virgin as the unburnt bush and the mystery of the Incarnation.

[^48]: Folio 37r opens the Sunday Midnight Office in Tone 2 with the Triadical Canon (*"В НЕДѢЛЮ, НА ПОЛꙊНОЩНИЦI, КАНОНЪ ТР(ОИ)ЧЕНЪ"*), bearing the attribution to Metrophanes, Metropolitan of Smyrna (*"Творе́ніе Митрофа́ново"*), meditating on the undivided Trinity of equal majesty and the co-eternal Godhead.

[^49]: Folio 38v — Paleographical Apparatus: Paper Damage and Physical Reconstruction. On Leaf p41 (Folios 38v and 39r), the lower inner and outer margins have suffered physical loss, attrition, and rodent or moisture damage. Standard liturgical restorations for the Tone 2 Sunday Midnight Office conclusion, Sessional Hymns (Sedalna), and Anabathmoi Antiphons are supplied in editorial square brackets `[...]` adhering to epigraphic paleographical standard MTS-1.

[^50]: Folio 39r — Liturgical Apparatus: Tone 2 Sunday Matins Anabathmoi and Resurrectional Prokeimenon. The Gradual Antiphons of Tone 2 (*"На небо очи пущаю моего сердца..."*, LXX Psalm 122:1; *"Аще не Господь бы былъ въ насъ..."*, LXX Psalm 123:1; *"Надѣющіися на Господа..."*, LXX Psalm 124:1) culminate in the Sunday Matins Prokeimenon from LXX Psalm 9:33 (*"Воскресни, Господи Боже мой..."*).

[^51]: Folio 39r — Codicological and Typographical Structure: Canon Selection and Abridgement. Tone 2 Sunday Matins features the Resurrectional Canon by Saint John of Damascus (*"Во глубинѣ потопи древле..."*) paired with the Cross-Resurrectional Canon (*"Нетренну не обычну..."*). The 1630 Lviv print sets Ode 1 on Folio 39r, then transitions directly across the leaf to Folio 39v where the pre-Kontakion Theotokion of Ode 6 leads immediately into the Resurrectional Kontakion and Ikos, followed by Odes 7, 8, and 9. Physical continuity of Leaf 39 (recto on p41, verso on p42) proves this is the intended typographic layout rather than a missing gathering.

[^52]: Folio 39v — Hymnographic Realia: Sunday Resurrectional Kontakion and Ikos in Tone 2. Composed by Saint Romanos the Melodist, the Kontakion (*"Воскреслъ еси отъ гроба, Спасе всесильне..."*) and Ikos (*"Ты еси свѣтъ омраченнымъ..."*) proclaim Christ's descent into Hades, the shattering of the infernal gates, and the liberation of Adam and all humanity.

[^53]: Folio 40r — Typikon Rubrics: Tone 2 Sunday Matins Ode 8 and 9 Heirmoi. The Heirmoi of Odes 8 (*"Пещь огненная иногда въ Вавулонѣ..."*) and 9 (*"Безначална Родителя и Господь..."*) frame the concluding glorification of the Incarnation, contrasting the Three Youths in the Babylonian furnace with the immaterial light revealed in Christ.

[^54]: Folio 40v — Codicological Apparatus: Omission of Printed Folio 41. In this exemplar, printed Folio 42 (`мв҃`) immediately follows Folio 40v (`м`), omitting Folio 41 (`ма҃`) in the printed foliation numbering sequence. The liturgical text is strictly continuous without omission or lacuna between the conclusion of Tone 2 Sunday Matins Ode 9 on Folio 40v and the Sunday Praises (*"Всяко дыханіе..."*) on Folio 42r.

[^55]: Folio 40v — Hymnographic Apparatus: Sunday Praises (Ainoi / Lauds) and Eastern Stichera. [^56]: Folio 42r — Liturgical Structure: Sunday Divine Liturgy Beatitudes (Makarismoi). Folio 42r introduces the Sunday Beatitudes in Tone 2 (*"Гласъ Ти приносимъ разбойничь..."*), commemorating the confession of the Good Thief and linking the Cross to Paradise.

[^57]: Folio 42r — Typikon Rubrics: Sunday Vespers for Monday (Incipient Weekday Cycle). Following the Divine Liturgy Beatitudes, Folio 42r initiates Sunday evening Vespers for Monday (*"Въ Недѣлю, въ вечеръ, на Господи, воззвахъ..."*) with Penitential Stichera (*"Имѣяй благоутробія источникъ..."*) modeled on the Podoben *"Егда отъ древа"*.

[^58]: Folio 42v — Hymnographic Apparatus: Monday Midnight Office and Vespers Stichera to the Bodiless Powers. The liturgical cycle transitions to the weekly commemoration of the Holy Angels and Bodiless Hosts (*"Престоли, Херувими, и Серафими..."*), invoking the nine angelic ranks as unceasing celebrants around the Divine Throne.

[^59]: Folio 43r — Typikon Rubrics: Monday Matins Kathisma Sessional Hymns (Sedalna). Monday Matins features Penitential Sessional Hymns after the 1st and 2nd Kathismata (*"Яко волны морскія восташа на мя..."*, *"Помилуй мя, рече Давидъ..."*), focusing on personal compunction and comparing the penitent's plight to the barren fig tree and David's repentance.

[^60]: Folio 43r — Hymnographic Realia: Monday Matins Canon of Repentance and Canon to the Bodiless Hosts. Monday Matins features the Penitential Canon (*"Грядите, людіе, поемъ пѣснь Христу Богу..."*) paired with the Canon to the Incorporeal Hosts by Saint Theophanes the Branded (*"Твореніе Ѳеофаново"*, Heirmos *"Нетренну, необычну..."*).

[^61]: Folio 46r — Typikon Rubrics: Monday Matins Aposticha and Monday Vespers for Tuesday. Concluding the Monday cycle with the Aposticha (*"Содѣянныхъ моихъ золъ помышляю безмѣстная..."*), Folio 46r transitions to Monday evening Vespers for Tuesday (*"Въ понедѣлокъ въ вечеръ, на Господи, воззвахъ..."*), initiating the weekly commemoration of Saint John the Forerunner and Baptist.

[^62]: Folio 46v — Hymnographic Realia: Tuesday Vespers Stichera to Saint John the Baptist. Dedicated to the Precursor and Baptist of the Lord (*"Проповѣдниче Христовъ и Крестителю..."*), highlighting John as angel, apostle, martyr, prophet, friend of the Bridegroom, and seal of the Prophets bridging the Old and New Covenants.

[^63]: Folio 46v — Typikon Rubrics: Tuesday Matins Kathisma Sessional Hymns. Tuesday Matins continues the cycle of repentance while weaving in petitions to the Forerunner, Apostles, and Martyrs (*"Апостоли, Пророцы, и Мученицы..."*).

[^64]: Folio 47r — Hymnographic Realia: Tuesday Matins Canon of Compunction and Canon to the Forerunner by Saint Joseph the Hymnographer. [^65]: Folio 49r — Paleographical Apparatus: Colophon and Transition to Tuesday Canon Odes 7–9. [^67]: Folio 50v — Typikon Rubrics: Tuesday Matins Aposticha and Beatitudes. [^68]: Folio 50v — Hymnographic Structure: Tuesday Vespers for Wednesday (Precious Cross & Theotokos). [^69]: Folio 51v — Typikon Rubrics: Wednesday Matins Kathisma Sessional Hymns (Sedalna) of the Precious Cross. [^74]: Folio 56r — Hymnographic Realia: Thursday Matins Canons to the Apostles and Saint Nicholas. [^75]: Folio 58v — Typikon Rubrics: Thursday Matins Aposticha and Beatitudes. [^76]: Folio 59r — Typikon Rubrics: Thursday Vespers for Friday (Precious Cross and Stavrotheotokia). [^82]: Folio 64r — Hymnographic Realia: Saturday Matins Canons to All Saints and the Departed.
