[^83]: Folio 67r — Typikon Rubrics: Saturday Matins Lauds (Ainoi) and Aposticha for the Departed (*Stichera Hymns for the Departed (Поко́инъ)*). Saturday Matins concludes with Stichera at the Praises praising the Martyrs whose relics are venerated by Kings and Hierarchs (quoting Psalm 115:6 [LXX 115:6 / MT 116:15]), followed by the funeral Aposticha (*"Стремле́нїе сме́ртное и тлю̀..."*) praying for the dead of the earth.

[^84]: Folio 67v — Codicological Apparatus & Epigraphic Transition: Conclusion of Tone 2 (*"КОНЕ́ЦЪ ВТОРО́МУ ГЛА́Сꙋ"*) and Folio 68 Lacuna. Folio 67v marks the solemn conclusion of the Second Tone with a large decorative woodcut tailpiece. In this exemplar, Folio 68 is wanting (lacuna) between Folio 67v (Leaf p69 Left) and Folio 69r (Leaf p69 Right). The missing leaf originally contained the Saturday Liturgy dismissal and the opening of Tone 3 Little Vespers (Mala Vechirnia). Folio 69r begins directly with Tone 3 Saturday Great Vespers.

[^85]: Folio 69r — Hymnographic Structure: Tone 3 Saturday Great Vespers at *"Lord, I call"*. Folio 69r opens with a woodcut headpiece and decorative title vyaz introducing Tone 3 (*"Гла́съ Тре́тій"*), featuring the Resurrection Stichera (*"Твои́мъ Крⷭто́мъ Хе҃ Сп҃се..."*), Anatolian (Eastern) Stichera, and the Dogmatikon Theotokion (*"Ка́кѡ недиви́мся, Бгомꙋ́жному рождествꙋ̀ ти́..."* / *"How should we not marvel..."*).

[^86]: Folio 69v — Typikon Rubrics: Tone 3 Great Vespers Aposticha and Sunday Resurrection Troparion. Great Vespers concludes with the Resurrection Aposticha (*"Стрⷭтїю твое́ю Хе҃..."*), the alphabetical stichera, and the Troparion of Tone 3 (*"Да веселя́тся нб҃наѧ..."* / *"Let the heavenly things rejoice..."*).

[^87]: Folio 69v — Hymnographic Realia: Tone 3 Sunday Midnight Office (Mesonyktikon) Triadical Canon by Saint Metrophanes of Smyrna. Folio 69v introduces the Sunday Midnight Office Canon to the Holy and Consubstantial Trinity (*"Творе́нїе Митрофа́ново"*, Heirmos *"И́же во́ды дре́вле мані́емъ..."*), an exalted patristic contemplation of the triune Godhead, praising the Father unbegotten, the Son begotten, and the Holy Spirit proceeding.

[^88]: Tone 3 Sunday Midnight Office, Triadical Canon: Metrophanes of Smyrna (9th century) composed the triadical canons for the Sunday Midnight Office across the eight tones of the Octoechos. In Greek hymnography, the acrostic forms Ἐν τῇ Τριάδι τὸν τρίτον πλέκω λόγον ("Unto the Trinity I weave this third discourse").

[^89]: Tone 3 Sunday Matins, Resurrection Sessional Hymns (after the First Kathisma): "Christ is risen from the dead, the firstfruits of them that slept..." quotes 1 Corinthians 15:20 verbatim. The Slavonic text reads: "Хс ѡ мертвыхъ воста, начатокъ оумершимъ, первенецъ твари, и содѣтель всѣмъ бывшимъ..."

[^90]: Tone 3 Sunday Matins, Resurrection Sessional Hymns (after the Second Kathisma): Meditating on the harrowing of Hades and Christ's voluntary passion in the flesh, cutting off the bitterness of death and destroying the ancient curse.

[^91]: Tone 3 Sunday Matins, Hypakoe: The Hypakoe (Greek: Ὑпакоή, "attentive listening" or "response") recounts the dazzling appearance of the Angel at the empty tomb and his announcement of the Resurrection unto the Myrrh-bearing women.

[^92]: Tone 3 Sunday Matins, Anabathmoi (Antiphons of the Steps) and Prokeimenon: The Anabathmoi are based on the Gradual Psalms (LXX 119–133). Antiphon 1 is rooted in Psalm 125 (LXX): "When the Lord turned again the captivity of Sion..." The Prokeimenon quotes Psalm 95:10 (LXX): "Say among the heathen that the Lord reigns: He hath also established the world so that it cannot be moved."

[^93]: Tone 3 Sunday Matins, Canon of the Resurrection: Composed by St. John of Damascus. In Greek hymnography, the acrostic is Ὁ τρίτος οὗτος ὕμνος ἐντὸς τῆς тριάδος ("This third hymn is within the Trinity").

[^94]: Tone 3 Sunday Matins, Canon of the Cross and Resurrection: A classic Byzantine liturgical composition meditating upon the mystery of Christ's life-giving death upon the Cross and His victorious descent into Hades.

[^95]: Tone 3 Sunday Matins, Resurrection Kontakion: Composed by St. Romanos the Melodist (Tone 3, Podoben: "The works of the day"): "Thou didst arise today from the tomb, O Compassionate One..."

[^96]: Tone 3 Sunday Matins, Resurrection Ikos: The Ikos follows the Kontakion after Ode 6, meditating upon the cosmic jubilation of heaven and earth at the shattering of the gates of Hades.

[^97]: Tone 3 Sunday Divine Liturgy, The Beatitudes (Makarismoi): In Byzantine and Ruthenian practice, these troparia are chanted during the Divine Liturgy with the Beatitudes (Matthew 5:3–12), alternating between the confession of the Good Thief and the redemption of Adam.

[^98]: Sunday Evening (Vespers for Monday), Tone 3: Penitential Stichera on "Lord, I have cried" (*Kyrie Ekekraxa*), marking the transition into the weekday liturgical cycle dedicated to personal repentance and the heavenly angelic hierarchy.

[^99]: Monday Matins, Tone 3 Sessional Hymns (after the First Kathisma): Penitential sessional hymns emphasizing personal mortality ("the dust in the grave sings not") and supplication before the dread judgment seat of Christ.

[^100]: Monday Matins, Penitential Canon: Composed by St. Joseph the Hymnographer (9th century), Tone 3, characterized by intimate compunction, tears of repentance, and the examples of the harlot and the publican.

[^101]: Monday Matins, Canon to the Holy Bodiless Powers (Angels): Composed by St. Theophanes the Branded (Graptos, 9th century), Tone 3, celebrating the nine celestial orders who stand before the throne of the Holy Trinity.

[^102]: Monday Matins, The Beatitudes: Troparia chanted with the Beatitudes on Monday, invoking the intercession of the heavenly angelic hosts and the holy martyrs before the second coming.

[^103]: Monday Evening (Vespers for Tuesday), Tone 3: Stichera on "Lord, I have cried" dedicated to the Holy Prophet, Forerunner, and Baptist John, inaugurating Tuesday's commemoration of the prophets and the Baptist.

[^104]: Tone 3 Tuesday Matins, Sessional Hymns (after the Third Kathisma): Tone 3, Podoben "Of the divine faith" (*Божественныя вѣры*), dedicated to the Holy Forerunner, beseeching him to quiet the tempest of afflictions and illnesses.

[^105]: Tone 3 Tuesday Matins, Penitential Canon: Composed by St. Joseph the Hymnographer (9th century), Tone 3. The Heirmos of Ode 1 refers to God drying the abyss of the Red Sea and drowning Pharaoh's chariots (Exodus 14–15).

[^106]: Tone 3 Tuesday Matins, Canon to the Holy Forerunner: Tone 3, Ode 1 Heirmos: "He Who of old by His divine nod gathered the waters into one gathering..." (referencing Genesis 1:9 and Exodus 14:21–22).

[^107]: Tone 3 Tuesday Matins, Penitential Canon, Ode 3 Heirmos: "O barren and childless soul, acquire blessed fruit..." Echoing the Canticle of Hannah in 1 Kingdoms 2:1–2 (LXX), "My heart is established in the Lord... there is none holy as the Lord."

[^108]: Tone 3 Tuesday Matins, Penitential Canon, Ode 4 Heirmos: "Foreseeing the overshadowed mountain, even thy pure womb, O pure one..." Drawing upon the Canticle of the Prophet Habakkuk (Habakkuk 3:3 LXX: "God shall come from Teman, and the Holy One from the thick and shadowy mountain of Paran").

[^109]: Tone 3 Tuesday Matins, Canon to the Forerunner, Ode 6: Drawing upon Jonah 2:1–3 (LXX) and Psalm 68:2–3 (LXX) ("The lowest depth of sins hath surrounded me..."), while celebrating John the Baptist baptizing Christ in the streams of the Jordan.

[^110]: Tone 3 Tuesday Matins, Penitential Canon, Ode 7 Heirmos: Meditating upon the Three Holy Children in the Babylonian furnace (Daniel 3:23–26 LXX), who were preserved unconsumed by the cooling angel of God.

[^111]: Tone 3 Tuesday Matins, Penitential Canon, Ode 9 Heirmos: Quoting the Canticle of Zechariah (Luke 1:68–79): "Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; for He hath visited and redeemed His people, and hath raised up an horn of salvation for us in the house of David His servant..."

[^112]: Tone 3 Tuesday Divine Liturgy, The Beatitudes (Makarismoi): Troparia chanted with the Beatitudes on Tuesday, alternating the confession of the Good Thief (Luke 23:42) with petitions through the intercession of the Baptist, the holy martyrs, and the angelic orders.

[^113]: Tuesday Evening (Vespers for Wednesday), Tone 3: Stichera on "Lord, I have cried" dedicated to the Precious and Life-Giving Cross, inaugurating the liturgical observance of Wednesday commemorating Christ's betrayal and crucifixion.

[^114]: Tuesday Evening (Vespers for Wednesday), Aposticha Stichera of the Cross: Typological meditation on Moses lifting up his hands upon the mountain against Amalek (Exodus 17:11–12) as a prefiguration of Christ stretching out His hands upon the Cross.

[^115]: Tone 3 Wednesday Matins, Sessional Hymns of the Cross (after the First Kathisma): Sessional hymns celebrating the wood of the Cross touching the earth and reaching unto the heavens, prefigured in the cypress, pine, and cedar (Isaiah 60:13).

[^116]: Tone 3 Wednesday Matins, Canon of the Precious Cross: Composed by St. Joseph the Hymnographer, Tone 3. The Heirmos of Ode 1 celebrates God gathering the waters into one gathering and dividing the Red Sea (Genesis 1:9; Exodus 14:21).

[^117]: Tone 3 Wednesday Matins, Canon to the Most Holy Theotokos: Companion canon to the Canon of the Cross for Wednesday Matins, meditating on the Mother of God standing beside the Cross and shedding maternal tears.

[^118]: Tone 3 Wednesday Matins, Canon of the Cross, Ode 4 Heirmos: "Thou hast placed toward us steadfast love, O Lord, for Thou didst give Thine Only-begotten Son unto death for us..." Reflecting John 3:16 and Romans 5:8.

[^119]: Tone 3 Wednesday Matins, Canon of the Cross, Ode 9 Heirmos: The Burning Bush upon Mount Sinai (Exodus 3:2) as a prophetic type of the Virgin Theotokos conceiving the unquenchable divine fire without being consumed.

[^120]: Tone 3 Wednesday Divine Liturgy, The Beatitudes: Troparia chanted with the Beatitudes on Wednesday, commemorating the piercing of Christ's side with a lance (John 19:34) and the fountain of immortality poured out for the life of the world.

[^121]: Wednesday Evening (Vespers for Thursday), Tone 3: Stichera on "Lord, I have cried" celebrating the Holy Apostles as witnesses of the Word, and St. Nicholas the Wonderworker of Myra in Lycia as a swift protector and deliverer.

[^122]: Tone 3 Thursday Matins, Sessional Hymns to the Apostles (after the First Kathisma): Hymning the Holy Apostles who like wise fishermen cast their nets into the deep and drew all nations to faith in the undivided Trinity.

[^123]: Tone 3 Thursday Matins, Sessional Hymns (after the Third Kathisma): Sessional hymn to St. Nicholas of Myra, celebrating his miraculous deliverance of the three innocent men condemned to death by an unjust judge (an event famously recorded in his Vita).

[^124]: Tone 3 Thursday Matins, Canon to the Holy Apostles: Composed by St. Theophanes the Branded (Graptos, 9th century), Tone 3, celebrating the Apostles as immovable pillars of the Church and heralds of the divine illumination of the Gospel.

[^125]: Tone 3 Thursday Matins, Canon to Saint Nicholas: Composed by St. Joseph the Hymnographer, Tone 3. The Heirmos of Ode 1 refers to the crossing of the Red Sea (Exodus 15:1–2), and praises Nicholas as an unwaning beacon and pillar of piety.

[^126]: Tone 3 Thursday Matins, Canons to the Apostles and St. Nicholas, Odes 5–6: Meditations on the Apostles as heralds of the unwaning Light and Nicholas as the wise pilot guiding souls tossed upon the tempestuous waves of life.

[^127]: Tone 3 Thursday Matins, Canons, Ode 7: Allusion to the Three Holy Children in the Persian furnace (Daniel 3:23–26 LXX), contrasted with Arius whose impious heresy Nicholas strangled with the sinews of his orthodox theological words.

[^128]: Tone 3 Thursday Matins, Ode 9 Heirmos: "In the shadow and letter of the Law, we the faithful perceive a figure..." Based on Exodus 13:2 and Luke 2:23 ("Every male that opens the womb shall be called holy to the Lord").

[^129]: Tone 3 Thursday Matins, Aposticha to the Apostles: Celebrating the universal proclamation of the Apostles according to Psalm 18:5 (LXX) / Romans 10:18 ("Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the world").

[^130]: Tone 3 Thursday Divine Liturgy, The Beatitudes (Makarismoi): Troparia chanted with the Beatitudes in Tone 3, specifically naming the Twelve Apostles: Peter, Paul, Mark, Luke, Matthew, Simon, James, Andrew, John, Bartholomew, Philip, and Thomas.

[^131]: Thursday Evening (Vespers for Friday), Tone 3: Stichera on "Lord, I have cried" dedicated to the Precious Cross, sung to the automelon "They weighed thirty pieces of silver" (*Поставиша тридесяте*), commemorating the price of betrayal (Zechariah 11:12; Matthew 26:15) and Christ's voluntary Passion.

[^132]: Thursday Evening Vespers, Aposticha of the Cross: Typological meditation on Moses stretching forth his hands upon the mountain against Amalek (Exodus 17:11–12) as a primordial prophetic type of Christ stretching out His hands upon the Cross.

[^133]: Friday Matins, Sessional Hymns of the Cross (after the First Kathisma): Celebrating the cosmic height of the Cross touching heaven and earth, prefigured in the wood of the cypress, pine, and cedar (Isaiah 60:13).

[^134]: Friday Matins, Canon of the Precious Cross: Composed by St. Joseph the Hymnographer, Tone 3. The Heirmos of Ode 1 refers to Israel passing dry-shod through the Red Sea (Exodus 14:21–22).

[^135]: Friday Matins, Canon of the Cross, Ode 4 Heirmos: Habakkuk 3:3 (LXX) typology of the divine virtue covering the heavens and the Virgin Mother bearing the Infant King in the temple of His glory (Luke 2:28).

[^136]: Friday Matins, Canon of the Cross, Ode 5 Heirmos: Isaiah's prophetic vision of the Lord seated upon a high and exalted throne surrounded by the Seraphim (Isaiah 6:1–3).

[^137]: Friday Matins, Canon of the Cross, Ode 7 Heirmos: The Three Holy Children in the Babylonian furnace (Daniel 3:23–26 LXX) preserved unburnt by the divine dew, prefiguring the unconsumed womb of the Virgin Mother.

[^138]: Friday Matins, Canon of the Cross, Ode 9: The cosmic convulsions at the Crucifixion (Matthew 27:45, 51–52: the sun darkened, rocks rent, and the temple veil torn in twain), and Christ drawing all things to Himself upon the Cross.

[^139]: Friday Evening (Vespers for Saturday), Tone 3: Stichera on "Lord, I have cried" honoring the Holy Martyrs, Hierarchs, and Venerable Monastics, sung to the automelon "Great is the power of Thy martyrs, O Christ" (*Веліа муникъ твоихъ*).

[^140]: Friday Evening Vespers, Aposticha for the Departed: Solemn funeral troparia (Hymns for the Departed (Поко́инъ)) meditating upon the transience of human life ("Smoke is our life, vapor, earth, and ash...", echoing James 4:14 and Job 30:19), imploring Christ to grant rest to the departed in Abraham's bosom (Luke 16:22).

[^141]: Saturday Matins, Sessional Hymns (after the First Kathisma): Commemorating the martyrs as undefeated athletes of Christ armed with the wood of the Cross.

[^142]: Saturday Matins, First Canon: Dedicated to All Saints (Martyrs, Hierarchs, Monastics) and the Faithful Departed, composed by St. Joseph the Hymnographer, Tone 3.

[^143]: Saturday Matins, Second Canon: Dedicated to the Faithful Departed, composed by St. Theophanes the Branded, Tone 3, beseeching Christ to grant rest to those translated from earth in the mansions of the righteous.

[^144]: Saturday Matins, Canons, Ode 7 Heirmos: The Three Holy Children in the Babylonian furnace preserving their fidelity to the God of their fathers (Daniel 3:26–28).

[^145]: Saturday Matins, Canons, Ode 9 Heirmos: Prophetic typologies of the Mother of God: the Burning Bush seen by Moses on Sinai (Exodus 3:2), the unhewn mountain in Daniel 2:34, and the rod budding from the root of Jesse (Isaiah 11:1).

[^146]: Saturday Matins, Canons, Ode 9 conclusion: Compositions of St. Joseph the Hymnographer and St. Theophanes the Branded, concluding the Saturday commemorations of All Saints (Hierarchs, Prophets, Monastics, Holy Women) and the Faithful Departed in Tone 3.

[^147]: Saturday Matins, Stichera at the Praises (Ainoi): Dedicated to the Holy Martyrs as unconquerable athletes who disregarded earthly tortures and rulers, obtaining crowns from Christ.

[^148]: Saturday Matins, Stichera at the Aposticha: Dedicated to the Faithful Departed in Tone 3, sung to the model melody "Great is the power of Thy Cross, O Lord," with psalm verses from Ps. 64:5 (LXX) ("Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen...") and Ps. 24:13 (LXX) ("Their souls shall abide in good things").

[^149]: Saturday Beatitudes (Makarismoi): Commemorating the confession of the Good Thief (Luke 23:42), the contests of the martyrs, the prayers of all the saints, and supplications for the departed to dwell in the light of Christ's countenance.

[^150]: Full-page woodcut concluding Tone 3 on Folio 101v (Leaf p102 Left Page): A framed woodcut depicting the Crucifixion on Golgotha, with Christ on the Cross flanked by the spear and the reed with sponge, the titulus inscribed ІС ХС ЦРЬ СЛВЫ (Jesus Christ, King of Glory), the walled city and towers of Jerusalem in the background, and the cavern below containing the skull and bones of Adam.

[^151]: Saturday Evening, Little Vespers in Tone 4: Opening Resurrection Stichera on "Lord, I have cried," celebrating the three-day rising of Christ, the harrowing of hades, and the wonder of the Virgin Mother nursing her Creator.

[^152]: Saturday Evening, Little Vespers Aposticha: Resurrection Sticheron in Tone 4 and penitential Stichera to the Mother of God, incorporating psalm verses from Ps. 44:11, 15, 18 (LXX) ("Hear, O daughter, and see...", "The virgins that follow her...", "I will remember Thy name...").

[^153]: Tone 4, Saturday Evening Great Vespers: Opening with the canonical rubric and display title (# TONE 4), followed by the Resurrection Stichera on "Lord, I have cried" in Tone 4 and Anatolian Stichera celebrating Christ's victory over hades and death.

[^154]: Saturday Great Vespers, Dogmatic Theotokion in Tone 4: "David the ancestor of God through Thee, O Prophet, musically proclaimed...", developing the royal and prophetic imagery of Psalm 44:10–11 (LXX) ("The Queen stood at Thy right hand...") and the Good Shepherd bearing the lost sheep upon His shoulders.

[^155]: Saturday Great Vespers, Aposticha Stichera: Resurrection Stichera in Tone 4 arranged alphabetically, accompanied by the Sabbath psalm verses from Ps. 92:1, 5 (LXX) ("The Lord is King...", "For He hath established the world...", "Holiness becomes Thy house...").

[^156]: Sunday Midnight Office, Triadicon Canon: Composed by Mitrofan (Metrophanes) of Smyrna in Tone 4, setting forth Orthodox Trinitarian theology on the co-essential, co-eternal, and co-enthroned Hypostases of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.

[^157]: Sunday Midnight Office, Triadicon Canon, Odes 4–6 and Sessional Hymn: Meditating on the Trinitarian revelation in the baptism of Christ, the vision of the Prophet Isaiah (Isa. 6:1–3), and the uncreated divine nature.

[^158]: Sunday Midnight Office, Triadicon Canon, Odes 7–9: Concluding odes based on the biblical canticles of Daniel and the Three Holy Children, confessing the one Godhead in three Persons.

[^159]: Sunday Matins, Sessional Hymns (Kathismata): Sung after the First and Second Psalter readings, depicting the terror of the guards at the tomb, the amazement of the Myrrh-bearers, the appearance of the Archangel Gabriel, and the contemplation of the Mystery of the Incarnation by St. Joseph the Betrothed.

[^160]: Sunday Matins, Hymns of Degrees (Anavathmoi) in Tone 4: Antiphon 1 ("From my youth many passions war against me..."), Antiphon 2 ("I cried unto Thee, O Lord, fervently from the depth of my soul..."), and Antiphon 3, based on the Gradual Psalms (Psalms of Ascents, LXX 119–133) and extolling the vivifying action of the Holy Spirit.

[^161]: Sunday Matins, Resurrection Canons, Ode 1: Comprising the Canon of the Resurrection (Heirmos: "Traversing of old the deep of the Red Sea with dry feet..."), the Canon of the Cross and Resurrection (Heirmos: "I will open my mouth..."), and the Canon to the Most-holy Mother of God (Heirmos: "The three mighty captains...").

[^162]: Sunday Matins Canons, Odes 3 and 4: Extolling the life-giving Cross as the true Vine, the harrowing of hades, the typological fulfilment of the Burning Bush, and the two natures of the incarnate Christ.

[^163]: Sunday Matins Canons, Odes 5 and 6: Proclaiming Christ as the Light of the world, the quickening of the saints in hades, the Incarnation from the Virgin's pure blood with rational soul and human will, and the deliverance from the serpent.

[^164]: Sunday Matins, Kontakion and Ikos in Tone 4: "My Savior and Deliverer from the tomb...", celebrating Christ as the mighty God and Master Who shattered the gates of hades, crushed the sting of death, and set free Adam and Eve.

[^165]: Sunday Matins Canons, Ode 8: Based on the Song of the Three Holy Children (Dan. 3:57–88) and the deliverance of Daniel from the pit of lions (Dan. 6:16–24), celebrating the resurrection of Christ and the gathering of all nations under the Cross.

[^166]: Sunday Matins Canons, Ode 9: Meditating on the Cornerstone cut out without hands from the unhewn mountain (Dan. 2:34, 45) and the reconciliation of heaven and earth in the Resurrection.

[^167]: Sunday Matins, Stichera at the Praises (Ainoi): Resurrection and Anatolian Stichera in Tone 4 on "Let every breath praise the Lord" (Ps. 148, 150 LXX), celebrating the stone rolled away from the tomb, the astonishment of Mary Magdalene, and the rebuke of the unbelieving guards.

[^168]: Sunday Divine Liturgy, The Beatitudes (Makarismoi) in Tone 4: Eight Resurrection troparia intercalated with the Beatitudes, contrasting Adam's exile with the Good Thief's entry into Paradise, and commemorating the Myrrh-bearing women and the appearance to the Apostles including Thomas.

[^169]: Sunday Evening, Vespers for Monday: Penitential Stichera on "Lord, I have cried" in Tone 4 to the melody "Thou hast given a sign," invoking models of repentance (the Thief, the Prodigal, Manasseh, the Publican), followed by Stichera to the Bodiless Powers (the nine angelic ranks: Seraphim, Cherubim, Thrones, Dominions, Principalities, Powers, Virtues, Archangels, and Angels).

[^170]: Monday Matins, Tone 4: Sessional Hymns after the 3rd Kathisma (or Ode/Poetic Kathisma) to the Bodiless Powers (Holy Angels and Archangels), invoking their constant standing before the Supradivine Trinity and their intercession for peace and remission of sins.

[^171]: Monday Matins, Tone 4: Penitential Canon and Canon to the Bodiless Powers, Ode 1, with the Heirmos "The three mighty captains..." (based on the drowning of Pharaoh's commanders in Exod. 15:4), invoking Christ's mercy shown unto the prodigal, the harlot, and the publican, followed by the contemplation of the angelic intellects before the Primal Mind.

[^172]: Monday Matins Canons, Tone 4, Odes 3 and 4: Extolling deliverance from the night of worldly passions by the Unwaning Light, the steadfastness of the Holy Martyrs in the shedding of their blood, and the nine angelic ranks praising the single, beginningless Godhead.

[^173]: Monday Matins Canons, Tone 4, Ode 7: Sessional themes and troparia to the Bodiless Powers based on the Song of the Three Holy Children in the Babylonian furnace (Dan. 3), and Isaiah's vision of the Seraphim before the divine throne (Isa. 6:1–3).

[^174]: Monday Matins Canons, Tone 4, Ode 8: Based on the Benedicite (Dan. 3:57–88), celebrating the bedewing of the faithful in the furnace, the deliverance of the soul from irrational passions and the wild boar of evils (Ps. 79:14 LXX), and the unceasing doxology of the Archangels.

[^175]: Monday Matins Canons, Tone 4, Ode 9, Aposticha, and Beatitudes: The eschatological call to trim lamps with the oil of virtues before the Bridechamber (Matt. 25:1–13), followed by the Monday Beatitudes (Makarismoi) in Tone 4, commemorating the Bodiless Powers and the Holy Martyrs.

[^176]: Monday Evening, Vespers for Tuesday, Tone 4: Dedicated to repentance and the Holy Forerunner and Baptist John, the greatest born of women (Matt. 11:11), opening with the Penitential Stichera on "Lord, I have cried" to the melody "With tears I desired," followed by Stichera to the Forerunner.

[^177]: Tuesday Matins, Tone 4: Sessional Hymns after the Kathismata, meditating on the impending judgment, the vigilance of the Wise Virgins, the endurance of the Holy Martyrs, and the sweet-singing Turtledove (the Forerunner) calling all to repentance.

[^178]: Tuesday Matins, Tone 4: Penitential Canon composed by St. Joseph the Hymnographer (with acrostic) and Canon to the Holy Forerunner John, Odes 1 and 3, beseeching deliverance from the sleep of slothfulness and spiritual barrenness through the prayers of the Baptist.

[^179]: Tuesday Matins Canons, Tone 4, Odes 4, 5, and 6: Praising the Forerunner as the spiritual morning star, the sweet-singing turtledove and swallow announcing the spiritual spring of Christ, and the baptizer of the Lord in the Jordan.

[^180]: Tuesday Matins Canons, Tone 4, Odes 7, 8, and 9: Based on the Three Children in Babylon (Dan. 3), praising the Forerunner who leaped in his mother's womb, calling upon the soul to bear fruits worthy of repentance before the axe strikes the barren fig tree (Luke 3:9).

[^181]: Tuesday Divine Liturgy, The Beatitudes (Makarismoi) in Tone 4: Intercalating the Beatitudes with troparia of repentance invoking the tears of Peter and the harlot, the intercession of the Holy Forerunner, and the steadfast confession of the Holy Martyrs.

[^182]: Tuesday Evening, Vespers for Wednesday, Tone 4: Dedicated to the Precious and Life-giving Cross of the Lord, with Cruciform Stichera (Stavropegial) at "Lord, I have cried" to the melody "As one noble," and Stavrotheotokia meditating on the maternal lamentations of the Virgin Mother at the foot of the Cross.

[^183]: Wednesday Matins, Tone 4: Sessional Hymns of the Precious Cross and the Holy Martyrs after the Kathismata, celebrating the wood of the Cross which abolished the ancient curse of the tree of knowledge and redeemed mankind by the Blood of Christ.

[^184]: Wednesday Matins, Tone 4: Canon of the Precious and Life-giving Cross of the Lord, composed by St. Joseph the Hymnographer, Ode 1, with the Heirmos "Traversing of old the deep of the Red Sea with dry feet..." (Exod. 14–15), prefiguring the Cross through Moses' hands stretched out crosswise over Amalek.

[^185]: Wednesday Matins, Tone 4: Odes 3 and 4 of the Canon of the Precious and Life-giving Cross and Canon to the Most-holy Theotokos, meditating upon the wood of the Cross that raised up those cast down into corruption, the blunting of the flaming sword that barred access to Eden (Gen. 3:24), the holy Martyrs extinguishing the rivers of polytheism, and the maternal lamentations of the Virgin Mother at the Crucifixion of Her Son.

[^186]: Wednesday Matins Canons, Tone 4: Odes 5 and 6, extolling the life-giving streams of incorruption flowing from the spear-pierced side of Christ, which healed the ancient wound incurred through the rib of the first-fashioned man, the bodily dissolution and spiritual victory of the Holy Martyrs, and the divine conception of Emmanuel by the all-pure Virgin.

[^187]: Wednesday Matins Canons, Tone 4: Odes 7 and 8, invoking the Three Holy Youths in the Babylonian furnace (Dan. 3), the stretching out of Christ's hands upon the Cross to heal our ancestral reaching for forbidden fruit, and the mystical dew of the Spirit cooling the souls of the faithful amidst burning passions.

[^188]: Codicological Note on Gathering Transposition in the 1630 Lviv Edition: In this physical exemplar, the inner bifolia of the gathering containing folios 121–125 were transposed during binding or imposition. Physical leaf p122 (Folio 122r) contains the conclusion of the Wednesday Beatitudes (Makarismoi) and the opening of Wednesday Evening Stichera for the Holy Apostles and St. Nicholas, while the completion of Wednesday Matins Canons (Odes 8–9) and Aposticha appears on physical leaves p123 (Folio 123r) and p124 (Folio 123v). Physical leaf coordinates are strictly preserved according to MTS-1 facsimile indexing.

[^189]: Wednesday Evening (Vespers for Thursday), Tone 4: Dedicated to the Holy Apostles and Saint Nicholas the Wonderworker, Archbishop of Myra in Lycia. Opening with Stichera on "Lord, I have cried" celebrating the Holy Twelve Apostles (Peter, Paul, Bartholomew, James, Andrew, Simon, Matthew, Luke, John, Mark, Philip, Thomas) and the Seventy Disciples, followed by Stichera to Saint Nicholas as the spiritual luminary and fragrant myrrh-bearer.

[^190]: Wednesday Evening Aposticha and Thursday Matins, Tone 4: Stichera at the Aposticha praising the unlettered Fishermen illumined by the Holy Spirit to overthrow pagan philosophy and idol-worship by the divine resonance of the Gospel, followed by the Sessional Hymns after the 1st Kathisma at Thursday Matins.

[^191]: Wednesday Matins Canons resumed, Tone 4: Continuation of Ode 8 and Ode 9 on physical leaf p123r (Folio 123r), meditating on the tearing up of the ancestral handwriting against Adam through the piercing of Christ's side, and the living Cross illumining the universe and shaking creation.

[^192]: Wednesday Matins Ode 9 conclusion, Aposticha, and Beatitudes (Makarismoi), Tone 4: Troparia honoring the Holy Martyrs who extinguished the darkness of passions, followed by the Cruciform Aposticha and the opening of the Wednesday Beatitudes on leaf p124v (connecting to leaf p122r).

[^193]: Thursday Matins Canons, Tone 4: Odes 4 and 5 of the Canon to the Holy Apostles and the Canon to Saint Nicholas (composed by St. Joseph the Hymnographer), depicting the Apostles as chosen steeds stirring up the sea of nations and Nicholas as the deliverer of the unjustly condemned generals.

[^194]: Thursday Matins Canons, Tone 4: Odes 6 and 7 to the Holy Apostles and St. Nicholas, praising the Apostles who transformed savage wolves into gentle sheep and St. Nicholas who overthrew invisible demonic adversaries and delivered souls from the burning pit.

[^195]: Thursday Matins, Tone 4: Sessional Hymns after the 2nd and 3rd Kathismata celebrating the Apostles as luminaries of the Sun of righteousness and St. Nicholas as a swift protector in tribulation, followed by the opening of the Thursday Canon (Ode 1) with the Heirmos "Traversing of old the deep of the Red Sea with dry feet...".

[^196]: Thursday Matins Canons, Tone 4: Odes 1 and 3 to the Holy Apostles and St. Nicholas, invoking healing from spiritual sloth and honoring St. Nicholas for tearing down the lifeless altars of Artemis.

[^197]: Thursday Matins Canons, Tone 4: Ode 8 to the Holy Apostles and St. Nicholas, praising the spiritual trumpets of Christ, Nicholas stopping the mouths of Arius' followers, and the unceasing hymn of all creation.

[^198]: Thursday Matins Canons and Aposticha, Tone 4: Ode 9 celebrating the Apostles as chosen cornerstones of faith and St. Nicholas streaming fragrant myrrh from his tomb, followed by the Aposticha Stichera to the Apostles and Martyrs.

[^199]: Thursday Divine Liturgy Beatitudes and Thursday Evening (Vespers for Friday), Tone 4: The Beatitudes commemorating the Apostles as spiritual sheep among wolves, followed by Friday Vespers Stichera of the Precious Cross to the melody "Thou hast given a sign."

[^200]: Thursday Evening Stichera of the Cross, Aposticha, and Friday Matins Kathisma 1, Tone 4: Meditations on the torn veil of the Temple, the maternal lamentation of the Theotokos before her crucified Son, and redemption from the curse of the law.

[^201]: Friday Matins Kathismata 2 & 3 and Canon of the Precious Cross, Tone 4: Sessional Hymns contemplating the darkening of the sun and the resurrection of the dead at Christ's death, followed by Ode 1 of the Canon with the Heirmos "I shall open my mouth...".

[^202]: Friday Matins Canons, Tone 4: Odes 1 and 3 of the Canon of the Precious Cross and Canon to the Theotokos, meditating upon Moses prefiguring the Cross by the bronze serpent (Num. 21) and Christ the Lamb willingly led to slaughter.

[^203]: Friday Matins Canons, Tone 4: Odes 3 and 4, reflecting upon the prophetic vision of Habakkuk (Hab. 3), Christ enduring blows upon the cheek to liberate humanity from the demonic ruler, and the holy Martyrs dismembering the ancient serpent.

[^204]: Friday Matins Canons, Tone 4: Odes 5 and 6, contemplating Christ tasting vinegar and gall upon the Cross, the Martyrs bedewed in the furnace of trials, and the universal shaking of creation at the death of the Creator.

[^205]: Friday Matins Canons, Tone 4: Odes 6 and 7, invoking the Prophet Jonah in the belly of the whale (Jonah 2) and the Three Children trampling the Babylonian flames (Dan. 3), celebrating Christ's victory over hades and the healing of our heart's wounds through His divine stripes.

[^206]: Friday Matins Canons, Tone 4: Odes 8 and 9 of the Canon of the Precious and Life-giving Cross and the Canon to the Most-holy Theotokos (physical leaf p131), meditating on Christ Who was bound by His own will to loose mankind from the temporal bonds of mortality, the holy Martyrs mounted upon their blood as upon a chariot to attain supramundane dwellings, and the maternal lamentations of the Virgin Mother at the foot of the Cross.

[^207]: Friday Matins Cruciform Aposticha and Friday Divine Liturgy Beatitudes (Makarismoi), Tone 4 (physical leaf p132): Stichera praising the Cross as an invincible rampart and standard of victory, followed by the Beatitudes meditating upon Adam's expulsion from paradise through the tree and the wise thief's entrance into Eden through the wood of the Cross.

[^208]: Friday Evening (Vespers for Saturday), Tone 4 (physical leaf p132): Stichera on "Lord, I have cried" to the holy Martyrs, Hierarchs, and Venerables to the melody "Thou hast given a sign," honoring the holy Shepherds who laid down their lives for their spiritual flocks against fierce wolves, and the holy Martyrs as rational whole-burnt offerings.

[^209]: Friday Evening Aposticha and Saturday Matins Kathismata 1 and 2, Tone 4 (physical leaves p132–p133): Sessional Hymns and Stichera for the departed, invoking Christ to grant repose to the souls of His servants in the company of the righteous, followed by Saturday Matins Sessional Hymns celebrating the angelic hosts rejoicing at the memory of the Passion-bearers.

[^210]: Saturday Matins Canons, Tone 4 (physical leaves p133–p134): Odes 1, 3, and 4 of the Canon to All Saints (Holy Martyrs, Hierarchs, and Venerables) and the Canon for the Departed, meditating upon the crossing of the Red Sea, the triumph of female martyrs, and intercessions for the faithful departed to attain the heavenly dwellings of the righteous.

[^211]: Saturday Matins Canons, Tone 4 (physical leaves p134–p135): Odes 5, 6, 7, and 8 to All Saints and for the Departed, invoking Christ who preserved the Three Children unconsumed in the Babylonian furnace, the holy Hierarchs and Venerables illumined by ascetic struggles, and supplications for the departed to be granted peaceful repose in the light of the Saints.

[^212]: Saturday Matins Ode 9 and Praises (Ainoi), Tone 4 (physical leaves p135–p136): Ode 9 contrasting Eve who brought in the curse through disobedience with the Virgin who blossomed forth divine blessing unto the world, followed by the Praises Stichera honoring the martyrs who armed themselves with the Cross to conquer the incorporeal enemy, and concluding with the Aposticha for the departed.

[^213]: Codicological Note on Foliation Omission in the 1630 Lviv Edition: In the original printed foliation of the 1630 Lviv Octoechos, folio number 136 (рл҃ѕ) is omitted in the printed sequence. Tone 4 concludes on Folio 135v (physical leaf p136 Left Page), and Tone 5 begins immediately on Folio 137r (physical leaf p136 Right Page), with complete textual and liturgical continuity. Physical leaf indexing (p136) strictly preserves the continuous leaf count of the physical codex.

[^214]: Tone 5 Little Vespers (physical leaves p136–p137): Beginning of Tone 5 on Saturday afternoon. Opening with Stichera on "Lord, I have cried" celebrating the Lord's Resurrection that shattered hades' gates and blunted the sting of sin, followed by the Resurrectional Aposticha and Stichera to the Most-holy Theotokos to the melody "Rejoice, life-bearing [Cross]".

[^215]: Tone 5 Saturday Great Vespers, "Lord, I have cried" (physical leaves p137–p138): The classical Sunday Resurrectional Stichera attributed to Saint John of Damascus in Tone 5, meditating on the shame of the devil and liberation from death, followed by the Anatolian (Eastern) Stichera contemplating the unwaning Light and the confession of the Holy Trinity in three Hypostases.

[^216]: Tone 5 Saturday Great Vespers Dogmatikon and Aposticha (physical leaf p138): The renowned Dogmatikon Theotokion in Tone 5 ("In the Red Sea of old an image of the unwedded Bride was prefigured..."), followed by the Resurrectional Aposticha arranged according to the Greek acrostic/alphabet, and the Resurrection Troparion in Tone 5 ("Let us, the faithful, hymn and worship the Word...").

[^217]: Tone 5 Sunday Midnight Office (Mesonyktikon) Canon to the Holy Trinity (physical leaves p138–p139): Composed by Saint Metrophanes of Smyrna, contemplating the tri-hypostatic, co-unoriginate, and undivided Godhead, the three-sunned illumination of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, and the vision of Daniel and the Thrice-Holy hymn of the Cherubim and Seraphim.

[^218]: Tone 5 Sunday Matins Resurrectional Sessional Hymns and Hypakoe (physical leaf p140): Sessional Hymns after the 1st and 2nd Kathismata contemplating the holy Myrrh-bearing women at the tomb, the remorse of Peter, the theological confession of the repentant thief upon the cross, and the Angel's proclamation to the Myrrh-bearers.

[^219]: Tone 5 Sunday Matins Anavathmoi and Sunday Canons, Ode 1 (physical leaf p140): Antiphons 1, 2, and 3 in Tone 5, based on the Gradual Psalms (Psalms 119–133 LXX), followed by the Prokeimenon (Psalm 9:33 LXX), and Ode 1 of the Sunday Resurrection Canon ("The steed and rider into the Red Sea..."), the Cross-Resurrection Canon, and the Canon to the Theotokos.

[^220]: Tone 5 Sunday Matins Canons, Odes 3–5 (physical leaves p141–p142): The Sunday Resurrection Canon, Cross-Resurrection Canon, and Canon to the Most-holy Theotokos, meditating upon Christ Who suspended the uncontainable weight of the earth upon nothing, the bitter gall offered in place of manna by ungrateful Israel, and the Virgin Mother prefigured in the unburned bush of Sinai.

[^221]: Tone 5 Sunday Matins Ode 6 and Resurrectional Kontakion and Ikos (physical leaf p142): Celebrating Christ's descent into hades, shattering its eternal gates as Almighty, breaking the sting of death, and delivering Adam from the ancient curse; followed by the Ikos recounting the Myrrh-bearing women hearing the angelic proclamation and the Risen Lord appearing to send them unto Galilee.

[^222]: Tone 5 Sunday Matins Canons, Odes 7 and 8 (physical leaves p142–p143): Contemplating Christ Who assumed human flesh as bait upon a fishhook to draw down the spiritual serpent, the two natural wills and two essences of the Incarnate Word in His voluntary agony in Gethsemane, and the mocking of hades at His life-giving descent.

[^223]: Tone 5 Sunday Matins Ode 9 and Praises (Ainoi) (physical leaves p143–p144): The concluding ninth ode taking as its biblical model Isaiah's prophecy of Emmanuel, followed by the Resurrectional Praises Stichera in Tone 5, meditating upon the guards and the unbroken seals of the sepulchre, and the Anatolian (Eastern) Stichera proclaiming the overthrow of death.

[^224]: Tone 5 Praises Stichera (concluding) and Sunday Divine Liturgy Beatitudes (Makarismoi) (physical leaf p144): Concluding stichera depicting the soldiers' terror and the angel rolling away the stone, followed by the Sunday Liturgy Beatitudes praising the good thief who confessed Christ upon the cross and received paradise.

[^225]: Tone 5 Sunday Evening (Vespers for Monday) Penitential Stichera and Stichera to the Bodiless Hosts (physical leaves p144–p145): Opening the liturgical week with profound compunction, mourning the squandering of baptismal grace before the unquenchable fire and the sickle of death, followed by supplications unto the holy Archangels and the heavenly angelic hierarchies.

[^226]: Tone 5 Monday Matins Sessional Hymns and Penitential/Bodiless Canons, Odes 1–3 (physical leaves p145–p146): Sessional Hymns after the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd Kathismata on the parable of the ten virgins and the impending judgment, followed by the Penitential Canon of Saint Joseph the Hymnographer and the Canon to the Bodiless Hosts.

[^227]: Tone 5 Monday Matins Canons (Odes 4–9), Aposticha, and Monday Divine Liturgy Beatitudes (physical leaves p146–p148): The completion of the Monday canons, celebrating the Archangels Michael and Gabriel as heralds and guardians, the Penitential Aposticha meditating upon the barren fig tree, and the Monday Liturgy Beatitudes.

[^228]: Tone 5 Monday Evening (Vespers for Tuesday) Penitential Stichera and Stichera to Saint John the Forerunner (physical leaves p148–p149): Stichera on "Lord, I have cried" to the melody "Rejoice, O container of ascetics," lamenting the violation of the second baptismal covenant and entreating the holy Forerunner and Baptist John as the radiant light of the spiritual Sun.

[^229]: Tone 5 Tuesday Matins Sessional Hymns and Penitential/Forerunner Canons, Odes 1–6 (physical leaves p149–p151): Sessional Hymns on the dread judgment seat and the holy Martyrs, followed by the Penitential Canon of Saint Joseph and the Canon to Saint John the Baptist, contemplating his immaculate and ascetic life in the wilderness as a mediator between the Old and New Covenants.

[^230]: Tone 5 Tuesday Matins Canons completion (Odes 7–9) (physical leaves p151–p152): The completion of the Penitential Canon of Saint Joseph the Hymnographer and the Canon to Saint John the Forerunner, contemplating the youths in the furnace, the Prodigal Son starving for heavenly bread, and the glorious Baptist as an unshakable light of the spiritual Sun.

[^231]: Tone 5 Tuesday Matins Aposticha and Liturgy Beatitudes; Tuesday Evening (Vespers for Wednesday) Stichera of the Precious Cross (physical leaves p152–p153): Concluding Tuesday Matins with penitential compunction and praises of the Holy Martyrs, followed by the Tuesday Evening Vespers Stichera on "Lord, I have cried" to the melody "Rejoice, O container of ascetics," meditating upon Christ uplifted upon the Cross like a Lamb, quenching the flaming sword that barred access to Eden.

[^232]: Tone 5 Tuesday Evening Vespers completion and Wednesday Matins Sessional Hymns (physical leaves p153–p154): Concluding Wednesday Vespers with the Cross Aposticha and Cross-Theotokion of the immaculate Mother weeping at Golgotha, followed by Wednesday Matins Sessional Hymns after the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd Kathismata celebrating Golgotha transformed into Paradise.

[^233]: Tone 5 Wednesday Matins Canon of the Precious Cross and Canon to the Most-holy Theotokos, Odes 1–4 (physical leaves p154–p155): Composed by Saint Joseph the Hymnographer, contemplating Christ as the fruitful Vine uplifted upon the Tree, distilling the wine of spiritual joy, and the Mother of God as the mystical cloud showering forth divine rain.

[^234]: Tone 5 Wednesday Matins Canons, Odes 5–8 (physical leaves p155–p156): Meditating upon the righteous Judge standing before an unjust judge to condemn ancient enmity in His flesh, the tearing of the veil and splitting of rocks at His expiration, and the Holy Martyrs who stood firm like adamants against fiery torments.

[^235]: Tone 5 Wednesday Matins Ode 9, Aposticha, and Wednesday Divine Liturgy Beatitudes (physical leaves p156–p157): Concluding the Matins canons with the Virgin beholding Her Son crowned with thorns, followed by the Cross Aposticha and Liturgy Beatitudes praising the Good Thief.

[^238]: Tone 5 Thursday Matins Canons to the Apostles and Saint Nicholas, Odes 5–8 (physical leaves p159–p160): Continuing the supplication unto the Apostles who seasoned corrupted souls with the salt of heavenly doctrine, and Saint Nicholas who silenced the blasphemous streams of Arius and delivered the unjustly condemned from execution.

[^339]: Tone 8 Saturday Matins Praises, Aposticha of the Departed, Saturday Divine Liturgy Beatitudes, and Monumental Conclusion of the 1630 Printed Octoechos (physical leaf p260 Left Page / Folio 260v to Right Page / Folio 261r): Concluding Saturday Matins with the Praises of the Martyrs ('What shall we call you, O holy ones?', 'Greatly did ye contend', 'Invincible Martyrs of Christ', and 'Clothed well in faith'), followed by the Aposticha of the Departed (Model: 'O most glorious wonder') on Christ signing man's liberation with the scarlet dye of His own Blood; continuing with the Saturday Divine Liturgy Beatitudes; and culminating on Folio 261r in the grand monumental printing boundary: 'КОНЕ́ЦЪ О́СМОМУ ГЛА́СУ.' ('END OF THE EIGHTH TONE.'), adorned with the Dormition Brotherhood Press's iconic woodcut ornamental ribbon-knot vignette and decorative floral stamps, marking the official completion of the entire cycle of the Eight Tones in the 1630 Lviv Octoechos.

[^340]: 1638 Purchase and Donation Charter (physical leaf p261 Left Page / Folio 261v): A seventeenth-century cursive inscription in Ukrainian chancery hand recording that Pope-cantor Tereshko Kuzmyn Vyshnevskyi purchased this 1630 Lviv Octoechos for the Church of Saint Nicholas, paid 2 zlotys unto Petrus the bookbinder to have it bound, and endowed it unto the village church for perpetual times immutably, dated in November 1638 (Anno Domini 1638), concluded by the solemn liturgical opening doxology: 'Blessed is the Kingdom of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.'

[^341]: Calligraphic Manuscript Supplement of the Eleven Resurrectional Exaposteilaria and Evangelical Stichera (physical leaf p261 Right Page / Manuscript Folio 1r): Inception of the contemporary seventeenth-century liturgical supplement appended to the printed 1630 Lviv Octoechos, supplying the full weekly cycle of the 11 Resurrectional Exaposteilaria (attributed to Byzantine Emperor Constantine VII Porphyrogenitus, 905–959) and the 11 Gospel Stichera (attributed to Emperor Leo VI the Wise, 866–912), designed to accompany the eleven Sunday Matins Resurrection Gospels; opening with Tone 1 Exaposteilarion 1 ('Let us go up with the disciples into the mountain of Galilee'), Theotokion ('Rejoice with the disciples, O Virgin Theotokos'), Tone 1 Evangelical Stichera 1 ('When the disciples went up into the mountain'), Tone 2 Exaposteilarion 2 ('Beholding the stone rolled away'), and Tone 2 Theotokion 2 incipit.

[^344]: Resurrectional Cycle Continued: Tone 4 through Tone 5 (physical leaf p263 Left Page): Completion of Tone 4 Evangelical Stichera 4 with Peter glorifying Christ's all-powerful wonders; Tone 5 Exaposteilarion 5 ('Christ, the Life and the Way, having risen from the dead') on the road to Emmaus with Cleopas and Luke; Tone 5 Theotokion ('The Creator of creation and God of all things'); and Tone 5 Evangelical Stichera 5 opening ('O how wise are Thy judgments, O Christ!') on Peter recognizing the Resurrection from the grave-clothes and the burning hearts of the Emmaus travelers.

[^350]: 1964 Zaliztsi Novyi Colophon and Soviet State Museum Stamps (physical leaf p266 Left Page & Right Page): Autograph memorandum by cantor Mykola Makar dated December 6, 1964, documenting his clandestine concealment and preservation of the historic 1630 Lviv Octoechos for the Church of the Protection in Zaliztsi Novi during Soviet state-enforced religious closures; facing the cataloguing stamps of the State Museum of the Book and Printing of the Ukrainian SSR in Kyiv (Fond 2124, Inventory No. CD-97).

[^351]: Historic 17th-Century Blind-Tooled Calfskin Binding (physical leaf p267 Left Page & Right Page): Concluding bibliographic examination of the original 1630 Lviv Dormition Brotherhood binding, featuring bevelled wooden boards covered in dark brown calfskin, blind-stamped with renaissance roll-stamps, concentric framing fillets, and diagonal lattice panels, with three original brass clasps and catches preserved on leather thongs along the fore-edge, marking the physical and codicological completion of Monument 9: 1630 Lviv Octoechos.
